nodes.title: Discrete Huber pairs are sheafy with Čech-acyclic rational coverings (Wedhorn Theorem 8.28(c))
nodes.statement: Let A be a ring with the discrete topology and A⁺ ⊆ A an integrally closed subring, so that (A, A⁺) is a complete Huber pair (pair of definition (A, 0)) and Spa(A, A⁺) = {v ∈ Spv A : v(a) ≤ 1 for all a ∈ A⁺}. Then: (a) for every rational subset U = R(T/s), 𝒪(U) = A_s with the discrete topology; (b) for every finite covering (U_j = R(T_j/s_j)) of a rational subset U = R(T/s) by rational subsets and every A-module M, the augmented Čech complex 0 → M_s → ∏ M_{s_{j₀}} → ∏ M_{s_{j₀}s_{j₁}} → ⋯ of the covering with coefficients M ⊗_A 𝒪 is exact in all degrees; (c) 𝒪 is a sheaf of complete topological rings on Spa(A, A⁺), i.e. (A, A⁺) is sheafy; 𝒪(W) is discrete for quasi-compact open W, but for a non-quasi-compact W it is only the (complete) limit of the discrete rings 𝒪(V), V ⊆ W rational. No noetherian hypothesis is made.
hypotheses: A a discrete ring (any commutative ring); A⁺ ⊆ A integrally closed.
M an arbitrary A-module (for (b)).
proofSteps: (a) With the pair of definition (A, 0), the uncompleted rational localisation A(T/s) is A_s with ring of definition A[T/s] and ideal of definition 0 (Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.locSubring`, `PairOfDefinition.locIdeal`), so its topology is discrete and it is complete: 𝒪(R(T/s)) = A_s (anchor Layer 3).

Covering: U_j ⊆ U gives a restriction A_s → A_{s_j}, so D(s_j) ⊆ D(s) in Spec A. For 𝔭 ∈ D(s) the trivial valuation v_𝔭 (value 0 on 𝔭, 1 elsewhere) lies in Spa(A, A⁺) (every valuation is continuous on a discrete ring) and in U, hence in some U_j, so s_j ∉ 𝔭: the D(s_j) cover D(s) = Spec A_s (anchor Layer 2).
Intersections: U_{j₀} ∩ ⋯ ∩ U_{j_p} is rational with ring A_{s_{j₀}⋯s_{j_p}} (anchor Layer 2, Wedhorn Remark 7.30(5)), and M ⊗_A A_{s_{j₀}⋯} = (M_s)_{s_{j₀}⋯} because s is a unit there.
(b) The complex is the extended Čech complex of the A_s-module M_s for the elements s_j of A_s, which generate the unit ideal; it is exact by R0/localization-cech-complex-exact.

(c) The structure presheaf on an arbitrary open W is the limit of 𝒪(V) over rational V ⊆ W (anchor Layer 3), so by EGA 0_I 3.2.2 together with Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.isSheaf_iff_isSheafFor_rationalCover` it suffices to check coverings (U_j)_{j∈J} of a rational U by rational subsets. U is quasi-compact, so finitely many U_{j₁}, …, U_{j_m} cover it. (b) with M = A in degrees −1, 0 gives injectivity and gluing for this finite subcovering. Applying the same injectivity to the finite rational coverings {U_{j_k} ∩ U_j}_k of each U_j shows that the glued section restricts correctly to every U_j. So the sheaf condition holds for (U_j). Topologically, 𝒪(U) = A_s is discrete and injects into the finite subproduct ∏_k 𝒪(U_{j_k}) of discrete rings, so 𝒪(U) → ∏_{j∈J} 𝒪(U_j) is a topological embedding for the product topology. Completeness holds on rational subsets (discrete) and passes to limits.
acceptance: The discrete ring ℤ[T₁, T₂, …] (not noetherian) with A⁺ = A gives a sheafy Spa(A, A).
For A = k[T] discrete and A⁺ = k, the covering R(1, T / T) ∪ R(T, 1 / 1) of Spa(A, A⁺) gives the exact complex 0 → k[T] → k[T, T⁻¹] × k[T] → k[T, T⁻¹] → 0.

nodes.title: Complete rings of noetherian type are stably sheafy
nodes.statement: Let A be a complete Hausdorff Huber ring of noetherian type. Then A is stably sheafy in the anchor's sense (`Huber.IsStablySheafyRing A`, Wedhorn Definition 8.26): for every complete Hausdorff Huber ring B topologically of finite type over A (Tau Ceti `IsTopologicallyFiniteType`) and every ring of integral elements B⁺ of B, the structure presheaf of Spa(B, B⁺) is a sheaf of complete topological rings. Three cases occur: (T) B Tate — B is strongly noetherian and the anchor's Layer 4.1 theorem applies, with all-degree exactness of augmented Čech complexes on finite rational covers of rational subsets; (N) B has a noetherian ring of definition (for instance ℤ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟦T⟧) — Huber 1994 Theorem 2.2, Case I (R0/noetherian-rod-sheafy), with exact strict Čech complexes on standard rational covers of rational subsets, which refine every open cover; (D) B discrete — R0/discrete-huber-pair-sheafy, with all-degree Čech exactness on finite rational covers (a special case of (N), since the prime subring of a discrete ring is a noetherian ring of definition, with an elementary proof).
hypotheses: A complete Hausdorff Huber ring of noetherian type.
proofSteps: Every complete B topologically of finite type over A is of noetherian type (R0/topologically-finite-type-noetherian-type): it has a noetherian ring of definition or is a strongly noetherian Tate ring (R0/noetherian-type-huber-ring).
Case (T): the anchor's Layer 4.1 proves `Huber.IsSheafyPair B B⁺` and all-degree Čech exactness for complete strongly noetherian Tate B (Wedhorn Theorem 8.28(b), Corollary 8.35).
Case (N): R0/noetherian-rod-sheafy (d) applied to (B, B⁺) (Huber 1994 Theorem 2.2, Case I: the blow-up construction (1.1)–(1.2), strictness (1.3.1), (1.3), refinement (1.5) with Lemma 2.6).
Case (D): R0/discrete-huber-pair-sheafy (c) applied to (B, B⁺).
acceptance: Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟨T⟩) and all its rational localisations are sheafy (case T).
Spa(ℤ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟨T⟩) and Spa(ℤ_p⟦T⟧⟨X⟩, ℤ_p⟦T⟧⟨X⟩) are sheafy (case N).
Spa(𝔽_p[T], 𝔽_p) is sheafy (case D).

nodes.title: The completed tensor product of Huber pairs along adic homomorphisms
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺), (B, B⁺), (C, C⁺) be Huber pairs (Tau Ceti `Pair`) and f : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺), g : (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) morphisms of Huber pairs (Tau Ceti `Pair.Hom`) whose underlying ring homomorphisms are adic (R0/adic-ring-homomorphism). Choose a pair of definition (A₀, I) of A and rings of definition B₀ ⊆ B⁺, C₀ ⊆ C⁺ with f(A₀) ⊆ B₀, g(A₀) ⊆ C₀ such that f(I)B₀ and g(I)C₀ are ideals of definition. Let E := B ⊗_A C (Mathlib `Algebra.TensorProduct`, B and C being A-algebras through f and g), let F ⊆ E be the image of B₀ ⊗_{A₀} C₀ (a subring), and give E the group topology for which {Iⁿ·F : n ≥ 0} is a fundamental system of neighbourhoods of 0, where Iⁿ·F is the additive subgroup generated by the products of images of elements of Iⁿ with elements of F. Then E is a Huber ring with pair of definition (F, I·F), the maps inl : b ↦ b ⊗ 1 and inr : c ↦ 1 ⊗ c are adic, the topology does not depend on the choice of (A₀, I, B₀, C₀), and E⁺ := the integral closure in E of the image of B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺ is a ring of integral elements of E. The *completed tensor product* is the complete Hausdorff Huber pair B ⊗̂_A C := (Ê, Ê⁺), where Ê is the Hausdorff completion of E (Tau Ceti `IsHuberRing.completion`) and Ê⁺ is the closure of the image of E⁺; it carries the morphisms of Huber pairs inl : (B, B⁺) → B ⊗̂_A C, inr : (C, C⁺) → B ⊗̂_A C with inl ∘ f = inr ∘ g. It is a Tate ring whenever B or C is. Pinned conventions: B ⊗̂_A C always means this completed pair; the plus ring is the integral closure of the image of B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺ (not the image itself), then closed up in the completion; no uniformisation is performed; the construction is not defined unless both f and g are adic. Lean name: `Huber.Pair.completedTensor f g hf hg`.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺), (B, B⁺), (C, C⁺) Huber pairs; B and C need not be complete.
f : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) and g : (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) morphisms of Huber pairs.
The ring homomorphisms underlying f and g are adic.
proofSteps: Common choice of rings of definition: choose a pair of definition (A₀, I) of A with A₀ ⊆ A⁺ (the intersection of a ring of definition with the open subring A⁺ is a ring of definition, Wedhorn Corollary 6.4(1),(2); anchor Layer 0.2). Since f is adic and B⁺ is an open subring containing f(A₀), Huber 1993 Lemma 1.8(iii) (R0/adic-hom-choice-independence) gives a ring of definition B₀ of B with f(A₀) ⊆ B₀ ⊆ B⁺, and likewise C₀ with g(A₀) ⊆ C₀ ⊆ C⁺; by Lemma 1.8(ii) f(I)B₀ and g(I)C₀ are then ideals of definition of B₀ and C₀. (The same lemma makes every later shrinking of A₀, B₀, C₀ admissible; no separate argument about (I¹)ᴺ ⊆ I is needed.)

Ring topology (Morel Proposition II.3.2.1): multiplication is continuous at 0 because F is a subring and Iᵃ F · Iᵇ F ⊆ I^{a+b} F; for a pure tensor b ⊗ c choose k with b·f(I)ᵏB₀ ⊆ B₀ and c·g(I)ᵏC₀ ⊆ C₀ (B₀, C₀ open and multiplication by b, c continuous), then (b ⊗ c)·I^{2k}F ⊆ F, so every x ↦ ax is continuous; Bourbaki's criterion (Topologie générale III §6 no. 3) gives a ring topology.

Pair of definition: F is open, I·F is generated by the finitely many images of generators of I, and Iⁿ·F = (I·F)ⁿ, so (F, I·F) is a pair of definition (Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition`); inl(B₀) ⊆ F and inl(f(I))·F = I·F, so inl (and likewise inr) is adic.

Independence of choices: for two admissible choices (A₀, I, B₀, C₀) and (A₀', I', B₀', C₀') take A₀'' = A₀ ∩ A₀' with an ideal of definition I'' ⊆ I ∩ I', B₀'' = B₀ ∩ B₀', C₀'' = C₀ ∩ C₀' (admissible by Lemma 1.8(ii), R0/adic-hom-choice-independence); the neighbourhood bases {Iⁿ·F}, {I''ⁿ·F''} are mutually cofinal because each ideal of definition is open in A and each ring of definition of B (resp. C) contains a power of the other's ideal of definition times it; likewise for the primed choice.

Plus ring: E⁺ contains F (B₀ ⊆ B⁺, C₀ ⊆ C⁺), so it is open; images of b ⊗ 1 with b ∈ B⁺ ⊆ B° are power-bounded because f(I)ᵏ·{bⁿ} ⊆ B₀ gives Iᵏ·{(b ⊗ 1)ⁿ}·F ⊆ F; E° is an integrally closed subring (anchor Layer 0.2), so the integral closure of the image of B⁺ ⊗ C⁺ lies in E°; Tau Ceti `Pair.isRingOfIntegralElements_integralClosure` concludes.

Completion: Ê is a Huber ring (Tau Ceti `IsHuberRing.completion`, `PairOfDefinition.completion`), and the closure of the image of E⁺ is a ring of integral elements of Ê with Spa(Ê, Ê⁺) ≅ Spa(E, E⁺) (completion of Huber pairs, anchor Layer 0.3; Wedhorn Lemma 7.47(4), Proposition 7.48).
Tate: the image of a pseudouniformiser of B under inl is a topologically nilpotent unit of Ê (Tau Ceti `IsTateRing.completion`).

nodes.title: Universal property of the completed tensor product
nodes.statement: Let f : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) and g : (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) be morphisms of Huber pairs with adic underlying ring homomorphisms, and let D = B ⊗̂_A C with inl, inr (R0/completed-tensor-product). Let R be a complete Hausdorff nonarchimedean topological commutative ring and R⁺ ⊆ R a closed subring integrally closed in R (for instance a complete Huber pair, or (O_X(X), O_X⁺(X)) for an adic space X). For all continuous ring homomorphisms φ : B → R, ψ : C → R with φ(B⁺) ⊆ R⁺, ψ(C⁺) ⊆ R⁺ and φ ∘ f = ψ ∘ g, there is exactly one continuous ring homomorphism χ : D → R with χ(D⁺) ⊆ R⁺, χ ∘ inl = φ and χ ∘ inr = ψ. In particular the square of f, g, inl, inr is cocartesian in the category of complete Hausdorff Huber pairs. If moreover R is Huber and φ is adic, then χ is adic. No adicness of φ or ψ is needed.
hypotheses: f, g morphisms of Huber pairs whose underlying ring homomorphisms are adic.
R complete Hausdorff, nonarchimedean (open additive subgroups form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0).
R⁺ ⊆ R a closed subring, integrally closed in R.
φ, ψ continuous, φ(B⁺) ⊆ R⁺, ψ(C⁺) ⊆ R⁺, φ ∘ f = ψ ∘ g.
proofSteps: Algebraic factorisation: Mathlib `Algebra.TensorProduct.lift` gives the unique ring homomorphism χ₀ : B ⊗_A C → R with χ₀(b ⊗ c) = φ(b)ψ(c) (R is commutative, so the commutation hypothesis is automatic).

Continuity of χ₀ for the topology {Iⁿ·F}: given an open subgroup U of R choose an open subgroup V with V·V ⊆ U (continuity of multiplication at (0, 0)), then k with φ(f(I)ᵏB₀) ⊆ V and ψ(g(I)ᵏC₀) ⊆ V (continuity of φ, ψ and f(I)B₀, g(I)C₀ ideals of definition — this is where adicness of f and g is used); I^{2k}·F is generated by images of (f(I)ᵏB₀) ⊗ (g(I)ᵏC₀), so χ₀(I^{2k}·F) ⊆ V·V ⊆ U.
Extension: Mathlib `UniformSpace.Completion.extensionHom` extends χ₀ to the completion D, with `UniformSpace.Completion.extensionHom_coe` giving χ ∘ inl = φ, χ ∘ inr = ψ.
Plus rings: χ maps the image of B⁺ ⊗ C⁺ into R⁺, hence its integral closure into the integral closure of R⁺ in R, which is R⁺; by continuity and closedness of R⁺ the closure D⁺ maps into R⁺.
Uniqueness: two such χ agree on the image of B ⊗_A C (Mathlib `Algebra.TensorProduct.ext`), which is dense (`Huber.Pair.completedTensor.denseRange_tmul`), and R is Hausdorff.

Adicness of χ when R is Huber and φ is adic: χ ∘ (ι ∘ inl) = φ, where ι : E → D is the completion map and ι ∘ inl : B → D is continuous; hence χ is adic by cancellation (`Huber.IsAdicHom.of_comp`, R0/adic-ring-homomorphism; Wedhorn Proposition 6.26(2) = Huber 1993 Corollary 1.9(ii)). (The previous argument placed φ(B₀)ψ(C₀) in a ring of definition of R, which needs boundedness of ψ(C₀) — not automatic for a merely continuous ψ.)
acceptance: For K⟨T⟩ and K⟨S⟩ over K, the unique map K⟨T⟩ ⊗̂_K K⟨S⟩ → K⟨T, S⟩ given by the two inclusions is an isomorphism (both represent pairs of power-bounded elements).

Without adicness of f the statement fails: for ℤ_p → ℤ_p⟦X⟧ and ℤ_p → ℚ_p no Huber topology on the tensor product makes the structure maps continuous (Morel Example II.3.2.2).

nodes.title: Base change of weighted restricted power series and of their quotients
nodes.statement: Let λ : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) be a morphism of Huber pairs whose ring homomorphism is adic, and let M = (M₁,…,M_n) be finite subsets of A with every M_i·A open in A. Then (a) every λ(M_i)·B is open in B, so the weighted restricted power-series pair B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)} = B⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩_{λ(M₁),…,λ(M_n)} is defined (Huber's plus ring: the integral closure of {∑ b_ν X^ν : b_ν ∈ λ(M)^ν·(B⁺)^ for all ν}); (b) the morphism A⟨X⟩_M ⊗̂_A B → B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)} induced by the natural extension λ' : A⟨X⟩_M → B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)} of λ (X_i ↦ X_i) and by the structure map B → B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)} is an isomorphism of complete Huber pairs; (c) if σ : A⟨X⟩_M → (C, C⁺) is a quotient mapping of complete Huber pairs (surjective, continuous and open, C⁺ the integral closure of σ(A⟨X⟩_M⁺)) with kernel 𝔞, then C ⊗̂_A B ≅ B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)}/𝔟 with 𝔟 the closure of λ'(𝔞)·B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)}, quotient topology and plus ring the integral closure of the image of B⟨X⟩⁺_{λ(M)}; if B is complete of noetherian type then 𝔟 = λ'(𝔞)·B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)}. Consequently B → C ⊗̂_A B is topologically of finite type as a morphism of Huber pairs (a quotient mapping out of B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)}) and as a ring homomorphism (Tau Ceti `IsTopologicallyFiniteType`). (d) Ring-level presentations: if μ : A → C is only topologically of finite type as a ring homomorphism (Tau Ceti `IsTopologicallyFiniteType μ`, presented by a surjective continuous open ring homomorphism σ : Â⟨X⟩_M → C with σ ∘ h = μ, finite weights M_i with M_i·A open) and C⁺ is any ring of integral elements of C with μ(A⁺) ⊆ C⁺ (μ adic by R0/topologically-finite-type-is-adic), then the topological ring underlying C ⊗̂_A B is still B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)}/𝔟 as in (c), its plus ring is the closure of the integral closure of the image of C⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} B⁺, and inl : B → C ⊗̂_A B is topologically of finite type as a ring homomorphism. This is the form used for morphisms locally of weakly finite type (R0/fibre-products-existence case (b), R0/completed-tensor-noetherian-stability).
hypotheses: λ : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) a morphism of Huber pairs with adic ring homomorphism.
M₁,…,M_n finite subsets of A with each M_i·A open.
For (c): σ a quotient mapping of complete Huber pairs out of A⟨X⟩_M.
proofSteps: (a) An open ideal of A contains Iᵏ·A for a pair of definition (A₀, I) (Wedhorn Lemma 6.6, anchor Layer 0.2), so λ(M_i)·B ⊇ λ(I)ᵏ·B ⊇ (λ(I)B₀)ᵏ, which is open because λ is adic. The weight-family hypothesis of Tau Ceti's `weightedRestrictedSubring` (λ(M_i)ᵐ·U a neighbourhood of 0 for all m and all neighbourhoods U) follows from openness of λ(M_i)·B by Wedhorn Lemma 6.20 = Huber Lemma 1.1, which the anchor's Layer 0.4 states as the equivalent form of its standing hypothesis (imported).

(b) The pair-level universal property of A⟨X⟩_M (Huber 1994 Lemma 3.5(i): morphisms A⟨X⟩_M → (R, R⁺) to complete pairs correspond to morphisms φ : A → R together with r_i ∈ R such that φ(m)·r_i ∈ R⁺ for m ∈ M_i), imported with the plus ring of A⟨X⟩_M from the anchor's Layer 5.2; its ring-level part is Tau Ceti `existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_completion_weightedRestrictedSubring` together with `isWeightBounded_of_isWeightedVarPowerBounded` (the finite set {φ(m)·r_i : m ∈ M_i} ⊆ R⁺ consists of power-bounded elements, so its multiplicative monoid is bounded; the combined form `…_of_isWeightedVarPowerBounded` also exists at the pinned commit, WeightedEval/Completion.lean, but is missing from the declaration index), and λ' is Tau Ceti `weightedMapCompletion` (λ(M_i) ⊆ λ(M_i)).

(b) cont.: by R0/completed-tensor-product-universal-property, morphisms A⟨X⟩_M ⊗̂_A B → (R, R⁺) correspond to pairs (A⟨X⟩_M → R, B → R) agreeing on A, hence to (ψ : B → R, r_i with ψ(λ(m))·r_i ∈ R⁺), which by Lemma 3.5(i) for B are the morphisms B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)} → (R, R⁺). Both objects represent the same functor on complete Hausdorff Huber pairs, and the comparison morphism is the one of the statement; so it is an isomorphism (Yoneda).

(c) C ⊗̂_A B represents pairs (C → R, B → R) agreeing on A; C → R is a morphism A⟨X⟩_M → R killing 𝔞 (universal property of the quotient pair, Tau Ceti `Pair.quotient` and `Pair.Hom.quotientLift`, plus continuity: a continuous map to a Hausdorff R killing 𝔞 kills its closure); so C ⊗̂_A B represents morphisms B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)} → R killing λ'(𝔞), which B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)}/𝔟 represents. The noetherian case: 𝔟 is closed by R0/noetherian-type-ideals-closed applied to B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)}, which is of noetherian type by R0/topologically-finite-type-noetherian-type.
Topologically finite type: B → B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)}/𝔟 is the composite of the presenting map with an open quotient map (Tau Ceti `IsTopologicallyFiniteType.comp_isOpenQuotientMap`).

(d) The ring and the topology of the completed tensor product depend only on rings and ideals of definition, not on plus rings (R0/completed-tensor-product). Let C⁺_σ be the integral closure of σ(Â⟨X⟩_M⁺): it is open (σ open), contained in C° (an open continuous surjection maps power-bounded elements to power-bounded elements, as in Tau Ceti `Pair.quotient`), so a ring of integral elements with μ(A⁺) ⊆ C⁺_σ, and σ : A⟨X⟩_M → (C, C⁺_σ) is a quotient mapping of pairs. Apply (c) to (C, C⁺_σ) to get the ring B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)}/𝔟 and topological finite type of inl; the plus ring for the given C⁺ comes from R0/completed-tensor-product.

nodes.title: Completed base change along a topologically-finite-type map preserves noetherian type and sheafiness
nodes.statement: Let λ : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) and μ : (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) be morphisms of complete Hausdorff Huber pairs with λ adic and μ topologically of finite type as a ring homomorphism (Tau Ceti `IsTopologicallyFiniteType`; then μ is adic by R0/topologically-finite-type-is-adic). If B is of noetherian type, then inl : B → B ⊗̂_A C is topologically of finite type, B ⊗̂_A C is a complete Hausdorff Huber ring of noetherian type, and B ⊗̂_A C (with its plus ring, or with any other ring of integral elements) is sheafy — indeed stably sheafy (R0/noetherian-type-stably-sheafy). If μ is topologically of finite type as a morphism of pairs, inl is so as a morphism of pairs.
hypotheses: λ adic; μ topologically of finite type (ring level); A, B, C complete Hausdorff.
B of noetherian type (R0/noetherian-type-huber-ring).
proofSteps: Present C by the ring-level presentation σ : Â⟨X⟩_M → C of `IsTopologicallyFiniteType μ` (for the pair-level statement, by a quotient mapping of pairs A⟨X⟩_M → (C, C⁺)).

R0/noetherian-type-stably-sheafy: it is stably sheafy, hence sheafy for every ring of integral elements.

nodes.title: Rational localisation commutes with completed tensor products
nodes.statement: Let f : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺), g : (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) be morphisms of complete Hausdorff Huber pairs with adic ring homomorphisms, D = B ⊗̂_A C, and p_B = Spa(inl) : Spa D → Spa B, p_C = Spa(inr) (Tau Ceti `Pair.Hom.spaComap`). Let U = R(T/s) ⊆ Spa B, V = R(T'/s') ⊆ Spa C, W = R(T''/s'') ⊆ Spa A be rational subsets with Spa(f)(U) ⊆ W and Spa(g)(V) ⊆ W, and let O(U) = B⟨T/s⟩ etc. denote the rational localisations as complete Huber pairs (anchor Layer 3.1; Tau Ceti `completionLocalization`). Then: (1) p_B⁻¹(U) = R(inl(T)/inl(s)) and p_C⁻¹(V) = R(inr(T')/inr(s')) are rational, and p_B⁻¹(U) ∩ p_C⁻¹(V) is the rational subset R(inl(T ∪ {s})·inr(T' ∪ {s'}) / inl(s)inr(s')); (2) the maps O(W) → O(U), O(W) → O(V) are adic and the canonical morphism O(U) ⊗̂_{O(W)} O(V) → O_D(p_B⁻¹(U) ∩ p_C⁻¹(V)) is an isomorphism of complete Huber pairs; (3) consequently Spa(O(U) ⊗̂_{O(W)} O(V)) → Spa D is a homeomorphism onto p_B⁻¹(U) ∩ p_C⁻¹(V) matching rational subsets.
hypotheses: f, g morphisms of complete Hausdorff Huber pairs with adic ring homomorphisms.
U, V, W rational subsets (T·B open, etc.) with Spa(f)(U) ⊆ W, Spa(g)(V) ⊆ W.
proofSteps: (1) Preimages: Tau Ceti `Pair.Hom.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset` computes p_B⁻¹(R(T/s)) = R(inl(T)/inl(s)) as sets; since inl is adic, inl(T)·D is open (T·B ⊇ power of an ideal of definition, Wedhorn Lemma 6.6), so this is a rational subset in Huber's sense (Wedhorn Lemma 7.46(3)). Finite intersections of rational subsets are rational with the product presentation (anchor Layer 2.2, Wedhorn Remark 7.30(5)).

(2) Adicness: B → O(U) is topologically of finite type (Wedhorn Example 6.38, Huber 1994 Corollary 3.4(i)) hence adic (R0/topologically-finite-type-is-adic); O(W) → O(U) is adic by cancellation (`Huber.IsAdicHom.of_comp`, R0/adic-ring-homomorphism) since A → O(W) → O(U) equals A → B → O(U).

(2) cont.: morphisms O(U) ⊗̂_{O(W)} O(V) → (R, R⁺) (complete Huber pairs) correspond (R0/completed-tensor-product-universal-property) to pairs (O(U) → R, O(V) → R) agreeing on O(W); by the universal property of rational localisation (Tau Ceti `existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset`, Huber 1994 Proposition 1.3) these are pairs (B → R with Spa R → U, C → R with Spa R → V) agreeing on A (agreement on O(W) follows from agreement on A by uniqueness in O(W)'s universal property), i.e. morphisms D → R whose Spa-image lies in p_B⁻¹(U) ∩ p_C⁻¹(V), i.e. morphisms O_D(p_B⁻¹(U) ∩ p_C⁻¹(V)) → R. Yoneda gives the isomorphism.

(3) The adic spectrum of a rational localisation is homeomorphic to the rational subset with rational subsets matched (Tau Ceti `spaLocalizationHomeomorph`, anchor Layer 3.1; Huber 1994 Lemma 1.5(ii)).
acceptance: For X = Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩), Y = Spa(ℚ_p⟨S⟩) over Spa ℚ_p, U = R(T/p) = {|T| ≤ |p|} ⊆ X and V = R(1/S) = {|S| = 1} ⊆ Y: p_X⁻¹(U) ∩ p_Y⁻¹(V) = {|T| ≤ |p|, |S| = 1} in the bidisc Spa(ℚ_p⟨T, S⟩), and ℚ_p⟨T/p⟩ ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} ℚ_p⟨S, S⁻¹⟩ ≅ ℚ_p⟨T, S⟩⟨T/p, 1/S⟩.

nodes.title: Valuations agreeing on a common subring extend jointly to the tensor product
nodes.statement: Let A → B and A → C be ring homomorphisms and let y ∈ Spv B, x ∈ Spv C be valuations whose pullbacks to A agree as points of Spv A (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.comap`). Then there is a valuation v on B ⊗_A C whose pullbacks along inl : B → B ⊗_A C and inr : C → B ⊗_A C are y and x. Field form: for field extensions K₁, K₂ of K₀ and valuation rings V_i ⊆ K_i with V₁ ∩ K₀ = V₂ ∩ K₀, there are a field L, K₀-embeddings K₁ → L, K₂ → L (L a residue field of K₁ ⊗_{K₀} K₂) and a valuation ring W ⊆ L with W ∩ K₁ = V₁ and W ∩ K₂ = V₂.
hypotheses: A → B, A → C commutative ring homomorphisms.
y, x valuations (points of Spv) with equal pullbacks to A.
proofSteps: Reduction to fields: equal pullbacks give equal supports 𝔯 = supp(y) ∩ A = supp(x) ∩ A; put K₁ = κ(supp y), K₂ = κ(supp x), K₀ = κ(𝔯), V₁, V₂ the valuation rings of y, x, V₀ = V₁ ∩ K₀ = V₂ ∩ K₀ (equal pullbacks).

Flatness: V₁ and V₂ are torsion-free over the valuation ring V₀, hence flat (Mathlib `Module.Flat.flat_iff_torsion_eq_bot_of_isBezout`; valuation rings are Bézout domains). Hence R := V₁ ⊗_{V₀} V₂ is flat over V₁ and over V₂, so nonzero elements of V₁ and V₂ are non-zero-divisors on R, and R embeds in K₁ ⊗_{K₀} K₂.

A prime over both maximal ideals: R/(𝔪₁R + 𝔪₂R) ≅ k₁ ⊗_{k₀} k₂ ≠ 0 (a tensor product of nonzero vector spaces over the field k₀), so some prime P of R contains 𝔪₁R + 𝔪₂R (Mathlib `Ideal.exists_le_maximal`).

A minimal prime Q ⊆ P (Mathlib `Ideal.exists_minimalPrimes_le`) consists of zero-divisors (Mathlib `Ideal.disjoint_nonZeroDivisors_of_mem_minimalPrimes`), so Q ∩ V₁ = 0 = Q ∩ V₂ and L := Frac(R/Q) contains K₁ and K₂ over K₀.

The local ring (R/Q)_{P/Q} is a local subring of L, dominated by a valuation subring W of L (Mathlib `LocalSubring.exists_le_valuationSubring`, Stacks 00IA). W ∩ K₁ is a valuation ring dominating V₁ (𝔪₁ ⊆ P), hence equal to V₁ (valuation rings are maximal for domination, Mathlib `ValuationSubring.isMax_toLocalSubring`); likewise W ∩ K₂ = V₂.
Ring form: v is the valuation of W composed with B ⊗_A C → K₁ ⊗_{K₀} K₂ → L.
acceptance: For K₀ = ℚ_p, K₁ = K₂ = ℚ_p(√p) with their p-adic valuations, L can be taken to be K₁ itself (either factor of K₁ ⊗ K₂ ≅ K₁ × K₁), and there are two different choices, which is the non-injectivity of R0/fibre-product-points.
Wedhorn Proposition 8.63 uses the same existence statement for a scheme and an adic space.

nodes.title: Spa of a sheafy completed tensor product is the fibre product
nodes.statement: Let f : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) and g : (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) be morphisms of complete Hausdorff Huber pairs with adic ring homomorphisms, such that Spa A, Spa B, Spa C are adic spaces (their pairs are sheafy), and let D = B ⊗̂_A C (R0/completed-tensor-product). If D is sheafy (the anchor's `Huber.IsSheafyPair`), then Spa D with the morphisms Spa(inl) : Spa D → Spa B and Spa(inr) : Spa D → Spa C is a fibre product of Spa B → Spa A ← Spa C in the category of adic spaces: for every adic space X and morphisms a : X → Spa B, b : X → Spa C with Spa(f) ∘ a = Spa(g) ∘ b there is a unique morphism X → Spa D composing to a and b. Sheafiness of D is a hypothesis, not a conclusion: it is supplied by R0/completed-tensor-noetherian-stability in the noetherian case and by other stages in other cases (perfectoid: PerfectoidSpaces:P2; sousperfectoid: AdicSpacesPartII:R5).
hypotheses: f, g morphisms of complete Hausdorff Huber pairs with adic ring homomorphisms.
(A, A⁺), (B, B⁺), (C, C⁺) sheafy.
D = B ⊗̂_A C sheafy.
proofSteps: Morphisms into an affinoid: for an adic space X and a complete Hausdorff sheafy pair (R, R⁺), morphisms X → Spa R correspond bijectively and naturally to morphisms of pairs (R, R⁺) → (O_X(X), O_X⁺(X)) (Huber 1994 Proposition 2.1(ii), Wedhorn Proposition 8.25; imported from the anchor's Layer 5).

(O_X(X), O_X⁺(X)) is a complete Hausdorff nonarchimedean topological ring with a closed integrally closed subring (the sheaf condition in complete topological rings, anchor Layer 3.2–3.4; O_X⁺ is defined by v_x ≤ 1).

Compatible pairs (a, b) correspond to morphisms φ : B → O_X(X), ψ : C → O_X(X) of pairs with φ ∘ f = ψ ∘ g; R0/completed-tensor-product-universal-property gives a unique χ : D → O_X(X) with χ ∘ inl = φ, χ ∘ inr = ψ; translate back by the first step (naturality gives the compositions).
acceptance: Spa(K⟨T⟩) ×_{Spa K} Spa(K⟨S⟩) = Spa(K⟨T, S⟩) (Hübner Example 9.3).

Spa(ℤ_p⟨T⟩) ×_{Spa ℤ_p} Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) = Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟨T⟩), the closed unit disc over ℚ_p (Hübner Example 9.4), and Spa(ℤ_p⟨T⟩) ×_{Spa ℤ_p} Spa(𝔽_p) = Spa(𝔽_p[T]) with the discrete topology (Hübner Example 9.5).
Spa(L, O_L) ×_{Spa ℚ_p} Spa(L, O_L) = Spa(L × L, O_L × O_L) for L = ℚ_p(√p).

nodes.title: Fibre products along a finite-type morphism over an arbitrary affinoid base change
nodes.statement: Let S = Spa(A, A⁺), X = Spa(C, C⁺), Y = Spa(B, B⁺) be affinoid adic spaces with complete Hausdorff pairs, B stably sheafy, f : X → S given by a morphism μ : (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) topologically of finite type (presented by a quotient mapping σ : A⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩_M → (C, C⁺) with kernel 𝔞), and g : Y → S given by an arbitrary morphism of pairs λ : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) (not assumed adic). Let L ⊆ B be a finite set generating an ideal of definition of a ring of definition of B. For m ≥ 1 put M_{L,m} := (λ(M₁) ∪ Lᵐ, …, λ(M_n) ∪ Lᵐ) (each λ(M_i) ∪ Lᵐ generates an open ideal of B), and W_m := Spa(B⟨X⟩_{M_{L,m}}/J_m) with J_m the closure of the ideal generated by λ'(𝔞) and the integral-closure plus ring. Then: (1) each W_m is an affinoid adic space topologically of finite type over Y; (2) for m ≤ m' the restriction B⟨X⟩_{M_{L,m'}}/J_{m'} → B⟨X⟩_{M_{L,m}}/J_m identifies W_m with the rational subset {w ∈ W_{m'} : w(ℓ·X_i) ≤ 1 for all ℓ ∈ Lᵐ and all i} of W_{m'}; (3) the adic space W := ⋃_m W_m obtained by gluing along these open embeddings, with its maps to X and Y, is a fibre product X ×_S Y in the category of adic spaces; (4) if λ is adic then W = W_∞ := Spa(B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)}/J) = Spa(C ⊗̂_A B) is affinoid; in general W is not quasi-compact.
hypotheses: S, X, Y affinoid with complete Hausdorff pairs; B stably sheafy (anchor `Huber.IsStablySheafyRing`).
μ topologically of finite type as a morphism of pairs (anchor Layer 5.2), presented by σ.
λ an arbitrary morphism of Huber pairs; L generates an ideal of definition of a ring of definition of B.
proofSteps: Openness: Lᵐ·B contains a power of an ideal of definition, so each λ(M_i) ∪ Lᵐ generates an open ideal and B⟨X⟩_{M_{L,m}} is defined (with Tau Ceti's weight-family hypothesis via anchor Layer 0.4, as in R0/completed-tensor-restricted-power-series (a)).

(1) B → B⟨X⟩_{M_{L,m}}/J_m is a quotient-mapping presentation, so it is topologically of finite type and its ring is sheafy because B is stably sheafy (anchor Layer 3.4 definition of `IsStablySheafyRing`).

(2) The pair-level universal property of weighted restricted series (Huber 1994 Lemma 3.5(i), anchor Layer 5.2) gives the restriction maps; they present the target as the rational localisation of the source at {ℓX_i ≤ 1 : ℓ ∈ Lᵐ} (both represent the same functor; Tau Ceti `existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset`), so W_m is a rational, hence open affinoid, subspace of W_{m'} (Huber 1994 proof of Proposition 3.8, the same argument with E(k)).

(3) Gluing the W_m along these open embeddings (anchor Layer 5.3) gives W with compatible maps to X (through C → B⟨X⟩_{M_{L,m}}/J_m) and to Y. Universal property: for an affinoid test object V = Spa(R, R⁺) with morphisms to X and Y over S, the images r_i ∈ R of X_i satisfy μ(m)·r_i ∈ R⁺, and for each ℓ ∈ L the image of ℓ is topologically nilpotent, so ℓᵐ·r_i ∈ R⁺ for m large (R⁺ is open and ℓᵐ r_i → 0); hence the pair of maps factors uniquely through W_m for m large (Lemma 3.5(i) and the quotient universal property, Tau Ceti `Pair.Hom.quotientLift`), compatibly in m. For general V, glue over an affinoid cover (morphisms of adic spaces form a sheaf, anchor Layer 5).

(4) If λ is adic, λ(M_i)·B is already open (R0/completed-tensor-restricted-power-series (a)), the weights Lᵐ are redundant for m large, and W = Spa(B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)}/J) ≅ Spa(C ⊗̂_A B) (R0/completed-tensor-restricted-power-series (c)).
Non-quasi-compactness: in the example of the acceptance list W is the open unit disc, which is an increasing union of closed discs with no finite subcover.
acceptance: S = Spa(ℤ_p, ℤ_p), X = Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) = Spa(ℤ_p⟨X⟩_{p}/(pX − 1)), Y = Spa(ℤ_p⟦T⟧, ℤ_p⟦T⟧) with the (p, T)-adic topology, L = {p, T}: W_m = {|T|ᵐ ≤ |p| ≠ 0} and X ×_S Y = ⋃_m W_m is the open unit disc over ℚ_p, which is not affinoid (Hübner Example 9.4; Scholze–Weinstein, Berkeley lectures, the open unit disc example).
If Y = Spa(ℤ_p⟨T⟩) (λ adic) then X ×_S Y = Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩) is affinoid.

nodes.title: Existence of fibre products of adic spaces
nodes.statement: Let f : X → S and g : Y → S be morphisms of adic spaces (the anchor's category, Layer 5). Assume that Y is covered by open affinoids Spa(B, B⁺) with B complete and stably sheafy (anchor `Huber.IsStablySheafyRing`) — for instance Y locally noetherian (R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space, by R0/noetherian-type-stably-sheafy) — and that one of the following holds: (a) f is locally of finite type (anchor Layer 5.2, which is Huber's notion); (b) f is locally of weakly finite type (R0/finite-type-morphism-classes) and g is adic (R0/adic-morphism). Then the fibre product X ×_S Y exists in the category of adic spaces (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Limits.HasPullback f g` for that category). Its projections p : X ×_S Y → X and q : X ×_S Y → Y satisfy: q is locally of finite type in case (a), and locally of weakly finite type (locally of finite type if f is) in case (b); p is adic whenever g is adic. X ×_S Y is covered by stably sheafy affinoids, and is locally noetherian if Y is. Local form: over affinoid S = Spa A, X = Spa C, Y = Spa B with g adic, X ×_S Y = Spa(C ⊗̂_A B) (R0/affinoid-fibre-product); with g not adic, X ×_S Y is the ascending union of affinoids of R0/fibre-product-along-finite-type and need not be affinoid. Nothing is asserted outside these hypotheses: fibre products of adic spaces do not exist in general.
hypotheses: f : X → S, g : Y → S morphisms of adic spaces.
Y covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings (e.g. Y locally noetherian).
(a) f locally of finite type, or (b) f locally of weakly finite type and g adic.
proofSteps: Gluing reduction (Wedhorn proof of Theorem 8.56(i)): if S = ⋃ S_i, f⁻¹(S_i) = ⋃ X_ij, g⁻¹(S_i) = ⋃ Y_ik are open covers such that all X_ij ×_{S_i} Y_ik exist, then X ×_S Y exists: open subspaces of a fibre product are fibre products of the corresponding opens, and adic spaces and their morphisms glue (anchor Layer 5.3; morphisms of adic spaces form a sheaf). Rational subsets of stably sheafy affinoids are stably sheafy (they are topologically of finite type over them, Huber 1994 Corollary 3.4(i) and composition of tft maps, Wedhorn Proposition 6.33(1)), so the affinoid Y_ik can be chosen stably sheafy and inside a given affinoid.

Case (b), affinoid: choose affinoid X_ij = Spa C, S_i = Spa A with A → C topologically of finite type (definition of lwft), hence adic (R0/topologically-finite-type-is-adic); A → B is adic because g is adic (R0/adic-iff-analytic-locus (i)). B → C ⊗̂_A B is topologically of finite type as a ring homomorphism (R0/completed-tensor-restricted-power-series (d): A → C is only ring-level topologically of finite type here), so C ⊗̂_A B is sheafy (stable sheafiness of B), and R0/affinoid-fibre-product gives X_ij ×_{S_i} Y_ik = Spa(C ⊗̂_A B).
Case (a), affinoid: R0/fibre-product-along-finite-type (no adicness of g needed).

Projections: locally q is B → B⟨X⟩_{M'}/𝔟, topologically of finite type (as pairs in case (a), and as pairs in case (b) when f is lft, as rings otherwise); p is locally C → C ⊗̂_A B = inl, which is adic (R0/completed-tensor-product) when g is adic.

Stability: the affinoid pieces are topologically of finite type over stably sheafy B, hence stably sheafy (composition of tft maps); if B is of noetherian type they are of noetherian type (R0/topologically-finite-type-noetherian-type).
acceptance: For S analytic every morphism is adic (R0/adic-iff-analytic-locus; Huber 1996 §1.2, printed p. 46: 'In particular, if Y is analytic then every morphism f: X → Y is adic'), so fibre products over an analytic base exist as soon as f is locally of weakly finite type and Y is locally noetherian.
Huber 1994 Proposition 3.7 is the special case (a) with g adic.
Spa(ℤ_p⟦T⟧) ×_{Spa ℤ_p} Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) exists and is the (non-affinoid) open unit disc over ℚ_p.
Non-example outside the hypotheses: Spa(ℤ[T₁, T₂, …], ℤ) × Spa K is not representable (Scholze–Weinstein, Berkeley Lecture 4, §4.1, p. 28); there f is not locally of finite type.

nodes.title: Points of a fibre product surject onto compatible pairs, not injectively
nodes.statement: In the situation of R0/fibre-products-existence with g adic (case (b), f locally of weakly finite type; this includes case (a) when g is adic), let Z = X ×_S Y with projections p : Z → X, q : Z → Y. For all x ∈ X and y ∈ Y with f(x) = g(y) there is z ∈ Z with p(z) = x and q(z) = y; that is, the map |Z| → |X| ×_{|S|} |Y| of underlying sets is surjective (Huber 1996 Corollary 1.2.3(iii)(d); Huber 1994 Lemma 3.9(i)). It is not injective in general: for L = ℚ_p(√p), X = Y = Spa(L, O_L) and S = Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p), |X|, |Y|, |S| are single points and |Z| = |Spa(L × L, O_L × O_L)| has two points; and over the pair of Gauss points of two closed unit discs over ℚ_p there are infinitely many points of the bidisc (the Gauss point and, for every 0 < r < 1, the point f ↦ sup{|f(T, S)| : |T| ≤ 1, |T − S| ≤ r}). Without adicness of g surjectivity fails, even in case (a): take S = Spa(ℤ_p, ℤ_p) with ℤ_p discrete, X = Spa(ℤ_p[T], ℤ_p[T]) discrete (f locally of finite type) and Y = Spa(ℤ_p⟦U⟧, ℤ_p⟦U⟧) with the U-adic topology (g not adic), so that X ×_S Y = Spa(ℤ_p⟦U⟧⟨T⟩) with the U-adic topology; the rank-2 valuation x of ℤ_p[T] with |p| < 1 and 0 < |T| < |p|ⁿ for all n and the Gauss point y of radius |p|^{1/2} of ℤ_p⟦U⟧ both restrict to the p-adic valuation of ℤ_p, but a valuation z over both has |U|ⁿ = |p|^{n/2} > |T| ≠ 0 for all n, so |U| is not cofinal and z is not continuous: no point of X ×_S Y lies over (x, y).
hypotheses: The hypotheses of R0/fibre-products-existence with g adic (f locally of weakly finite type).
proofSteps: Reduce to affinoid S = Spa A, X = Spa C, Y = Spa B (points lie in affinoid opens; open subspaces of fibre products are fibre products).

Case g adic (Z = Spa D, D = C ⊗̂_A B): regard x, y as continuous valuations of C, B with equal pullbacks to A. R0/valuation-amalgamation gives a valuation v of E = C ⊗_A B over x and y. Let H be the larger of the convex hulls of Γ_x and Γ_y in Γ_v; H contains the characteristic subgroup cΓ_v (every v(e) is bounded by products of values of x and y), so w := v|H is a valuation (restriction to a convex subgroup containing cΓ_v, Huber 1993 §2, anchor Layer 1.4) still over x and y.

w ∈ Spa(E, E⁺): w ≤ 1 on the image of C⁺ ⊗ B⁺ and hence on its integral closure E⁺; w is continuous because for the ideal of definition I·F the values w(I) are cofinal (x(I), y(I) are cofinal in Γ_x, Γ_y and w(i) < 1 on I) (Wedhorn Theorem 7.10 = anchor Layer 1.5 criterion for Cont); Spa(E, E⁺) = Spa(D, D⁺) (anchor Layer 0.3 / Wedhorn 7.48).

Failure without adicness (the counterexample of the statement): any valuation z of ℤ_p⟦U⟧[T] restricting to x and y has z(T) = x(T) ≠ 0, z(p) = |p| and z(U)² = z(p); since x(T) < |p|ⁿ for all n, z(Uⁿ) > z(T) for all n, so {a : z(a) < z(T)} contains no Uᴺ·ℤ_p⟦U⟧⟨T⟩ and z is not continuous (Wedhorn Theorem 7.10). In the adic case this cannot happen because x(I) and y(I) are both cofinal for the same ideal of definition I of A (step 3).

Non-injectivity: L ⊗_{ℚ_p} L ≅ L × L (as √p ∈ L), the completed tensor product needs no completion, and Spa(L × L, O_L × O_L) is the disjoint union of two copies of Spa(L, O_L) (R0/affinoid-fibre-product); the bidisc points are sup-norms over the polydiscs {|T| ≤ 1, |T − S| ≤ r}, which differ for different r and project to the Gauss points.
acceptance: Huber 1996 Corollary 1.2.3(iii)(d), printed p. 49 (f locally of weakly finite type, g adic).
Test: the counterexample in the statement (S = Spa ℤ_p discrete, X = Spa ℤ_p[T] discrete, Y = Spa ℤ_p⟦U⟧) — a version of the lemma claiming surjectivity whenever the fibre product exists fails it.

The étale-site coverings of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1 and AdicSpacesPartII:R4 are jointly surjective families; their base changes along adic morphisms are again jointly surjective by this lemma (base change along non-adic morphisms needs a separate argument, e.g. that residue value groups of étale maps are torsion over the base).

nodes.title: Stability of adicness and of the finite-type classes under base change
nodes.statement: Let the cartesian square Z = X ×_S Y (p : Z → X, q : Z → Y) be as in R0/fibre-products-existence, q being the base change of f along g and p the base change of g along f. Then: (i) if f is locally of finite type (anchor), so is q; (ii) if f is locally of weakly finite type and g is adic, q is locally of weakly finite type and p is adic; (iii) if f is locally of +weakly finite type (R0/plus-weakly-finite-type) and g is adic, q is locally of +weakly finite type; (iv) if f is locally of finite presentation (R0/locally-finite-presentation), then q is locally of finite type by (i), and q is locally of finite presentation provided that Y is analytic, or that every point of X has a chart of f — open affinoids U ⊆ X, W ⊆ S with f(U) ⊆ W and (O_S(W), O_S⁺(W)) → (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) topologically of finite type — with a presentation O_X(U) ≅ O_S(W)⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩_M/𝔞 whose kernel 𝔞 is a finitely generated ideal (automatic when O_S(W)⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩_M is a noetherian ring, or when O_S(W) is discrete, in particular when every point of S has an open affinoid neighbourhood with discrete ring of functions); without such a hypothesis local finite presentation is not stable under base change (see acceptance; Huber 1996 Corollary 1.2.3(i) asserts this stability without qualification, which is correct under the book's standing hypothesis (1.1.1) (p. 37: every f-adic ring has a completion finitely generated over a noetherian ring of definition, or is a strongly noetherian Tate ring, or is discrete; then O_S(W)⟨X⟩_M is noetherian or O_S(W) is discrete, so 𝔞 is finitely generated), but not in the generality of this node); (v) if g is adic, p is adic (R0/adic-morphism); (vi) if g is adic and f is quasi-compact (resp. quasi-separated), q is quasi-compact (resp. quasi-separated); if g is adic and quasi-compact (resp. quasi-separated), p is quasi-compact (resp. quasi-separated). Quasi-compactness is not preserved by base change along a non-adic g: the base change of the quasi-compact morphism Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) → Spa(ℤ_p, ℤ_p) along Spa(ℤ_p⟦T⟧) → Spa(ℤ_p) is the open unit disc over ℚ_p → Spa(ℤ_p⟦T⟧), which is not quasi-compact. The base-change properties of separated, proper, finite, étale and smooth morphisms are stated with those notions (R0b/R0c nodes) and are not part of this lemma.
hypotheses: The hypotheses of R0/fibre-products-existence for f and g.
proofSteps: All assertions are affinoid-local on Z (the classes are defined affinoid-locally and open subspaces of fibre products are fibre products); compute with the local forms.

(i), (ii): locally q is B → B⟨X⟩_{M'}/𝔟 (R0/completed-tensor-restricted-power-series, R0/fibre-product-along-finite-type), topologically of finite type as pairs, resp. as rings; p is locally inl : C → C ⊗̂_A B, adic when g is (R0/completed-tensor-product), i.e. (v).

(iii): if C⁺ is the integral closure of A⁺[E ∪ C°°] (E finite), then the plus ring of C ⊗̂_A B is the closure of the integral closure of the image of C⁺ ⊗ B⁺, which lies in the integral closure of B⁺[inl(E) ∪ D°°] because inl(C°°) consists of topologically nilpotent elements; so q is +wft with the finite set inl(E) (R0/plus-weakly-finite-type).

(iv): let z ∈ Z lie over x ∈ X; take a chart (U, W) of f at x with O_X(U) = O_S(W)⟨X⟩_M/𝔞, 𝔞 finitely generated, and an open affinoid V ∋ q(z) with g(V) ⊆ W, B := O_Y(V). If B is not discrete, lfp at z is lft at z, i.e. (i). If B is discrete, the finite set L of R0/fibre-product-along-finite-type may be taken empty, so the affinoid pieces of U ×_W V over V are Spa(B[X]/𝔞B[X]) (closure is trivial in a discrete ring), and B[X]/𝔞B[X] is a finitely presented B-algebra (Mathlib `Algebra.FinitePresentation.quotient`). When O_S(W) is discrete, lfp of f says O_X(U) = O_S(W)[X]/𝔞 is a finitely presented O_S(W)-algebra, so 𝔞 is finitely generated (Mathlib `Algebra.FinitePresentation.ker_fG_of_surjective`; equivalently `Algebra.FinitePresentation.baseChange`). In a space in which every point has an affinoid neighbourhood with discrete ring, every open affinoid W has discrete O_S(W) (it is quasi-compact, so O_S(W) embeds topologically into a finite product of discrete rings of rational subsets). If Y is analytic, lfp = lft for q (R0/locally-finite-presentation). Over a non-discrete O_S(W) the definition of lfp imposes no condition on 𝔞, while after base change to a discrete O_Y(V) it demands finite presentation; the acceptance example shows the hypothesis cannot be dropped.

(vi): with g adic the fibre product over affinoids is affinoid (R0/affinoid-fibre-product). For q: if W ⊆ Y is quasi-compact open, cover W by finitely many affinoids W_j with g(W_j) inside affinoids S_j; f⁻¹(S_j) is quasi-compact, covered by finitely many affinoids X_{jk}, and the affinoids X_{jk} ×_{S_j} W_j cover q⁻¹(W). For p (g quasi-compact) exchange the roles of f and g. Quasi-separatedness likewise from intersections of affinoids (Wedhorn Remark 8.57(2); Huber 1996 Corollary 1.2.3(iii)(b),(c)). The counterexample for non-adic g is R0/fibre-product-along-finite-type's open disc.
acceptance: The base change of the closed unit disc Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩) → Spa ℚ_p along Spa ℂ_p → Spa ℚ_p is the closed unit disc over ℂ_p, locally of finite type over Spa ℂ_p.
Non-example: quasi-compactness fails for the open-disc base change above.

Non-example for (iv) without its extra hypothesis (this A lies outside Huber 1996's standing hypothesis (1.1.1), since A = Â is not finitely generated over its noetherian ring of definition ℤ_p ⊕ 0; so it does not contradict Huber's Corollary 1.2.3(i), which is stated under (1.1.1)): let M = ⊕_{i∈ℕ} 𝔽_p·e_i and A = ℤ_p ⊕ M with M² = 0 (ℤ_p acting on M through 𝔽_p), topologised so that pⁿℤ_p ⊕ 0 (n ≥ 0) is a fundamental system of neighbourhoods of 0; then ℤ_p ⊕ 0 is a noetherian ring of definition, so Spa(A, A) is an adic space (Huber 1994 Theorem 2.2). f : Spa(ℤ_p, ℤ_p) → Spa(A, A), induced by the quotient mapping (a, m) ↦ a, is locally of finite presentation because A is not discrete. g : Spa(A/pA, A/pA) → Spa(A, A) with A/pA = 𝔽_p ⊕ M discrete is adic (pA ↦ 0, an ideal of definition of a discrete ring). The fibre product is Spa(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p) and q is induced by 𝔽_p ⊕ M → 𝔽_p, whose kernel M is not finitely generated; Spa(𝔽_p ⊕ M, 𝔽_p ⊕ M) is a single point whose only open affinoid neighbourhood has the discrete ring 𝔽_p ⊕ M, so q is not locally of finite presentation.

nodes.title: Adic morphisms of adic spaces
nodes.statement: A morphism f : X → Y of adic spaces (the anchor's category, Layer 5) is *adic* if every x ∈ X has an open affinoid neighbourhood U and there is an open affinoid V ⊆ Y with f(U) ⊆ V such that the ring homomorphism O_Y(V) → O_X(U) induced by f is adic (R0/adic-ring-homomorphism). Equivalently (R0/adic-iff-analytic-locus) f maps analytic points to analytic points, and then the ring maps O_Y(V) → O_X(U) are adic for all open affinoids with f(U) ⊆ V. Here a point is analytic if it has an open neighbourhood U whose ring O_X(U) contains a topologically nilpotent unit; on Spa(A, A⁺) this means that its support is not open (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.IsAnalyticPoint`). Every morphism into an analytic adic space is adic. Lean name: `AdicSpace.IsAdic f` (a `MorphismProperty` of the anchor's category).
hypotheses: f : X → Y a morphism of adic spaces.
proofSteps: Definition by an affinoid-local condition; independence of the chosen affinoids and the analytic-locus characterisation are R0/adic-iff-analytic-locus.
acceptance: Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩) → Spa(ℚ_p) is adic; Spa(ℤ_p⟦T⟧) → Spa(ℤ_p) is not.

nodes.title: A morphism is adic exactly when it preserves analytic points
nodes.statement: Let f : X → Y be a morphism of adic spaces. (i) If f is adic, then for all open affinoid U ⊆ X and V ⊆ Y with f(U) ⊆ V the ring homomorphism O_Y(V) → O_X(U) is adic. (ii) f is adic iff f(X_a) ⊆ Y_a. (iii) f(X_na) ⊆ Y_na. In particular every morphism to an analytic adic space is adic.
hypotheses: f : X → Y a morphism of adic spaces.
proofSteps: Analytic points are local: for an open subspace U, U_a = X_a ∩ U (Wedhorn Remark 8.37(2)), and on Spa(A, A⁺) a point is analytic iff its support is not open (Huber 1994 Remark 3.1; Tau Ceti `IsAnalyticPoint`; anchor Layer 2.3).

Affinoid statement (R0/spa-comap-analytic-locus = Wedhorn Lemma 7.46(1),(2)): for a continuous φ : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) with B complete and g = Spa(φ): g(X_na) ⊆ Y_na; φ adic ⇒ g(X_a) ⊆ Y_a; g(X_a) ⊆ Y_a ⇒ φ adic (the last via Wedhorn Lemma 7.45, requested from the anchor's Layer 2.3).

(ii) ⇒: cover X by affinoids U with adic O_Y(V) → O_X(U) and apply the affinoid statement; ⇐ and (i): for any affinoids U, V with f(U) ⊆ V, f(U_a) ⊆ V_a, so O_Y(V) → O_X(U) is adic by the affinoid statement.
(iii) from the affinoid statement; the analytic-target case is (ii) with Y_a = Y.
acceptance: For Spa(ℤ_p⟦T⟧) → Spa(ℤ_p) the analytic point with support (p) maps to a non-analytic point, so the morphism is not adic.
Every morphism of analytic adic spaces is adic.

nodes.title: Morphisms locally of weakly finite type and the finite-type hierarchy
nodes.statement: A morphism f : X → Y of adic spaces is *locally of weakly finite type* if every x ∈ X has an open affinoid neighbourhood U and there is an open affinoid V ⊆ Y with f(U) ⊆ V such that the ring homomorphism O_Y(V) → O_X(U) is topologically of finite type (Tau Ceti `IsTopologicallyFiniteType`, which is Huber 1994's and Wedhorn 6.29(i)'s notion; no condition on the plus rings); f is *of weakly finite type* if moreover f is quasi-compact. Hierarchy (Huber 1996 after 1.2.1): locally of finite presentation (R0/locally-finite-presentation) ⇒ locally of finite type ⇒ locally of +weakly finite type (R0/plus-weakly-finite-type) ⇒ locally of weakly finite type ⇒ adic (R0/adic-morphism). Here 'locally of finite type' is the anchor's Layer 5.2 notion — the ring map (O_Y(V), O_Y⁺(V)) → (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) is topologically of finite type as a map of pairs, i.e. presented by a quotient mapping out of a weighted restricted power-series pair A⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩_M — which is exactly Huber 1994's Definition following Lemma 3.5; this node does not redefine it. Comparison with Tau Ceti: the ring-level condition is Tau Ceti's `IsTopologicallyFiniteType`, whose weight families satisfy `IsWeightFamily`, equivalent for Huber rings to Huber's 'M_i·A open' by Huber 1994 Lemma 1.1 = Wedhorn Lemma 6.20 (the anchor's Layer 0.4 equivalence), and whose completeness hypothesis on the target is automatic here since O_X(U) is complete. Lean names: `AdicSpace.LocallyOfWeaklyFiniteType f`, `AdicSpace.IsWeaklyFiniteType f`.
hypotheses: f : X → Y a morphism of adic spaces.
proofSteps: Definition affinoid-locally; the hierarchy: lft ⇒ l+wft is R0/plus-weakly-finite-type's relation, l+wft ⇒ lwft by definition, lwft ⇒ adic by R0/topologically-finite-type-is-adic, lfp ⇒ lft by definition.

Composition and cancellation from Wedhorn Proposition 6.33 (tft maps compose; if ψ ∘ φ is tft then ψ is), restriction to open subspaces from Wedhorn Proposition 8.50 (rational localisations are tft, Huber 1994 Corollary 3.4(i)).
acceptance: Every open immersion is locally of finite type; the closed unit disc over ℚ_p is of finite type over Spa ℚ_p.
An affinoid morphism of weakly finite type need not have a topologically-finite-type global ring map (Wedhorn Remark 8.52).

nodes.title: Morphisms locally of +weakly finite type
nodes.statement: A morphism f : X → Y of adic spaces is *locally of +weakly finite type* if every x ∈ X has an open affinoid neighbourhood U and there is an open affinoid V ⊆ Y with f(U) ⊆ V such that O_Y(V) → O_X(U) is topologically of finite type (Tau Ceti `IsTopologicallyFiniteType`) and there is a finite set E ⊆ O_X(U) (necessarily contained in O_X⁺(U)) such that O_X⁺(U) is the smallest ring of integral elements of O_X(U) containing E and the image of O_Y⁺(V), i.e. the integral closure in O_X(U) of the subring generated by the image of O_Y⁺(V), E and the topologically nilpotent elements O_X(U)°° (Huber 1996 Definition 1.2.1(ii)). It is *of +weakly finite type* if moreover quasi-compact. This is the finiteness condition in Huber's definitions of proper morphisms (proper = of +weakly finite type, separated, universally closed; Huber 1996 Definition 1.3.2(ii)) and of partially proper morphisms (locally of +weakly finite type, separated, universally specializing; Definition 1.3.3(ii)). Lean names: `AdicSpace.LocallyOfPlusWeaklyFiniteType f`, `AdicSpace.IsPlusWeaklyFiniteType f`.
hypotheses: f : X → Y a morphism of adic spaces.
proofSteps: Definition affinoid-locally. lft ⇒ l+wft: for a quotient mapping π : A⟨X⟩_M → (C, C⁺), every element of the plus ring of A⟨X⟩_M is a polynomial in the m·X_i (m ∈ M_i) with coefficients in Â⁺ plus a topologically nilpotent tail, so C⁺ is integral over A⁺[π(m X_i) ; m ∈ M_i] ∪ C°°, and E = {π(m X_i)} works.
acceptance: Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟨T⟩) → Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) is of +weakly finite type (E = {T}).

nodes.title: Morphisms locally of finite presentation
nodes.statement: A morphism f : X → Y of adic spaces is *locally of finite presentation* if every x ∈ X has an open affinoid neighbourhood U and there is an open affinoid V ⊆ Y with f(U) ⊆ V such that (O_Y(V), O_Y⁺(V)) → (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) is topologically of finite type as a morphism of pairs (anchor Layer 5.2) and, whenever O_Y(V) carries the discrete topology, O_X(U) is a finitely presented O_Y(V)-algebra (Mathlib `RingHom.FinitePresentation`). This is Huber 1996 Definition 1.2.1(v) verbatim; the discrete case is the only one in which the condition adds anything. Consequences: over an analytic Y, locally of finite presentation = locally of finite type; over Y whose discrete affinoid rings are noetherian rings (for instance t(𝔜) for a locally noetherian formal scheme 𝔜) the two notions agree as well; they differ over discrete non-noetherian affinoids. Warning: unlike local finite type, local finite presentation is not stable under arbitrary base change (a non-discrete base chart imposes nothing, a discrete chart after base change does); R0/base-change-stability (iv) gives the correct hypotheses. (Huber 1996 Corollary 1.2.3(i) states unconditional stability under the book's standing hypothesis (1.1.1), which excludes such examples.) Lean name: `AdicSpace.LocallyOfFinitePresentation f`.
hypotheses: f : X → Y a morphism of adic spaces.
proofSteps: Definition affinoid-locally; agreement with lft: an analytic affinoid has no discrete ring of functions unless empty (a point of Spa of a discrete ring has open support), and over a discrete noetherian ring finite type equals finite presentation (Mathlib `Algebra.FinitePresentation.of_finiteType`).
acceptance: Spa(K⟨T⟩/(f)) → Spa K is locally of finite presentation for every f.

nodes.title: Locally noetherian adic spaces (Huber's noetherian hypothesis)
nodes.statement: An adic space X (the anchor's category, Layer 5) is *locally noetherian* if every x ∈ X has an open affinoid neighbourhood U whose complete Hausdorff ring O_X(U) is of noetherian type (R0/noetherian-type-huber-ring): it has a noetherian ring of definition, or it is a strongly noetherian Tate ring. This is the hypothesis of Huber 1994 Propositions 3.6–3.8 ('every point has an open affinoid neighbourhood U such that O(U) has a noetherian ring of definition or is a strongly noetherian Tate ring'). The condition places no restriction on plus rings. Conventions: a locally noetherian analytic adic space is one locally of the form Spa(A, A⁺) with A a complete strongly noetherian Tate ring (the setting of Zavyalov's foundational results); because every discrete ring is of noetherian type, every discretely ringed adic space is locally noetherian in this sense, and results that need honest noetherian rings (for instance on coherent sheaves) must add that hypothesis. Lean name: `AdicSpace.IsLocallyNoetherian X` (a class).
hypotheses: X an adic space.
proofSteps: Definition by the local condition on affinoid neighbourhoods; stability properties from R0/topologically-finite-type-noetherian-type (rational localisations and quotients are topologically of finite type).
acceptance: Closed discs and polydiscs over ℚ_p, Spa(ℤ_p⟦T⟧), and all rigid-analytic varieties over a complete nonarchimedean field (viewed as adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(k, k°)) are locally noetherian.

tests.name: not_isLocallyNoetherian_test_perfectoid
tests.statement: For a perfectoid field K with pseudouniformiser ϖ = (ϖ^♭)^♯, X = Spa(K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) (sheafy, perfectoid) is not locally noetherian: let x₀ be the point f ↦ |f(0)|. For every open affinoid U ∋ x₀, the points y_c (T^{1/pⁿ} ↦ c^{1/pⁿ}, c = ((ϖ^♭)^m)^♯) lie in U for m ≫ 0, and in the Tate ring O_X(U) the ideals (T^{1/pⁿ}) form a strictly increasing chain: T^{1/p^{n+1}} = g·T^{1/pⁿ} would give |c|^{1/p^{n+1} − 1/pⁿ} ≤ sup_U |g| < ∞ for all such c. So O_X(U) is not noetherian, hence not of noetherian type, because a Tate ring of noetherian type is strongly noetherian, in particular noetherian. A definition 'X is covered by sheafy affinoids' would accept X.

nodes.title: Closed adic subspaces cut out by ideal sheaves; closed, open and locally closed embeddings
nodes.statement: Let X be an adic space (the anchor's category). (1) Affinoid model: for a complete Hausdorff sheafy Huber pair (A, A⁺) and a closed ideal J ⊆ A with A/J sheafy, the quotient pair A/J := (A/J, integral closure of the image of A⁺) (Tau Ceti `Pair.quotient`; Huber's (A^▷/J, (A⁺/(J ∩ A⁺))^c)) gives Spa(A/J) → Spa(A), a homeomorphism onto the closed set {v : J ⊆ supp v} (Tau Ceti `Pair.Hom.isClosedEmbedding_spaComap_quotientHom`, `range_spaComap_quotientHom`). (2) An ideal sheaf 𝓘 ⊆ O_X (a sheaf of ideals of the underlying sheaf of rings) is *admissible* if X has a cover by open affinoids U = Spa(A, A⁺) such that J_U := 𝓘(U) is a closed ideal of A, A/J_U is sheafy, and for every rational W ⊆ U the ideal 𝓘(W) is the kernel of O_X(W) → O_{Spa(A/J_U)}(W ∩ V(J_U)). The *closed adic subspace* V(𝓘) is (Z, O_Z, (v_z)) with Z = {x ∈ X : 𝓘_x ≠ O_{X,x}}, O_Z = (O_X/𝓘)|_Z topologised on each such U as the structure sheaf of Spa(A/J_U) (so O_X(U) → O_Z(U ∩ Z) is continuous and open), and v_z induced through O_{X,z} → O_{X,z}/𝓘_z; it is an adic space with V(𝓘) ∩ U ≅ Spa(A/J_U) over U, and the inclusion ι : V(𝓘) → X is a morphism of adic spaces. V(𝓘) is retained as an adic space (a ringed space with valuations), never replaced by the closed subset Z. (3) A morphism h : T → X is a *closed embedding* if it is isomorphic over X to ι : V(𝓘) → X for an admissible 𝓘; an *open embedding* if it is an isomorphism onto an open subspace; a *locally closed embedding* if it factors as a closed embedding into an open subspace U ⊆ X followed by the inclusion of U. Comparison with the anchor (Layer 5.1): closed embeddings are exactly the anchor's closed immersions (affinoid-locally Spa(A/J) → Spa(A) with J closed and A/J sheafy), with 𝓘 = ker(O_X → h_*O_T); this node adds the ideal-sheaf description, the universal property and locally closed embeddings, and does not redefine closed immersions. On a locally noetherian X every ideal of an affinoid ring of noetherian type is closed and A/J is of noetherian type, hence sheafy (R0/noetherian-type-ideals-closed, R0/noetherian-type-stably-sheafy); the identification of admissible ideals with coherent ideals is AdicSpacesPartII:R3/coherent-ideal-closed-subspace. Lean names: `AdicSpace.closedSubspace 𝓘`, `AdicSpace.IsLocallyClosedImmersion`.
hypotheses: X an adic space; 𝓘 an admissible ideal sheaf.
proofSteps: Affinoid model from Tau Ceti `Pair.quotient` and Proposition 7.38 in Tau Ceti (`Pair.Hom.isClosedEmbedding_spaComap_quotientHom`).

Gluing: on overlaps of two admissible affinoids U, U' the subspaces Spa(A/J_U) and Spa(A'/J_{U'}) agree on common rational subsets W, because both are the closed subspace of Spa O(W) defined by the closed ideal 𝓘(W) (admissibility and the quotient universal property, Tau Ceti `Pair.Hom.quotientLift`); glue (anchor Layer 5.3).
Valuations and local rings: O_{Z,z} = O_{X,z}/𝓘_z is local and v_z factors through it because 𝓘_z ⊆ supp(v_z) for z ∈ Z (points of Spa(A/J) have support containing J).

Comparison with the anchor's closed immersions: V(𝓘) → X is affinoid-locally Spa(A/J) → Spa A; conversely for an anchor closed immersion h, affinoid-locally Spa(A/J) → Spa(A) with J closed and A/J sheafy, the kernel ideal sheaf is admissible: for a rational W = R(T/s) ⊆ Spa A, W ∩ V(J) is the rational subset R(T̄/s̄) of Spa(A/J), its ring (A/J)⟨T̄/s̄⟩ ≅ (A/J) ⊗̂_A A⟨T/s⟩ ≅ A⟨T/s⟩/𝔟 with 𝔟 the closure of J·A⟨T/s⟩ (R0/completed-tensor-restricted-power-series (c) with n = 0, A → A⟨T/s⟩ being adic), so 𝓘(W) = 𝔟 — the closure of J·O(W), which equals J·O(W) only in the noetherian case; independence of the affinoid cover is the anchor's; h ≅ V(ker h♯) over X by the universal property below.
Universal property: a morphism g : T → X factors through ι iff g♯(𝓘)·O_T = 0, and then uniquely (affinoid-locally the quotient universal property; morphisms of adic spaces form a sheaf).
acceptance: V(T·O) ⊆ Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩) is the origin Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p); V(T²·O) has the same underlying point and ring ℚ_p[T]/(T²).

For an affinoid algebra A over k and any ideal J, A/J = (A/J, (A/J)°) (Huber 1996 (1.4.1) with BGR 6.3.4/1; the plus-ring identity is AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor via Huber 1994 Lemma 4.4).

nodes.title: The diagonal of a morphism locally of weakly finite type is a locally closed embedding
nodes.statement: Let f : X → Y be a morphism of adic spaces that is locally of weakly finite type, with X covered by open affinoids whose rings are complete and stably sheafy (for instance X locally noetherian). Then X ×_Y X exists (R0/fibre-products-existence, case (b), f being adic) and the diagonal Δ_f : X → X ×_Y X is a locally closed embedding (R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings): with W the union of the open subspaces U ×_V U ⊆ X ×_Y X over all open affinoids U ⊆ X, V ⊆ Y with f(U) ⊆ V and O_Y(V) → O_X(U) topologically of finite type, W is open, contains Δ_f(X), and Δ_f : X → W is a closed embedding; over U ×_V U = Spa(O_X(U) ⊗̂_{O_Y(V)} O_X(U)) it is Spa of the multiplication map m : O_X(U) ⊗̂_{O_Y(V)} O_X(U) → O_X(U), a quotient mapping with closed kernel. Separatedness (R0b: AdicSpacesPartII:R0/separated-morphism) is the condition that Δ_f be a closed embedding into all of X ×_Y X.
hypotheses: f locally of weakly finite type (hence adic).
X covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings.
proofSteps: Existence and affinoid charts: f is adic (R0/finite-type-morphism-classes), so X ×_Y X exists and, for U, V as in the statement with C = O_X(U), A = O_Y(V), U ×_V U = p₁⁻¹(U) ∩ p₂⁻¹(U) = Spa(C ⊗̂_A C) (R0/fibre-products-existence, R0/affinoid-fibre-product; C ⊗̂_A C is topologically of finite type over the stably sheafy C, hence sheafy, R0/completed-tensor-restricted-power-series); these are open in X ×_Y X, so W is open.
Δ_f⁻¹(U ×_V U) = U because p₁ ∘ Δ_f = p₂ ∘ Δ_f = id_X; and Δ_f(x) ∈ U ×_V U for x ∈ U, so Δ_f(X) ⊆ W.

On U ×_V U, Δ_f corresponds to m : C ⊗̂_A C → C with m ∘ inl = m ∘ inr = id (R0/completed-tensor-product-universal-property). m is surjective and continuous; it is open because inl is a continuous section: for an open subgroup G, m(G) ⊇ inl⁻¹(G), which is open. ker m is closed (C Hausdorff). m(D⁺) ⊆ C⁺ and C⁺ = m(inl(C⁺)) ⊆ m(D⁺), so C⁺ is the integral closure of m(D⁺): m is a quotient mapping and (C, C⁺) ≅ (C ⊗̂_A C)/ker m as quotient pairs (Tau Ceti `Pair.quotient`, `Pair.Hom.quotientLift`); Spa(C) → Spa(C ⊗̂_A C) is a closed embedding (Tau Ceti `Pair.Hom.isClosedEmbedding_spaComap_quotientHom`).

Hence Δ_f : X → W is affinoid-locally over W the closed immersion Spa((C ⊗̂_A C)/ker m) → Spa(C ⊗̂_A C) with closed kernel and sheafy quotient C; closed immersions are local on the target (anchor Layer 5.1, independence of the affinoid cover), so Δ_f is a closed embedding into W and a locally closed embedding into X ×_Y X (R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings).
acceptance: For the closed disc D = Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩) over ℚ_p, W = D ×_{ℚ_p} D and Δ is the closed embedding cut out by T ⊗ 1 − 1 ⊗ T in ℚ_p⟨T, S⟩.

nodes.title: The norm of a Tate ring attached to a ring of definition, a pseudouniformiser and a radius
nodes.statement: Let A be a Tate ring (Tau Ceti `IsTateRing A`). A *norm datum* d = (A₀, ϖ, r) on A consists of a ring of definition A₀ (the `ringOfDefinition` of a Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition A`), a pseudouniformiser ϖ of A lying in A₀ (Tau Ceti `IsPseudoUniformizer ϖ`: a topologically nilpotent unit; A₀ contains one by Wedhorn Proposition 6.14) and a real number r with 0 < r < 1. The *norm of A attached to d* is α_d : A → ℝ≥0, α_d(x) := inf{ rⁿ : n ∈ ℤ, ϖ⁻ⁿx ∈ A₀ } (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 2.4.4). The exponent set is nonempty and downward closed, so α_d(x) = r^{N(x)} with N(x) = sup{ n ∈ ℤ : x ∈ ϖⁿA₀ } ∈ ℤ ∪ {+∞} (r^{+∞} := 0). Then α_d is a nonarchimedean ring seminorm (Mathlib `RingSeminorm A` with `IsNonarchimedean`), α_d(1) ≤ 1 and α_d(ϖx) = r·α_d(x); its closed balls are {α_d ≤ rⁿ} = ϖⁿA₀ (n ∈ ℤ), so it defines the topology of A; it vanishes exactly on the closure of {0} = ⋂ₙ ϖⁿA₀, so it is a norm iff A is Hausdorff, and (A, α_d) is a Banach ring in Kedlaya–Liu's sense iff A is moreover complete. Pinned conventions: ϖ must lie in A₀; the function depends on d, and only its equivalence class (for fixed ϖ and r) and the topology it defines are canonical. Lean names: `Huber.TateNormDatum A` for d and `Huber.tateNorm d` for α_d.
hypotheses: A is a Tate ring (Tau Ceti `IsTateRing`).
A₀ is the ring of definition of a Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition A`, and ϖ ∈ A₀ is a pseudouniformiser of A.
r is a real number with 0 < r < 1.
proofSteps: Nonempty exponent set: A₀ is an open neighbourhood of 0 and ϖ is topologically nilpotent, so ϖᵏx → 0 and ϖᵏx ∈ A₀ for k ≫ 0; downward closed: ϖ⁻ⁿx ∈ A₀ implies ϖ⁻⁽ⁿ⁻¹⁾x = ϖ·(ϖ⁻ⁿx) ∈ A₀ because ϖ ∈ A₀.

Seminorm axioms: A₀ is a subring, so ϖ⁻ⁿx, ϖ⁻ᵐy ∈ A₀ give ϖ⁻ⁿ⁻ᵐxy ∈ A₀ and, for m = n, ϖ⁻ⁿ(x ± y) ∈ A₀; hence α_d(xy) ≤ α_d(x)α_d(y), α_d(x + y) ≤ max(α_d(x), α_d(y)), α_d(−x) = α_d(x); 1 ∈ A₀ gives α_d(1) ≤ 1 and every n is allowed for x = 0. These are the fields of Mathlib `RingSeminorm` and the inequality `IsNonarchimedean`.
Balls and topology: α_d(x) ≤ rⁿ iff ϖ⁻ⁿx ∈ A₀ iff x ∈ ϖⁿA₀, and the sets ϖⁿA₀ (n ≥ 0) form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0 in A (Tau Ceti `IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero`).
Kernel: α_d(x) = 0 iff x ∈ ⋂ₙ ϖⁿA₀, the closure of {0} because the ϖⁿA₀ are a basis of open subgroups.

Change of datum: rings of definition A₀, A₀' both containing ϖ satisfy ϖᵏA₀ ⊆ A₀' and ϖᵏA₀' ⊆ A₀ for some k ≥ 0 (each is bounded, the other open), so α' ≤ r⁻ᵏα and α ≤ r⁻ᵏα'; replacing r by r' replaces α_d by α_d^{log r'/log r} because α_d takes values in r^ℤ ∪ {0}.
acceptance: For A = ℚ_p, A₀ = ℤ_p, ϖ = p and r = 1/p the norm is the p-adic absolute value.

For a Banach algebra (A, ‖·‖) over a complete nonarchimedean field K with ‖cy‖ = |c|·‖y‖ (c ∈ K) and ‖1‖ = 1, A₀ the unit ball, ϖ ∈ K with 0 < |ϖ| < 1 and r = |ϖ|: ‖x‖ ≤ α_d(x) ≤ r⁻¹‖x‖ for all x (strict inequality α_d(x) < r⁻¹‖x‖ for x ≠ 0), so α_d is equivalent to ‖·‖.

uses.how: a Tate f-adic ring is given the structure of a Banach ring by this norm, so the Banach-ring statements of Kedlaya–Liu §§2.3–2.8 apply to complete Tate Huber rings
every Tate Huber ring can be promoted to a Banach ring; bounded Banach morphisms correspond to continuous Huber morphisms
the spectral seminorm is the smoothing lim α_d(xⁿ)^{1/n} of α_d
the Banach norm of a complete Tate ring used in Kedlaya–Liu's uniformity criteria and strictness estimates

nodes.title: The spectral seminorm of a Tate ring
nodes.statement: Let A be a Tate ring with a norm datum d = (A₀, ϖ, r) and norm α_d (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/tate-ring-norm). The *spectral seminorm* of (A, d) is |x|_sp := lim_{n→∞} α_d(xⁿ)^{1/n} = inf_{n≥1} α_d(xⁿ)^{1/n} (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 2.1.9; the limit exists by Fekete's lemma), which is Mathlib's `smoothingSeminorm α_d` (defined because α_d(1) ≤ 1 and α_d is nonarchimedean). It is a power-multiplicative nonarchimedean ring seminorm (Mathlib `IsPowMul`: |xⁿ|_sp = |x|_spⁿ for n ≥ 1) with |x|_sp ≤ α_d(x). It does not change when A₀ is replaced by another ring of definition containing ϖ (equivalent norms have the same spectral seminorm), and replacing r by r' raises it to the power log r'/log r. Intrinsic properties: |x|_sp < 1 iff x is topologically nilpotent; |x|_sp ≤ 1 for every power-bounded x; the kernel {x : |x|_sp = 0} is the ideal ⋂ₙ ϖⁿ·A°° (A°° the topologically nilpotent elements), it contains the nilradical and the closure of {0}; |1|_sp = 1 if A is Hausdorff and nonzero. Functoriality: if φ : A → B is a continuous ring homomorphism of Tate rings and B carries a datum (B₀, φ(ϖ), r) with φ(A₀) ⊆ B₀ (such B₀ exists because φ is adic), then |φ(x)|_sp ≤ |x|_sp. Pinned convention: the Gel'fand-spectrum formula |x|_sp = max_{β ∈ M(A)} β(x) (Berkovich) is not part of this node; it is the input of AdicSpacesPartII:R3/uniform-spectral-seminorm. Lean name: `Huber.spectralSeminorm d`.
hypotheses: A is a Tate ring with a norm datum d = (A₀, ϖ, r) (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/tate-ring-norm).
proofSteps: Definition: `smoothingSeminorm α_d` with the hypotheses α_d(1) ≤ 1 and `IsNonarchimedean α_d` (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/tate-ring-norm, API tateNorm_one_le, isNonarchimedean_tateNorm); the limit formula is Mathlib `tendsto_smoothingFun_of_map_one_le_one`, power-multiplicativity is `isPowMul_smoothingFun`, and |x|_sp ≤ α_d(x) is `smoothingFun_le_self`.
Independence of A₀: if α' ≤ Cα then α'(xⁿ)^{1/n} ≤ C^{1/n}α(xⁿ)^{1/n}, and C^{1/n} → 1 (tate-ring-norm, API tateNorm_equiv_of_ringOfDefinition); the r-dependence follows from tateNorm_rpow.

|x|_sp < 1 iff x ∈ A°°: if |x|_sp < 1 then α_d(x^N) < 1 for some N, so α_d(x^{Nk+j}) ≤ α_d(x^N)^k α_d(x^j) → 0 and xⁿ → 0 (α_d defines the topology); conversely xⁿ → 0 gives α_d(x^N) ≤ r for some N and |x|_sp ≤ α_d(x^N)^{1/N} < 1 (Mathlib `smoothingFun_le`). Power-bounded x have bounded α_d(xⁿ), so |x|_sp ≤ 1.

Kernel: |x|_sp = 0 implies |ϖ⁻ⁿx|_sp ≤ |ϖ⁻¹|_spⁿ·|x|_sp = 0 < 1, so ϖ⁻ⁿx ∈ A°° for all n; conversely x ∈ ϖⁿA°° gives |x|_sp ≤ |ϖ|_spⁿ < rⁿ. Nilpotents and the closure of {0} (where α_d = 0) lie in the kernel. If A is Hausdorff and nonzero, α_d(1) > 0 and α_d(1ⁿ) = α_d(1), so |1|_sp = 1.

Functoriality: φ is adic because A is Tate (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-ring-homomorphism, API IsAdicHom.of_isTateRing), giving a ring of definition B₀ ⊇ φ(A₀); φ(ϖ) is a pseudouniformiser of B; α_{d'}(φ x) ≤ α_d(x) (tate-ring-norm, API tateNorm_map_le), and smoothing is monotone.
acceptance: For A = K⟨T⟩, A₀ = K°⟨T⟩, ϖ ∈ K° with 0 < |ϖ| < 1 and r = |ϖ|, |f|_sp is the Gauss norm sup |aₙ|.
For A = K[ε]/(ε²) (finite free over K, A₀ = K° ⊕ K°ε) |ε|_sp = 0 while α_d(ε) = 1.

nodes.title: The spectral topology of a Tate ring
nodes.statement: Let A be a Tate ring. The *spectral topology* on A is the topology defined by a spectral seminorm |·|_sp (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-seminorm): the ring topology whose neighbourhoods of 0 are generated by the balls {x : |x|_sp < ε}, ε > 0. For every pseudouniformiser ϖ of A the sets ϖⁿ·A°° (n ≥ 0; A°° the ideal of topologically nilpotent elements) form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0 for it; in particular it does not depend on the norm datum. Write A_sp for A with this topology (Lean: the type synonym `Huber.SpectralTop A`, with the ring equivalence `toSpectralTop : A ≃+* SpectralTop A`). Then: (i) the identity A → A_sp is continuous; (ii) A_sp is a Tate ring with pseudouniformiser ϖ and pair of definition (A_sp,≤1, ϖ·A_sp,≤1), where A_sp,≤1 = {x : |x|_sp ≤ 1}; (iii) the topologically nilpotent elements of A_sp are those of A, and A_sp° = {x : |x|_sp ≤ 1} is bounded, so A_sp is uniform (Hansen–Kedlaya Definition 2.3, the anchor's Layer 4.2 predicate); (iv) every ring of integral elements A⁺ of A is a ring of integral elements of A_sp, giving a Tau Ceti `Pair` on A_sp and a morphism of Huber pairs (A, A⁺) → (A_sp, A⁺); (v) every continuous ring homomorphism φ : A → B of Tate rings is continuous as a map A_sp → B_sp; (vi) the identity A → A_sp is a homeomorphism iff A° is bounded, i.e. iff A is uniform. Lean name: `Huber.SpectralTop A`.
hypotheses: A is a Tate ring (Tau Ceti `IsTateRing`).
proofSteps: Basis: ϖⁿ·A°° ⊆ {|x|_sp < rⁿ} because |ϖⁿy|_sp ≤ |ϖ|_spⁿ|y|_sp ≤ rⁿ|y|_sp and |y|_sp < 1 for y ∈ A°°; and {|x|_sp < rⁿ·|ϖ⁻¹|_sp⁻ⁿ} ⊆ ϖⁿ·A°° because |ϖ⁻ⁿx|_sp ≤ |ϖ⁻¹|_spⁿ|x|_sp < 1 (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-seminorm, API spectralSeminorm_lt_one_iff). A°° is an additive subgroup (Tau Ceti `topologicallyNilpotentIdeal`, an ideal of A°). Changing ϖ to ϖ' gives the same filter since ϖ'^m ∈ ϖ·A° and ϖ^m ∈ ϖ'·A° for m ≫ 0.
(i): A°° ⊇ ϖ·A₀ is open in A, so each ϖⁿA°° is an open subgroup of A.

(ii),(iii): A_sp,≤1 is a subring (|·|_sp is a nonarchimedean submultiplicative seminorm with |1|_sp ≤ 1), open (it contains A°°) and bounded (ϖⁿ⁺¹·A_sp,≤1 ⊆ ϖⁿA°°); ϖ is a unit with ϖⁿ ∈ ϖⁿ⁻¹A°°; so (A_sp,≤1, ϖ) is a pair of definition. If x is power-bounded in A_sp then |x|_spⁿ = |xⁿ|_sp is bounded, so |x|_sp ≤ 1; conversely |x|_sp ≤ 1 puts all powers in the bounded set A_sp,≤1.
(iv): A⁺ ⊆ A° ⊆ A_sp,≤1 = A_sp°; A⁺ contains A°° (Tau Ceti `IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`), which is open in A_sp; integral closedness does not involve the topology.
(v): φ maps A°° into B°° and ϖ to a pseudouniformiser φ(ϖ) of B (φ is adic, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-ring-homomorphism), so φ(ϖⁿA°°) ⊆ φ(ϖ)ⁿB°°, a basic neighbourhood of B_sp.

(vi): if A° is bounded it is a ring of definition, the sets ϖⁿA° are a basis of A (Tau Ceti `IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero`) and ϖⁿ⁺¹A° ⊆ ϖⁿA°° ⊆ ϖⁿA°; conversely equal topologies give A° = A_sp°, which is bounded by (iii).
acceptance: For K⟨T⟩ (uniform) the identity K⟨T⟩ → K⟨T⟩_sp is a homeomorphism.
For K[ε]/(ε²) the closure of {0} in the spectral topology is Kε.

A need not be complete for its spectral seminorm even when it is a norm, so the uniformization must complete A_sp
uniformity of a Huber ring (A° bounded) agrees with uniformity of a Banach ring (spectral seminorm defines the topology): API homeomorph_of_isBounded
A_sp has the same continuous valuations and adic spectrum
the uniformization is the Hausdorff completion of A_sp

nodes.title: The spectral topology has the same continuous valuations, adic spectrum and rational subsets
nodes.statement: Let A be a Tate ring and A_sp = `Huber.SpectralTop A` (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-topology). A valuation on A is continuous for the topology of A iff it is continuous for the spectral topology: Cont(A_sp) = Cont(A) as subsets of Spv(A) (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.cont`). Consequently, for every ring of integral elements A⁺ of A, Spa(A_sp, A⁺) = Spa(A, A⁺) as subspaces of Spv(A) (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.spa A⁺` for the two topologies), and for every finite T ⊆ A and s ∈ A the rational subsets R(T/s) (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset A⁺ T s`) of the two spectra are equal; a finite subset generates an open ideal of A iff it generates an open ideal of A_sp (in both Tate rings: iff it generates the unit ideal).
hypotheses: A is a Tate ring; A⁺ is a ring of integral elements of A.
proofSteps: Cont(A_sp) ⊆ Cont(A): the identity A → A_sp is continuous (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-topology (i)), and a valuation all of whose sets {x : v(x) < γ} are open for the coarser topology has them open for the finer one.

Cont(A) ⊆ Cont(A_sp): let v ∈ Cont(A) and γ ≠ 0 in its value group; for a pseudouniformiser ϖ some power satisfies v(ϖ)ⁿ < γ (Tau Ceti `Valuation.exists_pow_lt_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`, {v < γ} being a neighbourhood of 0), and v(y) < 1 for every topologically nilpotent y (Tau Ceti `Valuation.IsContinuous.lt_one_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`); so the subgroup {x : v(x) < γ} contains ϖⁿ·A°°, a neighbourhood of 0 in A_sp (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-topology, basis), and is open in A_sp.

Spa and rational subsets are defined inside Spv(A) from Cont, the plus ring and the elements T, s only (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.spa_def`, `ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`), and the subspace topology comes from Spv(A), which does not depend on the topology of A; so they coincide. In a Tate ring an ideal is open iff it is the unit ideal (Tau Ceti `IsTateRing.isOpen_iff_eq_top`), for both topologies.
acceptance: For A = K[ε]/(ε²) with A⁺ = K° + Kε and K = ℚ_p, Spa(A_sp, A⁺) = Spa(A, A⁺) is a single point, the valuation a + bε ↦ |a|_p.
For uniform A the statement is the identity (A_sp = A by AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-topology (vi)).
