nodes.title: The uniformization of a Tate Huber pair
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a Huber pair (Tau Ceti `Pair`) with A a Tate ring. Its *uniformization* is the Huber pair (A^u, A^{u+}) where A^u is the Hausdorff completion of A_sp = `Huber.SpectralTop A` (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-topology; Tau Ceti `IsHuberRing.completion`, `IsTateRing.completion`), i.e. the separated completion of A for its spectral seminorm (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 2.8.13), and A^{u+} is the closure of the image of A⁺ in A^u. It comes with the morphism of Huber pairs ι : (A, A⁺) → (A^u, A^{u+}), the composite of the continuous identity A → A_sp and the completion map. Properties: (a) (A^u, A^{u+}) is a complete Hausdorff Huber pair, A^u is a Tate ring, and A^u is uniform (A^{u°} is bounded; the continuous extension of |·|_sp to A^u is a power-multiplicative norm defining its topology); (b) ι has dense image and kernel {x : |x|_sp = 0}; (c) for every complete Hausdorff Huber pair (B, B⁺) with B° bounded and every morphism of Huber pairs φ : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) there is exactly one morphism φ^u : (A^u, A^{u+}) → (B, B⁺) with φ^u ∘ ι = φ, so uniformization is left adjoint to the inclusion of complete Hausdorff uniform Tate Huber pairs into Tate Huber pairs; (d) Spa(ι) : Spa(A^u, A^{u+}) → Spa(A, A⁺) is a homeomorphism under which rational subsets correspond to rational subsets; (e) if A is complete, Hausdorff and uniform, ι is an isomorphism. Pinned conventions: morphisms are Tau Ceti `Pair.Hom` (continuous, plus rings respected), which for Banach rings are the bounded morphisms (Hansen–Kedlaya Remark 2.11); the plus ring is the closure of the image of A⁺, not the image. Lean name: `Huber.Pair.uniformization`.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) is a Huber pair and A is a Tate ring.
For the universal property: (B, B⁺) is a complete Hausdorff Huber pair with B° bounded.
proofSteps: A_sp is a uniform Tate ring, A⁺ is a ring of integral elements of A_sp and the identity is a morphism of Huber pairs (A, A⁺) → (A_sp, A⁺) (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-topology).

Completion: Completion(A_sp) is a complete Hausdorff Tate ring with the completed pair of definition (Tau Ceti `IsHuberRing.completion`, `IsTateRing.completion`, `PairOfDefinition.completion`); the closure of the image of A⁺ is a ring of integral elements (anchor Layer 0: completion of Huber pairs, Wedhorn Lemma 7.47).

Uniformity: |·|_sp is uniformly continuous on A_sp and extends to a seminorm β on A^u; β is power-multiplicative (β(xⁿ) = β(x)ⁿ passes to limits), a norm (A^u is separated for it) and defines the topology of A^u; a power-bounded x has β(x)ⁿ = β(xⁿ) bounded, so A^{u°} ⊆ {β ≤ 1}, which is bounded.

Dense image and kernel: Mathlib `UniformSpace.Completion.denseRange_coe`; the kernel of A_sp → Completion(A_sp) is the closure of {0} in A_sp, which is {x : |x|_sp = 0} (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-seminorm, API spectralSeminorm_eq_zero_iff).

Universal property: φ is continuous as a map A_sp → B_sp (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-topology (v)) and B_sp = B because B° is bounded (spectral-topology (vi)); B being complete and Hausdorff, φ extends uniquely to a continuous ring homomorphism A^u → B (Mathlib `UniformSpace.Completion.extensionHom`, `extensionHom_coe`); it maps A^{u+} into B⁺ since B⁺ is an open, hence closed, subgroup containing φ(A⁺). Uniqueness: two continuous extensions agree on the dense image of ι. B is Tate because it receives a continuous map from a Tate ring (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-ring-homomorphism, API IsAdicHom.of_isTateRing).

Spa: the completion morphism induces a homeomorphism Spa(A^u, A^{u+}) → Spa(A_sp, A⁺) identifying rational subsets (anchor Layer 0: Spa of the completion, Wedhorn Proposition 7.48), and Spa(A_sp, A⁺) = Spa(A, A⁺) with the same rational subsets (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-topology-cont-eq); preimages of rational subsets are Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset`.
(e): for complete Hausdorff uniform A, A_sp = A (spectral-topology (vi)) and the completion map of a complete Hausdorff ring is an isomorphism.
acceptance: (K[ε]/(ε²), K° + Kε)^u = (K, K°) with ι the reduction map ε ↦ 0.
For A = {Σ aₙTⁿ ∈ K⟦T⟧ : |aₙ|(n+1) → 0} with ‖f‖ = sup |aₙ|(n+1), A^u = K⟨T⟩ and ι is the inclusion.
For a complete Hausdorff uniform (A, A⁺), for instance (K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩), ι is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: The uniform completed tensor product of Tate Huber pairs
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺), (B, B⁺), (C, C⁺) be complete Hausdorff Huber pairs with A a Tate ring, and f : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺), g : (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) morphisms of Huber pairs (Tau Ceti `Pair.Hom`; f and g are adic and B, C are Tate by Wedhorn Proposition 6.25). The *uniform completed tensor product* is B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C := (B ⊗̂_A C)^u, the uniformization (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization) of the completed tensor product (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product), with inlᵘ := ι ∘ inl and inrᵘ := ι ∘ inr. Properties: (a) it is a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate Huber pair and inlᵘ ∘ f = inrᵘ ∘ g; (b) it is a pushout of (f, g) in the category of complete Hausdorff uniform Tate Huber pairs: for every such (R, R⁺) and morphisms φ : (B, B⁺) → (R, R⁺), ψ : (C, C⁺) → (R, R⁺) with φ ∘ f = ψ ∘ g there is exactly one morphism χ : B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C → (R, R⁺) with χ ∘ inlᵘ = φ and χ ∘ inrᵘ = ψ; (c) the canonical morphism ι : B ⊗̂_A C → B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C induces a homeomorphism of adic spectra identifying rational subsets; (d) ι is an isomorphism iff B ⊗̂_A C is uniform (for instance K⟨T⟩ ⊗̂_K K⟨S⟩ = K⟨T, S⟩), and it is not an isomorphism in general: ℂ_p ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p is not uniform (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 2.8.5). No sheafiness of B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C and no fibre-product property of its Spa is claimed. Lean name: `Huber.Pair.uniformCompletedTensor f g`.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺), (B, B⁺), (C, C⁺) complete Hausdorff Huber pairs, A a Tate ring.
f : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺), g : (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) morphisms of Huber pairs.
proofSteps: f and g are adic and B, C are Tate (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-ring-homomorphism, API IsAdicHom.of_isTateRing), so B ⊗̂_A C is defined and is a complete Hausdorff Tate Huber pair (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product, API completedTensor.isTateRing).
(a), (c): uniformize (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization: uniformity, completeness, Spa homeomorphism).

(b): given φ, ψ into a complete Hausdorff uniform (R, R⁺) — R⁺ is closed and integrally closed — the universal property of the completed tensor product (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product-universal-property) gives a unique χ₀ : B ⊗̂_A C → (R, R⁺), and the universal property of the uniformization (R0/uniformization, lift) factors χ₀ uniquely through ι; uniqueness of χ follows from hom_ext of both constructions.
(d): R0/uniformization (isIso_of_isUniform) for ⇐; for ⇒ an isomorphic copy of a uniform pair is uniform. The non-example is Kedlaya–Liu Remark 2.8.5.
acceptance: K⟨T⟩ ⊗̂ᵘ_K K⟨S⟩ ≅ K⟨T, S⟩ for a complete nonarchimedean field K.
ℂ_p ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p → ℂ_p ⊗̂ᵘ_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p is not an isomorphism (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 2.8.5).

nodes.title: Completed tensor products of Banach modules over complete Tate rings
nodes.statement: Let A be a complete Tate ring (Tau Ceti IsTateRing, complete and Hausdorff) with a norm datum d = (A₀, ϖ, r) and norm α_d (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/tate-ring-norm); for instance A = L a complete nonarchimedean field with its absolute value. A Banach A-module is a complete Hausdorff topological A-module V whose topology is defined by an additive subgroup V₀ stable under A₀ with V = ⋃ₙ ϖ⁻ⁿV₀, the ϖⁿV₀ forming a basis of neighbourhoods of 0; equivalently, an A-module complete for a norm |·| with |av| ≤ c·α_d(a)·|v| (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 2.2.7), a lattice being the A₀-submodule generated by {|·| ≤ 1} (which is {|·| ≤ 1} itself when c ≤ 1). For Banach A-modules V, W the completed tensor product V ⊗̂_A W is the Hausdorff completion of V ⊗_A W for the tensor topology, in which the images of ϖⁿ·(V₀ ⊗_{A₀} W₀), n ≥ 0, form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0. Equivalently it is the completion for the product seminorm |x| = inf max_i |v_i|·|w_i| over presentations x = Σ v_i ⊗ w_i (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 2.1.10, stated there for rings). It is a Banach A-module whose lattice is the closure of the image of V₀ ⊗ W₀; up to equivalence of norms it does not depend on the lattices. (a) Universal property: (v, w) ↦ v ⊗ w is a continuous A-bilinear map whose image spans a dense submodule. Every continuous A-bilinear map β: V × W → M into a complete Hausdorff topological A-module M whose topology has a basis of neighbourhoods of 0 consisting of A₀-submodules (for instance a Banach A-module with lattice M₀, for which continuity of β is equivalent to boundedness: β(V₀ × W₀) ⊆ ϖ⁻ᵏM₀ for some k) factors uniquely as β = β̂ ∘ ⊗ with β̂: V ⊗̂_A W → M continuous and A-linear. (b) Functoriality: continuous A-linear f: V → V' and g: W → W' induce f ⊗̂ g, compatibly with identities and composition, and A ⊗̂_A V ≅ V. (c) Compatibility: if V = B and W = C are complete Huber A-algebras (adic structure maps; B₀, C₀ rings of definition containing the images of A₀), then V ⊗̂_A W is B ⊗̂_A C of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product as a topological A-module, and its multiplication is the continuous extension of that of B ⊗_A C. (d) Exactness: − ⊗̂_A W carries a topologically split short exact sequence of Banach A-modules (continuous maps with a continuous retraction and a continuous section) to a topologically split short exact sequence. The field statements of Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 2.2.9 (injectivity of V ⊗_L W → V ⊗̂_L W, the cross-norm property, kernels and strictness of f ⊗̂ X) are not part of this node: they are AdicSpacesPartII:R0/banach-completed-tensor-field-exactness, which is proved from (f) and the existence of t-orthogonal bases (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/banach-countable-type-orthogonal-basis). (e) Finite projective modules: for a finite projective A-module P with its natural topology (a finite Banach module, Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 2.2.12), P ⊗_A W → P ⊗̂_A W is an isomorphism. (f) Orthonormal bases: let A = L be a complete nonarchimedean field and let V have an orthonormal basis (e_i)_{i∈I}: every v ∈ V is uniquely Σ c_i e_i with c_i → 0 along the cofinite filter, and |v| = max |c_i|. Then for every Banach L-module E, E ⊗̂_L V ≅ c₀(I, E), the Banach module of I-indexed families in E tending to 0 with the supremum norm, via x ⊗ Σ c_i e_i ↦ (c_i x)_i, isometrically. If (e_i) is only t-orthogonal for some 0 < t ≤ 1 (t·max|c_i| ≤ |Σ c_i e_i| ≤ max|c_i|), the same map is a topological isomorphism with t·|·|_sup ≤ |·| ≤ |·|_sup. (g) Base change: for a continuous homomorphism A → A' of complete Tate rings, A' ⊗̂_A V is a Banach A'-module, and A'' ⊗̂_{A'} (A' ⊗̂_A V) ≅ A'' ⊗̂_A V for A → A' → A''. In particular M ⊗̂_A A⟨T/s⟩ is defined for a Banach A-module M and a rational localisation A → A⟨T/s⟩; it equals M ⊗_A A⟨T/s⟩ when M is finite projective (e) or finite over a strongly noetherian A (Huber 1994 Lemma 2.4(ii)). Conventions: the orthonormal description uses null families (c₀), not bounded families: E ⊗̂_L c₀(I, L) = c₀(I, E), whereas the mixed completed tensor product of AdicSpacesPartII:R5/mixed-completed-tensor with the profinite flat module ∏_I O gives bounded families. The existence of orthonormal or t-orthogonal bases, for instance for Banach spaces of countable type (Bosch–Güntzer–Remmert 2.7.2/3, cited by Hansen–Kedlaya Remark 7.8), is a hypothesis of (f); it is proved in AdicSpacesPartII:R0/banach-countable-type-orthogonal-basis.
hypotheses: A complete Hausdorff Tate ring with a norm datum (R0/tate-ring-norm); for (f), A = L a complete nonarchimedean field
V, W Banach A-modules; for (a), M a complete Hausdorff topological A-module with a basis of neighbourhoods of 0 consisting of A₀-submodules (e.g. a Banach A-module)
For (f): an orthonormal, or t-orthogonal, basis of V
proofSteps: Lattices and norms: for a lattice V₀, |v| = inf{rⁿ : v ∈ ϖⁿV₀} is a norm with |av| ≤ α_d(a)·|v| and |ϖv| = r|v|; conversely, for a norm with |av| ≤ c·α_d(a)|v| the A₀-submodule generated by {|·| ≤ 1} lies in {|·| ≤ c} and is a lattice (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 2.2.7 with the norm α_d of R0/tate-ring-norm). Two lattices defining the same topology satisfy ϖᵏV₀ ⊆ V₀' ⊆ ϖ⁻ᵏV₀. By Banach's open mapping theorem for Tate rings (Huber 1994 Lemma 2.4(i), quoted as Berkeley Proposition 4.3.4, which cites it as [Hub93]; anchor Layer 0.6) a continuous A-linear bijection between Banach A-modules is a homeomorphism, so comparable complete lattice topologies coincide.

Tensor topology: the images of ϖⁿ(V₀ ⊗_{A₀} W₀) are additive subgroups, stable under A₀ and with ϖ acting bijectively on V ⊗_A W, so they define an A-module topology; changing lattices changes n by a bounded amount. The product seminorm's balls are sandwiched between these images, so both define the same topology. The Hausdorff completion is Mathlib's UniformSpace.Completion of the additive group, and the A-action extends by uniform continuity.

(a): let U be a neighbourhood of 0 in M that is an A₀-submodule; continuity of β at (0, 0) gives k with β(ϖᵏV₀ × ϖᵏW₀) ⊆ U, so the induced A-linear map V ⊗_A W → M (Mathlib TensorProduct.lift) sends the image of ϖ²ᵏ(V₀ ⊗_{A₀} W₀), which is additively generated by such values, into U: it is continuous for the tensor topology. It extends uniquely to the completion because M is complete and Hausdorff (Mathlib UniformSpace.Completion.extension); uniqueness from density of the image of V ⊗_A W. (Without the hypothesis that M has a basis of A₀-submodule neighbourhoods the additive span of β(ϖᵏV₀ × ϖᵏW₀) need not be small, as for projective tensor products with non-locally-convex targets.)
(b): apply (a) to (v, w) ↦ f(v) ⊗ g(w) and to (a, v) ↦ av (A ⊗_A V = V is already complete for the tensor topology, whose lattice is the image of A₀ ⊗ V₀ = V₀).

(c): for Tate A the ideal ϖA₀ is an ideal of definition of A₀, so R0's tensor topology {Iⁿ·F} (F the image of B₀ ⊗_{A₀} C₀, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product) has the same basis {ϖⁿF}; the two completions coincide, and the ring structure extends by continuity.
(d): a topological splitting V ≅ V' ⊕ V'' (continuous projections) passes through the additive functor − ⊗̂_A W, by (b).
(e): P is a direct summand of Aⁿ with continuous projections (Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 2.2.12); Aⁿ ⊗_A W = Wⁿ is complete and Hausdorff, hence so is the summand P ⊗_A W, so no completion occurs.

(f): (x, Σ c_i e_i) ↦ (c_i x)_i is bilinear with |c_i x| ≤ |x|·max|c_j|, so it factors through E ⊗̂_L V by (a). On a finite sum Σ_j x_j ⊗ e_j the product norm equals max_j |x_j|, because the coordinate functionals of an orthonormal basis have norm ≤ 1. So the map is isometric, and its image contains the dense subspace of finitely supported families; hence it is an isometric isomorphism. For a t-orthogonal basis the same estimates hold up to the factor t. This is the computation behind CHJ Lemma 2.23(2).
(g): the A'-action on A' ⊗̂_A V extends that on A' ⊗_A V by continuity; transitivity follows from (a) applied to both sides, which represent the same continuous multilinear maps.
acceptance: K⟨T⟩ ⊗̂_K K⟨S⟩ ≅ K⟨T, S⟩ via Tᵐ ⊗ Sⁿ ↦ TᵐSⁿ (orthonormal bases of monomials), agreeing with the completed tensor product of Huber pairs.
Σ pⁿTⁿSⁿ ∈ ℚ_p⟨T, S⟩ is not in the image of the algebraic tensor product ℚ_p⟨T⟩ ⊗ ℚ_p⟨S⟩: the coefficient matrix of an element of that image has finite rank.
For a finite extension L/K of complete nonarchimedean fields and any Banach K-space V, L ⊗_K V → L ⊗̂_K V is an isomorphism.

A^G ⊗̂_K L → (A ⊗̂_K L)^G via an orthonormal basis of L over K (f) and the compatibility with completed tensor products of Huber pairs (c)

nodes.title: Separated morphism of adic spaces
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of adic spaces (the category of the AdicSpaces anchor, Layer 5) that is locally of weakly finite type (R0/finite-type-morphism-classes), with X covered by open affinoids Spa(A, A⁺) with A complete and stably sheafy (anchor `Huber.IsStablySheafyRing`; automatic if Y is so covered, Wedhorn Remark 8.55(2), and for X locally noetherian). Such an f is adic, so the fibre product X ×_Y X exists in the category of adic spaces (R0/fibre-products-existence, case (b) with g = f, the second factor X being covered by stably sheafy affinoids) and the diagonal Δ_f: X → X ×_Y X is the morphism with both projections equal to the identity. The morphism f is separated if the image Δ_f(|X|) is a closed subset of the underlying space |X ×_Y X| of the adic fibre product (Huber 1996, 1.3.1). Conventions: (1) X ×_Y X is the fibre product of adic spaces, never the topological fibre product |X| ×_{|Y|} |X|; the comparison map |X ×_Y X| → |X| ×_{|Y|} |X| is surjective and in general not injective (R0/fibre-product-points). (2) Separatedness is only defined for morphisms locally of weakly finite type whose source is covered by stably sheafy affinoids; no separatedness predicate is attached to a morphism outside that class. Huber states Definition 1.3.1 without the second condition because his standing hypothesis (1.1.1) makes every adic space locally of noetherian type, hence stable (Wedhorn Corollary 8.35); without it X ×_Y X need not exist. (3) By R0/diagonal-locally-closed the diagonal is a locally closed embedding, so a separated f has Δ_f a closed embedding (closed adic subspace in the sense of R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings) whenever X, Y are locally strongly noetherian analytic adic spaces and f is locally of finite type (Zavyalov, Quotients, Corollary B.7.4).
hypotheses: f: X → Y is a morphism of adic spaces, locally of weakly finite type
X is covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings (so that X ×_Y X exists); automatic if Y is, and under Huber's standing hypothesis (1.1.1)
Closedness is tested in the underlying topological space of the adic fibre product X ×_Y X
proofSteps: Existence of X ×_Y X: f locally of weakly finite type implies f adic (inclusion chain of R0/finite-type-morphism-classes), so case (b) of R0/fibre-products-existence applies with g = f; its covering hypothesis is required of the second factor, which is X, and holds by assumption (if only Y is assumed covered by stably sheafy affinoids, X inherits this because every affinoid of X locally of weakly finite type over a stably sheafy affinoid of Y has topologically-finite-type, hence stably sheafy, ring: Wedhorn Remark 8.55(2)).
The diagonal is the morphism given by the universal property of the fibre product (R0/fibre-products-existence); being separated is the property 'range of |Δ_f| is closed'.

Characterisation (3): Δ_f is a locally closed embedding (R0/diagonal-locally-closed); a locally closed embedding with closed image is a closed embedding (R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings; Zavyalov, Quotients, Lemma B.6.14 in the locally strongly noetherian analytic case).
acceptance: The structure morphism of the closed unit disc Spa(K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩) → Spa(K, K°) is separated: its diagonal is the closed subspace V(T₁ − T₂) of the closed bidisc.
The unit disc with doubled origin is not separated over Spa(K, K°).

uses.how: separatedness is a defining condition of proper and of partially proper morphisms (R0/universally-closed-and-proper-morphism, R0/partially-proper-morphism)
separatedness is characterised by uniqueness of centres of valuation rings

over a strongly noetherian Tate affinoid base, the intersection of two affinoid opens of a separated X is affinoid; this is what Čech computations of coherent cohomology (AdicSpacesPartII:R3, Kiehl proper mapping theorem) use
a section of a separated smooth morphism is a Zariski-closed (lci) immersion, via the diagonal
A2 imports separatedness of analytic adic spaces from R0
comparison of adic, rigid (Kiehl) and formal separatedness is stated for this predicate

tests.name: IsSeparated_test_closedDisc
tests.statement: Throughout the tests K is a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial rank-one valuation, K° its valuation ring, D = Spa(K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩) the closed unit disc and B = ⋃_n {|T|^n ≤ |ϖ|} ⊆ D the open unit disc (ϖ a pseudo-uniformiser), as in the AdicSpaces anchor, Layer 5.4. The structure morphism D → Spa(K, K°) is separated: D ×_K D is the closed bidisc Spa(K⟨T₁,T₂⟩, K°⟨T₁,T₂⟩) and Δ(D) = V(T₁ − T₂) is closed. At the same time the diagonal of |D| is not closed in the product of topological spaces |D| × |D|, because |D| is not Hausdorff (the Gauss point has proper specialisations); a definition testing closedness in |X| ×_{|Y|} |X| would wrongly declare D non-separated.

tests.name: IsSeparated_test_doubledOrigin
tests.statement: Throughout the tests K is a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial rank-one valuation, K° its valuation ring, D = Spa(K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩) the closed unit disc and B = ⋃_n {|T|^n ≤ |ϖ|} ⊆ D the open unit disc (ϖ a pseudo-uniformiser), as in the AdicSpaces anchor, Layer 5.4. Let 0 ∈ D be the point V(T) (a closed point) and let X be obtained by gluing two copies D₁, D₂ of D along the open subspace D ∖ {0} (AdicSpaces anchor, Layer 5.3). Then X → Spa(K, K°) is locally of finite type but not separated: the point (0₁, 0₂) of the open subspace D₁ ×_K D₂ of X ×_K X lies in the closure of Δ(D ∖ {0}) but not in Δ(X).

api.name: AdicSpace.IsSeparated.iff_valuativeCriterion
api.statement: For f quasi-separated, locally of weakly finite type, between analytic adic spaces: IsSeparated f ↔ uniqueness of centres (R0/valuative-criterion-separated).

sources.match: The definition itself, read in the book (page image of printed p. 51 checked): closed image of the diagonal in the adic fibre product, for f locally of weakly finite type.
Separatedness is the second of the three conditions of properness.

Huber's standing hypothesis, in force for Definitions 1.3.1-1.3.3 and (1.4.1): every adic space is locally of noetherian type, hence stable (Wedhorn Corollary 8.35), so all fibre products used in these definitions exist. Outside (1.1.1) this node must assume or quantify over the existence of the fibre products explicitly.

The existence theorem for fibre products needs the second factor to be stable (covered by stably sheafy affinoids); outside Huber's (1.1.1) this hypothesis is not automatic, so it is carried here. Remark 8.55(2) (same page): a space locally of weakly finite type over a stable space is stable.
Public statement of the same definition in the locally strongly noetherian analytic case: closed image of the diagonal in the adic fibre product.
The finiteness hypothesis is what makes X ×_Y X exist; this node keeps it.
Characterisation (3): closed image plus locally closed diagonal gives a closed immersion.

nodes.title: Universally closed morphism of adic spaces
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of adic spaces that is locally of weakly finite type. The morphism f is universally closed if, for every adic morphism g: Y' → Y and every pullback square of f along g in the category of adic spaces, with base change f': X' → Y', the continuous map |f'|: |X'| → |Y'| is a closed map (Huber 1996, 1.3.2(i)). Such pullbacks exist whenever Y' is covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings (R0/fibre-products-existence, case (b)), in particular always under Huber's standing hypothesis (1.1.1); the pullback along g = id_Y always exists (X' = X), so a universally closed f has |f| closed. The condition is independent of the choice of pullback (pullbacks are unique up to unique isomorphism), so quantifying over pullback squares (the shape of Mathlib's MorphismProperty.universally) is the same as quantifying over the base changes X ×_Y Y' that exist. Conventions: base change is only taken along adic morphisms, which is the class along which Huber's fibre product (b) exists; over an analytic Y every morphism is adic (R0/finite-type-morphism-classes), so there the condition is 'closed after every base change'.
hypotheses: f: X → Y locally of weakly finite type

Test morphisms g: Y' → Y range over all adic morphisms of adic spaces, and the condition is imposed on every pullback square of f along g (such squares exist when Y' is covered by complete stably sheafy affinoids)
proofSteps: The base changes along adic g: Y' → Y exist when Y' is covered by complete stably sheafy affinoids (R0/fibre-products-existence (b)); the property is the conjunction, over all adic g and all pullback squares (X', f', g') of f along g, of IsClosedMap |f'|.

Relation to specialisation: a closed map is specializing (Mathlib IsClosedMap.specializingMap), so universally closed implies universally specializing (R0/universally-specializing-morphism); the converse for quasi-compact f is R0/proper-iff-partially-proper-quasi-compact.
acceptance: Every finite morphism to an analytic adic space is universally closed (R0/finite-morphisms).
The closed unit disc D → Spa(K, K°) is not universally closed.

uses.how: one of the three defining conditions of properness (R0/universally-closed-and-proper-morphism)
a quasi-compact universally specializing morphism is universally closed
finite morphisms are shown universally closed
the proper mapping theorem is stated for proper, hence universally closed, morphisms

tests.name: UniversallyClosed_test_id
tests.statement: The identity of any adic space, and every closed embedding, is universally closed.

tests.name: UniversallyClosed_test_closedDisc
tests.statement: Throughout the tests K is a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial rank-one valuation, K° its valuation ring, D = Spa(K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩) the closed unit disc and B = ⋃_n {|T|^n ≤ |ϖ|} ⊆ D the open unit disc (ϖ a pseudo-uniformiser), as in the AdicSpaces anchor, Layer 5.4. The morphism D → Spa(K, K°) is quasi-compact, separated and of +weakly finite type but not universally closed: it is not universally specializing, since for the Gauss point x ∈ D and the valuation ring A ⊊ k(x)⁺ of k(x) that is the preimage of the valuation ring of the residue field k(T) at T = ∞, the pair (x, A) has a centre on Spa(K, K°) but none on D (T ∈ K°⟨T⟩ would have to lie in A). A definition requiring only that |f| itself be closed would accept D, since |D| → |Spa(K, K°)| (a point) is trivially closed.

tests.name: UniversallyClosed_test_specializing
tests.statement: If f is universally closed then every base change of |f| along an adic morphism is a specializing map in the sense of Mathlib's SpecializingMap; this mirrors Mathlib's universallyClosed_eq_universallySpecializing for schemes, whose other half (quasi-compact plus universally specializing implies universally closed) is R0/proper-iff-partially-proper-quasi-compact here.

api.name: AdicSpace.UniversallyClosed
api.statement: The class: f locally of weakly finite type and |f'| closed for every base change f' of f along an adic morphism.

api.name: AdicSpace.UniversallyClosed.isClosedMap

nodes.title: Proper morphism of adic spaces
nodes.statement: A morphism f: X → Y of adic spaces is proper if it is of +weakly finite type (quasi-compact and locally of +weakly finite type, R0/finite-type-morphism-classes), separated (R0/separated-morphism) and universally closed (R0/universally-closed-morphism) (Huber 1996, 1.3.2(ii)). Conventions: (1) the finiteness condition is '+weakly finite type', which includes quasi-compactness and the plus-ring condition O_X⁺(U) = integral closure of O_Y⁺(V)[E ∪ O_X(U)°°] for a finite E; it is neither 'locally of finite type' (Mathlib's IsProper for schemes) nor 'weakly finite type'. (2) Properness of rigid analytic varieties in Kiehl's sense (Conrad AWS, Definition 3.2.3) is a different definition; the comparison is AdicSpacesPartII:R1/proper-separated-comparisons. (3) Because separatedness (R0/separated-morphism) needs X ×_Y X to exist, the predicate is stated for X covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings (automatic under Huber's standing hypothesis (1.1.1), where every adic space is locally of noetherian type).
hypotheses: f: X → Y morphism of adic spaces
proofSteps: Conjunction of three predicates; the finiteness predicate comes from R0/finite-type-morphism-classes (of +weakly finite type = quasi-compact and locally of +weakly finite type).
acceptance: Every finite morphism to an analytic adic space is proper (R0/finite-morphisms).
Proper equals partially proper and quasi-compact (R0/proper-iff-partially-proper-quasi-compact).
The projective line over K is proper over Spa(K, K°); the closed unit disc is not.

nodes.title: Universally specializing morphism of adic spaces
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of adic spaces. For x ∈ X, f is specializing at x if for every specialization y' of f(x) (that is, y' ∈ closure{f(x)} in |Y|) there is a specialization x' of x with f(x') = y'. If f is locally of weakly finite type, f is universally specializing at x₀ ∈ X if for every adic morphism g: Y' → Y, every pullback square of f along g in the category of adic spaces with base change f': X' → Y' and projection p: X' → X, and every point x₀' ∈ X' with p(x₀') = x₀, the base change f' is specializing at x₀'; f is universally specializing if it is so at every point (Huber 1996, Definition 1.3.3(i)). Such pullbacks exist whenever Y' is covered by complete stably sheafy affinoids (R0/fibre-products-existence (b)), in particular always under Huber's standing hypothesis (1.1.1). Convention: 'f specializing at every point' is exactly Mathlib's SpecializingMap for the continuous map |f|.
hypotheses: f locally of weakly finite type for the 'universally' version
Base change along adic morphisms only, over every pullback square (such squares exist when Y' is covered by complete stably sheafy affinoids)
proofSteps: Pointwise definition, then quantified over all adic base changes (which exist by R0/fibre-products-existence (b)) and all points over x₀.
acceptance: Closed maps are specializing, so universally closed morphisms are universally specializing.
For the inclusion D ⊆ P¹ of the closed disc into the projective line, the specialization of the Gauss point in the direction |T| > 1 does not lift, so this open embedding is not specializing.

The open embedding D₀ → P¹ (notation of IsProper_test_projectiveLine) is not specializing at the Gauss point x: the type-5 point of D_∞ at the Gauss point in the direction |T| > 1 is a specialization of x in P¹ with no preimage specializing x in D₀. nodes.title: Valuation rings of an analytic adic space and their centres
nodes.statement: Let X be an analytic adic space. For x ∈ X let k(x) be the residue field of the local ring O_{X,x}, k(x)⁺ ⊆ k(x) the valuation ring of the valuation v_x, and κ(x) = (k(x)^∧, k(x)⁺^∧) the completed residue affinoid field with its canonical morphism ι_x: Spa κ(x) → X (AdicSpaces anchor, Layer 5; see requests). A valuation ring of X is a pair (x, A) with x ∈ X and A a valuation ring of the field k(x) such that A ⊆ k(x)⁺; X_v denotes the set of valuation rings of X (Huber 1996, 1.3.5). Since A ⊆ k(x)⁺ are valuation rings of the same field, A contains the maximal ideal of k(x)⁺, so A is open in k(x) and its closure Â in k(x)^∧ is a valuation ring making (k(x)^∧, Â) an affinoid field (Hübner, §2) with a canonical morphism j: Spa κ(x) → Spa(k(x)^∧, Â). For a morphism g: Spa κ(x) → Z to an adic space Z, a point z ∈ Z is a centre of (x, A) on Z with respect to g if there is a morphism c: Spa(k(x)^∧, Â) → Z with c ∘ j = g and c(s) = z, s the closed point of Spa(k(x)^∧, Â). A centre of (x, A) on X means a centre with respect to ι_x; for a morphism f: X → Y, a centre of (x, A) on Y means a centre with respect to f ∘ ι_x. Topology: X_v carries the topology generated by the sets D(U, h) = {(x, A) ∈ X_v : x ∈ U, h(x) ∈ A} for U ⊆ X open and h ∈ O_X(U), h(x) the image of h in k(x).
hypotheses: X analytic (every point analytic)
A ranges over valuation rings of k(x) contained in k(x)⁺ (not over all valuation rings of k(x))
The subbasic sets D(U, h) = {(x, A) : x ∈ U, h(x) ∈ A} are exactly Huber's (1.3.11)
proofSteps: Definition of X_v and of centres as stated; the morphism j and the affinoid field (k(x)^∧, Â) exist because A ⊇ 𝔪_{k(x)⁺} is open and A ⊆ k(x)⁺ ⊆ k(x)°.

Comparison with Huber's pointwise definition 1.3.5: by the description of morphisms from the spectrum of an affinoid field (Huber 1996, (1.1.8)), a morphism c: Spa(k(x)^∧, Â) → X with c ∘ j = ι_x and c(s) = y is the same as a specialization y of x with k(y)⁺ = i⁻¹(A); likewise over Y with f_v(x, A) = (f(x), A ∩ k(f(x))) (Huber 1.3.10).

Huber 1.3.6: (i) for x ≻ y there is a unique A with support x and centre y (from Huber 1.1.10(iii)); (ii) on an affinoid Z = Spa(B, B⁺) with g induced by φ: B → k(x)^∧, (x, A) has a centre with respect to g if and only if φ(B⁺) ⊆ Â, and then the centre is unique (universal property of Spa, Huber 1994, Proposition 2.1, anchor Layer 5).
acceptance: (x, k(x)⁺) has exactly one centre on X, namely x itself.
On D, at the Gauss point x_G, the valuation ring A_a (preimage of the valuation ring of k(T) at T = a, a ∈ k) has exactly one centre (the type-5 point in direction a), while A_∞ has none.

nodes.title: Valuative criterion for separatedness (Huber 1.3.7)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of analytic adic spaces which is quasi-separated and locally of weakly finite type, and assume X is covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings (for instance X locally noetherian), so that X ×_Y X and the affinoid products U₁ ×_V U₂ exist (R0/fibre-products-existence (b), R0/diagonal-locally-closed). Then f is separated if and only if for every (x, A) ∈ X_v (R0/adic-valuation-rings-and-centres) and every y ∈ Y there is at most one centre z of (x, A) on X with f(z) = y (Huber 1996, Proposition 1.3.7); equivalently, at most one centre over each centre y of (x, A) on Y.
hypotheses: X, Y analytic
f quasi-separated (equivalently the diagonal Δ_f is quasi-compact)
f locally of weakly finite type
X covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings (e.g. X locally noetherian), as in R0/diagonal-locally-closed
proofSteps: (⇒) Let z₁, z₂ be centres of (x, A) with f(z₁) = f(z₂) = y. Choose open affinoids U₁ ∋ z₁, U₂ ∋ z₂, V ∋ y with f(U_i) ⊆ V and O_X(U_i) topologically of finite type over O_Y(V). By Huber 1.3.6(ii) (api isCentre_iff_of_isAffinoid of R0/adic-valuation-rings-and-centres) Δ_v(x, A) has a centre z on the affinoid U₁ ×_V U₂ ⊆ X ×_Y X (R0/affinoid-fibre-product); p_i(z) is a centre of (x, A) on U_i, so z_i = p_i(z) by uniqueness on U_i. z is a specialization of Δ(x) and Δ(X) is closed (R0/separated-morphism), so z ∈ Δ(X) and z₁ = z₂.

(⇐) Δ_f is quasi-compact (f quasi-separated), so Δ(X) ∩ W is pro-constructible in every quasi-compact open W of X ×_Y X (R0/spectral-map-image-proconstructible); by R0/proconstructible-closure-specialization it suffices to show Δ(X) is stable under specialization.

Let x' ∈ Δ(X) specialize to y' ∈ X ×_Y X. By Huber 1.3.6(i) (api existsUnique_of_specializes) there is a valuation ring A of X ×_Y X with support x' and centre y'; p₁(y') and p₂(y') are centres of (p₁)_v(A) = (p₂)_v(A) ∈ X_v over the same point of Y, so p₁(y') = p₂(y') by hypothesis. Choose an open affinoid U ∋ p₁(y') over an affinoid V with O_X(U) topologically of finite type over O_Y(V); then y' ∈ p₁⁻¹(U) ∩ p₂⁻¹(U) = U ×_V U, and Δ(X) ∩ (U ×_V U) = Δ(U) is closed in U ×_V U (R0/diagonal-locally-closed), so y' ∈ Δ(X).
acceptance: For the unit disc with doubled origin X → Spa(K, K°) (R0/separated-morphism, test IsSeparated_test_doubledOrigin) uniqueness of centres fails, matching non-separatedness.
Mathlib's IsSeparated.eq_valuativeCriterion is the scheme analogue: separated = uniqueness part of the valuative criterion + quasi-separated.

Used for (⇐): a pro-constructible subset stable under specialization is closed.

nodes.title: Valuative criterion for universal specialization (Huber 1.3.8)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of analytic adic spaces, locally of weakly finite type, and x₀ ∈ X. Then f is universally specializing at x₀ (R0/universally-specializing-morphism) if and only if, for every valuation ring A of k(x₀) with A ⊆ k(x₀)⁺, every centre of (x₀, A) on Y is the image of a centre of (x₀, A) on X.
hypotheses: X, Y analytic
f locally of weakly finite type
x₀ fixed; the criterion is pointwise
proofSteps: (⇒) Let y be a centre of (x₀, A) on Y, given by c: Spa(k(x₀)^∧, Â) → Y extending f ∘ ι_{x₀}. c is adic (Y analytic). Spa(k(x₀)^∧, Â) is covered by a stably sheafy affinoid (k(x₀)^∧ is a complete nonarchimedean field, hence strongly noetherian: R0/nonarchimedean-field-strongly-noetherian), so X' = X ×_Y Spa(k(x₀)^∧, Â) exists (R0/fibre-products-existence (b)). The pair (ι_{x₀}, j) defines a point x₀' of X' over x₀ whose image is the generic point of Spa(k(x₀)^∧, Â); universal specialization lifts the specialization to the closed point s to a specialization x₁' of x₀' over s, and the image z of x₁' in X is a specialization of x₀ with f(z) = y which is a centre of (x₀, A) (Huber's 'Obviously z is a center of (x, A)'; via api isCentre_iff_specializes of R0/adic-valuation-rings-and-centres).

(⇐) Let g: Y' → Y be adic, X' = X ×_Y Y' (as in the definition of universal specialization), x₀' ∈ X' over x₀ and y' a specialization of y₀' = f'(x₀'). Choose a valuation ring A' of k(x₀') with A' ⊆ k(x₀')⁺ and i⁻¹(A' ∩ k(y₀')) = k(y')⁺, i: k(y') → k(y₀') (extension of valuation rings along k(y₀') ⊆ k(x₀'), Huber (1.1.14)(c)-(e); Mathlib LocalSubring.exists_le_valuationSubring); then y' is a centre of f'_v(x₀', A').

Put (x₀, A) = g'_v(x₀', A') ∈ X_v and y = g(y'); y is a centre of f_v(x₀, A), so by hypothesis (x₀, A) has a centre x ∈ X with f(x) = y. Choose open affinoids U ∋ x, V ∋ y, V' ∋ y' with f(U) ⊆ V, g(V') ⊆ V and O_X(U) topologically of finite type over O_Y(V); then x₀' ∈ U ×_V V' (an affinoid, R0/affinoid-fibre-product) and, since A' contains the images of O⁺_X(U) and O⁺_{Y'}(V'), it contains the image of O⁺(U ×_V V') (integral closure of the completed image of the plus rings, R0/completed-tensor-product), so (x₀', A') has a centre x' on U ×_V V' (Huber 1.3.6(ii)). f'(x') is a centre of f'_v(x₀', A') on V', hence f'(x') = y' by uniqueness of centres on the affinoid V'.
acceptance: For the closed disc D → Spa(K, K°) the criterion fails at the Gauss point with A = A_∞ (R0/adic-valuation-rings-and-centres, test ValuationRing_test_gaussPoint), so D → Spa(K, K°) is not universally specializing at x_G.
Mathlib's universallyClosed_eq_universallySpecializing and ValuativeCriterion.Existence are the scheme analogues.

nodes.title: Valuative criterion for partial properness and properness of analytic adic spaces (Huber 1.3.9)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of analytic adic spaces which is quasi-separated and locally of +weakly finite type, with X covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings (for instance X locally noetherian; needed for X ×_Y X, as in R0/valuative-criterion-separated). Then f is partially proper (R0/partially-proper-morphism) if and only if for every (x, A) ∈ X_v and every centre y of (x, A) on Y there is exactly one centre z of (x, A) on X with f(z) = y. If moreover f is of +weakly finite type (in particular quasi-compact), the same condition is equivalent to f being proper (R0/universally-closed-and-proper-morphism). Huber's Lemma 1.3.10 rephrases the condition as the unique extension of morphisms along Spa(K, K⁺) → Spa(K, K'⁺) for affinoid fields sharing the field K; the X_v form stated here is the declaration.
hypotheses: X, Y analytic adic spaces (the source proves the criterion only in this case)
f quasi-separated and locally of +weakly finite type; for the proper version f of +weakly finite type
X covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings (e.g. locally noetherian), the hypothesis under which the packet constructs X ×_Y X
proofSteps: Uniqueness of centres ⇔ separated: R0/valuative-criterion-separated (f is quasi-separated and locally of weakly finite type).
Existence of centres at every point ⇔ universally specializing: R0/valuative-criterion-specializing applied at each x₀ ∈ X.
Partially proper = locally +weakly finite type + separated + universally specializing (R0/partially-proper-morphism); combine the two steps.
Proper version: proper ⇔ partially proper and quasi-compact (R0/proper-iff-partially-proper-quasi-compact).
acceptance: Every finite morphism to an analytic adic space satisfies existence and uniqueness of centres, because integral plus rings are contained in every valuation ring containing the base plus ring (R0/finite-morphisms); hence finite ⇒ proper, and quasi-compact partially proper = proper (Huber 1.3.4).

Concrete instance: the closed unit disc D → Spa(K, K°) fails existence at (x_G, A_∞); the projective line P¹ → Spa(K, K°) satisfies existence and uniqueness; the open unit disc satisfies both and is partially proper but not quasi-compact.
For analytic adic spaces the criterion can be phrased with S = Spa(K, K⁺) → T = Spa(K, K'⁺), (K, K⁺) and (K, K'⁺) affinoid fields sharing the field K (Huber 1.3.10).

sources.match: Both parts of the node, with Huber's hypotheses (quasi-separated; locally of +weakly finite type, resp. of +weakly finite type; analytic).
The morphism form of the criterion mentioned in the statement and in acceptance.
Same shape (valuative criterion with unique lifts; proper = partially proper + quasi-compact) for v-sheaves.

nodes.title: Proper equals partially proper and quasi-compact (Huber 1.3.4)
nodes.statement: A morphism f: X → Y of adic spaces is proper if and only if it is partially proper and quasi-compact.
hypotheses: f: X → Y any morphism of adic spaces (no analyticity hypothesis)
proofSteps: (⇒) Of +weakly finite type means quasi-compact and locally of +weakly finite type (R0/finite-type-morphism-classes); universally closed implies universally specializing because a closed continuous map is specializing (Mathlib IsClosedMap.specializingMap), applied to every adic base change.
(⇐) Let g: Y' → Y be adic and f': X' → Y' the base change; f' is quasi-compact (R0/base-change-stability (vi)), adic (R0/base-change-stability (ii)) and specializing (universal specialization).

A quasi-compact specializing morphism is closed (Huber's proof of 1.3.4): closedness is local on Y', so take Y' affinoid (spectral, anchor Layer 2); X' is covered by finitely many affinoids U_i with f'|U_i: U_i → Y' a spectral map (Spa of an adic ring homomorphism, anchor Layer 2). For Z ⊆ X' closed, each Z ∩ U_i is pro-constructible (TauCeti IsClosed.isProConstructible), so f'(Z) = ⋃ f'(Z ∩ U_i) is pro-constructible in Y' (R0/spectral-map-image-proconstructible, TauCeti Set.Finite.isProConstructible_biUnion).

f'(Z) is stable under specialization (f' specializing, Z closed), so it is closed (R0/proconstructible-closure-specialization). Hence f is universally closed; with separatedness and +weakly finite type, f is proper.
acceptance: Open unit disc: partially proper, not quasi-compact, not proper. Closed unit disc: quasi-compact, not partially proper, not proper. P¹: proper.
Scheme analogue: Mathlib universallyClosed_eq_universallySpecializing (universally closed = universally specializing + quasi-compact).

nodes.title: The space of valuation rings of a qcqs analytic adic space is spectral (Huber 1.3.12)
nodes.statement: Let X be a quasi-compact quasi-separated analytic adic space. Then X_v, with the topology generated by the sets D(U, h) (R0/adic-valuation-rings-and-centres), is a spectral space, and for every quasi-compact open U ⊆ X and every h ∈ O_X(U) the subset D(U, h) of X_v is quasi-compact (Huber 1996, Lemma 1.3.12). Consequently the projection p: X_v → X, (x, A) ↦ x, is a spectral map (p⁻¹(U) = D(U, 1)).
hypotheses: X analytic, quasi-compact and quasi-separated
proofSteps: Let X_v^♯ be X_v with the topology generated by the sets D(U, h) and X_v ∖ D(U, h), U ⊆ X quasi-compact open, h ∈ O_X(U). These sets are clopen in X_v^♯ and generate the topology of X_v (every open of X is a union of quasi-compact opens); X_v is T0 because k(x) is the residue field of O_{X,x}, so A is determined by the germs h with h(x) ∈ A. By the patch criterion (TauCeti spectralSpace_of_isClopen_generateFrom, Wedhorn 3.31; Huber cites [Ho, Prop. 7]) it suffices to show that X_v^♯ is quasi-compact; the D(U, h) are then quasi-compact open in X_v.

Let X^c be X with the constructible topology (quasi-compact since X is spectral) and p: X_v^♯ → X^c the projection; p is continuous. For x ∈ X, p⁻¹(x) is homeomorphic to the Riemann–Zariski space of the residue field of k(x)⁺ (valuation rings of k(x) inside k(x)⁺, Huber (1.1.14)(c)) with its constructible topology, hence quasi-compact (spectrality of Spa of a discrete field, TauCeti ValuationSpectrum.spectralSpace_spa_of_pairOfDefinition).

p is closed: closed subsets of X_v^♯ are intersections of finite unions of sets D(L; U, E, F) = {(x, A) : x ∈ L, e(x) ∉ A (e ∈ E), f(x) ∈ A (f ∈ F)} (L constructible, U quasi-compact open constructible ⊇ L, E, F ⊆ O_X(U) finite), and since the fibres are quasi-compact it suffices that each p(D) is closed in X^c. Huber's formula (2): with P the set of polynomials a(Y, X) ∈ ℤ[Y₁..Y_m][X₁..X_n] having a coefficient a_μ(Y) = 1 at a multi-index μ that strictly dominates, in total degree and in each variable, every other monomial with nonzero coefficient, p(D) = {x ∈ L : |f_i(x)| ≤ 1 for all i, |a(f, e)(x)| ≥ 1 for all a ∈ P}, a constructible-closed set. The inclusion ⊆ is direct; for ⊇ one finds a valuation ring B of the residue field of k(x)⁺ containing the images of the f_i and with the images of 1/e_j in its maximal ideal (the ring they generate is proper by the P-inequalities, then Chevalley extension, Mathlib LocalSubring.exists_le_valuationSubring) and takes A = λ⁻¹(B).
A continuous closed map with quasi-compact fibres onto a quasi-compact space has quasi-compact source, so X_v^♯ is quasi-compact.
acceptance: For X = Spa(K, K°) with K a rank-one field and residue field k, X_v is the Riemann–Zariski space of valuation rings of k (with the generic point the trivial valuation ring k), which is spectral.

nodes.title: Closures of quasi-compact sets under partially proper morphisms (Huber 1.3.13)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a partially proper morphism of analytic adic spaces with Y quasi-compact and quasi-separated, X being covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings (for instance X locally noetherian; the setting in which the packet builds X ×_Y X). Then the closure in X of every quasi-compact subset of X is quasi-compact (Huber 1996, Lemma 1.3.13).
hypotheses: X, Y analytic
f partially proper
Y quasi-compact and quasi-separated
X covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings (e.g. locally noetherian)
proofSteps: f is quasi-separated: f is separated, so Δ_f(X) is closed, and Δ_f is a closed embedding into an open subspace (R0/diagonal-locally-closed), hence a closed embedding and quasi-compact; so the valuative criterion R0/separated-proper-partially-proper applies, and X is quasi-separated because Y is.

Reduce to T ⊆ X a quasi-compact open (enlarge T; T is then qcqs) and Y affinoid (Y is covered by finitely many affinoids and closures can be computed over each). Put S = {(x, A) ∈ T_v : (x, A) has a centre on Y} = {(x, A) ∈ T_v : h(x) ∈ A for all h ∈ O⁺_Y(Y)} (Huber 1.3.6(ii)); it is pro-constructible in the spectral space T_v (R0/valuation-ring-space-spectral, the sets D(T, h) being quasi-compact open), hence quasi-compact.

Each (x, A) ∈ S has a unique centre c(x, A) on X (R0/separated-proper-partially-proper with 1.3.6(ii)). c: S → X is continuous: for U ⊆ X open affinoid with O⁺_X(U) the smallest ring of integral elements containing a finite E and the image of O⁺_Y(Y) (f locally of +weakly finite type), c⁻¹(U) = {(x, A) ∈ S : x ∈ U, e(x) ∈ A for all e ∈ E} is open. Hence c(S) is quasi-compact.

By Huber 1.3.6(i) c(S) is exactly the set of specializations in X of points of T; since T is pro-constructible, this is the closure of T (R0/proconstructible-closure-specialization). So the closure of T is quasi-compact.
acceptance: For the open unit disc B → Spa(K, K°) and T = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|}, the closure of T in B is T together with its specializations and is quasi-compact.

sources.match: The statement (hypotheses match) and the proof followed by the proof steps.

nodes.title: The diagonal of a separated morphism is a closed embedding
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of adic spaces that is locally of weakly finite type (R0/finite-type-morphism-classes), with X covered by open affinoids Spa(B, B⁺) with B complete and stably sheafy (for instance X locally noetherian), so that X ×_Y X exists (R0/fibre-products-existence, case (b); f is adic). Then f is separated (R0/separated-morphism: the image of Δ_f is closed) if and only if the diagonal Δ_f: X → X ×_Y X is a closed embedding (R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings). The key step is general: a locally closed embedding h: T → Z of adic spaces whose image h(|T|) is closed in |Z| is a closed embedding.
hypotheses: f locally of weakly finite type
X covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings
proofSteps: (⇐) A closed embedding is a homeomorphism onto the closed set {z : 𝓘_z ≠ O_{Z,z}} (R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings), so the image of Δ_f is closed.
(⇒) By R0/diagonal-locally-closed, Δ_f factors as a closed embedding δ: X → W into the open subspace W ⊆ X ×_Y X (the union of the U ×_V U over affinoid charts) followed by the inclusion of W.

Locally closed with closed image ⇒ closed (the argument of Zavyalov, Lemma B.6.14): let 𝓘_W ⊆ O_W be the admissible ideal sheaf of δ and let 𝓘 be O on the open complement C of the closed set Δ_f(|X|). On W ∩ C the stalks of δ_*O_X vanish, so 𝓘_W = O there, and the two ideal sheaves glue to an ideal sheaf 𝓘 ⊆ O_{X ×_Y X} (gluing of sheaves along an open cover, anchor Layer 5).

𝓘 is admissible, since admissibility is affinoid-local: on affinoids of W it is the condition for 𝓘_W, and on affinoids Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ C the ideal is A itself with A/A = 0 sheafy. Hence V(𝓘) = δ(X) and Δ_f is X ×_Y X-isomorphic to the inclusion of V(𝓘), a closed embedding.
acceptance: For the closed unit disc X = Spa(K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩) over Spa(K, K°), Δ_X is the closed embedding of X into the closed bidisc cut out by the ideal (T ⊗ 1 − 1 ⊗ T) of K⟨T₁, T₂⟩.
For the closed disc with doubled origin, Δ is a locally closed embedding whose image is not closed; it is not a closed embedding, and the space is not separated.

nodes.title: Closed embeddings are proper
nodes.statement: Let i: Z → X be a closed embedding of adic spaces (R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings), with X covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings. Then i is proper (R0/universally-closed-and-proper-morphism): it is quasi-compact and locally of +weakly finite type (R0/plus-weakly-finite-type), separated (R0/separated-morphism) and universally closed (R0/universally-closed-morphism); for every adic morphism g: X' → X from an adic space X' covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings, the base change Z ×_X X' → X' is the closed embedding V(𝓘·O_{X'}) → X'. No analyticity of X is assumed (Huber's route through finite morphisms, 1.4.5(ii),(iii), needs an analytic target in this blueprint, R0/finite-morphisms).
hypotheses: i a closed embedding
X covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings
proofSteps: Finiteness conditions: over an affinoid Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X where 𝓘 is admissible, i is Spa(A/J) → Spa(A) for the quotient pair A/J (Tau Ceti Huber.Pair.quotient): A → A/J is a surjective open continuous homomorphism, hence topologically of finite type with no variables, and the plus ring of A/J is the integral closure of the image of A⁺ (E = ∅ in R0/plus-weakly-finite-type). The preimage Spa(A/J) of the affinoid Spa(A) is quasi-compact, so i is quasi-compact and locally of +weakly finite type, hence of +weakly finite type.

Separated: i is a monomorphism (uniqueness in the universal property of V(𝓘), API AdicSpace.closedSubspace.lift of R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings), so (id_Z, id_Z) is a kernel pair of i (Mathlib CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.id_of_mono): Z ×_X Z = Z and Δ_i is an isomorphism, whose image is all of |Z ×_X Z|, a closed set.

Universally closed: for adic g: X' → X the base change is V(𝓘·O_{X'}) → X' (API AdicSpace.closedSubspace.pullback of R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings), again a closed embedding; its underlying map is a homeomorphism onto a closed subset, hence a closed map.
acceptance: The origin Spa(K, K°) → Spa(K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩), cut out by (T), is proper; so is the non-reduced point V(T²).

The open embedding of the open unit disc into the closed unit disc is not proper: it is not quasi-compact and its image is not closed. A locally closed embedding is proper exactly when it is a closed embedding (a proper one has closed image, R0/separated-diagonal-closed-embedding).

nodes.title: Universally closed, separated and proper morphisms are stable under adic base change
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of adic spaces locally of weakly finite type and g: Y' → Y an adic morphism (R0/adic-morphism), where all adic spaces involved are covered by open affinoids Spa(B, B⁺) with B complete and stably sheafy (for instance locally noetherian adic spaces, R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space with R0/noetherian-type-stably-sheafy), so that the fibre products below exist by R0/fibre-products-existence. Let f': X' = X ×_Y Y' → Y' be the base change (R0/fibre-products-existence, case (b)). If f is universally closed (resp. separated, resp. quasi-compact, resp. proper), then so is f' (R0/universally-closed-morphism, R0/separated-morphism, R0/universally-closed-and-proper-morphism).
hypotheses: f locally of weakly finite type, g adic
all spaces covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings
proofSteps: f' is locally of weakly finite type and the projection X' → X is adic (R0/base-change-stability (ii)).

Universally closed: for an adic h: Y'' → Y', the composite g ∘ h is adic (composites of adic morphisms are adic, R0/adic-morphism), and pasting the cartesian squares (Mathlib CategoryTheory.IsPullback.paste_horiz, CategoryTheory.IsPullback.of_right) identifies X' ×_{Y'} Y'' → Y'' with the base change X ×_Y Y'' → Y'' of f along g ∘ h, which is a closed map because f is universally closed.

Separated: by the same pasting, Δ_{f'} is the base change of Δ_f along the canonical morphism X' ×_{Y'} X' → X ×_Y X; Δ_f is a closed embedding (R0/separated-diagonal-closed-embedding) and closed embeddings are stable under base change (API AdicSpace.closedSubspace.pullback of R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings), so Δ_{f'} is a closed embedding and its image is closed.
Quasi-compact: R0/base-change-stability (vi). Locally of +weakly finite type: R0/base-change-stability (iii). Hence proper passes to f'.
acceptance: The closed unit disc Spa(K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩) → Spa(K, K°) is separated and quasi-compact, and its base change along Spa(L, L°) → Spa(K, K°) for a complete extension L/K is Spa(L⟨T⟩, L°⟨T⟩) → Spa(L, L°), again separated and quasi-compact.

Adicness of g is needed: the base change of the quasi-compact Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) → Spa(ℤ_p, ℤ_p) along the non-adic Spa(ℤ_p⟦T⟧) → Spa(ℤ_p) is the open unit disc over ℚ_p, which is not quasi-compact over Spa(ℤ_p⟦T⟧) (R0/base-change-stability).

nodes.title: Composites of universally closed, separated and proper morphisms
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y and g: Y → Z be morphisms of adic spaces locally of weakly finite type, where all adic spaces involved are covered by open affinoids Spa(B, B⁺) with B complete and stably sheafy (for instance locally noetherian adic spaces, R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space with R0/noetherian-type-stably-sheafy), so that the fibre products below exist by R0/fibre-products-existence. If f and g are universally closed (resp. separated, resp. quasi-compact, resp. proper), then so is g ∘ f.
hypotheses: f, g locally of weakly finite type
all spaces covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings
proofSteps: g ∘ f is locally of weakly finite type (composites, R0/finite-type-morphism-classes) and locally of +weakly finite type if f and g are (composites, R0/plus-weakly-finite-type); preimages of quasi-compact opens under f and g are quasi-compact, so quasi-compactness composes.

Universally closed: for an adic Z' → Z, the base change Y' = Y ×_Z Z' → Y is adic (R0/base-change-stability (v)) and pasting (Mathlib CategoryTheory.IsPullback.paste_horiz, CategoryTheory.IsPullback.of_right) identifies X ×_Z Z' with X ×_Y Y'; the base change of g ∘ f is the composite of the base change of f along Y' → Y and of g along Z' → Z, both closed maps, and a composite of closed maps is closed (the argument of Stacks Tag 01W3).

Separated: Δ_{g∘f} is the composite of Δ_f with the canonical morphism j: X ×_Y X → X ×_Z X, and j is the base change of Δ_g: Y → Y ×_Z Y along X ×_Z X → Y ×_Z Y (pasting). Δ_g is a closed embedding (R0/separated-diagonal-closed-embedding), so j is a closed embedding (API AdicSpace.closedSubspace.pullback of R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings) and a closed map; hence Δ_{g∘f}(|X|) = j(Δ_f(|X|)) is closed.
Proper: combine the three clauses with R0/universally-closed-and-proper-morphism.
acceptance: For a finite extension L/K and a closed embedding X → Spa(L, L°) (for instance the point itself), X → Spa(L, L°) → Spa(K, K°) is proper: a closed embedding followed by the finite, hence proper, Spa(L, L°) → Spa(K, K°) (R0/finite-morphisms).
The converse fails: the origin Spa(K, K°) → D of the closed unit disc D is proper, D → Spa(K, K°) is not, and the composite is the identity of Spa(K, K°), which is proper.

nodes.title: Cancellation: g ∘ h proper and g separated imply h proper
nodes.statement: Let h: X → Y and g: Y → Z be morphisms of adic spaces with g ∘ h locally of weakly finite type and g separated (R0/separated-morphism; in particular g is locally of weakly finite type), where all adic spaces involved are covered by open affinoids Spa(B, B⁺) with B complete and stably sheafy (for instance locally noetherian adic spaces, R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space with R0/noetherian-type-stably-sheafy), so that the fibre products below exist by R0/fibre-products-existence. If g ∘ h is universally closed (resp. proper), then h is universally closed (resp. proper); in particular h(|X|) is closed in |Y|. This is the adic form of Stacks Tag 01W6 (Mathlib's AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper.of_comp for schemes).
hypotheses: g separated
g ∘ h locally of weakly finite type
all spaces covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings
proofSteps: h is locally of weakly finite type (R0/finite-type-morphism-classes: if g ∘ h is, so is h, Wedhorn 6.33(2)); if g ∘ h is locally of +weakly finite type so is h, because O_Z⁺(W) → O_X⁺(U) factors through O_Y⁺(V), so the integral closure of the image of O_Y⁺(V)[E ∪ O_X(U)°°] lies between that of O_Z⁺(W)[E ∪ O_X(U)°°] = O_X⁺(U) and O_X⁺(U) (R0/plus-weakly-finite-type).

The graph Γ_h = (id_X, h): X → X ×_Z Y is the base change of Δ_g: Y → Y ×_Z Y along h ×_Z id_Y: X ×_Z Y → Y ×_Z Y (pasting, Mathlib CategoryTheory.IsPullback.paste_horiz, CategoryTheory.IsPullback.of_right); Δ_g is a closed embedding (R0/separated-diagonal-closed-embedding), hence so is Γ_h (API AdicSpace.closedSubspace.pullback of R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings), and Γ_h is proper (R0/closed-embedding-proper).

The projection pr₂: X ×_Z Y → Y is the base change of g ∘ h along g, which is adic (locally of weakly finite type, R0/finite-type-morphism-classes); so pr₂ is universally closed (resp. proper) by R0/proper-base-change.
h = pr₂ ∘ Γ_h is universally closed (resp. proper) by R0/proper-comp.
acceptance: A section s: Y → X of a separated morphism p: X → Y is proper, since p ∘ s = id_Y is proper; in particular it is a closed embedding onto a closed subset (the zero section of the closed disc over Spa(K, K°) is the origin).

Separatedness of g is needed: let Y be the adic projective line over K (two closed unit discs glued along the unit circle) with its classical point ∞ doubled, and h the inclusion of one copy of the projective line. Then g ∘ h is the proper structure map of the projective line, but h(|X|) = |Y| ∖ {∞₂} is not closed, so h is not universally closed.

nodes.title: Universal closedness descends along surjections
nodes.statement: Let S be an adic space, p: X → S and q: Y → S morphisms locally of weakly finite type and π: X → Y a surjective morphism with q ∘ π = p, where all adic spaces involved are covered by open affinoids Spa(B, B⁺) with B complete and stably sheafy (for instance locally noetherian adic spaces, R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space with R0/noetherian-type-stably-sheafy), so that the fibre products below exist by R0/fibre-products-existence. If p is universally closed (R0/universally-closed-morphism), then q is universally closed. If moreover q is separated, quasi-compact and locally of +weakly finite type, then q is proper (R0/universally-closed-and-proper-morphism). Surjectivity of π need not be assumed after base change: it is preserved by every adic base change (proof step 2).
hypotheses: π surjective on underlying points
p, q locally of weakly finite type
all spaces covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings
proofSteps: For an adic S' → S put X' = X ×_S S' and Y' = Y ×_S S' (R0/fibre-products-existence, case (b)). The projection Y' → Y is adic (R0/base-change-stability (v)) and π is locally of weakly finite type (R0/finite-type-morphism-classes, since q ∘ π is), so X ×_Y Y' exists, and pasting (Mathlib CategoryTheory.IsPullback.paste_horiz, CategoryTheory.IsPullback.of_right) identifies it with X', the base change π': X' → Y' of π corresponding to the projection.

π' is surjective: for y' ∈ |Y'| with image y ∈ |Y| choose x ∈ |X| with π(x) = y; the compatible pair (x, y') lifts to a point of X ×_Y Y' (R0/fibre-product-points: the comparison map to the set-theoretic fibre product is surjective).

For a closed T ⊆ |Y'|, q'(T) = q'(π'(π'⁻¹(T))) = p'(π'⁻¹(T)) by surjectivity (Mathlib Set.image_preimage_eq), which is closed because p' is closed; so q' is closed for every adic S' → S (the argument of Stacks Tag 03GN).
The proper case is the definition of properness.
acceptance: Chow's lemma step of R1/analytification-separated-proper (ii): X'^ad → Y^ad proper and π^ad: X'^ad → X^ad surjective give X^ad → Y^ad universally closed.
Surjectivity is needed: the empty adic space is proper over Spa(K, K°) and maps to the closed disc, which is not universally closed over Spa(K, K°).

nodes.title: Finite morphism of complete Huber pairs
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) and (B, B⁺) be complete Huber pairs (Tau Ceti Huber.Pair on complete Hausdorff Huber rings A, B) and φ: (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) a morphism of Huber pairs (tauceti Huber.Pair.Hom: continuous, φ(A⁺) ⊆ B⁺). The morphism φ is finite if it is of topologically finite type as a morphism of affinoid rings (Huber 1994, §3: φ factors through a quotient mapping A⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩_M → B, i.e. a surjective continuous open ring map with B⁺ the integral closure of the image of the plus ring) and the ring maps A → B and A⁺ → B⁺ are integral (Huber 1996, 1.4.2). Consequences: B⁺ is the integral closure of φ(A⁺) in B (always); B is a finite A-module carrying the natural A-module topology when A is Tate (Zavyalov, Quotients, B.2.9 and B.3.4). Huber (1.4.2) states these consequences under his standing noetherian assumption (1.1.1), referring to [Hu4, 3.12.10] (unread); outside the Tate case they are not claimed here. For complete Tate pairs, φ is finite if and only if A → B is module-finite (Mathlib RingHom.Finite) and A⁺ → B⁺ is integral.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺), (B, B⁺) complete (Hausdorff) Huber pairs
φ a morphism of Huber pairs
proofSteps: Definition as stated.
B⁺ = integral closure of φ(A⁺): ⊆ because B⁺ is integral over φ(A⁺); ⊇ because B⁺ is integrally closed in B and contains φ(A⁺) (tauceti Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements).

Tate case equivalence: finite ring map + integral plus ⇒ topologically finite type (Zavyalov B.2.8, using the universal property of A⟨X⟩, Huber 1994 Lemma 3.5(i)); topologically finite type + integral plus ⇒ finite ring map (Zavyalov B.2.9: rings of definition A₀ → B₀ finite by reduction mod a pseudo-uniformiser and completeness).
Natural topology: B is complete and first countable, hence (open mapping, Huber 1994 Lemma 2.4(i); tauceti Huber.IsTateRing.isModuleTopology) carries the natural A-module topology (Zavyalov B.3.4).
acceptance: (Q_p, Z_p) → (Q_p(√p), Z_p[√p]) is finite.
(K, K⁺) → (K, K°) with K⁺ ⊊ K° is not finite although K → K is.

nodes.title: The Huber pair of a finite algebra over a noetherian affinoid ring
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Huber pair such that A is a complete noetherian Tate ring or has a noetherian ring of definition (for instance A strongly noetherian Tate, or an affinoid algebra over a complete nonarchimedean field). Let ψ: A → C be a finite A-algebra (C commutative and finitely generated as an A-module). Equip C with the natural A-module topology (the finest topology making C a topological A-module; Mathlib moduleTopology A C; Huber 1994, p. 524) and let C⁺ be the integral closure of ψ(A⁺) in C. Then: (i) C is a complete Hausdorff Huber ring, Tate if A is, every A-submodule of C is closed, and ψ is continuous; (ii) C⁺ is a ring of integral elements, so Huber.Pair.finiteAlgebra (C, C⁺) is a complete Huber pair; (iii) ψ is a finite morphism of Huber pairs (R0/finite-huber-pair-hom); (iv) universal property: for every complete Huber pair (D, D⁺) with a morphism χ: (A, A⁺) → (D, D⁺), morphisms of Huber pairs (C, C⁺) → (D, D⁺) under (A, A⁺) are exactly the A-algebra maps C → D; (v) if A is strongly noetherian Tate, so is C; (vi) Spa(C, C⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) is a finite morphism of adic spaces, and for A strongly noetherian Tate every finite morphism X → Spa(A, A⁺) is isomorphic over Spa(A, A⁺) to one of this form, with C = O_X(X). Convention: the noetherian hypothesis is part of the construction; for a non-noetherian complete Tate ring A a finite A-algebra C = A/J with J not closed has a non-Hausdorff natural topology, so no complete Huber pair structure exists on C itself.
hypotheses: A complete noetherian Tate ring, or A with a noetherian ring of definition
C finite A-algebra; natural A-module topology; C⁺ = integral closure of ψ(A⁺)
proofSteps: Topological ring: C with the module topology is a topological ring because C is module-finite (Mathlib IsModuleTopology.isTopologicalRing); ψ is continuous (IsModuleTopology.continuous_of_linearMap on A → C).

Completeness, Hausdorffness and closedness of submodules: Huber 1994 Lemma 2.3(ii) (noetherian ring of definition) and Lemma 2.4(ii) (complete noetherian Tate); in Tau Ceti tauceti TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.t2Space_moduleTopology, TauCeti.completeSpace_moduleTopology, TauCeti.Huber.isClosed_of_isNoetherian.

Huber ring: choose A-module generators 1 = c₀, c₁, …, c_m of C with structure constants c_i c_j = Σ a_{ijk} c_k; after multiplying the c_i (i ≥ 1) by a power of a pseudo-uniformiser (resp. of an element of the ideal of definition) all a_{ijk} lie in a ring of definition A₀, and C₀ = Σ A₀ c_i is an open bounded subring with the I·C₀-adic topology.

Ring of integral elements: after replacing each cᵢ (i ≥ 1) by ϖcᵢ the structure constants lie in ϖA₀ ⊆ A°° ⊆ A⁺, so R = ψ(A⁺)[c₁,…,c_m] is a subring of C that is finite over ψ(A⁺), hence integral over ψ(A⁺), and open (it contains ψ(ϖA₀)-multiples of the generators, hence ϖ²C₀). R ⊆ C° (bounded generators, adic ψ). Its integral closure equals the integral closure C⁺ of ψ(A⁺), which is therefore a ring of integral elements by tauceti TauCeti.Huber.Pair.isRingOfIntegralElements_integralClosure (integral closure of an open subring contained in the power-bounded subring).
Finite morphism: A → C module-finite and A⁺ → C⁺ integral; topologically finite type by the Tate-case lemma (Zavyalov B.2.8) or directly from the surjection A⟨X₁..X_m⟩ → C, X_i ↦ c_i.
Universal property: an A-algebra map C → D is continuous (source has the module topology) and maps C⁺ into D⁺ because D⁺ is integrally closed in D and contains χ(A⁺).
Strong noetherianity: C is topologically of finite type over A, so Huber 1994 Corollary 3.4(ii) applies.
Finite morphisms to Spa(A, A⁺) are of this form: Zavyalov B.2.18.

nodes.title: Finiteness from monic relations with topologically nilpotent values (Huber 1.4.3)
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) be a morphism of complete Tate Huber pairs which is of topologically finite type, presented by a quotient mapping A⟨T₁,…,Tₙ⟩ → B with images t₁,…,tₙ ∈ B⁺. Then the morphism is finite (R0/finite-huber-pair-hom) if and only if for each i there is a monic polynomial pᵢ ∈ A⁺[X] such that pᵢ(tᵢ) is topologically nilpotent in B.
hypotheses: A, B complete Tate; the presentation has tᵢ ∈ B⁺
proofSteps: (⇒) If the morphism is finite, B⁺ is integral over A⁺ (R0/finite-huber-pair-hom), so each tᵢ ∈ B⁺ satisfies a monic pᵢ ∈ A⁺[X] with pᵢ(tᵢ) = 0.

(⇐) Choose a ring of definition A₀ ⊆ A⁺ of A containing all coefficients of the pᵢ (a ring of definition inside A⁺ with finitely many power-bounded elements adjoined is still open and bounded) and an ideal of definition I of A₀. B₀ := p(A₀⟨T₁,…,Tₙ⟩) is a ring of definition of B with tᵢ ∈ B₀ and A₀[t₁,…,tₙ] dense in B₀. Since pᵢ(tᵢ) ∈ B°°, some power lies in I·B₀; replacing pᵢ by that power, pᵢ(tᵢ) ∈ I·B₀.

B₀/IB₀ = (A₀/I)[t̄₁,…,t̄ₙ] with each t̄ᵢ integral, so B₀/IB₀ is a finite A₀-module. B₀ is I-adically complete and separated and A₀ is I-adically complete, so lifting generators gives a surjection A₀^k → B₀ (complete Nakayama, Huber's [M, 28.P Lemma]; Mathlib surjective_of_mkQ_comp_surjective). Hence B₀ is finite, in particular integral, over A₀, and B = B₀[1/ϖ] is a finite A-module.

B⁺ is the integral closure of the image of A⟨T⟩⁺, which is the integral closure of A⁺·A₀⟨T⟩ in A⟨T⟩ (the presentation is a quotient mapping of affinoid rings); the image A⁺·B₀ is integral over A⁺, so B⁺ is integral over A⁺. Hence the morphism is finite (R0/finite-huber-pair-hom).
acceptance: For A = K, B = K⟨T⟩/(T² − ϖ) with t = T: p(X) = X² gives p(t) = ϖ topologically nilpotent, so B is finite over K (indeed of dimension 2).

nodes.title: Finite morphisms are proper (Huber 1.4.5(ii))
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a finite morphism of adic spaces (R0/finite-morphism) with Y analytic and covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings (for instance Y locally noetherian; then so is X, its affinoid rings being topologically of finite type over those of Y). Then f is proper (R0/universally-closed-and-proper-morphism). (Huber states 1.4.5(ii) for arbitrary adic spaces, deducing the specializing property from Huber–Knebusch [HK, 2.1.2, 2.1.6]; that general case is recorded as a gap.)
hypotheses: Y analytic (the proof via the valuative criterion 1.3.9 needs analytic spaces; X is then analytic)
Y covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings (needed for X ×_Y X and the valuative criterion as stated in R0/separated-proper-partially-proper)
f finite
proofSteps: Finite ⇒ quasi-compact, and quasi-separated (preimages of affinoids are affinoid, hence quasi-compact quasi-separated spectral spaces; AdicSpaces anchor Layer 2).

Finite ⇒ of +weakly finite type: affinoid-locally B is topologically of finite type over A and B⁺ is the integral closure of A⁺, which equals the integral closure of A⁺[B°°] because B°° ⊆ B⁺ (R0/finite-huber-pair-hom, R0/finite-type-morphism-classes).

Existence and uniqueness of centres: let (x, A) ∈ X_v and y a centre of (x, A) on Y; y and f(x) lie in a common affinoid V = Spa(A', A'⁺) (opens are stable under generalisation) with f⁻¹(V) = Spa(B, B⁺) finite over V. The image of A'⁺ in k(x) lies in A (API 1.3.6 of R0/adic-valuation-rings-and-centres); B⁺ is integral over A'⁺ and valuation rings are integrally closed, so the image of B⁺ lies in A, giving a centre on f⁻¹(V), unique by 1.3.6.
Apply the valuative criterion, proper version (R0/separated-proper-partially-proper).
acceptance: Spa(K⟨T⟩) → Spa(K⟨S⟩), S ↦ T², is proper.
Closed embeddings into analytic spaces are proper (combine with R0/closed-embedding-finite).

A → A/J (completed) is surjective, continuous and open, hence of topologically finite type with n = 0, and integral; the plus ring map is integral by construction. Hence the morphism of pairs is finite (R0/finite-huber-pair-hom; tauceti Huber.Pair.quotient).

nodes.title: Topological nilpotence in a fibre spreads to a rational neighbourhood (Huber 1.4.8)
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) be a morphism of complete Tate Huber pairs with B topologically of finite type over A (as pairs), g = Spa(φ): Spa(B, B⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺), x ∈ Spa(A, A⁺), and B ⊗̂_A k(x) the completion of B ⊗_A K, K the fraction field of A/supp(x) with the valuation topology of x (so that k(x)^∧ = K^∧ and B ⊗̂_A k(x) is the ring of global sections of the fibre Spa(B) ×_{Spa A} Spa κ(x)). Let b ∈ B be an element whose image in B ⊗̂_A k(x) is topologically nilpotent. Then there is a rational subset U ⊆ Spa(A, A⁺) containing x such that the image of b in O(g⁻¹(U)) = B ⊗̂_A O(U) is topologically nilpotent (Huber 1996, Lemma 1.4.8).
hypotheses: A, B complete Tate; B topologically of finite type over A as pairs (Huber's hypothesis; for affinoids of finite type over a strongly noetherian base this follows from Zavyalov B.2.17)
x ∈ Spa(A, A⁺); b topologically nilpotent in B ⊗̂_A k(x)
proofSteps: Setup (Huber): K₀ ⊆ K the valuation ring of x; rings of definition A₀, B₀ with φ(A₀) ⊆ B₀ and image of A₀ in K₀; s ∈ A₀ a topologically nilpotent unit. B ⊗̂_A k(x) is the completion of B ⊗_A K with ring of definition B₀K₀ := im(B₀ ⊗_{A₀} K₀) and ideal of definition s·B₀K₀. Replacing b by a power, the image b' of b in B ⊗_A K lies in s·B₀K₀: b' = s·(b₁ ⊗ e₁/d₁ + … + b_n ⊗ e_n/d_n) with bᵢ ∈ B₀, eᵢ, dᵢ ∈ A, eᵢ/dᵢ ∈ K₀; rescaling by powers of s, 1 ≤ |dᵢ(x)|.

U₁ := ⋂ᵢ R((eᵢ, 1)/dᵢ) ∋ x. With d = ∏ dᵢ, O(g⁻¹(U₁)) is the completion of B_d with ring of definition B' = B₀[eᵢ/dᵢ, 1/dᵢ] and ideal of definition s·B' (R0/completed-tensor-rational-localisation); b'' := s·Σ bᵢ eᵢ/dᵢ ∈ s·B' has the same image as b̄ in B ⊗_A K.

Kernel step (corrected): the kernel of φ: B_d → B ⊗_A K is not supp(x)·B_d in general but {c ∈ B_d : a·c ∈ supp(x)·B_d for some a ∈ A ∖ supp(x)} (B ⊗_A K = (B_d/supp(x)B_d) ⊗_{A/supp(x)} K localises at A/supp(x) ∖ 0). So a·(b̄ − b'') = p₁t₁ + … + p_m t_m with pⱼ ∈ supp(x), tⱼ ∈ B_d, and a ∈ A with a(x) ≠ 0; rescale so that tⱼ ∈ sB' and choose l with |s^l(x)| ≤ |a(x)|.

U := U₁ ∩ ⋂ⱼ R((pⱼ, 1)/1) ∩ R((s^l, 1)/a) contains x (pⱼ(x) = 0, a(x) ≠ 0). On g⁻¹(U) the ring B'' := B'[p₁, …, p_m, s^l/a] is a ring of definition with ideal of definition s·B''. Having rescaled so that tⱼ ∈ s^{l+1}B', b̄ − b'' = (s^l/a)·s^{-l}·Σ pⱼtⱼ ∈ s·B'', hence b̄ ∈ s·B'' and the image of b in O(g⁻¹(U)) is topologically nilpotent.
acceptance: For f the identity of Y and b ∈ A with b(y) = 0 in k(y)^∧, b is topologically nilpotent on the rational neighbourhood {|b| ≤ |ϖ|} of y, where ϖ is a pseudo-uniformiser of A.

nodes.title: Finiteness near a point with proper fibre (Huber 1.4.6-1.4.7)
nodes.statement: Let f: X = Spa(B, B⁺) → Y = Spa(A, A⁺) be a morphism of finite type between analytic affinoid adic spaces whose ring map (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) is topologically of finite type (automatic when A is a strongly noetherian Tate ring, Zavyalov B.2.17; Huber (1.2.1) under his standing assumption). For every y ∈ Y such that the fibre X ×_Y Spa κ(y) → Spa κ(y) (R0/fibre-over-point) is proper, there is an open neighbourhood U of y such that f⁻¹(U) → U is finite. In particular, if f is proper then f is finite; together with R0/finite-morphisms, f is proper iff finite (Huber 1996, Proposition 1.4.6 and Lemma 1.4.7).
hypotheses: X, Y analytic affinoid
f of finite type with (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) topologically of finite type
the fibre over y is proper
proofSteps: Shrink Y to a rational neighbourhood of y with Tate coordinate ring (anchor Layer 2: the analytic locus is covered by rational subsets with Tate rings). Let K = k(y)^∧ with plus ring K⁺ and ideal of definition I of K⁺, Z = X ×_Y Spa κ(y) the fibre (R0/fibre-over-point; affinoid with ring C = B ⊗̂_A K, R0/affinoid-fibre-product, R0/completed-tensor-product, sheafy since K is strongly noetherian, R0/nonarchimedean-field-strongly-noetherian), and C₀ ⊆ C⁺ an open subring topologically of finite type over K⁺ with C⁺ its integral closure.

The scheme morphism g: Spec(C₀/ϖC₀) → Spec(K⁺/ϖK⁺) is proper: properness of the adic fibre is transferred to g by the valuative criterion (Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper.eq_valuativeCriterion; the transfer is Huber's reference [Hu4, 3.12.5], recorded as a gap).
g is affine and proper, hence finite (Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite.iff_isProper_and_isAffineHom; Huber cites EGA IV 18.12.8); by completeness C₀ is finite over K⁺ and K → C is finite.

Choose topological generators tᵢ ∈ B⁺ of B over A; their images in C satisfy monic equations over K⁺; approximate the coefficients by elements of A⁺-localisations near y so that the resulting monic pᵢ(tᵢ) are topologically nilpotent in the fibre; spread this to a rational neighbourhood U (R0/fibre-nilpotence-spreading) and conclude finiteness over U by R0/finiteness-criterion-monic-relations.
If f is proper, every fibre is proper (R0/proper-base-change, the morphism Spa κ(y) → Y being adic); cover Y by the neighbourhoods U and use locality of finiteness on the target (R0/finite-morphism).
acceptance: Instance: for K = C_p, the morphism Spa(K⟨T⟩) → Spa(K⟨S⟩), S ↦ T² (finite) has proper fibres; conversely a proper morphism of finite type between affinoid rigid spaces is finite (the classical statement for affinoids, via R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor).
