nodes.title: Finiteness descends along finite faithfully flat affinoid covers (Huber 1.4.9)
nodes.statement: Let T = Spa(A, A⁺) be an affinoid adic space with A a complete strongly noetherian Tate ring, h: T' → T a finite morphism such that O_{T'}(T') is faithfully flat over A, and f: S → T a morphism of adic spaces locally of finite type, with S' = S ×_T T' → T' its base change (R0/fibre-products-existence (a)). If S' → T' is finite, then f is finite (Huber 1996, Lemma 1.4.9).
hypotheses: T affinoid with A a complete strongly noetherian Tate ring (Huber: T affinoid under his noetherian standing assumption; the strongly noetherian Tate case is the one used, in R0/quasi-finite-and-finiteness-criteria)
h finite with O(T') faithfully flat over A
f locally of finite type
proofSteps: For every affinoid open U ⊆ S, O_{S'}(r⁻¹(U)) = O_S(U) ⊗̂_A O_{T'}(T') = O_S(U) ⊗_A O_{T'}(T') (R0/affinoid-fibre-product; no completion is needed because O(T') is finite over A and O_S(U) is noetherian, R0/finite-algebra-tensor-complete (ii)); it is finite over O_S(U) with its natural topology, so O_S(U) → O_{S'}(r⁻¹(U)) is a topological embedding (strictness of maps of finite modules over complete noetherian Tate rings, Huber 1994 Lemma 2.4(ii)). By flatness of O(T') over A the same formula holds for every quasi-compact quasi-separated open V ⊆ S (Čech complexes of a finite affinoid cover).

Assume S' → T' finite. Then S' is affinoid; r: S' → S is surjective (faithful flatness, R0/fibre-product-points) and quasi-compact, so S is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and O_{S'}(S') = O_S(S) ⊗_A O(T') is finite over O(T'); by faithfully flat descent O_S(S) is a finite A-module (Mathlib Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat; Huber cites EGA IV 2.7.1).

Let Z → T be the finite adic space attached to the finite A-algebra O_S(S) (R0/finite-algebra-over-affinoid, A noetherian) and p: S → Z the canonical T-morphism; its base change p': S' → Z' = Z ×_T T' is an isomorphism (both are Spa of O_S(S) ⊗_A O(T')).

p is injective (p' injective, t: Z' → Z surjective, and points of Z' ×_Z S lift, R0/fibre-product-points), surjective (p' and t surjective) and closed (r surjective, p' and t closed, finite morphisms being closed, R0/finite-morphisms), hence a homeomorphism. For U ⊆ Z quasi-compact open, p*: O_Z(U) → O_S(p⁻¹U) is a topological embedding (since p'*, t*, r* are) and bijective (p'* is, and O(T') is faithfully flat over A). Hence p is an isomorphism and S is affinoid and finite over T.
acceptance: The finite faithfully flat cover W → V used in the proof of Huber 1.5.5 (to make residue fields purely inseparable) is an instance of h.

nodes.title: Base change of a finite algebra over a complete Tate ring needs no completion
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) be a finite morphism of complete Tate Huber pairs (R0/finite-huber-pair-hom) and φ: A → C a continuous homomorphism to a complete Tate ring C. Give B ⊗_A C the tensor-product topology (the topology of R0/completed-tensor-product before completion). (i) This is the natural C-module topology of the finite C-module B ⊗_A C (Mathlib moduleTopology). (ii) If A and C are noetherian, or if B is a finite projective A-module, then B ⊗_A C is complete and Hausdorff, so the canonical map B ⊗_A C → B ⊗̂_A C to the completed tensor product (R0/completed-tensor-product) is an isomorphism of topological rings, and (C, C⁺) → (B ⊗_A C, integral closure of the image of C⁺ ⊗ B⁺) is a finite morphism of complete Huber pairs. (iii) Consequently, if A is strongly noetherian or B is a finite projective A-module, then for f₁, …, f_n, g ∈ A generating the unit ideal the map B ⊗_A A⟨f/g⟩ → B⟨φ(f)/φ(g)⟩ is an isomorphism of topological rings: the preimage of the rational subset V = R(f/g) under Spa(B, B⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) is the rational subset R(φ(f)/φ(g)), with ring B ⊗_A O(V). No claim is made that f⁻¹(Spa A) is affinoid for a finite morphism f of adic spaces over a non-noetherian sheafy Spa(A, A⁺) (Zavyalov, Remark B.2.19).
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) a finite morphism of complete Tate Huber pairs
C a complete Tate ring with a continuous A → C
in (ii)-(iii): A and C noetherian, or B finite projective over A
proofSteps: (i) Zavyalov, Lemma B.3.5: choose a ring of definition B₀ and a surjection Aⁿ → B mapping A₀ⁿ onto B₀ (the natural topology of B, R0/finite-huber-pair-hom); tensoring gives surjections Cⁿ → B ⊗_A C and C₀ⁿ → (B ⊗_A C)₀, so Cⁿ → B ⊗_A C is open and the tensor topology is the quotient topology, i.e. the natural C-module topology (Mathlib IsModuleTopology.isOpenQuotientMap_of_surjective).

(ii), noetherian case: B ⊗_A C is a finite module over the complete noetherian Tate ring C, complete for its natural topology (Tau Ceti TauCeti.completeSpace_moduleTopology) and Hausdorff (Tau Ceti TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.t2Space_moduleTopology); this is Huber 1994 Lemma 2.4(ii) as used in Zavyalov, Lemma B.3.6.

(ii), projective case: B ⊗_A C is a finite projective C-module (Mathlib Module.Projective.tensorProduct), hence a direct summand of Cⁿ via an idempotent e; with the natural topology it is the closed subgroup ker(1 − e) of the complete Hausdorff Cⁿ, so complete and Hausdorff (Kedlaya–Liu, Lemma 2.2.12(a)); completeness also follows from Tau Ceti TauCeti.completeSpace_moduleTopology.

The completed tensor product B ⊗̂_A C is the Hausdorff completion of B ⊗_A C with plus ring the integral closure of the image (R0/completed-tensor-product), so the completion map is an isomorphism; B ⊗_A C is module-finite over C (Mathlib Module.Finite.base_change) with integral plus ring, i.e. finite over (C, C⁺).

(iii) Take C = A⟨f/g⟩: rational localisation commutes with completed tensor products (R0/completed-tensor-rational-localisation), and by (ii) the completion is not needed; for A strongly noetherian, A⟨f/g⟩ is noetherian (Zavyalov, Corollary B.3.7).

nodes.title: Locally quasi-finite and quasi-finite morphisms of adic spaces
nodes.statement: A morphism f: X → Y of adic spaces is locally quasi-finite if it is locally of weakly finite type (R0/finite-type-morphism-classes) and for every y ∈ Y the fibre f⁻¹(y) is a discrete subspace of |X|; it is quasi-finite if moreover it is quasi-compact (Huber 1996, 1.5.1). Conventions: discreteness is of the fibre with the subspace topology of |X| (not of the fibre adic space X ×_Y Spa κ(y)); for f of weakly finite type between analytic adic spaces quasi-finite is equivalent to finiteness of all fibres (R0/quasi-finite-fibre-criteria).
hypotheses: f locally of weakly finite type
proofSteps: Definition as stated; QuasiFinite is the conjunction LocallyQuasiFinite ∧ QuasiCompact.
acceptance: Finite morphisms locally of weakly finite type are quasi-finite; open embeddings are locally quasi-finite; unramified morphisms are locally quasi-finite (R0/unramified-locally-quasi-finite).

nodes.title: Fibre criteria for quasi-finiteness (Huber 1.5.2)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of weakly finite type between analytic adic spaces. The following are equivalent: (a) f is quasi-finite; (b) f⁻¹(y) is finite for every y ∈ Y; (c) f⁻¹(y) is finite for every maximal point y ∈ Y; (d) k(x)^∧ is a finite extension of k(f(x))^∧ for every x ∈ X; (e) the same for every maximal point x ∈ X; (f) for every maximal point y of Y, X ×_Y Spa κ(y) → Spa κ(y) is finite. Conditions (a), (b), (d) are equivalent without the analyticity hypothesis.
hypotheses: f of weakly finite type (quasi-compact and locally of weakly finite type)
X, Y analytic for the equivalence with (c), (e), (f)
proofSteps: Reduce to the fibre over a point: by Huber (1.2.4) (R0/fibre-over-point) the fibre X_y = X ×_Y Spa κ(y) maps homeomorphically onto f⁻¹(G), G the generalizations of y, with dense residue field extensions; X_y is quasi-compact, so one may assume Y = Spa(K, K⁺) for a complete affinoid field and X = Spa(A, A⁺) ≠ ∅ with A topologically of finite type over K (finitely many affinoid pieces).

Analytic case: choose a finite injective K⟨T₁,…,T_d⟩ → A (Noether normalisation, R0/affinoid-noether-normalisation) and use integrality of A° over K°⟨T⟩ (R0/affinoid-power-bounded-integral) to get the finite surjective Spa(A, A°) → Spa(K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩) and the closed embedding Spa(A, A°) → Spa(A, A⁺); each of (b)-(e) is then equivalent to d = 0 (Huber's diagrams (*) and (**)).

Non-analytic case (for the equivalence of (a), (b), (d)): k(y) is discrete and A is a finitely generated k(y)-algebra with the discrete topology; (a), (b), (d) are each equivalent to dim A = 0, i.e. A finite over k(y) (Noether normalisation, Mathlib exists_finite_inj_algHom_of_fg; for dim A > 0 the fibre contains infinitely many points, e.g. the trivial valuations at the infinitely many primes of A).

(a) ⇒ (b): fibres of quasi-compact morphisms are quasi-compact, and a quasi-compact discrete space is finite; (b) ⇒ (a) since d = 0. (f) ⇒ (c) trivially; (c) ⇒ (f): d = 0, and after passing to K⁺ = K° (A° integral over K°) A⁺ = A°, so f is finite.
acceptance: For S ↦ T² on discs every fibre has at most two points and all residue field extensions have degree ≤ 2, so all six conditions hold.

nodes.title: Stalk criterion for local quasi-finiteness (Huber 1.5.4)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism locally of weakly finite type between analytic adic spaces. Then f is locally quasi-finite if and only if for every maximal point x ∈ X the local ring O_{X,x} is a finite O_{Y,f(x)}-module. If f is locally of finite type, this is further equivalent to: every maximal point x ∈ X has open neighbourhoods U ∋ x, V ⊇ f(U) with f|_U: U → V finite.
hypotheses: X, Y analytic
f locally of weakly finite type (resp. locally of finite type for the last equivalence)
proofSteps: For B topologically of finite type over A (affinoid pieces) and x maximal, use condition (f) of R0/quasi-finite-fibre-criteria and R0/finite-from-proper-fibre to get finiteness over a neighbourhood of f(x) of a neighbourhood of x (the fibre is finite, hence proper).
Identify O_{Y,y₀} ⊗ O_X(f⁻¹V) with the product of the stalks O_{X,x} over y₀ (finite morphisms: stalks of the pushforward), giving module-finiteness of the stalk.
For the +weakly finite type case pass through Z = Spa(B, B°) as in the source; the converse uses that a finite stalk has finitely many points over y₀.
acceptance: For S ↦ T² the stalk of the source at T = 0 is a free module of rank 2 over the stalk of the target at S = 0.

nodes.title: Quasi-finite and proper equals finite (Huber 1.5.5)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism locally of finite type between analytic adic spaces, with Y locally noetherian (R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space; for analytic Y: locally Spa of strongly noetherian Tate rings, which is Huber's standing assumption (1.1.1) for analytic spaces). Then f is finite (R0/finite-morphism) if and only if f is quasi-finite (R0/quasi-finite-morphism) and proper (R0/universally-closed-and-proper-morphism) (Huber 1996, Proposition 1.5.5).
hypotheses: X, Y analytic adic spaces; Y locally noetherian (needed by R0/finiteness-faithfully-flat-descent and the valuative criterion)
f locally of finite type
properness in the sense of Huber 1.3.2 (+weakly finite type, separated, universally closed)
proofSteps: (finite ⇒ quasi-finite and proper) Proper: R0/finite-morphisms. Quasi-finite: finite morphisms are quasi-compact and, by (f) of R0/quasi-finite-fibre-criteria, have finite fibres (a finite algebra over an affinoid field has finitely many points).

(⇐) Fix y ∈ Y. Choose an affinoid V ∋ y and a finite faithfully flat affinoid cover h: W → V such that the residue fields of the points of Z = f⁻¹(V) ×_V W over a point w ∈ W over y are purely inseparable over k(w)^∧ (the source asserts that such W exists without reference; see gaps).

The generalisation sets Gᵢ of the finitely many points zᵢ of Z over w are pairwise disjoint and open-closed in g⁻¹(G): this uses uniqueness of centres (Huber 1.3.6, R0/adic-valuation-rings-and-centres) and separatedness (R0/valuative-criterion-separated).

Choose affinoid Kᵢ ⊆ Z around zᵢ and obtain finiteness of Kᵢ ∩ g⁻¹(Lᵢ) → Lᵢ from R0/finite-from-proper-fibre (the fibre is finite, hence proper) and (1.2.4) (R0/fibre-product-points); shrink to L with g⁻¹(L) ⊆ ∪Kᵢ; conclude finiteness over h⁻¹(U) for an affinoid U ∋ y.
Descend finiteness along h (R0/finiteness-faithfully-flat-descent); finiteness is local on the target (R0/finite-morphism).
acceptance: Concrete instance: Spa(K⟨T⟩) → Spa(K⟨S⟩), S ↦ T², is proper, quasi-finite and finite.

The rational embedding {|T| ≤ |ϖ|} ⊆ D is quasi-finite and not proper (not partially proper), hence not finite; the open unit disc B ⊆ D is locally quasi-finite and partially proper but not quasi-compact, hence not finite.

nodes.title: Partially proper locally quasi-finite morphisms are finite near closures of points (Huber 1.5.6)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism locally of finite type between analytic adic spaces, with X quasi-separated, Y quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and Y locally noetherian (Huber's standing assumption (1.1.1); needed by R0/quasi-finite-and-finiteness-criteria). Then f is locally quasi-finite and partially proper if and only if every x ∈ X has open subspaces U ⊇ closure{x} and V ⊇ closure{f(x)} with f(U) ⊆ V and f|_U: U → V finite (Huber 1996, Proposition 1.5.6).
hypotheses: X, Y analytic; X quasi-separated; Y quasi-compact quasi-separated and locally noetherian
f locally of finite type
proofSteps: (⇐) Finite morphisms are locally quasi-finite (R0/quasi-finite-fibre-criteria) and proper (R0/finite-morphisms); since the U cover X and closures of points are contained in them, the valuative criterion (R0/separated-proper-partially-proper) gives partial properness.

(⇒) It suffices to treat a maximal point x₀ (every point specialises from a maximal one, and closures only grow); y₀ = f(x₀) is maximal (Huber 1.1.10(iv)). By R0/partially-proper-closure-quasi-compact, closure{x₀} lies in a quasi-compact open W'. The maximal points of W' over y₀ are finitely many, x₀, …, xₙ (R0/quasi-finite-fibre-criteria), their closures are disjoint and f⁻¹(closure{y₀}) ∩ W' = ⋃ᵢ (closure{xᵢ} ∩ W') (Huber 1.1.10(i),(v)); hence there is a quasi-compact open W with closure{x₀} = f⁻¹(closure{y₀}) ∩ W.

Claim: there is an open V ⊇ closure{y₀} such that W ∩ f⁻¹(V) → V is proper; then it is quasi-finite and proper, hence finite (R0/quasi-finite-and-finiteness-criteria). Let S ⊆ W_v be the set of (x, A) having a centre y on Y but no centre on f⁻¹(y) ∩ W. Covering Y by finitely many affinoids Y_i and f⁻¹(Y_i) ∩ W by affinoids W_j with topologically finite type rings (finite sets E_j), S = ⋃ᵢ (T ∖ ⋃ⱼ T_j) with T, T_j described by Huber 1.3.6(ii); by R0/valuation-ring-space-spectral (quasi-compactness of the D(U, h)) S is pro-constructible in the spectral space W_v.

For U ranging over the quasi-compact opens containing closure{y₀} (whose intersection is closure{y₀}, as it is stable under generalization), the sets S(U) = {(x, A) ∈ S : x ∈ f⁻¹(U)} are pro-constructible and ⋂_U S(U) = S(closure{y₀}) = ∅, because f is partially proper and f⁻¹(closure{y₀}) ∩ W = closure{x₀} is closed in X (R0/separated-proper-partially-proper). By compactness of the constructible topology (Mathlib compactSpace_withConstructibleTopology) some S(V) is empty, and the valuative criterion shows W ∩ f⁻¹(V) → V is proper (W is quasi-compact).
acceptance: For the open embedding of the open unit disc B into the closed unit disc D (partially proper and locally quasi-finite) and x ∈ B with |T(x)| ≤ r < 1, the condition holds with U = V = {|T| ≤ r'} for any r < r' < 1 in |K^×|, which contains closure{x}.

This proposition is the input of Huber's Lemma 1.5.9 comparing rigid and adic partial properness for locally quasi-finite maps without discreteness of the valuation (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/proper-separated-comparisons).

nodes.title: Module of continuous differentials of a topologically finite type map
nodes.statement: Let φ: A → B be a continuous homomorphism of complete Huber rings (complete Hausdorff f-adic rings) which is topologically of finite type (tauceti TauCeti.Huber.IsTopologicallyFiniteType), with A of noetherian type (R0/noetherian-type-huber-ring: a noetherian ring of definition, or strongly noetherian Tate — Huber's standing assumption (1.1.1)); then B and B ⊗̂_A B are of noetherian type (R0/topologically-finite-type-noetherian-type, R0/completed-tensor-noetherian-stability), their ideals are closed and finite modules with the natural topology are complete and Hausdorff. Let m: B ⊗̂_A B → B be the continuous extension of b ⊗ b' ↦ bb' to the completed tensor product (R0/completed-tensor-product) and I = ker m. The module of continuous differentials is Ωᶜ_{B/A} := I/I², a B-module via (B ⊗̂_A B)/I ≅ B, with the natural B-module topology, and d = d_{B/A}: B → Ωᶜ_{B/A}, d(b) = class of 1 ⊗ b − b ⊗ 1 (Huber 1996, (1.6.2)). Properties: (a) for every finite N ⊆ B with A[N] dense in B, I is generated by the 1 ⊗ n − n ⊗ 1 (n ∈ N); hence Ωᶜ_{B/A} is a finitely generated B-module generated by d(N). (b) d is a continuous A-derivation and is universal: for every complete Hausdorff topological B-module M and every continuous A-derivation D: B → M there is a unique continuous B-linear u: Ωᶜ_{B/A} → M with u ∘ d = D. (c) If A⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩_M → B is a quotient mapping with kernel 𝔞, then Ωᶜ_{B/A} ≅ (⊕ᵢ B dXᵢ)/(B-span of Σᵢ (∂P/∂Xᵢ) dXᵢ, P ∈ 𝔞), where ∂/∂Xᵢ are the termwise partial derivatives (which preserve A⟨X⟩_M); in particular Ωᶜ_{A⟨X⟩_M/A} is free with basis dX₁,…,dXₙ. (d) If B is a finite A-module, the canonical B-linear map Ω[B⁄A] → Ωᶜ_{B/A} from Mathlib's KaehlerDifferential (induced by d) is an isomorphism. Under this hypothesis Ωᶜ_{B/A} is complete and Hausdorff; without it (non-noetherian A) the ideal generated by the 1 ⊗ n − n ⊗ 1 need not be closed and none of (a)-(d) is asserted. The coherent sheaf Ω¹_{X/Y} on a locally noetherian analytic adic space is glued from these modules by the localisation compatibility (API localizationEquiv); it is AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheaf-of-continuous-differentials.
hypotheses: A → B continuous, topologically of finite type, between complete Huber rings
A of noetherian type (Huber's standing assumption); hence B, B ⊗̂_A B of noetherian type
M ranges over complete Hausdorff topological B-modules in the universal property
proofSteps: B ⊗̂_A B and the continuous multiplication m exist by R0/completed-tensor-product and its universal property (R0/completed-tensor-product-universal-property).

(a) Density argument (Huber's proof of (1.6.2)(ii)): the ideal J generated by the 1 ⊗ n − n ⊗ 1 (n ∈ N) satisfies J ⊆ I, contains 1 ⊗ c − c ⊗ 1 for c ∈ A[N] (Leibniz identity, as for Mathlib KaehlerDifferential.submodule_span_range_eq_ideal), and is dense in I; J is closed because B ⊗̂_A B is of noetherian type (R0/completed-tensor-noetherian-stability, R0/noetherian-type-ideals-closed); hence J = I.

(b) Derivation property as in the algebraic case (Mathlib KaehlerDifferential.D). Universality: for D continuous define B ⊗_A B → M, b ⊗ b' ↦ b·D(b'), extend by continuity to B ⊗̂_A B (M complete Hausdorff), restrict to I; it vanishes on I² and on 1 ⊗ a − a ⊗ 1 correctly, giving u; uniqueness since d(N) generates.

(c) For R = A⟨X⟩_M: polynomials are dense (AdicSpaces anchor Layer 0.4, Wedhorn 5.49), so a continuous derivation is determined by the values D(Xᵢ), and any values mᵢ ∈ M give the continuous derivation f ↦ Σ ∂f/∂Xᵢ·mᵢ (convergence from completeness of M); hence Ωᶜ_{R/A} is free on dXᵢ. For B = R/𝔞 a continuous derivation of B is one of R killing 𝔞, which gives the presentation (FK Corollary 5.1.11 in the formal case).

(d) For B module-finite over A, B ⊗_A B is a finite B-module with the natural topology (Zavyalov B.3.5) and complete when B is noetherian (Zavyalov B.3.6), so B ⊗̂_A B = B ⊗_A B and I/I² is the algebraic Ω[B⁄A] (Mathlib definition KaehlerDifferential = (ideal R S).Cotangent); the general finite case is Huber (1.6.2)(iii).

Completeness and Hausdorffness of Ωᶜ_{B/A} = I/I²: I is finitely generated and I² closed (noetherian type), and finite modules over complete rings of noetherian type are complete with closed submodules (R0/noetherian-rod-module-complete; Tate case TauCeti isClosed_of_isNoetherian).
acceptance: Ωᶜ_{K⟨T⟩/K} is free of rank 1 on dT, whereas Mathlib's Ω[K⟨T⟩⁄K] is not finitely generated.

nodes.title: First fundamental exact sequence of continuous differentials (Huber 1.6.3)
nodes.statement: Let A → B → C be continuous homomorphisms of complete Huber rings, with A of noetherian type (as in R0/continuous-differentials), with B topologically of finite type over A and C topologically of finite type over B (so C is topologically of finite type over A, Huber 1994 Lemma 3.3(iv)). Then the sequence of C-modules C ⊗_B Ωᶜ_{B/A} → Ωᶜ_{C/A} → Ωᶜ_{C/B} → 0 is exact, the maps being induced by functoriality (R0/continuous-differentials).
hypotheses: A → B → C topologically of finite type between complete Huber rings
A of noetherian type (Huber's standing assumption), so that finite C-modules are complete Hausdorff with closed submodules
proofSteps: Surjectivity of Ωᶜ_{C/A} → Ωᶜ_{C/B}: both are generated by d(N) for a finite N ⊆ C with A[N] dense in C (property (a) of R0/continuous-differentials).

Exactness in the middle: let Q be the cokernel of C ⊗_B Ωᶜ_{B/A} → Ωᶜ_{C/A}. It is a finite C-module, hence complete and Hausdorff because the image is closed (C of noetherian type, R0/noetherian-type-ideals-closed, R0/noetherian-rod-module-complete). The composite C → Ωᶜ_{C/A} → Q is a continuous derivation vanishing on the image of B, i.e. a continuous B-derivation, so by the universal property (b) it factors through Ωᶜ_{C/B}; hence the kernel of Ωᶜ_{C/A} → Ωᶜ_{C/B} maps to 0 in Q, which is exactness (the algebraic analogue is Mathlib KaehlerDifferential.exact_mapBaseChange_map).
acceptance: For A = K, B = K⟨S⟩, C = K⟨T⟩ with S ↦ T² (2 ∈ K^×): C·dS → C·dT, dS ↦ 2T dT, has cokernel C/(2T)·dT = Ωᶜ_{C/B}.

nodes.title: Conormal exact sequence for quotient mappings (Huber 1.6.3)
nodes.statement: Let A → B be a continuous homomorphism of complete Huber rings, topologically of finite type, with A of noetherian type (as in R0/continuous-differentials), and J ⊆ B a closed ideal with quotient mapping B → C = B/J. Then the sequence of C-modules J/J² → C ⊗_B Ωᶜ_{B/A} → Ωᶜ_{C/A} → 0, with first map j ↦ 1 ⊗ dj, is exact.
hypotheses: A → B topologically of finite type; A of noetherian type
J ⊆ B an ideal (closed, B being of noetherian type), C = B/J with the quotient topology, B → C open and surjective
proofSteps: Surjectivity: Ωᶜ_{C/A} is generated by the images of d(N) (R0/continuous-differentials (a)).

Exactness in the middle: let Q be the cokernel of J/J² → C ⊗_B Ωᶜ_{B/A}, a finite C-module, complete and Hausdorff (closed image, C of noetherian type: R0/noetherian-type-ideals-closed, R0/noetherian-rod-module-complete). The map c = b + J ↦ class of 1 ⊗ d b is a well-defined A-derivation C → Q (d(J) lands in the image of J/J²), continuous because C carries the quotient topology; by the universal property (b) of Ωᶜ_{C/A} it factors through Ωᶜ_{C/A}, which yields a retraction proving exactness (algebraic analogue: Mathlib KaehlerDifferential.exact_kerCotangentToTensor_mapBaseChange).
acceptance: For A = K, B = K⟨T⟩, J = (T²) with 2 ∈ K^×: C = K[T]/(T²), J/J² is generated by the class of T², which maps to 2T·dT in C·dT; the cokernel C·dT/(2T·dT) is Ωᶜ_{C/K} = Ω[C⁄K] (finite case of R0/continuous-differentials (d)).

nodes.title: Stalks of continuous differentials of locally quasi-finite morphisms (Huber 1.6.4(i))
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a locally quasi-finite morphism between locally noetherian analytic adic spaces (R0/quasi-finite-morphism, R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space; the setting in which R0/continuous-differentials yields finite modules with the natural topology) and x ∈ X a maximal point, y = f(x). Then O_{X,x} is a finite O_{Y,y}-algebra (R0/quasi-finite-stalk-criterion), and the stalk Ωᶜ_{X/Y,x} := colim Ωᶜ_{O_X(U)/O_Y(V)} (over affinoid neighbourhoods U ∋ x, V ⊇ f(U); well defined by the localisation compatibility of R0/continuous-differentials) is canonically isomorphic, compatibly with the derivations, to Mathlib's Ω[O_{X,x}⁄O_{Y,y}].
hypotheses: X, Y analytic and locally noetherian
f locally quasi-finite
x maximal
proofSteps: Finiteness of the stalk and the identification O_{Y,y} ⊗_{O_Y(V)} O_X(f⁻¹V) ≅ ∏ O_{X,x'} over the points x' over y, as in the proof of Huber 1.5.4 (R0/quasi-finite-stalk-criterion), after shrinking to affinoid V where f⁻¹(V) → V is finite.

For finite A → B the continuous differentials are the algebraic ones (R0/continuous-differentials (d), Huber (1.6.2)(iii)); base change of Kähler differentials along A → O_{Y,y} (Mathlib KaehlerDifferential.tensorKaehlerEquiv, the square being a pushout) and the product decomposition identify Ω[O_{X,x}⁄O_{Y,y}] with the stalk of Ωᶜ_{X/Y} at x, compatibly with the derivations, which is the universality claimed (Huber: '(i) follows from (1.6.2.iii) and the proof of (1.5.4)').
acceptance: For S ↦ T² at the maximal point T = 0 (over S = 0): O_{X,0} is free of rank 2 over O_{Y,0} and Ωᶜ_{X/Y,0} ≅ O_{X,0}/(2T)·dT.

nodes.title: Flat morphism of adic spaces
nodes.statement: A morphism f: X → Y of adic spaces is flat if for every x ∈ X the local homomorphism of stalks O_{Y,f(x)} → O_{X,x} is flat (Mathlib Module.Flat) (Huber 1996, 1.7.5(b); Zavyalov, Quotients, Definition B.4.1). Stalks are colimits of rings, with no topology (AdicSpaces anchor, Layer 3.3). Conventions: flatness is stalkwise; for morphisms of strongly noetherian Tate affinoids it implies flatness of O_Y(Y) → O_X(X) (Zavyalov B.4.3), and for affinoids of topologically finite type over a nonarchimedean field the two are equivalent (Zavyalov B.4.3, B.4.6); in general the converse is not known (Zavyalov B.4.9) and is not asserted.
hypotheses: f: X → Y morphism of adic spaces
proofSteps: Definition as stated (stalk maps exist for morphisms of adic spaces: anchor Layer 3.3-3.4).
acceptance: Open embeddings are flat; the closed embedding of the origin into the closed disc is not.

nodes.title: Unramified morphism of adic spaces
nodes.statement: A morphism f: X → Y of adic spaces is unramified if it is locally of finite type (R0/finite-type-morphism-classes) and for every complete Huber pair A, every closed ideal I ⊆ A with I² = 0 and every morphism Spa A → Y, the restriction map Hom_Y(Spa A, X) → Hom_Y(Spa(A/I), X) is injective (Huber 1996, 1.6.5). Test objects: A ranges over complete Huber pairs (A, A⁺) (Tau Ceti Huber.Pair on complete Hausdorff rings), Spa A is the affinoid pre-adic space of the AdicSpaces anchor (Layer 3.4; A need not be sheafy), and morphisms Spa A → Y are morphisms of pre-adic spaces; I ⊆ A is a closed ideal with I² = 0 and A/I is the quotient Huber pair (tauceti Huber.Pair.quotient), whose plus ring is A⁺/I because I ⊆ A°° ⊆ A⁺. Huber allows non-complete affinoid rings and arbitrary square-zero I; since Spa A = Spa Â and the closure of a square-zero ideal is square-zero, restricting to complete A and closed I changes nothing. The morphism Spa(A/I) → Spa A is a homeomorphism.
hypotheses: f locally of finite type
lifting tested against all square-zero thickenings Spa(A/I) → Spa A of affinoid pre-adic spaces over Y
proofSteps: Definition as stated; Hom sets are taken in the category of pre-adic spaces over Y (anchor Layer 3.4).
acceptance: Monomorphisms locally of finite type (in particular locally closed embeddings) are unramified (R0/immersion-unramified).
Unramified ⇔ Ω_{X/Y} = 0 ⇔ Δ_f open embedding (R0/infinitesimal-criteria).

nodes.title: Smooth morphism of adic spaces
nodes.statement: A morphism f: X → Y of adic spaces is smooth if it is locally of finite presentation (R0/locally-finite-presentation) and for every complete Huber pair A, every closed ideal I ⊆ A with I² = 0 and every morphism Spa A → Y, the restriction map Hom_Y(Spa A, X) → Hom_Y(Spa(A/I), X) is surjective (Huber 1996, 1.6.5). Test objects: A ranges over complete Huber pairs (A, A⁺) (Tau Ceti Huber.Pair on complete Hausdorff rings), Spa A is the affinoid pre-adic space of the AdicSpaces anchor (Layer 3.4; A need not be sheafy), and morphisms Spa A → Y are morphisms of pre-adic spaces; I ⊆ A is a closed ideal with I² = 0 and A/I is the quotient Huber pair (tauceti Huber.Pair.quotient), whose plus ring is A⁺/I because I ⊆ A°° ⊆ A⁺. Huber allows non-complete affinoid rings and arbitrary square-zero I; since Spa A = Spa Â and the closure of a square-zero ideal is square-zero, restricting to complete A and closed I changes nothing. The morphism Spa(A/I) → Spa A is a homeomorphism. The relative dimension of f at x is the rank of the (locally free, R0/smooth-differentials-locally-free) module of continuous differentials near x.

nodes.title: Étale morphism of adic spaces
nodes.statement: A morphism f: X → Y of adic spaces is étale if it is locally of finite presentation (R0/locally-finite-presentation) and for every complete Huber pair A, every closed ideal I ⊆ A with I² = 0 and every morphism Spa A → Y, the restriction map Hom_Y(Spa A, X) → Hom_Y(Spa(A/I), X) is bijective (Huber 1996, 1.6.5). Equivalently, f is smooth (R0/smooth-morphism) and unramified (R0/unramified-morphism). Test objects: A ranges over complete Huber pairs (A, A⁺) (Tau Ceti Huber.Pair on complete Hausdorff rings), Spa A is the affinoid pre-adic space of the AdicSpaces anchor (Layer 3.4; A need not be sheafy), and morphisms Spa A → Y are morphisms of pre-adic spaces; I ⊆ A is a closed ideal with I² = 0 and A/I is the quotient Huber pair (tauceti Huber.Pair.quotient), whose plus ring is A⁺/I because I ⊆ A°° ⊆ A⁺. Huber allows non-complete affinoid rings and arbitrary square-zero I; since Spa A = Spa Â and the closure of a square-zero ideal is square-zero, restricting to complete A and closed I changes nothing. The morphism Spa(A/I) → Spa A is a homeomorphism. Conventions: this is Huber's infinitesimal definition; the Kedlaya–Liu and Scholze–Weinstein definition ('locally an open immersion followed by a finite étale map') agrees with it for analytic adic spaces by R0/etale-local-open-finite-etale-factorisation, and the algebraic notion Algebra.Etale of Mathlib applied to coordinate rings does not (a rational embedding is étale but its ring map is not of finite type).
hypotheses: f locally of finite presentation
lifting tested against square-zero thickenings of affinoid pre-adic spaces
proofSteps: Definition as stated; equivalence with smooth ∧ unramified: bijective = injective ∧ surjective, and locally of finite presentation implies locally of finite type (R0/finite-type-morphism-classes).
acceptance: Open embeddings are étale (R0/open-embedding-etale); étale affinoid maps are standard étale (R0/etale-local-structure); étale ⇔ flat + unramified for analytic spaces (R0/etale-flat-unramified).

tests.statement: Notation: K complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial rank-one valuation, K° its valuation ring, ϖ a pseudo-uniformiser, D = Spa(K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩). Let n ∈ K^× (as an integer) and T^± denote the annulus Spa(K⟨T, T⁻¹⟩, K°⟨T, T⁻¹⟩). The map T^± → T^±, S ↦ Tⁿ, is finite and étale: it is the standard presentation K⟨S^±⟩⟨T⟩/(Tⁿ − S) with Jacobian nTⁿ⁻¹ a unit (R0/etale-local-structure).

tests.name: Etale_test_rationalEmbedding
tests.statement: Notation: K complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial rank-one valuation, K° its valuation ring, ϖ a pseudo-uniformiser, D = Spa(K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩). For K = Q_p the rational embedding {|T| ≤ |p|} → D is étale (an open embedding), but Q_p⟨T⟩ → Q_p⟨T, T/p⟩ is not of finite type as an algebra (the image of Spec is an infinite, co-infinite set of closed points, contradicting Chevalley's theorem), so it is not Algebra.Etale: 'étale' cannot be defined as Mathlib's Algebra.Etale on coordinate rings.

tests.name: Etale_test_frobenius

nodes.title: Open embeddings are étale (Huber 1.6.7)
nodes.statement: Every open embedding j: U → X of adic spaces is étale (R0/differentials-unramified-smooth-etale).
hypotheses: j an open embedding (isomorphism onto an open adic subspace, AdicSpaces anchor Layer 5.1)
proofSteps: Locally of finite presentation: locally U is a rational subset of an affinoid Spa A with coordinate ring A⟨T/s⟩, which is topologically of finite type over A (Huber 1994 Corollary 3.4(i)); the finite presentation condition of R0/locally-finite-presentation only involves discrete bases, where rational localisations are localisations A[1/s], finitely presented.

Lifting: let Spa A → X be a morphism and ḡ: Spa(A/I) → U an X-morphism (I² = 0). Hom_X(Spa A, U) and Hom_X(Spa(A/I), U) have at most one element each (j is a monomorphism), and a morphism into X factors through the open subspace U iff its image lies in U (universal property of open subspaces, anchor Layer 5.1). Since Spa(A/I) → Spa A is a homeomorphism (every continuous valuation kills the nilpotent ideal I), Spa A → X has image in U iff Spa(A/I) → X does, so the restriction map is bijective.
acceptance: The rational embedding {|T| ≤ |p|} ⊆ Spa(Q_p⟨T⟩, Z_p⟨T⟩) is étale.

nodes.title: Locally closed embeddings are unramified (Huber 1.6.7)
nodes.statement: Every morphism of adic spaces that is locally of finite type and a monomorphism is unramified; in particular every locally closed embedding (R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings) is unramified (R0/unramified-morphism).

nodes.title: Relative polydiscs are smooth (Huber 1.6.7)
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Huber pair and M₁,…,Mₙ finite subsets of A with each MᵢA open. Then the structure morphism Spa A⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩_M → Spa A (Huber 1994, §3: plus ring the integral closure of the series with coefficients in M^ν·A⁺) is smooth (R0/smooth-morphism), of relative dimension n.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) complete Huber pair
M_i finite with M_iA open
proofSteps: Locally of finite presentation: A → A⟨X⟩_M is of topologically finite type (definition); over a discrete A the ring A⟨X⟩_M is the polynomial ring A[X], of finite presentation (R0/locally-finite-presentation).

Lifting: morphisms Spa C → Spa A⟨X⟩_M over Spa A correspond to continuous A-homomorphisms A⟨X⟩_M → C, i.e. (universal property, Huber 1994 Lemma 3.5(i)) to tuples (c₁,…,cₙ) ∈ Cⁿ with m·cᵢ ∈ C⁺ for m ∈ Mᵢ (Hom into affinoid adic spaces: Huber 1994 Proposition 2.1, anchor Layer 5). Given (c̄ᵢ) for C/I, choose any lifts cᵢ ∈ C; then m·cᵢ ∈ C⁺ + I = C⁺ since I ⊆ C°° ⊆ C⁺. Hence the restriction map is surjective.
Relative dimension n: Ωᶜ is free on dX₁,…,dXₙ (R0/continuous-differentials (c)).
acceptance: Spa(K⟨T₁,…,Tₙ⟩) → Spa(K, K°) is smooth; this is the model in R0/smooth-local-structure.

nodes.title: Cancellation for unramified, smooth and étale morphisms (Huber 1.6.7)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y and g: Y → Z be morphisms of adic spaces. (i) If g ∘ f is unramified, then f is unramified. (ii) If g ∘ f is smooth (resp. étale) and g is unramified, then f is smooth (resp. étale) (Huber 1996, Proposition 1.6.7(iii)).
hypotheses: no hypothesis on g in (i); in (ii) g is unramified, hence locally of finite type
proofSteps: Finiteness: if g ∘ f is locally of finite type, so is f (cancellation for topologically finite type maps of affinoid rings, Huber 1994 Lemma 3.5(iv), the affinoid analogue of Lemma 3.3(iv)); in (ii), g is locally of finite type, so if g ∘ f is locally of finite presentation so is f (over discrete bases this is the algebraic cancellation, Stacks 00F4).
(i) Two Y-lifts Spa A → X of a Y-morphism Spa(A/I) → X are in particular Z-lifts, hence equal.

(ii) Given Spa A → Y and a Y-morphism Spa(A/I) → X, a Z-lift h: Spa A → X exists (g ∘ f smooth); the two Y-morphisms f ∘ h and the given Spa A → Y agree on Spa(A/I) and are Z-morphisms, so they are equal because g is unramified; hence h is a Y-lift. Uniqueness in the étale case follows from (i).
acceptance: If U → D is étale over D and D → Spa(K, K°) is smooth, the composite is smooth; conversely a morphism between étale D-spaces is étale.

nodes.title: Unramified, smooth and étale are local on the source (Huber 1.6.7)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of adic spaces and X = ⋃ᵢ Uᵢ an open cover. If each f|_{Uᵢ} is unramified (resp. étale, resp. smooth), then f is unramified (resp. étale, resp. smooth).
hypotheses: Open cover of the source
proofSteps: Finiteness conditions are local on the source by definition (R0/finite-type-morphism-classes, R0/locally-finite-presentation).

Unramified: two lifts g₁, g₂: Spa A → X agreeing on Spa(A/I) have the same underlying map (Spa(A/I) → Spa A is a homeomorphism); cover Spa A by rational subsets Wⱼ with images in some Uᵢ; the restrictions to Wⱼ = Spa(A_{Wⱼ}), thickenings of Spa(A_{Wⱼ}/I A_{Wⱼ}), agree by unramifiedness of f|_{Uᵢ}. To conclude g₁ = g₂ one needs that morphisms out of Spa A are determined by their restrictions to a rational cover; this holds when the structure presheaf of Spa A is separated (e.g. A sheafy, in particular of noetherian type), but not for arbitrary complete Huber pairs, which the R0 definitions admit as test objects — the same gap R0/smooth-etale-base-change records.
Étale: local lifts on the Wⱼ exist and are unique; gluing them into a morphism Spa A → X again needs the sheaf property of O_{Spa A} (gap as above for non-sheafy test objects).

Smooth: local lifts exist; gluing them requires the scheme argument (the local lifts form a torsor under Hom(ḡ*Ω_{X/Y}, I), and one needs vanishing of the first Čech cohomology of the corresponding module on rational covers of the test object Spa A). For arbitrary complete Huber pairs A this vanishing is not available (Tate acyclicity for modules is proved only under noetherian hypotheses, Huber 1994 Theorem 2.5); this step is recorded as a gap. If the test objects of Definition 1.6.5 are restricted to Huber's class (complete pairs of noetherian type, Huber's standing assumption (1.1.1)), the gluing works: the obstruction lies in Čech H¹ of the finite module Hom(ḡ*Ω_{X/Y}, I) on a rational cover, which vanishes by Tate acyclicity for finite modules (Huber 1994 Theorem 2.5).
acceptance: X = D covered by {|T| ≤ |ϖ|} and {|ϖ| ≤ |T|}: each piece is smooth over Spa(K, K°), and so is D.

nodes.title: Base change of unramified, smooth and étale morphisms
nodes.statement: Let f: X → S and g: Y → S be morphisms of adic spaces such that the fibre product exists by R0/fibre-products-existence, case (a): Y is covered by open affinoids Spa(B, B⁺) with B complete and stably sheafy (for instance Y locally noetherian) and f is locally of finite type; g is arbitrary (not necessarily adic). Let Z = X ×_S Y with projections p: Z → X and q: Z → Y. If f is unramified (R0/unramified-morphism), resp. smooth (R0/smooth-morphism), resp. étale (R0/differentials-unramified-smooth-etale), then q is unramified, resp. smooth, resp. étale. If f is smooth of relative dimension n at p(z), then q is smooth of relative dimension n at z; affinoid-locally Ωᶜ_{Z/Y} ≅ O_Z ⊗ Ωᶜ_{X/S} (R0/continuous-differentials). Every unramified, smooth or étale morphism is locally of finite type, so the fibre product exists for every such g. The lifting conditions are Huber's (Definition 1.6.5) with the test objects of R0: Spa T for complete Huber pairs (T, T⁺), not necessarily sheafy, and closed ideals I ⊆ T with I² = 0. Flatness is not part of this lemma: base change of flat morphisms is stated only for locally quasi-finite ones (R0/flat-morphism, Huber 1996 1.6.4(ii)), and étale morphisms of analytic adic spaces are flat by R0/etale-flat-unramified.
hypotheses: f: X → S locally of finite type and unramified, smooth or étale; g: Y → S any morphism of adic spaces with Y covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy coordinate rings (the hypotheses of R0/fibre-products-existence, case (a)).
proofSteps: Finiteness conditions: q is locally of finite type if f is and locally of finite presentation if f is (R0/base-change-stability (i), (iv)).

Morphisms from test objects into affinoids: for complete Huber pairs (T, T⁺) and (D, D⁺), morphisms of pre-adic spaces Spa T → Spa D correspond bijectively to continuous ring homomorphisms D → T carrying D⁺ into T⁺ (Huber 1994 Proposition 2.1(i); Wedhorn Proposition 8.19 for the category of pre-adic spaces, so T need not be sheafy). T/I is again a complete Huber pair because I is closed (tauceti TauCeti.Huber.Pair.quotient), and Spa(T/I) → Spa T is a homeomorphism.

Chart case, universal property against test objects: let S = Spa A, X = Spa C with A → C topologically of finite type, Y = Spa B, and Z = X ×_S Y. Claim: for every complete Huber pair T the map Hom(Spa T, Z) → Hom(Spa T, X) ×_{Hom(Spa T, S)} Hom(Spa T, Y) is bijective. If A → B is adic, Z = Spa(C ⊗̂_A B) (R0/affinoid-fibre-product, R0/fibre-product-along-finite-type (4)) and the claim is the previous step together with the universal property of C ⊗̂_A B among complete Huber pairs (R0/completed-tensor-product-universal-property), which uses no sheafiness of T. In general Z is the increasing union of the affinoid opens W_m = Spa(B⟨X⟩_{M_{L,m}}/J_m) (R0/fibre-product-along-finite-type); Spa T is quasi-compact, so a morphism Spa T → Z lands in some W_m and factors uniquely through it, and a compatible pair (C → T, B → T) factors through W_m as soon as ℓ·tᵢ ∈ T⁺ for ℓ ∈ Lᵐ, tᵢ the image of Xᵢ (universal property of restricted power series, Huber 1994 Lemma 3.5(i)), which holds for m large because the images of the finitely many elements of L are topologically nilpotent.

Lifting in the chart case, using the claim for T and for T/I. Unramified: two Y-morphisms u₁, u₂: Spa T → Z restricting to the same ū on Spa(T/I) satisfy q∘u₁ = q∘u₂, and p∘u₁, p∘u₂ are S-morphisms restricting to p∘ū, so p∘u₁ = p∘u₂ because f is unramified; by injectivity in the claim u₁ = u₂. Smooth: given k: Spa T → Y and a Y-morphism ū: Spa(T/I) → Z, smoothness of f (test morphism g∘k: Spa T → S) extends p∘ū to h: Spa T → X with f∘h = g∘k; by surjectivity in the claim (h, k) comes from some u: Spa T → Z, and u restricts to ū because both have the same composites with p and q (injectivity for T/I). Étale: both.

Restriction to open subspaces: if f is unramified (smooth, étale) and U ⊆ X, V ⊆ S are open with f(U) ⊆ V, then f|_U: U → V is unramified (smooth, étale): a morphism from Spa T to X whose underlying map lands in U factors uniquely through the open subspace U (anchor Layer 5), and a lift of a morphism Spa(T/I) → U lands in U because Spa(T/I) → Spa T is a homeomorphism.

General case: Z is covered by the open subspaces Z_{ijk} = X_j ×_{S_i} Y_k, for affinoid opens S_i ⊆ S, X_j ⊆ f⁻¹(S_i) with O_S(S_i) → O_X(X_j) topologically of finite type, and Y_k ⊆ g⁻¹(S_i) (R0/fibre-products-existence). By the two previous steps Z_{ijk} → Y_k is unramified (smooth, étale), and so is Z_{ijk} → Y, a composite with the open embedding Y_k ⊆ Y (R0/open-embedding-etale, R0/etale-smooth-composition). Hence q is unramified (smooth, étale) by locality on the source (R0/etale-smooth-locality). This step inherits the gap recorded for locality on the source: for a test object Spa T with T not sheafy, morphisms Spa T → Z are not determined by their restrictions to a rational covering of Spa T, and for smooth morphisms local lifts must also be glued.

Relative dimension: in the chart case Ωᶜ of the coordinate ring of Z over B is that ring tensored over C with Ωᶜ_{C/A}: for adic A → B by the base-change isomorphism of R0/continuous-differentials (API baseChangeEquiv), and for the W_m because B⟨X⟩_{M_{L,m}}/J_m has the presentation of C with the same generators dXᵢ and relations dP, P in the kernel of A⟨X⟩_M → C (R0/continuous-differentials (c)). So the local rank of Ωᶜ, which is the relative dimension (R0/smooth-differentials-locally-free), is preserved.
acceptance: For a complete extension L/K of nonarchimedean fields, the base change of the étale Kummer map on the unit annulus Spa(K⟨T^{±1}⟩) → Spa(K⟨S^{±1}⟩), S ↦ Tⁿ (n ∈ K^×), along Spa(L, L°) → Spa(K, K°) is the Kummer map on the unit annulus over L, again étale.
The relative polydisc Spa A⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩ → Spa A pulled back along an adic Spa B → Spa A is Spa B⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩ → Spa B, smooth of relative dimension n (R0/restricted-power-series-smooth).

Non-adic g: the open embedding Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) → Spa(ℤ_p, ℤ_p), which is étale, pulled back along Spa(ℤ_p⟦T⟧, ℤ_p⟦T⟧) → Spa(ℤ_p, ℤ_p) is the open embedding of the open unit disc over ℚ_p (the analytic locus of Spa ℤ_p⟦T⟧), étale and not quasi-compact (R0/base-change-stability).

nodes.title: Unramified morphisms are locally quasi-finite (Huber 1.7.4)
nodes.statement: Every unramified morphism of adic spaces is locally quasi-finite (R0/quasi-finite-morphism). In particular étale morphisms are locally quasi-finite.
hypotheses: f unramified
proofSteps: Locally on X, f factors as a closed embedding into an étale Y-space (R0/infinitesimal-criteria, condition (d)); closed embeddings have singleton fibres and are injective, so it suffices to treat étale f with X, Y affinoid.

Algebraic model (Huber 1.7.3(iii), R0/etale-algebraic-model): X ≅ Spa B with A → B of algebraically finite type and A^▷ → B^▷ étale in the algebraic sense. For x ∈ X over y ∈ Y, supp(x) lies over supp(y) and k(supp x) is a finite separable extension of k(supp y) (fibres of algebraically étale maps), so k(x)^∧ is finite over k(y)^∧ — condition (d) of Huber 1.5.2, which characterises quasi-finiteness of the quasi-compact X → Y without any analyticity hypothesis (R0/quasi-finite-fibre-criteria). Hence f is locally quasi-finite.
acceptance: The squaring map restricted to {|T| = 1} is étale with fibres of cardinality at most 2.

nodes.title: Characterisations of unramified morphisms (Huber 1.6.8)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of locally noetherian adic spaces, locally of finite type. The following are equivalent: (a) f is unramified (R0/unramified-morphism); (b) Ω_{X/Y} = 0, i.e. Ωᶜ_{O_X(U)/O_Y(V)} = 0 for all affinoid opens U ⊆ X, V ⊆ Y with f(U) ⊆ V (equivalently, for the members of one such affinoid cover, by the localisation compatibility of R0/continuous-differentials); (c) the diagonal Δ_f: X → X ×_Y X is an open embedding; (d) every x ∈ X has an open neighbourhood U such that f|_U factors as a closed embedding U → Z followed by an étale morphism Z → Y. (Huber's condition (d) is the stronger 'for every open affinoid U with f(U) inside an open affinoid of Y, f|_U factors through a closed embedding into an affinoid Z étale over Y'; the node proves and uses the local form, which is equivalent to (a).)
hypotheses: f locally of finite type
X, Y locally noetherian (continuous differentials, closedness of I²)
proofSteps: (a) ⇒ (b): affinoid-locally, the two continuous A-homomorphisms B → (B ⊗̂_A B)/I², b ↦ b ⊗ 1 and b ↦ 1 ⊗ b, agree modulo the square-zero ideal I/I² (I = kernel of multiplication, R0/continuous-differentials); unramifiedness forces them to be equal, so d = 0 and Ωᶜ = I/I² = 0 (EGA IV 17.4.1 transported). The thickening Spa((B ⊗̂_A B)/I²) is a test object of Definition 1.6.5.

(b) ⇒ (a): two lifts Spa A → X of Spa(A/I) → X over Y differ by an A-derivation into I (since I² = 0), which factors through Ωᶜ = 0 by the universal property (b) of R0/continuous-differentials (I is complete Hausdorff as a closed ideal); hence they agree.

(b) ⇔ (c): the ideal I of the diagonal is finitely generated (R0/continuous-differentials (a)) and I = I² locally, so I is locally generated by an idempotent and the diagonal (a locally closed embedding, R0/diagonal-locally-closed) is locally open and closed; conversely an open diagonal has I = 0 near Δ(X).

(a) ⇒ (d): locally embed X as a closed subspace of a relative polydisc Z' = Spa A⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩_M (definition of finite type); Ω_{X/Y} = 0 makes J/J² → Ω_{Z'/Y} ⊗ O_X surjective (R0/conormal-sequence); choose f₁,…,fₙ ∈ J whose differentials form a basis near x and let Z = V(f₁,…,fₙ), étale over Y near x by R0/jacobian-criterion-closed-subspace; X is closed in Z.

(d) ⇒ (a): closed embeddings and étale morphisms are unramified (R0/immersion-unramified, R0/differentials-unramified-smooth-etale) and composites of unramified morphisms are unramified (R0/etale-smooth-composition).
acceptance: The squaring map D → D (2 ∈ K^×) has Ωᶜ = K⟨T⟩/(2T)·dT, supported at the origin; it is unramified exactly on the complement of the origin.

Scheme analogue: Mathlib Algebra.FormallyUnramified (defined by Ω = 0) and Algebra.FormallyUnramified.iff_comp_injective; Mathlib instance Algebra.FormallyUnramified.isOpenImmersion_SpecMap_lmul (the diagonal of a formally unramified finite-type map is an open immersion).

nodes.title: Continuous differentials of a smooth morphism are locally free (Huber 1.6.9(i))
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a smooth morphism of locally noetherian adic spaces (R0/smooth-morphism; locally noetherian as required by R0/continuous-differentials). Then Ω_{X/Y} is locally free of finite rank: every x ∈ X has affinoid neighbourhoods U ∋ x, V ⊇ f(U) such that Ωᶜ_{O_X(U)/O_Y(V)} is a finite free O_X(U)-module (Huber 1996, Proposition 1.6.9(i)).
hypotheses: f smooth
X, Y locally noetherian
proofSteps: Locally embed X as a closed subspace V(J) of a relative polydisc Z' = Spa C, C = A⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩_M (f locally of finite presentation).

Smoothness of X gives a retraction of the square-zero thickening Spa(C/J²) ⊇ X over Y (lift id_X along X → Spa(C/J²), Definition 1.6.5), hence the conormal sequence J/J² → Ω_{C/A} ⊗ C/J → Ωᶜ_{X/Y} → 0 (R0/conormal-sequence) is split exact on the left (EGA IV 17.2.3 transported), so Ωᶜ_{X/Y} is a direct summand of the free module ⊕ C/J·dXᵢ (R0/continuous-differentials (c)), hence finite projective.

A finite projective module over O_X(U) is free after inverting each g_k of a family generating the unit ideal (Mathlib Module.Projective, local freeness on Spec). For x ∈ U some g_k(x) ≠ 0; choose a rational neighbourhood W ∋ x on which |g_k| ≠ 0 (for analytic U, W = R(ϖ^N/g_k) for N ≫ 0). g_k has no zeros on W, hence is a unit of O_X(W) (every maximal ideal of O_X(W) is the support of a point of W, Huber 1994 Lemma 1.4), and Ωᶜ_{O_X(W)/O_Y(V)} = O_X(W) ⊗ Ωᶜ_{O_X(U)/O_Y(V)} (localisation compatibility, Huber 1.6.3(iv), R0/continuous-differentials) is free.
acceptance: For D → Spa(K, K°) the module Ωᶜ is free of rank 1; for the node Spa(K⟨T₁,T₂⟩/(T₁T₂)) it is not locally free at the origin, so that space is not smooth.
Scheme analogue: Mathlib Algebra.FormallySmooth (Ω projective and H¹ of the cotangent complex zero).

nodes.title: Jacobian criterion for closed subspaces of smooth spaces (Huber 1.6.9(ii))
nodes.statement: Let g: Z → Y be a smooth morphism of locally noetherian adic spaces (so that J is finitely generated and R0/continuous-differentials applies), X ⊆ Z a closed adic subspace with ideal sheaf J (R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings), and x ∈ X. Then X → Y is étale (resp. smooth) on an open neighbourhood of x if and only if there are sections g₁,…,g_r of J on a neighbourhood of x generating J there such that dg₁,…,dg_r form a basis (resp. part of a basis) of the free module Ω_{Z/Y} near x (R0/smooth-differentials-locally-free). (Huber 1996, Proposition 1.6.9(ii), stated there with generators of the stalk J_x whose differentials form (resp. extend to) a basis of the stalk (Ω_{Z/Y})_x; the two forms agree after shrinking, the modules being of finite presentation.)
hypotheses: g smooth; Z, Y locally noetherian
X closed in Z with finitely generated ideal J, x ∈ X
proofSteps: (⇐) With generators whose differentials are (part of) a basis, the conormal map J/J² → Ω_{Z/Y} ⊗ O_X (R0/conormal-sequence) is split injective and its cokernel Ω_{X/Y} is free (resp. zero); lift morphisms from square-zero thickenings along the smooth Z (Definition 1.6.5) and correct the lift by a derivation to land in X, using the splitting (EGA IV 17.12.1 transported).

(⇒) If X is smooth near x, the conormal sequence of X ⊆ Z is split exact on the left (as in R0/smooth-differentials-locally-free), so J/J² is locally free and a basis of J/J² near x maps to part of a basis of Ω_{Z/Y}; lift it to generators of J on a rational neighbourhood (J finitely generated, Nakayama); for étale X the cokernel Ω_{X/Y} is 0 (unramified part, by the lifting definition and the universal derivation), so the image is a full basis.
acceptance: For Z = D over Spa(K, K°) and X = V(T² − a) with a ∈ K^×, 2 ∈ K^×: d(T² − a) = 2T dT is a basis on X (T is a unit there), so X → Spa(K, K°) is étale.
Public use: Zavyalov, Foundational results, Lemma 5.9.

nodes.title: Differential criterion for étale and smooth morphisms between smooth spaces (Huber 1.6.9(iii))
nodes.statement: Let X and X' be locally noetherian adic spaces smooth over Y and h: X → X' a Y-morphism, x ∈ X. Then h is étale on a neighbourhood of x if and only if the canonical map h*Ω_{X'/Y} → Ω_{X/Y} is bijective at x (on the stalk, equivalently after ⊗ k(x)); h is smooth on a neighbourhood of x if and only if this map is injective with a left inverse (split injective) near x. (Huber 1996, Proposition 1.6.9(iii), states this with X smooth over Y and X' = Z only locally of finite type over Y; the node assumes X' smooth, which is the case used downstream and the hypothesis EGA IV 17.11.2 needs in the étale direction.)
hypotheses: X, X' smooth over Y; X, X', Y locally noetherian
h a Y-morphism
proofSteps: Both sides are locally free (R0/smooth-differentials-locally-free); the map comes from the first fundamental sequence O_X ⊗ Ω_{X'/Y} → Ω_{X/Y} → Ω_{X/X'} → 0 (R0/first-fundamental-sequence).

(⇐) Bijectivity at x spreads to a neighbourhood (finite free modules, determinant a unit on a rational neighbourhood); then Ω_{X/X'} = 0, so h is unramified (R0/infinitesimal-criteria); h is locally of finite presentation (cancellation of finiteness, Huber 1994 Lemma 3.5(iv)); smoothness of h follows by lifting along X' and correcting with the split derivations (EGA IV 17.11.1-17.11.2 transported); étale = smooth + unramified.
(⇒) If h is étale then Ω_{X/X'} = 0 and the left exactness of the first fundamental sequence for smooth h (EGA IV 17.2.3 transported) gives bijectivity; the smooth case is analogous.
acceptance: The map U → D^d of Zavyalov (Foundational results, Lemma 5.9), sending Tᵢ to functions gᵢ with dgᵢ a basis of Ω, is étale; this is the step used in R0/smooth-local-structure.

nodes.title: Finite étale adic spaces over a noetherian affinoid are finite étale algebras (Huber 1.6.6(ii))
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a complete strongly noetherian Tate Huber pair. The functor C ↦ Spa(Huber.Pair.finiteAlgebra C) (R0/finite-algebra-over-affinoid), from finite étale A-algebras (Mathlib Algebra.Etale A C with C a finite A-module) and A-algebra maps, to adic spaces X with a finite (R0/finite-morphism) and étale (R0/differentials-unramified-smooth-etale) morphism X → Spa(A, A⁺) and Spa(A, A⁺)-morphisms, is an equivalence of categories, with quasi-inverse X ↦ O_X(X). The plus ring of the adic space attached to C is the integral closure of A⁺ in C. (Huber states 1.6.6(ii) for noetherian complete f-adic A; the essential surjectivity beyond the strongly noetherian Tate case rests on [Hu4] and is recorded as a gap.)
hypotheses: A complete strongly noetherian Tate ring (the construction of R0/finite-algebra-over-affinoid and Zavyalov B.2.18 are available here)
proofSteps: Full faithfulness: Spa(A, A⁺)-morphisms Spa(C', C'⁺) → Spa(C, C⁺) are morphisms of Huber pairs (C, C⁺) → (C', C'⁺) over (A, A⁺) (Huber 1994 Proposition 2.1, anchor Layer 5; the spaces are adic since C, C' are strongly noetherian, Huber 1994 Theorem 2.2), which are the A-algebra maps C → C' (universal property of R0/finite-algebra-over-affinoid).

Algebraic étale ⇒ adic étale: Spa C → Spa A is finite, hence locally of finite type = locally of finite presentation over the analytic base; for the lifting, Y-morphisms Spa D → Spa C are A-algebra maps C → D (continuity and plus rings automatic), and Algebra.FormallyEtale A C gives bijectivity of Hom_A(C, D) → Hom_A(C, D/I) (Mathlib Algebra.FormallyEtale.iff_comp_bijective).

Finite and adic étale ⇒ algebraic étale: X = Spa(C, C⁺) with C finite over A (Zavyalov B.2.18); Ω_{X/Y} = 0 (R0/infinitesimal-criteria) and Ωᶜ = Ω[C⁄A] for finite C (R0/continuous-differentials (d)), so C is formally unramified; A → C is flat (R0/etale-flat-unramified and R0/etale-ring-flatness, or Zavyalov B.4.3); C is finitely presented (finite over noetherian); hence Algebra.Etale A C (Mathlib Algebra.Etale.of_formallyUnramified_of_flat).
acceptance: For A = K a complete nonarchimedean field: finite étale adic spaces over Spa(K, K°) are the finite disjoint unions of Spa(L, L°) for L/K finite separable (Mathlib Algebra.Etale.iff_exists_algEquiv_prod over a field).

Kedlaya–Liu, Lemma 8.2.17(a): for adic Banach rings, finite étale morphisms to Spa(A, A⁺) (in their ad hoc sense) ≃ FÉt(A); this node identifies Huber's finite étale morphisms with the same category in the strongly noetherian case.

nodes.title: Morphisms of Huber pairs of algebraically finite type
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a Huber pair (not necessarily complete). For finite subsets M₁,…,Mₙ ⊆ A with each MᵢA open, let A[X₁,…,Xₙ]_M be the polynomial ring A[X] with the subspace topology of A⟨X⟩_M (Huber 1994, §3; for Tate A and Mᵢ = {1} the Gauss-norm topology) and plus ring the integral closure of A⁺[m·Xᵢ : m ∈ Mᵢ, 1 ≤ i ≤ n]. A morphism of Huber pairs φ: (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) is of algebraically finite type if it factors through a quotient mapping A[X₁,…,Xₙ]_M → B, i.e. a surjective, continuous, open ring homomorphism with B⁺ the integral closure of the image of the plus ring. This is the polynomial analogue of Huber's topologically finite type and is equivalent to Huber 1996, Definition 1.2.5(ii) (A^▷ → B^▷ adic with rings of definition A₀ → B₀ of finite type, and B⁺ the integral closure of an open subring D with A⁺ → D of algebraically finite type), by Remark 1.2.6(ii)-(iii) (choose the weights so that the images of the m·Xᵢ generate a ring of definition over A₀); it is the notion used in Corollary 1.7.3(iii); the completion of such a φ is topologically of finite type, and Spa B = Spa B̂.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) Huber pair, completeness not required
Mᵢ finite with MᵢA open
proofSteps: Definition as stated; the topology of A[X]_M is the one induced from A⟨X⟩_M (Huber 1994, p. 533).

Completion: the completion of A[X]_M is A⟨X⟩_M (Huber 1994, §3; anchor Layer 0.4, Wedhorn 5.49 density of polynomials), and completion preserves quotient mappings, so φ̂ is topologically of finite type.
acceptance: For the p-adic Huber pair (W(κ)[1/p][T^{±1}], W(κ)[T^{±1}]) → (R₀, R₀⁺) of Scholze 2013 Lemma 6.12, (R₀, R₀⁺) is of algebraically finite type and its completion is the étale affinoid (R, R⁺).

nodes.title: Standard étale presentation of étale affinoid maps (Huber 1.7.1)
nodes.statement: Let A = (A, A⁺) be a Huber pair (not necessarily complete) whose completion is of noetherian type or discrete (R0/noetherian-type-huber-ring; Huber's standing assumption (1.1.1), used in point (3) of the proof) and s: X → Y = Spa A a morphism of adic spaces with X affinoid. The following are equivalent: (i) s is étale (R0/differentials-unramified-smooth-etale); (ii) there are n ≥ 0, finite subsets T₁,…,Tₙ ⊆ A with each TᵢA open, and f₁,…,fₙ ∈ B := A⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩_{T₁,…,Tₙ} such that, with I = (f₁,…,fₙ) ⊆ B, the image of det(∂fᵢ/∂Xⱼ) in B/I is a unit and X is Y-isomorphic to Spa(B/I); (iii) the same with f₁,…,fₙ ∈ A[X₁,…,Xₙ]. Here B/I is the quotient Huber pair (plus ring the integral closure of the image), and Spa(B/I) is Spa of its completion. The number of equations equals the number of variables. If A is Tate, the presentation in (iii) can be chosen with T₁ = … = Tₙ = {1} (Huber 1996, Corollary 1.7.2(ii)).
hypotheses: X affinoid, Y = Spa A affinoid (A not necessarily complete)
Â of noetherian type or discrete (so every affinoid ring topologically of finite type over A is noetherian or discrete)
proofSteps: (i) ⇒ (ii): the affinoid ring map of an affinoid morphism locally of finite type is of topologically finite type (R0/finite-type-morphism-classes), so X ≅ Spa(C/J) with C = A⟨X₁,…,X_m⟩_T; since X is étale, Ω_{X/Y} = 0 and J/J² ≅ Ω_{C/A} ⊗ C/J (R0/conormal-sequence, R0/infinitesimal-criteria, R0/jacobian-criterion-closed-subspace), a free module on the dXᵢ (R0/continuous-differentials (c)). Choose f₁,…,f_m ∈ J whose classes form a basis of J/J²; then J = (f₁,…,f_m) + J² gives j ∈ J with (1 + j)J ⊆ (f₁,…,f_m) (J finitely generated); invert 1 + j by a rational localisation (X ⊆ {1 + j invertible}; R0/open-embedding-etale) presented by an extra variable X_{m+1} with f_{m+1} = 1 − (1 + j)X_{m+1}; the Jacobian of (f₁,…,f_{m+1}) is a unit on X.

(ii) ⇒ (iii) (Huber pp. 84-85): with Δ the Jacobian, choose s₁,…,s_m ∈ A with {sⱼ}·A open and v(sⱼ) ≤ v(Δ) ≠ 0 on Spa(B/I), and U = {v(sⱼ) ≤ v(Δ) ≠ 0} rational in Spa B; replace the fᵢ by nearby polynomials fᵢ + sᵢ' (polynomials are dense in A⟨X⟩_T) — R0/etale-presentation-perturbation (Huber 1.7.2(i), whose proof contains Huber's preparatory points (1)-(4)) gives Spa(B/I') ≅ Spa(B/I) over Spa A with unit Jacobian.

(iii) ⇒ (i): Spa B → Y is smooth (R0/restricted-power-series-smooth); Spa(B/I) is a closed subspace cut out by f₁,…,fₙ whose differentials form a basis of Ωᶜ_{B/A} ⊗ B/I (unit Jacobian), hence étale over Y (R0/jacobian-criterion-closed-subspace); isomorphisms and open embeddings are étale (R0/open-embedding-etale).

Tate refinement (Huber 1.7.2(ii)): over a Tate A every affinoid ring topologically of finite type over A is a quotient of some A⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩ (Huber 1994 Lemma 3.5(iii)), so (i) ⇒ (ii) can be run with all weights {1} (the variable inverting 1 + j has weight {1}), and (ii) ⇒ (iii) does not change the weights.
acceptance: Tate case: over a Tate A all Tᵢ can be taken {1}, so X ≅ Spa(A⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩/(f₁,…,fₙ)) with unit Jacobian (Huber 1.7.2(ii)).
Instance: for n ∈ K^×, the Kummer cover of the annulus is Spa(K⟨S^{±1}⟩⟨T⟩/(Tⁿ − S)) with Jacobian nTⁿ⁻¹ a unit.

nodes.title: Stability of standard étale presentations under perturbation (Huber 1.7.2)
nodes.statement: Let A be a Huber pair whose completion is of noetherian type or discrete (Huber's standing assumption), B = A⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩_{T₁,…,Tₙ} and f₁,…,fₙ ∈ B such that det(∂fᵢ/∂Xⱼ) is a unit in B/(f₁,…,fₙ). For every neighbourhood V of 0 in B/(f) there is a neighbourhood S of 0 in B such that for all f'₁,…,f'ₙ with f'ᵢ − fᵢ ∈ S, the Jacobian of (f') is a unit in B/(f') and there is a Spa A-isomorphism e: Spa(B/(f)) → Spa(B/(f')) with e*(x̄'ᵢ) ∈ x̄ᵢ + V (x̄ᵢ, x̄'ᵢ the images of Xᵢ) (Huber 1996, Corollary 1.7.2(i)). The Tate refinement Tᵢ = {1} (Corollary 1.7.2(ii)) is stated in R0/etale-local-structure.
hypotheses: As in Huber 1.7.1(ii); Â of noetherian type or discrete (point (3) below)
proofSteps: Point (1) (Huber p. 81): for fᵢ = Σ a_{i,ν}X^ν ∈ A[[X]] (A complete f-adic) with coefficients in powers of a bounded set, fᵢ(0) = 0 and det(a_{i,e_j}) ∈ A^×, the fᵢ converge on a neighbourhood U of 0 in Aⁿ and map every neighbourhood of 0 in U onto a neighbourhood of 0 (formal inverse function theorem, Bourbaki Algèbre III.4.4 Prop. 5 — not in the baseline — plus convergence estimates).

Point (2) (p. 82): if g: A⟨X⟩_T → C is adic with the Jacobian invertible in C, every small (v₁,…,vₙ) equals (h(fᵢ) − g(fᵢ)) for a continuous h with h(Xᵢ) − g(Xᵢ) small (from (1) applied to m_i = s(r(fᵢ) − g(fᵢ)) in C⟨X⟩).

Point (3) (p. 83): for C complete, topologically of finite type over A with topological generators bᵢ, every continuous A-endomorphism f of C with f(bᵢ) close to bᵢ is an automorphism with f⁻¹(bᵢ) close to bᵢ (uses that C is noetherian or discrete, and Bourbaki Algèbre commutative III.2.9 Cor. 3). Point (4) (pp. 83-84): for U rational in Spa A⟨X⟩_T, Spa A-morphisms U → Spa A⟨X⟩_T with f*(Xᵢ) close to Xᵢ|U map U isomorphically onto U (with Huber 1993, 3.10, stability of rational subsets under perturbation).

Corollary 1.7.2(i) (p. 85): with Δ the Jacobian and U = {v(sᵢ) ≤ v(Δ) ≠ 0} ⊇ Spa(B/I) rational in Spa B, the morphisms f_h: U → U with f_h*(Xᵢ) = hᵢ + Xᵢ|U (h small) are automorphisms close to the identity by (4), every small perturbation of the fᵢ is realised as f_h*(fᵢ) by (2), and the f_h⁻¹ induce e.
acceptance: Over K: Spa(K⟨T⟩/(T² − a − ε)) ≅ Spa(K⟨T⟩/(T² − a)) for a ∈ K with |a| = 1, 2 ∈ K^×, and |ε| small (Krasner-type perturbation).

nodes.title: Algebraic models of affinoid étale maps (Huber 1.7.3(iii))
nodes.statement: Let A = (A, A⁺) be a Huber pair (not necessarily complete) whose completion is of noetherian type or discrete (as in R0/etale-local-structure) and Y → Spa A a morphism with Y affinoid. Then Y → Spa A is étale if and only if Y is Spa A-isomorphic to Spa B for a morphism of Huber pairs A → B of algebraically finite type (R0/algebraically-finite-type-ring-map) whose underlying ring map A → B is étale (Mathlib Algebra.Etale). (Huber 1996, Corollary 1.7.3(iii).)
hypotheses: Y affinoid; A need not be complete (e.g. the p-adic pair (W(κ)[1/p][T^{±1}], W(κ)[T^{±1}]))
Â of noetherian type or discrete (inherited from R0/etale-local-structure)
proofSteps: (⇒) By R0/etale-local-structure (iii), Y ≅ Spa(B'/I) with B' = A⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩_T and f₁,…,fₙ ∈ A[X] with Jacobian Δ a unit on Y. Let B = A[X₁,…,Xₙ, X_{n+1}]/(f₁,…,fₙ, 1 − ΔX_{n+1}) with weights T and, for X_{n+1}, a finite set T_{n+1} with T_{n+1}·Δ⁻¹ power-bounded on Y. Then A → B has a submersive presentation of relative dimension 0 (Jacobian −Δ·det(∂f/∂X) invertible), so Algebra.Etale A B (Mathlib Algebra.Etale.iff_isStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension_zero), A → B is of algebraically finite type, and Spa B ≅ Y (completion, R0/algebraically-finite-type-ring-map).

(⇐) Let A → B be of algebraically finite type with A → B étale, L ⊆ B⁺ finite with A₀[L] a ring of definition of B and B⁺ the integral closure of A⁺[L] (Huber Remark 1.2.6(ii)-(iii); api exists_fg_plus of R0/algebraically-finite-type-ring-map). Mathlib gives a submersive presentation B = A[Y₁,…,Y_m]/(g₁,…,g_m) with unit Jacobian (Algebra.Etale.iff_isStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension_zero). Adjoin variables Z_l (l ∈ L) with relations Z_l − p_l(Y), p_l a polynomial representing l: the Jacobian stays a unit (block triangular) and the numbers of variables and relations stay equal. Give Z_l the weight {1} and Y_j weights T_j ⊆ A with T_j·y_j ⊆ A₀[L] (possible since y_j times a topologically nilpotent sequence of A tends to 0); then A[Y, Z]_{T,1} → B is a quotient mapping (its image contains the ring of definition A₀[L]). Completing (ideals of the noetherian completion are closed, R0/noetherian-type-ideals-closed) gives a presentation as in R0/etale-local-structure (iii), so Spa B → Spa A is étale. (Huber instead argues via Corollary 1.7.3(i)-(ii), the étaleness of X^ad for étale schemes X.)
acceptance: Consumer instance (Scholze 2013, Lemma 6.12; PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/etale-algebras-over-torus-models): for U = Spa(R, R⁺) affinoid of finite type over Spa(W(κ)[1/p], W(κ)) with an étale map U → Tⁿ, apply this lemma with A = (W(κ)[1/p][T^{±1}], W(κ)[T^{±1}]) (Spa A = Tⁿ) to get (R₀, R₀⁺) with R₀ étale over W(κ)[1/p][T^{±1}] and completion (R, R⁺); Huber's Remark 1.2.6(iii) (API exists_fg_plus of R0/algebraically-finite-type-ring-map, see gaps) and excellence of W(κ) then give R₀⁺ finitely generated with R⁺ its p-adic completion.

nodes.title: Smooth morphisms are locally étale over relative polydiscs (Huber 1.6.10)
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a Huber pair whose completion is of noetherian type or discrete, and f: X → Spa A a morphism of adic spaces (Huber 1996, Corollary 1.6.10). Then f is smooth if and only if every x ∈ X has an open neighbourhood U for which there are n ≥ 0, finite subsets M₁,…,Mₙ ⊆ A with each MᵢA open, and an étale morphism g: U → Spa A⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩_M with f|_U equal to the composite of g and the structure morphism (Huber's diagram (*)). If A is Tate and f is smooth, one can take M₁ = … = Mₙ = {1}, i.e. g: U → Spa A⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩ étale.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) Huber pair with Â of noetherian type or discrete (continuous differentials, R0/smooth-differentials-locally-free); Tate for the simplified form
proofSteps: (⇒) Ω_{X/Spa A} is locally free (R0/smooth-differentials-locally-free); choose sᵢ ∈ O_X(U) with dsᵢ a basis near x, and finite Mᵢ with Mᵢ·sᵢ ⊆ O_X⁺(U) (if A is Tate, replace sᵢ by ϖ^k sᵢ, which keeps dsᵢ a basis, so Mᵢ = {1} suffices).

Define g by the universal property of A⟨X⟩_M (Huber 1994 Lemma 3.5(i)), Xᵢ ↦ sᵢ; g*Ω of the polydisc (free on dXᵢ, R0/continuous-differentials (c)) → Ω_{U/Spa A} is bijective near x, so g is étale near x (R0/differential-criterion-morphism; the polydisc is smooth, R0/restricted-power-series-smooth).

(⇐) The polydisc is smooth (R0/restricted-power-series-smooth), composites are smooth (R0/etale-smooth-composition) and smoothness is local on the source (R0/etale-smooth-locality; see the gap recorded there).

nodes.title: Étale morphisms of affinoids over a field embed locally into finite étale covers (de Jong–van der Put 3.1.4)
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field with a nontrivial rank-one valuation and f: Y → X an étale morphism (R0/differentials-unramified-smooth-etale) of affinoid adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°), X = Spa(A, A°) and Y = Spa(B, B°) with A, B K-affinoid algebras. (i) For every rank-one point a ∈ X there are a rational subset U ⊆ X containing the closure of {a}, a K-affinoid algebra C that is finite étale over O_X(U) (so that g: Z = Spa(C, C°) → U is finite and étale, R0/finite-etale-algebra-comparison) and an open embedding h: f⁻¹(U) → Z with f|_{f⁻¹(U)} = g ∘ h. (ii) Consequently X is covered by finitely many such rational subsets U_1, …, U_m, and each f⁻¹(U_j) is covered by finitely many subsets T' that are rational in Y and (via h_j) in Z_j; on each T' the morphism f is the composite of a rational embedding T' ⊆ Z_j, the finite étale Z_j → U_j and the rational embedding U_j ⊆ X.
hypotheses: K complete, nontrivially rank-one valued
X, Y affinoid and locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°)
f étale
proofSteps: (i) is R0/etale-local-open-finite-etale-factorisation (b) (Huber 2.2.8 with Scholze's refinement to a rational neighbourhood U of the closure of a rank-one point a), applied to the étale f: Y → X of affinoids of finite type over Spa(K, K°) (coordinate rings strongly noetherian); Z = Spa(C, C°) with C finite étale over O_X(U) (R0/finite-algebra-over-affinoid, R0/finite-etale-algebra-comparison).

(ii): every point of X specialises from a rank-one point (anchor Layer 2), and a rational subset containing the closure of a rank-one point contains its specialisations; X is quasi-compact and the rank-one points' neighbourhoods U from (i) are open, so finitely many U_j cover X.

Rational refinements: every quasi-compact open subset of an affinoid adic space is a finite union of rational subsets, and a rational subset of a rational subset is rational (anchor Layer 2); a rational subset of Z_j contained in the rational subset h_j(f⁻¹(U_j)) is rational there, hence in f⁻¹(U_j) and in Y.

Comparison with the source: de Jong–van der Put prove (i) for rigid affinoids with wide neighbourhoods, using their Lemma 2.1.1/Remark 2.1.2 (finite separable extensions of the completed residue field spread to finite étale covers of a wide neighbourhood), Lemma 3.1.5 and Lemma 3.1.6; under the dictionary (étale = flat with Ω = 0, dJvdP Observation 3.1.1; analytic points = rank-one points; wide neighbourhoods = rational neighbourhoods of closures) their statement is the one above. The adic proof via Huber 2.2.8 avoids formalising those rigid-analytic lemmas.
acceptance: The Kummer map f: Y = {|T| = 1} → X = {|T| = 1}, T ↦ Tⁿ, on the unit circle over K of characteristic prime to n is finite étale; (i) holds with U = X, Z = Y, h = id.
The rational embedding Y = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|} ⊆ X = Spa(K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩) is étale and not finite; (i) holds with Z = U = X and h the inclusion, so the finite étale factor can be trivial.
Scholze 2013, Proposition 9.2(ii): the étale base change of proper coherent cohomology reduces by (ii) to rational embeddings and finite étale maps.

nodes.title: Étale maps are locally open embeddings into finite étale covers (Huber 2.2.8)
nodes.statement: (a) (Huber 1996, Lemma 2.2.8) Let f: X → Y be an étale morphism between analytic affinoid adic spaces with noetherian (strongly noetherian Tate) coordinate rings. Then every y ∈ Y has an open neighbourhood U such that f⁻¹(U) → U factors as an open embedding f⁻¹(U) → Z followed by a finite étale morphism Z → U. (b) (Scholze 2013, proof of Lemma 5.2: 'with similar analysis of its proof') If y is a maximal point, U can be taken to be a rational subset containing the closure of {y}. (c) Consequently, a morphism f: X → Y of locally noetherian analytic adic spaces (R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space) is étale (R0/differentials-unramified-smooth-etale) if and only if for every x ∈ X there are open subspaces U ∋ x of X and V ⊇ f(U) of Y, an adic space W, an open embedding U → W and a finite (R0/finite-morphism) étale morphism W → V such that f|_U: U → V is the composite. (This is the characterisation of étale maps used as a definition by Kedlaya–Liu, Definition 8.2.16, and for perfectoid spaces by Scholze–Weinstein, Definition 7.5.1.)
hypotheses: X, Y locally noetherian analytic adic spaces (Huber: analytic affinoid under the standing assumption (1.1.1))
f étale
proofSteps: (c) (⇐): open embeddings and finite étale maps are étale (R0/open-embedding-etale), composites of étale maps are étale (R0/etale-smooth-composition), and étaleness is local on the source (R0/etale-smooth-locality). (c) (⇒) follows from (a) applied to affinoid opens X' ∋ x, Y' ⊇ f(X').

(a), algebraic model: by Huber 1.7.3(iii) (R0/etale-algebraic-model) X ≅ Spa B with A → B of algebraically finite type and A^▷ → B^▷ étale (Y = Spa A). Zariski's main theorem, local form (Mathlib Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt.exists_fg_and_exists_notMem_and_awayMap_bijective, applied at the finitely many primes of B over supp(y) and combining the finite subalgebras): a finite A-subalgebra C ⊆ B and g ∈ C, invertible at those primes, with C_g ≅ B_g. Put T = Spa(C, C⁺) (R0/finite-algebra-over-affinoid; h: T → Y finite), S = {t : g(t) ≠ 0} ⊆ T (Zariski-open; its rational pieces are Spa of algebraically finite type étale algebras C_g, so h|S is étale by R0/etale-algebraic-model), and X' = {x ∈ X : g(x) ≠ 0} ⊆ X, which contains every point over the generalisations G of y (they have support over supp(y), Huber 1.1.9) and maps by an open embedding j into S. Since X ∖ X' is closed and f(X ∖ X') is pro-constructible and disjoint from G (R0/spectral-map-image-proconstructible), shrinking Y around y reduces to X = X'.

(a), separation (Huber): the maximal points tᵢ of h⁻¹(G) are finitely many (h finite, generalizing; R0/quasi-finite-fibre-criteria) and lie over the maximal point of G; the closures T̄ᵢ of {tᵢ} in h⁻¹(G) are disjoint with union h⁻¹(G) (Huber 1.1.10(i),(v)), and each lies in S or in T ∖ S (analytic specialisations have the same support). Choose quasi-compact opens V' ⊆ S, V'' of T cutting out ⋃_{T̄ᵢ ⊆ S} T̄ᵢ and ⋃_{T̄ᵢ ⊄ S} T̄ᵢ on h⁻¹(G); then h⁻¹(G) ⊆ V' ∪ V'', h⁻¹(G) ∩ V' ∩ V'' = ∅, h⁻¹(G) ∩ j(X) ⊆ V'. As G is the intersection of the quasi-compact open neighbourhoods of y, some quasi-compact open U ∋ y satisfies the same three conditions with h⁻¹(U) (compactness in the constructible topology). Z := h⁻¹(U) ∩ V' is closed in h⁻¹(U), so g = h|_Z is finite; V' ⊆ S, so g is étale; j restricts to an open embedding f⁻¹(U) → Z.

(b): run the same argument with N = closure{y} in place of G: h⁻¹(N) is the disjoint union of the closures of the maximal points of h⁻¹(y) (h finite hence specializing, Huber 1.1.10), each inside S or T ∖ S, and N is the intersection of the rational subsets containing it (R0/maximal-point-closure-rational), so U can be chosen rational ⊇ N.
acceptance: Scholze 2013, proof of Lemma 5.2: for f: V → Bⁿ étale with V affinoid and y ∈ Bⁿ with closure N, there is a rational W ⊆ Bⁿ containing N such that f⁻¹(W) → W factors as an open embedding into Z followed by a finite étale Z → W.

nodes.title: Étale toric charts on smooth affinoids (Scholze 2013, Lemma 5.2)
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field, V an affinoid adic space smooth over Spa(K, K°), and x ∈ V with closure M = closure{x} ⊆ V. Then there is a rational subset U ⊆ V containing M together with an étale morphism U → Tⁿ = Spa(K⟨T₁^{±1},…,Tₙ^{±1}⟩, K°⟨T₁^{±1},…,Tₙ^{±1}⟩) which factors as a composite of rational embeddings and finite étale maps.
hypotheses: K complete nonarchimedean field (rank one)
V affinoid, smooth over Spa(K, K°)
proofSteps: Replace x by its maximal (rank-one) generalisation a: closure{x} ⊆ closure{a}, so it suffices to treat a (a rational U ⊇ closure{a} contains M). For maximal a, closure{a} is the intersection of the rational subsets of V containing it, and every open subset containing closure{a} contains such a rational subset (R0/maximal-point-closure-rational, Huber 1.5.10). (Scholze asserts this intersection property for arbitrary x; it fails for non-maximal x, since every open containing x contains a.)

There is an étale map f: V' → Bⁿ on a rational V' ⊆ V containing closure{a}: R0/smooth-local-structure (Tate case) gives sᵢ with dsᵢ a basis of Ω near a and g: → Bⁿ étale near a; the loci where the dsᵢ form a basis and where g is étale are of the form {|Δ| ≠ 0} for a determinant Δ (R0/differential-criterion-morphism), hence contain every specialisation of a (analytic specialisations have the same support), i.e. closure{a}; shrink to a rational subset by R0/maximal-point-closure-rational.

With y = f(x), a its rank-one generalisation and N the closure of y (contained in the closure of a), there is a rational W ⊆ Bⁿ containing the closure of a, hence N, such that f⁻¹(W) → W factors as an open embedding f⁻¹(W) → Z followed by a finite étale Z → W (R0/etale-local-open-finite-etale-factorisation (b), Huber 2.2.8 with Scholze's refinement; equivalently R0/etale-affinoid-finite-etale-embedding (i)).
Choose an open U ⊆ f⁻¹(W) containing M that is rational in Z (hence in f⁻¹(W) and in V; anchor Layer 2, rational subsets of rational subsets are rational).
Embed Bⁿ ⊆ Tⁿ as the rational subset {|Tᵢ − 1| ≤ |ϖ|} (Tᵢ = 1 + ϖXᵢ); then U → Z → W ⊆ Bⁿ ⊆ Tⁿ is the required composite.
acceptance: For V = Bⁿ itself and any x, U = V and the chart Bⁿ ⊆ Tⁿ (a rational embedding).

Consumers: Scholze 2013, Lemmas 4.5, 5.3 and §6 (PadicHodgeTheory:P8), where étale maps V → Tⁿ that are composites of rational embeddings and finite étale maps are the input to the perfectoid tower V ×_{Tⁿ} T̃ⁿ.
