nodes.title: Étale equals flat and unramified for analytic adic spaces (Huber 1.7.5)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism locally of finite type between analytic adic spaces, with Y locally noetherian (Huber's standing assumption (1.1.1); needed by Lemma 1.7.6, R0/etale-ring-flatness). The following are equivalent: (a) f is étale; (b) f is flat (R0/flat-morphism) and unramified (R0/unramified-morphism); (c) for every maximal point x ∈ X, O_{X,x} is flat over O_{Y,f(x)} and O_{X,x}/𝔪_{f(x)}O_{X,x} is a finite separable field extension of the residue field of O_{Y,f(x)}.
hypotheses: X, Y analytic; Y locally noetherian
f locally of finite type
proofSteps: (a) ⇒ (b): f is unramified by definition. Flatness: for x ∈ X choose affinoid neighbourhoods U ∋ x, V ⊇ f(U); for every rational V' ⊆ V and rational U' ⊆ U ∩ f⁻¹(V'), U' → V' is étale (R0/etale-smooth-locality restricted to opens) between affinoids, so O_Y(V') → O_X(U') is flat (Huber Lemma 1.7.6, R0/etale-ring-flatness); passing to the filtered colimits gives flatness of O_{Y,f(x)} → O_{X,x}.

(b) ⇒ (c): f is locally quasi-finite (R0/unramified-locally-quasi-finite); at a maximal x the stalk is finite over O_{Y,f(x)} (R0/quasi-finite-stalk-criterion), and A := O_{X,x}/𝔪_{f(x)}O_{X,x} is finite over k(f(x)) with Ω_{A/k(f(x))} = 0 (Ω_{X/Y} = 0 by R0/infinitesimal-criteria and R0/quasi-finite-stalk-differentials), hence a finite separable field extension (A is local).

(c) ⇒ (b): flatness at maximal points spreads to all points because O_{X,y} → O_{X,x} is local and flat for x ≻ y (Huber 1.1.10(iii)); f is locally quasi-finite by R0/quasi-finite-fibre-criteria; by R0/quasi-finite-stalk-differentials and Nakayama Ω_{X/Y,x} = 0 at maximal points, hence Ω_{X/Y} = 0 and f is unramified (R0/infinitesimal-criteria).

(b) ⇒ (a): assume X, Y affinoid; by R0/infinitesimal-criteria (d) f = h ∘ g with g: X → Z a closed embedding and h: Z → Y étale; it suffices that g is flat (a flat closed embedding cut out by a finitely generated ideal is an open embedding: the ideal is stalkwise idempotent, Stacks 04PW for schemes; then f is étale by R0/open-embedding-etale, R0/etale-smooth-composition). Write g = p ∘ s with s: X → X ×_Y Z the graph and p the projection. f is locally quasi-finite (R0/unramified-locally-quasi-finite) and flat, so its base change p is flat (Huber 1.6.4(ii), proposed node R0/flat-quasi-finite-base-change); s is the pullback of the diagonal of h, an open embedding since h is unramified (R0/infinitesimal-criteria (c)), hence flat.
acceptance: The closed embedding of the origin into D is unramified but not flat, hence not étale; the Frobenius S ↦ T^p in characteristic p is flat but not unramified, hence not étale.
Scheme analogue: Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.iff_flat_and_formallyUnramified; ring analogue Algebra.Etale.of_formallyUnramified_of_flat.

nodes.title: Flatness of the ring map of an étale affinoid morphism (Huber 1.7.6)
nodes.statement: Let s: X → Y be an étale morphism between affinoid adic spaces, Y = Spa(A, A⁺) with A complete, and assume that A has a noetherian ring of definition or that A is a strongly noetherian Tate ring. Then O_Y(Y) → O_X(X) is flat.
hypotheses: Y affinoid with A having a noetherian ring of definition, or A strongly noetherian Tate (the only two cases proved in the source)
proofSteps: Case (i), noetherian ring of definition: by R0/etale-local-structure, O_X(X) is the completion of an algebraically étale A-algebra C_Δ; B is flat over A[X] ([Hu1, 1.7.i], completion of noetherian adic rings), and C_Δ is étale over A, hence flat.

Case (ii), strongly noetherian Tate: reduce to n = 1, show that pA⟨X⟩ is prime for the relevant p, and use that torsion-free modules over localisations of Dedekind rings are flat (as in Huber's proof).
acceptance: For A = K a field every module is flat; for the rational embedding {|T| ≤ |ϖ|} ⊆ D, K⟨T⟩ → K⟨T, T/ϖ⟩ is flat (also tauceti TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.flat_toCompletionLoc for rational localisations).
Zavyalov, Quotients, Remark B.4.4: without a strongly noetherian hypothesis, even flatness of rational localisations is open; this lemma asserts nothing beyond the two cases.

Why only the two noetherian cases are asserted.

nodes.title: Smooth and étale morphisms are open (Huber 1.7.7-1.7.9)
nodes.statement: Every smooth morphism f: X → Y of adic spaces is an open map |X| → |Y|; in particular étale morphisms are open.
hypotheses: f smooth
proofSteps: (1.7.7) Locally, f is algebraically smooth: by R0/smooth-local-structure and R0/etale-algebraic-model, f is locally Spa B → Spa A with A → B adic, A → B flat and finitely presented, and B⁺ the integral closure of A⁺[L] for a finite L (R0/algebraically-finite-type-ring-map).

(1.7.9) For such A → B, Spa B → Spa A is open: Spv(f) is open by [HK, 2.1.4] (Huber–Knebusch, not public; recorded as a gap), and the retractions r_A, r_B of the valuation spectra onto Spa (AdicSpaces anchor Layer 1.4) transport openness to Spa.
Openness is local on the source, and open embeddings are open.
acceptance: The squaring map on {|T| = 1} (étale) is open; the closed embedding of the origin is not open (not smooth).
Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 8.2.17(b) and §9 use that étale maps are open.

nodes.title: The affine chart of X ×_Y S: the increasing union of the affinoids Spa(A_k, A_k⁺) and its universal property on affinoid test objects
nodes.statement: Let λ: B → A be a ring homomorphism, where (A, A⁺) is a complete Huber pair such that A has a noetherian ring of definition or is a strongly noetherian Tate ring, and let C = B[T₁,…,Tₙ]/I be a finitely generated B-algebra. Choose a finite set E of topologically nilpotent elements of A with E·A open, and put E(k) = {e₁⋯e_k : eᵢ ∈ E} for k ≥ 1. Let A(k) = A⟨T₁,…,Tₙ⟩_{E(k),…,E(k)} be Huber's restricted power-series ring with weights E(k) (the separated completion of the weighted restricted series ring, with plus ring the integral closure of the series whose ν-th coefficient lies in E(k)^{|ν|}·A⁺), let λ_k: B[T] → A(k) extend λ by Tᵢ ↦ Tᵢ, let A_k = A(k)/λ_k(I)·A(k) with the quotient topology, A_k⁺ the integral closure in A_k of the image of A(k)⁺, and R_k = Spa(A_k, A_k⁺). Then: (i) A_k is complete, has a noetherian ring of definition or is strongly noetherian Tate, and R_k is an affinoid adic space satisfying Huber's condition; (ii) for k ≤ h the continuous A-algebra map A_h → A_k with Tᵢ ↦ Tᵢ induces an isomorphism of R_k onto the rational subset {x ∈ R_h : |e·Tᵢ|_x ≤ 1 for all e ∈ E(k), i = 1,…,n} of R_h; (iii) the adic space R = ⋃_k R_k (increasing union along (ii)), with p: R → Spa(A, A⁺) and the morphism of locally ringed spaces q: R_ → Spec C induced by the ring maps C → A_k, satisfies: for every complete affinoid adic space U = Spa(D, D⁺) over Spa(A, A⁺) (structure map given by μ: A → D), the map w ↦ q ∘ w_ is a bijection from Hom_{Spa(A,A⁺)}(U, R) to the set of B-algebra homomorphisms C → D (B acting on D through μ∘λ), equivalently to Hom_{LRS/Spec B}(U_, Spec C). For a Tate ring A with pseudo-uniformizer ϖ one may take E = {ϖ}, so A(k) = A⟨ϖ^k T₁,…,ϖ^k Tₙ⟩ (the relative closed polydisc of radius |ϖ|^{-k}).
hypotheses: A complete with a noetherian ring of definition, or A a complete strongly noetherian Tate ring (Huber 1994 3.8 hypotheses at an affinoid chart)
E finite, consisting of topologically nilpotent elements, with E·A open; the result does not depend on E (by the universal property)
test objects in (iii) are affinoid adic spaces Spa(D, D⁺) with D complete; the general test object is handled in AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification by gluing
proofSteps: Weights: E·A open implies E(k)·A = (E·A)^k open, and then each constant family (E(k),…,E(k)) is a Tau Ceti weight family (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsWeightFamily) by Huber 1994 Lemma 1.1 = Wedhorn Lemma 6.20 (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/open-ideal-weight-family); in the Tate case E = {ϖ} this is tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsWeightFamily.of_exists_isUnit. So A(k) = completion of tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.weightedRestrictedSubring E(k) is defined and A → A(k) is topologically of finite type (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTopologicallyFiniteType).

(i): A(k) and its quotient A_k are topologically of finite type over A, hence have a noetherian ring of definition or are strongly noetherian Tate (Huber 1994 Cor 3.4(ii),(iii); AdicSpacesPartII:R0/topologically-finite-type-noetherian-type); every ideal of such a complete ring is closed, so A_k = A(k)/λ_k(I)·A(k) is complete Hausdorff and (A_k, A_k⁺) is the quotient pair (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-type-ideals-closed; tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair); (A_k, A_k⁺) is stably sheafy (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-type-stably-sheafy; Huber 1994 Thm 2.2), so R_k is an affinoid adic space satisfying Huber's condition.

(ii): the map A_h → A_k and the rational localisation of (A_h, A_h⁺) at {|e·Tᵢ| ≤ 1} satisfy the same universal property: a continuous map from A_h to a complete Huber pair extends through A_k exactly when the images of e·Tᵢ (e ∈ E(k)) are power-bounded and lie in the plus ring (weighted universal property tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_completion_weightedRestrictedSubring; rational-localisation universal property tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset).

(iii) existence: given a B-algebra map φ: C → D, let dᵢ = φ(Tᵢ). Since E is finite and consists of topologically nilpotent elements, E(k) tends to 0, so for k large μ(e)·dᵢ ∈ D⁺ for all e ∈ E(k) (D⁺ is open). The ring-level weighted universal property (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_completion_weightedRestrictedSubring; its hypothesis IsWeightBounded holds because every weighted monomial is a product of the finitely many power-bounded elements μ(e)dᵢ ∈ D⁺ ⊆ D°, and the monoid they generate is bounded) gives a continuous A-algebra map A(k) → D with Tᵢ ↦ dᵢ. It carries A(k)⁺ into D⁺ (Huber 1994 Lemma 3.5(i)): a series whose ν-th coefficient lies in E(k)^{|ν|}·A⁺ maps to a convergent sum of elements of the open, hence closed, subring D⁺, and D⁺ is integrally closed in D. The map kills λ_k(I) because φ is a B-algebra map, so it factors through the quotient mapping A(k) → A_k, and A_k⁺ maps into D⁺ because D⁺ is integrally closed. This gives U → R_k ⊆ R.

(iii) uniqueness: U is quasi-compact (anchor Layer 2: Spa is spectral), so any morphism U → R lands in some R_k; morphisms Spa(D,D⁺) → R_k over Spa(A,A⁺) are continuous A-algebra maps (A_k, A_k⁺) → (D, D⁺) (full faithfulness of Spa on complete sheafy pairs, anchor Layers 3–5), which are determined by the images of the Tᵢ (uniqueness in the weighted universal property); compatibility in k is (ii).

The identification with Hom_{LRS/Spec B}(U_, Spec C) is the Γ–Spec adjunction for locally ringed spaces (mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.ΓSpec.locallyRingedSpaceAdjunction; Stacks 01I1) together with O_U(U) = D (anchor Layer 3.5).
acceptance: A = K complete rank-one field, E = {ϖ}, B = K, C = K[T]: A_k = K⟨ϖ^k T⟩, A_k⁺ = K°⟨ϖ^k T⟩, R_k is the closed disc of radius |ϖ|^{-k}, and R_k ⊆ R_{k+1} is the rational subset {|ϖ^k T| ≤ 1} (Hübner Example 4.3).
For D = K and φ(T) = ϖ^{-3}, the map Spa(K,K°) → R factors through R_3 but not through R_2.

R is the inductive limit (increasing union) of the R_k along the rational embeddings φ_kh (the page image reads: for k ≤ h, φ_kh is an isomorphism of R_k onto {x ∈ R_h | v_x(eπ_h(X_i)) ≤ 1 for every e ∈ E(k)}).

nodes.title: Huber's fibre product X ×_Y S of a scheme locally of finite type with an adic space over a scheme
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type, S an adic space satisfying Huber's condition (every point has an open affinoid neighbourhood Spa(A, A⁺) with A having a noetherian ring of definition or A a strongly noetherian Tate ring; AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space), and g: S_ → Y a morphism of locally ringed spaces, where S_ = (|S|, O_S) is the underlying locally ringed space of S (forgetting the topology of O_S and the valuations). Then there are an adic space R = X ×_Y S, a morphism of adic spaces p: R → S and a morphism of locally ringed spaces q: R_ → X with g ∘ p_ = f ∘ q, such that for every adic space U, every morphism of adic spaces u: U → S and every morphism of locally ringed spaces v: U_ → X with g ∘ u_ = f ∘ v there is a unique morphism of adic spaces w: U → R with p ∘ w = u and q ∘ w_ = v. The morphism p is locally of finite type (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-type-morphism-classes) and R satisfies Huber's condition. Over an affine open Spec B ⊆ Y, an affine open Spec C ⊆ f⁻¹(Spec B) with C = B[T₁,…,Tₙ]/I and an open affinoid Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ g⁻¹(Spec B), the open subspace p⁻¹(Spa(A,A⁺)) ∩ q⁻¹(Spec C) of R is the increasing union ⋃_k Spa(A_k, A_k⁺) of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affine-chart-analytification. A Y-morphism h: X₁ → X₂ of Y-schemes locally of finite type induces h_S: X₁ ×_Y S → X₂ ×_Y S; this is functorial, and the triple (R, p, q) is unique up to unique isomorphism, so the construction is independent of the charts, presentations and sets E chosen.
hypotheses: f: X → Y a morphism of schemes, locally of finite type
S satisfies Huber's condition (Huber 1994 3.8); Wedhorn 8.61 and Hübner 10.2 give the same construction for stable (stably sheafy) adic spaces S
g: S_ → Y is a morphism of locally ringed spaces; no topology on O_Y enters
proofSteps: Localisation on the source of test morphisms: morphisms of adic spaces glue along open covers (anchor Layer 5), so the universal property may be checked on affinoid test objects U = Spa(D, D⁺) with D complete.

Affine–affinoid case: AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affine-chart-analytification gives (R, p, q) with the universal property for affinoid U; for general U cover U by affinoids and glue the unique morphisms (uniqueness forces agreement on overlaps).

Localisation on X, Y and S: if (R, p, q) has the universal property for X → Y and S, then for Zariski opens X' ⊆ X, Y' ⊆ Y with f(X') ⊆ Y' and an open S' ⊆ S ∩ g⁻¹(Y'), the open subspace p⁻¹(S') ∩ q⁻¹(X') has it for X' → Y' and S', because a morphism of adic spaces into R factors through an open subspace iff its underlying map does (anchor Layer 5), and a morphism of locally ringed spaces v: U_ → X factors (uniquely) through the open subspace X' iff v(U) ⊆ X' (Stacks 01HI, Lemma 26.3.5; Stacks 01HD).

Gluing: cover Y by affine opens Spec B, f⁻¹(Spec B) by affine opens Spec C, and g⁻¹(Spec B) by open affinoids of the kind in Huber's condition; glue the affine–affinoid pieces along the open subspaces of the previous step, the gluing isomorphisms and the cocycle condition being forced by uniqueness in the universal property; the glued adic space exists by the anchor's gluing (Layer 5.3).

p is locally of finite type because on each chart A → A_k factors through a quotient mapping from A⟨T⟩_{E(k)} (Huber 1994 Lemma 3.5(ii)); R satisfies Huber's condition by step (i) of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affine-chart-analytification.
Functoriality h_S and independence of choices follow formally from the universal property (Yoneda).
acceptance: Y = Spec K, X = A¹_K = Spec K[T], S = Spa(K, K°): R is the adic affine line ⋃_k Spa(K⟨ϖ^k T⟩, K°⟨ϖ^k T⟩) (Hübner Example 10.4; AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytic-affine-space).
X = Y and f = id: R = S with p = id and q = g.
Every pair (x, s) with f(x) = g(s) is the image of a point of R (Huber 1994 Lemma 3.9(ii); AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-points).

nodes.title: For a Tate ring of topologically finite type over K, the power-bounded subring is the only ring of integral elements making it of topologically finite type over (K, K°)
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete rank-one nonarchimedean field and A a Tate ring topologically of finite type over K (a K-affinoid algebra: a quotient of some K⟨T₁,…,Tₙ⟩ by a continuous open surjection). Among the rings of integral elements A⁺ of A containing the image of K°, exactly one makes the morphism of affinoid rings (K, K°) → (A, A⁺) topologically of finite type, namely A⁺ = A°. Equivalently, for every continuous open surjection g: K⟨T₁,…,Tₙ⟩ → A, the power-bounded subring A° is the integral closure of g(K°⟨T₁,…,Tₙ⟩) in A.
hypotheses: K complete for a nontrivial rank-one nonarchimedean absolute value
A a K-affinoid algebra, i.e. Tate and topologically of finite type over K (Wedhorn Definition 5.57)
proofSteps: If (K,K°) → (A,A⁺) is of topologically finite type, it factors through a quotient mapping g: (K,K°)⟨T₁,…,Tₙ⟩ → (A, A⁺) (Huber 1994 Lemma 3.5(iii), Tate case), so A⁺ is the integral closure of g(K°⟨T⟩) in A.
K⟨T⟩° = K°⟨T⟩ (power-bounded = Gauss norm at most 1).
Since g is surjective, A° is the integral closure of g(K°⟨T⟩) in A (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-power-bounded-integral, which is BGR 6.3.4/1 and 6.4.3 as cited by Huber); hence A⁺ = A°.
Conversely g itself exhibits (K,K°) → (A, A°) as topologically of finite type, since A° is the integral closure of g(K°⟨T⟩).
acceptance: A = K⟨T⟩/(T²) = K ⊕ K·T: A° = K° ⊕ K·T, which strictly contains the image K° ⊕ K°·T of K°⟨T⟩; the nilpotent elements b·T with |b| > 1 are integral over that image. So 'plus ring = image of K°⟨T⟩' is wrong and the integral closure is needed.
For A = K⟨T⟩ one gets A° = K°⟨T⟩, the plus ring of the anchor's closed polydisc (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.closedPolydisc).

nodes.title: The adic analytification X ↦ X^ad = X ×_{Spec K} Spa(K, K°) of schemes locally of finite type over K
nodes.statement: Fix a field K complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one, its valuation ring K° = {|x| ≤ 1}, a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ (0 < |ϖ| < 1), and Spa K := Spa(K, K°), a one-point adic space. The identity of K defines a morphism of locally ringed spaces c_K: (Spa K)_ → Spec K. For a scheme X locally of finite type over K, its analytification is X^ad := X ×_{Spec K} Spa K (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification), an adic space locally of finite type over Spa K, with the morphism of locally ringed spaces q_X: X^ad_ → X lying over c_K; a K-morphism h: X₁ → X₂ gives h^ad := h_{Spa K}. This defines a functor (·)^ad: Sch^{lft}_K → Adic^{lft}_K from K-schemes locally of finite type to adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa K, and q is a natural transformation (·)^ad_ → (·) of functors to locally ringed spaces over Spec K. For X = Spec K[T₁,…,Tₙ]/I, X^ad = ⋃_{k≥0} Spa(A_k, A_k°) with A_k = K⟨ϖ^k T₁,…,ϖ^k Tₙ⟩/I·K⟨ϖ^k T⟩ (functions on the closed polydisc of radius |ϖ|^{-k} modulo I), glued along the rational embeddings Spa(A_k, A_k°) = {|ϖ^k Tᵢ| ≤ 1 for all i} ⊆ Spa(A_h, A_h°) for k ≤ h; the plus ring of each chart is its power-bounded subring (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/tft-plus-ring-power-bounded). The result does not depend on ϖ or on the presentation, up to unique isomorphism over Spa K compatible with q.
hypotheses: K complete, nontrivially valued, rank one; the construction itself only uses that K is a complete Tate field that is strongly noetherian, which the anchor's Layer 0.5 proves for complete rank-one fields (BGR 5.2.6)
X locally of finite type over K, with no separatedness or quasi-compactness assumption
proofSteps: Spa K satisfies Huber's condition: K is strongly noetherian (anchor Layer 0.5; tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsStronglyNoetherian) and sheafy (anchor Layer 4).
Apply AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification with Y = Spec K, S = Spa K and g = c_K; functoriality and naturality of q are schemePullback.map.

Explicit charts: AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affine-chart-analytification with A = K, B = K, E = {ϖ}, so A(k) = K⟨ϖ^k T⟩; the chart plus ring (integral closure of the image of K°⟨ϖ^k T⟩) equals A_k° by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/tft-plus-ring-power-bounded because (K, K°) → (A_k, A_k⁺) is of topologically finite type.

nodes.title: Universal property of X^ad: morphisms from adic spaces over Spa K into X^ad are morphisms of locally ringed spaces into X
nodes.statement: Let X be a scheme locally of finite type over K and Y an adic space over Spa K with structure morphism π: Y → Spa K. Composition with q_X gives a bijection, natural in Y and in X, Hom_{Spa K}(Y, X^ad) → Hom_{LRS/Spec K}(Y_, X), w ↦ q_X ∘ w_, onto the set of morphisms of locally ringed spaces v: Y_ → X whose composite with X → Spec K is c_K ∘ π_. In particular, for an affinoid Y = Spa(D, D⁺) over Spa K with D complete and an affine X = Spec C, Hom_{Spa K}(Y, X^ad) ≅ Hom_{K-alg}(C, D) = X(D); for X = A^n_K this is D^n; and for a finite field extension L/K, Hom_{Spa K}(Spa(L, L°), X^ad) = X(L).
hypotheses: X locally of finite type over K (K complete, rank one)
Y an arbitrary adic space over Spa K; no finiteness hypothesis on Y
proofSteps: Specialise the universal property of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification to Y = Spec K, S = Spa K, g = c_K: the datum u: Y → Spa K is forced to be π, so the lift w ↦ q_X ∘ w_ is bijective.
Naturality in Y is composition; naturality in X is schemePullback.map (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-functor).

Affinoid Y, affine X: morphisms of locally ringed spaces Y_ → Spec C are ring maps C → O_Y(Y) (mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.ΓSpec.locallyRingedSpaceAdjunction; Stacks 01I1), and O_Y(Y) = D for a complete sheafy pair (anchor Layer 3.5).
For L/K finite, Spa(L, L°) is an adic space over Spa K with O(Spa(L,L°)) = L, so the previous step gives X(L).
acceptance: (A¹_K)^ad represents Y ↦ O_Y(Y) on adic spaces over Spa K, while the closed unit disc represents Y ↦ O⁺_Y(Y) (Scholze–Weinstein, Berkeley Lecture 4, 'the adic affine line').
Over a strongly noetherian Tate affinoid base S = Spa(A, A⁺) the same bijection is Zavyalov's Definition 6.1 of relative analytification.
X^ad(Spa(L, L°)) = X(L) for finite L/K (Conrad, genpaper §1.3 (i), rigid form).

nodes.title: The adic affine space A^{n,ad}: an increasing union of closed polydiscs, not quasi-compact, with entire functions as global sections
nodes.statement: Let n ≥ 1 and ϖ a pseudo-uniformizer of K. (i) A^{n,ad}_K := (A^n_K)^ad is the increasing union of the closed polydiscs D_k = Spa(K⟨ϖ^k T₁,…,ϖ^k Tₙ⟩, K°⟨ϖ^k T₁,…,ϖ^k Tₙ⟩), k ≥ 0, where D_k ⊆ D_{k+1} is the rational subset {|ϖ^k Tᵢ| ≤ 1, i = 1,…,n}; D_0 is the closed unit polydisc. (ii) A^{n,ad}_K is not quasi-compact, hence not affinoid. (iii) Restriction identifies O(A^{n,ad}_K) with lim_k K⟨ϖ^k T⟩ = {Σ_ν a_ν T^ν : |a_ν| r^{|ν|} → 0 for every real r > 0}, the ring of entire power series; it contains K[T₁,…,Tₙ] as a proper subring. (iv) A^{n,ad}_K represents Y ↦ O_Y(Y)^n on adic spaces over Spa K.
hypotheses: K complete of rank one with pseudo-uniformizer ϖ; the union and the answer in (iii) do not depend on ϖ
proofSteps: (i): AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-functor with I = 0 and E = {ϖ}; the identification of D_0 with the anchor's polydisc is tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.closedPolydisc.

(ii): the classical point Tᵢ = ϖ^{-k-1} (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.classicalPoint, transported by the scaling Tᵢ ↦ ϖ^{k+1}Tᵢ) lies in D_{k+1} but not in D_k, so the open cover {D_k} has no finite subcover; affinoid adic spaces are quasi-compact because Spa is spectral (anchor Layer 2).

(iii): sheaf property of O for the open cover {D_k} (anchor Layers 4–5), with D_k ∩ D_h = D_{min(k,h)}; an element of lim_k K⟨ϖ^k T⟩ is a power series whose coefficients satisfy |a_ν||ϖ|^{-k|ν|} → 0 for every k.

(iv): AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-universal-property with X = A^n_K; directly, for affinoid U = Spa(D, D⁺), Hom(U, ⋃ D_k) = colim_k (ϖ^{-k} D⁺)^n = D^n because U is quasi-compact and D⁺[1/ϖ] = D.
acceptance: The classical point T = ϖ^{-2} lies in D_2 \ D_1.
Σ_m ϖ^{m²} T^m is an entire function on A^{1,ad}_K that is not a polynomial.

nodes.title: Analytification of open and closed immersions: open subspaces and closed adic subspaces cut out by the analytified ideal
nodes.statement: Let X be a K-scheme locally of finite type. (i) If j: U → X is an open immersion, j^ad is an open embedding with image q_X⁻¹(j(U)). (ii) If i: Z → X is a closed immersion with quasi-coherent ideal sheaf I ⊆ O_X, then i^ad is a closed embedding in the sense of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings: it identifies Z^ad with the closed adic subspace of X^ad defined by the ideal sheaf I·O_{X^ad} generated by q_X⁻¹I, and its image is q_X⁻¹(i(Z)). On an affine chart X = Spec K[T]/J, Z = Spec K[T]/(J + J'), the piece of Z^ad over Spa(A_k, A_k°) is Spa(A_k/J'A_k, (A_k/J'A_k)°), the quotient pair of the anchor's Layer 2.4. (iii) Consequently immersions analytify to locally closed embeddings, and (i)–(ii) hold verbatim for X ×_Y S → X' ×_Y S in the relative setting of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification.
hypotheses: X locally of finite type over K; I quasi-coherent (automatically of finite type since X is locally noetherian)
proofSteps: (i): the open subspace q_X⁻¹(j(U)) satisfies the universal property of U^ad (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-universal-property): a morphism into X^ad factors through it iff its composite with q_X factors through U (schemePullback.isoOpenSubscheme).

(ii) affine charts: X = Spec C, C = K[T]/J, Z = Spec C/J'. On the chart Spa(A_k, A_k°) the ideal J'A_k is closed and the quotient pair (A_k/J'A_k, integral closure of the image of A_k°) is a complete Huber pair (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-type-ideals-closed; tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.quotient), whose plus ring is (A_k/J'A_k)° by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/tft-plus-ring-power-bounded; it is sheafy (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-type-stably-sheafy) and satisfies the universal property of the chart of Z^ad: a continuous map A_k → D kills J'A_k iff the corresponding B-algebra map C → D factors through C/J' (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affine-chart-analytification).
(ii) image: a point x of Spa(A_k, A_k°) lies in the image iff J'A_k ⊆ supp(x) (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.range_spaComap_quotientHom), iff J' ⊆ ker(C → k(x)), iff q_X(x) ∈ Z.

(ii) gluing: the chart descriptions are compatible with restriction to rational subsets, so they glue to the closed adic subspace defined by I·O_{X^ad} (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings; anchor Layer 5 closed immersions via closed ideals).
(iii): an immersion is a closed immersion followed by an open immersion; combine (i) and (ii). The relative case uses the same charts over Spa(A, A⁺).
acceptance: V(T) ⊆ A¹_K analytifies to the single classical point 0 of A^{1,ad}_K; D(T) = G_m analytifies to A^{1,ad}_K \ {0} = ⋃_k {|ϖ^k| ≤ |T| ≤ |ϖ|^{-k}}.

For a closed immersion Y ↪ X of quasi-projective varieties over K, Y^ad is the closed adic subspace of X^ad cut out by I_Y·O_{X^ad} (the input requested by PerfectoidSpaces:P8/closed-subvariety-pullback-is-zariski-closed).

nodes.title: Points of X ×_Y S and of X^ad: surjectivity onto compatible pairs; classical points correspond to closed points; q_X is not injective
nodes.statement: (i) In the situation of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification, for every x ∈ X and s ∈ S with f(x) = g(s) there is r ∈ X ×_Y S with q(r) = x and p(r) = s. In particular q_X: X^ad → X is surjective onto the set of all points of X, closed and non-closed. (ii) Call x ∈ X^ad classical if its residue field k(x) = O_{X^ad,x}/m_x is finite over K. Then q_X restricts to a bijection from the classical points of X^ad onto the closed points of X; for a closed point x₀, q_X⁻¹(x₀) consists of exactly one point, it is classical, and q_X induces k(x₀) ≅ k(x). (iii) If dim X ≥ 1, q_X is not injective: the fibre over the generic point of a positive-dimensional irreducible component is infinite; for X = A¹_K the fibre over the generic point contains every non-classical point, among them the Gauss point of each disc |T| ≤ |ϖ|^{-k} and the rank-2 points.
hypotheses: (i) needs only Huber's hypotheses of 3.8; (ii)–(iii) are for K complete of rank one and X locally of finite type over K
proofSteps: (i): reduce to Y = Spec B, X = Spec C with C = B[T₁,…,Tₙ]/I_C, S = Spa(A, A⁺); choose a prime q of C ⊗_B A over the given prime of C and supp(s) (mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pullback.exists_preimage_pullback), and a valuation r of C ⊗_B A with supp(r) = q, extending s, with Γ_r/Γ_s torsion (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/valuation-extension-divisible-hull); then s(I) cofinal in Γ_s gives r(I) cofinal in Γ_r. Take the chart set E to be a finite generating set of an ideal of definition I of a ring of definition A₀ (R is independent of E); choose k with r(Tⱼ ⊗ i) ≤ 1 for all j and i ∈ I^k. Then r is continuous and ≤ 1 on the integral closure of A⁺[E(k)T] in C ⊗_B A, so r is a point of Spa of the completion of that pair, which is (A_k, A_k⁺), i.e. r ∈ R_k ⊆ R (Huber 1994 Lemma 3.9(ii); Wedhorn Proposition 8.63).
Surjectivity of q_X: apply (i) with S = Spa K, whose only point maps to the only point of Spec K.

(ii) closed points: for x₀ closed with residue field L (finite over K by the Nullstellensatz; mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.isClosed_singleton_iff_locallyOfFiniteType, mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType.jacobsonSpace), the closed immersion Spec L → X analytifies to a closed embedding with image q_X⁻¹(x₀) (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-immersions), and (Spec L)^ad = Spa(L, L°) is one point with residue field L (a continuous valuation of L bounded by 1 on L° is the unique extension of |·|).

(ii) classical points: if k(x) is finite over K then k(q_X(x)) ⊆ k(x) (the stalk map is local) is finite over K, so q_X(x) is closed; hence q_X maps classical points to closed points, and by the previous step bijectively.

(iii): the Gauss point of K⟨ϖ^k T⟩ has support 0, so its image in Spec K[T] is the generic point; the rank-2 points of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytic-affine-space likewise have support 0. For general X, Noether normalisation (mathlib:exists_finite_inj_algHom_of_fg) gives an affine open U of a positive-dimensional component (with reduced structure) and a finite injective, hence surjective, map U → A^d, d ≥ 1, sending the generic point to the generic point; the fibre of q_{A^d} over the generic point is infinite (Gauss points of the polydiscs of radius |ϖ|^{-k}), and by (i) applied to U ×_{A^d} (A^d)^ad = U^ad (schemePullback.trans) each of these points lifts to a point of U^ad over the generic point of U.
acceptance: Classical points of (A¹_K)^ad are in bijection with the closed points of A¹_K: over an algebraically closed K with K itself; over general K with the Aut(K̄/K)-orbits in an algebraic closure K̄, i.e. with the monic irreducible polynomials in K[T] (for imperfect K the inseparable ones have no roots in the separable closure).
The Gauss point of the unit disc maps to the generic point of A¹_K.

nodes.title: Analytification preserves and reflects surjectivity
nodes.statement: Let h: X₁ → X₂ be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type over Y and S → Y as in AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification. If h is surjective then h_S: X₁ ×_Y S → X₂ ×_Y S is surjective. For K-schemes locally of finite type, h is surjective if and only if h^ad: X₁^ad → X₂^ad is surjective.
hypotheses: h a morphism of Y-schemes locally of finite type; for the converse, K complete of rank one and S = Spa K
proofSteps: X₁ ×_Y S ≅ X₁ ×_{X₂} (X₂ ×_Y S) (schemePullback.trans in AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification).
If h is surjective: for r ∈ X₂ ×_Y S choose x ∈ X₁ with h(x) = q(r); AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-points (i) applied to X₁ → X₂ and X₂ ×_Y S gives a point of X₁ ×_Y S over r.

nodes.title: Analytification commutes with fibre products and preserves finite products
nodes.statement: For morphisms X → Z ← Y of K-schemes locally of finite type, the natural morphism (X ×_Z Y)^ad → X^ad ×_{Z^ad} Y^ad (induced by the two projections) is an isomorphism of adic spaces over Spa K; the right side is the fibre product of adic spaces, which exists by AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence because X^ad → Z^ad is locally of finite type. Since (Spec K)^ad = Spa K is terminal among adic spaces over Spa K, (·)^ad preserves finite products: (X ×_K Y)^ad ≅ X^ad ×_{Spa K} Y^ad and (Spec K)^ad ≅ Spa K. Relatively, for S satisfying Huber's condition over Y and Y-schemes X₁ → X₂ ← X₃ locally of finite type, (X₁ ×_{X₂} X₃) ×_Y S ≅ (X₁ ×_Y S) ×_{(X₂ ×_Y S)} (X₃ ×_Y S).
hypotheses: all schemes locally of finite type over K (resp. over Y)
the fibre product on the right is taken in the category of all adic spaces; it exists because one leg is locally of finite type
proofSteps: For an adic space T over Spa K: Hom(T, (X ×_Z Y)^ad) = Hom_{LRS/Spec K}(T_, X ×_Z Y) (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-universal-property).

A fibre product of schemes is a fibre product in locally ringed spaces (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-pullback-is-lrs-pullback; Stacks 01I4 affine case, Stacks 01JN), so Hom_{LRS}(T_, X ×_Z Y) = Hom_{LRS}(T_, X) ×_{Hom_{LRS}(T_, Z)} Hom_{LRS}(T_, Y), compatibly with the structure maps to Spec K.

By the universal property again this is Hom(T, X^ad) ×_{Hom(T, Z^ad)} Hom(T, Y^ad) = Hom(T, X^ad ×_{Z^ad} Y^ad), using existence of the adic fibre product (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence); conclude by Yoneda.
Terminality: a morphism T → Spa K over Spa K is unique; (Spec K)^ad ≅ Spa K by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-functor.
The relative statement is the same argument with the universal property of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification.

nodes.title: Analytification of finite and finite locally free morphisms
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a finite morphism of schemes and S → Y as in AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification. For every open affinoid V = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ S mapping into an affine open Spec B ⊆ Y with f⁻¹(Spec B) = Spec C (C finite over B), the preimage of V in X ×_Y S is the affinoid Spa(C ⊗_B A, (C ⊗_B A)⁺), where C ⊗_B A carries its natural topology as a finite A-module and (C ⊗_B A)⁺ is the integral closure of the image of A⁺; hence p: X ×_Y S → S is finite in the sense of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-morphism. If moreover f is finite locally free of constant rank d (f_*O_X locally free of rank d), then for every such V the ring O(p⁻¹V) = C ⊗_B A is a finite projective A-module of constant rank d. In particular, for K-schemes locally of finite type: f finite ⇒ f^ad finite; f finite locally free of rank d ⇒ f^ad finite and O((f^ad)⁻¹V) finite projective of rank d over O(V) for every open affinoid V ⊆ Y^ad.
hypotheses: f finite (resp. finite locally free of rank d); S satisfies Huber's condition
proofSteps: Reduce to Y = Spec B, X = Spec C, S = Spa(A, A⁺); write C = B[T₁,…,Tₙ]/I with each Tᵢ satisfying a monic equation over B.

Put D = C ⊗_B A with its finite A-module topology and D⁺ the integral closure of the image of A⁺; (D, D⁺) is a complete Huber pair of the same noetherian type, finite over (A, A⁺) (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-algebra-over-affinoid).

If tᵢ^m + a₁tᵢ^{m-1} + … + a_m = 0 in D with a_j ∈ A, then for e ∈ E(k) the element e·tᵢ satisfies (e tᵢ)^m + (e a₁)(e tᵢ)^{m-1} + … + e^m a_m = 0; since E(k) → 0 and A⁺ is open, e^j a_j ∈ A⁺ for k large, so e·tᵢ is integral over A⁺ and lies in D⁺.

Hence, for k large, the universal property of the chart R_k (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affine-chart-analytification) gives a map A_k → D inverse to the evident continuous map D → A_k (continuity of A-linear maps from a finite module), so R_k = Spa(D, D⁺) for all large k and the increasing union stabilises: X ×_Y S = Spa(D, D⁺) over V.

Finiteness in the sense of R0 (Huber 1996 (1.4.2), (1.4.4)): D is finite over A with the module topology and D⁺ is the integral closure of A⁺; so p is finite over every open affinoid V mapping into an affine open of Y, and such V cover S.
If C is a finite projective B-module of rank d then C ⊗_B A is a finite projective A-module of rank d (base change).

Arbitrary open affinoid V ⊆ Y^ad (the 'in particular' clause, where V need not map into one affine open of Y): (f^ad)⁻¹V is affinoid and O((f^ad)⁻¹V) =: M is finite over O(V) by AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-morphism (global form, O(V) strongly noetherian Tate). Cover V by finitely many rational subsets V_i, each mapping into an affine open of Y; by the base-change description of finite morphisms (Huber 1996, proof of Lemma 1.4.5(i)) O((f^ad)⁻¹V_i) = M ⊗_{O(V)} O(V_i), which is finite projective of rank d by the affine case. O(V) → ∏_i O(V_i) is faithfully flat (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.faithfullyFlat_pi_toCompletionLoc), so M is O(V)-flat by faithfully flat descent (mathlib:Module.Flat.of_flat_tensorProduct), hence projective since it is finitely presented over the noetherian ring O(V) (mathlib:Module.Flat.projective_of_finitePresentation); its rank is d at every prime because every prime of O(V) lies under a prime of some O(V_i).

nodes.title: Affinoid subdomains of the maximal spectrum of a K-affinoid algebra
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one, A a K-affinoid algebra and X = Max A. A subset U ⊆ X is an affinoid subdomain if there is a homomorphism of K-affinoid algebras i : A → A_U such that Max(i) : Max A_U → X (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-residue-fields-finite) has image in U and is universal for this property: for every homomorphism φ : A → B into a K-affinoid algebra with Max(φ)(Max B) ⊆ U there is a unique K-algebra homomorphism φ_U : A_U → B with φ_U ∘ i = φ. The A-algebra A_U (the coordinate ring of U) is unique up to unique A-isomorphism; Max(i) is a bijection onto U inducing isomorphisms of residue fields; for affinoid subdomains V ⊆ U there is a unique A-algebra map ρ^U_V : A_U → A_V, with ρ^V_W ∘ ρ^U_V = ρ^U_W. Rational subdomains X(f₁,…,f_n/f₀) = {x : |f_j(x)| ≤ |f₀(x)| for all j}, for f₀,…,f_n ∈ A without common zero, are affinoid subdomains with coordinate ring A⟨f/f₀⟩ = A⟨T₁,…,T_n⟩/(f₀T_j − f_j) (Weierstrass domains f₀ = 1, Laurent domains as intersections). Lean name: RigidSpace.IsAffinoidSubdomain A U, with coordinate ring RigidSpace.IsAffinoidSubdomain.coordRing.
hypotheses: K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one

A is a K-affinoid algebra: a commutative K-algebra with a complete Hausdorff first-countable ring topology for which K → A is strictly topologically of finite type (Tau Ceti IsStrictlyTopologicallyFiniteType (algebraMap K A): a continuous open surjection of K-algebras K⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩ = restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n K → A; Wedhorn Definition 5.57)
proofSteps: Definition by the universal property; uniqueness of A_U by the Yoneda lemma.

Points, residue fields and quotient_pow_equiv (BGR 7.2.2/1, derived from the universal property): for x ∈ U with maximal ideal m ⊆ A and k ≥ 1, A/mᵏ and A_U/mᵏA_U are K-affinoid (finite-dimensional, resp. a quotient of A_U) and Max of each maps into U, so the projection A → A/mᵏ factors uniquely as ψ ∘ i; ψ kills mᵏA_U and induces ψ̄ : A_U/mᵏA_U → A/mᵏ with ψ̄ ∘ ī = id, and ī ∘ ψ̄ = id because q and ī ∘ ψ̄ ∘ q (q : A_U → A_U/mᵏA_U) agree after composing with i, so uniqueness in the universal property forces them to be equal. For k = 1 this gives A_U/mA_U ≅ A/m, a field: exactly one maximal ideal of A_U lies over x, namely mA_U, with the same residue field; together with Max(i)(Max A_U) ⊆ U (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-residue-fields-finite) Max(i) is a bijection onto U.

Rational subdomains: for φ : A → B, the elements φ(f_j)/φ(f₀) exist and are power-bounded iff |φ(f_j)(y)| ≤ |φ(f₀)(y)| for all y ∈ Max B (φ(f₀) is a unit because it has no zero on Max B, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-jacobson; power-boundedness by AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-power-bounded-iff-sup), and the universal property of the relative Tate algebra A⟨T₁,…,T_n⟩ (the trivial-weight case of tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_completion_weightedRestrictedSubring; anchor Layer 0.4 request for the pair-level form) gives the factorisation (Conrad, Several approaches, Lemma 2.1.8).

Intersections and preimages: A_{U∩U'} = A_U ⊗̂_A A_{U'} and the coordinate ring of Max(φ)⁻¹(U) is A_U ⊗̂_A B, by the universal property of the completed tensor product (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product) and the universal property of A_U.
acceptance: U = X with A_U = A, and U = ∅ with A_U = 0, are affinoid subdomains.
{|T| ≤ |c|} ⊆ Max K⟨T⟩ (0 < |c| ≤ 1) has coordinate ring K⟨T, S⟩/(T − cS) ≅ K⟨S⟩; the open disc {|T| < 1} is not an affinoid subdomain.

nodes.title: Coordinate rings of affinoid subdomains are flat
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one, A a K-affinoid algebra and U ⊆ Max A an affinoid subdomain (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affinoid-subdomain). Then A → A_U is flat. If U₁,…,U_n are affinoid subdomains covering Max A, then A → ∏_i A_{U_i} is faithfully flat. Lean name: RigidSpace.IsAffinoidSubdomain.flat and RigidSpace.faithfullyFlat_pi_coordRing.
hypotheses: K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one

A is a K-affinoid algebra: a commutative K-algebra with a complete Hausdorff first-countable ring topology for which K → A is strictly topologically of finite type (Tau Ceti IsStrictlyTopologicallyFiniteType (algebraMap K A): a continuous open surjection of K-algebras K⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩ = restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n K → A; Wedhorn Definition 5.57)
U an affinoid subdomain; for the second statement a finite covering by affinoid subdomains
proofSteps: Completions: let n be a maximal ideal of A_U; it lies over a point x ∈ U with maximal ideal m ⊆ A (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-residue-fields-finite). By quotient_pow_equiv of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affinoid-subdomain, n = mA_U and A/mᵏ ≅ A_U/mᵏA_U = A_U/nᵏ = (A_U)_n/nᵏ(A_U)_n for all k, so A_m → (A_U)_n induces an isomorphism of adic completions Â_m ≅ (A_U)^_n (mathlib AdicCompletion).

Flatness at n: (A_U)_n → (A_U)^_n is flat (mathlib:AdicCompletion.flat_of_isNoetherian) and local, hence faithfully flat (mathlib:Module.FaithfullyFlat.of_flat_of_isLocalHom); A → A_m → Â_m is flat. For an injective map N → N' of A-modules, (A_U)^_n ⊗_{(A_U)_n} ((A_U)_n ⊗_A N → (A_U)_n ⊗_A N') is Â_m ⊗_A (N → N'), which is injective, so (A_U)_n ⊗_A N → (A_U)_n ⊗_A N' is injective (mathlib:Module.FaithfullyFlat.lTensor_injective_iff_injective): (A_U)_n is A-flat.

A → A_U is flat, because flatness can be tested after localising A_U at its maximal ideals (mathlib:Module.flat_of_isLocalized_maximal). This is BGR 7.3.2/6 as cited by Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 2.5.17; for rational subdomains it is also Tau Ceti's tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.flat_toCompletionLoc via the API item rational_compat.

Faithful flatness of the covering: the product is flat, and every maximal ideal m of A lies under a maximal ideal of some A_{U_i} (the U_i cover Max A and Max A_{U_i} → U_i is bijective), so m·∏A_{U_i} ≠ ∏A_{U_i} (mathlib Module.FaithfullyFlat criterion Module.FaithfullyFlat.iff_flat_and_proper_ideal; Kedlaya–Liu Proposition 2.5.18).
acceptance: For the covering of Max K⟨T⟩ by {|T| ≤ |ϖ|} and {|T| ≥ |ϖ|}, K⟨T⟩ → K⟨S⟩ × K⟨T, U⟩/(TU − ϖ) (T ↦ (ϖS, T)) is faithfully flat.
The single affinoid subdomain {|T| ≤ |ϖ|} gives a flat but not faithfully flat map K⟨T⟩ → K⟨S⟩ (the point T = 1 is missed).

nodes.title: The Gerritzen–Grauert theorem
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one, A a K-affinoid algebra and U ⊆ Max A an affinoid subdomain. Then there are finitely many rational subdomains V₁,…,V_n covering Max A — induced by a rational covering of Spa(A, A°) — such that U ∩ V_i is a rational subdomain of Max A_{V_i} for every i. In particular U is a finite union of rational subdomains of Max A, and affinoid subdomains are open in the canonical topology. Lean name: RigidSpace.IsAffinoidSubdomain.exists_rationalCover.
hypotheses: K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one

A is a K-affinoid algebra: a commutative K-algebra with a complete Hausdorff first-countable ring topology for which K → A is strictly topologically of finite type (Tau Ceti IsStrictlyTopologicallyFiniteType (algebraMap K A): a continuous open surjection of K-algebras K⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩ = restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n K → A; Wedhorn Definition 5.57)
U an affinoid subdomain (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affinoid-subdomain)
proofSteps: BGR 7.3.5/1: there are finitely many rational subdomains W_j covering Max A with U ∩ W_j rational in W_j. Proof source: BGR 7.3.5, or Temkin's proof (J. reine angew. Math. 2005, Theorem 3.1); neither is among the sources read; recorded as a gap on this node.

Refinement to a covering induced by a rational covering of Spa(A, A°): the finite covering {W_j} of Max A by rational subdomains is refined by X(S/f), f ∈ S, for a finite S generating the unit ideal (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/max-rational-covering-refinement, the Max A form of Huber's product trick, = Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 2.5.10). Tau Ceti's exists_span_eq_top_forall_rationalSubset_subset(_of_isTateRing) cannot be applied directly: it needs a covering of all of Spa(A, A°), and deducing that the R(T_j/s_j) cover Spa from the fact that the W_j cover Max A is Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 2.5.12, whose proof uses Lemma 2.5.10 itself. Put V_i = X(S/f_i); if V_i ⊆ W_k then U ∩ V_i is the preimage in Max A_{V_i} of the rational subdomain U ∩ W_k of Max A_{W_k}, hence rational in V_i (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affinoid-subdomain, API inter and preimage).

Finite union: U = ⋃_i (U ∩ V_i), and a rational subdomain of a rational subdomain of Max A is a rational subdomain of Max A (BGR 7.2.4/2; the adic form is Wedhorn Proposition 8.2(2), requested from the anchor's Layer 2 — Tau Ceti only has the denominator-clearing half, exists_comap_preimage_rationalSubset_inter_spa_eq). Openness in the canonical topology follows since rational subdomains are open (Conrad, Several approaches, Exercise 2.2.2).
acceptance: Every Weierstrass, Laurent or rational domain satisfies the theorem trivially (n = 1).

The converse fails: not every finite union of rational subdomains is an affinoid subdomain (Kedlaya–Liu, Theorem 2.5.11, final sentence); the theorem asserts only that affinoid subdomains are finite unions of rational ones.

nodes.title: Tate's acyclicity theorem for finite coverings by affinoid subdomains
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one, A a K-affinoid algebra, M an A-module and U₁,…,U_n affinoid subdomains covering Max A (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affinoid-subdomain). Then the augmented Čech complex 0 → M → ∏_i M ⊗_A A_{U_i} → ∏_{i<j} M ⊗_A A_{U_i ∩ U_j} → ⋯ is exact. In particular U ↦ A_U is a sheaf for finite coverings of affinoid subdomains by affinoid subdomains, with vanishing higher Čech cohomology, and it extends uniquely to a sheaf O_A for the Tate topology on Max A. Lean name: RigidSpace.cech_exact_of_affinoidCover.
hypotheses: K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one

A is a K-affinoid algebra: a commutative K-algebra with a complete Hausdorff first-countable ring topology for which K → A is strictly topologically of finite type (Tau Ceti IsStrictlyTopologicallyFiniteType (algebraMap K A): a continuous open surjection of K-algebras K⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩ = restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n K → A; Wedhorn Definition 5.57)
M an arbitrary A-module
{U_i} a finite covering of Max A by affinoid subdomains
proofSteps: Reduction to M = A: every term A_{U_I} (U_I a finite intersection) is A-flat (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affinoid-subdomain-flat), and so is A; a bounded exact complex of flat modules has flat cycle modules and stays exact after ⊗_A M. The Čech complex of M is M ⊗_A (Čech complex of A).

Rational refinement: by the Gerritzen–Grauert theorem (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/gerritzen-grauert), applied to each U_i and intersected, there is a covering {V_j} of Max A induced by a rational covering of Spa(A, A°) such that each U_i ∩ V_j is rational in V_j; on each V_j and each finite intersection the induced finite coverings by rational subdomains are refined by standard rational coverings (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/max-rational-covering-refinement; Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 2.5.10).

Standard rational coverings of the strongly noetherian Tate rings A_V (V rational) are Čech acyclic in all degrees (anchor Layer 4.1, requested; the coordinate rings of rational subdomains are the anchor's completed rational localisations, API rational_compat of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affinoid-subdomain).

Passage along refinements: if a covering 𝔙 refines 𝔘 and the restrictions of 𝔙 to all finite intersections of members of 𝔘, and of 𝔘 to all members of 𝔙, are acyclic, then 𝔘 is acyclic (the Čech double-complex comparison of BGR 8.1.4 and 8.2.1–8.2.2). Proof source BGR, not public; recorded as a gap on this node.
The extension to the Tate topology follows by the definition of admissible coverings (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytic-space uses this node).
acceptance: For the Laurent covering {|f| ≤ 1}, {|f| ≥ 1} of Max A: 0 → A → A⟨f⟩ × A⟨f⁻¹⟩ → A⟨f, f⁻¹⟩ → 0 is exact.
For the covering of Max K⟨T⟩ by {|T| ≤ |ϖ|} and {|T| ≥ |ϖ|} (Conrad, Several approaches, Exercise 2.3.4), a pair of compatible functions glues to a unique element of K⟨T⟩.

nodes.title: Local rings of affinoid spaces at points are noetherian with the algebraic completion
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one, A a K-affinoid algebra, x ∈ Max A with maximal ideal m, and O_x = colim_{U ∋ x} A_U the colimit over the affinoid subdomains of Max A containing x (the stalk of Sp A at x). Then O_x is a noetherian local ring with maximal ideal m·O_x, the map A_m → O_x is faithfully flat, and A/mᵏ → O_x/mᵏO_x is an isomorphism for every k ≥ 1; hence the completions agree, Â_m ≅ Ô_x. Lean name: RigidSpace.stalk_completion_equiv.
hypotheses: K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one

A is a K-affinoid algebra: a commutative K-algebra with a complete Hausdorff first-countable ring topology for which K → A is strictly topologically of finite type (Tau Ceti IsStrictlyTopologicallyFiniteType (algebraMap K A): a continuous open surjection of K-algebras K⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩ = restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n K → A; Wedhorn Definition 5.57)
x ∈ Max A
proofSteps: A/mᵏ ≅ A_U/mᵏA_U for every affinoid subdomain U ∋ x (API quotient_pow_equiv of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affinoid-subdomain, derived there from the universal property); pass to the colimit: A/mᵏ ≅ O_x/mᵏO_x.

O_x is local with maximal ideal m·O_x: if f(x) ≠ 0, choose c ∈ K× with |c| ≤ |f(x)| (|K×| is nontrivial); f is a unit on the Laurent domain {|f| ≥ |c|}, an affinoid subdomain containing x (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affinoid-subdomain, API rational; AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-jacobson for units). Moreover O_x is the filtered colimit of the local rings R_U = (A_U)_{n_U} (n_U = mA_U the unique maximal ideal over x), whose transition maps are flat and local (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affinoid-subdomain-flat).
Faithful flatness: A_m → O_x is a filtered colimit of the flat maps A_m → R_U, hence flat, and it is local, hence faithfully flat (mathlib:Module.FaithfullyFlat.of_flat_of_isLocalHom).

O_x is noetherian: its m-adic completion is Â_m (by step 1), and Â_m is the n_U-adic completion of each noetherian R_U, so each R_U → Â_m is flat (mathlib:AdicCompletion.flat_of_isNoetherian) and so is the colimit O_x → Â_m (relations over O_x come from some R_U; mathlib Module.Flat.of_forall_isTrivialRelation); it is local, hence faithfully flat. Â_m is noetherian (Stacks 05GH; not in the pinned Mathlib, which has only the flatness and locality of adic completions — a baseline gap), so O_x is noetherian by faithfully flat descent (mathlib:Submodule.IsNoetherian.of_isNoetherian_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat with M = O_x). This replaces the BGR 7.3.2/3 citation.
acceptance: At the origin of Max K⟨T⟩, O_0 is the ring of power series converging on some disc around 0, strictly between K[T]_{(T)} and K⟦T⟧, with completion K⟦T⟧ (Conrad, Several approaches, Exercise 2.3.6).
For A = K⟨T⟩/(T²) at the origin, O_0 = A (every affinoid subdomain containing the only point is all of Max A).

nodes.title: Rigid-analytic spaces over K in the sense of Tate (BGR 9.3.1)
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete rank-one nonarchimedean field. For a K-affinoid algebra A (a quotient of some Tate algebra K⟨T₁,…,Tₙ⟩, with its Banach topology), the affinoid space Sp(A) is the set Max A of maximal ideals with the Tate (strong) G-topology: a subset U ⊆ Max A is admissible open if it has a set-theoretic covering {U_i} by affinoid subdomains such that for every homomorphism of K-affinoid algebras φ : A → B with Max(φ)(Max B) ⊆ U finitely many U_i cover Max(φ)(Max B), and a family {V_j} of admissible opens is an admissible covering of its union V if for every φ : A → B with Max(φ)(Max B) ⊆ V the covering {Max(φ)⁻¹(V_j)} of Max B has a refinement by finitely many affinoid subdomains (Conrad AWS Definition 2.2.6; BGR 9.1.4); together with Tate's structure sheaf O_A, U ↦ A_U on affinoid subdomains. A rigid-analytic space over K is a pair (X, O_X) of a G-topologized set X and a sheaf of K-algebras O_X with local stalks, admitting an admissible covering by open subspaces isomorphic to affinoid spaces Sp(A_i). Morphisms are morphisms of locally G-ringed K-spaces. Rig_K denotes this category. A morphism f is a closed immersion if there is an admissible affinoid covering {U_i} of the target with each f⁻¹(U_i) affinoid and O(U_i) → O(f⁻¹U_i) surjective (Conrad AWS Example 3.1.5); f is separated if its diagonal is a closed immersion, quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact, and proper (Kiehl) if it is separated, quasi-compact and relatively compact over an admissible affinoid covering of the target (Conrad AWS Definition 3.2.3).
hypotheses: K complete for a nontrivial rank-one nonarchimedean absolute value

K-affinoid algebras are strongly noetherian Tate rings (anchor Layer 0.5), so Tate's acyclicity for finite rational coverings is the anchor's Layer 4; the extension to finite coverings by affinoid subdomains uses the Gerritzen–Grauert theorem, whose proof (BGR 7.3.5) is not in a public source read here
proofSteps: Affinoid subdomains, rational subdomains and the weak/strong G-topologies on Max A (BGR 7.2, 9.1); by the Gerritzen–Grauert theorem every affinoid subdomain is a finite union of rational subdomains, so the Tate topology is generated by finite rational coverings.

Tate's acyclicity: U ↦ A_U is a sheaf for finite rational coverings (anchor Layer 4, strongly noetherian Tate rings; tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.faithfullyFlat_pi_toCompletionLoc for injectivity) and hence for the Tate topology.
Locally G-ringed spaces, open subspaces and gluing along admissible opens (Conrad AWS §2.3–2.4; BGR 9.1–9.3); Sp is a fully faithful contravariant functor from K-affinoid algebras.
acceptance: Sp(K) is a point with structure sheaf K; O(Sp A) = A.
In the closed unit disc, {|T| < 1} and {|T| = 1} are admissible opens that cover the disc set-theoretically but do not form an admissible covering (Conrad AWS Example 2.2.8).

nodes.title: Every maximal ideal of a K-affinoid domain has height equal to its dimension
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete rank-one nonarchimedean field and A a K-affinoid algebra (a quotient of a Tate algebra T_n(K) = K⟨X_1, …, X_n⟩; AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytic-space) which is an integral domain of Krull dimension d. Then every maximal ideal m of A has height d (Ideal.height m = d); equivalently dim A_m = d for every point of Sp(A). In particular every maximal ideal of T_d(K) has height d, and if T_e(K) → A is a finite injective K-algebra homomorphism then e = d. (Conrad, Irreducible components of rigid spaces, Lemma 2.1.5, first assertion.)
hypotheses: K complete for a nontrivial rank-one nonarchimedean absolute value
A a K-affinoid algebra that is an integral domain
proofSteps: A is noetherian: K-affinoid algebras are complete strongly noetherian Tate rings (anchor Layer 0.5; tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isNoetherianRing_of_isStronglyNoetherian), so heights are finite (mathlib Ideal.height).

Tate algebras at rational points: for a ∈ (K°)^d the K-algebra automorphism X ↦ X + a of T_d(K) (defined since |a_i| ≤ 1) carries m₀ = (X_1, …, X_d) = ker(ev₀) to m_a = ker(ev_a) (every g with g(0) = 0 is Σ X_i g_i), so ht m_a = ht m₀. Upper bound: m₀ has d generators, so ht m₀ ≤ d by Krull's height theorem (mathlib:Ideal.height_le_spanFinrank). Lower bound: 0 ⊊ (X_1) ⊊ (X_1, X_2) ⊊ ⋯ ⊊ (X_1, …, X_d) is a chain of primes, since T_d(K)/(X_1, …, X_i) ≅ T_{d−i}(K) is a domain (Tate algebras are domains, indeed factorial, BGR 5.2.6/1 — the same input as step 4), so ht m₀ ≥ d. This replaces the comparison with the completion K⟦X − a⟧, whose input 'a noetherian local ring and its completion have the same dimension' is not in the pinned Mathlib.

Tate algebras at all maximal ideals: the residue field T_d(K)/m is finite over K (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-residue-fields-finite); for a finite extension K′/K containing it, T_d(K′) = T_d(K) ⊗_K K′ is finite free over T_d(K), there is a K′-rational maximal ideal m′ lying over m (mathlib Ideal.exists_ideal_over_prime_of_isIntegral), and since the extension is flat it has going down (mathlib Algebra.HasGoingDown.of_flat), so ht m′ = ht m + ht(m′/mT_d(K′)) (mathlib Ideal.height_eq_height_add_of_liesOver_of_hasGoingDown); the fibre T_d(K′)/mT_d(K′) is finite over the field T_d(K)/m, so its primes are minimal and the second summand is 0 (mathlib Ideal.height_eq_zero_iff); hence ht m = d.

General A: Noether normalisation (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-noether-normalisation) gives a finite injective K-algebra homomorphism T_e(K) → A. T_e(K) is factorial, hence integrally closed (mathlib IsIntegrallyClosed), so the integral extension of domains T_e(K) ⊆ A has going down (mathlib Algebra.HasGoingDown; the instance for integral extensions of integrally closed domains, Stacks 00H8). For a maximal ideal m of A, n = m ∩ T_e(K) is maximal (mathlib Ideal.isMaximal_comap_of_isIntegral_of_isMaximal) and ht m = ht n + ht(m/nA) = e + 0, because A/nA is finite over the field T_e(K)/n. So all maximal ideals of A have height e, and d = dim A, the supremum of these heights, equals e (Conrad, Lemma 2.1.5).
acceptance: For A = K⟨X, Y⟩/(XY − ϖ) (the annulus |ϖ| ≤ |X| ≤ 1, an integral domain of dimension 1) every maximal ideal has height 1.
The domain hypothesis cannot be dropped: in A = K⟨X⟩ × K (a closed disc and a point) the maximal ideals have heights 1 and 0.

nodes.title: Identity principle on connected normal rigid spaces
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete rank-one nonarchimedean field and X a rigid-analytic space over K (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytic-space) that is connected (every admissible covering {V, W} of X by disjoint admissible opens has V = ∅ or W = ∅; equivalently O_X(X) has no idempotents other than 0 and 1) and normal (every local ring O_{X,x} is a normal domain; for an affinoid open Sp(A) ⊆ X this holds at its points iff A is a normal ring). An analytic subset of X is the zero locus Z = {x ∈ X : 𝓘_x ≠ O_{X,x}} of a coherent ideal sheaf 𝓘 ⊆ O_X (on an affinoid open Sp(A), Z ∩ Sp(A) = {m ∈ Max A : I ⊆ m} for the ideal I = 𝓘(Sp A)). Let U ⊆ X be a nonempty admissible open. Then: (i) the only analytic subset of X containing U is X; (ii) if X = Z₁ ∪ Z₂ for analytic subsets Z₁, Z₂, then Z₁ = X or Z₂ = X; (iii) if f ∈ O_X(X) has f|_U = 0, then f = 0, and more generally a section s of a locally free O_X-module ℰ of finite rank with s|_U = 0 is 0. Parts (i)–(ii) are Conrad, Irreducible components of rigid spaces, Lemma 2.1.4; (iii) is the argument in the proof of his Theorem 2.1.2.
hypotheses: K complete for a nontrivial rank-one nonarchimedean absolute value
X connected and normal
U ⊆ X a nonempty admissible open
proofSteps: Constant dimension: for x in an affinoid open Sp(A) ⊆ X with maximal ideal m, A_m → O_{X,x} is flat and local with m·O_{X,x} the maximal ideal (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-local-ring-completion), so by the going-down height formula (mathlib:Algebra.HasGoingDown.of_flat, mathlib:Ideal.height_eq_height_add_of_liesOver_of_hasGoingDown; the fibre O_{X,x}/mO_{X,x} is a field) dim O_{X,x} = ht m; the same argument on Sp(A/I) gives dim O_{Z,z} = ht of the image of m in A/I. O_{X,x} is normal iff A_m is (Conrad §1.2, via excellence; recorded gap). A connected normal affinoid Sp(A) has A a normal noetherian ring without nontrivial idempotents, hence a domain, so all its points have dim O_{X,x} = dim A (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affinoid-domain-equidimensional). Covering X by connected affinoids and using that X is connected (chains of overlapping connected affinoids), all O_{X,x} have one dimension n (Conrad, proof of Lemma 2.1.4).

(i) Give Z its reduced structure (the radical of 𝓘). Shrink U to a nonempty connected affinoid subdomain V₀ ⊆ U (an affinoid Sp(C) is the disjoint union of the finitely many connected affinoids Sp(Ce_i), e_i the primitive idempotents of the noetherian ring C) and replace Z by its connected component containing V₀. Put Z_n = {z ∈ Z : dim O_{Z,z} = n} and Z_< = {z ∈ Z : dim O_{Z,z} < n}.

Normality: if Z_n meets a connected affinoid subdomain V = Sp(C) of X, then V ⊆ Z_n. Indeed C is a normal domain of dimension n, Z ∩ V = V(I) with I radical, and if I ≠ 0 then for every maximal m ⊇ I the ideal I·C_m has height ≥ 1 (0 is the only minimal prime of the domain C_m; mathlib Ideal.height_eq_zero_iff), so dim (C/I)_m ≤ dim C_m − 1 < n and no point of V lies in Z_n; hence I = 0. Therefore Z_n and Z_< are unions of intersections of Z with members of an admissible covering of X by connected affinoids, {Z_n, Z_<} is an admissible covering of Z by disjoint admissible opens, and since Z is connected and V₀ ⊆ Z_n, Z = Z_n (Conrad, proof of Lemma 2.1.4).
Z therefore contains every connected affinoid subdomain of X that it meets, so {Z, X − Z} is an admissible covering of X by disjoint admissible opens; X is connected and Z ⊇ V₀ is nonempty, so Z = X.
(ii) If Z₁ ≠ X, then X − Z₁ is a nonempty admissible open contained in Z₂, so Z₂ = X by (i).

(iii) The zero locus of f is the analytic subset of the coherent ideal f·O_X and contains U, so it is X by (i): f vanishes in the residue field of every point. On each affinoid open Sp(A) ⊆ X, A is reduced (normal, mathlib IsReduced) and Jacobson (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-jacobson, mathlib IsJacobsonRing), so f|_{Sp A} lies in the intersection of all maximal ideals, which is the nilradical 0; hence f = 0 (Conrad, proof of Theorem 2.1.2). For ℰ, choose an admissible affinoid covering on which ℰ is free; the zero locus of s is an analytic subset (locally the common zero locus of the coordinates of s) containing U, hence X, and each coordinate vanishes at every point of a reduced affinoid, hence is 0.
acceptance: In the closed unit disc Sp K⟨T⟩ (connected and normal) an f ∈ K⟨T⟩ vanishing on the open disc {|T| < 1} (an admissible open) is 0, and the only analytic subset containing {|T − 1| ≤ |ϖ|} is the disc.

Normality is needed: X = Sp K⟨S, T⟩/(ST) (two discs meeting in one point) is connected and not normal; its Laurent domain {|T| ≥ |ϖ|} is a nonempty admissible open on which T is a unit and hence S = 0, so the analytic subset {S = 0} ≠ X contains it and the nonzero function S restricts to 0 on it.
Connectedness is needed: on X = Sp(K⟨T⟩ × K⟨T⟩) the idempotent (1, 0) vanishes on the second disc and is nonzero.

nodes.title: Huber's functor r_K from rigid-analytic spaces to adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°)
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete rank-one nonarchimedean field. There is a functor r_K: Rig_K → Adic^{lft}_K together with, for each rigid space X, a morphism of ringed sites ρ_X: (|r_K(X)|, O_{r_K(X)}) → (X, O_X) over Sp K = Spa K (Huber 1994 Proposition 4.3) such that r_K(X) is locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°), ρ_X is locally coherent, and (r_K(X), ρ_X) is final: for every adic space Z locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°) and every locally coherent morphism of ringed sites λ: (|Z|, O_Z) → (X, O_X) over Sp K there is a unique morphism f: Z → r_K(X) over Spa K with ρ_X ∘ f = λ. Moreover (Huber 1996 (1.1.11) and (1.4.1)): (a) r_K(Sp A) = Spa(A, A°) and r_K of a morphism of affinoids is induced by the K-algebra map; (b) r_K carries open immersions to open embeddings and r_K(U ∩ V) = r_K(U) ∩ r_K(V); (c) a family of admissible opens is an admissible covering iff the r_K(U_i) cover r_K(X); (d) the points of X correspond bijectively to the classical points of r_K(X) (points x with k(x) finite over K), with r_K(U) ∩ X = U for admissible U; if X is quasi-separated, U ↦ r_K(U) is a bijection from the quasi-compact admissible opens of X onto the quasi-compact opens of r_K(X), under which affinoid opens correspond to affinoid opens; (e) r_K commutes with fibre products; (f) a morphism f of rigid spaces is a closed immersion iff r_K(f) is a closed embedding (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings).
hypotheses: K complete of rank one (Huber 1994 §4 hypothesis)
rigid-analytic varieties in the sense of BGR 9.3.1 (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytic-space)
proofSteps: Affinoid case: r_K(Sp A) := Spa(A, A°), an adic space because A is strongly noetherian Tate (anchor Layer 4), locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°) by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/tft-plus-ring-power-bounded.

Rational subsets of Spa(A, A°) correspond bijectively to rational subdomains of Max A via U ↦ U ∩ Max A, because constructible subsets of Spa(A, A°) are determined by their classical points (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/classical-points-constructible-density: Huber 1993 Theorem 4.1, Corollaries 4.2–4.3 and the paragraph after 4.3); this extends uniquely to a coherent morphism of sites m: |Spa(A, A°)| → |Sp A| (admissible opens and coverings of Sp A are locally refined by finite rational ones, AdicSpacesPartII:R1/gerritzen-grauert and the definition of the strong G-topology in AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytic-space), and the rings A_U agree on both sides, giving an isomorphism of structure sheaves θ; ρ_{Sp A} = (m, θ).

Universal property on affinoids (proof of Huber 1994 4.3): a locally coherent λ lifts uniquely to a morphism of ringed sites μ into |r_K(X)|, hence to a morphism of ringed spaces g (SGA 4 IV.4.2.3). g is a morphism of topologically ringed spaces because K-algebra maps between K-affinoid algebras are continuous (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-homomorphism-continuous, BGR 6.1.3). g respects the valuations: at points z ∈ Z with k(z) finite over K because the valuation of K extends uniquely to finite extensions; in general because on the affinoid opens Spa(B, B°) of Z (B⁺ = B° by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/tft-plus-ring-power-bounded = Huber 1994 Lemma 4.4) the sets {|f| ≤ |a|} and {|f| < |a|} are constructible and hence determined by those points (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/classical-points-constructible-density).
Globalisation: glue along admissible opens, which r_K sends to open subspaces (b); the universal property makes the gluing canonical.

(c)–(f): (c) from the correspondence of rational subsets and quasi-compactness of rational subsets; (d) from AdicSpacesPartII:R1/classical-points-constructible-density on affinoids (Wedhorn Example 7.58), the quasi-compact bijection for quasi-separated X by gluing the affinoid correspondence; (e) from the universal property and the affinoid fibre product Spa(B ⊗̂_A C, (B ⊗̂_A C)°) (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-fibre-product); (f) because for a K-affinoid A and an ideal J the quotient pair (A, A°)/J (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.quotient) is (A/J, (A/J)°) — the integral closure of the image of A° contains that of the image of K°⟨T⟩, which is (A/J)° by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/tft-plus-ring-power-bounded (Huber 1996 (1.4.1), citing BGR 6.3.4/1) — together with AdicSpacesPartII:R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings.
Details beyond the affinoid step are stated but not written out in Huber 1994 ('(i)-(iv) follow from the proof of (4.3)'); the missing write-up is recorded as a gap.
acceptance: r_K(Sp A) = Spa(A, A°); admissibility of a covering is detected by set-theoretic covering of r_K(X).
r_K(B¹) is the adic closed unit disc, whose non-classical points (e.g. the Gauss point) are not points of the rigid disc.

nodes.title: At a classical point, the local ring of X^ad has the same completion as the local ring of X
nodes.statement: Let X be a K-scheme locally of finite type, x ∈ X^ad a classical point and x₀ = q_X(x) the corresponding closed point (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-points). Then O_{X^ad,x} is a noetherian local ring, q^♯_x: O_{X,x₀} → O_{X^ad,x} is a local homomorphism inducing an isomorphism of residue fields and an isomorphism of completions Ô_{X,x₀} ≅ Ô_{X^ad,x}; in particular the Zariski cotangent spaces m_{x₀}/m_{x₀}² ≅ m_x/m_x² agree and dim O_{X,x₀} = dim O_{X^ad,x}.
hypotheses: K complete of rank one; x classical (k(x) finite over K)
proofSteps: Reduce to X affine, then to a chart Spa(A_k, A_k°) containing x, where x corresponds to a maximal ideal m of the affinoid algebra A_k (Wedhorn Example 7.58).

The stalk of Spa(A_k, A_k°) at the classical point x (colimit of the rings A_U over rational U ∋ x) equals the local ring O_{Sp A_k, m} of the rigid space (colimit of A_V over affinoid subdomains V ∋ m) (Conrad, adic notes, paragraph after Example 3.15): U ↦ U ∩ Max A_k is a bijection from rational subsets of Spa(A_k, A_k°) onto rational subdomains of Max A_k with the same rings A_U (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/classical-points-constructible-density = Huber 1993 Corollaries 4.2–4.3 and the paragraph after 4.3), and rational subdomains are cofinal among the affinoid subdomains containing m because every affinoid subdomain is a finite union of rational subdomains (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/gerritzen-grauert).

The rigid local ring O_{Sp A_k, m} is noetherian with completion equal to the m-adic completion of A_k (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-local-ring-completion; Conrad AWS §2.3, after Exercise 2.3.6), and the local map O_{X,x₀} → (A_k)_m induces an isomorphism on completions because every maximal ideal of K⟨ϖ^k T⟩ ≅ K⟨T'⟩ (T' = ϖ^k T) is generated by polynomials with the same residue field (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/tate-algebra-maximal-ideals-polynomial; Conrad 1999 Lemma A.1.2(2), citing BGR 7.1.1/3), and passing to the quotient by I.

Residue fields: both are the finite extension k(x₀) = A_k/m. Cotangent spaces: for a noetherian local ring R with maximal ideal 𝔪, R/𝔪² ≅ R̂/𝔪̂² (mathlib:AdicCompletion), so the completion isomorphism identifies the Zariski cotangent spaces (mathlib:IsLocalRing.CotangentSpace, tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.ZariskiCotangentSpace). Dimension: R → R̂ is flat (mathlib:AdicCompletion.flat_of_isNoetherian) with closed fibre R̂/𝔪R̂ a field, so dim R̂ = dim R by going down (mathlib:Algebra.HasGoingDown.of_flat, mathlib:Ideal.height_eq_height_add_of_liesOver_of_hasGoingDown); apply this to O_{X,x₀} and O_{X^ad,x}, whose completions are isomorphic.
acceptance: At the origin of A^{1,ad}_K, O_{X^ad,0} is the ring of power series converging on some disc around 0, strictly between K[T]_{(T)} and K[[T]], and both complete to K[[T]].
For the node y² = x²(x + 1) (char K ≠ 2) the completed local ring of X^ad at the origin is K[[x, y]]/(y² − x²(x+1)), which is not a domain although O_{X,0} is.

nodes.title: The analytification morphism q_X: X^ad → X is flat
nodes.statement: Let X be a K-scheme locally of finite type. For every point x ∈ X^ad (classical or not) the local homomorphism q^♯_x: O_{X,q_X(x)} → O_{X^ad,x} is flat. Relatively (Zavyalov Lemma 6.7): for a strongly noetherian Tate affinoid S = Spa(A, A⁺) and a scheme X locally of finite type over Spec A, the morphism X ×_{Spec A} S → X is flat.
hypotheses: K complete of rank one (absolute case); S a strongly noetherian Tate affinoid (relative case)
proofSteps: Reduce to X = Spec C affine and a chart Spa(A_k, A_k°) containing x, with C → A_k the chart map.

C → A_k is flat: A_k is noetherian, so it suffices that C_n → (A_k)_m is flat for every maximal ideal m of A_k, n = m ∩ C (maximal, as A_k/m is finite over K); this local map of noetherian local rings induces an isomorphism on completions (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-completed-local-rings, Conrad Lemma A.1.2(2)), so C_n → Ĉ_n ≅ (A_k)^_m is flat and flatness descends along the faithfully flat (A_k)_m → (A_k)^_m.

O_{X^ad,x} is the filtered colimit of the rings A_U over rational neighbourhoods U of x in the chart, each A_k → A_U flat (Wedhorn Proposition 8.30; tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.flat_toCompletionLoc, stated for complete Hausdorff strongly noetherian Tate rings and any presentation (T, s)), so O_{X^ad,x} is flat over A_k, hence over C, and, being a C_{q_X(x)}-module, over O_{X,q_X(x)}.

Relative case (Zavyalov Lemma 6.7): reduce to X affine with a closed immersion X = V(f₁,…,f_s) ⊆ A^d_A; on both sides the stalks of X are the stalks of A^d modulo (f₁,…,f_s) (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-immersions (ii), AdicSpacesPartII:R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings), and flatness is stable under this base change, so X = A^d_A; by Zavyalov Example 6.4 and scaling by ϖ^n reduce to the relative unit polydisc and factor Spa(A⟨T⟩, A⁺⟨T⟩) → Spec A⟨T⟩ → Spec A[T]: the stalks of the first map are flat by tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.flat_toCompletionLoc for the strongly noetherian Tate ring A⟨T⟩ and filtered colimits; the second map is flat by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/restricted-series-flat-over-polynomials (Zavyalov, citing Fujiwara–Kato).
acceptance: The Gauss point x of the unit disc: O_{X^ad,x} is a field extension of K(T) = O_{A¹,η}, flat as every module over a field.
Consequently F ↦ q_X^*F is exact on O_X-modules (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-of-modules).

nodes.title: Analytification of O_X-modules F ↦ F^ad = q_X^*F, its exactness, and analytified ideal sheaves
nodes.statement: For a K-scheme X locally of finite type and an O_X-module F, put F^ad := q_X^*F = O_{X^ad} ⊗_{q_X⁻¹O_X} q_X⁻¹F, the pullback of sheaves of modules along the morphism of ringed spaces q_X: X^ad_ → X (mathlib:SheafOfModules.pullback for the continuous functor of opens V ↦ q_X⁻¹(V) and the ring map q_X^♯; O_{X^ad} regarded as a sheaf of rings). Then F ↦ F^ad is an exact functor O_X-Mod → O_{X^ad}-Mod with stalks (F^ad)_x ≅ O_{X^ad,x} ⊗_{O_{X,q(x)}} F_{q(x)}; it commutes with tensor products (the sheafified tensor product of sheaves of modules — Mathlib has the monoidal structure only on presheaves of modules, so this is built here) and with pullback along analytified morphisms ((h^*G)^ad ≅ (h^ad)^*G^ad), (O_X)^ad = O_{X^ad}, and for a quasi-coherent ideal I ⊆ O_X the map I^ad → O_{X^ad} is injective with image the ideal sheaf I·O_{X^ad} of the closed adic subspace V(I)^ad (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-immersions). The same holds relatively for the analytification X ×_{Spec A} S → X of a scheme X locally of finite type over Spec A, with S = Spa(A, A⁺) a strongly noetherian Tate affinoid (Zavyalov §6). It does not hold for X ×_Y S → X with an arbitrary scheme Y and morphism S → Y, whose projection need not be flat (Y = X = A¹_K and S = Spa K mapping to the origin: the projection is the inclusion of a point and q^* is not exact).
hypotheses: X locally of finite type over K; F an arbitrary O_X-module (exactness uses flatness of q_X only)
coherence of F^ad for coherent F uses the coherent-sheaf notion of AdicSpacesPartII:R3/coherent-sheaf and is proved there
proofSteps: Define F^ad as the pullback of sheaves of modules along q_X (mathlib:SheafOfModules.pullback; the structure sheaf of X^ad is the anchor's sheaf of complete rings with its topology forgotten).

Stalks and exactness: (F^ad)_x ≅ O_{X^ad,x} ⊗_{O_{X,q(x)}} F_{q(x)} (pullback commutes with stalks of the inverse image and tensoring); pullback is right exact, and left exact because the stalk maps O_{X,q(x)} → O_{X^ad,x} are flat (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-map-flat); exactness of sheaves is checked on stalks.

(O_X)^ad = O_{X^ad}: the canonical map pullback(unit) → unit (mathlib:SheafOfModules.pullbackObjUnitToUnit) is an isomorphism since V ↦ q_X⁻¹(V) preserves finite intersections and the top element. Tensor products: Mathlib provides the monoidal structure only on presheaves of modules (mathlib:PresheafOfModules.monoidalCategory); the tensor product of sheaves of modules is its sheafification, and (F ⊗ G)^ad ≅ F^ad ⊗ G^ad is checked on stalks with the stalk formula of the previous step.
Pullback along analytified morphisms: q_{X₂} ∘ h^ad_ = h ∘ q_{X₁} and pullback is pseudo-functorial (mathlib:SheafOfModules.pullbackComp).

Ideal sheaves: tensoring 0 → I → O_X with the flat O_{X^ad,x} over O_{X,q(x)} keeps the map injective, and its image is I·O_{X^ad}, the ideal of V(I)^ad by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-immersions (ii).
Relative case: the same argument with the relative flatness of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-map-flat (Zavyalov Lemma 6.7), which is stated for X ×_{Spec A} Spa(A, A⁺) only.
acceptance: For X = A¹_K and F = O_X/(T), F^ad is the skyscraper K at the classical point 0.
For a closed immersion Z ↪ X with ideal I, (O_X/I)^ad = O_{X^ad}/I·O_{X^ad} = i^ad_* O_{Z^ad}.
