nodes.title: Continuous differentials of the analytification charts: Ωᶜ_{A_k/A'} ≅ A_k ⊗_C Ω_{C/B'} (chart form of Ω_{X^ad/Y^ad} ≅ (Ω_{X/Y})^ad)
nodes.statement: Let h: X → Y be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type over a scheme B₀ and S → B₀ as in AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification (in particular B₀ = Spec K, S = Spa K); write h_S: X_S → Y_S for the analytified morphism and q_X: X_S → X. Chart form (the content of this node): let Spec C ⊆ X and Spec B' ⊆ Y be affine opens with h(Spec C) ⊆ Spec B' and C = B'[T₁,…,Tₙ]/I, let Spa(A', A'⁺) ⊆ Y_S be an affinoid open lying over Spec B', and let Spa(A_k, A_k⁺) be the charts of X_S over it (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affine-chart-analytification: A_k = A'⟨T⟩_{E(k)}/I·A'⟨T⟩_{E(k)}). Then the A_k-linear map A_k ⊗_C Ω_{C/B'} → Ωᶜ_{A_k/A'}, 1 ⊗ dc ↦ d(c), induced by the B'-derivation C → A_k → Ωᶜ_{A_k/A'} (Ω_{C/B'} the Kähler module, mathlib:KaehlerDifferential; Ωᶜ the module of continuous differentials of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/continuous-differentials), is an isomorphism of finite A_k-modules with 1 ⊗ dTᵢ ↦ dTᵢ; it is compatible with the chart maps A_h → A_k (k ≤ h), with rational localisation and with shrinking Spec C, Spec B' and Spa(A', A'⁺). Global form: once the coherent sheaf Ω¹_{X_S/Y_S} is glued from the modules Ωᶜ in AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheaf-of-continuous-differentials (which takes this node as an input), these isomorphisms glue to the unique isomorphism Ω¹_{X_S/Y_S} ≅ O_{X_S} ⊗_{q_X⁻¹O_X} q_X⁻¹Ω_{X/Y} = (Ω_{X/Y})^ad compatible with the universal derivations; that gluing is stated and proved there, so that this node does not depend on R3.
hypotheses: h locally of finite type; continuous differentials exist for morphisms locally of weakly finite type between adic spaces (Huber 1996 (1.6.2)); on the charts the maps A' → A_k are of topologically finite type
proofSteps: Chart presentation of continuous differentials: A_k = A'⟨T⟩_{E(k)}/𝔞 with 𝔞 generated by the images of generators g_j of I, so Ωᶜ_{A_k/A'} = (⊕ᵢ A_k dTᵢ)/⟨dg_j⟩ (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/continuous-differentials (c) = Huber 1996 (1.6.2)(i); for P = Σ a_j g_j one has dP ≡ Σ a_j dg_j modulo 𝔞).

Algebraic presentation: Ω_{B'[T]/B'} is free on the dTᵢ (mathlib:KaehlerDifferential.mvPolynomialBasis) and Ω_{C/B'} is its quotient by the dg_j (conormal sequence, mathlib:KaehlerDifferential.exact_kerCotangentToTensor_mapBaseChange); A_k ⊗_C (−) is right exact.

Both presentations have the same generators and relations, so dTᵢ ↦ dTᵢ defines the isomorphism A_k ⊗_C Ω_{C/B'} ≅ Ωᶜ_{A_k/A'}; it is the map induced by the derivation because d(φ(c)) is the image of dc.

Compatibilities with A_h → A_k, rational localisation and base change follow from the functoriality and localisation compatibility of Ωᶜ (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/continuous-differentials, API map, localizationEquiv, baseChangeEquiv; Huber 1996 Proposition 1.6.3) and uniqueness (the dTᵢ generate). Gluing to sheaves is left to AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheaf-of-continuous-differentials.

nodes.title: Analytification preserves étale, smooth and unramified morphisms
nodes.statement: Let h: X₁ → X₂ be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type over Y and S → Y as in AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification. If h is étale (resp. smooth, resp. unramified) then h_S: X₁ ×_Y S → X₂ ×_Y S is étale (resp. smooth, resp. unramified) in the sense of Huber 1996 Definition 1.6.5 (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/differentials-unramified-smooth-etale, R0/smooth-morphism, R0/unramified-morphism). In particular, for K-schemes locally of finite type, h étale / smooth / unramified ⇒ h^ad étale / smooth / unramified, and a smooth X of pure dimension d gives X^ad smooth over Spa K with Ωᶜ_{O(U)/K} finite projective of rank d on every chart U (so Ω¹_{X^ad/Spa K}, glued in AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheaf-of-continuous-differentials, is locally free of rank d).
hypotheses: h a morphism of Y-schemes locally of finite type; S satisfies Huber's condition
proofSteps: Local structure: a smooth h is, locally on X₁ and X₂, given by a standard smooth ring map B' → C = B'[T₁,…,Tₙ]/(f₁,…,f_c) whose c×c Jacobian minor det(∂fᵢ/∂T_{σ(j)}) is a unit in C (mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth.exists_isStandardSmooth, mathlib:Algebra.IsStandardSmooth, mathlib:Algebra.SubmersivePresentation); an étale h is locally standard smooth of relative dimension 0, i.e. c = n (mathlib:Algebra.Etale.iff_isStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension_zero).

Reduction to charts: X₁ ×_Y S = X₁ ×_{X₂} (X₂ ×_Y S), so over an affinoid open Spa(A', A'⁺) of X₂ ×_Y S lying over Spec B' the preimage of Spec C is the union of the charts Spa(A_k, A_k⁺), A_k = A'⟨T⟩_{E(k)}/(f₁,…,f_c) (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affine-chart-analytification); unramified, smooth and étale are local on the source (Huber 1996 1.6.7(v), AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-smooth-locality).

Smooth case: Spa A_k is the closed adic subspace of the relative polydisc Z = Spa A'⟨T₁,…,Tₙ⟩_{E(k)} cut out by f₁,…,f_c (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings); Z is smooth over Spa A' with Ωᶜ free on dT₁,…,dTₙ (Huber 1996 1.6.7(i), AdicSpacesPartII:R0/restricted-power-series-smooth; AdicSpacesPartII:R0/continuous-differentials (c)). The Jacobian minor is a unit in A_k, hence in every stalk O_{Z,x}, x ∈ Spa A_k, so df₁,…,df_c together with the dT_j of the n − c remaining indices form a basis of (Ω_{Z/Spa A'})_x; by the Jacobian criterion (Huber 1996 1.6.9(ii), AdicSpacesPartII:R0/jacobian-criterion-closed-subspace) Spa A_k → Spa A' is smooth. (This avoids re-presenting A'⟨T⟩_{E(k)} as an iterated weighted series ring, for which tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.iterateAlgEquiv — unit weights only, no plus rings — does not suffice.)

Étale case: c = n, so the minor is the full Jacobian and Huber 1996 Proposition 1.7.1 ((ii) ⇒ (i), AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-local-structure, with Tᵢ = E(k)) shows Spa A_k → Spa A' étale — the proof of Huber 1996 Corollary 1.7.3(i).

Unramified case: Ω_{C/B'} = 0, so Ωᶜ_{A_k/A'} ≅ A_k ⊗_C Ω_{C/B'} = 0 (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytic-kahler-differentials), and a morphism locally of finite type with vanishing continuous differentials is unramified (Huber 1996 Proposition 1.6.8 (b) ⇒ (a), AdicSpacesPartII:R0/infinitesimal-criteria).
Local freeness for smooth X of pure dimension d: Ωᶜ_{A_k/K} ≅ A_k ⊗_C Ω_{C/K} (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytic-kahler-differentials) is finite projective of rank d because Ω_{C/K} is.
acceptance: For n invertible in K, the Kummer map G_m → G_m, x ↦ xⁿ, is finite étale; its analytification A^{1,ad} \ {0} → A^{1,ad} \ {0} is finite étale.

nodes.title: Rigid analytification X ↦ X^an of schemes locally of finite type over K
nodes.statement: For a K-scheme X locally of finite type there is a rigid-analytic space X^an with a morphism of locally G-ringed K-spaces i_X: X^an → X that is final among rigid spaces over K with such a morphism: for every rigid space Y over K, composition with i_X is a bijection Hom_{Rig_K}(Y, X^an) → Hom_K(Y, X). X ↦ X^an is a functor; A^{n,an} is the union of the closed polydiscs of radius |c|^{-j} (0 < |c| < 1); for affine X = V(I) ⊆ A^n, X^an is the closed analytic subspace of A^{n,an} cut out by I; and i_X is a bijection onto the closed points of X; for a Zariski-open U ⊆ X the analytification of the open immersion U → X is an isomorphism of U^an onto the admissible open i_X⁻¹(U) of X^an; and for morphisms X → Z, Y → Z of K-schemes locally of finite type the canonical map (X ×_Z Y)^an → X^an ×_{Z^an} Y^an is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: K complete of rank one; X locally of finite type over K
proofSteps: A morphism Y → Spec C from a rigid space is a K-algebra map C → O_Y(Y) (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-gamma-spec = Conrad irred. Lemma A.1.1, the rigid form of Stacks 01I1).

A^{n,an}: glue the balls D_j = Sp K⟨ξ_{1,j}, …, ξ_{n,j}⟩ along D_j ≅ {|ξ_{i,j+1}| ≤ |c|} ⊆ D_{j+1} (ξ_{i,j+1} ↦ cξ_{i,j}), with global coordinates ξ_i = ξ_{i,j}/c^j; for a K-affinoid A and a_1, …, a_n ∈ A, some c^j a_i are power-bounded (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-supremum-seminorm, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-power-bounded-iff-sup, maximum modulus AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-maximum-modulus), so Hom(Sp A, A^{n,an}) = Aⁿ via the Tate-algebra universal property; for general Y glue over an admissible affinoid covering (Conrad AWS Example 2.4.3; Conrad irred. §A.1).

Affine X = Spec K[T]/I: V(I) := the closed analytic subspace of A^{n,an} with V(I) ∩ D_j = Sp(K⟨ξ_{·,j}⟩/I(c^{-j}ξ_{·,j})) (API closedSubspace of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytic-space); a morphism Y → A^{n,an} (an n-tuple in O_Y(Y)) factors through V(I) iff the tuple is killed by I (check on affinoids Sp B → D_j), which by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-gamma-spec is Hom_K(Y, X).
General X: glue the affine pieces along Zariski opens, which are admissible and satisfy the universal property of U^an (method of SGA 1 XII 1.1, Conrad irred. Appendix A.1).
Closed points: Spec(k')^an = Sp(k') for finite k'/K, and closed points of X are the images of K-morphisms Spec k' → X (Conrad irred. Lemma A.1.2(1)).

Open subschemes: for Zariski-open U ⊆ X, i_X⁻¹(U) is an admissible open of X^an (a morphism to X pulls Zariski opens back to admissible opens, Conrad irred. §A.1), and a morphism Y → X from a rigid space factors through U iff its image lies in U, so i_X⁻¹(U) → U represents Hom_K(·, U); hence U^an ≅ i_X⁻¹(U) by uniqueness of representing objects (this is also the gluing step of SGA 1 XII 1.1).

Fibre products (Conrad irred. Lemma A.1.2(3)): by the open-subscheme step reduce to X, Y, Z affine; then X ×_Z Y = Spec(B_X ⊗_{B_Z} B_Y), and by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-gamma-spec both (X ×_Z Y)^an and X^an ×_{Z^an} Y^an represent Y' ↦ Hom_K(B_X ⊗_{B_Z} B_Y, O_{Y'}(Y')) = Hom_K(Y', X) ×_{Hom_K(Y', Z)} Hom_K(Y', Y).
acceptance: (A¹_K)^an is not quasi-compact; (Spec L)^an = Sp(L) for L/K finite.
The analytification of the affine line with doubled origin is not quasi-separated (Conrad irred. Appendix A.1).

nodes.title: r_K is fully faithful, generates the lft adic spaces, restricts to an equivalence on quasi-separated objects, and detects affinoids
nodes.statement: Let K be complete of rank one. (i) r_K: Rig_K → Adic_K is fully faithful (Huber 1994 4.5(ii)). (ii) The smallest saturated full subcategory of adic spaces over Spa(K, K°) containing the image of r_K (closed under open subspaces, open covers and isomorphism) consists of the adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°) (4.5(iii)). (iii) r_K restricts to an equivalence between quasi-separated rigid-analytic spaces over K and quasi-separated adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°) (4.5(iv); Huber 1996 (1.1.11), also over a rigid base X and r_K(X)). (iv) For a rigid space X, r_K(X) is affinoid iff X is affinoid (4.5(v)).
hypotheses: K complete of rank one; in (iii) both sides quasi-separated
proofSteps: (i), (iii): from the universal property of r_K (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor) and, for (iii), the bijection between the quasi-compact admissible opens of a quasi-separated X and the quasi-compact opens of r_K(X), matching affinoids (comparison functor (d), Huber 1996 (1.1.11)); Huber states that (i)–(iv) follow from the proof of 4.3, citing [H1, 4.6] for (i) (a mis-citation of Huber 1993 Corollary 4.4), without writing the argument; the write-up is recorded as a gap.

(ii): r_K(X) is locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°) (Huber 1994 4.3), and being locally of finite type passes to open subspaces and is local on the source, so the lft adic spaces form a saturated subcategory containing the image of r_K. Conversely, by the definition of 'locally of finite type' (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-type-morphism-classes; Huber 1994 definition after Lemma 3.5, with V = Spa(K, K°)) every point of an lft X has an affinoid neighbourhood Spa(B, B⁺) with (K, K°) → (B, B⁺) of topologically finite type; then B is K-affinoid and B⁺ = B° (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/tft-plus-ring-power-bounded), so the neighbourhood is r_K(Sp B) and X belongs to every saturated subcategory containing the image.

(iv): if r_K(X) = Y is affinoid then (K, K°) → (O_Y(Y), O⁺_Y(Y)) is of topologically finite type (Huber 1994 Proposition 3.6, AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affinoid-over-noetherian-base-tft — no public proof, gap), so O⁺_Y(Y) = O_Y(Y)° (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/tft-plus-ring-power-bounded) and Y ≅ r_K(Sp O_Y(Y)); by (i) X ≅ Sp O_Y(Y). Conversely r_K(Sp A) = Spa(A, A°) is affinoid.
acceptance: The adic affine line A^{1,ad}_K is quasi-separated and locally of finite type, so it is r_K of the rigid affine line.
The open unit disc {|T| < 1} ⊆ Spa(K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩) is not affinoid, matching the rigid open disc not being affinoid.

nodes.title: The rigid and adic ringed topoi agree: ρ_X induces an equivalence Shv(r_K(X)) ≃ Shv(X)
nodes.statement: Let K be complete of rank one and X a rigid-analytic space over K. The morphism of ringed sites ρ_X: (|r_K(X)|, O_{r_K(X)}) → (X, O_X) induces an equivalence of ringed topoi (Shv(r_K(X)), O_{r_K(X)}) ≃ (Shv(X), O_X) (Huber 1994 Proposition 4.5(i)). For X = Sp(A) this is Huber 1993 Corollary 4.4: sheaves for the Grothendieck topology of rational subdomains of Max A are the same as sheaves on the topological space Spa(A, A°).
hypotheses: K complete of rank one
proofSteps: Affinoid case, adic side: rational subsets of Spa(A, A°) are quasi-compact and form a basis stable under finite intersections, so sheaves on the space Spa(A, A°) are the sheaves on the site of rational subsets with finite coverings (EGA 0.3.2.2 as used by Huber; the dense-subsite comparison lemma mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.IsDenseSubsite.sheafEquiv).

Affinoid case, rigid side: Huber 1993 Corollary 4.4 is stated for the weak G-topology 𝒯_A of rational subdomains of Max A with finite coverings; U ↦ U ∩ Max A identifies rational subsets and finite coverings on both sides (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/classical-points-constructible-density; Huber 1993 Corollary 4.3). The strong G-topology of Sp A (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytic-space), whose topos is Shv(X), contains 𝒯_A as a dense subsite: affinoid subdomains are finite unions of rational subdomains (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/gerritzen-grauert) and admissibility is local finite refinement by definition (BGR 9.1.4); so the two topoi agree (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.IsDenseSubsite.sheafEquiv).
Global case: the affinoid equivalences are compatible with restriction to admissible opens (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor (b)–(c)) and glue along an admissible affinoid covering.
The structure sheaves match because both are U ↦ A_U on rational subsets, and the equivalence is the one induced by ρ_X.
acceptance: Global sections: Γ(r_K(X), O) = Γ(X, O_X); for X = Sp A both equal A.

On the closed disc X = Sp K⟨T⟩, the sheaf corresponding to the skyscraper sheaf at the Gauss point of r_K(X) is nonzero although its stalks at all points of X vanish (each classical point has a rational neighbourhood avoiding the Gauss point): the rigid topos lacks enough classical points, while the adic space, a topological space, has enough points.

nodes.title: r_K(X^an) ≅ X^ad: the adic space of the rigid analytification is the adic analytification
nodes.statement: Let K be complete of rank one and X a K-scheme locally of finite type. There is a unique isomorphism r_K(X^an) ≅ X^ad over Spa(K, K°) compatible with the maps to X (i_X ∘ ρ_{X^an} and q_X); it is natural in X and commutes with fibre products.
hypotheses: K complete of rank one; X locally of finite type over K (no separatedness)
proofSteps: Both sides are built by gluing along Zariski opens of X, and both constructions commute with open immersions: U^ad → X^ad is the open q_X⁻¹(U) (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-immersions (i)); U^an = i_X⁻¹(U) is an admissible open of X^an by the gluing construction of X^an (Conrad 1999 Appendix A.1, SGA 1 XII 1.1; AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytification); r_K carries open immersions to open embeddings (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor (b)). So it suffices to treat X = Spec K[T]/I.

For affine X, r_K(X^an) is the union of the r_K of the rigid discs {|T| ≤ |c|^{-j}} cut out by I, i.e. ⋃_j Spa(K⟨c^j T⟩/I, (K⟨c^j T⟩/I)°), which is the chart description of X^ad (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-functor with ϖ = c) — Huber 1994 Remark 4.6(i).
Uniqueness and naturality: both sides map to X compatibly, and an automorphism of X^ad over Spa K commuting with q_X is the identity by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-universal-property.

Fibre products: (X ×_Z Y)^an ≅ X^an ×_{Z^an} Y^an (Conrad 1999 Lemma A.1.2(3)), r_K commutes with fibre products (comparison functor (e)), and (X ×_Z Y)^ad ≅ X^ad ×_{Z^ad} Y^ad (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-fibre-products); by uniqueness the three isomorphisms are compatible.
acceptance: For X = A¹_K: r_K((A¹)^an) = A^{1,ad}_K, the union of the discs Spa(K⟨ϖ^k T⟩, K°⟨ϖ^k T⟩).
The classical points of X^ad are the points of X^an, i.e. the closed points of X (compatibility with AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-points).

uses.how: X^rig in Huber 3.8.1 is identified with X^ad through r_K

nodes.title: Separated, partially proper and proper morphisms of rigid spaces versus their adic counterparts (Huber 1996 1.3.19)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of rigid-analytic spaces over K (K complete of rank one), with Kiehl's notions: separated (diagonal a closed immersion), partially proper (relative compactness of affinoid pieces, BGR/Kiehl) and proper (= quasi-compact and partially proper, AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytic-space). (i) f is separated iff r_K(f) is separated (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/separated-morphism). (ii) If f is partially proper then r_K(f) is partially proper (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/partially-proper-morphism); the converse holds when K° is discretely valued. (iii) If f is proper then r_K(f) is proper (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/universally-closed-and-proper-morphism); the converse holds when K° is discretely valued. (iv) If f is locally quasi-finite, the converses in (ii)–(iii) hold for arbitrary K (Huber 1996 Lemma 1.5.9, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/quasi-finite-and-finiteness-criteria).
hypotheses: K complete of rank one; the converses of (ii)–(iii) need K° discrete in the source
the proofs of (i) and of the converses are in Huber's habilitation [Hu4, 3.11.21] and Lütkebohmert [L1], neither read
proofSteps: (i) forward: r_K commutes with fibre products and a morphism of rigid spaces is a closed immersion iff its r_K is a closed embedding (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor (e), (f)); so if Δ_f is a closed immersion, r_K(Δ_f) = Δ_{r_K(f)} is a closed embedding, its image is closed and r_K(f) is separated (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/separated-morphism).

(ii), (iii) forward: r_K(f) is separated by (i); relative compactness U ⋐_W V of affinoid pieces yields existence of centres for valuation rings, i.e. the valuative criterion of Huber 1996 Corollary 1.3.9 for r_K(f) (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/separated-proper-partially-proper) — this is the argument written in the proof of Huber 1996 Lemma 1.5.9 (b) ⇒ (c), which the source points to. Properness then follows from proper = partially proper + quasi-compact, quasi-compactness being preserved by r_K on quasi-separated spaces (comparison functor (d)).
(i) converse and the converses of (ii)–(iii): delegated by the source to [Hu4, 3.11.21(ii)] and to [L1] with 1.3.18(iii) (formal models over a discrete valuation ring); recorded as a gap.

(iv): Huber 1996 Lemma 1.5.9, read with its proof (pp. 73–75): (c) ⇒ (a) uses Huber 1.5.6 (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/partially-proper-quasi-finite-local-finiteness) to get finite U → V around the closure of a maximal point, Lemma 1.5.10 (a maximal point is the intersection of the rational neighbourhoods of its closure; not decomposed, see the packet gap on Huber 1.5.7–1.5.10) and integrality over A at maximal points; the properness converse adds quasi-compactness, which r_K preserves and reflects through the bijection of quasi-compact opens (comparison functor (d)).
acceptance: r_K of the inclusion of the open unit disc into the closed unit disc is partially proper but not proper (not quasi-compact).
r_K(P^{1,an}) → Spa(K, K°) is proper, P^{1,an} being proper in Kiehl's sense (Conrad AWS Example 3.2.5).

nodes.title: Closures of constructible sets are compatible with analytification; closedness is detected on X^ad
nodes.statement: Let X be a K-scheme locally of finite type and T ⊆ X a locally constructible subset. Then q_X⁻¹(closure(T)) = closure(q_X⁻¹(T)) in X^ad. Consequently T is closed (resp. open, resp. dense) in X iff q_X⁻¹(T) is closed (resp. open, resp. dense) in X^ad.
hypotheses: K complete of rank one; X locally of finite type over K; T locally constructible (for instance the image of an immersion)
proofSteps: q_X is continuous, so q_X⁻¹(closure T) is closed and contains closure(q_X⁻¹ T).

Reduction to classical points: let r ∈ q_X⁻¹(closure T) and N a rational neighbourhood of r in an affinoid chart Spa(A_k, A_k°). Put Z = closure(T) with its reduced structure; by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-immersions (ii) the set N ∩ q_X⁻¹(Z) is the underlying set of the rational subset N ∩ Z^ad of the closed adic subspace Z^ad, i.e. of Spa(B, B°) with B = O(N)/J·O(N) (J the ideal of Z), a K-affinoid algebra. It contains r, so B ≠ 0 and B has a maximal ideal; it gives a classical point r' ∈ N ∩ q_X⁻¹(Z) (residue field finite over K, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-residue-fields-finite; AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-points (ii)). N is also a neighbourhood of r', and w = q_X(r') is a closed point of closure(T). (Constructibility of N ∩ q_X⁻¹(closure T) cannot be used here: a Zariski-closed subset of an affinoid such as a classical point {x} ⊆ Spa(K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩) is closed but not constructible, its complement not being quasi-compact; density of classical points in the constructible topology (Huber 1993 Corollary 4.2) is therefore not the right tool, Zariski-closedness is.)

Classical case: write T as a finite union of locally closed sets E; w ∈ closure(E) for some E, and w is a specialisation of a point of E (Stacks 0060, 02JQ). Let Z = closure(E) with reduced structure, J the ideal of Z \ E. If N ∩ q_X⁻¹(E) were empty, J would vanish at every point of the neighbourhood N ∩ Z^ad of r' (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-immersions), hence be nilpotent on an affinoid neighbourhood of r' (a function vanishing at all classical points of a K-affinoid lies in every maximal ideal, and the nilradical of a K-affinoid algebra is the intersection of its maximal ideals — the Jacobson property, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-jacobson; residue fields at maximal ideals are finite by AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-residue-fields-finite), hence in Ô_{Z^ad,r'} ≅ Ô_{Z,w} (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-completed-local-rings), hence J_w is nilpotent (faithful flatness of completion) and Z \ E contains all generalisations of w, contradicting w being a specialisation of a point of E.

Closedness: if q_X⁻¹(T) is closed then q_X⁻¹(closure T) = q_X⁻¹(T), and surjectivity of q_X (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-points (i)) gives closure(T) = T. Openness and density follow by complements.
acceptance: The image of the diagonal of the affine line with doubled origin is not closed, and neither is its preimage in the analytification of the self-product; this is how non-separatedness is seen on X^ad.
For T = G_m ⊆ A¹_K, q⁻¹(T) = A^{1,ad} \ {0} is open and dense but not closed.

nodes.title: X is connected iff X^ad is connected
nodes.statement: Let X be a K-scheme locally of finite type (K complete of rank one). Then X is connected iff X^ad is connected; more precisely, T ↦ q_X⁻¹(T) is a bijection from the open and closed subsets of X to those of X^ad.
hypotheses: K complete of rank one; X locally of finite type
proofSteps: Injectivity and preservation of clopenness: q_X is continuous and surjective (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-points (i)), so T ↦ q_X⁻¹(T) is injective and sends clopens to clopens.

Connected components: X is locally noetherian, so its connected components X_i are open and closed; by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-immersions (i) each X_i^ad is an open subspace of X^ad with underlying set q_X⁻¹(X_i), and these partition X^ad. Hence surjectivity of T ↦ q_X⁻¹(T) reduces to: X connected ⇒ X^ad connected.
X connected ⇒ X^an connected: AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytification-connected (Conrad 1999, Theorem A.1.3(1) via Theorem 2.3.1).

X^an connected ⇒ r_K(X^an) connected: a decomposition of |r_K(X^an)| into two disjoint nonempty open sets U, V writes each as a union of quasi-compact opens r_K(W) with W quasi-compact admissible opens; all these W together form an admissible covering of X^an (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor (c)), so the unions of the W's in U and in V are disjoint nonempty admissible opens covering X^an admissibly — equivalently, U ⊔ V is a decomposition of the terminal sheaf, transported by the topos equivalence AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-topos-equivalence. Finally r_K(X^an) ≅ X^ad (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytification-comparison).
acceptance: A¹_K is connected, so A^{1,ad}_K is connected (and locally connected, Zavyalov 2024 Lemma 2.2), although its subspace of classical points is totally disconnected.
Spec(K × K) analytifies to two points.

nodes.title: The analytified projective space P^{n,ad} → Spa K is proper; relatively (P^n_Y)^ad → Y^ad is proper
nodes.statement: For every n ≥ 0 the morphism (P^n_K)^ad → Spa(K, K°) is proper in Huber's sense (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/universally-closed-and-proper-morphism), and (P^n_K)^ad is covered by the n+1 closed unit polydiscs D_i = {|T_j| ≤ |T_i| for all j}, i = 0,…,n. For a K-scheme Y locally of finite type, (P^n_Y)^ad ≅ (P^n_K)^ad ×_{Spa K} Y^ad → Y^ad is proper. Relatively, for a scheme Y and an analytic adic space S satisfying Huber's condition with a morphism S_ → Y, P^n_Y ×_Y S → S is proper; over an affinoid Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ S it is covered by the n+1 relative closed unit polydiscs Spa(A⟨T_j/T_i⟩, (A⁺⟨T_j/T_i⟩)^~).
hypotheses: K complete of rank one
proofSteps: Cover: the i-th standard chart U_i = Spec K[T_j/T_i] ≅ A^n_K has analytification the open subspace U_i^ad = q⁻¹(U_i) (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-immersions (i)), and D_i ⊆ U_i^ad is its closed unit polydisc {|T_j/T_i| ≤ 1 for all j}, an affinoid (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytic-affine-space). Every x ∈ (P^n)^ad lies in some U_i^ad (q is surjective, AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-points). Choose m with |T_m/T_i|_x maximal among m = 0,…,n; it is ≥ |T_i/T_i|_x = 1, so T_m/T_i ∉ supp(x), hence q(x) ∈ U_m, x ∈ U_m^ad and |T_j/T_m|_x = |T_j/T_i|_x / |T_m/T_i|_x ≤ 1 for all j, i.e. x ∈ D_m. Hence (P^n)^ad is quasi-compact.

Separated: P^n_K is separated (mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.isSeparated), so its diagonal is a closed immersion, whose analytification is the diagonal of (P^n)^ad (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-fibre-products) and a closed embedding (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-immersions); hence the diagonal of (P^n)^ad has closed image.

Universally closed (valuative criterion, Huber 1996 Corollary 1.3.9, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/separated-proper-partially-proper, applicable since (P^n)^ad → Spa K is quasi-separated, quasi-compact by the first step and locally of finite type): let (x, A) be a point of X_v, i.e. A ⊆ k(x)⁺ a valuation ring of k(x) (finer than v_x) containing the image of K°. Choose i with x ∈ U_i^ad and then m maximising the A-valuation of T_m/T_i (the maximum is ≥ the value of T_i/T_i = 1, so T_m/T_i ≠ 0 in k(x) and x ∈ U_m^ad). Then T_j/T_m ∈ A for all j, so (x, A) has a centre on D_m = Spa(K⟨T_j/T_m⟩, K°⟨T_j/T_m⟩) lying over the unique centre on Spa K. The index must be chosen with respect to the valuation of A, not of v_x: elements with |·|_x = 1 need not lie in A. Centres are unique by separatedness.

Alternatively: P^{n,an} is Kiehl-proper (Conrad AWS Example 3.2.5) and properness passes to r_K (forward direction of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/proper-separated-comparisons (iii)), with r_K(P^{n,an}) ≅ (P^n)^ad (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytification-comparison).

Relative: (P^n_Y)^ad ≅ (P^n_K)^ad ×_{Spa K} Y^ad (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-fibre-products) and properness is stable under adic base change (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/proper-base-change). Over an analytic S the same three steps apply verbatim with the relative polydiscs Spa(A⟨T_j/T_i⟩) over affinoids Spa(A, A⁺) of S (quasi-compact over S), the relative diagonal, and Huber's valuative criterion for morphisms of analytic adic spaces.

nodes.title: Separatedness and properness comparison: f is separated (proper) iff f^ad is
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of K-schemes locally of finite type (K complete of rank one). (i) f is separated iff f^ad is separated (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/separated-morphism). (ii) If f is proper then f^ad is proper (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/universally-closed-and-proper-morphism). (iii) If f is of finite type (quasi-compact) and f^ad is proper, then f is proper. In particular a K-scheme X of finite type is separated (resp. proper) iff X^ad is separated (resp. proper) over Spa(K, K°); for instance P^{n,ad} is proper and A^{1,ad} is separated but not proper. (ii′) Relatively: for a proper morphism f: X → Y of schemes and an analytic adic space S satisfying Huber's condition with S_ → Y, the projection X ×_Y S → S is proper; the forward direction of (i) also holds relatively.
hypotheses: K complete of rank one; in (iii) f quasi-compact (A^{1,ad} → Spa K is not quasi-compact, and neither is A¹ → Spec K proper)
proofSteps: (i) ⇒: Δ_f is a closed immersion, (Δ_f)^ad = Δ_{f^ad} (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-fibre-products) is a closed embedding (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-immersions), so its image is closed; f^ad is locally of finite type, hence locally of weakly finite type (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-type-morphism-classes): f^ad is separated in the sense of Huber 1996 1.3.1.

(i) ⇐: Δ_f is an immersion (Stacks 01KJ), quasi-compact because X ×_Y X is locally noetherian (Stacks 01OX); the image of Δ_{f^ad} = (Δ_f)^ad is q⁻¹(Δ_f(X)) (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-immersions (iii)). If it is closed, Δ_f(X) is closed by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-constructible-closure, so Δ_f is a closed immersion.

(ii): properness of f^ad is local on Y^ad (the V^ad for affine opens V ⊆ Y cover Y^ad), so let Y be affine, hence noetherian. By Chow's lemma (Stacks 0200) there are a proper surjective π: X' → X and an immersion X' → P^n_Y, which is a closed immersion because f∘π is proper and P^n_Y is separated. Thus (f∘π)^ad is a closed embedding (proper: AdicSpacesPartII:R0/closed-embedding-proper) followed by (P^n_Y)^ad → Y^ad (proper: AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytic-projective-space-proper), hence proper (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/proper-comp). π^ad is surjective after any base change (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-surjective; AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-product-points), so for closed Z ⊆ X^ad_T the image f^ad_T(Z) = (f∘π)^ad_T((π^ad_T)⁻¹ Z) is closed: f^ad is universally closed. f^ad is quasi-compact: for a quasi-compact open W ⊆ Y^ad, (f^ad)⁻¹(W) = π^ad(((f∘π)^ad)⁻¹(W)) by surjectivity of π^ad, the continuous image of a quasi-compact set ((f∘π)^ad is proper, hence quasi-compact). (Quasi-compactness of f^ad does not follow from that of f: A¹ → Spec K is quasi-compact, A^{1,ad} → Spa K is not.) f^ad is separated by (i) and locally of finite type, hence locally of +weakly finite type; so it is proper (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/universally-closed-of-surjective, whose properness clause requires the quasi-compactness just shown; Huber 1996 Definition 1.3.2(ii) requires f of +weakly finite type, which includes quasi-compactness).

(ii′): properness is local on S, and an analytic adic space is covered by Tate affinoids, so let S = Spa(A, A⁺) with A Tate, mapping into Spec B ⊆ Y; under Huber's condition A is noetherian (A = A₀[1/ϖ] for a noetherian ring of definition A₀, or A strongly noetherian Tate). X ×_Y S = (X ×_Y Spec A) ×_{Spec A} S (schemePullback.trans, AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification), so replace Y by the noetherian scheme Spec A and run the argument of (ii) (with AdicSpacesPartII:R0/proper-base-change for the base change to S, and the relative forms of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-immersions (iii), AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-surjective and AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytic-projective-space-proper); this is the adic form of Zavyalov Remark 6.3 and of the remark after Huber 1996 Lemma 3.7.3 used by ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H5.

(iii): f is separated by (i). With Y affine noetherian, Chow's lemma gives π: X' → X proper surjective and an open immersion j of X' onto a dense open of a closed subscheme P̄ ⊆ P^n_Y. (f∘π)^ad = f^ad ∘ π^ad is proper by (ii) and the hypothesis; since P̄^ad → Y^ad is separated, j^ad is proper (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/proper-of-comp-separated), so its image q⁻¹(j(X')) is open and closed in P̄^ad. By AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-constructible-closure j(X') is closed in P̄, hence equal to P̄ by density; so f∘π: X' ≅ P̄ → Y is proper, and f is proper because π is surjective and f is separated of finite type (Stacks 03GN).
acceptance: P^{n,ad}_K → Spa K is proper; the affine line A^{1,ad}_K is separated but not proper (not quasi-compact).

nodes.title: For f of finite type: f is finite (resp. a closed immersion) iff f^ad is
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of finite type between K-schemes locally of finite type (K complete of rank one). Then f is finite iff f^ad is finite (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-morphism), and f is a closed immersion iff f^ad is a closed embedding (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings).
hypotheses: f of finite type (quasi-compact); K complete of rank one
proofSteps: ⇒ in both cases: AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-finite and AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-immersions.

Finite ⇐: finite morphisms to analytic adic spaces are proper (Huber 1996 Lemma 1.4.5(ii), AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-morphisms), so f is proper by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-separated-proper (iii) (f is quasi-compact by hypothesis). For a closed point y with classical point y' above it (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-points (ii)), the fibre X_y analytifies to X^ad ×_{Y^ad} Spa(k(y), k(y)°) (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-fibre-products), which is finite over Spa(k(y), k(y)°) (base change of finite morphisms, R0/finite-morphism API IsFinite.baseChange), hence a finite set. By AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-points (ii) X_y has finitely many closed points, hence is finite (a scheme of finite type over a field with finitely many closed points is zero-dimensional). The locus of y with dim X_y ≥ 1 is constructible (upper semicontinuity of fibre dimension and Chevalley) and contains no closed point of the Jacobson scheme Y, so it is empty: f is quasi-finite. Proper with finite fibres over a locally noetherian base is finite (Stacks 02OG).

Closed immersion ⇐: a closed embedding is finite (Huber 1996 Lemma 1.4.5(iii), AdicSpacesPartII:R0/closed-embedding-finite), so f is finite by the previous step. The cokernel Q of O_Y → f_*O_X is coherent, and Q^ad is the cokernel of O_{Y^ad} → f^ad_* O_{X^ad} (chart formula C ⊗_B A of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-finite and exactness of analytification, AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-of-modules), which vanishes because f^ad is a closed embedding. At a closed point y with classical point y', Q_y ⊗ Ô_{Y,y} ≅ (Q^ad)_{y'} ⊗ Ô_{Y^ad,y'} = 0 (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-completed-local-rings), so Q_y = 0 by faithful flatness of completion; Q is coherent on the Jacobson scheme Y, so Q = 0. A finite morphism with O_Y → f_*O_X surjective is a closed immersion.
acceptance: The normalisation of the cuspidal cubic A¹ → V(y² − x³), t ↦ (t², t³), is finite and bijective but not a closed immersion; its analytification is finite, bijective on points and not a closed embedding (the stalk map at the cusp is not surjective).
G_m → A¹ is not finite, and neither is its analytification (preimage of the unit disc is not affinoid).

nodes.title: f is étale (resp. smooth) iff f^ad is
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of K-schemes locally of finite type (K complete of rank one). Then f is étale (resp. smooth, resp. unramified) iff f^ad is étale (resp. smooth, resp. unramified) in the sense of Huber 1996 Definition 1.6.5.
hypotheses: K complete of rank one
proofSteps: ⇒: AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-etale-smooth.

Reduction to closed points: the étale, smooth and unramified loci of f are open (Zariski) and X is Jacobson (mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType.jacobsonSpace), so it suffices to check closed points x, with y = f(x) and the classical points x', y' above them (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-points).

Unramified: Ω_{X^ad/Y^ad} = (Ω_{X/Y})^ad (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytic-kahler-differentials) vanishes near x' iff Ω_{X/Y,x} ⊗ Ô_{X,x} = 0 (completed local rings agree, AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-completed-local-rings), iff Ω_{X/Y,x} = 0 (faithful flatness of completion, Nakayama).

Flatness: first O_{Y^ad,y'} → O_{X^ad,x'} is flat. If f^ad is étale this is AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-flat-unramified ((a) ⇒ (b), Huber 1996 Proposition 1.7.5). Huber 1.7.5 is about étale morphisms only; if f^ad is smooth, write it near x' as an étale U → D^d_{Y^ad} followed by the relative polydisc projection (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-local-structure, Tate case); the étale part is flat at the image of x' by R0/etale-flat-unramified, and D^d_{Y^ad} ⊆ (A^d_Y)^ad → Y^ad is flat at classical points because its completed local rings there are those of the flat morphism A^d_Y → Y (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-completed-local-rings, applied to A^d_Y and Y) and flatness of a local homomorphism of noetherian local rings follows from flatness of the completed map. Then Ô_{Y^ad,y'} → Ô_{X^ad,x'} is flat (completion of a flat local homomorphism of noetherian local rings), i.e. Ô_{Y,y} → Ô_{X,x} is flat, hence O_{Y,y} → O_{X,x} is flat (O_{X,x} → Ô_{X,x} is faithfully flat).

Smooth: f is flat at x by the previous step. Let d be the rank of the locally free module Ω_{X^ad/Y^ad} near x' (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-differentials-locally-free, Huber 1996 Proposition 1.6.9(i)); by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytic-kahler-differentials, Ω_{X/Y,x} ⊗ k(x) has dimension d, so Ω_{X/Y,x} is generated by d elements (Nakayama). The fibre (X_y)^ad = X^ad ×_{Y^ad} Spa(k(y), k(y)°) (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-fibre-products) is smooth of relative dimension d over Spa(k(y), k(y)°) (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-etale-base-change), hence locally étale over the d-dimensional polydisc, so its local ring at the classical point above x has dimension d; by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-completed-local-rings dim O_{X_y,x} = d = dim_x(X_y). Stacks 01V9 (flat, Ω_{X/Y,x} generated by dim_x(X_y) elements) gives smoothness at x; étale = smooth + unramified.
acceptance: The Frobenius-type map A¹ → A¹, T ↦ T^p over K of characteristic p is flat, not étale; its analytification is not étale (Ω = K dT ≠ 0 relatively).
T ↦ T² (char K ≠ 2) is not étale at 0 and its analytification is not étale at the classical point 0.

nodes.title: Analytic groups: analytification of group schemes, finite locally free group schemes, abelian varieties and isogenies
nodes.statement: Let Sch^{lft}_K be the category of K-schemes locally of finite type (a full subcategory of Over(Spec K) closed under finite products, with its cartesian monoidal structure) and Adic^{lft}_K the category of adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa K = Spa(K, K°), which has finite products X ×_{Spa K} Y (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence) and terminal object Spa K. Because (·)^ad preserves finite products (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-fibre-products), it is a monoidal functor and carries group objects to group objects: a group scheme (G, m, e, i) locally of finite type over K gives the analytic group G^ad with multiplication m^ad, unit e^ad: Spa K → G^ad and inverse i^ad, and a homomorphism φ gives the homomorphism φ^ad; commutative group schemes give commutative group objects. Relatively, for a group scheme G → Y locally of finite type and S → Y as in AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification, G ×_Y S is a group object over S. Properties: (a) for an affinoid Spa(D, D⁺) over Spa K, the group of its points in G^ad is G(D); (b) if G is finite locally free of rank d over Y then G^ad → Y^ad is finite, with O over each affinoid finite projective of rank d; (c) if A is an abelian variety over K then A^ad is a commutative analytic group that is proper, smooth of dimension dim A and connected over Spa K; (d) if φ: A → B is an isogeny (a finite surjective homomorphism) then φ^ad is a finite surjective homomorphism whose kernel A^ad ×_{B^ad, e^ad} Spa K is (ker φ)^ad, a finite analytic group.
hypotheses: K complete of rank one; group schemes locally of finite type over K (resp. over Y)
the target category is adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa K, where finite products exist
proofSteps: Adic^{lft}_K has finite products (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence) and a terminal object, hence a cartesian monoidal structure (mathlib:CategoryTheory.CartesianMonoidalCategory).

The analytification functor preserves the terminal object and binary products (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-fibre-products), so it carries a monoidal structure (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.Monoidal.ofChosenFiniteProducts) and maps group objects to group objects (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.mapGrp, mathlib:CategoryTheory.GrpObj).
(a): AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-universal-property; the group law on points is induced by m.
(b): AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-finite.

(c): commutativity is preserved by mapGrp (Mathlib's rigidity gives commutativity of A: tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.isCommMonObj); properness by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-separated-proper; smoothness and dimension by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-etale-smooth with tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.smooth; connectedness by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-connected (A is geometrically integral).

(d): finiteness and surjectivity by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-finite and AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-surjective (tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.isIsogeny_iff: an isogeny is finite and surjective); the kernel is the fibre product A ×_{B, e} Spec K, preserved by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-fibre-products.
acceptance: G_a^ad = A^{1,ad}_K with addition, and G_m^ad = A^{1,ad}_K \ {0} with multiplication.
For n invertible in K, μ_n^ad = Spa(K[T]/(Tⁿ − 1)) is a finite étale analytic group of rank n.

nodes.title: A finite locally free surjection of adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa K is an effective epimorphism
nodes.statement: Let p: X → Y be a morphism of adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa K that is finite, surjective and locally free (for every open affinoid V ⊆ Y, p⁻¹(V) is affinoid and O(p⁻¹V) is a finite projective O(V)-module). Then for every adic space Z locally of finite type over Spa K, composition with p is a bijection from Hom_{Spa K}(Y, Z) onto the set of morphisms h: X → Z with h ∘ pr₁ = h ∘ pr₂ on X ×_Y X; i.e. Y is the coequalizer of X ×_Y X ⇉ X in Adic^{lft}_K.
hypotheses: K complete of rank one; X, Y, Z locally of finite type over Spa K
the statement is not claimed for test objects Z outside Adic^{lft}_K; this is recorded as a gap
proofSteps: Injectivity: p is surjective and, O(V) → O(p⁻¹V) being injective, determined maps agree (morphisms into Z are determined by the underlying map and the pullback of functions).

Topology: p is finite, hence proper and universally closed (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-morphisms), and surjective, so it is a quotient map; h is constant on fibres of p because points of X ×_Y X surject onto pairs of points with equal image (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-product-points), so h induces a continuous map h̄: |Y| → |Z|.

Faithful flatness on affinoids: for V = Spa(A, A°) ⊆ Y with p⁻¹V = Spa(B, B°), A → B is finite and flat; every maximal ideal of A is a classical point with a preimage (surjectivity), so A → B is faithfully flat; B ⊗̂_A B = B ⊗_A B as B is finite over A (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-algebra-over-affinoid).

Descent of functions: for an open affinoid W = Spa(C, C°) ⊆ Z and a rational V' ⊆ V with h̄(V') ⊆ W, h gives C → B' = O(p⁻¹V') whose two images in B' ⊗_{A'} B' agree; by exactness of the Amitsur complex (Stacks 023M) it factors through A' = O(V'); the map C → A' is continuous (K-algebra maps between affinoid algebras are continuous, Wedhorn Proposition 5.60) and sends C° into A°, since an element of A' power-bounded in B' has |a(x)| ≤ 1 at all points of Spa A' (surjectivity of Spa B' → Spa A'; anchor Layer 2.3 description of the plus ring).
Gluing: these affinoid morphisms V' → W agree on overlaps by injectivity, glue to Y → Z (anchor Layer 5), and compose with p to h.
acceptance: For the Kummer covering G_m^ad → G_m^ad, x ↦ xⁿ (n invertible), functions on G_m^ad invariant under μ_n-translation descend.
The finite surjection Spa(K[T]/(T²)) → Spa K is locally free, and Spa K is its coequalizer.

nodes.title: Analytification of quotient maps by finite locally free subgroups: (A/G)^ad ≅ A^ad/G^ad
nodes.statement: Let π: A → B be a homomorphism of group schemes locally of finite type over K that is finite locally free and surjective, with kernel G = A ×_{B, e} Spec K (a finite locally free subgroup scheme) — for instance the quotient A → A/G of an abelian variety by a finite locally free subgroup scheme (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A3) or the isogeny E → E/C of an elliptic curve by a finite locally free subgroup (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves#2b-isogenies-and-quotients). Then π^ad: A^ad → B^ad is a finite locally free surjective homomorphism of analytic groups with kernel G^ad; the morphism A^ad ×_{Spa K} G^ad → A^ad ×_{B^ad} A^ad, (a, g) ↦ (a, a·g), is an isomorphism; and B^ad is the quotient of A^ad by the right action of G^ad in Adic^{lft}_K: for every adic space Z locally of finite type over Spa K, composition with π^ad identifies Hom(B^ad, Z) with the morphisms h: A^ad → Z satisfying h(a·g) = h(a). In this sense (A/G)^ad ≅ A^ad/G^ad.
hypotheses: π finite locally free and surjective with kernel G; the algebraic quotient is an input (constructed by AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A3 for abelian schemes and by tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves 2B for elliptic curves)

the quotient property is proved against test objects locally of finite type over Spa K; the existence of quotients of analytic groups by finite flat analytic subgroups not arising from algebra is not claimed
proofSteps: π^ad is finite (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-finite) and surjective (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-surjective), a homomorphism with kernel (ker π)^ad = G^ad (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-group-objects (d)). π is finite locally free of constant rank equal to the rank of G (every fibre of the surjective homomorphism π is, after a finite field extension, a translate of G), so the locally-free clause of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-finite applies: O((π^ad)⁻¹V) is finite projective over O(V) for every open affinoid V ⊆ B^ad.

Algebraic torsor isomorphism: A ×_{Spec K} G → A ×_B A, (a, g) ↦ (a, ag), is an isomorphism of schemes because on T-points a pair (a, a') satisfies π(a) = π(a') iff a⁻¹a' ∈ G(T); analytify with AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-fibre-products to get A^ad ×_{Spa K} G^ad ≅ A^ad ×_{B^ad} A^ad.
Hence h ∘ pr₁ = h ∘ pr₂ on A^ad ×_{B^ad} A^ad iff h(a·g) = h(a); apply AdicSpacesPartII:R1/finite-locally-free-quotient to π^ad.
acceptance: For an elliptic curve E over K and n invertible, [n]: E → E has kernel E[n]; [n]^ad: E^ad → E^ad identifies E^ad with E^ad/E[n]^ad.

For E with a K-rational subgroup C of order p (possibly non-étale in characteristic p), (E/C)^ad is the quotient of E^ad by C^ad; in characteristic p with C = ker(Frobenius) the quotient map is the analytified relative Frobenius, finite flat of degree p and purely inseparable.

nodes.title: Invariant differentials of an analytified group: ω_{G^ad/Y^ad} ≅ (ω_{G/Y})^ad
nodes.statement: Let Y be a K-scheme locally of finite type, (G, m, e, i) a group scheme over Y locally of finite type with structure map f, and put ω_{G/Y} := e^*Ω¹_{G/Y} (an O_Y-module) and ω_{G^ad/Y^ad} := (e^ad)^*Ω¹_{G^ad/Y^ad}. There is a natural isomorphism of O_{Y^ad}-modules ω_{G^ad/Y^ad} ≅ (ω_{G/Y})^ad, compatible with pullback along homomorphisms (φ^* on ω) and with base change in Y. Moreover Ω¹_{G^ad/Y^ad} ≅ (f^ad)^*ω_{G^ad/Y^ad} (differentials of an analytic group are generated by invariant ones), and for G smooth of relative dimension g, ω_{G^ad/Y^ad} is locally free of rank g. For Y = Spec K, ω_{G^ad} = ω_G as K-vector spaces, and both equal the Zariski cotangent space m_e/m_e² of G at e; for G = Spec H affine this is the Hopf-algebra cotangent space I/I² of the augmentation ideal, and for an abelian variety it is the K-dual of its tangent space at 0.
hypotheses: K complete of rank one; G → Y a group scheme locally of finite type (smooth for the local-freeness statement)
proofSteps: Ω¹_{G^ad/Y^ad} ≅ (Ω¹_{G/Y})^ad (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytic-kahler-differentials).
(e^ad)^*(Ω¹_{G/Y})^ad ≅ (e^*Ω¹_{G/Y})^ad, using q_G ∘ e^ad_ = e ∘ q_Y and pseudo-functoriality of pullback (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-of-modules, pullbackIso).

Algebraic invariance Ω¹_{G/Y} ≅ f^*e^*Ω¹_{G/Y} (Stacks 047I) analytifies to Ω¹_{G^ad/Y^ad} ≅ (f^ad)^*ω_{G^ad/Y^ad}; local freeness of rank g for smooth G from Stacks 02G1 and exactness of analytification.

Y = Spec K: e is a K-rational point, (·)^ad over Spa K is ⊗_K K, and e^*Ω¹_{G/K} ≅ m_e/m_e² (the conormal sequence of a section, Stacks 0474), which is the Zariski cotangent space tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.ZariskiCotangentSpace; the adic side agrees by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-completed-local-rings. For affine G = Spec H it is I/I² (tauceti:TauCeti.Bialgebra.CotangentSpace).
Compatibility with homomorphisms and base change: naturality of the isomorphisms in AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytic-kahler-differentials and of pullback.
acceptance: G_m: ω_{G_m^ad} is spanned by dT/T, the analytification of the invariant differential of G_m.

For an elliptic curve E: y² + a₁xy + a₃y = x³ + … over K, ω_{E^ad} is spanned by the analytification of dx/(2y + a₁x + a₃) (tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.invariantDifferential), and [n]^* acts on ω_{E^ad} as multiplication by n.

For the universal elliptic curve over a modular curve, ω_{E^ad/X^ad} is the analytification of the Hodge line bundle ω_{E/X}, the sheaf whose (p−1)-st power carries the Hasse invariant used by AdicSpacesPartII:R2/hasse-domain.

nodes.title: Rigid and adic étale, unramified and smooth morphisms agree under Huber's functor
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete rank-one nonarchimedean field and f: Y → X a morphism of rigid analytic spaces over K (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytic-space), with r_K(f): r_K(Y) → r_K(X) the morphism of adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa K given by Huber's functor (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor). Call f étale (resp. unramified) in the rigid sense if for every point y of Y the local homomorphism O_{X,f(y)} → O_{Y,y} is flat and unramified (resp. unramified); for affinoids Y = Sp B → X = Sp A this means that A → B is flat and the universal finite differential module Ω^f_{B/A} vanishes (resp. that Ω^f_{B/A} = 0). Call f smooth in the rigid sense if Y has an admissible covering by affinoid opens V, each mapping into an affinoid open W of X and admitting an étale morphism in the rigid sense V → 𝔹^n_W over W to a relative closed polydisc; this is equivalent to Huber's pointwise Definition 1.7.10(ii) (for every point y, affinoid neighbourhoods V of y and W of f(y) with such a factorisation), see the last proof step. Then: (a) r_K(f) is étale in Huber's sense (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/differentials-unramified-smooth-etale) iff f is étale in the rigid sense; (b) r_K(f) is unramified (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/unramified-morphism) iff f is unramified in the rigid sense; (c) r_K(f) is smooth (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-morphism) iff f is smooth in the rigid sense. In particular, for K-affinoid algebras A → B the morphism Spa(B, B°) → Spa(A, A°) is étale iff B ≅ A⟨T₁,…,Tₙ⟩/(G₁,…,Gₙ) with det(∂Gᵢ/∂Tⱼ) invertible in B (a special étale presentation). (a) and (c) are Huber 1996, Definition 1.7.10 and Proposition 1.7.11 (printed p. 89); (b) is not in Huber's proposition (Diao–Lan–Liu–Zhu Remark 3.2.15 cite 1.7.11 for it) and is proved here from Huber 1.6.8 and de Jong–van der Put §3.1.
hypotheses: K complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value of rank one.
f: Y → X a morphism of rigid analytic spaces over K; r_K is Huber's functor to adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa K.
Rigid étale and unramified are defined through the local rings of the rigid spaces (de Jong–van der Put §3.1); rigid smooth is 'locally étale over a relative closed polydisc'.
proofSteps: Locality: all six notions are local on Y and on X, and r_K carries admissible affinoid coverings to open affinoid coverings (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor), so one may assume X = Sp A, Y = Sp B affinoid with r_K(Y) = Spa(B, B°) and r_K(X) = Spa(A, A°).

(a), adic ⇒ rigid: if r_K(f): Spa(B, B°) → Spa(A, A°) is étale then A → B is flat (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-ring-flatness, Huber 1.7.6; A is strongly noetherian Tate) and Ωᶜ_{B/A} = 0 (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/infinitesimal-criteria), and Ωᶜ_{B/A} is de Jong–van der Put's Ω^f_{B/A} (both are the quotient of ⊕ B dT_i by the dG_j for a presentation B = A⟨T⟩/(G), AdicSpacesPartII:R0/continuous-differentials (c)); so f is étale in the rigid sense (de Jong–van der Put Observation 3.1.1). (Going through a standard étale presentation of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-local-structure would give weights T_i with T_i·A = A, and A⟨X⟩_T is in general not A⟨X⟩ globally over Spa A, so the flatness route is used instead.)

(a), rigid ⇒ adic: if A → B is flat with Ω^f_{B/A} = 0, then by Huber's argument reproduced in de Jong–van der Put (Observation 3.1.2) B ≅ A⟨T₀, T₁,…,Tₙ⟩/(T₀G − 1, G₁,…,Gₙ) is special étale, with invertible Jacobian determinant; with weights T_i = {1} this is a standard étale presentation, so r_K(f) is étale by AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-local-structure ((ii) ⇒ (i)).

(b): unramifiedness of r_K(f) is the vanishing of the continuous differentials Ωᶜ_{B/A} (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/infinitesimal-criteria); by the presentation formula of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/continuous-differentials, Ωᶜ_{B/A} is the quotient of the free B-module on dT₁,…,dTₙ by the dG_j, which is de Jong–van der Put's Ω^f_{B/A}; its vanishing is checked at the completed local rings, which are the same for the rigid and the adic space at classical points (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-local-ring-completion), and a finite module over the Jacobson ring B vanishes iff it vanishes at every maximal ideal (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-jacobson).

(c): with the admissible-covering form of rigid smoothness: if f is rigid smooth, r_K(V) → r_K(𝔹^n_W) = Spa(A_W⟨T⟩, A_W⟨T⟩°) is étale by (a) and the polydisc projection is smooth (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/restricted-power-series-smooth; its plus ring is A_W⟨T⟩° by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/tft-plus-ring-power-bounded), so r_K(f)|r_K(V) is smooth (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-smooth-composition); the r_K(V) cover r_K(Y) because {V} is admissible (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor (c)), so r_K(f) is smooth (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-smooth-locality). Conversely, if r_K(f) is smooth, every point of r_K(Y) has an open affinoid neighbourhood U with an étale map U → Spa(A⟨T₁,…,Tₙ⟩) over an affinoid Spa(A, A°) = r_K(W) (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-local-structure, Tate case with trivial weights); U = r_K(V) for an affinoid subdomain V, V → 𝔹^n_W is rigid étale by (a), and the V form an admissible covering by (c) of the comparison functor.

Pointwise definition (Huber 1996 Definition 1.7.10(ii)) ⇒ admissible-covering definition, following Huber's proof of 1.7.11(ii): the pointwise hypothesis and (a) make r_K(f) smooth at every classical point, so the coherent module Ω_{r_K(Y)/r_K(X)} is free at all classical points of each affinoid and hence locally free (a finite module over a K-affinoid algebra is projective iff free at all maximal ideals; AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-jacobson). Near an arbitrary point x choose s₁,…,s_n ∈ O⁺ with ds_i a basis of Ω; the map g: U → Spa(O(W)⟨T₁,…,Tₙ⟩), T_i ↦ s_i, is étale at every classical point (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/differential-criterion-morphism), hence rigid étale, hence étale by (a); so r_K(f) is smooth at x and the second half of (c) gives the admissible covering. The converse implication is immediate. (Huber's own proofs are available in the book; the packet recorded them as not public.)
acceptance: The Kummer map T ↦ Tⁿ on the rigid annulus |T| = 1 over Q_p with p ∤ n is étale on both sides; T ↦ T^p on the closed unit disc over Q_p is neither (Jacobian pT^{p−1} vanishes at 0).

nodes.title: Adic rings of finite ideal type and their ideals of definition
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative topological ring. An ideal J of A is an ideal of definition when J is open and every neighbourhood of 0 contains J^n for some n ≥ 1 (EGA 0, 7.1.2). The ring A is an adic ring of finite ideal type, written IsAdicRing A, when there is a finitely generated ideal I of A such that the topology of A is the I-adic topology (Mathlib IsAdic I: the powers I^n are open and form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0) and A is I-adically separated and complete (Mathlib IsAdicComplete I A). An adic noetherian ring is an adic ring of finite ideal type whose underlying ring is noetherian; then every ideal of definition is finitely generated. Conventions: completeness always includes separatedness; the topology is part of the data, so k⟦t⟧ with the discrete topology and k⟦t⟧ with the t-adic topology are different adic rings; morphisms of adic rings are continuous ring homomorphisms. For I as above, an ideal J is an ideal of definition if and only if IsAdic J holds, if and only if J is open and J^n ⊆ I for some n (EGA 0, 7.1.4(i)); so every statement below may use any ideal of definition.
hypotheses: A is a commutative ring with a topology making it a topological ring
the witnessing ideal I is finitely generated (automatic when A is noetherian)
IsAdicComplete I A: separated and complete for the I-adic filtration
proofSteps: This is a definition. Independence of the chosen ideal of definition: if IsAdic I and J is open with J^n ⊆ I, then I^m ⊆ J for some m (openness of J and IsAdic I, Mathlib isAdic_iff), so the I-adic and J-adic filtrations are cofinal and IsAdic J, IsAdicComplete J A follow (Mathlib IsAdic.isAdicComplete_iff, which reduces completeness to CompleteSpace and T2Space of the common topology).
Every ideal of definition lies in the Jacobson radical (Mathlib IsAdicComplete.le_jacobson_bot; EGA 0, 7.1.10), hence x ∈ A is a unit iff its image in A/I is a unit.

For noetherian A the set of topologically nilpotent elements is the radical of I, which is itself an ideal of definition, the largest one (EGA 0, 7.1.6–7.1.7): the radical is finitely generated, hence a power of it lies in I.
acceptance: ℤ_p with the p-adic topology, k⟦t₁,…,t_n⟧ with the (t₁,…,t_n)-adic topology and every complete noetherian local ring with the maximal-ideal-adic topology are adic noetherian rings; every ring with the discrete topology is adic with I = 0.
ℚ_p is not an adic ring: its only open ideal is ℚ_p itself, whose powers do not tend to 0.

O_K⟨X⟩ for a complete rank-one valuation ring O_K with pseudo-uniformiser ϖ, with the ϖ-adic topology, is an adic ring of finite ideal type which is not noetherian when the value group is not discrete (the finite-ideal-type setting is the one type-(S) formal schemes need).

uses.how: Spf A is defined for such A; its points are the open primes and its structure sheaf is the limit over the ideals of definition.
condition (S) asks the rings of affine formal opens to be adic with a finitely generated ideal of definition, noetherian in case (a) and not noetherian in case (b); R2 takes Spf of these rings.

an adic noetherian ring A is a Huber ring with ring of definition A and pair of definition (A, I); Huber’s functor t sends Spf A to Spa(A, A).
the base of Grothendieck existence and algebraization is an adic noetherian ring A with ideal of definition I.

nodes.title: Noetherianity of adically complete rings and of adic completions
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring and I a finitely generated ideal. (i) If R is I-adically complete (IsAdicComplete I R) and R ⧸ I is noetherian, then R is noetherian. (ii) If R is noetherian, then R̂ := AdicCompletion I R is noetherian; it is I·R̂-adically separated and complete, I^n·R̂ is the kernel of R̂ → R ⧸ I^n, and R̂ ⧸ I^n·R̂ ≅ R ⧸ I^n for all n. Consequently AdicCompletion I R with its I·R̂-adic topology is an adic noetherian ring (EGA 0, 7.2.6, 7.2.12, 7.3.1).
hypotheses: I finitely generated
(i): R is I-adically complete and R ⧸ I is noetherian
(ii): R noetherian
proofSteps: (i) Choose generators a₁,…,a_r of I. The associated graded ring gr_I R = ⊕ I^n/I^{n+1} is a quotient of (R/I)[T₁,…,T_r], hence noetherian (Mathlib MvPolynomial.isNoetherianRing).

(i) For an ideal J of R, the associated graded ideal of J in gr_I R is finitely generated; lift homogeneous generators to elements of J and show by successive approximation, using IsPrecomplete I R, that they generate J (every x ∈ J is a convergent series in them); IsHausdorff I R gives uniqueness. This is the argument of EGA 0, 7.2.6 and of the lemma isNoetherianRing_of_isAdicComplete_of_fg of mathlib4#38331, whose name and shape the node follows.

(ii) R̂ is I·R̂-adically complete because I is finitely generated (Mathlib AdicCompletion.isAdicComplete); the kernel of the evaluation R̂ → R ⧸ I^n is I^n·R̂ (Mathlib AdicCompletion.pow_smul_top_eq_ker_eval) and evaluation is surjective (Mathlib AdicCompletion.surjective_evalₐ), so R̂ ⧸ I·R̂ ≅ R ⧸ I is noetherian; apply (i).
acceptance: ℤ_p = AdicCompletion (p) ℤ and k⟦t⟧ = AdicCompletion (t) k[t] are noetherian (base cases).
For R = k[t₁, t₂, …] (infinitely many variables, not noetherian) and I = (t₁), (i) does not apply; the hypothesis that R ⧸ I is noetherian cannot be dropped.

nodes.title: The completed localisation A_{f} of an adic ring
nodes.statement: Let A be an adic ring of finite ideal type with ideal of definition I and let f ∈ A. The completed localisation is A_{f} := AdicCompletion (I·A_f) A_f, where A_f = Localization.Away f, with the I·A_{f}-adic topology; equivalently A_{f} = lim_n (A ⧸ I^{n+1})_f (EGA 0, 7.6.1–7.6.2, 7.6.15). It does not depend on the choice of I. The canonical map A → A_{f} is continuous and sends f to a unit; it has the universal property: every continuous ring homomorphism u : A → B into a complete separated linearly topologised ring B with u(f) a unit factors uniquely through a continuous homomorphism A_{f} → B (EGA 0, 7.6.6). A_{f} is an adic ring of finite ideal type with ideal of definition I·A_{f}, and A_{f} ⧸ I^{n+1}A_{f} ≅ (A ⧸ I^{n+1})_f; if A is noetherian then A_{f} is noetherian and flat over A (EGA 0, 7.6.11, 7.6.13). For g a multiple of f in A (g ∈ √(fA) mod I suffices) there is a unique continuous A-algebra map A_{f} → A_{g}.
hypotheses: A adic of finite ideal type (IsAdicRing A), with ideal of definition I
f ∈ A arbitrary; A_{f} = 0 exactly when f is nilpotent modulo I
proofSteps: Define A_{f} as the I·A_f-adic completion of A_f; I·A_f is finitely generated, so A_{f} is complete (Mathlib AdicCompletion.isAdicComplete) and A_{f}/I^{n+1}A_{f} ≅ A_f/I^{n+1}A_f = (A/I^{n+1})_f (Mathlib AdicCompletion.pow_smul_top_eq_ker_eval, AdicCompletion.surjective_evalₐ, exactness of localisation).
Independence of I: two ideals of definition give cofinal systems of powers (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring).

Universal property: given u with u(f) a unit, u factors through A_f; the preimage of each open ideal of B contains some I^n A_f by continuity, so the maps A_f → B/𝔟 factor through (A/I^n)_f and assemble by completeness of B (Mathlib IsAdicComplete.liftRingHom when B is adic; the limit over open ideals in general).

Noetherianity for noetherian A: A_f is noetherian, apply AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-completion-noetherian (ii). Flatness: A_f is flat over A and the adic completion of a noetherian ring is flat (Mathlib AdicCompletion.flat_of_isNoetherian); compose.
acceptance: For A = ℤ_p (I = (p)) and f = p, A_{f} = 0 since p is nilpotent in A/I; for f = 1, A_{f} = A.
For A = ℤ_p⟦T⟧ with I = (p, T) and f = 1 + T (a unit), A_{f} = A; for A = k⟦T⟧[X] completed along (T) (that is k[X]⟦T⟧) and f = X, A_{f} = k[X, X⁻¹]⟦T⟧.

uses.how: Γ(D(f) ∩ Spf A, O) = A_{f} and (D(f) ∩ Spf A, O|) ≅ Spf A_{f}; this identifies basic opens of Spf A.
the stalk of O_{Spf A} at an open prime p is colim_{f ∉ p} A_{f}, a local ring with residue field Frac(A/p).
a continuous φ : A → B induces continuous maps A_{f} → B_{φ(f)} compatible with restriction; this builds the morphism Spf B → Spf A.
for A = O_K⟨X⟩ the rings A_{f} are the rings of the affine formal opens D(f) of the formal model.

nodes.title: Restricted power series over an adic noetherian ring
nodes.statement: Let A be an adic ring of finite ideal type with ideal of definition I, and let A{T₁,…,T_r} be the ring of restricted power series (Tau Ceti restrictedMvPowerSeriesSubring r A: power series whose coefficients tend to 0 along the cofinite filter), with the topology in which the ideals I^n·A{T} form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0. Then: (i) A{T} is an adic ring of finite ideal type with ideal of definition I·A{T}, and A{T} ⧸ I^{n+1}A{T} ≅ (A ⧸ I^{n+1})[T₁,…,T_r]; (ii) if A is noetherian, A{T} is noetherian; (iii) universal property: for every complete separated linearly topologised A-algebra B (continuous structure map u) and elements b₁,…,b_r ∈ B there is a unique continuous A-algebra homomorphism A{T} → B with T_i ↦ b_i (EGA 0, 7.5.1–7.5.4).
hypotheses: A adic of finite ideal type with ideal of definition I
(ii) needs A noetherian

(iii) B complete, separated and linearly topologised; no condition on the b_i (in contrast with Huber-ring restricted series, where the b_i must be power-bounded, every element of a linearly topologised ring is power-bounded)
proofSteps: (i) A{T} = lim_n (A/I^{n+1})[T]: the reduction of coefficients modulo I^{n+1} kills all but finitely many terms of a restricted series (definition of Tau Ceti IsRestricted), giving a surjection with kernel I^{n+1}A{T} (EGA 0, 7.5.1 and the proof of 7.5.4 (ii)); completeness and separatedness pass to the limit.
(ii) A{T} is I·A{T}-adically complete with A{T}/I·A{T} = (A/I)[T] noetherian (Mathlib MvPolynomial.isNoetherianRing); apply AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-completion-noetherian (i).

(iii) Define the map on a restricted series Σ c_α T^α as Σ u(c_α) b^α, which converges because u(c_α) → 0 and B is complete and linearly topologised; uniqueness because polynomials are dense (EGA 0, 7.5.3).
acceptance: For A = ℤ_p, A{T} = ℤ_p⟨T⟩ is the ring of power series Σ a_n T^n with a_n → 0 p-adically; ℤ_p⟨T⟩/p^{n+1} = (ℤ/p^{n+1})[T].
For A discrete (I = 0), A{T} = A[T].

uses.how: quotients of A{T} are exactly the adic noetherian A-algebras topologically of finite type.

nodes.title: Adic algebras topologically of finite type over an adic noetherian ring
nodes.statement: Let A be an adic noetherian ring with ideal of definition I and φ : A → B a continuous homomorphism to a complete separated linearly topologised ring B. The following are equivalent (EGA 0, 7.5.5): (a) B is noetherian and I·B-adic (IsAdic (I.map φ) and IsAdicComplete), and B ⧸ I·B is a finitely generated A ⧸ I-algebra; (b) B ≅ lim_n B_n topologically as A-algebras, with B_n := B ⧸ I^{n+1}B, and B₁ = B ⧸ I²B is a finitely generated A ⧸ I²-algebra; (c) B is topologically A-isomorphic to a quotient A{T₁,…,T_r} ⧸ 𝔞 by an ideal 𝔞 (necessarily closed).
hypotheses: A adic noetherian with ideal of definition I
φ : A → B continuous, B complete separated linearly topologised
proofSteps: (c) ⇒ (a): A{T} is adic noetherian with ideal of definition I·A{T} (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/restricted-power-series-adic); quotients by ideals of a noetherian adic ring are adic noetherian with the image ideal (API IsAdicRing.quotient of AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring), and B/IB is a quotient of (A/I)[T].

(a) ⇒ (b): B ≅ lim B/I^{n+1}B since B is IB-adically complete (Mathlib IsAdicComplete); B/I²B is generated over A/I² by lifts of generators of B/IB together with generators of IB/I²B, a finite B/IB-module since B is noetherian.

(b) ⇒ (c): (b) says B is I·B-adically separated and complete. Choose c_1,…,c_r ∈ B whose classes generate B ⧸ I·B as an A ⧸ I-algebra (possible since B₁ is a finitely generated A ⧸ I²-algebra); let u : A{T} → B be the continuous A-algebra map with T_i ↦ c_i (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/restricted-power-series-adic (iii)). Then u composed with B → B ⧸ I·B is surjective, A{T} is I·A{T}-adically precomplete and B is (I·A{T}).map u = I·B-adically Hausdorff, so u is surjective (Mathlib surjective_of_mk_map_comp_surjective, the complete-Nakayama criterion that replaces EGA's appeal to associated graded rings, Bourbaki AC III §2 no 8); since u(I^n A{T}) = I^n B, u is strict, i.e. B ≅ A{T} ⧸ ker u topologically, and ker u is closed (EGA 0, 7.5.5, 7.3.6).
acceptance: B = ℤ_p⟦T⟧ is not topologically of finite type over A = ℤ_p (p-adic topology): B is not pB-adic, since its topology is the (p,T)-adic one; condition (a) fails although B is noetherian.
B = ℤ_p⟨T⟩ ⧸ (T² − p) ≅ ℤ_p[√p] is topologically of finite type over ℤ_p.

nodes.title: Completed tensor product of adic rings of finite ideal type
nodes.statement: Let φ : A → B and ψ : A → C be continuous homomorphisms of adic rings of finite ideal type, with ideals of definition I_B ⊆ B and I_C ⊆ C. Let J ⊆ B ⊗_A C be the ideal generated by I_B ⊗ 1 and 1 ⊗ I_C (finitely generated). The completed tensor product is B ⊗̂_A C := AdicCompletion J (B ⊗_A C) with its J-adic topology. It is an adic ring of finite ideal type (ideal of definition J·(B ⊗̂_A C)), independent of the choice of I_B, I_C, and B ⊗̂_A C ⧸ J^{n+1} ≅ (B ⧸ I_B^{n+1}) ⊗_{A} (C ⧸ I_C^{n+1}) modulo J^{n+1}. Universal property (EGA 0, 7.7.6, used in EGA I, 10.7.2): the canonical continuous maps B → B ⊗̂_A C ← C induce a bijection between continuous A-algebra maps B ⊗̂_A C → D and pairs of continuous A-algebra maps (B → D, C → D), for every adic ring D of finite ideal type (more generally every complete separated linearly topologised A-algebra D). Warning: B ⊗̂_A C need not be noetherian when B and C are (EGA I, 10.7.4); it is noetherian when B is topologically of finite type over A and C is noetherian (EGA I, 10.13.5).
hypotheses: A, B, C adic rings of finite ideal type; φ, ψ continuous (not necessarily adic)
noetherianity of the result only under the finite-type hypothesis of AdicSpacesPartII:F0/topologically-finite-type-criterion
proofSteps: J is finitely generated, so B ⊗̂_A C is J-adically complete (Mathlib AdicCompletion.isAdicComplete) with quotients (B ⊗_A C)/J^n (Mathlib AdicCompletion.pow_smul_top_eq_ker_eval).
Independence: replacing I_B, I_C by other ideals of definition changes J to an ideal with cofinal powers (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring).

Universal property: continuous maps β : B → D, γ : C → D give β ⊗ γ : B ⊗_A C → D sending J into a topologically nilpotent ideal, hence continuous for the J-adic topology; extend to the completion by completeness of D (Mathlib IsAdicComplete.liftRingHom for adic D). Uniqueness: the image of B ⊗_A C is dense.
Noetherian case: if B ≅ A{T}/𝔞 (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/topologically-finite-type-criterion) then B ⊗̂_A C ≅ C{T}/𝔞C{T}, which is noetherian by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/restricted-power-series-adic (ii).
acceptance: ℤ_p⟦S⟧ ⊗̂_{ℤ_p} ℤ_p⟦T⟧ ≅ ℤ_p⟦S, T⟧ (ideals of definition (p,S), (p,T)); here neither structure map is adic.
A{S} ⊗̂_A A{T} ≅ A{S, T}.

the completion of X ×_S Y along the preimage of closed subsets is the fibre product of completions, via (B ⊗_A C)^ = B̂ ⊗̂_Â Ĉ (EGA 0, 7.7.2).

nodes.title: Inverse limits of Mittag-Leffler systems of abelian groups
nodes.statement: Let 0 → (A_n) → (B_n) → (C_n) → 0 be a short exact sequence of inverse systems of abelian groups indexed by ℕ. (i) If (B_n) satisfies the Mittag-Leffler condition, so does (C_n); if (A_n) and (C_n) do, so does (B_n) (EGA 0_III, 13.2.1). (ii) If (A_n) satisfies the Mittag-Leffler condition, then 0 → lim A_n → lim B_n → lim C_n → 0 is exact (EGA 0_III, 13.2.2). (iii) An inverse system with surjective transition maps satisfies the Mittag-Leffler condition; a system of artinian modules does (EGA 0_III, 13.1.2). The Mittag-Leffler condition is Mathlib's CategoryTheory.Functor.IsMittagLeffler for the functor ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ Type.
hypotheses: systems indexed by ℕ (a countable cofinal subset suffices)
Mittag-Leffler condition on the kernel system for (ii)
proofSteps: (i) Diagram chase with eventual images (EGA 0_III, 13.2.1).

(ii) Left exactness of lim is formal; for surjectivity, the fibres over a compatible (c_n) form an inverse system of nonempty torsors under (A_n); by Mittag-Leffler, the eventual images are nonempty with surjective transitions, and a countable inverse system of nonempty sets with surjective transitions has nonempty limit (Mathlib CategoryTheory.Functor.IsMittagLeffler with its eventual-range API).
(iii) Surjective transitions: the images are constant; artinian: descending chains of images stabilise.
acceptance: For A_n = p^n ℤ ⊂ ℤ = B_n (inclusions as transitions) the system (A_n) is not Mittag-Leffler and lim(ℤ/p^n) = ℤ_p is not the image of lim ℤ = ℤ: exactness on the right fails without the hypothesis.

uses.how: passing to the limit in 0 → H/R_k → H_k → Q_k → 0.
limits of compatible systems of finite modules (surjective transitions).

nodes.title: The formal spectrum Spf A of an adic ring
nodes.statement: Let A be an adic ring of finite ideal type (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring) with ideal of definition I. The formal spectrum Spf A is the locally ringed space defined as follows. Its underlying space is the closed subspace of Spec A consisting of the open prime ideals, which is V(I) = PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus I and is homeomorphic to Spec(A ⧸ I^{n+1}) for every n via the quotient maps (EGA I, 10.1.1–10.1.2). For each n let O_n be the structure sheaf of Spec(A ⧸ I^{n+1}) transported to V(I); the structure sheaf is O_{Spf A} := lim_n O_n, the limit in sheaves of commutative rings along the reduction maps. Then: Γ(Spf A, O) ≅ A (EGA I, 10.1.3); for f ∈ A and D(f) := D(f) ∩ V(I), Γ(D(f), O) ≅ A_{f} (the completed localisation, AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completed-localization) and (D(f), O|_{D(f)}) ≅ Spf A_{f} (EGA I, 10.1.4); the stalk at an open prime p is colim_{f ∉ p} A_{f}, a local ring with residue field Frac(A ⧸ p), noetherian when A is noetherian (EGA I, 10.1.6). A continuous homomorphism φ : B → A induces a morphism of locally ringed spaces Spf φ : Spf A → Spf B, q ↦ φ⁻¹(q) (EGA I, 10.2.1). Convention: Spf A is a locally ringed space (Mathlib LocallyRingedSpace); the topology of the rings of sections is not part of the data (see AdicSpacesPartII:F0/locally-noetherian-formal-scheme), and for quasi-compact open U the ring Γ(U, O) carries the limit topology of the discrete rings Γ(U, O_n), recorded as an API item.
hypotheses: A adic of finite ideal type; noetherianity only for the noetherian statements (noetherian stalks)
φ continuous for functoriality
proofSteps: Underlying space: an open prime contains some power of I, hence I (primality), so the open primes are V(I); V(I) = V(I^{n+1}) and Spec(A/I^{n+1}) → Spec A is a closed embedding with image V(I^{n+1}) (Mathlib PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus, PrimeSpectrum.isClosed_zeroLocus, PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus_radical).

Structure sheaf: the reduction maps A/I^{n+2} → A/I^{n+1} induce morphisms O_{n+1} → O_n of sheaves of rings on V(I) (O_n is the pushforward of the structure sheaf of Spec(A/I^{n+1}) along the homeomorphism onto V(I), Mathlib TopCat.Presheaf.pushforward); take the limit in sheaves of commutative rings (limits of sheaves are created by the forgetful functor to presheaves, i.e. computed sectionwise: Mathlib CategoryTheory.Sheaf.createsLimits, applied to TopCat.Sheaf).

Sections over D(f): Γ(D(f), O) = lim_n Γ(D(f), O_n) = lim_n (A/I^{n+1})_f, which is A_{f} by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completed-localization (quotient equivalence); for f = 1 this is lim A/I^{n+1} = A because A is I-adically complete (Mathlib IsAdicComplete).
Restriction to D(f): the systems (Spec(A/I^{n+1}) restricted to D(f)) and (Spec(A_{f}/I^{n+1}A_{f})) agree, since A_{f}/I^{n+1} ≅ (A/I^{n+1})_f; hence (D(f), O|) ≅ Spf A_{f}.

Stalks: the D(f) ∩ V(I) form a basis of V(I) (Mathlib PrimeSpectrum.isTopologicalBasis_basic_opens, restricted to the subspace), so the stalk (Mathlib TopCat.Presheaf.stalk) at p is colim_{f∉p} A_{f}; it is local with residue field Frac(A/p), and noetherian for noetherian A (EGA 0, 7.6.17–7.6.18, recorded in AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completed-localization).

Functoriality: φ(I_B)^N ⊆ I_A for some N by continuity, so φ induces compatible maps B/I_B^{N(n+1)} → A/I_A^{n+1}; the induced maps on basic opens B_{g} → A_{φ(g)} (universal property of completed localisation) give the sheaf map, and stalk maps are local because φ⁻¹ of an open prime is open (EGA I, 10.2.1).

nodes.title: Spf A depends only on the topology of A
nodes.statement: Let A be an adic ring of finite ideal type and I, J two ideals of definition of A. The locally ringed spaces Spf_I A and Spf_J A constructed from the systems (Spec A ⧸ I^{n+1})_n and (Spec A ⧸ J^{n+1})_n are canonically isomorphic: the isomorphism is the identity on the common underlying space V(I) = V(J) ⊆ Spec A, is compatible with the identifications of global sections with A, and commutes with the canonical morphisms Spec(A ⧸ I^{n+1}) → Spf A and Spec(A ⧸ J^{m+1}) → Spf A. Both agree with EGA's limit over the filtered set of all ideals of definition (EGA I, 10.1.1–10.1.2). Consequently Spf A is a functor of the topological ring A alone.
hypotheses: I, J ideals of definition of the same adic ring A (same topology)
proofSteps: By AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring (API isAdic_iff_of_isAdic), there are m, n with I^m ⊆ J and J^n ⊆ I; hence √I = √J and V(I) = V(J) (Mathlib PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus_radical).

The systems (A/I^{k})_k and (A/J^{k})_k are mutually cofinal among the quotients by ideals of definition (ideals of definition form a filtered fundamental system, EGA 0, 7.1.2); the limits of the corresponding structure sheaves over mutually cofinal subdiagrams are canonically isomorphic (a final subdiagram does not change the limit).
Compatibility with global sections: both identifications with A are the canonical maps A → lim A/I^k and A → lim A/J^k (Mathlib IsAdicComplete), which correspond under the cofinality isomorphism.
acceptance: For A = k[x]⟦t⟧, I = (t) and J = (t², x t) are ideals of definition; both constructions give underlying space Spec k[x] and the same sheaf.
For A = ℤ_p⟦T⟧ with I = (p, T) and J = (p², T), Spf is a single point in both constructions.
