nodes.title: Formal functions at a point of the base
nodes.statement: Let Y be a locally noetherian scheme, f : X → Y proper, F a coherent O_X-module, y ∈ Y and X_k := X ×_Y Spec(O_{Y,y}/𝔪_y^{k+1}) (underlying space f⁻¹(y)). Then (R^p f_*F)_y is a finite O_{Y,y}-module, hence 𝔪_y-adically separated, and there is a canonical isomorphism ((R^p f_*F)_y)^∧ ≅ lim_k H^p(X_k, F ⊗ O_{Y,y}/𝔪_y^{k+1}) (EGA III, 4.2.1). For p = 0: ((f_*F)_y)^∧ ≅ lim_k H^0(f⁻¹(y), F ⊗ O_{Y,y}/𝔪_y^{k+1}) (EGA III, 4.2.4).
hypotheses: Y locally noetherian; f proper; F coherent; y ∈ Y
proofSteps: R^p f_*F is coherent (supplier tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction Layer 2), so its stalk is finite over the noetherian local ring O_{Y,y} and separated (Krull; Mathlib Ideal.iInf_pow_smul_eq_bot_of_le_jacobson).

Flat base change along Spec O_{Y,y} → Y (supplier tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge Layer C; EGA III, 1.4.15): (R^p f_*F)_y ≅ H^p(X ×_Y Spec O_{Y,y}, F′), with X ×_Y Spec O_{Y,y} proper over Spec O_{Y,y} (Mathlib IsProper.isStableUnderBaseChange).
Apply AdicSpacesPartII:F0/theorem-on-formal-functions with A = O_{Y,y}, I = 𝔪_y.
acceptance: Zariski’s connectedness (EGA III, 4.3.1): if f_*O_X = O_Y then (f_*O_X)_y^∧ = Ô_{Y,y} is local, so lim_k H^0(X_k, O) has no nontrivial idempotents and f⁻¹(y) is connected.
Fibre dimension vanishing (EGA III, 4.2.2): if dim f⁻¹(y) = r then H^p(X_k, ·) = 0 for p > r, so R^p f_*F = 0 near y for p > r.

nodes.title: Cohomology of an inverse limit of sheaves
nodes.statement: Let X be a topological space, (F_k)_{k∈ℕ} an inverse system of sheaves of abelian groups and F = lim_k F_k. Assume: (i) there is a basis 𝔅 of the topology such that for every U ∈ 𝔅 and every i ≥ 0 the system (H^i(U, F_k))_k is Mittag-Leffler; (ii) for every x ∈ X and i > 0, colim_{x∈U∈𝔅} lim_k H^i(U, F_k) = 0; (iii) the transition maps F_{k+1} → F_k are surjective. Then for every i ≥ 0 the canonical map H^i(X, F) → lim_k H^i(X, F_k) is surjective, and it is bijective when (H^{i−1}(X, F_k))_k is Mittag-Leffler (EGA 0_III, 13.3.1). Cohomology is Mathlib CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H of the Zariski site of X.
hypotheses: X any topological space; ℕ-indexed systems; hypotheses (i)–(iii)
proofSteps: Flasque case (EGA 0_III, 13.3.1 a): if all F_k and all kernels of F_{k+1} → F_k are flasque (Mathlib TopCat.Presheaf.IsFlasque), the alternating Čech complexes of any open cover form systems with surjective transitions whose cohomology vanishes in positive degrees (Čech cohomology of flasque sheaves; supplier SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2), so by the limit form of AdicSpacesPartII:F0/mittag-leffler-exactness for complexes (EGA 0_III, 13.2.3) the Čech cohomology of F = lim F_k vanishes on every open, hence H^i(X, F) = 0 for i > 0 (Tau Ceti subsingleton_H_succ_of_isFlasque for the flasque terms, Čech-to-derived comparison from SF.2).

General case (EGA 0_III, 13.3.1 b): apply Godement’s canonical flasque resolution F_k → C^•(X, F_k), an exact functor with flasque terms (supplier SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2); by (iii) the systems (C^i(X, F_k))_k have surjective transitions with flasque kernels, so their limits are acyclic by the flasque case; hypotheses (i)–(ii) with AdicSpacesPartII:F0/mittag-leffler-exactness show that lim_k C^•(X, F_k) is a resolution of F; therefore H^i(X, F) = H^i(lim_k Γ(X, C^•(X, F_k))), and EGA 0_III, 13.2.3 (limits of Mittag-Leffler systems of complexes, from AdicSpacesPartII:F0/mittag-leffler-exactness) gives surjectivity onto lim H^i(X, F_k), and bijectivity when (H^{i−1}(X, F_k)) is Mittag-Leffler.
acceptance: For X a point, H^i = 0 for i > 0 and the statement reduces to H^0(lim F_k) = lim H^0(F_k).
On a noetherian formal scheme 𝔛 with ideal of definition 𝒥 and a coherent F, the system F_k = F/𝒥^{k+1}F on the affine formal basis satisfies (i)–(iii).

sources.locator: Ch. 0, proof of (13.3.1) b), printed p. 68

nodes.title: Comparison of algebraic and formal higher direct images
nodes.statement: Let Y be a locally noetherian scheme, f : X → Y proper, Y′ ⊆ Y closed with coherent ideal 𝓘, X′ = f⁻¹(Y′), f̂ : X̂ → Ŷ the completion (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-morphism), F a coherent O_X-module, F̂ its completion and F_k = F/𝒥^{k+1}F with 𝒥 = f*(𝓘)O_X. Let R^n f̂_*(F̂) be the sheaf on Ŷ associated with V ↦ H^n(f̂⁻¹(V), F̂) (cohomology of the underlying abelian sheaves). Then R^n f̂_*(F̂) is a coherent O_Ŷ-module and the canonical maps φ_n : (R^n f_*F)^ → R^n f̂_*(F̂) and ψ_n : R^n f̂_*(F̂) → lim_k R^n f_*(F_k) are isomorphisms of O_Ŷ-modules; ψ_n ∘ φ_n is the canonical map (EGA III, 4.1.5). For Y = Spec A affine noetherian: H^n(X̂, F̂) ≅ H^n(X, F)^∧ ≅ lim_k H^n(X, F_k) (EGA III, 4.1.7), and for every affine open V of Y, H^n(X̂ ∩ f⁻¹(V), F̂) ≅ Γ(V ∩ Y′, R^n f̂_*(F̂)) (EGA III, 4.1.9).
hypotheses: Y locally noetherian; f proper; F coherent
proofSteps: Affine case Y = Spec A: F_k is supported on X′ and H^n(X, F_k) = H^n(X̂, F_k) (EGA III, 4.1.3.2). Apply AdicSpacesPartII:F0/cohomology-of-mittag-leffler-limit to F̂ = lim F_k on the space X′ with 𝔅 the affine opens: on affine U, H^i(U, F_k) = 0 for i > 0 (affine acyclicity, supplier tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge Layer B) and H^0(U, F_{k+1}) → H^0(U, F_k) is surjective, so (i)–(iii) hold; (H^{n−1}(X, F_k)) is Mittag-Leffler by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-functions-affine. Hence ψ_{n,X} : H^n(X̂, F̂) ≅ lim_k H^n(X, F_k).
The composite with φ is the isomorphism of AdicSpacesPartII:F0/theorem-on-formal-functions, so φ is an isomorphism too.

Sheaf form: Γ(V, R^n f_*F) = H^n(f⁻¹(V), F) for affine V (supplier StableReduction Layer 2; EGA III, 1.4.11), Γ(V ∩ Y′, (R^n f_*F)^) is its completion since R^n f_*F is coherent (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-coherent-sheaf), and the affine case applied to f⁻¹(V) → V gives φ_n, ψ_n on the basis of affine opens; coherence of R^n f̂_*(F̂) follows from φ_n (EGA III, 4.1.8).
acceptance: For X = P¹_{ℤ_p}, Y = Spec ℤ_p, Y′ = V(p) and F = O(−2): H^1(X̂, Ô(−2)) = ℤ_p, the cohomology of the formal completion P̂¹ agrees with that of P¹.

nodes.title: Over a complete base, every neighbourhood of the closed fibre is everything
nodes.statement: Let A be an adic noetherian ring with ideal of definition I, f : X → Spec A a morphism whose underlying map is closed (for instance f proper), and X′ = f⁻¹(V(I)). Then every open subset V ⊆ X containing X′ equals X (EGA III, 5.1.3.1).
hypotheses: A adic noetherian; f a closed map
proofSteps: f(X ∖ V) is closed in Spec A and disjoint from V(I).

Every nonempty closed subset of Spec A contains a closed point, a maximal ideal 𝔪, and I ⊆ 𝔪 because I lies in the Jacobson radical (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring; Mathlib IsAdicComplete.le_jacobson_bot); so every nonempty closed subset meets V(I). Hence X ∖ V = ∅.
acceptance: For X = P¹_{ℤ_p}, any open containing the special fibre P¹_{F_p} is all of X.
For the non-closed morphism X = Spec ℚ_p → Spec ℤ_p, X′ = ∅ and V = ∅ is a neighbourhood of X′ different from X.

nodes.title: Completion of coherent sheaves is fully faithful over a complete base
nodes.statement: Let A be an adic noetherian ring with ideal of definition I, f : X → Spec A of finite type (EGA III, 5.1.1; no separatedness is needed), X̂ the completion along X′ = f⁻¹(V(I)), and F, G coherent O_X-modules such that Supp F ∩ Supp G is proper over Spec A. Then u ↦ û is a bijection Hom_{O_X}(F, G) ≅ Hom_{O_X̂}(F̂, Ĝ). If moreover f is closed (e.g. X proper over A), u is injective (resp. surjective) iff û is (EGA III, 5.1.3; Stacks Tag 0883 for X proper).
hypotheses: A adic noetherian; f of finite type (EGA III, 5.1.1)
Supp F ∩ Supp G proper over Spec A (automatic if X is proper)
proofSteps: H := ℋom(F, G) (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/internal-hom-sheaf-of-modules) is coherent with Supp H ⊆ Supp F ∩ Supp G, hence Supp H is proper over Spec A. Choose a closed subscheme Z ⊆ X with underlying space Supp H, proper over Spec A (the annihilator ideal of H has zero locus Supp H), so H is the pushforward of a coherent O_Z-module and cohomology of H on X equals that on Z (EGA III, 4.1.10).

Hom(F̂, Ĝ) = Γ(X̂, Hom(F̂, Ĝ)) = Γ(X̂, Ĥ) (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-exact (iv)), and Γ(X̂, Ĥ) = lim_n H^0(X, H/I^{n+1}H) (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-coherent-sheaf, sectionsIso on the quasi-compact X′).

By AdicSpacesPartII:F0/theorem-on-formal-functions (complete base, p = 0, applied on Z proper over A): lim_n H^0(X, H/I^{n+1}H) = H^0(X, H) = Hom(F, G); the composite is u ↦ û (Stacks Tag 0883 via Tag 0882).

Injectivity/surjectivity: û injective (surjective) iff u is so on a neighbourhood of X′ (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-detects-near-closed (iv)), and every neighbourhood of X′ is X when f is closed (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-fibre-neighbourhood).
acceptance: For X = P¹_{ℤ_p}: Hom(O(a), O(b)) = H^0(P¹, O(b − a)) and its completion Hom(Ô(a), Ô(b)) agree (both free of rank b − a + 1, or 0).
Without properness the map is not surjective: for X = A¹_{ℤ_p}, Hom(O, O) = ℤ_p[x] whereas Hom(Ô, Ô) = ℤ_p⟨x⟩.

nodes.title: Uniform vanishing and lifting of sections on a proper formal scheme with an ample reduction
nodes.statement: Let A be an adic noetherian ring with ideal of definition I, A_n = A/I^{n+1}, 𝔛 → Spf A a proper morphism of formal schemes with adic system X_n = 𝔛 ×_{Spf A} Spec A_n (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-systems-equivalence), L an invertible O_𝔛-module with L_0 = L ⊗ O_{X_0} ample on X_0, and F a coherent O_𝔛-module with reductions F_n = F ⊗ O_{X_n} (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-as-inverse-system); write F_n(d) = F_n ⊗ L_n^{⊗d}. There is n_0 such that for all d ≥ n_0 and all k ≥ 0: (i) H^q(X_0, (I^{k+1}F_{k+1}) ⊗ L_0^{⊗d}) = 0 for q > 0, where I^{k+1}F_{k+1} = Ker(F_{k+1} → F_k) is viewed as a coherent O_{X_0}-module; (ii) H^0(X_{k+1}, F_{k+1}(d)) → H^0(X_k, F_k(d)) is surjective; (iii) if also H^q(X_0, F_0(d)) = 0 for q > 0, then H^q(X_k, F_k(d)) = 0 for all q > 0 and k; (iv) Γ(𝔛, F ⊗ L^{⊗d}) → H^0(X_k, F_k(d)) is surjective for every k (EGA III, 5.2.3; Stacks Tags 0884 and the proof of 089A).
hypotheses: A adic noetherian; 𝔛 proper over Spf A; L invertible with L_0 ample on X_0; F coherent
proofSteps: The kernels K_k := Ker(F_{k+1} → F_k) = I^{k+1}F_{k+1} are killed by I, so are coherent O_{X_0}-modules, and K := ⊕_k K_k is a finite type graded module over f_0*(gr_I A)~ (affine-locally ⊕ I^{k+1}M/I^{k+2}M over ⊕ I^k/I^{k+1}; Stacks Tag 087Z, via AdicSpacesPartII:F0/affine-coherent-equivalence).

(i) X_0 is proper over the noetherian ring A_0 = A/I and gr_I A is a finitely generated graded A_0-algebra; apply AdicSpacesPartII:F0/graded-cohomology-finiteness (ii) with L_0 ample (ampleness in the sense of the supplier AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.1).
(ii) Long exact sequence of 0 → K_k(d) → F_{k+1}(d) → F_k(d) → 0 on X_{k+1} (Tau Ceti cohomologyδ; sections_surjective): H^1(X_{k+1}, K_k(d)) = H^1(X_0, K_k ⊗ L_0^d) = 0 gives surjectivity.
(iii) Induction on k with the same sequences.

(iv) Γ(𝔛, F ⊗ L^d) = lim_k H^0(X_k, F_k(d)) (sheaf limit, AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-as-inverse-system), and a limit of a system with surjective transitions surjects onto each term (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/mittag-leffler-exactness).

nodes.title: Grothendieck existence for projective schemes
nodes.statement: Let A be an adic noetherian ring with ideal of definition I and f : X → Spec A proper with an ample invertible O_X-module L (X projective over A). Then completion F ↦ F̂ is an equivalence Coh(X) ≃ Coh(X̂) (EGA III, 5.2.5; Stacks Tag 0885).
hypotheses: A adic noetherian; X proper over Spec A with an ample invertible sheaf L
proofSteps: Fully faithful by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-fully-faithful.

Every G ∈ Coh(X̂) is a quotient of a completion: L_0 = L|_{X_0} is ample (restriction of an ample sheaf to a closed subscheme; supplier AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.1); choose d with d ≥ n_0 of AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-serre-vanishing for G and L̂ and with G_0 ⊗ L_0^d globally generated (Serre’s theorem, supplier R09.1); lift finitely many generating sections compatibly through the surjections (formal-serre-vanishing (ii)) to maps ((L^{−d})^{⊕t})_n → G_n; the induced map ((L^{−d})^{⊕t})^ → G is surjective because it is surjective on reductions at n = 0 (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-as-inverse-system (iii)).

Apply this to the kernel (Coh(X̂) is abelian, AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-formal-module-properties (ii)) to get a presentation û′ : ((L^{−e})^{⊕s})^ → ((L^{−d})^{⊕t})^ → G → 0; by full faithfulness û′ = û for u : (L^{−e})^{⊕s} → (L^{−d})^{⊕t}; by exactness of completion (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-exact), G ≅ (coker u)^.
acceptance: On X = P^r_{ℤ_p}, every compatible system of coherent sheaves on P^r_{ℤ/p^{n+1}} is the reduction of a coherent sheaf on P^r_{ℤ_p}; e.g. compatible line bundles are O(d) for a single d.

nodes.title: Comparison along a proper modification up to a power of the exceptional ideal
nodes.statement: Let Y be a noetherian scheme, 𝓙, 𝓚 ⊆ O_Y quasi-coherent ideals, π : X → Y proper and an isomorphism over Y ∖ V(𝓚), 𝓘 = π⁻¹𝓙·O_X, G ∈ Coh(Ŷ_{/V(𝓙)}) (a compatible system (G_n)), F a coherent O_X-module and β : π̂*G ≅ F̂ in Coh(X̂_{/V(𝓘)}). Then there is a morphism α : G → (π_*F)^ in Coh(Ŷ) whose kernel and cokernel are annihilated by a power of 𝓚 (Stacks Tag 088B; EGA III, 5.3.4).
hypotheses: Y noetherian; π proper, isomorphism over the complement of V(𝓚)
proofSteps: π_*F is coherent (supplier tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction Layer 2), so (π_*F)^ makes sense.

Define γ_n : G_n → π_*π*G_n → π_*(F/𝓘^nF) (adjunction, then π_*β_n); on an affine open Spec B of Y, lim_n H^0(X_B, F/𝓘^nF) is the 𝓙-adic completion of H^0(X_B, F) by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/theorem-on-formal-functions (p = 0); via AdicSpacesPartII:F0/affine-coherent-equivalence the limit of the γ_n is a map α of finite B̂-modules, unique, hence glues (Stacks Tag 088B).

Kernel and cokernel (Stacks Tag 088B proof; EGA III, 5.3.4 proof): by uniqueness of α the question is local on Y, and by Remark Tag 0888 it suffices to bound the torsion on a finite affine cover, so let Y = Spec B. Base change along the flat map Spec B̂ → Spec B (B → B̂ flat, Mathlib AdicCompletion.flat_of_isNoetherian; π_* commutes with flat base change, supplier tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge Layer C) does not change modules killed by powers of 𝓙, so one may assume B is 𝓙-adically complete. Then G = Ĝ₀ for a coherent G₀ on Spec B (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/affine-coherent-equivalence (iv)), π̂*G = (π*G₀)^ (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-exact (v)), and β = b̂ for an isomorphism b : π*G₀ ≅ F because completion is fully faithful for X proper over the complete B (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-fully-faithful); so α is the completion of the adjunction map G₀ → π_*π*G₀ ≅ π_*F. Its kernel and cokernel are coherent and vanish on Y ∖ V(𝓚), where π is an isomorphism, hence are killed by a power of 𝓚 (EGA I, 9.3.4), and so are their completions (exactness of completion, AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-exact).
acceptance: If π is an isomorphism (𝓚 = O_Y allowed), α is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Algebraizing a formal module that maps to a completion with bounded torsion kernel and cokernel
nodes.statement: Let X be a noetherian scheme, 𝓘 ⊆ O_X a quasi-coherent ideal, H a coherent O_X-module and G ∈ Coh(X̂_{/V(𝓘)}) (equivalently a compatible system (G_n), AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-as-inverse-system). If α : G → Ĥ is a morphism whose kernel and cokernel are annihilated by a power of 𝓘, then there is a triple (F, a, β), unique up to unique isomorphism, with F a coherent O_X-module, a : F → H a morphism whose kernel and cokernel are annihilated by a power of 𝓘, and β : G ≅ F̂ with α = â ∘ β (Stacks Tag 0889 (1)). X is not assumed complete along 𝓘.
hypotheses: X noetherian (not necessarily complete along V(𝓘)); H coherent; kernel and cokernel of α killed by 𝓘^t for some t
proofSteps: Uniqueness reduces the construction to affine opens X = Spec A (A noetherian), 𝓘 = I~, where G corresponds to a finite Â-module M′ (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-as-inverse-system with AdicSpacesPartII:F0/affine-coherent-equivalence and AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-completion, specIso), H to a finite A-module N with Ĥ ↔ N ⊗_A Â (Mathlib AdicCompletion.ofTensorProductEquivOfFiniteNoetherian), and α to φ : M′ → N ⊗_A Â with I^t-torsion kernel and cokernel.

By the formal glueing lemma (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-glueing-of-modules = Stacks Tag 0ALK, applicable because A → Â is flat, Mathlib AdicCompletion.flat_of_isNoetherian, I is finitely generated and A/I ≅ Â/IÂ), there are an A-module M, ψ : M → N and M ⊗_A Â ≅ M′ compatible with φ, with ker ψ ≅ ker φ and coker ψ ≅ coker φ I^t-torsion. (The fibre product N ×_{N ⊗ Â} M′ is one model of M, but that M ⊗_A Â ≅ M′ is exactly the content of the formal glueing lemma, not a formal consequence of flatness.)

M is finite over A: it is an extension of a submodule of the finite module N by the I^t-torsion module ker φ, which is a finite Â-module killed by I^t, hence a finite A/I^t = Â/I^tÂ-module (Stacks Tag 05EU); so M^ = M ⊗_A Â ≅ M′ and F := M~ works.
Uniqueness: two triples differ by a map inducing an isomorphism on completions and on the parts away from V(𝓘); glue the affine constructions.
acceptance: If α is an isomorphism, F = H. For X = Spec ℤ, 𝓘 = (p), H = O and G = (p ℤ_p)^Δ ⊂ Ô (α the inclusion, cokernel F_p killed by p), the triple is F = pℤ ⊂ ℤ = H.

nodes.title: Dévissage: extending algebraizability from thickenings of a closed subscheme
nodes.statement: Let X be a noetherian scheme, 𝓘, 𝓚 ⊆ O_X quasi-coherent ideals, X_e = V(𝓚^e) with 𝓘_e = 𝓘O_{X_e}, and G ∈ Coh(X̂_{/V(𝓘)}) (a compatible system (G_n)). Assume: (1) completion Coh(X_e) → Coh((X_e)^_{/V(𝓘_e)}) is an equivalence for every e ≥ 1; (2) there are a coherent O_X-module H and a morphism α : G → Ĥ whose kernel and cokernel are annihilated by a power of 𝓚. Then G ≅ F̂ for a coherent O_X-module F (Stacks Tag 088A; EGA III, 5.3.1–5.3.2).
hypotheses: X noetherian; (1) for all e; (2) as stated
proofSteps: Identify coherent O_{X_e}-modules with coherent O_X-modules killed by 𝓚^e. By (1), for each e the system (G_n/𝓚^eG_n)_n is the completion of a coherent G_e killed by 𝓚^e; the maps G_{e+1} → G_e induce G_{e+1}/𝓚^eG_{e+1} ≅ G_e, so (G_e)_e is a compatible system for 𝓚, i.e. an object of Coh(X̂_{/V(𝓚)}) (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-as-inverse-system).

α induces maps G_e → H/𝓚^eH (full faithfulness in (1)); if 𝓚^t kills kernel and cokernel of α, then 𝓚^{4t} kills kernel and cokernel of all G_e → H/𝓚^eH (Stacks Tag 0888, Remark 30.25.1, an affine-local statement about finite modules).
AdicSpacesPartII:F0/bounded-torsion-algebraization, applied to (G_e) → Ĥ_{/V(𝓚)}, gives a coherent F with F/𝓚^eF ≅ G_e compatibly.

Reducing modulo 𝓘^n, the triple (F/𝓘^nF, …) algebraizes (G_n/𝓚^eG_n)_e → (H/(𝓘^n + 𝓚^e)H)_e, so by the uniqueness in AdicSpacesPartII:F0/bounded-torsion-algebraization, F/𝓘^nF ≅ G_n compatibly in n; hence G ≅ F̂ (Stacks Tag 088A).
acceptance: If 𝓚 = 0 then X_e = X for every e and hypothesis (1) is already the conclusion.
If α is an isomorphism the conclusion holds with F = H; the lemma is used when α is an isomorphism only away from V(𝓚), as produced by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-modification.

nodes.title: Coherent formal modules with proper support live on a proper closed subscheme
nodes.statement: Let A be an adic noetherian ring with ideal of definition I, X separated of finite type over Spec A, and G ∈ Coh(X̂) whose support is proper over Spf A (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/proper-formal-morphism, IsProperSupport). Then there is a closed subscheme Z ⊆ X, proper over Spec A, such that G is annihilated by the completed ideal of Z, i.e. G is the pushforward of a coherent module on Ẑ (Stacks Tag 088E, first part of the proof; EGA III, 5.3.5).
hypotheses: A adic noetherian; X separated of finite type over Spec A
proofSteps: Noetherian induction on quasi-coherent ideals 𝓚 ⊆ O_X for which the claim holds for all G annihilated by 𝓚 (Stacks Tag 088E): assume the claim for all proper closed subschemes of X.

Chow’s lemma (supplier AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.2): π : X′ → X proper surjective, an isomorphism over a dense open U, with an open immersion j : X′ → P into a scheme P projective over Spec A (supplier R09.1). The support of π̂*G is π⁻¹ of the support of G, proper over A because π is proper (Stacks Tag 0CYQ (3)), hence its image under j is closed in P (Tag 0CYQ (1), P separated); so j_*π*(G_n) is a compatible system of coherent modules on P (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-as-inverse-system), and by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-projective-case it is the completion of a coherent F′ on P.

Supp F′ ⊆ j(X′): the image in Spec A of the closed set Supp F′ ∖ j(X′) is closed (P → Spec A is proper) and does not meet V(I) (its points over V(I) lie in the support of F′/IF′ = j_*π*G_0, contained in j(X′)); a nonempty closed subset of Spec A meets V(I) since I lies in the Jacobson radical (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring), so the set is empty. Hence F′|_{X′} is supported on a closed subscheme of X′ proper over A and (F′|_{X′})^ ≅ π̂*G.

H := π_*(F′|_{X′}) is coherent (supplier StableReduction Layer 2) with support proper over A; AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-modification gives α : G → Ĥ with kernel and cokernel killed by 𝓚^t, 𝓚 the ideal of the reduced complement X ∖ U ≠ X; kernel and cokernel are coherent formal modules with proper support annihilated by 𝓚^t, so by the induction hypothesis they are supported on proper closed subschemes; Ĥ is supported on a proper closed subscheme (its scheme-theoretic support lies in π(Z′), proper by Tag 0CYQ (2)); modules supported on proper closed subschemes form a Serre subcategory (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/proper-support-serre-subcategory = Stacks Tag 0CYV, Lemma 30.26.11), so G is supported on one.
acceptance: For X = A¹_{ℤ_p} and G = Ô_{V(x)} (the completion of the structure sheaf of the section x = 0, proper over ℤ_p), Z = V(x).

nodes.title: Grothendieck’s existence theorem
nodes.statement: Let A be an adic noetherian ring with ideal of definition I, Y = Spec A, f : X → Y a separated morphism of finite type, X′ = f⁻¹(V(I)), X̂ = X̂_{/X′} and Ŷ = Spf A. Then F ↦ F̂ is an equivalence from the category of coherent O_X-modules whose support is proper over Spec A to the category of coherent O_X̂-modules whose support is proper over Spf A (EGA III, 5.1.4; Stacks Tag 088E). In particular, if X is proper over Spec A then Coh(X) ≃ Coh(X̂) (EGA III, 5.1.6); equivalently, with X_n = X ×_Y Spec(A/I^{n+1}), coherent O_X-modules correspond to compatible systems (F_n) of coherent O_{X_n}-modules with F_{n+1} ⊗ O_{X_n} ≅ F_n, morphisms to compatible systems of morphisms (EGA III, 5.1.7; Stacks Tag 088F).
hypotheses: A adic noetherian (complete and separated for the I-adic topology)
f separated of finite type; supports proper over Spec A (automatic when X is proper)
proofSteps: Full faithfulness: AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-fully-faithful.

Proper case, essential surjectivity (Stacks Tag 088C): noetherian induction on quasi-coherent ideals 𝓚, assuming the statement for all closed subschemes V(𝓚), 𝓚 ≠ 0; Chow’s lemma for X proper over A (supplier AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.2) gives π : X′ → X proper surjective, an isomorphism over a dense open U, with X′ projective over A; by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-projective-case, π̂*G ≅ F̂′; by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-modification there is α : G → (π_*F′)^ with kernel and cokernel killed by a power of 𝓚 = ideal of X ∖ U; AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-devissage concludes.

Proper supports: by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-proper-support-reduction both sides are supported on completions of closed subschemes Z ⊆ X proper over A, and coherent modules on Z are coherent O_X-modules killed by the ideal of Z (and likewise on Ẑ ⊆ X̂, AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-formal-subscheme); apply the proper case to Z.
System form: AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-as-inverse-system for X̂, whose thickenings are the X_n (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-completion).
acceptance: For X = P^r_{ℤ_p}: Coh(P^r_{ℤ_p}) ≃ Coh(P̂^r) ≃ compatible systems on P^r_{ℤ/p^{n+1}}; in particular Pic(P̂^r) = ℤ.
EGA III after 5.1.7: over a local adic noetherian A the Y_n are spectra of artinian local rings, so geometry over A reduces largely to geometry over artinian rings.
Properness of supports is needed: for X = A¹_{ℤ_p}, O_X̂ has non-proper support and End(O_X̂) = ℤ_p⟨x⟩ ≠ ℤ_p[x] = End(O_X), so completion is not an equivalence on all coherent sheaves.

nodes.title: Closed formal subschemes proper over Spf A are completions
nodes.statement: Let A be an adic noetherian ring with ideal of definition I and f : X → Spec A separated of finite type. Then Z ↦ Ẑ is a bijection from closed subschemes of X proper over Spec A to closed formal subschemes of X̂ proper over Spf A (EGA III, 5.1.8). Equivalently (Stacks Tag 0899): a compatible system of closed subschemes Z_n ⊆ X_n = X ×_{Spec A} Spec A/I^{n+1} with Z_{n+1} ∩ X_n = Z_n and Z_0 proper over A/I comes from a unique closed subscheme Z ⊆ X proper over A.
hypotheses: A adic noetherian; f separated of finite type
proofSteps: A closed formal subscheme 𝔜 ⊆ X̂ proper over Spf A is X̂.subscheme 𝒜 with O_X̂/𝒜 coherent of proper support (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-formal-subscheme); by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/grothendieck-existence O_X̂/𝒜 ≅ Ĝ with G coherent of proper support, and the quotient map O_X̂ → Ĝ is û for a unique u : O_X → G (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-fully-faithful, Supp O_X ∩ Supp G = Supp G proper). Q := Coker u is coherent with Supp Q ⊆ Supp G proper over A and Q̂ = Coker û = 0 (exactness, AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-exact), so Supp Q ∩ X′ = ∅ (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-detects-near-closed (ii)); the image of the closed set Supp Q in Spec A is closed (Supp Q is proper over A) and misses V(I), hence is empty because I lies in the Jacobson radical (the argument of AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-fibre-neighbourhood). Thus u is surjective and G = O_X/𝓐 for a coherent ideal 𝓐 with V(𝓐) = Supp G proper over A (Stacks Tag 0899 proof).
Then 𝒜 = 𝓐̂ (exactness, AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-exact) and 𝔜 = Ẑ for Z = V(𝓐) (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-formal-subscheme, completion_subscheme).
Injectivity: Ẑ determines 𝓐̂ and hence the surjection O_X → O_Z up to isomorphism by full faithfulness.
acceptance: For X = A¹_{ℤ_p} and a ∈ ℤ_p, the closed formal subscheme V(x − a) of X̂ = Spf ℤ_p⟨x⟩ is proper over Spf ℤ_p and is the completion of the closed subscheme V(x − a) ≅ Spec ℤ_p of A¹_{ℤ_p}.
Properness is needed: X̂ = Spf ℤ_p⟨x⟩ is a closed formal subscheme of itself that is not proper over Spf ℤ_p, and it is not the completion of a closed subscheme proper over ℤ_p.

nodes.title: Isomorphisms and closed immersions of proper schemes are detected on completions
nodes.statement: Let Z be a locally noetherian scheme, g : X → Z and h : Y → Z proper, Z′ ⊆ Z closed, X′ = g⁻¹(Z′), Y′ = h⁻¹(Z′), and f : X → Y a Z-morphism with completion f̂ : X̂ → Ŷ. Then f̂ is an isomorphism (resp. a closed immersion) iff there is an open neighbourhood U of Z′ such that f restricted to g⁻¹(U) → h⁻¹(U) is an isomorphism (resp. a closed immersion) (EGA III, 4.6.8).
hypotheses: Z locally noetherian; g, h proper
proofSteps: Sufficiency: completion is local on a neighbourhood and preserves isomorphisms and closed immersions (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-morphism, AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-formal-subscheme).

Necessity, local around y ∈ Y′: f̂ injective on X′ implies f⁻¹(y) is at most one point, so f is quasi-finite at the points of f⁻¹(y); the quasi-finite locus is open (Mathlib Scheme.Hom.isOpen_quasiFiniteAt), and since f is proper (a Z-morphism between proper Z-schemes) its complement has closed image not containing y; over the complement V of that image f is proper and locally quasi-finite, hence finite (Mathlib IsFinite.of_isProper_of_locallyQuasiFinite).

For finite f over V, X = Spec_V(ℬ) with ℬ = f_*O_X coherent, and f̂ corresponds to Ô_Y → ℬ̂; f̂ an isomorphism (resp. closed immersion) means û is bijective (resp. surjective) for u : O_Y → ℬ, hence u is so on a neighbourhood of Y′ (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-detects-near-closed (iv)).

Neighbourhoods: if u is an isomorphism (surjective) on an open W ⊇ Y′, then U := Z ∖ h(Y ∖ W) is an open neighbourhood of Z′ since h is closed (Mathlib UniversallyClosed), and g⁻¹(U) → h⁻¹(U) has the property.
acceptance: For Z = Spec ℤ_p, Z′ = V(p), X = Y = P¹_{ℤ_p} and f an automorphism: f is determined by f̂, and a Z-morphism f with f̂ an isomorphism is an isomorphism over U = Z (every neighbourhood of V(p) in Spec ℤ_p is everything).

Properness is needed: for Z = Y = Spec ℤ, Z′ = V(p) and X = Spec ℤ_(p) with its canonical map f (X is not proper over Z), f̂ : Spf ℤ_p → Spf ℤ_p is an isomorphism but f is not an isomorphism over any open neighbourhood of V(p).

sources.match: EGA III, 4.6.8: f̂ is an isomorphism (closed immersion) iff f is one over a neighbourhood of Z′.

nodes.title: Morphisms from proper schemes are determined by their completions
nodes.statement: Let A be an adic noetherian ring with ideal of definition I, S = Spec A, S_n = Spec A/I^{n+1}, X → S proper and Y → S separated of finite type, and let X̂, Ŷ be the completions along the preimages of V(I). Then f ↦ f̂ is a bijection Hom_S(X, Y) ≅ Hom_{Spf A}(X̂, Ŷ) (EGA III, 5.4.1). Equivalently, S-morphisms X → Y correspond to compatible systems of S_n-morphisms X_n → Y_n (EGA III, 5.4.2; Stacks Tag 0A42). Consequently X ↦ X̂ is a fully faithful functor from schemes proper over Spec A to formal schemes proper over Spf A; formal schemes in its essential image are called algebraizable.
hypotheses: A adic noetherian; X proper over S; Y separated of finite type over S
proofSteps: Injectivity: if f̂ = ĝ then f = g on a neighbourhood of X′ (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-morphism-germ, Y of finite type over S), and that neighbourhood is X (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-fibre-neighbourhood, X → S closed).

Surjectivity: given h : X̂ → Ŷ, let W = X ×_S Y (separated of finite type over S, noetherian); Ŵ = X̂ ×_{Spf A} Ŷ (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-morphism, prodIso). The graph Γ_h : X̂ → Ŵ is a closed immersion: on each thickening it is the graph X_n → X_n ×_{S_n} Y_n, a closed immersion because Y_n → S_n is separated (base change of the diagonal, Mathlib IsSeparated), Γ_h is adic because it is a Spf A-morphism between formal schemes adic over Spf A (EGA I, 10.12.1: AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-morphism-of-formal-schemes), and an adic morphism whose reduction is a closed immersion is one (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-closed-immersion-criterion).
Its image is a closed formal subscheme of Ŵ proper over Spf A (isomorphic to X̂), hence equal to T̂ for a closed subscheme T ⊆ W proper over S (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-subscheme-algebraization).

The projection p : T → X is a morphism of proper S-schemes with p̂ an isomorphism, hence an isomorphism over a neighbourhood of X′ (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-detects-isomorphism), hence everywhere (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-fibre-neighbourhood); f := q ∘ p⁻¹ has graph T, so f̂ = h (graph compatibility of completion, EGA I, 10.9.8).
System form: AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-systems-equivalence identifies Hom_{Spf A}(X̂, Ŷ) with lim_n Hom_{S_n}(X_n, Y_n).
acceptance: Aut_S(P¹_{ℤ_p}) = PGL_2(ℤ_p) = lim_n PGL_2(ℤ/p^{n+1}) = Aut(P̂¹).
Separatedness of Y is needed for the graph argument; properness of X is needed: Hom_S(A¹_{ℤ_p}, A¹_{ℤ_p}) = ℤ_p[x] is strictly smaller than Hom(Spf ℤ_p⟨x⟩, Spf ℤ_p⟨x⟩) = ℤ_p⟨x⟩.

nodes.title: Grothendieck’s algebraization theorem (formal GAGA)
nodes.statement: Let A be an adic noetherian ring with ideal of definition I, S = Spec A, 𝔖 = Spf A, S_n = Spec A/I^{n+1}, f : 𝔛 → 𝔖 a proper morphism of formal schemes (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/proper-formal-morphism) with X_n = 𝔛 ×_𝔖 S_n, and L an invertible O_𝔛-module such that L_0 = L ⊗ O_{X_0} is ample on X_0. Then 𝔛 is algebraizable: there are a scheme X proper over S and an isomorphism X̂ ≅ 𝔛 (X is unique up to unique isomorphism by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-morphism-full-faithfulness), and for any such X there is an ample invertible O_X-module M with M̂ ≅ L; in particular X is projective over S (EGA III, 5.4.5). Equivalently (Stacks Tag 089A): a compatible system of schemes X_n over S_n with cartesian squares, X_0 proper over S_0, and invertible L_n with L_{n+1}|_{X_n} ≅ L_n and L_0 ample, comes from a proper X → S with an ample invertible L, X_n ≅ X ×_S S_n and L_n ≅ L|_{X_n}. The ampleness hypothesis cannot be dropped: there are formal schemes proper over Spf A that are not algebraizable (EGA III, 5.4.3).
hypotheses: A adic noetherian with ideal of definition I
𝔛 → Spf A proper
L invertible on 𝔛 with L_0 ample on the reduction X_0 (only the reduction modulo I is assumed ample)
proofSteps: By AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-serre-vanishing (iv) with F = O_𝔛 there is n_0 with Γ(𝔛, L^n) → Γ(X_0, L_0^n) surjective for n ≥ n_0; choose n ≥ n_0 with L_0^n very ample over S_0 (supplier AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.1: some power of an ample sheaf on a proper scheme over a noetherian ring is very ample).

Γ(X_0, L_0^n) is a finite A-module (supplier tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction Layer 2); choose a finitely generated A-submodule E ⊆ Γ(𝔛, L^n) mapping onto it. The maps E/I^{k+1}E ⊗ O_{X_k} → L_k^n are surjective (surjective at k = 0 by very ampleness, then by Nakayama) and define S_k-morphisms g_k : X_k → P(E) ×_S S_k (universal property of the projective bundle P(E), supplier R09.1) forming a compatible system, hence a morphism g : 𝔛 → P̂(E) over 𝔖 (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-systems-equivalence).

g_0 is a closed immersion (very ampleness), so g is a closed immersion (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-closed-immersion-criterion); 𝔛 is thus a closed formal subscheme of P̂(E), proper over 𝔖, hence 𝔛 ≅ T̂ for a closed subscheme T ⊆ P(E) proper over S (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-subscheme-algebraization). Set X := T; it is projective over S.

L is coherent on X̂, so L ≅ M̂ for a coherent O_X-module M (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/grothendieck-existence); M is invertible: M̂ is invertible, so M is invertible on a neighbourhood of X′ (Nakayama at points of X′; AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-detects-near-closed), which is X (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-fibre-neighbourhood).

M^n ≅ O_{P(E)}(1)|_X because their completions agree (full faithfulness on coherent sheaves, AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-fully-faithful); O(1)|_X is very ample, so M is ample (supplier R09.1). Uniqueness of X: AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-morphism-full-faithfulness.
acceptance: For X_n = P¹_{ℤ/p^{n+1}} with L_n = O(1), the algebraization is P¹_{ℤ_p} with O(1).

Every formal deformation over Spf A (A complete local noetherian with residue field k) of a smooth projective curve C_0 over k is algebraizable: an ample line bundle on C_0 lifts to every thickening because the obstruction lies in H²(C_0, O) = 0, so the hypothesis of the theorem holds.

EGA III, 5.4.3: proper formal schemes over Spf A need not be algebraizable (formal deformations of complex tori or K3 surfaces along which no ample line bundle lifts); the theorem does not apply because no L with L_0 ample exists.

nodes.title: Algebras topologically of finite type and of finite presentation over a complete rank-one valuation ring; admissible algebras
nodes.statement: Standing data: K is a field complete for a nontrivial rank-one nonarchimedean absolute value |·|, not assumed discretely valued; O_K = K° = {|x| ≤ 1} is its valuation ring (so O_K is noetherian if and only if K is discretely valued); ϖ ∈ O_K is a pseudouniformiser, 0 < |ϖ| < 1; k = O_K/m_K is the residue field. The ϖ-adic topology on O_K is its valuation topology and does not depend on ϖ. For variables ξ = (ξ_1, …, ξ_n), O_K⟨ξ⟩ is the ring of restricted power series Σ c_ν ξ^ν with c_ν ∈ O_K and c_ν → 0, equivalently the ϖ-adic completion of O_K[ξ]. An O_K-algebra A is topologically of finite type (tft) if A ≅ O_K⟨ξ⟩/a for some n and some ideal a; it is topologically of finite presentation (tfp) if moreover a is finitely generated (this does not depend on the chosen presentation); it is admissible if it is tfp and has no ϖ-torsion, equivalently (O_K being a valuation ring) if it is tfp and flat over O_K. Such A carries the ϖ-adic topology; every O_K-algebra homomorphism between tft algebras is continuous. The word 'admissible' is Bosch–Lütkebohmert's and must not be confused with EGA's admissible topological rings. The same definitions are made verbatim over a noetherian ring R complete for the I-adic topology of an ideal I (Bosch–Lütkebohmert's case (II)), where tft and tfp agree.
hypotheses: K complete, |·| nontrivial of rank one; discreteness is not assumed
The topology is the ϖ-adic one, never the m_K-adic one (the two differ when m_K = m_K², e.g. K = C_p)
Presentations use finitely many variables
proofSteps: Define O_K⟨ξ⟩ as Tau Ceti's completed restricted power-series ring restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion over O_K with its ϖ-adic topology, which is the ϖ-adic completion of O_K[ξ].

Independence of the finite presentation from the presentation: given surjections O_K⟨ξ⟩ → A and O_K⟨η⟩ → A, the kernel of O_K⟨ξ,η⟩ → A is generated by the kernel on O_K⟨ξ⟩ and the elements η_j − g_j(ξ) with g_j lifting the images of η_j; compare the two presentations through this one (Bosch–Lütkebohmert I §1, 'as is easily seen').

A tft algebra is ϖ-adically complete (Bosch–Lütkebohmert I Proposition 1.1(a), routine). Separatedness of tfp algebras (1.1(b)) and finite generation of the ϖ-power torsion of a tfp algebra (Lemma 1.4(c)) need the finiteness of saturated submodules, which is proved downstream of this definition; they are nodes flat-tft-is-tfp and tfp-algebra-coherent and are not part of this node's API.
Flat over O_K is equivalent to torsion-free because O_K is a valuation ring (Conrad, Several approaches, Exercise 3.3.3).
acceptance: O_K⟨T⟩ is admissible and O_K⟨T⟩ ⊗_{O_K} K = K⟨T⟩ is the Tate algebra.
O_K⟨T⟩/(ϖT) is tfp but not admissible.
For K = C_p the m_K-adic completion of O_K[T] is k[T], not O_K⟨T⟩, so the ϖ-adic topology is forced.

api.statement: If A is tft and O_K⟨η⟩ → A is any continuous surjection, then A is tfp if and only if its kernel is finitely generated.

(That it is a complete strongly noetherian Tate ring with ring of definition the image of A is not claimed here: it needs the Layer 0 request (C),(D) and, for the image of A, node tfp-algebra-coherent.)

api.statement: A is IsTopologicallyFinitePresentation and Submodule.torsionBy O_K A ϖ = 0 (no ϖ-torsion, hence no ϖ-power torsion).

nodes.title: Saturated submodules of finite free modules over tft algebras are finitely generated
nodes.statement: Let A be a tft O_K-algebra (node topologically-finitely-presented-algebra), F a finite free A-module and M ⊆ F an A-submodule that is ϖ-saturated: if f ∈ F and ϖ^m f ∈ M for some m ≥ 1, then f ∈ M. Then M is finitely generated. Equivalently, for every finitely generated A-module N the ϖ-power torsion N[ϖ^∞] is finitely generated and N/N[ϖ^∞] is finitely presented (the pair (A, ϖA) is adhesive in the sense of Fujiwara–Kato). Moreover (Bosch–Lütkebohmert I Lemma 1.2(a),(b)): the ϖ-adic topology of F induces the ϖ-adic topology on any submodule M, a finitely generated M is complete, and it is closed in F provided A (or M) is ϖ-adically separated — for instance when A is tfp (node flat-tft-is-tfp).
hypotheses: O_K a complete valuation ring of rank one (Fujiwara–Kato: any height), ϖ ∈ m_K nonzero
A topologically of finite type over O_K
Saturation cannot be dropped: m_K ⊂ O_K (non-discrete K) is not finitely generated and not saturated
proofSteps: Reduce to A = O_K⟨ξ⟩: if A = O_K⟨ξ⟩/a and M ⊆ A^r is saturated, its preimage M' ⊆ O_K⟨ξ⟩^r is saturated and M = M'/a^r.
For A = O_K⟨ξ⟩: M_K = M ⊗_{O_K} K ⊆ K⟨ξ⟩^r is finitely generated because K⟨ξ⟩ is noetherian (anchor Layer 0.5, item 4), and saturation gives M = M_K ∩ O_K⟨ξ⟩^r.

Finite generation of M_K ∩ O_K⟨ξ⟩^r: Bosch–Lütkebohmert I refer to [B, Satz 2.1] or [BGR 5.2.7/7] (Gauss-norm / orthonormal-basis arguments), or alternatively to Raynaud–Gruson I (3.4.6) applied to F/M, which is O_K-flat, after reduction mod ϖ; Fujiwara–Kato prove the equivalent adhesiveness of (O_K⟨ξ⟩, ϖ) in Theorem 9.2.1 (via Raynaud–Gruson (3.4.6) or Gabber's Lemma 9.2.6) and Proposition 8.5.3. None of [B], [BGR], [RG] is in the library: this step is a recorded gap.
Equivalence with the adhesive formulation: Fujiwara–Kato Proposition 8.5.3 ((a) ⇔ (c)).

Topological statements: Lemma 1.2(a) from the saturation M^sat ⊇ M with ϖ^m M^sat ⊆ M (finite generation of M^sat); 1.2(b): a finitely generated M is ϖ-adically complete (image of a finite free module over the complete A), and a complete submodule of a separated F is closed, which is why BL require M or A to be separated.
acceptance: A = O_K⟨T⟩, M = (T − c) with c ∈ O_K: saturated, generated by one element.
Necessity of saturation: for K = C_p, the O_K-submodule m_K ⊂ O_K (A = O_K, F = O_K) is not finitely generated and is not saturated (ϖ·1 ∈ m_K, 1 ∉ m_K).

nodes.title: A flat algebra topologically of finite type over O_K is topologically finitely presented
nodes.statement: Let A = O_K⟨ξ_1, …, ξ_n⟩/a be tft over O_K. (a) A is ϖ-adically complete. (b) If a is finitely generated, a is closed in O_K⟨ξ⟩, so A is ϖ-adically complete and separated. (c) If A has no ϖ-torsion (equivalently A is O_K-flat), then a is finitely generated; hence A is admissible. Globally (Fujiwara–Kato I, Corollary 2.3.2): if a formal scheme over Spf O_K is covered by formal affine opens Spf A_i with each A_i tft and its structure sheaf is ϖ-torsion-free, then each A_i is admissible.
hypotheses: O_K complete of rank one (Fujiwara–Kato: any height); K need not be discretely valued
(c) needs the absence of ϖ-torsion: O_K⟨T⟩/(m_K T) is tft but not tfp for non-discrete K
proofSteps: (a): the quotient of a complete module by any ideal is complete for the quotient topology, which is the ϖ-adic topology.
(b): node saturated-submodule-finitely-generated, parts (a),(b) of Bosch–Lütkebohmert Lemma 1.2: a finitely generated ideal of O_K⟨ξ⟩ is complete hence closed, and O_K⟨ξ⟩ is ϖ-adically separated.
(c): if A has no ϖ-torsion then a is ϖ-saturated in O_K⟨ξ⟩ (ϖ^m f ∈ a implies ϖ^m f̄ = 0 in A, so f̄ = 0); apply node saturated-submodule-finitely-generated with F = O_K⟨ξ⟩.
Globalisation: chartwise, A_i = Γ(Spf A_i, O_X) is ϖ-torsion-free, so (c) applies to each A_i; no locality statement is needed.
acceptance: Every K-affinoid algebra B = K⟨ξ⟩/b has the admissible model A = O_K⟨ξ⟩/(b ∩ O_K⟨ξ⟩) with A[1/ϖ] = B.
For non-discrete K, O_K⟨T⟩/(m_K T) is tft, has ϖ-torsion, and is not tfp: the flatness hypothesis in (c) is necessary.

nodes.title: Algebras topologically of finite presentation are coherent; torsion and annihilators are coherent
nodes.statement: Let A be a tfp O_K-algebra. (a) A is a coherent ring: every finitely generated ideal is finitely presented; hence every finitely presented A-module is coherent, and kernels, cokernels, images, sums, intersections, tensor products and Hom of coherent modules are coherent. (b) For a coherent ideal b ⊆ A and a coherent module M: Ann_A(M), Ann_M(b) and the ϖ-power torsion M[ϖ^∞] are coherent.
hypotheses: O_K complete of rank one; in the noetherian case (II) the statement is noetherianity
proofSteps: (a) for admissible A: for a finitely generated ideal b and a presentation 0 → M → F → b → 0 with F finite free, M is saturated in F because b has no ϖ-torsion; apply node saturated-submodule-finitely-generated.

(a) in general: A = O_K⟨ξ⟩/a with a finitely generated, and O_K⟨ξ⟩ is coherent by the admissible case; a quotient of a coherent ring by a finitely generated ideal is coherent ([EGA I, 0.5.3.2] two-out-of-three for coherent modules).
(b): Ann_A(M) and Ann_M(b) are kernels of maps into Hom-modules; M[ϖ^∞] is saturated in M and finitely generated by node saturated-submodule-finitely-generated after reducing to M finite free.
acceptance: The ϖ-torsion ideal of O_K⟨T⟩/(ϖT) is (T), finitely generated, and the quotient O_K is admissible.

nodes.title: Being topologically finitely presented or admissible is local on Spf; flatness mod ϖ^m and faithful flatness of covers
nodes.statement: Let A be an O_K-algebra that is ϖ-adically complete and separated, and let (Spf B_i)_{i∈I} be an affine open cover of Spf A (EGA I §10), I finite without loss. Then A is tfp (resp. admissible) if and only if every B_i is. In that case each A → B_i is flat and A → ∏_i B_i is faithfully flat. Flatness criterion (Bosch–Lütkebohmert I 1.6): for A tfp, B tfp (or tft and separated) and M a coherent B-module, M is flat (resp. faithfully flat) over A if and only if M/ϖ^{m}M is flat (resp. faithfully flat) over A/ϖ^{m}A for all m ≥ 1. For f ∈ A, the map A → A⟨f⁻¹⟩ is flat.
hypotheses: A ϖ-adically complete and separated
The cover is by formal affine opens, each B_i with the ϖ-adic topology
proofSteps: Tft is local: A/ϖ is of finite type over O_K/ϖ iff the B_i/ϖ are, by the scheme case and Bosch–Lütkebohmert I Lemma 1.5 (lifting generators mod ϖ).

Finite presentation: reduce mod ϖ^{m}; each A/ϖ^{m} is locally of finite presentation over O_K/ϖ^{m} hence of finite presentation ([EGA I_new 6.2.9]); so a/(a ∩ ϖ^{m}O_K⟨ξ⟩) is finitely generated, and since the ϖ-adic topology of O_K⟨ξ⟩ restricts to the ϖ-adic topology of a (node saturated-submodule-finitely-generated, Lemma 1.2(a)), a/ϖa finitely generated lifts to a finitely generated a by the limit argument of Lemma 1.5.

Flatness criterion 1.6: apply node adic-local-flatness-criterion (the proof of Bourbaki AC III §5 no 2 Thm 1), whose hypotheses are (1) the ϖ-adic topology of A restricts to that of every finitely generated ideal (Lemma 1.2(a), node saturated-submodule-finitely-generated) and (2) b ⊗_A M is ϖ-adically separated: b ⊗_A M is a finitely presented B-module by coherence (node tfp-algebra-coherent), and a finitely presented B-module F/L is separated because L is closed in F by Lemma 1.2(b), which needs B separated (Proposition 1.1(b), node flat-tft-is-tfp, or the hypothesis 'tft and separated').

A → B_i flat and A → ∏ B_i faithfully flat: flatness mod ϖ^{m} is the scheme statement for the open cover of Spec A/ϖ^{m}; apply 1.6. Admissibility is then local because a faithfully flat extension of a torsion-free algebra is torsion-free and conversely.
acceptance: The cover of Spf O_K⟨T⟩ by Spf O_K⟨T⟩⟨T⁻¹⟩ = Spf O_K⟨T, T⁻¹⟩ and Spf O_K⟨T⟩⟨(1 − T)⁻¹⟩ gives a faithfully flat map O_K⟨T⟩ → O_K⟨T,T⁻¹⟩ × O_K⟨T,(1−T)⁻¹⟩.

nodes.title: Admissible formal O_K-schemes (formal schemes locally topologically of finite presentation without ϖ-torsion)
nodes.statement: A formal O_K-scheme locally of tf presentation is a formal scheme X of finite ideal type in the sense of F0 (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/locally-noetherian-formal-scheme: locally Spf A with A an adic ring with finitely generated ideal of definition) with a morphism to Spf O_K, that is covered by open formal subschemes isomorphic to Spf A with A a tfp O_K-algebra carrying the ϖ-adic topology; equivalently ϖO_X is an ideal of definition and each X_m = X ⊗_{O_K} O_K/ϖ^{m+1} is a scheme locally of finite presentation over O_K/ϖ^{m+1}. X is admissible if moreover O_X has no ϖ-torsion; by node tfp-locality this holds iff every (equivalently: some covering family of) formal affine open Spf A has A admissible, iff every local ring O_{X,x} is O_K-flat. Morphisms are morphisms of formal O_K-schemes; they are automatically adic. The special fibre is X_s = X ⊗_{O_K} k; the underlying topological spaces of X, X_0 and X_s coincide and are locally noetherian (noetherian when X is quasi-compact) although O_X need not be noetherian. The category of admissible formal O_K-schemes has fibre products: the formal fibre product X ×_Z Y divided by its ϖ-torsion ideal (which is zero if X or Y is flat over Z). A coherent open ideal on X is a coherent ideal sheaf 𝒜 ⊆ O_X which locally on X contains ϖ^m O_X for some m (a single m works when X is quasi-compact). When K is discretely valued, admissible formal O_K-schemes are exactly the locally noetherian formal schemes flat and adic locally of finite type over Spf O_K (F0's notions).

Admissible is Bosch–Lütkebohmert's notion (tfp + ϖ-torsion-free), distinct from EGA's 'admissible ring'

proofSteps: Define via local charts Spf A with A admissible; well-definedness and locality from node tfp-locality.

Topological space: identified with that of the scheme X_0, locally of finite type over O_K/ϖ, hence locally noetherian (Bosch–Lütkebohmert I p. 298; Conrad, Several approaches after Definition 3.3.5).

Fibre products: form F0's formal fibre product (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-fibre-product) — charts Spf(B ⊗̂_A C) with F0's completed tensor product, tfp by node topologically-finitely-presented-algebra — and kill the ϖ-torsion ideal, which is coherent by node tfp-algebra-coherent; the quotient is admissible and has the universal property among admissible formal schemes.
Discretely valued case: tft = tfp, O_K⟨ξ⟩ noetherian, and flat adic formal schemes of finite type over Spf O_K in F0's sense coincide with admissible ones.

The ϖ-adic completion of P¹_{O_K} is admissible, glued from two copies of Spf O_K⟨T⟩.

nodes.title: Formal schemes of type (S): the class on which Huber's generic-fibre functor is defined, and its relation to admissible formal schemes and to Conrad's FS_C
nodes.statement: A formal scheme X = (X, O_X) is of type (S) if every point has an open affine neighbourhood U such that the topology of A := O_X(U) is adic and either (a) A is noetherian, or (b) there is s ∈ A such that sA is an ideal of definition and the Tate ring A(1/s) — the localisation A_s topologised by the images of s^m A — is strongly noetherian. For X of type (S) every formal affine open has an adic topology with a finitely generated ideal of definition. Morphisms of type-(S) formal schemes are adic (resp. locally of finite type) when locally the ring maps are adic (resp. topologically of finite type) in Huber's sense. Relations, all proved as part of this node's API: (i) every locally noetherian formal scheme (F0) is of type (S) via (a); (ii) every formal O_K-scheme locally of tf type (covered by Spf A with A tft over O_K with the ϖ-adic topology), in particular every locally tfp and every admissible one, is of type (S) via (b) with s = ϖ, since A[1/ϖ] is a quotient of K⟨ξ⟩ (K-affinoid after separated completion) and hence strongly noetherian; (iii) every object of Conrad's category FS_C (C an adic noetherian ring) is locally noetherian, hence of type (S) via (a); (iv) when K is not discretely valued, admissible formal O_K-schemes such as Spf O_K⟨T⟩ satisfy (b) but not (a) and are not objects of any FS_C, whereas Spf R_0[[T]] for a complete discrete valuation ring R_0 ⊆ O_K lies in FS_{R_0} and satisfies (a) but not (b); (v) for non-discrete K, Spf O_K[[T]] with the (ϖ, T)-adic topology is not of type (S) at all. Formal completions of morphisms locally of finite type along finite-type ideals preserve type (S) and are adic (Huber 1996 (1.9.5)).
hypotheses: Condition (S) is local on X and is stated for the rings of affine opens with adic topologies
The strongly noetherian hypothesis in (b) is on the Tate ring A(1/s), not on A
Conrad's FS_C requires C noetherian; type (S) does not
proofSteps: Define as in the source; locality in U is part of the definition.
Relation (i): immediate from (a).

Relation (ii): for A tft (in particular tfp) over O_K, ϖA is an ideal of definition and A(1/ϖ) = A[1/ϖ] is a quotient of K⟨ξ⟩ (node topologically-finitely-presented-algebra), strongly noetherian because every complete rank-one field is strongly noetherian and quotients and iterated restricted power series preserve noetherianity (anchor Layer 0.5, items 4–5; TauCeti.Huber.IsStronglyNoetherian).
Relation (iii): objects of FS_C are locally noetherian by Conrad's Definition 3.1.1.

Relation (iv): O_K⟨T⟩ is not noetherian when O_K is not; R_0[[T]] with the (m_{R_0}, T)-adic topology has no principal ideal of definition, since a principal ideal of the two-dimensional regular local ring R_0[[T]] has height at most one (Krull).

Relation (v): O_K[[T]] is not noetherian for non-discrete K. Suppose sO_K[[T]] were an ideal of definition, so T^m = sg and ϖ^m = sh for some m. Some coefficient of s is a unit (otherwise s ∈ m_K O_K[[T]] and T^m = sg would vanish in k[[T]]); by Weierstrass preparation over the complete valuation ring O_K, s = u·P with u a unit and P a distinguished polynomial of degree d ≥ 1 (d ≥ 1 because s(0) ∈ m_K, s being topologically nilpotent). Then P divides T^m in O_K[[T]], hence in O_K[T] by uniqueness in Weierstrass division, so P = T^d; but P(0) = s(0)/u(0) ≠ 0 since ϖ^m = s(0)h(0). (Krull's principal ideal theorem is not available: O_K[[T]] is not noetherian.)
(1.9.5) is asserted in the source for completions along finite-type ideals; for the ϖ-adic completion of an O_K-scheme locally of finite type it is relation (ii).

nodes.title: Huber's functor t from locally noetherian formal schemes to adic spaces
nodes.statement: For a locally noetherian formal scheme X (F0) there are an adic space t(X) and a morphism of locally and topologically ringed spaces π_X: (t(X), O⁺_{t(X)}) → (X, O_X) such that every morphism of locally and topologically ringed spaces (Z, O⁺_Z) → (X, O_X) from an adic space Z factors uniquely through a morphism of adic spaces Z → t(X). On affines t(Spf A) = Spa(A, A), and π_X(x) = {a ∈ A : |a(x)| < 1}, the centre of x. The universal property makes t a functor; t is fully faithful; a morphism f of locally noetherian formal schemes is adic (EGA I 10.12) resp. locally of finite type (EGA I 10.13) if and only if t(f) is adic resp. locally of finite type (Huber 1994 Proposition 4.2(i)). The trivial valuations form a subspace t(X)_t ⊆ t(X) and π_X restricts to an isomorphism of locally ringed spaces (t(X)_t, O⁺|) ≅ (X, O_X); in particular π_X has a section ι_X by trivial valuations. The smallest saturated subcategory of adic spaces containing the image of t consists of the adic spaces locally of the form Spa(A, A⁺) with A finitely generated over a noetherian ring of definition A_0 and A⁺ the integral closure of A_0 in A (4.2(ii)).
hypotheses: X locally noetherian (F0); for non-noetherian formal models use node generic-fibre-functor-d instead
Spa(A, A) must be an adic space: the structure presheaf of Spa(A, A) for a noetherian adic ring A is a sheaf (Huber 1994 Theorem 2.2; AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-type-stably-sheafy)
proofSteps: Affine case: t(Spf A) := Spa(A, A); the identity of A gives π (Huber 1994, proof of 4.1, point (1): morphisms of locally and topologically ringed spaces (Y, O⁺_Y) → (Spf A, O) correspond to continuous ring maps A → O_Y(Y), with the map on points y ↦ {a : v_y(a) < 1}).

Every open U of Spf A induces the open π⁻¹(U) of t(Spf A); morphisms between opens of affines induce morphisms of adic spaces; glue along the gluing data of X using the anchor's gluing of adic spaces (Layer 5).

Full faithfulness: a morphism t(X) → t(Y) preserves trivial-valuation loci and induces a morphism of locally ringed spaces X ≅ X_t → Y_t ≅ Y, which is a morphism of formal schemes because X is locally noetherian (proof of 4.2(i)).

Adic and finite-type criteria: a map of noetherian adic rings is topologically of finite type iff it factors through a continuous open surjection A⟨X_1, …, X_n⟩ → B (Huber 1994 (3.3.ii)); combine with the characterisation of adic maps (3.2.i) and (3.6).

Sheafiness of Spa(A, A) (A noetherian adic) is Huber 1994 Theorem 2.2, not in the anchor's Layer 4 (which covers strongly noetherian Tate rings); it is AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-type-stably-sheafy, case (N).

The analytic locus of t(Spf Z_p[[T]]) is the open unit disc over Q_p, the union of the rational subsets R(Tⁿ/p) (Hübner, Example 8.7).

nodes.title: Huber's analytic adic space d(X) of a formal scheme of type (S)
nodes.statement: Proposition 1.9.1: for X of type (S) there are an adic space d(X) and a morphism of topologically ringed spaces λ = λ_X: d(X) → X such that (a) d(X) is analytic: for the ideal sheaf I ⊆ O_X of sections vanishing at every point, λ⁻¹(I)·O_{d(X)} = O_{d(X)}; (b) O_X → λ_* O_{d(X)} factors through λ_* O⁺_{d(X)} and λ: (d(X), O⁺_{d(X)}) → (X, O_X) is a morphism of locally ringed spaces; (c) (d(X), λ) is universal among adic spaces with a morphism to X satisfying (a) and (b). Hence d is a functor from type-(S) formal schemes with adic morphisms to analytic adic spaces, and λ is natural. Affine formulas: for X = Spf A with A noetherian, d(X) = t(X)_a with the restriction of π_X (node noetherian-formal-scheme-as-adic-space); in case (b), with B the integral closure of (the image of) A in A(1/s), d(X) = Spa(A(1/s), B) and λ(x) = {a ∈ A : |a(x)| < 1}. For X locally tfp over O_K (in particular admissible), d(Spf A) = Spa(A[1/ϖ], B); when K is discretely valued (so X is locally noetherian and t(X) is defined) d(X) is the open locus {|ϖ| ≠ 0} of t(X) over Spa(O_K, O_K) (Hübner §8), while for non-discrete K no adic space t(X) is available and only the affine formula is used; d(X) = d(X^{tf}) so ϖ-torsion is invisible. Open formal subschemes U ⊆ X give open subspaces d(U) = λ⁻¹(U), and for every affine U satisfying (S), d(U) is spectral (1.9.3).
hypotheses: X of type (S); morphisms adic
Case (a) of the construction uses Huber 1994 §4 (node noetherian-formal-scheme-as-adic-space); d(Spf A) in case (b) is an adic space because A(1/s) is strongly noetherian Tate (anchor Layer 4)
proofSteps: Reduce to affine X by gluing (anchor Layer 5) using d(U) = λ⁻¹(U) for open U, itself a consequence of the universal property.
Case (a): d(X) := t(X)_a with π_X restricted; (a) holds because analytic points have non-open support; universality from the universal property of t.

Case (b): B = integral closure of A in A(1/s); (A(1/s), B) is a complete affinoid ring (Huber pair) since B is open (contains the image of A) and integrally closed; d(X) := Spa(A(1/s), B), sheafy since A(1/s) is strongly noetherian Tate; λ is induced by A → B through Huber 1994 proof of 4.1, point (1); (a) holds since s is a unit; (c): a morphism Z → Spf A satisfying (a),(b) inverts s and lands in the power-bounded, integrally closed plus ring, so factors through Spa(A(1/s), B) (universal property of rational localisation, anchor Layer 3).
Functoriality d(f) and naturality of λ from (c).

nodes.title: For formal O_K-schemes locally of tf presentation, d(X) is the adic space of Raynaud's rigid generic fibre
nodes.statement: Let X be a formal O_K-scheme locally of tf presentation (in particular admissible), K complete of rank one. (i) For X = Spf A the integral closure B of the image of A in A_K = A ⊗_{O_K} K equals the power-bounded subring A_K°, so d(Spf A) = Spa(A_K, A_K°) = r(Sp A_K), where r is Huber's rigid–adic comparison functor (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor). (ii) Raynaud's generic fibre X_rig (Bosch–Lütkebohmert I §4: glue Sp(A_K) over formal affine opens Spf A, basic opens Spf A⟨f⁻¹⟩ going to Laurent domains Sp A_K⟨f⁻¹⟩ = {|f| ≥ 1}) is a quasi-separated rigid K-space, and there is an isomorphism of adic spaces d(X) ≅ r(X_rig), functorial in X and compatible with open formal subschemes (U ↦ λ⁻¹(U)). (iii) In particular d(X) is locally of finite type over Spa(K, O_K), and d(X) is quasi-compact (resp. quasi-separated) when X is quasi-compact (resp. always).
hypotheses: K complete, nontrivial rank-one valuation; O_K may be non-noetherian
X locally tfp over Spf O_K
r and its properties are those of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor
proofSteps: (i): choose a surjection O_K⟨ξ⟩ → A; B is the integral closure of the image of O_K⟨ξ⟩ in A_K, which is A_K° by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/tft-plus-ring-power-bounded (Huber 1994 Lemma 4.4, via [BGR 6.4.3]).
Affine comparison: r(Sp A_K) = Spa(A_K, A_K°) (R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor (a)) = d(Spf A) by node generic-fibre-functor-d.

Basic opens: A⟨f⁻¹⟩ ⊗ K = A_K⟨ζ⟩/(1 − fζ) is the Laurent domain {|f| ≥ 1} (Bosch–Lütkebohmert I §4), and the generic fibre of Spf A⟨f⁻¹⟩ is the rational subset {x : |f(x)| ≥ 1} of d(Spf A) by the affine formula of node generic-fibre-functor-d; r takes rational subdomains to rational subsets (R1).
Glue both sides along the same gluing data; functoriality from the universal property of d and full faithfulness of r.

(iii): d(X) is covered by affinoids of finite type over Spa(K, O_K); quasi-compactness from finite covers; quasi-separatedness from BL1 §4 ('the functor X ↦ X_rig can produce only quasi-separated rigid K-spaces') and R1's equivalence for quasi-separated spaces.

Huber 1996 Example 1.9.2(ii) states d(X) ≅ r(s(X)) for X locally of finite type over Spf A, A a rank-one valuation ring, without proof; Huber 1994 Remark 4.6(ii)-(iii) states the discretely valued case.
acceptance: d(Spf O_K⟨T⟩) = r(Sp K⟨T⟩) is the closed unit disc; d of the ϖ-adic completion of P¹_{O_K} is r of the rigid projective line glued from two closed unit discs along {|T| = 1} (Conrad, Several approaches, Example 3.3.9).

nodes.title: The generic fibre commutes with fibre products and with completed extension of the base field
nodes.statement: (a) For morphisms X → Z ← Y of formal O_K-schemes locally of tf presentation, the natural map d(X ×_Z Y) → d(X) ×_{d(Z)} d(Y) is an isomorphism of adic spaces, where the right side is the fibre product of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence (it exists because d(X) → d(Z) is locally of finite type). Since d kills ϖ-torsion, the same holds for the fibre product in the admissible category. (b) For a complete nonarchimedean extension K'/K, d(X ⊗̂_{O_K} O_{K'}) ≅ d(X) ×_{Spa(K,O_K)} Spa(K', O_{K'}), functorially in X.

proofSteps: Affine case of (a): X = Spf B, Y = Spf C, Z = Spf A; X ×_Z Y = Spf(B ⊗̂_A C), whose generic fibre is Spa of (B ⊗̂_A C)[1/ϖ] = B_K ⊗̂_{A_K} C_K with plus ring the integral closure of the image of B ⊗ C (node raynaud-generic-fibre (i)); this is the completed tensor product of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product, whose Spa is the fibre product by R0/affinoid-fibre-product.

(b): the same computation with A = O_K and C = O_{K'}: (B ⊗̂_{O_K} O_{K'})[1/ϖ] = B_K ⊗̂_K K'.

nodes.title: The specialisation map λ_X = sp: d(X) → X
nodes.statement: For X of type (S) the specialisation map is the continuous map λ_X: d(X) → X underlying Proposition 1.9.1. For X = Spf A and x ∈ d(X), λ(x) = {a ∈ A : |a(x)| < 1}, an open prime of A; equivalently λ(x) is the centre of x, the image of the closed point of Spec κ(x)⁺ under the map Spec κ(x)⁺ → Spec A induced by A → κ(x)⁺ (|A(x)| ≤ 1). Properties: (i) λ is continuous: for s ∈ A, λ⁻¹(D(s)) = {|s| = 1} = {|s| ≥ 1} is open and λ⁻¹(V(s)) = {|s| < 1} is closed; (ii) λ is natural: λ_Y ∘ d(f) = f ∘ λ_X; (iii) for X admissible over O_K, λ maps each classical point (residue field finite over K) to a closed point of X_s, and every closed point of X_s is the image of a classical point (Bosch–Lütkebohmert I 3.4, 3.5), λ of the classical point attached to a rig-point being its special point; the restriction sp: X_rig → X to classical points is Berthelot's specialisation map of rigid geometry, which is anticontinuous: preimages of closed subsets are admissible opens (the tubes of node tube); (iv) λ is compatible with admissible blow-ups φ: X' → X, i.e. φ ∘ λ_{X'} = λ_X ∘ d(φ) with d(φ) an isomorphism (node generic-fibre-inverts-admissible-blow-ups); (v) for X quasi-compact admissible, the maps λ_{X'} over all admissible blow-ups X' → X induce a homeomorphism d(X) → lim_{X'} |X'| and an isomorphism (d(X), O⁺) ≅ lim (X', O_{X'}) (Zariski–Riemann description; Hübner Theorem 8.9, proof cited from Bhatt's notes Proposition 8.1.3, and Conrad, Several approaches §4.1).
hypotheses: X of type (S) for (i),(ii); admissible over O_K for (iii)–(v)
Care: in the adic space, λ⁻¹ of a closed set is closed, not open; the rigid 'anticontinuity' concerns classical points and corresponds to the interior (node tube)
proofSteps: λ is part of the data of node generic-fibre-functor-d; the pointwise formula is Huber 1994, proof of 4.1, point (1), applied to A → B.

(i): λ⁻¹(D(s)) = {x : s ∉ λ(x)} = {x : |s(x)| ≥ 1} and |s| ≤ 1 on d(Spf A) since s lies in the plus ring; this is a rational subset (TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset with T = {1}, denominator s).
(ii): from functoriality of d.

(iii): Conrad, Several approaches Example 3.3.13 (sp(x) is the closed point given by A_i/(π) → k̃(x)); surjectivity onto closed points from node rig-point (Bosch–Lütkebohmert I 3.5) and the bijection rig-points ↔ classical points.
(iv): naturality (ii) applied to φ.

(v): Hübner Theorem 8.9 reduces to the statement that the ϖ-adic completion of colim O_{X',x'} is a microbial valuation ring (Bhatt, Lecture notes on perfectoid spaces, Proposition 8.1.3 — not in the library): recorded gap; the homeomorphism on underlying spaces is Conrad, Several approaches §4.1, whose proof (rig-points, Hochster) is not given there.

nodes.title: Tubes ]T[ of locally closed subsets of the special fibre, adic and rigid
nodes.statement: Let X be an admissible formal O_K-scheme with specialisation λ: d(X) → X (node specialisation-map). For T ⊆ X locally closed (X and X_s have the same space): (i) if T = U is open, ]U[ := λ⁻¹(U) = d(X|_U), an open subspace; (ii) if T = Z is closed and X = Spf A with Z = V(f_1, …, f_r) ⊆ Spec A/ϖ (f_i ∈ A), then ]Z[ := ⋃_{m≥1} {x ∈ d(X) : |f_i(x)|^m ≤ |ϖ| for all i}; this is independent of the chosen f_i and of ϖ, equals the interior of the closed set λ⁻¹(Z), and glues over affine covers; (iii) for T = U ∩ Z, ]T[ := λ⁻¹(U) ∩ ]Z[. Each ]T[ is open in d(X). Rigid comparison: the classical points of ]T[ are exactly the classical points x with sp(x) ∈ T, i.e. Berthelot's tube sp⁻¹(T), which is an admissible open of X_rig, and r(sp⁻¹(T)) = ]T[ under AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor. For closed Z and rational q > 0, the closed tube of radius |ϖ|^q is [Z]_q := {x : |f_i(x)| ≤ |ϖ|^q for all i}, in the convention of node fractional-valuation-bound; it is quasi-compact and ]Z[ = ⋃_{q>0} [Z]_q. The set λ⁻¹(Z) itself is closed, and in general strictly larger than ]Z[ by non-classical boundary points; Huber's pseudo-adic spaces d(X, L) use λ⁻¹(L), not the interior.
hypotheses: X admissible over O_K (the definitions make sense for X of type (S) with ϖ replaced by s)
T locally closed in X_s
Radii |ϖ|^q with q ∈ ℚ_{>0} use node fractional-valuation-bound, never an element ϖ^q of K
proofSteps: (i): node generic-fibre-functor-d gives d(U) = λ⁻¹(U).

(ii) independence: if Z = V(g_1, …, g_s) as well then each g_j^N lies in (f_1, …, f_r) + ϖA for some N, and conversely, so the unions over m agree; changing ϖ to another pseudouniformiser ϖ' changes m by a bounded factor since ϖ^a ∈ ϖ'O_K and ϖ'^b ∈ ϖO_K.

(ii) interior: each {|f_i|^m ≤ |ϖ|} is an open (rational) subset contained in λ⁻¹(Z) = {|f_i| < 1 ∀i}; conversely a point of λ⁻¹(Z) with a rational neighbourhood inside λ⁻¹(Z) has |f_i|^m ≤ |ϖ| for some m, since by quasi-compactness of that neighbourhood the maximum modulus of f_i on it is < 1 (maximum modulus principle for affinoids, anchor Layer 2 and [BGR 6.2.1]).
Gluing: the formula is compatible with restriction to basic opens Spf A⟨g⁻¹⟩.

Rigid comparison: classical points x have |f_i(x)| < 1 iff |f_i(x)|^m ≤ |ϖ| for some m (value group of a finite extension is discrete over |K^×| up to finite index); admissibility of sp⁻¹(T): Conrad, Several approaches Example 3.3.13 and Grosse-Klönne 2.3; R1's r takes admissible opens to opens.
Closed tubes [Z]_q are rational subsets (fractional bound realised as |f_i^b| ≤ |ϖ^a|, q = a/b), hence quasi-compact.
acceptance: X = Spf O_K⟨T⟩, Z = {0}: ]Z[ is the open unit disc ⋃_m {|T|^m ≤ |ϖ|}.

X = Spf O_K⟨T⟩, U = A¹_k ∖ {0}: ]U[ = {|T| = 1}; ]U[ ∪ ]{0}[ misses the point η_{1⁻}, matching the non-admissible rigid covering {|t| = 1} ⊔ {|t| < 1} of {|t| ≤ 1} (Conrad, genpaper, before the proof of A.1.4).

nodes.title: Rig-points of admissible formal schemes
nodes.statement: Let X be an admissible formal O_K-scheme. A rig-point of X is a morphism u: T → X of admissible formal O_K-schemes that is a closed immersion, with T = Spf B affine and B a local integral domain of dimension 1; its residue field is Frac(B). (Bosch–Lütkebohmert allow locally closed immersions; over a complete rank-one valuation ring locally closed rig-points are closed.) Properties: (3.2) B is finite over O_K and the integral closure of B in Frac(B) is the valuation ring O_{K'} of the finite extension K' = Frac(B) of K; (3.3) for an admissible blow-up X' → X the induced map on rig-points is bijective and preserves residue fields; (3.4) for X = Spf A the rig-points correspond bijectively to primes p ⊂ A with ϖ ∉ p and dim A/p = 1, and to closed points of Spec A[1/ϖ], i.e. to maximal ideals of the K-affinoid algebra A_K; (3.5) every closed point of X_s is the special point of some rig-point. Consequently rig-points of X correspond bijectively to the classical points of d(X) (residue field finite over K); the compatibility with the specialisation map λ (the special point of u is λ of the corresponding classical point) is proved in node specialisation-map, which depends on this node. Conrad's Lemma A.1.5: for Y flat and locally tfp over Spf O_K, every point y: Sp(K') → Y_rig is y_rig for a unique closed immersion Spf B → Y with B a finite flat O_K-domain, and every closed point of Y_s underlies such a map.
hypotheses: X admissible over a complete rank-one O_K

Existence (3.5) in the rank-one case applies [BGR 7.1.5/4] to the integral closure of A in A ⊗ K (the packet gap entry describes it as the lifting of closed points of the reduction to points of Sp A); BGR is not in the library
proofSteps: Definition as stated; the image of A in Frac(B) is an admissible O_K-algebra.

(3.2): the special point of T is a closed point of X_s, finite over k; T is finite over O_K by the argument of Lemma 1.5; Frac(B) is finite over K and the integral closure of O_K in it is a complete valuation ring equal to the integral closure of B ([BGR 3.2.4/2]).

(3.3): pull back the blown-up coherent open ideal to B; it becomes invertible over the valuation ring O_{K'} and already over a finite local extension B' of B; the universal property of the blow-up (node admissible-blow-up) lifts Spf B' → X uniquely; residue fields are unchanged.
(3.4): a closed point of Spec A_K is a surjection A_K → K' with K'/K finite ([BGR 6.1.2/3]); the image B of A lies in O_{K'}, is integral over O_K, local of dimension 1.
(3.5): reduce to X = Spf A affine and apply [BGR 7.1.5/4] to the integral closure of A in A ⊗ K (gap: BGR unread).
Classical points: combine (3.4) with node raynaud-generic-fibre (points of Spa(A_K, A_K°) with finite residue field are the maximal ideals of A_K, R1).
acceptance: Rig-points of Spf O_K⟨T⟩ correspond to Galois orbits of c ∈ K̄ with |c| ≤ 1; for c ∈ O_K, u is Spf O_K → Spf O_K⟨T⟩, T ↦ c.

nodes.title: Admissible formal blow-ups and strict transforms
nodes.statement: Let X be an admissible formal O_K-scheme and 𝒜 ⊆ O_X a coherent open ideal (coherent, and locally ϖ^N O_X ⊆ 𝒜 for some N; a single N when X is quasi-compact). The admissible blow-up of 𝒜 is X' := lim_m Proj(⊕_{n≥0} 𝒜ⁿ ⊗_{O_X} O_X/ϖ^{m+1}) with its projection φ: X' → X. (a) Over a formal affine open Spf A with 𝒜 ↔ a = (f_0, …, f_r) ∋ ϖ^N, φ⁻¹(Spf A) is the ϖ-adic completion of the scheme-theoretic blow-up of a on Spec A, covered by the charts Spf A'_i with A'_i = A⟨ζ_j : j ≠ i⟩/(f_iζ_j − f_j)_{j≠i} modulo its ϖ-torsion (which equals its f_i-torsion), Spf A'_i being the locus where f_i generates 𝒜O_{X'}. (b) X' is admissible and 𝒜O_{X'} is invertible. (c) Universal property: every morphism ψ: Z → X of formal O_K-schemes (Z not necessarily admissible) with 𝒜O_Z invertible factors uniquely through φ. Further: φ is an isomorphism over X ∖ V(𝒜); formation commutes with flat base change and, in the admissible category, with arbitrary base change (strict transform); φ is proper and surjective on special fibres; blowing up 𝒜 and then ℬO_{X'} is blowing up 𝒜ℬ; for X quasi-compact a composite of admissible blow-ups is an admissible blow-up (Bosch–Lütkebohmert I 2.5), blow-ups of finitely many opens extend to X and are dominated by one admissible blow-up of X (2.6), and any two admissible blow-ups of X are dominated by a third, so admissible blow-ups of X form a cofiltered system. The strict transform of a coherent O_X-module ℳ is ℳ' = φ*ℳ/𝒩, where 𝒩 is the 𝒜O_{X'}-power torsion of φ*ℳ (sections killed locally by a power of 𝒜O_{X'}; the scheme-theoretic 'sections supported in φ⁻¹(V(𝒜))' of Raynaud–Gruson 5.1.1, V(𝒜) being read scheme-theoretically since the underlying space of X' is its special fibre); 𝒩 lies in the ϖ-power torsion, and if ℳ' has no ϖ-torsion, 𝒩 is the ϖ-power torsion of φ*ℳ, which is coherent (Lemma 1.4(c)).
hypotheses: X admissible over O_K; X quasi-compact for composition (2.5) and extension (2.6)
𝒜 coherent and open; a non-open centre changes the generic fibre
Composition 2.5 uses [RG, 5.1.4] and [EGA I_new 6.9.9]; extension 2.6 uses [EGA I_new 6.9.7]
proofSteps: Define X' as the formal scheme attached to the adic thickening system of projective schemes Proj(⊕ 𝒜ⁿ ⊗ O/ϖ^{m+1}) (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/colimit-of-thickenings, valid for finite ideal type); locally this is the ϖ-adic completion of the scheme blow-up (Rees algebra ⊕ aⁿ, mathlib reesAlgebra).

(a) Chart description: Bosch–Lütkebohmert I Lemma 2.2; in the non-noetherian case, completion of A[ζ]/(f_iζ_j − f_j) is computed by the exact sequence of completions, the ideal being closed by node flat-tft-is-tfp (Lemma 1.2(b)); the ϖ-torsion of the completed chart is finitely generated by node saturated-submodule-finitely-generated and coincides with the f_i-torsion.
(b) Charts are tft and ϖ-torsion-free, hence admissible by node flat-tft-is-tfp; 𝒜O_{X'} is locally principal and open, hence contains ϖ^N, and has no ϖ-torsion, so it is invertible.

(c) From the universal property of the scheme blow-up on each Spec A/ϖ^{m+1} and passage to the limit; morphisms into X' are compatible systems of morphisms into the levels (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/morphisms-as-compatible-systems-finite-ideal-type (ii), with the ideal of definition ϖ·O_{X'} of X' and, on Z, an ideal of definition of finite type containing ϖ·O_Z).

Isomorphism away from V(𝒜), properness (Proj), surjectivity on special fibres (a non-empty X has X'_0 non-empty: otherwise aⁿ = 0 mod ϖ for n ≫ 0 forces A = 0 since A has no ϖ-torsion), multiplicativity: Bosch–Lütkebohmert I Remark 2.4.
Composition (2.5), extension (2.6) and domination: blow up the product of the relevant ideals; the non-noetherian steps cite [RG 5.1.4] and [EGA I_new 6.9.7, 6.9.9] (recorded as unread imports).

Strict transform: 𝒩 is the 𝒜O_{X'}-power torsion; it is contained in the ϖ-power torsion (locally 𝒜O_{X'} = (g) with g | ϖ^N), and when φ*ℳ/𝒩 is ϖ-torsion-free it equals the ϖ-power torsion, which is coherent by node tfp-algebra-coherent (Lemma 1.4(c)). Bosch–Lütkebohmert I p. 301 write 𝒩 = Ann_{φ*ℳ}(𝒜O_{X'}) (first-order annihilator) and deduce coherence from Lemma 1.4(b); that description does not agree with 'sections supported in φ⁻¹(Y)' (see the recorded source mistake), but both give the ϖ-power torsion in the torsion-free case, which is the only case used downstream.
acceptance: The admissible blow-up of (T, ϖ) on Spf O_K⟨T⟩ has charts Spf O_K⟨U⟩ (T = ϖU) and Spf O_K⟨T, V⟩/(TV − ϖ); its special fibre is P¹_k ∪ A¹_k meeting in one point.
Blowing up an invertible open ideal (e.g. ϖ^n O_X) is an isomorphism.

api.statement: For f: X → T locally of tf presentation, a coherent O_X-module ℳ and the admissible blow-up φ: T' → T of a coherent open ideal 𝒜: ℳ' = ℳ_{X'}/(sections of ℳ_{X'} supported over V(𝒜), i.e. killed by a power of 𝒜O_{X'}) on X' = X ×_T T' (Raynaud–Gruson I 5.1.1(ii)); this torsion lies in the ϖ-power torsion, and for ℳ = O_X it defines the strict transform of X, a closed formal subscheme of X ×_T T'.

api.name: FormalScheme.strictTransformBaseChange_comp

api.name: FormalScheme.admissibleBlowUp.comp_of_disjoint

nodes.title: The generic fibre of an admissible blow-up is an isomorphism
nodes.statement: Let φ: X' → X be the admissible blow-up of a coherent open ideal 𝒜 on an admissible formal O_K-scheme X. Then d(φ): d(X') → d(X) is an isomorphism of adic spaces (equivalently φ_rig is an isomorphism of rigid spaces). Over Spf A with 𝒜 = (f_0, …, f_r): the f_i generate the unit ideal of A_K, the chart Spf A'_i has generic fibre the rational subset R(f_0, …, f_r / f_i) of Spa(A_K, A_K°) (the locus where |f_i| is maximal), and these rational subsets cover Spa(A_K, A_K°).
hypotheses: 𝒜 coherent and open (ϖ^N ∈ 𝒜)
X admissible
proofSteps: Reduce to X = Spf A affine.

ϖ^N ∈ (f_0, …, f_r) and ϖ is a unit in A_K, so the f_i generate the unit ideal of A_K; hence the standard rational subsets R(f/f_i) cover Spa(A_K, A_K°) (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa_eq_biUnion_rationalSubset_of_span_eq_top).

A'_i ⊗ K = A_K⟨f_j/f_i⟩ in the notation of [BGR 6.1.4] (Bosch–Lütkebohmert I proof of 4.1(a)), the rational localisation of the anchor's Layer 3, whose Spa with plus ring the integral closure of A⟨f/f_i⟩ is homeomorphic to R(f/f_i) (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spaLocalizationHomeomorph); the plus rings agree with those of node raynaud-generic-fibre (i).
The charts glue compatibly on overlaps (both sides compute R(f/f_i) ∩ R(f/f_j)), so d(φ) is a bijective local isomorphism onto a cover, hence an isomorphism.
acceptance: For 𝒜 = (T, ϖ) on Spf O_K⟨T⟩ the charts have generic fibres {|T| ≤ |ϖ|} and {|ϖ| ≤ |T| ≤ 1}, which cover the closed unit disc (Conrad, Several approaches, Exercise 3.3.12).

nodes.title: Adjoining power-bounded functions to an admissible algebra is an admissible blow-up
nodes.statement: Let A be an admissible O_K-algebra and f_1, …, f_n ∈ A_K = A ⊗_{O_K} K with |f_i|_sup ≤ 1 (i.e. f_i ∈ A_K°). Then B = A[f_1, …, f_n] ⊆ A_K is an admissible O_K-algebra, finite over A, with B_K = A_K; and if r ∈ ℕ satisfies ϖ^r f_i ∈ A for all i, then Spf B → Spf A is the admissible blow-up of the coherent open ideal (ϖ^r, ϖ^r f_1, …, ϖ^r f_n).
hypotheses: A admissible; f_i power-bounded in the affinoid algebra A_K
Uses [BGR 6.3.4/1]: A_K° is integral over the image of O_K⟨ξ⟩ for any presentation
proofSteps: B is integral over A because the f_i are integral over the image of O_K⟨ξ⟩ ([BGR 6.3.4/1]); B is of finite type over A, hence finite, hence tfp and torsion-free (⊆ A_K), i.e. admissible.
Let Y' → Spec A be the scheme blow-up of a = (ϖ^r, ϖ^r f_i); a·B = ϖ^r B is invertible, so Spec B → Spec A factors through Y', identifying Spec B with the open where ϖ^r generates.
That open is all of Y': on the chart where ϖ^r f_i generates, f_i has an inverse and is integral, so f_i⁻¹ ∈ the chart ring and ϖ^r generates there too (Bosch–Lütkebohmert I, proof of 4.5).
ϖ-adic completion is trivial since B is finite over A; conclude with node admissible-blow-up (a).
acceptance: For p ≠ 2 and A = O_K[X]/(X² − ϖ²): f = X/ϖ ∈ A_K° ∖ A, B = A[f] ≅ O_K × O_K, and Spf B → Spf A is the admissible blow-up of (ϖ, X).
