nodes.title: One step of the flattening induction: enlarging the locus of flatness in dimension ≥ m (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Lemma 4.7)
nodes.statement: Let T be a quasi-compact admissible formal O_K-scheme, f: X → T a morphism of quasi-compact formal O_K-schemes locally of tf presentation, and ℳ a coherent O_X-module that is rig-flat over T in dimension ≥ n and T-flat in dimension ≥ m + 1, m ≥ n. Let T(1) → T be an admissible blow-up, X(1) = X ×_T T(1), ℳ̄(1) the strict transform of the pull-back of ℳ, and U_0 ⊊ T_0 an open subset such that ℳ̄(1) is flat in dimension ≥ m over U_0(1) = U_0 ×_T T(1). There are an admissible blow-up T(2) → T(1) with centre disjoint from U_0(1) and an open W_0 ⊆ T_0 with U_0 ⊊ W_0 such that the strict transform ℳ̄(2) of ℳ on X(2) = X ×_T T(2) is flat in dimension ≥ m over W_0(2).
hypotheses: Strict transforms are taken with respect to the composite blow-ups T(i) → T
proofSteps: Let t be a generic point of T_0 ∖ U_0 (T_0 is a noetherian space, node admissible-formal-scheme) and x ∈ X_0 a generic point of an m-dimensional component of the non-flat locus of ℳ̄(1) above t; there are finitely many such x (X quasi-compact). It suffices to find T(2) → T(1), with centre outside U_0(1), making the strict transform flat at all points above x: repeating for the finitely many x (composites of admissible blow-ups, node admissible-blow-up) makes it flat in dimension ≥ m above t, and upper semicontinuity of fibre dimension then yields W_0 ∋ t.
It suffices to work locally around t: blow-ups of open neighbourhoods extend to T (node admissible-blow-up, extension; Bosch–Lütkebohmert cite [FI, 2.5], see sourceIssues AdicSpacesPartII/E18).

Reduction to a dévissage over T: node formal-devissage-existence gives elementary étale affine neighbourhoods (X', x') → (X, x), (T', t') → (T, t) and a dévissage of ℳ' at x' in dimensions n¹ > … > n^r = m. A blow-up of T(1)' = T(1) ×_T T' with centre outside U(1)'_0 near t' is induced by one of T(1): after shrinking, the closure of t' maps isomorphically onto an open of the closure of t, and étale maps inducing isomorphisms on reductions are isomorphisms on thickenings (node formal-etale-site-invariance), so the centre is a subscheme of T(1); rig-flatness pulls back and flatness of strict transforms descends along the étale T' → T (nodes rig-flat-in-dimension, flat-in-dimension).

By node devissage-injectivity-and-rig-flatness, after shrinking, α^i is T-universally injective for i ≤ r − 1, hence an isomorphism at ζ^i (surjective by Nakayama); base change to T(1) gives a T(1)-dévissage of ℳ(1) at every point above x with the α^i (i ≤ r − 1) still injective.

Let 𝒩̄^i, 𝒫̄^i, ℳ̄^i be the strict transforms along T(1) → T. By node devissage-torsion-lemma, (D̄¹, …, D̄^{r−1}) is a T(1)-dévissage in dimensions ≥ m + 1; 𝒩̄^r := g^r_*𝒫̄^{r−1} on Z^r is T(1)-flat in dimension ≥ m over U_0 (node devissage-flatness-criterion) and rig-flat in dimension ≥ n (node devissage-injectivity-and-rig-flatness), and Z^r → T is smooth with geometrically irreducible fibres of dimension m.

Node flattening-smooth-special-case gives an admissible blow-up T(2) → T(1) with centre in T(1)_0 ∖ U(1)_0 such that the strict transform of 𝒩̄^r (equal to the strict transform of 𝒩^r along T(2) → T; strict transforms compose, node admissible-blow-up) is T(2)-flat in dimension ≥ m.

Pull (D¹, …, D^{r−1}) back to T(2) (the α^i stay injective) and take strict transforms along T(2) → T to obtain a T(2)-dévissage of ℳ̄(2) (node devissage-torsion-lemma); the ϖ-torsion of 𝒩^r(2) is induced by that of 𝒩^{r−1}(2), hence by that of ℳ(2), so the strict transform of ℳ induces that of 𝒩^r, and node devissage-flatness-criterion shows ℳ̄(2) T(2)-flat in dimension ≥ m at x.
acceptance: For X = Spf O_K⟨ζ, ξ⟩/(ζξ − ϖ) → T = Spf O_K⟨ζ⟩, ℳ = O_X, n = 0, m = 1, T(1) = T and U_0 = T_0 ∖ {ζ = 0}: t is the point ζ = 0, x the generic point of the line ζ = 0 of X_0 (the one-dimensional non-flat locus), T(2) is the blow-up of (ζ, ϖ) with centre {t} outside U_0, and W_0 = T_0.

nodes.title: Lowering the dimension of the non-flat locus by one admissible blow-up (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Proposition 4.2)
nodes.statement: Let T be a quasi-compact admissible formal O_K-scheme, f: X → T a morphism of quasi-compact formal O_K-schemes locally of tf presentation, and ℳ a coherent O_X-module that is rig-flat over T in dimension ≥ n. Let m ≥ n be an integer such that ℳ is T-flat in dimension ≥ m + 1. There is an admissible blow-up T' → T such that the strict transform ℳ' of ℳ on X' = X ×_T T' is T'-flat in dimension ≥ m. Moreover, for any open U_0 ⊆ T_0 over which ℳ is T-flat in dimension ≥ m, the centre can be chosen disjoint from U_0.
hypotheses: X and T quasi-compact
m ≥ n
proofSteps: Start with T(1) = T and the given U_0 (possibly empty).

While U_0 ≠ T_0, node flattening-local-step gives an admissible blow-up with centre outside U_0 and an open W_0 ⊋ U_0 over which the strict transform is flat in dimension ≥ m; the composite with T(1) → T is an admissible blow-up of T whose centre avoids U_0 (node admissible-blow-up: composites of admissible blow-ups of the quasi-compact T, with centres avoiding U_0, Raynaud–Gruson 5.1.4).
T_0 is a noetherian topological space (node admissible-formal-scheme), so the strictly increasing chain of opens U_0 ⊊ W_0 ⊊ … stops, which happens only when W_0 = T_0.

nodes.title: Flattening a coherent module by an admissible blow-up of the base (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Theorem 4.1)
nodes.statement: Let T be a quasi-compact admissible formal O_K-scheme (K complete of rank one, not necessarily discretely valued), f: X → T a morphism of quasi-compact formal O_K-schemes locally of tf presentation, ℳ a coherent O_X-module and n ∈ ℕ such that ℳ is rig-flat over T in dimension ≥ n (node rig-flat-in-dimension). Then there is an admissible blow-up T' → T such that the strict transform ℳ' of ℳ on X' = X ×_T T' (node admissible-blow-up) is T'-flat in dimension ≥ n (node flat-in-dimension).
hypotheses: T quasi-compact admissible; X quasi-compact (Bosch–Lütkebohmert's standing assumption in §3) and locally of tf presentation, possibly with ϖ-torsion
The blow-up is of the base T, and ℳ' is the strict transform, not the pull-back
Classical rigid case only: Bosch–Lütkebohmert's noetherian base case uses parallel arguments that are not decomposed here
proofSteps: X is quasi-compact, so N := dim(X/T) = sup_x dim_x(X ⊗ k(f(x))) is finite and ℳ is T-flat in dimension ≥ N + 1 (node flat-in-dimension).

Descending induction on m from N to n: if the current strict transform is flat in dimension ≥ m + 1, node flattening-induction-step gives an admissible blow-up after which its strict transform is flat in dimension ≥ m. Rig-flatness in dimension ≥ n survives admissible blow-ups and passage to strict transforms (node rig-flat-in-dimension: invariance under admissible blow-ups; the strict transform differs from the pull-back by ϖ-power torsion, invisible at rig-points), strict transforms along composite blow-ups are iterated strict transforms, and composites of admissible blow-ups of the quasi-compact T are admissible blow-ups (node admissible-blow-up).

n > dim(X/T): nothing to do, T' = T.

nodes.title: Flattening by admissible blow-up (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Theorem 5.2)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of quasi-compact admissible formal O_K-schemes (K complete of rank one, not necessarily discretely valued; Bosch–Lütkebohmert work over an admissible quasi-compact base S, and an S-morphism is in particular a morphism over Spf O_K) and n ∈ ℕ. If f_rig is flat, i.e. O_X is rig-flat over Y at every rig-point (resp. f_rig is flat in dimension ≥ n, i.e. O_X is rig-flat over Y in dimension ≥ n; node rig-flat-in-dimension), there is an admissible blow-up Y' → Y such that the induced morphism f': X' → Y' is flat (resp. flat in dimension ≥ n; node flat-in-dimension), where X' is the strict transform of X: the closed formal subscheme of X ×_Y Y' defined by the ideal of sections supported over the centre, i.e. the strict transform of the module O_X (node admissible-blow-up). This is the case T = Y, ℳ = O_X of the module flattening theorem (node module-flattening-by-blow-up, Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Theorem 4.1).
hypotheses: X, Y quasi-compact admissible over Spf O_K; f_rig flat (resp. flat in dimension ≥ n) in the sense of rig-flatness at rig-points
The blow-up is of Y (the target), and X' is the strict transform, not the total transform
Classical rigid case: the base is Spf O_K; Bosch–Lütkebohmert's noetherian base case (II) is proved by parallel noetherian arguments that are not decomposed here
proofSteps: f_rig flat (resp. flat in dimension ≥ n) means that O_X is rig-flat over Y in dimension ≥ 0 (resp. ≥ n) (node rig-flat-in-dimension).
Node module-flattening-by-blow-up with T = Y and ℳ = O_X gives an admissible blow-up Y' → Y such that the strict transform of O_X on X ×_Y Y' is Y'-flat in dimension ≥ n (n = 0 in the flat case).

The strict transform of O_X is O_{X'} (node admissible-blow-up, strict transforms along base change), so f' is flat in dimension ≥ n; flatness in dimension ≥ 0 is flatness (node formal-flat-locus-open).
In the flat case X' is flat over the admissible Y', hence admissible.
acceptance: Y = Spf O_K⟨ζ⟩, X = Spf O_K⟨ζ, ξ⟩/(ζξ − ϖ): f_rig is the open immersion of the annulus {|ϖ| ≤ |ζ| ≤ 1} into the disc, hence flat, but f is not flat (ζ is a zero-divisor on the special fibre k[ζ, ξ]/(ζξ)); after blowing up (ζ, ϖ) on Y the strict transform of X maps isomorphically onto the chart {ζ generates} of Y', so f' is an open immersion, in particular flat.

nodes.title: Quasi-finite and bounded-fibre-dimension formal models (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Corollary 5.3)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of quasi-compact admissible formal O_K-schemes (K complete of rank one). (a) If all fibres of f_rig have dimension ≤ n (dim(X/Y)_rig ≤ n, node rig-flat-in-dimension), there is an admissible blow-up Y' → Y such that the induced f': X' → Y' (X' the strict transform) has relative dimension ≤ n: every fibre of f'_0: X'_0 → Y'_0 has dimension ≤ n. Dimensions of rigid fibres are taken at rig-points (node rig-flat-in-dimension)

For every formal point Spf V → Y' with V a complete valuation ring of height one (for instance the normalisation of a rig-point, node rig-point), the base change f'_V is flat in dimension ≥ n + 1 and its generic fibre has dimension ≤ n, so its special fibre has dimension ≤ n (Bosch–Lütkebohmert: 'as in [EGA IV_3, 14.3.10]', recorded gap).

Every closed point of Y'_0 is the special point of a rig-point (node rig-point, 3.5), so the fibres of f'_0 over closed points have dimension ≤ n; by upper semicontinuity of fibre dimension this holds over all points (recorded gap).

nodes.title: Formal completion of a scheme, the morphism σ: d(X̂) → X and the comparison φ: d(X̂) → X ×_Y d(Ŷ)
nodes.statement: (1.9.4) For a scheme X and its formal completion X̂ along a closed subscheme, assumed of type (S), there is a natural morphism of locally ringed spaces σ_X: d(X̂) → X, the unique one such that for every open U ⊆ X, with e = (X̂ → X) ∘ λ, one has e⁻¹(U) ⊆ σ⁻¹(U) and e* = σ* on O_X(U). (1.9.5) Let f: X → Y be locally of finite type between schemes, Y' ⊆ Y closed and defined by a quasi-coherent ideal of finite type, X' = X ×_Y Y', and X̂, Ŷ the completions along X' and Y'. If Ŷ is of type (S) then so is X̂, f̂ is adic, and the square formed by σ_X, σ_Y, d(f̂) and f induces a d(Ŷ)-morphism φ: d(X̂) → X ×_Y d(Ŷ) into the fibre product of a scheme locally of finite type with an adic space (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification). Proposition 1.9.6: (i) φ is a local isomorphism; (ii) if f is separated, φ is injective; (iii) if f is universally specializing (e.g. universally closed, e.g. proper), φ is surjective. Hence if f is separated and universally specializing, φ is an isomorphism. The source says 'One can easily prove' and gives no proof; the proofs below are supplied here.
hypotheses: X̂ (resp. Ŷ) of type (S); the ideal defining Y' of finite type; f locally of finite type
(ii) requires f separated; (iii) requires f universally specializing
σ and the fibre product X ×_Y d(Ŷ) come from Huber 1994 [Hu, 4.6.iv], [Hu4, 3.10.7] and [Hu, 3.8]; [Hu4] is not public
proofSteps: σ_X: glue the maps d(Spf Â) → Spec A over affine opens Spec A ⊆ X induced by A → Â → O⁺; uniqueness by the stated characterisation (Huber 1994 Remark 4.6(iv) in the noetherian case).
φ: universal property of X ×_Y d(Ŷ) (R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification).

(i) Local isomorphism: reduce to Y = Spec A, X = Spec B with B = A[T_1, …, T_n]/J and Ŷ = Spf Â of type (S)(b) with s ∈ Â; then X ×_Y d(Ŷ) is the increasing union over m of the affinoids Spa(Â(1/s)⟨s^m T⟩/J) (construction of [Hu, 3.8], R1), and d(X̂) = Spa(B̂(1/s), integral closure) is the member m = 0, i.e. the rational subset {|T_i| ≤ 1}; so φ is an open immersion on each affine chart of X̂.

(ii) Injectivity: if φ(x_1) = φ(x_2) = y, the centres of x_1, x_2 give two extensions Spec κ(y)⁺ → X of Spec κ(y) → X over Spec κ(y)⁺ → Y; separatedness gives uniqueness of such extensions (valuative criterion, mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated.valuativeCriterion), so x_1, x_2 lie in one affine chart, on which φ is injective by (i).

(iii) Surjectivity: for y ∈ X ×_Y d(Ŷ), its image in d(Ŷ) has a centre in Ŷ giving Spec κ(y)⁺ → Y; universal specialisation lifts the specialisation in X ×_Y Spec κ(y)⁺ from the generic point, giving an extension Spec κ(y)⁺ → X whose closed point lies over Y'; this defines a point of d(X̂) over y (universal property of d on the affine chart containing the centre).
Proper implies universally closed implies universally specializing (mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.UniversallyClosed.eq_valuativeCriterion); the source statement is used with this implication.
acceptance: For X = A¹_{O_K} → Y = Spec O_K (not proper), φ identifies d(X̂) with the closed unit disc inside the adic affine line over Spa(K, O_K): a local isomorphism which is injective but not surjective.
For X proper over Y, d(X̂) ≅ X ×_Y d(Ŷ).

Then the comparison map φ_X: d(X̂) → X_K^ad of node formal-completion-and-algebraic-comparison (with Y = Spec O_K, Y' = V(ϖ)) is an open embedding, whose image is the integral locus X_K^{ad,int} := {x ∈ X_K^ad : the morphism Spec κ(x) → X extends to Spec κ(x)⁺ → X}, κ(x) the completed residue field and κ(x)⁺ its valuation ring. Under φ_X the specialisation λ(x) ∈ X_s of x ∈ d(X̂) is the image of the closed point of that extension. If X is proper over O_K, φ_X is an isomorphism d(X̂) ≅ X_K^ad. A classical point of X_K^ad (residue field K' finite over K) lies in the integral locus iff it extends to an O_{K'}-point of X.

nodes.title: If the completion's generic fibre is all of the analytified generic fibre, a flat quasi-projective model is proper
nodes.statement: Let X be a quasi-projective O_K-scheme, flat and of finite type over O_K (hence of finite presentation). If φ_X: d(X̂) → X_K^ad is surjective, then X is proper over O_K. Flatness cannot be dropped: X = Spec O_K ⊔ A¹_{O_K/ϖ} is separated and of finite presentation, φ_X is an isomorphism (both sides are Spa(K, O_K)), and X is not proper.
hypotheses: X quasi-projective over O_K (for general separated X of finite type the compactification step needs Nagata's theorem over O_K, which this roadmap does not own)
X flat over O_K
proofSteps: Finite presentation: flat and of finite type over the domain O_K implies finitely presented (Fujiwara–Kato 0.9.2.3, after Raynaud–Gruson I (3.4.7)).

Compactify: X ⊆ P^N_{O_K} locally closed; let X̄ be the schematic closure of X_K in P^N_{O_K}. X̄ is projective and flat, X is open in X̄ (locally closed ⇒ open in its closure; X = closure of X_K ∩ X by flatness), and X̄_K ⊇ X_K is dense.

X̄ proper, so φ_X̄ is an isomorphism (node good-reduction-locus); by naturality φ_X = φ_X̄ restricted to d(X̂) = λ_X̄⁻¹(X_s) (generic fibre of an open formal subscheme). Surjectivity of φ_X gives X_K^ad = λ_X̄⁻¹(X_s), hence W^ad = λ_X̄⁻¹(Z) for W = X̄_K ∖ X_K and Z = X̄_s ∖ X_s (closed).

Z = ∅: otherwise take a closed point z ∈ Z and a rig-point of the completion of X̄ over z (node rig-point, 3.5); its classical point lies in the open tube ]Z[ (node tube), a nonempty open subset of X̄_K^ad contained in W^ad. But X_K is dense in X̄_K, so X_K^ad = q⁻¹(X_K) is dense in X̄_K^ad (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-constructible-closure), and its complement W^ad has empty interior: contradiction. (Alternatively: at a classical point, a non-zero-divisor vanishing on W would be nilpotent in the completed local ring, which is that of X̄_K by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-completed-local-rings.)

X_K = X̄_K: a classical point w ∈ X̄_K with residue field K' extends to Spec O_{K'} → X̄ (valuative criterion for X̄ proper); its special point lies in X̄_s = X_s ⊆ X, and Spec O_{K'} is local, so the whole O_{K'}-point lies in the open X, i.e. w ∈ X_K. Classical points are dense in the Jacobson scheme X̄_K, so W = ∅.
Hence X = X̄ as an open subscheme with the same points, so X is proper.
acceptance: X = P¹_{O_K} minus a closed point x of the special fibre: φ_X has image λ⁻¹(P¹_k ∖ {x}) = P^{1,ad}_K ∖ λ⁻¹(x) (λ⁻¹(x) is closed and strictly larger than the open residue disc ]x[), which is not all of X_K^ad = P^{1,ad}_K, and X is not proper — consistent with the lemma.

X = P¹_{O_K} ⊔ Spec K (Spec K = Spec O_K[1/ϖ] open in P⁰_{O_K}, so X is quasi-projective): flat, separated, of finite type, with proper generic fibre P¹_K ⊔ Spec K and proper special fibre P¹_k, but not proper; φ_X: d(X̂) = P^{1,ad}_K → P^{1,ad}_K ⊔ Spa(K, O_K) misses the extra point, as the lemma predicts.

nodes.title: Conrad's Berthelot-type functor (·)^rig on FS_C for arbitrary complete k
nodes.statement: Fix an adic noetherian ring C with a continuous map C → R to the valuation ring R of a complete nonarchimedean field k (no discreteness assumption on k; examples: C = R if k is discretely valued; C = R_0 a complete discrete valuation ring with R_0 → R local; C = Z discrete). FS_C is the category of locally noetherian formal schemes X over Spf C whose underlying reduced scheme is locally of finite type over C_red; affine opens have algebras that are quotients of C[[q_1, …, q_n]]{{T_1, …, T_m}} with the (I, q)-adic topology. For X in FS_C and a rigid space Z over k, Hom^cont_C(Z, X) is the set of morphisms of locally ringed G-topologised spaces whose ring maps are C-algebra maps landing in locally power-bounded sections and carrying locally topologically nilpotent sections to locally topologically nilpotent sections. Theorem 3.1.5: Hom^cont_C(·, X) is represented by a quasi-separated rigid space X^rig; (·)^rig takes open/closed immersions to open/closed immersions and open covers to admissible covers, commutes with fibre products (a), with analytic extension of k (b) and with change of C (c), preserves separatedness (d), and sends topologically finite type maps to quasi-compact maps (e). Spf(C[[q]])^rig is the open unit disc Δ = {|t| < 1}. Through AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor this gives an adic space r(X^rig) over Spa(k, R).
hypotheses: C adic noetherian with continuous C → R; k arbitrary complete nonarchimedean

Objects of FS_C are locally noetherian: the functor does not apply to non-noetherian formal O_K-models when k is not discretely valued (those are handled by nodes generic-fibre-functor-d and raynaud-generic-fibre)
Theorem 3.1.6 (preservation of finiteness, smoothness, properness, flatness, fibre dimension) is the separate node berthelot-rig-functor-preserves-properties
proofSteps: Δ → Spf(C[[q]]) pulling q back to the coordinate represents Spf(C[[q]])^rig, because Δ is admissibly covered by the discs Δ_r (r ∈ (0,1) ∩ √|k^×|) and topologically nilpotent elements of a k-affinoid have sup-norm < 1.
For X = Spf(C[[q]]{{T}}/J) take the zero locus of J in Δ^n × B^m (power-boundedness condition gives the B^m factor).
Localisation: (Spf A_{a})^rig is the locus where a is a unit with power-bounded inverse, via A_{a} ≅ A{{T}}/(1 − aT); so open immersions of formal affines give quasi-compact open immersions.
Glue over open covers, first for separated X then in general; deduce (a)–(e) from the construction.
acceptance: Spf(Z[[q]])^rig over any k (C = Z discrete) is the open unit disc over k.
When k is discretely valued and C = R the functor recovers de Jong's [deJ, 7.2.4, 7.2.6].

nodes.title: Conrad's scheme lemma: a flat, locally finitely presented, separated morphism with finite fibres of locally constant rank is finite
nodes.statement: Lemma A.1.4: a flat morphism of schemes f: X → Y that is locally of finite presentation is finite if and only if it is separated with finite fibres and its fibre rank y ↦ dim_{κ(y)} Γ(X_y, O) is locally constant on Y. No quasi-compactness and no noetherian hypothesis is needed.
hypotheses: f flat and locally of finite presentation
Uses [EGA IV_4 18.5.11(c)] (structure of separated locally quasi-finite maps over henselian local bases), unread

The reduction 'by fpqc base change we may assume Y henselian' uses fpqc descent of finiteness (of affineness, not only of module-finiteness) along Spec O^h_{Y,y} → Spec O_{Y,y}; Mathlib at the pin has only the ring-level RingHom.Finite.codescendsAlong_faithfullyFlat, so this is a further unread import (EGA IV_2 2.7.1) not listed in the packet gap
proofSteps: Only if: a finite flat locally finitely presented morphism is given by a locally free O_Y-algebra of finite rank.

If, local case: reduce to constant rank d; by fpqc base change assume Y = Spec of a henselian local ring; [EGA IV_4 18.5.11(c)] splits X = X' ⊔ X'' with X' → Y finite and X'' with empty closed fibre; X' is finite free of rank d' and d' = d from the closed fibre; so X' → X is an isomorphism on all fibres, hence an isomorphism.

If, general case: for y ∈ Y the base change to Spec O_{Y,y} is finite flat of rank d; choose a quasi-compact open U ⊆ X containing X ×_Y Spec O_{Y,y}; by finite presentation, U → Y is finite locally free of rank d over a neighbourhood of y, and U → X is an isomorphism on fibres there, hence an isomorphism.
acceptance: Over Y = Spec k[t], X = Spec k[t] ⊔ Spec k[t, t⁻¹] → Y is flat, separated, of finite presentation with finite fibres, but its fibre rank is 2 over t ≠ 0 and 1 over t = 0 (not locally constant) and it is not finite, as the lemma predicts.

nodes.title: Conrad's fibral finiteness criterion for flat rigid (adic) morphisms
nodes.statement: Theorem A.1.2: a flat map f: X → Y of rigid spaces over k (k complete nonarchimedean, not necessarily discretely valued) is finite if and only if it is quasi-compact and separated with finite fibres and locally constant fibre rank on Y. Through AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor the same holds for flat morphisms of quasi-separated adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(k, k°), with fibres and ranks taken at classical points.
hypotheses: f flat; quasi-compact; separated (quasi-separated is insufficient, cf. Remark A.1.3); finite fibres; fibre rank locally constant on Y
k arbitrary complete nonarchimedean; formal models over Spf R with R possibly non-noetherian
Quasi-compactness is necessary: {|t| = 1} ⊔ {|t| < 1} → {|t| ≤ 1} is a bijective local isomorphism, flat with fibres of rank 1, not finite
proofSteps: Only if: finite rigid maps are classified by coherent O_Y-algebras, locally free for flat f.
If: work locally on Y; assume X, Y quasi-compact separated and constant fibre rank d; choose a formal model f: X → Y (node raynaud-theorem (c),(e)).

f is separated (node formal-model-separatedness); after admissible blow-up of Y and strict transform f is quasi-finite (node quasi-finite-formal-model) and flat (node flattening-by-blow-up); base change and passage to closed formal subschemes keep quasi-finiteness and separatedness.

It suffices that each f_n = f mod ϖ^{n+1} is finite; each is quasi-finite, separated, flat and finitely presented, so by node fibral-finiteness-scheme-lemma it suffices that the special-fibre map f̄ has fibres of constant rank d.

The locus of fibres of a given rank is constructible ([EGA IV_3 9.8.8], unread), so it suffices to check closed points y_0; by node rig-point (Conrad A.1.5) pick Spf B → Y through y_0 with B finite flat local over R; T = X ×_Y Spf B is quasi-finite flat over Spf B with one-point special fibre, hence T = Spf C with C finite free of rank d' over B; C ⊗_R k is the affinoid algebra of f⁻¹(y_k), of rank d, so d' = d.
acceptance: A finite flat rigid map has locally constant fibre rank, and conversely under the stated hypotheses.
Over a discretely valued k the statement is Abbes–Mokrane Lemme A.1 with 'separated' in place of 'quasi-separated'.

nodes.title: Topological invariance of affinoidness and finiteness (Conrad A.1.1)
nodes.statement: A rigid space X over k is affinoid iff X_red is affinoid; hence a morphism f: Y → Z of rigid spaces is finite iff Y_red → Z_red is finite. Through AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor (affinoids correspond to affinoids, 1.1.11) the same holds for quasi-separated adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(k, k°). No Serre-type cohomological criterion is available: over every nonarchimedean k there is a quasi-compact separated surface with vanishing higher coherent cohomology that is not affinoid [Liu].
hypotheses: Rigid spaces over a complete nonarchimedean field k; no discreteness
Inputs [BGR 6.1.1/4, 7.3.5/3, 9.5.3/5] are unread (recorded gap)
proofSteps: i: Y_red → Y induces a bijection of admissible opens and admissible coverings (reduce to affinoid Y; Gerritzen–Grauert [BGR 7.3.5/3]: affinoid subdomains are finite unions of rational subdomains, whose defining inequalities lift through nil-thickenings).
Hence X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated when X_red is affinoid; induct on a nilpotent coherent ideal to the square-zero case X_0 = Sp A_0 ⊆ X.
A = O_X(X) is a k-Banach algebra of countable type (left exact Čech sequence over a finite affinoid cover); 0 → I → A → A_0 → 0 with I a finite A_0-module.

Lift topological generators of A_0 to power-bounded a_r ∈ A (power-boundedness is insensitive to nilpotents) and generators of I; [BGR 6.1.1/4] gives a surjection k⟨t, u⟩ → A, and ι: X → Sp A is a closed immersion by [BGR 9.5.3/5], hence an isomorphism.
Finiteness statement: f finite iff f is affinoid over affinoids with module-finite rings; both conditions are insensitive to nilpotents by the first part and Nakayama.

nodes.title: Smooth and étale morphisms of formal schemes locally of tf presentation; continuous differentials
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of formal O_K-schemes locally of tf presentation (for P7: O_K = W(κ), κ perfect). f is smooth at x ∈ X of relative dimension d if there are an open neighbourhood U of x and a Y-immersion j: U → D^n_Y = Spf O_Y⟨ζ_1, …, ζ_n⟩ such that, locally at j(x), the ideal of j(U) is generated by n − d sections g_{d+1}, …, g_n whose differentials are linearly independent in Ω¹_{D^n_Y/Y} ⊗ κ(j(x)); f is smooth if smooth at all points, and étale if smooth of relative dimension 0 (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Definition 1.1). Equivalently (II Lemma 1.2): f is flat at x and f_0: X_0 → Y_0 is smooth at x of relative dimension d; equivalently every reduction f_m: X_m → Y_m modulo ϖ^{m+1} is smooth at x of relative dimension d (Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth for schemes). Equivalently f is formally smooth and locally topologically of finite presentation, and then locally f factors as an étale morphism to D^d_Y. The module of continuous differentials Ω¹_{X/Y} := lim_m Ω¹_{X_m/Y_m} is coherent; for f smooth of relative dimension d it is locally free of rank d, with basis dT_1, …, dT_d on an étale chart X → D^d_Y. A formal scheme smooth over Spf O_K is admissible.
hypotheses: X, Y locally of tf presentation over O_K (K complete of rank one) or noetherian (Bosch–Lütkebohmert's case II)
Smoothness is a condition on all levels X_m, not on the generic fibre: d(f) smooth does not imply f smooth
proofSteps: Definition via local Jacobian presentations; equivalence with flatness plus smoothness of f_0, and with smoothness of all f_m, by the flatness criterion of node tfp-locality (Bosch–Lütkebohmert I 1.6) and the scheme case.

Local structure: the scheme-theoretic structure theorem for smooth morphisms gives étale coordinates on X_0 → Y_0, which lift to all X_m by the topological invariance of the étale site (node formal-etale-site-invariance), as in Conrad, genpaper, proof of Theorem 3.1.6 ([EGA IV_4 17.11.4, 18.4.5(ii), 18.1.2]).
Ω¹: each Ω¹_{X_m/Y_m} is locally free of rank d with compatible bases dT_i; the limit is locally free (mathlib KaehlerDifferential, Algebra.Smooth).
Admissibility: smooth over Spf O_K implies flat, hence ϖ-torsion-free.
acceptance: Spf O_K⟨T_1, …, T_d⟩ and the formal torus Spf O_K⟨T_1^{±1}, …, T_d^{±1}⟩ are smooth of relative dimension d with Ω¹ free on dT_i.

nodes.title: The étale site of a formal scheme is the étale site of its special fibre; the generic-fibre functor on étale objects
nodes.statement: Let 𝔛 be a formal O_K-scheme locally of tf presentation, 𝔛_m = 𝔛 ⊗ O_K/ϖ^{m+1}. (a) The functor 𝔜 ↦ 𝔜_0 is an equivalence from the category of formal schemes étale over 𝔛 (adic, locally tfp, each 𝔜_m → 𝔛_m étale) to the category of schemes étale over 𝔛_0; composing with the topological invariance for 𝔛_{s,red} ⊆ 𝔛_0, both are equivalent to schemes étale over 𝔛_{s,red}. The equivalence preserves fibre products, open immersions and jointly surjective families, so it is an equivalence of small étale sites 𝔛_ét ≃ (𝔛_0)_ét ≃ (𝔛_{s,red})_ét. (b) For 𝔜 → 𝔛 étale, d(𝔜) → d(𝔛) is an étale morphism of adic spaces (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/differentials-unramified-smooth-etale); d preserves fibre products (node generic-fibre-fibre-products); and if (𝔜_i → 𝔛) is a covering of 𝔛_ét then (d(𝔜_i) → d(𝔛)) is jointly surjective. Hence 𝔜 ↦ d(𝔜) is a continuous functor 𝔛_ét → d(𝔛)_ét, and O_{𝔛_ét}(𝔜) := Γ(𝔜, O_𝔜) is a sheaf on 𝔛_ét.
hypotheses: 𝔛 locally tfp over O_K (the same holds for adic noetherian formal schemes with an ideal of definition)
The étale site of the adic space d(𝔛) is AdicEtaleGeometry A1's; the morphism of topoi w: X_proét → 𝔛_ét is built by the consumer from the functor of (b)
proofSteps: Each 𝔛_m ⊆ 𝔛_{m+1} is a closed subscheme with the same underlying space; by Stacks Theorem 039R (EGA IV 18.1.2), 𝔜 ↦ 𝔜 ×_{𝔛_{m+1}} 𝔛_m is an equivalence of étale sites; so étale 𝔛_0-schemes lift uniquely to compatible systems (𝔜_m), whose colimit (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/colimit-of-thickenings) is a formal scheme adic and étale over 𝔛, and morphisms of étale formal 𝔛-schemes are compatible systems of morphisms of the levels (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-systems-equivalence-finite-ideal-type, applied over 𝔛 with ideal of definition ϖ·O_𝔛; 𝔛 need not be noetherian). The passage 𝔛_{s,red} ⊆ 𝔛_0 is the same theorem.
Fibre products and coverings: computed levelwise.

(b) Étaleness of d(𝔜) → d(𝔛): locally 𝔜_0 → 𝔛_0 is standard étale, A_0 → (A_0[T]_g/(h)) with h monic and h' invertible; lift h, g to A (039R) so that 𝔜 = Spf A⟨T, g⁻¹⟩/(h), whose generic fibre is A_K⟨T, g⁻¹⟩/(h) with h' a unit: a standard étale presentation (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-local-structure).

Joint surjectivity: for x ∈ d(𝔛) with λ(x) in the image of 𝔜_{i,s}, the ring C = B ⊗̂_A κ(x)⁺ is étale, hence flat, over the valuation ring κ(x)⁺ and has a prime over the closed point; by going-down it has a prime over the generic point, with residue field κ(y) finite separable over κ(x); a valuation ring of κ(y) dominating the local ring of C at the first prime restricts to κ(x)⁺ (valuation rings are maximal for domination), and defines a point y of d(Spf B) over x.
Sheaf property of 𝔜 ↦ Γ(𝔜, O_𝔜): levelwise étale descent for the quasi-coherent sheaves O_{𝔜_m} and passage to the limit.
acceptance: For 𝔛 = Spf Z_p⟨T⟩ the étale 𝔛-schemes correspond to étale F_p[T]-schemes; Spf Z_p⟨T, (T^{p−1} − 1)⁻¹⟩ corresponds to the open D(T^{p−1} − 1) ⊆ A¹_{F_p}.
The finite étale cover Spf W(F_{p²}) → Spf Z_p corresponds to Spec F_{p²} → Spec F_p, and its generic fibre is Spa(Q_{p²}) → Spa(Q_p), finite étale of degree 2.

nodes.title: Unique Frobenius lift on a formal scheme étale over the formal torus
nodes.statement: Let κ be a perfect field of characteristic p, W = W(κ) with Witt-vector Frobenius σ (mathlib WittVector.frobenius), and 𝕋^d = Spf W⟨T_1^{±1}, …, T_d^{±1}⟩ the formal torus. Let 𝔛 = Spf R be affine with an étale morphism 𝔛 → 𝕋^d, T_i ↦ T_i ∈ R. There is a unique ring endomorphism φ: R → R such that φ is σ-semilinear (φ(a·r) = σ(a)φ(r) for a ∈ W), φ(T_i) = T_i^p for all i, and φ(r) ≡ r^p mod pR for all r ∈ R. More generally: if A → R is a formally étale map of p-adically complete rings (étale modulo every p^m) and φ_A is a Frobenius lift on A, there is a unique Frobenius lift φ_R on R extending φ_A. Frobenius lifts are compatible with étale maps over 𝕋^d. In general a smooth formal scheme over W admits no global Frobenius lift; lifts exist on each open étale over a torus.
hypotheses: κ perfect of characteristic p; R p-adically complete, étale (levelwise) over W⟨T^{±1}⟩
Uniqueness uses p-adic completeness and formal unramifiedness
proofSteps: φ_0 on W⟨T^{±1}⟩: σ on coefficients and T_i ↦ T_i^p; it lifts Frobenius because σ lifts the Frobenius of κ and (Σ a_ν T^ν)^p ≡ Σ σ(a_ν) T^{pν} mod p.
Level 1: the absolute Frobenius F: R/p → R/p is a ring map compatible with φ_0 mod p on W⟨T^{±1}⟩/p.

Lift F to R → R/p^m for each m, over W⟨T^{±1}⟩ → R via φ_0, using formal étaleness of W⟨T^{±1}⟩/p^m → R/p^m and the nilpotent ideal pR/p^m (mathlib Algebra.FormallyEtale.iff_comp_bijective, applied iteratively to square-zero steps); uniqueness at each level by Algebra.FormallyUnramified.lift_unique, so the lifts are compatible in m.
Pass to the limit using p-adic completeness of R (IsAdicComplete) to get φ; uniqueness of φ from uniqueness at every level.
Compatibility with étale maps: both composites are Frobenius lifts extending φ_0, hence equal by uniqueness.
acceptance: On the torus itself φ(Σ a_ν T^ν) = Σ σ(a_ν) T^{pν}.
On 𝔛 = Spf W⟨T^{±1}, (T − 1)⁻¹⟩ (open in the torus), φ((T − 1)⁻¹) = (T^p − 1)⁻¹, which lies in R because T^p − 1 ≡ (T − 1)^p mod p is invertible.

nodes.title: The residue disc of a rational smooth point is an open unit polydisc
nodes.statement: Let 𝔛 be a formal O_K-scheme smooth of relative dimension d at a closed point x of the special fibre with residue field κ(x) = k (a k-rational point), and let t_1, …, t_d ∈ Γ(U, O_𝔛) on an open U ∋ x be local parameters at x: their reductions lie in m_{𝔛_s,x} and form a regular system of parameters of O_{𝔛_s,x}. Let ]x[ ⊆ d(𝔛) be the tube of {x} (node tube) and D^d_{<1} = ⋃_{m≥1} {|T_i|^m ≤ |ϖ| ∀i} ⊆ Spa(K⟨T⟩, O_K⟨T⟩) the open unit polydisc. Then t = (t_1, …, t_d): ]x[ → D^d_{<1} is an isomorphism of adic spaces. If t' is another system of local parameters at x, then t' = Φ(t) for an automorphism Φ of D^d_{<1} given by power series Φ_i ∈ O_K[[T_1, …, T_d]] with Φ(0) ∈ m_K^d and invertible linear part modulo m_K; for d = 1 and t, t' vanishing at a common K-point of ]x[, t' = u·t·(1 + h) with |u| = 1 and |h| < 1 on the disc. For a closed point x with residue field k' ⊋ k, ]x[ becomes, after base change to the unramified extension of K with residue field k', a disjoint union of [k':k] open polydiscs; ]x[ itself is in general a twisted form of D^d_{<1} and has no K-rational point.
hypotheses: 𝔛 smooth over Spf O_K of relative dimension d near x (node smooth-formal-scheme); K complete of rank one
x a k-rational closed point for the isomorphism with D^d_{<1}
proofSteps: Choose an affine neighbourhood Spf A of x on which g = (t_1, …, t_d): Spf A → D^d = Spf O_K⟨T⟩ is étale (node smooth-formal-scheme: parameters give étale coordinates) and, shrinking, g_s⁻¹(0) = {x} (étale implies quasi-finite).
Tubes: ]x[ = d(g)⁻¹(]0[) because g_s⁻¹(0) = {x} (node tube, functoriality), and ]0[ = D^d_{<1}.

For each m ≥ 1 put B_m = O_K⟨T, S⟩/(T_i^m − ϖS_i), a formal model of {|T_i|^m ≤ |ϖ|}. The base change A ⊗̂_{O_K⟨T⟩} B_m → B_m is étale; on special fibres it is (A_0/(t^m))[S] → (k[T]/(T^m))[S], and A_0/(t^m) ≅ k[T]/(T^m) since g_0 is étale at x, g_0⁻¹(0) = {x} and κ(x) = k. An étale morphism inducing an isomorphism on special fibres is an isomorphism on every level (node formal-etale-site-invariance), hence an isomorphism of formal schemes; taking generic fibres, t maps {|t_i|^m ≤ |ϖ|} ∩ d(Spf A) isomorphically onto {|T_i|^m ≤ |ϖ|}.
Take the union over m.

Change of parameters: t'_i restricted to ]x[ ≅ D^d_{<1} is a bounded function on the open polydisc whose reduction vanishes at 0, hence Φ_i ∈ O_K[[T]] with Φ_i(0) ∈ m_K; its linear part is invertible mod m_K because both are regular parameter systems; Φ is invertible by the same argument applied to t.

Non-rational points: base change to the unramified extension K' (residue field k') splits x into [k':k] rational points (node generic-fibre-fibre-products (b) and the splitting of κ(x) ⊗_k k'); Conrad, Several approaches Example 5.2.5 for the disc.

Consistency with the Berthelot-type functor: for K discretely valued ]x[ = (Spf Ô_{𝔛,x})^rig with Ô_{𝔛,x} ≅ O_K[[t_1, …, t_d]] (node berthelot-type-rig-functor-nonnoetherian-base: Spf(C[[q]])^rig is the open disc).
acceptance: For K discretely valued and a smooth proper curve X over O_K with x ∈ X_k(k), a local parameter at a lift of x identifies ]x[ with the open unit disc (ColemanIntegration request).

Non-example: for K = Q_p and x ∈ P¹_{F_p} the closed point T² = 2 (p odd, 2 a non-square mod p), ]x[ has no Q_p-point and is not isomorphic to the open unit disc over Q_p; over Q_{p²} it splits into two open unit discs.

nodes.title: Fractional valuation bounds |f| ≤ |g|^q and |f| ≥ |g|^q for q ∈ ℚ_{≥0}
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative ring, f, g ∈ A and q ∈ ℚ_{≥0}. For v ∈ Spv A write q = a/b with a ∈ ℕ, b ∈ ℕ_{>0}, and define |f(v)| ≤ |g(v)|^q to mean v(f^b) ≤ v(g^a) (the valuative relation f^b ≤_v g^a), and |f(v)| ≥ |g(v)|^q to mean v(f^b) ≥ v(g^a); strict versions likewise. This does not depend on the representative (a, b) of q, because x ↦ x^n is strictly increasing on a totally ordered value monoid. Put fracPowLE f g q := {v ∈ Spv A : v(f^b) ≤ v(g^a)} and fracPowGE f g q := {v : v(f^b) ≥ v(g^a)}. No element 'g^q' of A (or of the base field) is used: when K = Q_p, |p|^{1/2} is not the absolute value of any element of K, yet {|f| ≤ |p|^{1/2}} is defined. Second convention, compatible with the first: if B is an A⁺-algebra containing c and a unit u of B⁺ with c^b = g^a u (e.g. c = ϖ^{a/b} ∈ L = K(ϖ^{1/b}), or c = p^ε ∈ Z_p^cycl of p-adic valuation ε), then for v ∈ Spa(B, B⁺) one has |f(v)| ≤ |g(v)|^q ⟺ v(f) ≤ v(c). When g is a unit (e.g. g = ϖ in a Tate ring), fracPowLE f g q ∩ Spa(A, A⁺) is the rational subset R({f^b, g^a}/g^a) and fracPowGE f g q ∩ Spa(A, A⁺) is R({g^a, f^b}/f^b).
hypotheses: A arbitrary commutative ring for the definition; A Huber, g a unit, for the rational-subset descriptions
q ∈ ℚ_{≥0}; the representative (a, b) is arbitrary with b > 0
The threshold |g|^q is realised by an element only after an explicit extension (second convention)
proofSteps: Independence: if a/b = a'/b', then v(f^b) ≤ v(g^a) ⟺ v(f^{bb'}) ≤ v(g^{ab'}) = v(g^{a'b}) ⟺ v(f^{b'}) ≤ v(g^{a'}), using that n-th powers are strictly monotone on the value group with zero of a valuative relation (mathlib ValuativeRel; points of TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum are valuative relations).

Rational-subset descriptions: with g a unit, g^a generates the unit ideal, so the numerator sets {f^b, g^a} and {g^a, f^b} satisfy Wedhorn's openness condition; membership unfolds by TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.mem_rationalSubset_iff (for ≥, v(f^b) ≥ v(g^a) ≠ 0 gives v(f^b) ≠ 0).
Second convention: v(c^b) = v(g^a) v(u) = v(g^a) since u, u⁻¹ ∈ B⁺ force v(u) = 1; then v(f^b) ≤ v(c^b) ⟺ v(f) ≤ v(c) by monotonicity of b-th powers.
Unit invariance: for u with u, u⁻¹ ∈ A⁺, v(uf) = v(f) on Spa(A, A⁺) (TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset_image_mul_right for the rational form).
acceptance: {|T| ≤ |p|^{1/2}} ⊆ Spa(Q_p⟨T⟩, Z_p⟨T⟩) is {|T²| ≤ |p|}; its Q_p-rational points are those with |T| ≤ |p|, while its points over Q_p(√p) include T = √p.

nodes.title: The domain {|s| ≥ |ϖ|^q} cut out by a section of an invertible sheaf on a formal model
nodes.statement: Let 𝔛 be an admissible formal O_K-scheme, ℒ an invertible O_𝔛-module, s ∈ Γ(𝔛, ℒ) and q ∈ ℚ_{≥0}. Choose an open cover 𝔛 = ⋃ U_j by formal affines U_j = Spf A_j with generators ℒ|_{U_j} = O e_j, and write s|_{U_j} = f_j e_j. Define 𝔛_η(|s| ≥ |ϖ|^q) := ⋃_j (fracPowGE f_j ϖ q ∩ d(U_j)) ⊆ d(𝔛), and likewise 𝔛_η(|s| ≤ |ϖ|^q) with fracPowLE. These sets do not depend on the cover or the generators: on U_j ∩ U_k one has e_k = u e_j with u ∈ O(U_j ∩ U_k)^×, so f_j = u f_k, and |u(x)| = 1 on d(U_j ∩ U_k) because u, u⁻¹ ∈ O ⊆ O⁺. They are open (finite unions of rational subsets when 𝔛 is quasi-compact) and functorial under pull-back. Independence of lifts: if s' ∈ Γ(𝔛, ℒ) with s − s' ∈ ϖ^c ℒ for some c ∈ ℚ with c > q (ϖ^c ℒ meaning sections whose local coordinates satisfy |·| ≤ |ϖ|^c), then 𝔛_η(|s| ≥ |ϖ|^q) = 𝔛_η(|s'| ≥ |ϖ|^q); hence a section s̄ of ℒ ⊗ O_K/ϖ^m (m > q) determines a well-defined domain 𝔛_η(|s̄| ≥ |ϖ|^q) through arbitrary local lifts. The domain depends on the integral structure ℒ, not only on the invertible sheaf ℒ_η on d(𝔛).
hypotheses: 𝔛 admissible (the construction works verbatim for 𝔛 of type (S) with ϖ replaced by s)
ℒ invertible on the formal model; s a global section (or local lifts of a section modulo ϖ^m with m > q)
q ∈ ℚ_{≥0}, interpreted by node fractional-valuation-bound
proofSteps: Local definition via node fractional-valuation-bound; on a trivialising affine it is the rational subset R({ϖ^a, f^b}/f^b) (fracPowGE_inter_spa).
Independence of generators: ValuationSpectrum.fracPowGE_mul_unit with u a unit of the formal model's ring, whose image lies in the plus ring of the generic fibre (node generic-fibre-functor-d).
Gluing: the local sets agree on overlaps by independence, so their union is well defined.

Independence of lifts: |s(x) − s'(x)| ≤ |ϖ(x)|^c < |ϖ(x)|^q, so by the ultrametric inequality |s(x)| ≥ |ϖ(x)|^q iff |s'(x)| ≥ |ϖ(x)|^q (compare the b-th powers after writing q, c over a common denominator).
Functoriality: pull back generators along g: 𝔜 → 𝔛 and use comap_fracPowLE / comap for GE.
q = 0: |f_j| ≥ 1 iff |f_j| = 1 iff λ(x) ∉ V(f̄_j) (node specialisation-map), so the domain is the tube of the open 𝔛_s ∖ V(s̄).
acceptance: For 𝔛 = P̂¹_{O_K}, ℒ = O(1), s = T_0: 𝔛_η(|s| ≥ |ϖ|^q) is P^{1,ad}_K minus the open disc {|z| < |ϖ|^q} around z = T_0/T_1 = 0.

nodes.title: Formal model of a section domain: the open chart of the admissible blow-up of (s, c)
nodes.statement: Let 𝔛 be an admissible formal O_K-scheme, ℒ invertible, s ∈ Γ(𝔛, ℒ), and c ∈ O_K ∖ {0} (the threshold, e.g. c = ϖ^a, or c = p^ε when K contains such an element; for a fractional q = a/b without such an element use (s^{⊗b}, ϖ^a) in ℒ^{⊗b}). Let 𝒜 ⊆ O_𝔛 be the coherent open ideal locally generated by (f_j, c) where s = f_j e_j (independent of generators), and let 𝔛(|s| ≥ |c|) ⊆ Bl_𝒜 𝔛 be the open formal subscheme where s generates 𝒜O. Locally, over U = Spf A with ℒ|_U = Ae and s = fe, 𝔛(|s| ≥ |c|) ×_𝔛 U = Spf(A⟨u⟩/(fu − c) modulo ϖ-torsion), with u ∈ Γ(ℒ⁻¹) the section with u·s = c. Universal property: for a ϖ-torsion-free formal scheme Z over Spf O_K with g: Z → 𝔛, lifts of g to 𝔛(|s| ≥ |c|) correspond bijectively to sections u ∈ Γ(Z, g*ℒ⁻¹) with u·g*s = c (such u is unique if it exists). Generic fibre: d(𝔛(|s| ≥ |c|)) → d(𝔛) is an open immersion with image {x : |s(x)| ≥ |c(x)|} = sectionDomainGE s q when |c| = |ϖ|^q. Change of lift: if s' = s + c' t with c' ∈ c·m_K (so |c'| < |c|) and t ∈ Γ(𝔛, ℒ), the models for s and s' are canonically isomorphic over 𝔛 via u' = u(1 + (c'/c) u t)⁻¹, compatibly with the equality of generic-fibre domains; if c'' = wc with w ∈ O_K^×, the models for c and c'' are isomorphic via u'' = wu. Flatness: if f̄ is a non-zero-divisor on A/ϖ and c ∈ m_K (or c a unit), A⟨u⟩/(fu − c) is already ϖ-torsion-free.
hypotheses: 𝔛 admissible; ℒ invertible; c ∈ O_K nonzero, so 𝒜 ⊇ c O_𝔛 is open
The model is an open formal subscheme of an admissible blow-up, not the blow-up itself: its generic fibre is the domain {|s| ≥ |c|}, not d(𝔛)
proofSteps: 𝒜 is coherent and open (it contains c, and ϖ^N ∈ cO_K for N ≫ 0); independence of generators since (uf, c) = (f, c) for units u.
Chart: node admissible-blow-up (a) with generators f_0 = f, f_1 = c gives the chart where f generates: A⟨ζ⟩/(fζ − c) modulo ϖ-torsion, ζ = u.

Universal property: from node admissible-blow-up (c): on torsion-free Z, 𝒜O_Z invertible and generated by s iff c ∈ g*s·O_Z, i.e. iff u exists; uniqueness since Z has no ϖ-torsion and g*s is then a non-zero-divisor.

Generic fibre: node generic-fibre-inverts-admissible-blow-ups identifies the chart's generic fibre with the rational subset R({f, c}/f) = {|f| ≥ |c|} (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spaLocalizationHomeomorph), equal to sectionDomainGE by node section-valuation-domain.

Change of lift: u s = c implies u s' = c(1 + (c'/c) u t) and 1 + (c'/c)ut is a unit since c'/c ∈ m_K is topologically nilpotent; uniqueness from the universal property (Scholze's Lemma III.2.13 argument).

Flatness: work modulo c (a pseudo-uniformiser when c ∈ m_K; the c-adic and ϖ-adic topologies agree). Since A is ϖ-torsion-free and f̄ is a non-zero-divisor on A/ϖ, f is a non-zero-divisor on A/cA (if fx ∈ cA and |c| ≥ |ϖ| then f(ϖ/c)x ∈ ϖA gives (ϖ/c)x ∈ ϖA and x ∈ cA; for |c| < |ϖ| use A/ϖ^k by induction). Hence fu − c ≡ fu is a non-zero-divisor on (A/c)[u], and the flatness criterion modulo c^m (node tfp-locality) shows that A⟨u⟩/(fu − c) is O_K-flat (Scholze Lemma III.2.10, first assertion). For c a unit, fu − c is already a unit multiple of a monic in u modulo m_K. (Reducing modulo ϖ, as previously written, only works when ϖ ∈ cO_K.)
acceptance: 𝔛 = Spf O_K⟨T⟩, ℒ = O, s = T, c = ϖ: the model is Spf O_K⟨T, u⟩/(Tu − ϖ), with generic fibre the annulus {|ϖ| ≤ |T| ≤ 1}.
Scholze's X*(ε) → X* for the Hasse invariant (Lemma III.2.13) is this construction with ℒ = ω^{⊗(p−1)}, s = H̃a, c = p^ε.

nodes.title: Hasse domains X(ε) = {|Ha| ≥ |p|^ε} and their formal models
nodes.statement: Let p be a prime, K a complete extension of Q_p (|p| = p⁻¹), 𝔛 an admissible formal O_K-scheme, ω an invertible O_𝔛-module, and Ha ∈ Γ(𝔛 ⊗_{O_K} O_K/p, ω^{⊗(p−1)}) a section (the Hasse invariant; for modular curves and Shimura varieties it is supplied by the moduli roadmaps). For ε ∈ ℚ with 0 ≤ ε < 1 the Hasse domain is X(ε) := 𝔛_η(|Ha| ≥ |p|^ε) ⊆ d(𝔛), the section domain (node section-valuation-domain) of any local lift H̃a of Ha to ω^{⊗(p−1)}, with the fractional convention of node fractional-valuation-bound; it is well defined because two lifts differ by p·(section) and |p| < |p|^ε for ε < 1. If O_K contains an element p^ε of p-adic valuation ε (an explicitly chosen element; for instance the completion of Q_p(μ_{p^∞}) contains such elements for every ε ∈ (1/(p−1))·ℤ[1/p]), the formal model 𝔛(ε) := 𝔛(|H̃a| ≥ |p^ε|) (node section-domain-formal-model) is independent of the local lift up to canonical isomorphism — equivalently it represents, on p-adically complete flat O_K-algebras S, pairs (g: Spf S → 𝔛, u ∈ Γ(Spf S, g*ω^{⊗(1−p)})) with u·Ha(ḡ) = p^ε in S/p, modulo u ~ u(1 + p^{1−ε}h) — and d(𝔛(ε)) = X(ε). X(0) = {|Ha| = 1} is the tube of the ordinary locus 𝔛_s ∖ V(Ha). Formation of X(ε) and 𝔛(ε) commutes with pull-back along morphisms 𝔜 → 𝔛 (with the pulled-back ω and Ha) and with base change along complete extensions of K.
hypotheses: K complete over Q_p; 𝔛 admissible over O_K; ω invertible; Ha a section of ω^{⊗(p−1)} modulo p
0 ≤ ε < 1 (for ε = 1 the domain depends on the lift)
The formal model needs an element p^ε ∈ O_K; otherwise use the fractional-bound domain on the generic fibre or pass to an explicit extension
proofSteps: X(ε): node section-valuation-domain with ℒ = ω^{⊗(p−1)}, s = any local lift and the pseudouniformiser ϖ = p of K, so that |H̃a| ≥ |p|^ε means |H̃a^b| ≥ |p^a| for ε = a/b (node fractional-valuation-bound); lift independence is sectionDomainGE_congr with c = 1 > ε.

𝔛(ε): node section-domain-formal-model with c = p^ε; lift independence from sectionDomainModel_isoOfLift with c' = p (p/p^ε = p^{1−ε} ∈ m_K); the functorial description is the universal property (Scholze, Definition III.2.12 and Lemma III.2.13).
d(𝔛(ε)) = X(ε): sectionDomainModel_genericFibre.
X(0): sectionDomainGE_zero.
Pull-back and base change: sectionDomainGE_preimage, node generic-fibre-fibre-products (b), and the universal property of the model.
acceptance: Toy case 𝔛 = Spf Z_p⟨T⟩, ω = O, Ha = T mod p, ε = 1/2: X(1/2) = {|T²| ≥ |p|}; over O_K = Z_p[√p] the model is Spf O_K⟨T, u⟩/(Tu − √p).
For the modular curve (Γ(N), N ≥ 3) with ω the Hodge bundle, X(ε) is BHW's ε-nearly ordinary locus X*(ε), and 𝔛(ε) is the canonical formal model of BHW Definition 4.1.

nodes.title: Transition maps between Hasse domains as the radius changes
nodes.statement: In the situation of node hasse-domain, let 0 ≤ ε' ≤ ε < 1. (a) X(ε') ⊆ X(ε) is an open immersion of adic spaces; X(ε') is a rational subset of X(ε) on every affine chart. (b) If c_ε, c_{ε'} ∈ O_K are chosen elements of valuations ε, ε' (so c_ε/c_{ε'} ∈ O_K), there is a unique morphism of formal models ι_{ε',ε}: 𝔛(ε') → 𝔛(ε) over 𝔛 with u = (c_ε/c_{ε'})·u', inducing the inclusion (a) on generic fibres. (c) ι_{ε,ε} = id and ι_{ε',ε} ∘ ι_{ε'',ε'} = ι_{ε'',ε} for ε'' ≤ ε' ≤ ε, and the ι are compatible with the lift-change isomorphisms. (d) The open set X(<ε) := ⋃_{ε'<ε, ε' ∈ ℚ} X(ε') is the interior of the set {x : |Ha(x)| > |p(x)|^ε}; the two sets have the same classical points, and they differ by higher-rank points x with |Ha(x)| infinitesimally larger than |p(x)|^ε; under R1's r, X(<ε) corresponds to Conrad's admissible open {h > |p|^ε} with its admissible cover by the X(ε'). (e) For every ε > 0, the closure of X(0) in d(𝔛) is contained in X(ε).
hypotheses: 0 ≤ ε'' ≤ ε' ≤ ε < 1; chosen elements c_ε ∈ O_K of valuation ε for the formal statements (b),(c)
proofSteps: (a): sectionDomainGE_mono (node section-valuation-domain), and on a trivialising affine a rational subset of a rational subset is rational (anchor Layer 2).
(b): node section-domain-formal-model, sectionDomainModel_mapOfDvd with c = c_{ε'}, c' = c_ε (c_{ε'} ∣ c_ε).
(c): (c_ε/c_{ε'})(c_{ε'}/c_{ε''}) = c_ε/c_{ε''} and uniqueness in the universal property; compatibility with lift changes by uniqueness.

(d): each X(ε') with ε' < ε is an open subset of {|Ha| > |p|^ε}, so X(<ε) lies in the interior. Conversely, if a rational affinoid neighbourhood W of x lies in {|H̃a| > |p|^ε} (with H̃a^b, p^a for ε = a/b), then H̃a is invertible on W and the maximum of |p^a/H̃a^b| on W (spectral seminorm, attained on rank-one points) is < 1, so |H̃a^{b'}| ≥ |p^{a'}| on W for some rational a'/b' < ε. Classical points have rank-one valuations, for which > |p|^ε implies ≥ |p|^{ε'} for some ε' < ε by density of ℚ in ℝ.

(e): if y ∉ X(ε), then |Ha(y)| < |p(y)|^ε ≤ |p(y)|^{ε'''} for a rational 0 < ε''' < ε, and the rational neighbourhood {|H̃a^{b}| ≤ |p^{a}|} (ε''' = a/b) of y is disjoint from X(0) = {|Ha| = 1}; so y is not in the closure of X(0).
acceptance: Conrad's admissible cover of S^{>h_0} by the S^{≥h}, h ∈ (h_0, 1), is (d) in the elliptic case.

nodes.title: Conrad's Hasse-invariant loci S^{>h}, S^{≥h} of a generalized elliptic curve are admissible opens
nodes.statement: For a generalized elliptic curve E → S over a rigid space S over k (k complete over Q_p, |p| = p⁻¹), the Hasse invariant of a fibre E_s is h(E_s) = max(|a|, 1/p) ∈ [1/p, 1] (Definition B.3.3: a lifts the coefficient of X^p in [p]*(X) mod p on the formal group of a semistable model). The loci S^{>h} (h ∈ [1/p, 1) ∩ √|k^×|) and S^{≥h} (h ∈ (1/p, 1] ∩ √|k^×|) of points with h(E_s) > h (resp. ≥ h) are admissible opens; their formation commutes with base change on S and, for quasi-separated or pseudo-separated S (Conrad 4.1.1(2)), with analytic extension of k; S^{≥h} → S is quasi-compact; and {S^{≥h}}_{h ∈ (h_0,1)} is an admissible cover of S^{>h_0}. Local description: on a formal affine Spf A of the formal completion M̂ of the proper moduli scheme M over which e*Ω̂¹ is trivial, with Γ_A ≅ Spf A[[X]] the formal group and a_{Γ_A} the coefficient of X^p in [p]*(X), S^{>h} ∩ (Spf A)^rig = {|a_{Γ_A}| > h} and S^{≥h} ∩ (Spf A)^rig = {|a_{Γ_A}| ≥ h}, independent of the coordinate X. Thresholds h ∈ √|k^×| are read with the convention of node fractional-valuation-bound. Through R1's comparison r these are opens of the adic space, and for h = |p|^ε with 0 ≤ ε < 1 (so h ∈ (1/p, 1]) S^{≥h} is the Hasse domain X(ε) of node hasse-domain for ω the Hodge bundle and Ha the Hasse invariant (a ≡ Ha in the trivialisation of ω by the dual of dX).
hypotheses: k complete nonarchimedean of residue characteristic p, analytic over Q_p

E → S a generalized elliptic curve over a rigid space; the reduction to the universal case uses the analytified moduli (Conrad Theorem 3.2.3) and fpqc descent of admissible opens ([C3, 4.2.4, 4.2.7]), not read
M̂^rig ≅ M^an_k and Ê^rig ≅ E^an_k use properness (node good-reduction-locus)
proofSteps: fpqc descent of admissible opens and of 'open immersion' and 'quasi-compact' reduces to the universal Γ(N)- or Γ_1(N)-structure over the proper finitely presented R-scheme M ([C3, 4.2.4, 4.2.7], Theorem 3.2.3 — unread imports).
Properness: M̂ generic fibre = M^an_k and Ê generic fibre = E^an_k (node good-reduction-locus).

On Spf A with e*Ω̂¹ trivial, write Γ_A ≅ Spf A[[X]]; for h in the stated ranges the locus |a_{Γ_A}| > h (≥ h) is independent of X (change of coordinate multiplies a by a unit modulo p and h > 1/p = |p| absorbs the ambiguity; node section-valuation-domain, lift independence).

By node rig-point (Conrad A.1.5) every point s of M^an_k is ŝ^rig for A → R_0 into the valuation ring of a finite extension; E_s has semistable reduction with formal group the completion of Ê_ŝ, so h(E_s) = max(1/p, |a_{Γ_A}(s)|) (Definition B.3.3).

Hence S^{>h} ∩ (Spf A)^rig = {|a_{Γ_A}| > h}, an admissible open (a union of rational domains for thresholds in √|k^×|), and similarly for ≥; quasi-compactness and the cover statement follow from the local description (node hasse-domain-transition-maps (d)).
Comparison with the Hasse domain: [KM 12.4.4] and the Serre–Tate/Verschiebung description a ≡ Ha (Conrad Remark B.3.4 and B.3) — unread import.
acceptance: {h(E) = 1} is the locus of potentially ordinary or potentially toric reduction; h(E) < 1 iff potentially supersingular reduction (Conrad after Remark B.3.4).
S^{≥h} → S is quasi-compact for non-strict inequalities.

nodes.title: The sheaf M̃ = M ⊗ 𝒪_X associated with a finite module on a noetherian affinoid
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) is a Huber pair with A complete and Hausdorff, and A is of one of Huber's two noetherian types: (I) A has a noetherian ring of definition, or (II) A is a strongly noetherian Tate ring (TauCeti.Huber.IsStronglyNoetherian: every A⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩ is noetherian), let X = Spa(A, A⁺) and let M be a finitely generated A-module. The associated presheaf M̃ (Huber's M ⊗ 𝒪_A) is the presheaf of topological 𝒪_X-modules on X defined on the rational basis by M̃(U) = M ⊗_A 𝒪_X(U) for U = R(T/s), where 𝒪_X(U) = A⟨T/s⟩ is the complete rational localisation of anchor Layer 3.1 and the ordinary (uncompleted) tensor product carries its natural 𝒪_X(U)-module topology (the quotient topology along any surjection 𝒪_X(U)ⁿ ↠ M ⊗_A 𝒪_X(U)); the restriction for rational V ⊆ U is id_M ⊗ ρ_{V,U}. On an arbitrary open W ⊆ X, M̃(W) = lim M̃(V) over the rational V ⊆ W, with the inverse-limit topology. An A-linear map φ : M → N induces φ̃ : M̃ → Ñ, functorially. Convention: the tensor product is not completed; for finite M over these rings M ⊗_A 𝒪_X(U) is already complete and equals the completed tensor product (Huber Lemmas 2.3(iii), 2.4(ii)), and the construction is only made for finitely generated M.
hypotheses: A complete and Hausdorff; A has a noetherian ring of definition or is a strongly noetherian Tate ring
A⁺ ⊆ A a ring of integral elements (anchor Layer 0.2)
M a finitely generated A-module
proofSteps: On rational subsets: for U = R(T/s), set M̃(U) = M ⊗_A A⟨T/s⟩; independence of the presentation (T, s) is transported along the canonical isomorphisms between localisations of two presentations of the same rational subset (anchor Layer 3.1).

Topology: 𝒪_X(U) is complete noetherian (type II: rational localisations of strongly noetherian Tate rings are strongly noetherian, tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.isStronglyNoetherian_completion; type I: 𝒪_X(U) again has a noetherian ring of definition, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-rod-sheafy (a), Huber 1994 before (1.4)); the natural topology on the finite module M ⊗_A 𝒪_X(U) is its module topology (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isModuleTopology in type II; Huber Lemma 2.3 in type I), complete and Hausdorff with every submodule closed (type II: tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isClosed_of_isNoetherian, which is stated over a complete Tate ring only; type I: AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-rod-module-complete, Huber Lemma 2.3(ii)).
Restriction maps id_M ⊗ ρ_{V,U} are continuous because every A-linear map of finite modules with module topologies is continuous; the cocycle identities are those of 𝒪_X (anchor Layer 3.3).

Extension to all opens by the limit over rational subsets, exactly as for 𝒪_X in anchor Layer 3.3; the two definitions agree on rational subsets because the rational subsets contained in a rational U are cofinal and U is one of them.
Functoriality: φ ⊗ id on rational subsets, compatible with restriction.
acceptance: For A = K⟨T⟩ over a complete nonarchimedean field K and M = A/(T), M̃(U) = 𝒪_X(U)/T·𝒪_X(U) on every rational U; on U = {|T| ≥ 1} it is 0.
For M = A, Ã is the structure presheaf 𝒪_X itself.
For finite M the natural map M ⊗_A 𝒪_X(U) → M ⊗̂_A 𝒪_X(U) is a topological isomorphism (Huber Lemma 2.3(iii)).

uses.how: the sheaf and acyclicity theorem is stated for M ⊗ 𝒪_A, so the object must exist with its topology
M̃ is the functor whose essential image is the coherent sheaves (Kiehl) and whose Čech cohomology is computed

nodes.title: Tate acyclicity for finite modules over a strongly noetherian Tate affinoid
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) is a Huber pair with A a complete Hausdorff strongly noetherian Tate ring and A⁺ a ring of integral elements, X = Spa(A, A⁺) and M a finite A-module. Then: (i) for every rational subset U ⊆ X and every finite covering 𝔘 of U by rational subsets, the augmented alternating Čech complex 0 → M̃(U) → ∏ M̃(U_i) → ∏ M̃(U_i ∩ U_j) → ⋯ is exact and all its differentials are strict; (ii) M̃ is a sheaf of complete Hausdorff topological 𝒪_X-modules; (iii) Hⁱ(U, M̃) = 0 for i > 0 and H⁰(U, M̃) = M ⊗_A 𝒪_X(U) for every rational U. In particular M̃(X) = M.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) is a Huber pair with A a complete Hausdorff strongly noetherian Tate ring and A⁺ a ring of integral elements
M finitely generated
Hⁱ is sheaf cohomology of the underlying abelian sheaf on the topological space U
proofSteps: Intersections of rational subsets are rational (anchor Layer 2.2), so for a finite rational covering the Čech complex of M̃ is M ⊗_A Č(𝔘, 𝒪_X) termwise (finite products commute with ⊗).
Č(𝔘, 𝒪_X) augmented is exact in all degrees for every finite rational covering of every rational subset (anchor Layer 4.1 conclusion, imported).
Each 𝒪_X(V), V rational, is flat over A (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.flat_toCompletionLoc), so M ↦ Č(𝔘, M̃) is exact (mathlib:Module.Flat.lTensor_exact).

Choose 0 → N → Aⁿ → M → 0 with N finite (A noetherian, tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isNoetherianRing_of_isStronglyNoetherian); the long exact homology sequence (mathlib:CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.ShortExact.homology_exact₂) and the vanishing of Čech cohomology above the length of 𝔘 give Ȟⁱ(𝔘, M̃) ≅ Ȟ^{i+1}(𝔘, Ñ) for i ≥ 1, hence 0 by descending induction; exactness in degree 0 follows from the five lemma (Huber (II.3): reduce to M = Aⁿ).

Strictness: each M̃(V) is complete Hausdorff with the module topology over the complete noetherian Tate ring 𝒪_X(V) (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.isStronglyNoetherian_completion, tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isModuleTopology); images of differentials are kernels of the next differential, hence closed, so the differentials are strict (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isStrictMap_of_isClosed_range).

Sheaf property for arbitrary open covers: reduce to rational covers (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.isSheaf_iff_isSheafFor_rationalCover) refined by standard rational covers (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.exists_span_eq_top_forall_rationalSubset_subset_of_isTateRing; Huber Lemma 2.6); the limit topology is the product-subspace topology because the equaliser is closed (Huber, via EGA 0.3.2.2).

Sheaf cohomology: Čech acyclicity for the cofinal system of finite rational covers of every rational subset of the basis gives Hⁱ = 0 (Cartan's criterion, Stacks Tag 01EW, supplied by DiamondsAndVStacks:D0).
acceptance: Concrete instance (Tate's theorem with coefficients): A = K⟨T⟩, M = A/(T), covering U₁ = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|}, U₂ = {|T| ≥ |ϖ|}: the Čech complex is 0 → K → K ⊕ 0 → 0 → 0, exact.
For M = A the theorem is the anchor's Tate acyclicity for 𝒪_X; the node adds no new case for M = A.
M̃(X) = M for every finite M, so M ↦ M̃ is fully faithful (Hom(M̃, Ñ) = Hom_A(M, N)).

nodes.title: Acyclicity of M̃ when A has a noetherian ring of definition (Huber Theorem 2.5, Case I)
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a complete affinoid ring such that A has a noetherian ring of definition, X = Spa(A, A⁺) and M a finite A-module. Then M̃ is a sheaf of complete topological groups on X, and Hⁱ(U, M̃) = 0 for every i > 0 and every rational subset U ⊆ X. The Čech input — exact strict Čech complexes of M ⊗ 𝒪 on standard rational coverings of rational subsets, which refine every open covering, and the case M = A (sheafiness of 𝒪_X) — is AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-rod-sheafy (Huber (1.5)); this node adds the sheaf M̃ and sheaf-cohomology vanishing.
hypotheses: A complete with a noetherian ring of definition
M finitely generated
U rational
proofSteps: For every rational U, M̃(U) = M ⊗_A 𝒪_X(U) with its natural topology is complete (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-rod-module-complete over 𝒪_X(U), which has a noetherian ring of definition by AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-rod-sheafy (a)), and M̃|_U ≅ (M ⊗_A 𝒪_X(U))~ (Huber (1.4); AdicSpacesPartII:R3/associated-module-sheaf, API tildeRestrictIso).

Every open covering of a rational U is refined by a standard rational covering whose augmented Čech complex of M̃ is exact with strict differentials (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-rod-sheafy (b), (c)); hence M̃ is a sheaf of complete topological groups on the basis of rational subsets and on X (EGA 0_I 3.2.2; tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.isSheaf_iff_isSheafFor_rationalCover).

Čech acyclicity on the cofinal system of standard rational coverings of every rational subset gives sheaf-cohomology vanishing (Cartan's criterion, Stacks Tag 01EW, supplied by DiamondsAndVStacks:D0).
acceptance: For A = ℤ_p⟨T⟩ with the p-adic topology (A⁺ = A), Ã = 𝒪_X is a sheaf and H¹(X, 𝒪_X) = 0 for X = Spa(A, A), the adic space t(Spf ℤ_p⟨T⟩) of Huber §4.
The statement includes non-analytic points: for A = ℤ_p (discrete ring of definition ℤ_p) X = Spa(ℤ_p, ℤ_p) has a closed non-analytic point and the theorem still applies.

nodes.title: Reduction of local transitive properties of rational coverings to simple Laurent coverings
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Tate Huber pair (A contains a topologically nilpotent unit). Let P be a property of finite rational coverings of rational subsets of Spa(A, A⁺) such that (a) P is local: if P holds for a refinement of a covering then it holds for the covering; (b) P is transitive: if P holds for {U → V_i} and for coverings {V_i → W_ij} of each V_i then it holds for the composite covering {U → W_ij}; (c) P holds for every simple Laurent covering {v(f) ≤ 1}, {v(f) ≥ 1} of every rational subset. Then P holds for every finite rational covering of every rational subset.
hypotheses: A Tate (a topologically nilpotent unit exists, used to rescale in Lemma 2.4.19(b))
P local, transitive, true for simple Laurent coverings
proofSteps: Lemma 2.4.19(a): every rational covering is refined by a standard rational covering (in the Tate case: tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.exists_span_eq_top_forall_rationalSubset_subset_of_isTateRing).

Lemma 2.4.19(b): for a standard rational covering generated by f₁,…,fₙ, rescale by a power of the pseudouniformiser so that inf_x max_i |f_i(x)| > 1 on Spa(A, A⁺) (units of A are detected pointwise: anchor Layer 2); the standard Laurent covering generated by the f_i restricts to standard rational coverings generated by units.
Lemma 2.4.19(c): a standard rational covering generated by units is refined by the Laurent covering generated by the f_i f_j⁻¹ (a total order has a maximum).

Assemble: Laurent coverings by units are composites of simple Laurent coverings (use (b),(c)); standard rational coverings by units follow by (a); general standard rational coverings by (b) and the restriction step; general coverings by (a).
acceptance: For P = 'the augmented Čech complex of a presheaf F is exact on every refinement pulled back to every rational subset' the lemma is KL Proposition 2.4.21's reduction.
For P = 'every finite glueing datum of finite modules on the covering is effective' the lemma reduces Kiehl's theorem to simple Laurent coverings (used by AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid).

nodes.title: The two edges of a double complex with exact augmented rows and columns have the same cohomology
nodes.statement: Let K = (K^{p,q})_{p,q ≥ 0} be a first-quadrant double complex of abelian groups, with commuting differentials d′ : K^{p,q} → K^{p+1,q} and d″ : K^{p,q} → K^{p,q+1}. Let C^• and R^• be cochain complexes of abelian groups (C^p = R^q = 0 in negative degrees) with morphisms ε′ : C^p → K^{p,0} commuting with d′ and ε″ : R^q → K^{0,q} commuting with d″, such that (i) for every p ≥ 0 the augmented column 0 → C^p → K^{p,0} → K^{p,1} → ⋯ (maps ε′, d″) is exact, and (ii) for every q ≥ 0 the augmented row 0 → R^q → K^{0,q} → K^{1,q} → ⋯ (maps ε″, d′) is exact. Let Tot(K) be the total complex, Tot(K)ⁿ = ⊕_{p+q=n} K^{p,q} with differential d′ + (−1)^p d″. Then ε′ : C^• → Tot(K) and ε″ : R^• → Tot(K) (the latter composed with the sign (−1)^0 = 1 on K^{0,q}) are morphisms of complexes and quasi-isomorphisms; in particular Hⁿ(C^•) ≅ Hⁿ(R^•) for every n ≥ 0, naturally in the data (K, C, R, ε′, ε″). This is the cohomological form of Stacks Tag 00M1, which is stated for chain complexes; the proof is the same staircase argument with the indices reversed.
hypotheses: K a first-quadrant double complex of abelian groups
every augmented column 0 → C^p → K^{p,•} and every augmented row 0 → R^q → K^{•,q} exact
proofSteps: Tot(K) is the total complex of the bicomplex (Mathlib `HomologicalComplex₂` with `HomologicalComplex₂.total`; first quadrant, so each Tot(K)ⁿ is a finite direct sum); ε′ and ε″ are chain maps because d″ ∘ ε′ = 0 and d′ ∘ ε″ = 0, which hold since ε′(C^p) = ker(d″ : K^{p,0} → K^{p,1}) and dually by (i), (ii).

Staircase: a cocycle of Tot(K)ⁿ is (x_{n,0}, x_{n−1,1}, …, x_{0,n}); using exactness of the columns (resp. rows) one modifies it by a coboundary step by step until only the component in K^{n,0} (resp. K^{0,n}) survives, and that component lies in ε′(Cⁿ) (resp. ε″(Rⁿ)); this gives surjectivity of Hⁿ(C) → Hⁿ(Tot) (resp. Hⁿ(R) → Hⁿ(Tot)).

Injectivity is the same staircase argument applied to a primitive in Tot(K)^{n−1} of the image of a cocycle of C (resp. R): exactness of the columns (resp. rows) pushes the primitive into the edge. This is the proof of Stacks Tag 00M1, which identifies both edge cohomologies with the group of staircase cocycles modulo staircase coboundaries.
Naturality: a morphism of the data (K, C, R, ε′, ε″) commutes with the edge maps into Tot(K), hence with the induced isomorphisms.
acceptance: Degenerate case: if K^{p,q} = 0 for p > 0 then (ii) says R^• ≅ K^{0,•}, (i) says C^0 = ker(K^{0,0} → K^{0,1}) and C^p = 0 for p > 0, and the lemma reduces to Hⁿ(K^{0,•}) = C^0 for n = 0 and 0 otherwise, which is (i) for p = 0.

For finite coverings 𝔙 and 𝔚 of an open U with 𝔚 refining 𝔙 and K^{p,q} = ∏ F(V_{i₀…i_p} ∩ W_{j₀…j_q}), C = Č(𝔙, F), R = Č(𝔚, F), the lemma is the comparison Ȟⁿ(𝔙, F) ≅ Ȟⁿ(𝔚, F) of AdicSpacesPartII:R3/cech-acyclicity-refinement.

nodes.title: Čech acyclicity is inherited from a refinement whose restrictions are acyclic
nodes.statement: Let X be a topological space, ℬ a family of open subsets of X closed under finite intersections, and F a presheaf of abelian groups on ℬ (restriction maps along inclusions in ℬ, functorial). For U ∈ ℬ and a finite covering 𝔘 = (U_i)_{i∈I} of U by members of ℬ, call 𝔘 F-acyclic if the augmented alternating Čech complex 0 → F(U) → ∏_{i₀} F(U_{i₀}) → ∏_{i₀<i₁} F(U_{i₀i₁}) → ⋯ (for a chosen total order of I) is exact. Let 𝔙 = (V_i)_{i∈I} and 𝔚 = (W_j)_{j∈J} be finite coverings of U ∈ ℬ by members of ℬ such that 𝔚 refines 𝔙 (every W_j is contained in some V_i). Suppose that for every p ≥ 0 and every i₀ < ⋯ < i_p in I the covering 𝔚 ∩ V_{i₀…i_p} = (W_j ∩ V_{i₀…i_p})_{j∈J} of V_{i₀…i_p} is F-acyclic. Then Ȟⁿ(U, F; 𝔙) ≅ Ȟⁿ(U, F; 𝔚) for every n ≥ 0, compatibly with the maps from F(U) in degree 0; in particular 𝔙 is F-acyclic if and only if 𝔚 is. Consequence (the locality used by Kedlaya–Liu): if 𝔚 refines 𝔙 and the restriction of 𝔚 to every member of ℬ contained in U is F-acyclic ('𝔚 is universally F-acyclic'), then so is every restriction of 𝔙.
hypotheses: ℬ closed under finite intersections; F a presheaf of abelian groups on ℬ
𝔙, 𝔚 finite coverings of U by members of ℬ, 𝔚 refining 𝔙
the restrictions of 𝔚 to all finite intersections of members of 𝔙 are F-acyclic
proofSteps: The alternating Čech complex is homotopy equivalent to the full Čech complex (Stacks Tag 01FM), so it suffices to argue with full Čech complexes; all intersections below lie in ℬ.

Form the Čech double complex K^{p,q} = ∏_{(i₀…i_p) ∈ I^{p+1}} ∏_{(j₀…j_q) ∈ J^{q+1}} F(V_{i₀…i_p} ∩ W_{j₀…j_q}) with the two Čech differentials; C = Č^•(𝔙, F) maps to the column edge and R = Č^•(𝔚, F) to the row edge by restriction.
Columns: for fixed (i₀…i_p) the augmented column is the augmented Čech complex of the covering 𝔚 ∩ V_{i₀…i_p} of V_{i₀…i_p}, exact by hypothesis.

Rows: for fixed (j₀…j_q), W_{j₀} ⊆ V_i for some i, so the covering 𝔙 ∩ W_{j₀…j_q} of W_{j₀…j_q} has the member V_i ∩ W_{j₀…j_q} = W_{j₀…j_q}; its augmented Čech complex is homotopy equivalent to 0 (Stacks Tag 0G6S), hence exact.

AdicSpacesPartII:R3/cech-double-complex-comparison gives Hⁿ(C) ≅ Hⁿ(Tot K) ≅ Hⁿ(R); the two maps F(U) → C⁰ → K^{0,0} and F(U) → R⁰ → K^{0,0} are both restriction to the V_i ∩ W_j, so the isomorphism in degree 0 is compatible with the maps from F(U), and exactness of one augmented complex is equivalent to exactness of the other.
Consequence: for U′ ∈ ℬ with U′ ⊆ U, 𝔚 ∩ U′ refines 𝔙 ∩ U′ and its restrictions to the intersections V_{i₀…i_p} ∩ U′ are restrictions of 𝔚, hence F-acyclic; apply the first part.
acceptance: If 𝔙 = (U) is the trivial covering, every 𝔚 refines it and the lemma says 𝔚 is F-acyclic iff its restriction to U is, which is a tautology; if 𝔚 = 𝔙 the hypothesis is that 𝔙 is universally acyclic on its own intersections.
Kedlaya–Liu's use: universal Čech acyclicity satisfies the locality condition (a) of Proposition 2.4.20 (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/cech-acyclicity-simple-laurent-reduction).

nodes.title: Čech acyclicity of a presheaf on all rational coverings follows from simple Laurent coverings (Kedlaya–Liu Proposition 2.4.21)
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Hausdorff Tate Huber pair, X = Spa(A, A⁺), and F a presheaf of abelian groups on the rational subsets of X. Suppose that for every rational subset U ⊆ X and every f ∈ 𝒪_X(U), with V₁ = {x ∈ U : |f(x)| ≤ 1} and V₂ = {x ∈ U : |f(x)| ≥ 1} (rational subsets of X, anchor Layer 3.1), the sequence 0 → F(U) → F(V₁) ⊕ F(V₂) → F(V₁ ∩ V₂) → 0, (s ↦ (s|V₁, s|V₂), (a, b) ↦ a|V₁₂ − b|V₁₂), is exact. Then for every rational subset U ⊆ X and every finite covering 𝔘 of U by rational subsets, the augmented alternating Čech complex of F on 𝔘 is exact: Ȟ⁰(U, F; 𝔘) = F(U) and Ȟⁱ(U, F; 𝔘) = 0 for i > 0.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) complete Hausdorff Tate
F a presheaf of abelian groups on the rational subsets of Spa(A, A⁺)
the two-term Čech sequence of every simple Laurent covering of every rational subset is exact
proofSteps: Rational subsets of X form a family closed under finite intersections (anchor Layer 2.2), and the rational subsets of a rational U = Spa(B, B⁺) are the rational subsets of X contained in U (anchor Layer 3.1); so the restriction of a finite rational covering to a rational subset is again one.
Let P(𝔘) for a finite rational covering 𝔘 of a rational U be: 'for every rational U′ ⊆ U the covering 𝔘 ∩ U′ of U′ is F-acyclic' (Kedlaya–Liu's universal Čech acyclicity, including degree 0).

(c) P holds for simple Laurent coverings: the restriction of the simple Laurent covering of U defined by f to a rational U′ ⊆ U is the simple Laurent covering of U′ defined by f|U′, and for a two-member covering the augmented alternating Čech complex is the displayed sequence, exact by hypothesis.
(a) P is local: if a refinement 𝔚 of 𝔘 satisfies P, the consequence clause of AdicSpacesPartII:R3/cech-acyclicity-refinement (with ℬ the rational subsets) gives P(𝔘).

(b) P is transitive: let {C_i} satisfy P and each {D_ij}_j satisfy P as coverings of C_i; for the composite covering 𝔇 = {D_ij} of U and any rational U′ ⊆ U, 𝔇 ∩ U′ refines {C_i ∩ U′}, and the restriction of 𝔇 ∩ U′ to C_{i₀…i_p} ∩ U′ contains the covering {D_{i₀ j} ∩ C_{i₀…i_p} ∩ U′}_j, which is F-acyclic by P for {D_{i₀ j}}_j and refines the whole restriction; two applications of AdicSpacesPartII:R3/cech-acyclicity-refinement give acyclicity of 𝔇 ∩ U′.
AdicSpacesPartII:R3/rational-covering-reduction (Kedlaya–Liu Proposition 2.4.20) turns (a)–(c) into P for every finite rational covering of every rational subset; P with U′ = U is the conclusion.
acceptance: For F = 𝒪_X of a complete strongly noetherian Tate pair the hypothesis is anchor Layer 4.1's two-piece Laurent exactness (Wedhorn Lemma 8.33) and the conclusion is its all-degree Čech exactness.
For F = M ⊗_A 𝒪_X with M finite projective over a sheafy Tate A, the hypothesis follows from the case F = 𝒪_X by taking direct summands (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-projective-module-acyclicity).

nodes.title: For a simple Laurent covering the difference map B₁ ⊕ B₂ → B₁₂ is surjective (Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 2.4.22)
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Hausdorff Huber pair and f ∈ A. Let A → B₁, A → B₂, A → B₁₂ be the rational localisations (anchor Layer 3.1, Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.completionLocObj`) of the rational subsets S₋ = R({f, 1}/1) = {v(f) ≤ 1}, S₊ = R({1, f}/f) = {v(f) ≥ 1} and S₋ ∩ S₊ = R({1, f, f²}/f) = {v(f) = 1} of Spa(A, A⁺), and ρ₁ : B₁ → B₁₂, ρ₂ : B₂ → B₁₂ the restriction maps. Then the map B₁ ⊕ B₂ → B₁₂, (b₁, b₂) ↦ ρ₁(b₁) − ρ₂(b₂), is surjective. No sheafiness, noetherian or Tate hypothesis is made.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) complete Hausdorff Huber pair
f ∈ A arbitrary
proofSteps: Evaluation maps: A⟨T⟩ → B₁ (T ↦ f), A⟨U⟩ → B₂ (U ↦ 1/f) and A⟨T, U⟩ → B₁₂ (T ↦ f, U ↦ 1/f) are continuous and surjective (Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.continuous_rationalEvalHom` and `PairOfDefinition.rationalEvalHom_surjective`, applied with numerator families (f, 1), (1, f), (1, f, f²) and then specialising the variable sent to 1; the neighbourhoods of 0 of a Huber ring are countably generated by the powers of an ideal of definition).

Compatibility: ρ₁ composed with A⟨T⟩ → B₁ and ρ₂ composed with A⟨U⟩ → B₂ are the restrictions of A⟨T, U⟩ → B₁₂ to A⟨T⟩ and A⟨U⟩, since continuous homomorphisms out of a restricted power-series ring are determined by the images of the constants and the variables (Tau Ceti `existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_completion_weightedRestrictedSubring`); and TU ↦ f · f⁻¹ = 1 in B₁₂.
Given b ∈ B₁₂ choose a lift Σ_{i,j ≥ 0} a_{ij} TⁱUʲ ∈ A⟨T, U⟩, so a_{ij} → 0. For n ∈ ℤ the series a′_n = Σ_{i−j=n} a_{ij} converges in the complete nonarchimedean ring A and a′_n → 0 as |n| → ∞.
Put b₁ = image of Σ_{n≥0} a′_n Tⁿ in B₁ and b₂ = image of −Σ_{n≥1} a′_{−n} Uⁿ in B₂. Rearranging the convergent series in B₁₂ using TU = 1 gives ρ₁(b₁) − ρ₂(b₂) = Σ a_{ij} f^{i−j} = b.
acceptance: For A = ℚ_p⟨X⟩ and f = X: B₁ = ℚ_p⟨X⟩, B₂ = ℚ_p⟨X, X⁻¹⟩ = B₁₂, and ρ₂ is the identity, so the map is onto for trivial reasons; for f = X/p the lemma is the splitting of a Laurent series on the annulus |X| = |p| into its parts of nonnegative and negative degree.
Outside sheafy rings the lemma still holds: for a non-sheafy pair (Kedlaya–Liu Example 2.8.7) the two-term Čech sequence can fail to be exact only at A or at B₁ ⊕ B₂.
