nodes.title: Čech acyclicity of the structure sheaf on every sheafy Tate affinoid (Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 2.4.23)
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Hausdorff Tate Huber pair which is sheafy (`Huber.IsSheafyPair A A⁺`, anchor Layer 3.4: the structure presheaf 𝒪_X of X = Spa(A, A⁺) is a sheaf). Then (1) for every rational subset U ⊆ X and every finite covering 𝔘 = (U_i) of U by rational subsets, the augmented alternating Čech complex 0 → 𝒪_X(U) → ∏_i 𝒪_X(U_i) → ∏_{i<j} 𝒪_X(U_i ∩ U_j) → ⋯ is exact in every degree; (2) Hⁱ(U, 𝒪_X) = 0 for every i > 0 and every rational subset U, where Hⁱ is sheaf cohomology of the underlying sheaf of abelian groups on the topological space U. In particular H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = A and Hⁱ(X, 𝒪_X) = Ȟⁱ(X, 𝒪_X; 𝔘) = 0 for i > 0 and every finite rational covering 𝔘 of X. No noetherian or uniformity hypothesis is made: the anchor's Layer 4.1 gives (1) for strongly noetherian A, and this theorem extends it to every sheafy Tate pair (for instance perfectoid and sousperfectoid ones).
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) complete Hausdorff Tate Huber pair
(A, A⁺) sheafy: 𝒪_X is a sheaf on X = Spa(A, A⁺)
proofSteps: Sheafiness passes to rational subsets: for a rational U with coordinate ring (B, B⁺) = (𝒪_X(U), 𝒪_X⁺(U)), Spa(B, B⁺) → U is a homeomorphism matching rational subsets and their coordinate rings (anchor Layer 3.1), so the structure presheaf of Spa(B, B⁺) is the restriction of 𝒪_X to U, which is a sheaf; (B, B⁺) is again a complete Tate sheafy pair.

Simple Laurent coverings: for U = Spa(B, B⁺) rational and f ∈ B, with B₁, B₂, B₁₂ the coordinate rings of {|f| ≤ 1}, {|f| ≥ 1} and their intersection, the sequence 0 → B → B₁ ⊕ B₂ → B₁₂ → 0 is exact at B₁₂ by AdicSpacesPartII:R3/simple-laurent-difference-surjective applied to (B, B⁺), and exact at B and at B₁ ⊕ B₂ by the sheaf property of 𝒪_X for the two-member covering of U.
AdicSpacesPartII:R3/cech-acyclicity-simple-laurent-reduction applied to F = 𝒪_X restricted to rational subsets gives (1).

(2): rational subsets form a basis of the topology of X closed under finite intersections (anchor Layer 2.2), and every open covering of a rational subset is refined by a finite rational covering (rational subsets are quasi-compact, anchor Layer 3.5); with (1), Cartan's criterion (Stacks Tag 01EW, requested from DiamondsAndVStacks:D0) gives Hⁱ(U, 𝒪_X) = 0 for i > 0 and U rational, and Ȟⁱ(X, 𝒪_X; 𝔘) = Hⁱ(X, 𝒪_X).
acceptance: Tate's acyclicity on the disc: for A = K⟨T⟩ (K a complete nonarchimedean field, ϖ a pseudouniformiser; sheafy by anchor Layer 4.1) and the covering {|T| ≤ |ϖ|}, {|T| ≥ |ϖ|}, the sequence 0 → K⟨T⟩ → K⟨T/ϖ⟩ ⊕ K⟨T, ϖ/T⟩ → K⟨T/ϖ, ϖ/T⟩ → 0 is exact.

Beyond the anchor: for a perfectoid affinoid (R, R⁺) (sheafy, Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 3.6.15; R is not noetherian) every finite rational covering of Spa(R, R⁺) has exact augmented Čech complex and Hⁱ(Spa(R, R⁺), 𝒪) = 0 for i > 0.

The sheafiness hypothesis cannot be dropped: for a non-sheafy Tate pair some simple Laurent covering of some rational subset has a sequence 0 → B → B₁ ⊕ B₂ → B₁₂ → 0 that is not exact at B or at B₁ ⊕ B₂ (otherwise AdicSpacesPartII:R3/cech-acyclicity-simple-laurent-reduction and the basis criterion of anchor Layer 3.5 would make 𝒪_X a sheaf), while exactness at B₁₂ persists (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/simple-laurent-difference-surjective).

nodes.title: Glueing squares of complete Tate rings
nodes.statement: A glueing square is a commutative square of complete Hausdorff Tate rings with continuous homomorphisms R → R₁, R → R₂, R₁ → R₁₂, R₂ → R₁₂ such that (a) the sequence 0 → R → R₁ × R₂ → R₁₂ → 0, (r₁, r₂) ↦ r₁ − r₂, is exact and strict (R carries the subspace topology of R₁ × R₂ and R₁ × R₂ → R₁₂ is open onto R₁₂); (b) R₂ → R₁₂ has dense image; (c) every maximal ideal of R is the contraction of a prime ideal of R₁ × R₂. A finite (resp. finite projective) glueing datum on it is a triple of finite (resp. finite projective) modules M₁, M₂, M₁₂ over R₁, R₂, R₁₂ with isomorphisms ψ_i : M_i ⊗_{R_i} R₁₂ ≅ M₁₂; its module of sections is M = ker(ψ₁ − ψ₂ : M₁ × M₂ → M₁₂). Convention: condition (c) replaces Kedlaya–Liu's surjectivity of Gel'fand spectra M(R₁ ⊕ R₂) → M(R), which they use only through (c); every topological ring here is metrised by the norm |x| = inf{cⁿ : ϖ⁻ⁿx ∈ R₀} of a pseudouniformiser ϖ and ring of definition R₀ (KL Remark 2.4.4).
hypotheses: all four rings complete Hausdorff Tate rings; maps continuous
(a) strict exactness, (b) density, (c) maximal ideals lift
proofSteps: Data: the four rings and maps plus proofs of (a)–(c); glueing data and their section module are defined from these as in KL Definition 1.3.7.

The norm α_d of a norm datum (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/tate-ring-norm, Kedlaya–Liu Remark 2.4.4) makes each ring a Banach ring; strictness in (a) is independent of the chosen norms (equivalent norms, API Huber.tateNorm_equiv_of_ringOfDefinition).
acceptance: The simple Laurent square A → A⟨f⟩, A⟨1/f⟩ → A⟨f, 1/f⟩ of a complete sheafy Tate ring is a glueing square (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/simple-laurent-glueing-square).
For a finite glueing datum the section module M satisfies M ⊗ R_i ↠ M_i (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/glueing-square-finite-surjectivity).

nodes.title: Factorisation of matrices near the identity along a strict surjection
nodes.statement: Let R₁ → S and R₂ → S be bounded homomorphisms of Banach rings such that ψ : R₁ ⊕ R₂ → S, (x, y) ↦ x + y, is a strict surjection of groups. Then there is c > 0 such that for every n ≥ 1 every U ∈ GLₙ(S) with |U − 1| < c factors as U = ψ(U₁)ψ(U₂) with U_i ∈ GLₙ(R_i); if every x ∈ S lifts to (y₁, y₂) with |y_i| ≤ d|x| one can take c = d⁻².
hypotheses: R₁, R₂, S Banach rings, bounded homomorphisms
ψ strict surjective
proofSteps: Choose d ≥ 1 with lifts of norm ≤ d|x| (strictness).
For |U − 1| < d⁻², lift V = U − 1 entrywise to (X, Y) and put U' = ψ(1 − X) U ψ(1 − Y); then |U' − 1| ≤ d|U − 1|².
Iterate; the partial products converge in GLₙ(R₁) and GLₙ(R₂) because the errors decrease geometrically (completeness).
acceptance: For R₁ = ℚ_p⟨T⟩, R₂ = ℚ_p⟨T⁻¹⟩, S = ℚ_p⟨T, T⁻¹⟩ (d = 1) every U ∈ GLₙ(S) with |U − 1| < 1 factors as a product of a matrix over ℚ_p⟨T⟩ and one over ℚ_p⟨T⁻¹⟩ (Cartan's lemma for the annulus).

nodes.title: Sections of a finite glueing datum generate each piece
nodes.statement: Let R → R₁, R₂ → R₁₂ be a glueing square and (M₁, M₂, M₁₂) a finite glueing datum with section module M. Then (a) M ⊗_R R_i → M_i is surjective for i = 1, 2; (b) ψ₁ − ψ₂ : M₁ × M₂ → M₁₂ is surjective; (c) there is a finitely generated R-submodule M₀ ⊆ M with M₀ ⊗_R R_i → M_i surjective for i = 1, 2.
hypotheses: glueing square (conditions (a), (b); condition (c) is not used)
M₁, M₂, M₁₂ finite
proofSteps: Choose generators v₁,…,vₙ of M₁ and w₁,…,wₙ of M₂ and matrices A, B over R₁₂ with ψ₂(w_j) = Σ A_ij ψ₁(v_i), ψ₁(v_j) = Σ B_ij ψ₂(w_i).
By density of R₂ → R₁₂ choose B' over R₂ with |A(B' − B)| < c (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/matrix-factorisation-strict-surjection), and write 1 + A(B' − B) = C₁C₂⁻¹ with C_i ∈ GLₙ(R_i).
The elements x_j = (Σ(C₁)_ij v_i, Σ(B'C₂)_ij w_i) lie in M and their first components generate M₁, so M ⊗ R₁ ↠ M₁.
KL Lemma 1.3.8: surjectivity for i = 1 gives (b), then surjectivity for i = 2, and a finitely generated M₀ containing the x_j and lifts of generators of M₂.
acceptance: For the simple Laurent square of ℚ_p⟨T⟩ at f = T/p (R₁ = ℚ_p⟨T/p⟩, R₂ = ℚ_p⟨T, p/T⟩, R₁₂ = ℚ_p⟨T/p, p/T⟩) and the datum (R₁, R₂, R₁₂) with ψ₁ = id and ψ₂ = multiplication by the unit T/p (already a unit of R₂), the section module {(a, b) : a = (T/p)·b} is free of rank one over ℚ_p⟨T⟩, generated by (1, p/T), and M ⊗ R_i → M_i is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: The simple Laurent covering of a sheafy Tate affinoid is a glueing square
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Tate Huber pair whose structure presheaf is a sheaf on rational subsets (sheafy), and f ∈ A. Let B₁, B₂, B₁₂ be the rational localisations for S₋ = {v(f) ≤ 1}, S₊ = {v(f) ≥ 1} and S₋ ∩ S₊. Then A → B₁, B₂ → B₁₂ is a glueing square (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/glueing-square).
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) complete Tate, sheafy
f ∈ A arbitrary
proofSteps: B₁ = A⟨T⟩/closure(T − f), B₂ = A⟨U⟩/closure(1 − fU), B₁₂ = A⟨T, U⟩/closure(T − f, 1 − fU) (anchor Layer 3.1 rational localisation).
Surjectivity of B₁ × B₂ → B₁₂ is AdicSpacesPartII:R3/simple-laurent-difference-surjective (KL Lemma 2.4.22).
Exactness at A and at B₁ × B₂ is the sheaf property for the covering {S₋, S₊} (sheafy hypothesis).

Strictness: the surjection B₁ × B₂ → B₁₂ is open by the open mapping theorem (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isOpenMap); A → B₁ × B₂ has closed image (kernel of a continuous map to a Hausdorff ring) and is a homeomorphism onto it by the open mapping theorem applied to A → image.
Density of B₂ → B₁₂: B₁₂ is the rational localisation of B₂ at {v(f) ≤ 1}, and the image of B₂[T] is dense in B₂⟨T⟩ (anchor Layer 0.4).

Maximal ideals: every maximal ideal of A is the support of a point v ∈ Spa(A, A⁺) (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.exists_mem_spa_supp_eq_of_isMaximal), v lies in S₋ or S₊, and its support stays proper in the corresponding B_i (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.map_supp_toCompletionLoc_ne_top).
acceptance: For A = K⟨T⟩ and f = T/ϖ the square is K⟨T⟩ → K⟨T/ϖ⟩, K⟨ϖ/T, T⟩ → K⟨T/ϖ, ϖ/T⟩ (disc of radius |ϖ| and annulus |ϖ| ≤ |T| ≤ 1).

nodes.title: Finite glueing data on a simple Laurent covering of a strongly noetherian Tate affinoid are effective
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) is a Huber pair with A a complete Hausdorff strongly noetherian Tate ring and A⁺ a ring of integral elements, f ∈ A, and let A → B₁, B₂ → B₁₂ be the simple Laurent glueing square of f. For every finite glueing datum (M₁, M₂, M₁₂) there is a finite A-module M with isomorphisms M ⊗_A B_i ≅ M_i compatible with the ψ_i; M is the section module and is unique up to unique isomorphism.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) is a Huber pair with A a complete Hausdorff strongly noetherian Tate ring and A⁺ a ring of integral elements
(M₁, M₂, M₁₂) finite glueing datum on the simple Laurent square of f
proofSteps: By AdicSpacesPartII:R3/glueing-square-finite-surjectivity there is a finitely generated M₀ ⊆ M with M₀ ⊗ B_i ↠ M_i; choose Aⁿ ↠ M₀.

The kernels K_i = ker(B_iⁿ → M_i) are finite B_i-modules (B_i noetherian: tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.isStronglyNoetherian_completion) and K_i ⊗ B₁₂ ≅ K₁₂ because B_i → B₁₂ is flat (B₁₂ is a rational localisation of the complete strongly noetherian Tate ring B_i, anchor Layer 3.1, and tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.flat_toCompletionLoc applies to B_i); so (K₁, K₂, K₁₂) is again a finite glueing datum.
Apply the first step to (K₁, K₂, K₁₂): there is h : Aᵐ → Aⁿ whose base changes map onto the K_i (Kiehl's second free module G).
Put M = coker(h), a finite A-module; right exactness of ⊗ gives M ⊗ B_i ≅ coker(B_iᵐ → B_iⁿ) ≅ M_i compatibly with the ψ_i.
Uniqueness: by exactness of 0 → M → M ⊗ B₁ × M ⊗ B₂ → M ⊗ B₁₂ (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-acyclicity-finite-modules) M is the section module.
acceptance: For A = K⟨T⟩, f = T/ϖ, M₁ = B₁, M₂ = B₂ with ψ given by multiplication by the unit T/ϖ of B₁₂, the glued module is free of rank one.

nodes.title: Coherent sheaves on locally noetherian adic spaces
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally noetherian adic space (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space) with structure sheaf 𝒪_X (anchor Layer 5). A sheaf F of 𝒪_X-modules on the topological space X is coherent if there is an open covering of X by affinoid open subspaces U_i ≅ Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) with A_i complete of noetherian type (noetherian ring of definition, or strongly noetherian Tate) and finitely generated A_i-modules M_i with F|_{U_i} ≅ M̃_i (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/associated-module-sheaf). Coh(X) is the full subcategory of 𝒪_X-modules on coherent objects. On strongly noetherian Tate affinoid opens U the condition then holds with M = F(U) (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid); on affinoid opens with a noetherian ring of definition the definition is used only through such coverings.
hypotheses: X locally noetherian adic space
𝒪_X a sheaf (X an adic space, anchor Layer 5)
proofSteps: Coherence is a property of an object of SheafOfModules over the ring sheaf 𝒪_X on Opens(X) (Mathlib SheafOfModules).
Isomorphism invariance and locality on X are immediate from the definition by coverings.
M̃_i is a sheaf by AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-acyclicity-finite-modules and AdicSpacesPartII:R3/noetherian-rod-acyclicity-finite-modules, so the local models are objects of the category.
acceptance: On the closed disc X = Spa(K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩) the ideal sheaf (T) ⊆ 𝒪_X is coherent and equals (T·K⟨T⟩)~.
The extension by zero j_!𝒪_U of 𝒪_U for U = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|} is not coherent.

nodes.title: Kiehl's theorem: coherent sheaves on a strongly noetherian Tate affinoid are the M̃
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) is a Huber pair with A a complete Hausdorff strongly noetherian Tate ring and A⁺ a ring of integral elements and X = Spa(A, A⁺). (i) A sheaf of 𝒪_X-modules F is coherent (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/coherent-sheaf) iff F ≅ M̃ for a finite A-module M, and then M ≅ F(X). (ii) M ↦ M̃ is an exact equivalence of categories from finite A-modules to Coh(X), with quasi-inverse F ↦ F(X), compatible with ⊗ and internal Hom (a tensor equivalence). (iii) Equivalently, for every finite rational covering {U_i = Spa(B_i, B_i⁺)} of X, A → ∏ B_i is an effective descent morphism for finite modules: every system of finite B_i-modules with compatible isomorphisms on the U_i ∩ U_j (cocycle condition) comes from a finite A-module. In particular (A affinoid algebra over a complete nonarchimedean field K) this is Kiehl's theorem in Kedlaya–Liu's adic form (KL Theorem 2.5.20(b)).
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) is a Huber pair with A a complete Hausdorff strongly noetherian Tate ring and A⁺ a ring of integral elements
proofSteps: Full faithfulness: M̃(X) = M (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-acyclicity-finite-modules) and M̃(U) is generated over 𝒪_X(U) by the image of M, so a morphism M̃ → Ñ is determined by, and determined from, its value on global sections.
Exactness and tensor compatibility: API tilde_exact and tildeTensorIso of AdicSpacesPartII:R3/associated-module-sheaf.

Essential surjectivity: let P(𝔘) for a finite rational covering 𝔘 of a rational U be 'every sheaf of 𝒪_U-modules whose restrictions to the members of 𝔘 are associated to finite modules is associated to a finite 𝒪_X(U)-module'. P is local (restrictions of associated sheaves to rational subsets are associated: tildeRestrictIso) and transitive; it holds for simple Laurent coverings (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/strongly-noetherian-laurent-gluing: glue the sections, then compare the two sheaves on the covering). By AdicSpacesPartII:R3/rational-covering-reduction P holds for all finite rational coverings.

A coherent F on X is associated on a covering by affinoid opens V_i; each V_i is covered by rational subsets W ⊆ V_i of X, which are rational subsets of V_i with 𝒪_{V_i}(W) = 𝒪_X(W), so F|_W is associated; refine to a finite standard rational covering (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.exists_span_eq_top_forall_rationalSubset_subset_of_isTateRing) and apply P.
(iii) is (i) for the sheaf glued from the descent datum (sheaves glue along open coverings).
acceptance: For A = K⟨T⟩, U₁ = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|}, U₂ = {|T| ≥ |ϖ|} and the datum 𝒪_{U₁}, 𝒪_{U₂} glued by s₁ = (T/ϖ)·s₂ on U₁ ∩ U₂, the glued coherent sheaf is (A)~ (T/ϖ is already a unit on U₂, so the datum is trivial), with global generator (1, ϖ/T); the section (T/ϖ, 1) lies in it but generates only T·Ã.
For A an affinoid K-algebra this recovers KL Theorem 2.5.20(b) and Kiehl's Theorem 1.2 (Cartanscher Verheftungssatz).

nodes.title: Small perturbations of surjections of complete modules are surjective
nodes.statement: Let B be a complete Hausdorff Tate ring and f : M → N a continuous surjective B-linear map of complete Hausdorff topological B-modules whose topologies are defined by open bounded B₀-submodules M₀, N₀ for a ring of definition B₀ (Banach B-modules, normed by |m| = inf{|c| : c ∈ K or B^×, m ∈ cM₀} for a pseudouniformiser; Kiehl's standing setting of §1). There is c > 0 (for chosen norms) such that f − ε is surjective for every continuous B-linear ε : M → N with |ε| < c. In particular, if m₁,…,m_r generate a finite B-module N with its module topology, every family m'_j sufficiently close to the m_j generates N.
hypotheses: B complete Hausdorff Tate; M, N complete, with topology defined by open bounded B₀-submodules (normable)
f continuous surjective
proofSteps: By the open mapping theorem (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isOpenMap) f has a bounded, not necessarily linear, section b with f ∘ b = id.
If |ε| · |b| < 1 the series g = Σ_{i≥0} (bε)ⁱ b converges and (f − ε) ∘ g = id (Kiehl, Lemma 1.3).
For generators: apply this to Bʳ → N, e_j ↦ m_j, perturbed by e_j ↦ m'_j − m_j.
acceptance: For B = K and N = K² with generators (1,0), (0,1), any (1, δ), (δ', 1) with |δ|, |δ'| < 1 still generate.

nodes.title: The abelian tensor category of coherent sheaves and pullback
nodes.statement: Let X is a locally noetherian analytic adic space in the sense of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space whose points all have affinoid neighbourhoods Spa(A, A⁺) with A a complete strongly noetherian Tate ring (for instance X locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°), K a complete nonarchimedean field). Coh(X) is an abelian full subcategory of 𝒪_X-modules closed under kernels, cokernels, images, extensions, ⊗_{𝒪_X} and the internal Hom sheaf ℋom_{𝒪_X}(F, G); the inclusion is exact. For a morphism f : Y → X of such spaces, the pullback f*F = 𝒪_Y ⊗_{f⁻¹𝒪_X} f⁻¹F defines a right exact monoidal functor f* : Coh(X) → Coh(Y) with (id)* ≅ id and (g ∘ f)* ≅ f* ∘ g*; affinoid-locally, for Spa(B, B⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) induced by a continuous A → B, f*M̃ ≅ (M ⊗_A B)~. Base change of coherent sheaves along a fibre product square (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence) is pullback along the projection.
hypotheses: X, Y locally noetherian analytic with strongly noetherian Tate affinoid charts
f a morphism of adic spaces
proofSteps: Kernels and cokernels: on a strongly noetherian Tate affinoid chart, a morphism of coherent sheaves is φ̃ for φ : M → N (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid); ker and coker of φ̃ are ker(φ)~, coker(φ)~ because M ↦ M̃(U) is exact (flatness); hence coherent.
Tensor and Hom: (M ⊗ N)~ = M̃ ⊗ Ñ; ℋom(M̃, Ñ)(U) = Hom_{𝒪(U)}(M ⊗ 𝒪(U), N ⊗ 𝒪(U)) = Hom_A(M, N) ⊗_A 𝒪(U) by finite presentation of M and flatness of A → 𝒪(U).

Pullback: use Mathlib SheafOfModules.pullback for the morphism of ringed sites; on affinoid charts compute f*M̃ by the universal property of M̃ as the sheaf associated with M ⊗_A B (both sides agree on rational subsets of Spa(B, B⁺) mapping into a rational subset of Spa(A, A⁺)).
Functoriality and monoidality are inherited from Mathlib's pullback of sheaves of modules.
acceptance: On the closed disc, coker(T : 𝒪 → 𝒪) = (K⟨T⟩/(T))~, the skyscraper K at the origin.
For the inclusion i : {0} = Spa(K) → disc, i* of 0 → 𝒪 → 𝒪 → i_*K → 0 (the middle map multiplication by T) is not left exact.

nodes.title: Closed adic subspaces correspond to coherent ideals
nodes.statement: Let X is a locally noetherian analytic adic space in the sense of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space whose points all have affinoid neighbourhoods Spa(A, A⁺) with A a complete strongly noetherian Tate ring (for instance X locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°), K a complete nonarchimedean field). The assignment I ↦ V(I) = (Supp(𝒪_X/I), (𝒪_X/I)|_{Supp}) is a bijection from coherent ideal sheaves I ⊆ 𝒪_X to closed adic subspaces of X (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings), with inverse Z ↦ ker(𝒪_X → i_*𝒪_Z); on a strongly noetherian Tate affinoid Spa(A, A⁺) the coherent ideals are the J̃ for ideals J ⊆ A (automatically closed) and V(J̃) = Spa(A/J, (A/J)⁺) with (A/J)⁺ the integral closure of the image of A⁺. The ringed-space structure is retained: V(I) and V(I') can have the same support with I ≠ I'.
hypotheses: X is a locally noetherian analytic adic space in the sense of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space whose points all have affinoid neighbourhoods Spa(A, A⁺) with A a complete strongly noetherian Tate ring (for instance X locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°), K a complete nonarchimedean field)
proofSteps: On an affinoid chart a coherent ideal is J̃ with J = I(X) an ideal of A (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid applied to the injection I → 𝒪_X).
J is closed (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isClosed_of_isNoetherian), A/J is complete strongly noetherian Tate (IsOpenQuotientMap.isStronglyNoetherian), hence sheafy (anchor Layer 4).

Spa(A/J) → Spa(A) is a closed embedding with image {v : J ⊆ supp v} = Supp(Ã/J̃) (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.isClosedEmbedding_spaComap_quotientHom, tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.range_spaComap_quotientHom).

i_*𝒪_{Spa(A/J)} ≅ (A/J)~ as 𝒪_X-algebras: rational subsets of Spa(A/J) are preimages of rational subsets of Spa(A) and 𝒪(U) ⊗_A A/J is the rational localisation of A/J (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-acyclicity-finite-modules for the module A/J).

Globalise using independence of the affinoid covering (anchor Layer 5.1) and the locality of coherent ideals; conversely a closed adic subspace is affinoid-locally Spa(A/J) with J closed (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings), whose kernel J̃ is coherent.

nodes.title: Finite morphisms correspond to coherent 𝒪_X-algebras
nodes.statement: Let X is a locally noetherian analytic adic space in the sense of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space whose points all have affinoid neighbourhoods Spa(A, A⁺) with A a complete strongly noetherian Tate ring (for instance X locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°), K a complete nonarchimedean field). The functor (f : Y → X) ↦ f_*𝒪_Y is an anti-equivalence from the category of finite morphisms of adic spaces to X (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-morphism) to the category of sheaves of 𝒪_X-algebras that are coherent as 𝒪_X-modules. Its quasi-inverse 𝒜 ↦ Spa_X(𝒜) is glued from Spa(𝒜(U), 𝒜(U)⁺) over affinoid opens U = Spa(A, A⁺), with 𝒜(U) a finite A-algebra carrying its module topology and 𝒜(U)⁺ the integral closure of the image of A⁺. Formation of Spa_X commutes with base change along morphisms X' → X.
hypotheses: X is a locally noetherian analytic adic space in the sense of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space whose points all have affinoid neighbourhoods Spa(A, A⁺) with A a complete strongly noetherian Tate ring (for instance X locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°), K a complete nonarchimedean field)
proofSteps: Affinoid case: a finite A-algebra B with module topology is complete, and (B, B⁺) is an affinoid ring finite over (A, A⁺) (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-algebra-over-affinoid).

For f = Spa(B) → Spa(A) and rational V ⊆ Spa(A), f⁻¹(V) = Spa(B ⊗_A 𝒪(V)) (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-rational-localisation; ⊗̂ = ⊗ since B is finite over the strongly noetherian A: AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-algebra-tensor-complete (iii)), so f_*𝒪_Y = B̃ as 𝒪_X-algebras.
A coherent 𝒪_X-algebra on an affinoid is B̃ with B = 𝒜(X) a finite A-algebra (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid; the multiplication 𝒜 ⊗ 𝒜 → 𝒜 is determined on global sections).
Morphisms: Hom_X(Spa B, Spa B') = Hom_{A-alg}(B', B) (continuous homomorphisms of affinoid rings over A correspond to morphisms of affinoid adic spaces; anchor Layer 5 / Huber 1994 Proposition 2.1).
Glue over an affinoid covering of X (anchor Layer 5.3); base change is the formula (B ⊗_A A')~.

nodes.title: Quasi-Stein adic spaces
nodes.statement: Let X an adic space locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°), K a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value. X is quasi-Stein if there is a sequence U₁ ⊆ U₂ ⊆ ⋯ of affinoid open subspaces with X = ⋃ₙ Uₙ such that each restriction 𝒪_X(U_{n+1}) → 𝒪_X(Uₙ) has dense image. It is Stein if moreover, for every n, Uₙ = {x ∈ U_{n+1} : |f₁(x)| ≤ 1, …, |f_r(x)| ≤ 1} is the Weierstrass domain of U_{n+1} defined by some f₁, …, f_r ∈ 𝒪_X(U_{n+1}) and there is aₙ ∈ K with 0 < |aₙ| < 1 such that f₁/aₙ, …, f_r/aₙ topologically generate the affinoid K-algebra 𝒪_X(U_{n+1}) (Kiehl's condition after Definition 2.3). The data of the exhausting sequence is not part of the predicate; theorems quantify over any such sequence.
hypotheses: X an adic space locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°), K a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value
proofSteps: The predicate is ∃ (U : ℕ → affinoid opens), monotone, covering, with dense restriction maps; 𝒪_X(Uₙ) carries its topology as a complete Tate ring (anchor Layer 3.5).
In the adic setting the covering by the open Uₙ is automatically a covering; for X = r(X_rig) this matches Kiehl's admissibility requirement through AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor.
acceptance: The open unit disc D = ⋃ₙ {|T|ⁿ ≤ |ϖ|} is quasi-Stein (indeed Stein).
Every affinoid X lft over K is quasi-Stein (constant sequence).

nodes.title: Dense restriction of coherent sections on a quasi-Stein space
nodes.statement: Let X be quasi-Stein with exhaustion (Uₙ) and F a coherent 𝒪_X-module. Then F(U_{n+1}) → F(Uₙ) has dense image for every n, and F(X) = lim F(Uₙ) → F(Uₙ) has dense image.
hypotheses: X quasi-Stein (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/quasi-stein-space)
F coherent
proofSteps: Write Aₙ = 𝒪_X(Uₙ), Mₙ = F(Uₙ); Mₙ = Aₙ ⊗_{A_{n+1}} M_{n+1} (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid on U_{n+1}, applied to the affinoid open Uₙ ⊆ U_{n+1}).
Choose a surjection A_{n+1}^r ↠ M_{n+1}; its base change Aₙ^r ↠ Mₙ is open, and A_{n+1}^r → Aₙ^r has dense image, so M_{n+1} → Mₙ has dense image (Kiehl Hilfssatz 2.5).
F(X) = lim F(Uₙ) (sheaf property for the covering by the Uₙ); a Mittag-Leffler approximation with the complete metrisable Mₙ shows the limit is dense in each Mₙ (Kiehl 2.4.1).
acceptance: For F = 𝒪 on the open disc: polynomials (hence global entire-on-the-disc functions) are dense in every 𝒪(Uₙ).

nodes.title: Kiehl's Theorem B on quasi-Stein spaces
nodes.statement: Let X be a quasi-Stein adic space lft over K and F a coherent 𝒪_X-module. Then Hⁱ(X, F) = 0 for all i > 0.
hypotheses: X quasi-Stein
F coherent
Hⁱ sheaf cohomology on the topological space X
proofSteps: Let 𝔘 = {Uₙ}. Every finite intersection of members is some U_m (increasing sequence), which is affinoid, so F is acyclic on all of them (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-acyclicity-finite-modules with AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid); hence Hⁱ(X, F) = Ȟⁱ(𝔘, F) (Leray's acyclic-cover comparison, supplied by DiamondsAndVStacks:D0).

Degree 1: a 1-cocycle reduces to g_i ∈ F(U_i) and one must solve g_i = f_i − φ_i(f_{i+1}). Choose norms with |φ_i| ≤ 1; on the Banach space of null sequences (g_i) the operator id − φ is invertible; by density (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/quasi-stein-dense-restriction) modify the cocycle so that |g_i| → 0 (Kiehl §2).

Degree ≥ 2: C(𝔘, F) = lim C(𝔘_i, F|_{U_i}) with 𝔘_i = {U₁,…,U_i} a covering of U_i; each C(𝔘_i, F|_{U_i}) is acyclic (affinoid acyclicity), transition maps surjective, and the maps on (n−1)-cycles are surjective, so lim commutes with Hⁿ (Kiehl Hilfssatz 2.6).
acceptance: For F = 𝒪 on the open unit disc D, H¹(D, 𝒪) = 0, computed with the exhaustion Uₙ = {|T|ⁿ ≤ |ϖ|}; for the punctured open disc D ∖ {0} (also quasi-Stein, exhausted by annuli) H¹ vanishes as well.
For the tube ]X[ of an affine frame (quasi-Stein), coherent cohomology vanishes in positive degrees (the use in RD.3).

nodes.title: Kiehl's Theorem A on quasi-Stein spaces
nodes.statement: Let X be quasi-Stein with exhaustion (Uₙ) and F coherent. Then for every n the image of F(X) generates F(Uₙ) as an 𝒪_X(Uₙ)-module, and for every point x ∈ X the image of F(X) generates the stalk F_x as an 𝒪_{X,x}-module.
hypotheses: X quasi-Stein
F coherent
proofSteps: F(Uₙ) is a finite module over the complete Tate ring 𝒪_X(Uₙ) (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid); choose generators m₁,…,m_r.

F(X) is dense in F(Uₙ) (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/quasi-stein-dense-restriction), so there are global sections s_j arbitrarily close to m_j; close enough families still generate (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/surjection-small-perturbation).
For x ∈ Uₙ, F_x = F(Uₙ) ⊗_{𝒪(Uₙ)} 𝒪_{X,x} (F|_{Uₙ} associated), so the s_j generate F_x.

nodes.title: Coherent cohomology of the open polydisc vanishes
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field, m ≥ 0, r = (r₁,…,r_m) ∈ ℝ_{>0}^m and D = ⋃_{ρ} {x ∈ A^{m,ad}_K : |T_i(x)| ≤ ρ_i for all i}, the union over ρ ∈ ∏_i (0, r_i) with ρ_i ∈ √|K^×|, the open polydisc (pointwise: |T_i(x̃)| < r_i for the maximal generization x̃ of x; the naive set {x : |T_i(x)| < r_i} would also contain the rank-2 points below the boundary Gauss points, which lie in no closed subpolydisc). For every coherent 𝒪_D-module F, Hⁱ(D, F) = 0 for i > 0, and F(D) generates every stalk; in particular Hⁱ(D, 𝒪_D) = 0 for i > 0.
hypotheses: K complete nonarchimedean, nontrivially valued
F coherent on D
proofSteps: Choose ρ_{i,n} ∈ √|K^×| increasing to r_i; Dₙ = {|T_i| ≤ ρ_{i,n}} are affinoid (Weierstrass domains of D_{n+1}) and exhaust D.
𝒪(D_{n+1}) → 𝒪(Dₙ) has dense image (polynomials are dense in both), so D is quasi-Stein (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/quasi-stein-space, API isQuasiStein_openPolydisc).

nodes.title: Vector bundles (locally free sheaves of finite rank) on adic spaces
nodes.statement: Let X be an adic space (anchor Layer 5; 𝒪_X is a sheaf). A vector bundle on X is a sheaf of 𝒪_X-modules E such that X has an open covering {U_i} with E|_{U_i} ≅ 𝒪_{U_i}^{n_i} for some n_i ∈ ℕ; equivalently E satisfies Mathlib's SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFree with local bases of finite type. The rank is the locally constant function x ↦ n_i on U_i. Vector bundles form the full subcategory VectorBundle(X) of 𝒪_X-modules. No noetherian hypothesis is imposed; on locally noetherian X every vector bundle is coherent, but not conversely.
hypotheses: X an adic space (structure presheaf a sheaf)
proofSteps: Define the predicate by existence of local trivialisations of finite rank on an open covering (Mathlib SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData with IsLocallyFreeData and finite index sets).
The rank is well defined on overlaps because a free module of finite rank over a nonzero commutative ring has a well-defined rank; it is locally constant by construction.
acceptance: On Spa(A, A⁺) with A = A₁ × A₂, the module A₁ × 0 gives a vector bundle of rank 1 on Spa(A₁) and rank 0 on Spa(A₂).
(K⟨T⟩/(T))~ on the closed disc is coherent but not a vector bundle.

nodes.title: The coherent sheaf of continuous differentials Ω¹_{X/Y} and its exterior powers
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism locally of finite type (anchor Layer 5.2) between locally noetherian analytic adic spaces (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space). There is a coherent O_X-module Ω¹_{X/Y} (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/coherent-sheaf) with an f⁻¹O_Y-linear derivation d = d_{X/Y}: O_X → Ω¹_{X/Y}, characterised as follows. For every pair of affinoid opens U = Spa(B, B⁺) ⊆ X and V = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ Y with f(U) ⊆ V and A → B topologically of finite type (such U cover X), Ω¹_{X/Y}|_U ≅ (Ωᶜ_{B/A})~ (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/associated-module-sheaf), with d = d_{B/A} on sections over U (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/continuous-differentials). The identifications on a rational U' = Spa(B⟨T/s⟩) ⊆ U are the localisation isomorphisms Ωᶜ_{B⟨T/s⟩/A} ≅ B⟨T/s⟩ ⊗_B Ωᶜ_{B/A}. Shrinking V to a rational V' ⊇ f(U), A' = A⟨T'/s'⟩, does not change Ωᶜ_{B/A} = Ωᶜ_{B/A'}. Properties: (a) universal property: for every coherent O_X-module F, Hom_{O_X}(Ω¹_{X/Y}, F) is the set of f⁻¹O_Y-linear derivations D: O_X → F that are continuous on sections over affinoid opens, via u ↦ u ∘ d; (b) exact sequences: for X → Y → Z (both locally of finite type) the sequence f*Ω¹_{Y/Z} → Ω¹_{X/Z} → Ω¹_{X/Y} → 0 is exact, and for a closed embedding i: X → P over Y with coherent ideal 𝓘 (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/coherent-ideal-closed-subspace), 𝓘/𝓘² → i*Ω¹_{P/Y} → Ω¹_{X/Y} → 0 is exact; (c) f is unramified iff Ω¹_{X/Y} = 0; if f is smooth of relative dimension n at x, Ω¹_{X/Y} is a vector bundle of rank n near x (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/locally-free-sheaf), and for X → Y → Z with f smooth the sequence of (b) is left exact and locally split; if f is étale, f*Ω¹_{Y/Z} ≅ Ω¹_{X/Z}, in particular u*Ω¹_{X/Y} ≅ Ω¹_{U/Y} for every étale u: U → X, which makes U ↦ Ω¹_{U/Y}(U) a sheaf on the small étale site of X; (d) base change: for a cartesian square X' = X ×_Y Y' (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence) with projection p: X' → X, p*Ω¹_{X/Y} ≅ Ω¹_{X'/Y'} compatibly with d; (e) analytification: for a morphism h of schemes locally of finite type over a complete nonarchimedean field K, Ω¹_{X^ad/Y^ad} ≅ (Ω¹_{X/Y})^ad compatibly with d (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytic-kahler-differentials); (f) exterior powers: Ωⁱ_{X/Y} := ⋀ⁱ_{O_X} Ω¹_{X/Y}, the sheaf associated with U ↦ ⋀ⁱ_{O(U)} Ω¹_{X/Y}(U), is coherent, with sections (⋀ⁱ_B Ωᶜ_{B/A})~ over U as above; for f smooth of relative dimension n it is a vector bundle of rank C(n, i); d extends uniquely to f⁻¹O_Y-linear maps d: Ωⁱ_{X/Y} → Ωⁱ⁺¹_{X/Y} with d ∘ d = 0 and d(ω ∧ η) = dω ∧ η + (−1)ⁱ ω ∧ dη, the relative de Rham complex Ω•_{X/Y}. Conventions: this is the coherent sheaf of the continuous differentials of R0 (Huber 1996 (1.6.2)); Mathlib's algebraic KaehlerDifferential of the rings O_X(U) is not the object (it is not finitely generated). The Kähler differentials of rigid and dagger spaces (Grosse-Klönne) and the log differentials of Diao–Lan–Liu–Zhu with trivial log structures are the same sheaf. The sheaf on the étale site in (c) and the pro-étale sheaves built from it are AdicEtaleGeometry A2's and PadicHodgeTheory's.
hypotheses: f: X → Y locally of finite type; X, Y locally noetherian analytic adic spaces (every point has an affinoid neighbourhood with a strongly noetherian complete Tate ring)
For (b): the second morphism locally of finite type; for (c): f unramified, smooth or étale as in R0; for (d): the hypotheses of R0/fibre-products-existence, case (a)
proofSteps: Local pieces: for U, V as in the statement, Ωᶜ_{B/A} is a finite B-module (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/continuous-differentials (a)), and B is strongly noetherian Tate, so (Ωᶜ_{B/A})~ is a coherent sheaf on U (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/associated-module-sheaf, AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-acyclicity-finite-modules, AdicSpacesPartII:R3/coherent-sheaf).

Gluing data: on a rational U' = Spa(B⟨T/s⟩) ⊆ U the restriction (Ωᶜ_{B/A})~|_{U'} is (B⟨T/s⟩ ⊗_B Ωᶜ_{B/A})~ (API tildeRestrictIso), which is (Ωᶜ_{B⟨T/s⟩/A})~ by the localisation isomorphism of R0/continuous-differentials (API localizationEquiv). Independence of V: if A' = A⟨T'/s'⟩ with f(U) ⊆ Spa A', every continuous A-derivation of B kills the dense image of A[T'/s'] (D(t/s) = (s·Dt − t·Ds)/s² = 0), hence A', so Ωᶜ_{B/A} = Ωᶜ_{B/A'}. Two affinoid opens intersect in a union of opens that are rational in both, so the isomorphisms satisfy the cocycle condition on triple intersections; the sheaves glue along the open cover (anchor Layer 5.3; sheaves of modules glue on open covers), and the derivations d_{B/A} glue to d.

Independence of choices and (a): a coherent F is (F(U))~ on each affinoid U (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid), and a derivation continuous on sections is, on each U, a continuous A-derivation B → F(U), which factors uniquely through Ωᶜ_{B/A} (API lift of R0/continuous-differentials; F(U) is complete and Hausdorff as a finite module over the noetherian B). These factorisations are compatible with restriction, so glue to a unique O_X-linear map (morphisms of sheaves are local). Applied to another choice of covering, this gives a unique isomorphism compatible with d.

(b): on affinoid pieces these are the first fundamental and conormal sequences of R0/first-fundamental-sequence and R0/conormal-sequence; M ↦ M̃ is exact (API tilde_exact) and pullback of coherent sheaves is computed by M ⊗_A B on affinoids (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/coherent-sheaf-operations, API pullback_tilde); exactness of sheaves is local.

(c): unramified ⇔ Ωᶜ = 0 on affinoid pieces (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/infinitesimal-criteria). Smooth: Ωᶜ is finite free of rank n on small affinoid neighbourhoods (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-differentials-locally-free); locally f is étale over a relative polydisc (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-local-structure), and the differential criterion (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/differential-criterion-morphism) makes the sequence of (b) split injective on the left. Étale: Ω¹_{X/Y} = 0 and the sequence of (b) is left exact, so f*Ω¹_{Y/Z} ≅ Ω¹_{X/Z}; for u: U → X étale and X → Y this gives u*Ω¹_{X/Y} ≅ Ω¹_{U/Y}, and the étale-sheaf property follows from these isomorphisms and the sheaf property of coherent sheaves for étale covers of affinoids (for the finite étale pieces: faithfully flat descent for arbitrary modules — exactness of M → M ⊗_A B ⇉ M ⊗_A B ⊗_A B for A → B faithfully flat, KL Theorem 1.3.4, the input imported by AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-projective-etale-descent from tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves#0e-effective-descent-and-spreading-out; that node's statement covers only finite projective modules, while Ω¹_{X/Y} need not be projective when f is not smooth; R0/etale-local-open-finite-etale-factorisation for the local structure).

(d): on affinoid charts with adic base change, Ωᶜ_{(B ⊗̂_A A')/A'} ≅ (B ⊗̂_A A') ⊗_B Ωᶜ_{B/A} (R0/continuous-differentials, API baseChangeEquiv); along a non-adic Y' → Y the charts W_m of R0/fibre-product-along-finite-type have the presentation of B with the same generators dXᵢ and relations (R0/continuous-differentials (c)); these glue by the uniqueness in (a). Stability of smooth and étale morphisms under the same base change is AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-etale-base-change.

(e): AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytic-kahler-differentials gives the isomorphism on the affine charts of the analytification (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-of-modules for (·)^ad); by (a) it agrees with the glued sheaf.

(f): the exterior power of a coherent sheaf is coherent (it is (⋀ⁱ_B M)~ on affinoid pieces, M finite; Mathlib exteriorPower, compatible with base change B → B⟨T/s⟩), and ⋀ⁱ of a free module of rank n is free of rank C(n, i). The de Rham differential is defined on affinoid pieces by d(b db₁ ∧ … ∧ dbᵢ) = db ∧ db₁ ∧ … ∧ dbᵢ, well defined by the universal property of Ωᶜ and d(db) = 0, and it commutes with the localisation isomorphisms; d ∘ d = 0 and the Leibniz rule are checked on these generators.

nodes.title: Finite projective glueing data on a glueing square are effective
nodes.statement: Let R → R₁, R₂ → R₁₂ be a glueing square (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/glueing-square) and (M₁, M₂, M₁₂) a finite projective glueing datum with section module M. Then M is a finite projective R-module and the natural maps M ⊗_R R_i → M_i are isomorphisms.
hypotheses: glueing square with conditions (a)–(c)
M₁, M₂, M₁₂ finite projective
proofSteps: By AdicSpacesPartII:R3/glueing-square-finite-surjectivity, M ⊗ R₁ → M₁ is surjective for every finite projective datum, which is the hypothesis of KL Lemma 1.3.9.

KL Lemma 1.3.9(a): choose M₀ and F ↠ M₀ free; the kernels N_i of F_i ↠ M_i are finite projective and form a glueing datum (splitting of F_i ↠ M_i); a diagram chase shows M is finitely presented and M ⊗ R_i ≅ M_i.

KL Lemma 1.3.9(b): M is flat at every maximal ideal of R because each maximal ideal is the contraction of a prime of R₁ × R₂ (condition (c)) and M ⊗ R_i is projective; finitely presented and pointwise free gives finite projective (KL Definition 1.1.2(c)).
acceptance: On the Laurent square of ℚ_p⟨T⟩, the datum (R₁, R₂, R₁₂) twisted by Tᵏ glues to a free module of rank one.

nodes.title: Kiehl glueing of finite projective modules over sheafy Tate affinoids
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Tate Huber pair which is sheafy (its structure presheaf is a sheaf on every rational subset). For every rational subset U = Spa(B, B⁺) of X = Spa(A, A⁺), the functor P ↦ P̃ (P̃(V) = P ⊗_B 𝒪_X(V) on rational V ⊆ U) is an equivalence from finite projective B-modules to vector bundles on U (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/locally-free-sheaf), with quasi-inverse E ↦ E(U); it is compatible with ⊗, duals and pullback along rational localisations. The Tate sheaf property of 𝒪_X (Čech acyclicity on all rational coverings of rational subsets, KL Theorem 2.4.23) is AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheafy-cech-acyclicity. No noetherian hypothesis is made; since rational localisation need not be flat (e.g. for perfectoid A), only finite projective modules are glued.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) complete Tate and sheafy
modules finite projective
proofSteps: P̃ is a sheaf with P̃(U) = P for finite projective P (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-projective-module-acyclicity), so the functor is fully faithful (Hom(P̃, Q̃) = Hom_B(P, Q) since P̃ is a direct summand of 𝒪ⁿ).

Essential surjectivity: property P(𝔘) = 'every vector bundle trivialised as P̃_i on the members of 𝔘 is P̃ for a finite projective P' is local and transitive, and holds for simple Laurent coverings by AdicSpacesPartII:R3/simple-laurent-glueing-square and AdicSpacesPartII:R3/glueing-square-finite-projective-descent; AdicSpacesPartII:R3/rational-covering-reduction gives all finite rational coverings.

A vector bundle is trivial on an open covering, refined by a finite standard rational covering (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.exists_span_eq_top_forall_rationalSubset_subset_of_isTateRing), on whose members it is 𝒪ⁿ = (Bⁿ)~.
Structure-sheaf acyclicity is AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheafy-cech-acyclicity (KL Theorem 2.4.23); the sheafiness hypothesis is the anchor's predicate `Huber.IsSheafyPair` (Layer 3.4).
acceptance: For A an affinoid K-algebra, vector bundles on Spa(A, A°) are finite projective A-modules.
For a perfectoid affinoid (A, A⁺) (sheafy by PerfectoidSpaces), vector bundles are finite projective A-modules even though A → A⟨f/g⟩ is not flat in general.
Line bundles on the closed disc Spa(K⟨T⟩) are trivial (K⟨T⟩ is a PID).

nodes.title: Acyclicity of P̃ for finite projective P over a sheafy Tate affinoid
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a complete sheafy Tate Huber pair, X = Spa(A, A⁺) and P a finite projective A-module. Then P̃ (P ⊗_A 𝒪_X(V) on rational V, extended by limits) is a sheaf, for every rational U and every finite rational covering 𝔘 of U the augmented Čech complex of P̃ is exact, P̃(U) = P ⊗_A 𝒪_X(U), and Hⁱ(U, P̃) = 0 for i > 0.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) complete Tate, sheafy
P finite projective
proofSteps: Construction: AdicSpacesPartII:R3/associated-module-sheaf builds M̃ only over noetherian A (noetherian ring of definition or strongly noetherian Tate), so it does not apply here. For finite projective P over an arbitrary complete Tate A put P̃(V) = P ⊗_A 𝒪_X(V) on rational V, with the topology of a direct summand of 𝒪_X(V)ⁿ (for any splitting Aⁿ = P ⊕ Q; the summand is closed, being the kernel of the continuous idempotent, and the topology does not depend on the splitting), restriction id_P ⊗ ρ_{V,W}, and extend to all opens by limits as for 𝒪_X; then P̃ ⊕ Q̃ ≅ 𝒪_Xⁿ as presheaves of topological 𝒪_X-modules.
P is a direct summand of Aⁿ (KL Definition 1.1.2(b)); the Čech complex of P̃ is a direct summand of that of 𝒪ⁿ, termwise P ⊗_A (−).

The augmented Čech complexes of 𝒪_X on finite rational coverings of rational subsets are exact and Hⁱ(U, 𝒪_X) = 0 for i > 0 (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheafy-cech-acyclicity, Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 2.4.23); direct summands of exact complexes are exact.
Sheaf-cohomology vanishing likewise passes to the direct summand P̃ of 𝒪ⁿ.
acceptance: For P = A the lemma is the Tate sheaf property of 𝒪_X.
For A = A₁ × A₂ and P = A₁ × 0, P̃ is 𝒪 on Spa(A₁) and 0 on Spa(A₂).

nodes.title: Descent of finite projective modules along finite étale covers of affinoids
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) be a morphism of complete Tate Huber pairs with (A, A⁺) and (B, B⁺) sheafy (automatic when A is strongly noetherian, e.g. an affinoid K-algebra, since B is then finite over A and strongly noetherian), B a finite étale A-algebra which is faithfully flat over A (B⁺ the integral closure of A⁺), so that Spa(B, B⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) is a finite étale surjection. Then P ↦ (P ⊗_A B, canonical descent datum on B ⊗_A B) is an equivalence from finite projective A-modules to finite projective B-modules with an effective-descent datum relative to A → B; consequently the stack of vector bundles for the analytic topology satisfies descent for finite étale surjections of affinoids.
hypotheses: A, B sheafy complete Tate (e.g. A strongly noetherian)

nodes.title: Uniformity of a Banach ring via the square bound, and its relation to boundedness of A°
nodes.statement: Let A be a complete Tate ring metrised by a submultiplicative norm |·| defining its topology (KL Remark 2.4.4), for instance the norm α_d of a norm datum (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/tate-ring-norm). (i) The following are equivalent: (a) |·| is equivalent to a power-multiplicative norm; (b) |·| is equivalent to the spectral seminorm |x|_sp = lim |xⁿ|^{1/n} (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-seminorm); (c) there is c > 0 with |x²| ≥ c|x|² for all x. A is a uniform Banach ring when they hold (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 2.8.1 as corrected in Kedlaya–Liu II, Appendix A). (ii) (a)–(c) imply (d): the subring A° of power-bounded elements is bounded; and (d) alone implies that |·|_sp is a norm defining the topology of A. (iii) If A contains a topologically nilpotent unit z with |z|·|z⁻¹| = 1, then (d) implies (a)–(c). This holds for the norms α_d, with z = ϖ: α_d(ϖ) = r and α_d(ϖ⁻¹) = r⁻¹ when A ≠ 0 is Hausdorff (R0/tate-ring-norm, API tateNorm_pseudoUniformizer_mul). So for a complete Tate ring the topological condition (d), which is uniformity in the anchor (Layer 4.2) and in Hansen–Kedlaya Definition 2.3, is equivalent to (a)–(c) for every norm α_d. (iv) Without the hypothesis of (iii), (d) does not imply (a)–(c): on a complete nonarchimedean field K the function |x|' = |x| for |x| ≤ 1 and |x|' = |x|(1 + log|x|) for |x| > 1 is a submultiplicative norm defining the topology of K, with K° bounded, and it is not equivalent to its spectral norm |·| (Kedlaya–Liu II, Appendix A). Kedlaya–Liu I, Definition 2.8.1 states the four conditions as equivalent for every Banach ring; that is false, and only (i)–(iii) are asserted here.
hypotheses: A complete Tate ring with a submultiplicative norm defining its topology
For (iii): a topologically nilpotent unit z with |z|·|z⁻¹| = 1 (automatic for the norms α_d of R0/tate-ring-norm)
proofSteps: (a)⇒(c): for a power-multiplicative norm |x²|' = |x|'²; transport the constant through the equivalence.
(c)⇒(b): iterating gives |x^{2^k}| ≥ c^{2^k − 1}|x|^{2^k}, so |x|_sp = lim_k |x^{2^k}|^{2^{−k}} ≥ c|x|; since |x|_sp ≤ |x| always, the spectral seminorm is a norm equivalent to |·|.
(b)⇒(a): the spectral seminorm is power-multiplicative (Mathlib isPowMul_smoothingFun, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-seminorm).

(b)⇒(d): a power-bounded x has |x|_sp ≤ 1 (bounded |xⁿ|), so A° ⊆ {|·|_sp ≤ 1} ⊆ {|·| ≤ C}, which is bounded because |·| defines the topology. (d) ⇒ |·|_sp defines the topology: {|·|_sp < 1} = A°° (R0/spectral-seminorm, API spectralSeminorm_lt_one_iff) and, A° being bounded, the sets zⁿA°° form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0 (R0/spectral-topology (vi)).

(iii): from |z||z⁻¹| = 1 and submultiplicativity, |zx| ≤ |z||x| ≤ |z||z⁻¹||zx| = |zx|, so |zⁿx| = |z|ⁿ|x| for n ∈ ℤ, and likewise |zⁿx|_sp = |z|ⁿ|x|_sp. Let A° ⊆ {|·| ≤ C}. If |x|_sp > 0, choose n ∈ ℤ with |z|^{n+1} < |x|_sp ≤ |z|ⁿ; then y = z^{1−n}x has |y|_sp ≤ |z| < 1, so y is topologically nilpotent, hence power-bounded, and |y| ≤ C gives |x| = |z|^{n−1}|y| ≤ C|z|^{−2}|x|_sp. If |x|_sp = 0, the same argument gives |z^{−n}x| ≤ C for all n, so x = 0. Hence |·| ≤ C|z|^{−2}|·|_sp, which is (b).

(iv) is the example of Kedlaya–Liu II, Appendix A: the norm |·|' dominates |·|, its spectral norm is |·| (|x|'^{1/n} of xⁿ tends to |x|), and |x|'/|x| = 1 + log|x| is unbounded; K° is the unit ball of |·|, bounded for |·|'.
acceptance: K⟨T⟩ with the Gauss norm is uniform; K[ε]/(ε²) with any Banach norm is not: every aε (a ∈ K) squares to 0, so A° ⊇ K·ε is unbounded.
Non-example to the four-way equivalence: K = ℚ_p with |x|' = |x| for |x| ≤ 1 and |x|(1 + log|x|) otherwise satisfies (d) but not (a)–(c); here |p|'·|p⁻¹|' = 1 + log p > 1, so (iii) does not apply.

nodes.title: A split injection into a stably uniform ring gives stable uniformity (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 2.8.12)
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) be a continuous morphism of complete Tate Huber pairs such that B is stably uniform (every rational localisation of (B, B⁺) is uniform) and A → B splits as a map of topological A-modules (there is a continuous A-linear s : B → A with s|_A = id). Then (A, A⁺) is stably uniform, hence sheafy by the Buzzard–Verberkmoes theorem (anchor Layer 4.2). Similarly, if A is a complete Tate algebra over a complete nonarchimedean field K, K → L an extension of complete nonarchimedean fields and A ⊗̂_K L stably uniform, then A is stably uniform.
hypotheses: A, B complete Tate
B stably uniform
A → B has a continuous A-linear retraction
proofSteps: Uniformity of A: norm A by α_d and B by α_{d'} with d' = (B₀, image of ϖ, r) (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/tate-ring-norm). B° is bounded and |ϖ|·|ϖ⁻¹| = 1 for α_{d'}, so B satisfies criterion (c), |x²|_B ≥ c|x|_B² (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/uniform-iff-power-bound (iii)). A split injection of Banach A-modules is strict (s bounded), so |x²|_A ≍ |x²|_B ≥ c|x|_B² ≍ c|x|_A²; hence A satisfies (c), and A° is bounded (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/uniform-iff-power-bound (ii)).

The splitting persists under rational localisation: for a rational localisation A → A' = A⟨T/s⟩ with B' = B ⊗̂_A A' (the rational localisation of B at the image of (T, s); AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-rational-localisation), s ⊗̂ id_{A'} is a continuous A'-linear retraction of A' → B' (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product).
Hence every rational localisation of A is uniform: A is stably uniform; sheafiness is the anchor's Buzzard–Verberkmoes theorem.

Field-extension variant: A → A ⊗̂_K L is a strict injection (KL Lemma 2.2.9(c), K → L being isometric; AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-banach-module (d)), which already suffices for criterion (c); every rational localisation B of A has B ⊗̂_K L a rational localisation of A ⊗̂_K L (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-rational-localisation) and B → B ⊗̂_K L is again strict.
acceptance: Sousperfectoid rings (ScholzeWeinstein Berkeley Definition 6.3.1) are stably uniform and sheafy: R → R̃ perfectoid splits as topological R-modules (Berkeley Proposition 6.3.4, owned by AdicSpacesPartII:R5).
RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0: the chart ring B_{S,[0,n]} splits off B_{S,[0,n]} ⊗̂_{O_E} O_{E∞}, which is perfectoid, so the chart is stably uniform and sheafy.

nodes.title: Spectral norms of uniform rings and isometric maps
nodes.statement: Let A → B be a continuous homomorphism of uniform complete Tate rings (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/uniform-iff-power-bound), each equipped with its spectral norm (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-seminorm; B carries the norm datum (B₀, φ(ϖ), r) with φ(A₀) ⊆ B₀, so that the spectral seminorms are compatible). Then |φ(x)|_sp ≤ |x|_sp for all x (φ is submetric); φ is isometric if and only if the image of the induced map of Gel'fand spectra M(B) → M(A) is a boundary for A (for every x ∈ A, max_{β∈M(B)} β(φ(x)) = max_{α∈M(A)} α(x)); in particular φ is isometric when M(B) → M(A) is surjective. Surjectivity is not necessary: K⟨T⟩ → K⟨T, T⁻¹⟩ is isometric for the spectral (Gauss) norms while M(K⟨T, T⁻¹⟩) → M(K⟨T⟩) misses the points with |T| < 1 (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 2.8.3(a) states 'if and only if', which is false). Here |x|_sp = max_{α ∈ M(A)} α(x) (Berkovich's spectral radius theorem, KL Theorem 2.3.10, supplied with M(A) by TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0).
hypotheses: A, B uniform complete Tate rings
spectral norms
M(·) the Gel'fand (Berkovich) spectrum of bounded multiplicative seminorms
proofSteps: Submetric: |φ(xⁿ)| ≤ C|xⁿ| for the bounded φ; take n-th roots and n → ∞.

Isometry criterion: by the spectral radius theorem (from TB.0), |x|_sp = max_{α∈M(A)} α(x) and |φ(x)|_sp = max_{β∈M(B)} β(φ(x)) = max over the image of M(B) → M(A) of α(x); so φ is isometric iff the image is a boundary, and in particular if M(B) → M(A) is surjective.

The spectral norm of a uniform complete Tate ring (A° bounded) is a norm defining its topology, and it is equivalent to α_d (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/uniform-iff-power-bound (ii), (iii); |ϖ|·|ϖ⁻¹| = 1 for α_d), so 'isometric' is meaningful for the chosen norms.
acceptance: For A = K⟨T⟩ → B = K⟨T/ϖ⟩ (restriction to the disc |T| ≤ |ϖ|), M(B) → M(A) misses the Gauss point and the map is not isometric: |T|_{sp,A} = 1 while |T|_{sp,B} = |ϖ|.
For A → A ⊗̂_K L (L/K an extension of complete nonarchimedean fields) M(A_L) → M(A) is surjective, so the map is isometric for the spectral norms.

For A = K⟨T⟩ → B = K⟨T, T⁻¹⟩ (restriction to the annulus |T| = 1): |Σ aₙTⁿ|_{sp,B} = max|aₙ| = |Σ aₙTⁿ|_{sp,A}, so the map is isometric, but the image of M(B) is {|T| = 1} ≠ M(A): the image contains the Gauss (Shilov boundary) point, which is all isometry needs.

nodes.title: Completely continuous maps of Banach modules over an affinoid algebra
nodes.statement: Let K a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value; adic spaces are locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°); A denotes an affinoid K-algebra (a quotient of some K⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩, strongly noetherian Tate) with A⁺ = A°, and fix a ring of definition A₀ ⊆ A containing the image of K°. A Banach A-module is a complete topological A-module M whose topology is defined by an open A₀-submodule M₀ (so the ϖⁿM₀ form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0), with the norm |m| = inf{|a| : a ∈ K, m ∈ aM₀}. A continuous A-linear map f : M → N of Banach A-modules is completely continuous if it is the limit, in the operator norm, of continuous A-linear maps f_i : M → N with finitely generated image. It is strictly completely continuous if there are such f_i and a ∈ K° ∖ {0} such that for every i, a·f_i(M₀) lies in some finitely generated A₀-submodule of N₀, which may depend on i (Kiehl's 'streng vollständig stetig': 'in einem — von i abhängigen — endlichen B₀-Untermodul von N₀'); the scalar a, and hence the bound a·f_i(M₀) ⊆ N₀, is uniform in i.
hypotheses: K a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value; adic spaces are locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°); A denotes an affinoid K-algebra (a quotient of some K⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩, strongly noetherian Tate) with A⁺ = A°
M, N Banach A-modules
f continuous A-linear
proofSteps: The operator norm on continuous A-linear maps is the norm induced by M₀ and N₀; completely continuous maps form the closure of the finite-rank maps (Kiehl, Definition 1.1).
The strict variant is a condition on a fixed approximating sequence and a scalar a; it implies complete continuity.
acceptance: Over A = K, the restriction K⟨T⟩ → K⟨T/ϖ⟩ is strictly completely continuous.
Over A = K, the identity of K⟨T⟩ is not completely continuous (over A = K⟨T⟩ it is, having finitely generated image).

nodes.title: The Schwartz finiteness theorem over affinoid algebras
nodes.statement: Let K a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value; adic spaces are locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°); A denotes an affinoid K-algebra (a quotient of some K⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩, strongly noetherian Tate) with A⁺ = A°. If f : M → N is a continuous surjective A-linear map of Banach A-modules and g : M → N is completely continuous, then (f + g)(M) is closed in N and N/(f + g)(M) is a finitely generated A-module.
hypotheses: K a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value; adic spaces are locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°); A denotes an affinoid K-algebra (a quotient of some K⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩, strongly noetherian Tate) with A⁺ = A°
f continuous surjective
g completely continuous
proofSteps: Choose finite-rank g_i → g; for i large h = f + (g − g_i) is surjective (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/surjection-small-perturbation).

f + g = h + g_i with g_i of finite rank: with H = ker h and K' = ker g_i (closed of finite index, as g_i(M) is finitely generated and every submodule of a finite A-module is closed), (h + g_i)(K') = h(K' + H) is closed of finite index; hence so is (f + g)(M) (Kiehl, proof of Satz 1.2).
acceptance: For M = N = K⟨T⟩, f = id and g = −h with h(T) = ϖT (strictly completely continuous), (id − h)(Σ aₙTⁿ) = Σ aₙ(1 − ϖⁿ)Tⁿ has closed image T·K⟨T⟩ and cokernel K.

nodes.title: Strict complete continuity descends to a closed submodule for topologically free sources
nodes.statement: Let K a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value; adic spaces are locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°); A denotes an affinoid K-algebra (a quotient of some K⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩, strongly noetherian Tate) with A⁺ = A°. Let f : M → N be A-linear, N ⊆ G a closed submodule of a Banach A-module, and suppose j ∘ f : M → G is strictly completely continuous. If M is topologically free (the completed direct sum of copies of A with respect to A₀), then f : M → N is strictly completely continuous. Every Banach A-module is the image of a continuous surjection from a topologically free one.
hypotheses: K a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value; adic spaces are locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°); A denotes an affinoid K-algebra (a quotient of some K⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩, strongly noetherian Tate) with A⁺ = A°
N closed in G
M topologically free
proofSteps: Normalise so that f(M₀) ⊆ N₀ := G₀ ∩ N. Given 0 < ε < 1 choose an approximant h of j∘f with |j∘f − h| ≤ ε/2 and h(M₀) inside a finitely generated A₀-submodule of G₀. By Kiehl's Satz 5.1 (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/almost-noetherian-integral-affinoid-modules) there are m₁,…,m_r ∈ M₀ and τ ∈ K° with ½ < |τ| < 1 and ε/(2|τ|) ≤ ε (τ = 1 if K is discretely valued) such that τ·h(M₀) ⊆ Σ_j A₀h(m_j). Writing τh(e_s) = Σ_j a_j^s h(m_j) with a_j^s ∈ A₀, put g(e_s) = τ⁻¹Σ_j a_j^s f(m_j) ∈ N; as M is topologically free on the e_s and these values are bounded, g extends to a continuous A-linear M → N with |f − g| ≤ ε and a·g(M₀) ⊆ Σ_j A₀ f(m_j) ⊆ N₀ for all a ∈ K° with |a| ≤ ½ (Kiehl pp. 200-201). Letting ε → 0 shows f is strictly completely continuous (uniform scalar a with |a| ≤ ½).
Topologically free sources: a surjection from a free A₀-module onto M₀ extends to the completion (Kiehl, after Satz 1.4).
acceptance: For G = K⟨T⟩, N = T·K⟨T⟩ and M topologically free, a strictly completely continuous map into G landing in N is strictly completely continuous into N.

nodes.title: Proper morphisms to an affinoid admit relatively compact affinoid covers
nodes.statement: Let K a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value; adic spaces are locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°); A denotes an affinoid K-algebra (a quotient of some K⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩, strongly noetherian Tate) with A⁺ = A°. Let f : X → Spa(A, A°) be a proper morphism of adic spaces (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/universally-closed-and-proper-morphism). Then X is quasi-compact and separated over A. If moreover K° is discretely valued (or, for general K, granting Temkin's comparison 'adic proper ⇒ Kiehl-proper', which no source in this packet states; AdicSpacesPartII:R1/proper-separated-comparisons (iii) records it as a gap), there are finite affinoid open coverings {U_i}_{i=1..r}, {V_i}_{i=1..r} of X with V_i ⋐_A U_i for every i; that is, r⁻¹(f) is proper in Kiehl's sense. Conversely a Kiehl-proper morphism is proper (for every K).
hypotheses: K a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value; adic spaces are locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°); A denotes an affinoid K-algebra (a quotient of some K⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩, strongly noetherian Tate) with A⁺ = A°
f proper (adic sense: +weakly finite type, separated, universally closed)
proofSteps: Proper morphisms are quasi-compact (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/separated-proper-partially-proper, proper ⇔ partially proper and quasi-compact).

Comparison of adic properness with Kiehl-properness for morphisms of rigid spaces (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/proper-separated-comparisons, Huber 1996 Remark 1.3.19(iv)): Kiehl-proper ⇒ proper for every K; proper ⇒ Kiehl-proper when K° is discretely valued (Lütkebohmert). For non-discretely valued K the converse is Temkin's theorem; Conrad's Appendix A.1 lists other consequences of Temkin's work (algebraic ⇔ analytic properness, stability under composition) but not this comparison, so it remains an external input (gap) for general K.

nodes.title: Restriction along a relatively compact inclusion is strictly completely continuous
nodes.statement: Let K a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value; adic spaces are locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°); A denotes an affinoid K-algebra (a quotient of some K⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩, strongly noetherian Tate) with A⁺ = A°, U = Spa(B) and V = Spa(C) affinoid over Spa(A) with V ⋐_A U, and F a coherent sheaf on U with M = F(U), N = F(V) = M ⊗_B C (finite modules with their Banach topologies). Then there is a continuous surjection M' ↠ M from a topologically free Banach A-module such that the composite M' → M → N is strictly completely continuous over A. The same holds for finite intersections of such pairs inside an A-separated space.
hypotheses: K a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value; adic spaces are locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°); A denotes an affinoid K-algebra (a quotient of some K⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩, strongly noetherian Tate) with A⁺ = A°
V ⋐_A U
F coherent on U
proofSteps: Choose U ↪ Dⁿ_A with V ⊆ {|X_i| ≤ ε}; after a finite extension of K (harmless: finite field extensions preserve all notions, Kiehl) choose a ∈ K with ε ≤ |a| < 1; then B → C factors through h_a : A⟨X⟩ → A⟨X⟩, X ↦ aX.
h_a = Σ_ν u_ν(·) X^ν a^{|ν|} is strictly completely continuous (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/completely-continuous-map, API isStrictlyCompletelyContinuous_tsum).
Every finite B-module is a quotient of a finite free one; pass to a topologically free cover and use AdicSpacesPartII:R3/strictly-completely-continuous-closed-target.

nodes.title: Finiteness of coherent cohomology over an affinoid base (Kiehl Satz 2.6)
nodes.statement: Let K a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value; adic spaces are locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°); A denotes an affinoid K-algebra (a quotient of some K⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩, strongly noetherian Tate) with A⁺ = A°, f : X → Spa(A, A°) proper and F a coherent 𝒪_X-module. Then Hⁱ(X, F) is a finite A-module for every i, and for every finite affinoid covering 𝔘 of X the differentials of the Čech complex C•(𝔘, F) have closed image (the complex is strict).
hypotheses: K a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value; adic spaces are locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°); A denotes an affinoid K-algebra (a quotient of some K⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩, strongly noetherian Tate) with A⁺ = A°
f proper
F coherent
proofSteps: Choose coverings 𝔘 = {U_i}, 𝔙 = {V_i} with V_i ⋐_A U_i (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/proper-relatively-compact-covers); by separatedness finite intersections are affinoid and V_I ⋐_A U_I.

Both Čech complexes compute H*(X, F) because F is acyclic on affinoids (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-acyclicity-finite-modules, AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid; Leray comparison from DiamondsAndVStacks:D0), so restriction ρ : C•(𝔘) → C•(𝔙) is a quasi-isomorphism.
Kiehl Satz 2.5: there is a continuous surjection F^r ↠ C^r(𝔘) with F^r → C^r(𝔘) → C^r(𝔙) strictly completely continuous (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/restriction-strictly-completely-continuous).

Cartan–Serre (Kiehl p.205): since ρ is a quasi-isomorphism, (a, b) ↦ λ(a) + d(b) is a surjection G^r ⊕ C^{r−1}(𝔙) → Z^r(𝔙), where G^r is the preimage of Z^r(𝔘) in F^r and λ the induced map; the map (a, b) ↦ d(b) is this surjection plus (a, b) ↦ −λ(a). The latter is strictly completely continuous only as a map into C^r(𝔙) ⊇ Z^r(𝔙), so Kiehl's Korollar 1.5 is needed: pass to a topologically free cover of G^r ⊕ C^{r−1}(𝔙) on which the composite into the closed submodule Z^r(𝔙) is strictly completely continuous (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/strictly-completely-continuous-closed-target), then apply the Schwartz theorem (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/completely-continuous-finite-cokernel): d(C^{r−1}(𝔙)) is closed of finite index in Z^r(𝔙), so H^r is finite. For an arbitrary finite affinoid covering 𝔘′, H^r(𝔘′) ≅ H^r(X, F) is finite, and a submodule of Z^r(𝔘′) that is the image of a Banach module with finitely generated cokernel is closed (open mapping for C^{r−1}(𝔘′) ⊕ A^n → Z^r(𝔘′)), which gives strictness for every covering.
acceptance: For X = P^{1,an}_K → Spa(K) and F = 𝒪(−2), H¹(X, F) is one-dimensional over K (consistent with GAGA).
For a finite morphism X = Spa(B) → Spa(A), H⁰ = B is finite and Hⁱ = 0 for i > 0.

nodes.title: Completion of proper coherent cohomology (Kiehl Theorems 3.4 and 3.7)
nodes.statement: Let K a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value; adic spaces are locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°); A denotes an affinoid K-algebra (a quotient of some K⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩, strongly noetherian Tate) with A⁺ = A°, f : X → Spa(A, A°) proper, F coherent and 𝔞 ⊆ A an ideal. Then the 𝔞-adic completion of Hⁱ(X, F) is canonically isomorphic to lim_k Hⁱ(X, F/𝔞ᵏF) (Kiehl Theorem 3.7). For a principal ideal 𝔞 = (a) more precisely (Kiehl Theorem 3.4) the filtration R_k = ker(Hⁱ(X, F) → Hⁱ(X, F/aᵏF)) is a-good and the kernel and cokernel systems of Hⁱ(X, F)/aᵏ → Hⁱ(X, F/aᵏF) are null systems.
hypotheses: K a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value; adic spaces are locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°); A denotes an affinoid K-algebra (a quotient of some K⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩, strongly noetherian Tate) with A⁺ = A°
f proper
F coherent
𝔞 ⊆ A an ideal (finitely generated since A is noetherian)
proofSteps: Principal case 𝔞 = (a): M^r = ⊕_k H^r(X, aᵏF) is a finite module over the Rees ring S = ⊕_k aᵏA. For a-torsion-free F multiplication by aᵏ identifies H^r(X, aᵏF) with H^r(X, F), finite over A (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/proper-affinoid-cohomology-finite); in general the kernels of aⁿ on F stabilise to a coherent L killed by a power of a, F/L is a-torsion-free, and the Artin–Rees lemma makes the filtration aᵏF ∩ L a-good (Kiehl §3).

Then argue exactly as in EGA III (4.1.5) (Mittag-Leffler systems and null systems; the scheme version is AdicSpacesPartII:F0/theorem-on-formal-functions, whose Mittag-Leffler lemma AdicSpacesPartII:F0/mittag-leffler-exactness is reused).

General 𝔞 = (a₁,…,a_s) by induction on s (Kiehl Theorem 3.7, deduced from Theorem 3.4 as in EGA III (4.1.5)); this yields the completion isomorphism only — Kiehl does not prove the a-goodness/null-system refinement for non-principal 𝔞.
acceptance: For X = Spa(A) finite over itself, the statement is the Artin–Rees lemma for the finite module F(X).
For a maximal ideal 𝔪 of A with empty fibre, the 𝔪-adic completion of Hⁱ(X, F) vanishes (used in Kiehl §4).

nodes.title: Proper coherent cohomology commutes with affinoid subdomains (Kiehl Satz 3.5)
nodes.statement: Let K a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value; adic spaces are locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°); A denotes an affinoid K-algebra (a quotient of some K⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩, strongly noetherian Tate) with A⁺ = A°, f : X → Spa(A, A°) proper, F coherent and U = Spa(B, B°) ⊆ Spa(A, A°) an affinoid subdomain (for instance a rational subset). Then the natural map Hⁱ(X, F) ⊗_A B → Hⁱ(f⁻¹(U), F) is an isomorphism for every i.
hypotheses: K a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value; adic spaces are locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°); A denotes an affinoid K-algebra (a quotient of some K⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩, strongly noetherian Tate) with A⁺ = A°

nodes.title: Kiehl's proper mapping theorem
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value and f : X → Y a proper morphism (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/universally-closed-and-proper-morphism) of adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°). For every coherent 𝒪_X-module F and every i ≥ 0, Rⁱf_*F is a coherent 𝒪_Y-module; for every affinoid open V ⊆ Y, (Rⁱf_*F)(V) = Hⁱ(f⁻¹(V), F), a finite 𝒪_Y(V)-module, and (Rⁱf_*F)|_V ≅ (Hⁱ(f⁻¹V, F))~. Huber's adic form over locally noetherian bases with a noetherian ring of definition (Huber 1996, Remark 1.3.17, citing [Hu4, 3.12.13]) is not covered by this node.
hypotheses: K complete nonarchimedean, nontrivially valued
f proper, X and Y lft over Spa(K, K°)
F coherent
proofSteps: Coherence is local on Y; let V = Spa(A, A°) ⊆ Y be affinoid, so f⁻¹(V) → V is proper (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/base-change-stability).

Hⁱ(f⁻¹V, F) is a finite A-module (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/proper-affinoid-cohomology-finite) and for affinoid subdomains W ⊆ V, Hⁱ(f⁻¹W, F) = Hⁱ(f⁻¹V, F) ⊗_A 𝒪(W) (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/proper-cohomology-affinoid-subdomain).

Rⁱf_*F is the sheaf associated with W ↦ Hⁱ(f⁻¹W, F) (supplied by DiamondsAndVStacks:D0); on the basis of affinoid W ⊆ V this presheaf is already the sheaf (Hⁱ(f⁻¹V, F))~ (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-acyclicity-finite-modules), so Rⁱf_*F|_V is coherent (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/coherent-sheaf).
The identification (Rⁱf_*F)(V) = Hⁱ(f⁻¹V, F) is Conrad's Remark A.1.1 (Leray spectral sequence plus Tate–Kiehl acyclicity).
acceptance: For X = P^{1,an}_K → Spa(K): R⁰f_*𝒪 = K and R¹f_*𝒪(−2) = K, finite-dimensional.
For a finite morphism f, R⁰f_*F = f_*F is coherent and Rⁱf_*F = 0 for i > 0.

nodes.title: Closed subspaces of Banach spaces of countable type have continuous linear sections
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value, E a K-Banach space of countable type (containing a dense subspace of countable dimension) and F ⊆ E a closed subspace. Then the quotient map E → E/F has a continuous K-linear section; equivalently F has a closed complement. Consequently every strict exact sequence of K-Banach spaces of countable type is topologically split, and K' ⊗̂_K (−) preserves strict exactness of such sequences for every complete extension K'/K.
hypotheses: K nontrivially valued complete
E of countable type
F closed
proofSteps: E has, for every t ∈ (0, 1), a t-orthogonal Schauder basis (Banach spaces of countable type); choose one adapted to F by a Gram–Schmidt procedure on a countable dense sequence (BGR 2.7.1/4, as used by Conrad).
Split exact sequences are preserved by any additive functor, in particular by K' ⊗̂_K (−) (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-banach-module (d)).
acceptance: For E = K⟨T⟩ (countable type) and F = T·K⟨T⟩, the constant-term projection splits E → E/F ≅ K.

nodes.title: Completed extension of the base field for affinoid algebras is faithfully flat
nodes.statement: Let A be an affinoid K-algebra, K'/K an extension of complete nonarchimedean fields and A' = K' ⊗̂_K A. Then A → A' is faithfully flat, and for every finite A-module M the natural map A' ⊗_A M → A' ⊗̂_A M ≅ K' ⊗̂_K M is a topological isomorphism.
hypotheses: A affinoid K-algebra
K'/K complete extension
proofSteps: For finite M, A' ⊗_A M → A' ⊗̂_A M is a topological isomorphism (finite modules over the noetherian Banach ring A'; BGR 3.7.3 via Conrad).

Flatness: an injection M → N of finite A-modules is a closed embedding of countable-type K-Banach spaces, hence split (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/countable-type-closed-subspace-section); so K' ⊗̂_K M → K' ⊗̂_K N is injective (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-banach-module (d)), and A' ⊗̂_A M = K' ⊗̂_K M (transitivity of completed base change, same node (g)).
Faithfulness: A'/𝔪A' = K' ⊗̂_K A/𝔪 = K' ⊗_K A/𝔪 ≠ 0 for every maximal 𝔪 (A/𝔪 finite over K).

nodes.title: Proper coherent cohomology commutes with completed extension of the base field
nodes.statement: Let A be an affinoid K-algebra, f : X → Spa(A, A°) proper, F coherent on X, K'/K an extension of complete nonarchimedean fields, A' = K' ⊗̂_K A, and X' = X ⊗̂_K K' → Spa(A', A'°) with the pullback F' of F. Then the natural δ-functorial map A' ⊗_A Hⁱ(X, F) → Hⁱ(X', F') is an isomorphism of finite A'-modules for every i. In particular, for X proper over Spa(K, K°), Hⁱ(X, F) is finite-dimensional over K and Hⁱ(X_{K'}, F_{K'}) = Hⁱ(X, F) ⊗_K K'.

f proper
F coherent
K'/K complete extension
proofSteps: Compute Hⁱ(X, F) by the Čech complex C• of a finite affinoid covering: its terms are finite products of Banach A-modules of countable type over K, and its differentials are strict (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/proper-affinoid-cohomology-finite).

nodes.title: Analytification carries coherent sheaves to coherent sheaves
nodes.statement: Let K a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value and A an affinoid K-algebra (A = K allowed); X is a scheme locally of finite type over Spec A, X^an = X ×_{Spec A} Spa(A, A°) its relative analytification (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification; for A = K AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-functor) with the morphism of locally ringed spaces ι_X : X^an → X, and let F ↦ F^an = ι_X*F be the analytification of 𝒪_X-modules (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-of-modules). If F is coherent then F^an is coherent (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/coherent-sheaf); more precisely, for X = Spec B affine, F = M̃ with M a finite B-module and an affinoid open Spa(C, C⁺) ⊆ X^an over Spec B (via B → C), F^an|_{Spa C} ≅ (M ⊗_B C)~ as 𝒪-modules, naturally in M.
hypotheses: K a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value and A an affinoid K-algebra (A = K allowed); X is a scheme locally of finite type over Spec A, X^an = X ×_{Spec A} Spa(A, A°) its relative analytification (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification; for A = K AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-functor) with the morphism of locally ringed spaces ι_X : X^an → X
F coherent
proofSteps: Locality: coherence is local on X^an and X^an is covered by the affinoid charts Spa(A_k, A_k⁺) over affine opens Spec B of X (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification).

On such a chart the restriction of ι_X*M̃ is the pullback of M̃ along Spa(C) → Spec B, which by the universal property of M ↦ (M ⊗_B C)~ on rational subsets (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/coherent-sheaf-operations, API pullback_tilde, and AdicSpacesPartII:R3/associated-module-sheaf) is (M ⊗_B C)~ with M ⊗_B C a finite C-module.
Hence F^an is locally associated to finite modules over strongly noetherian Tate affinoids, i.e. coherent.

nodes.title: The GAGA comparison maps on cohomology and higher direct images
nodes.statement: Let K a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value and A an affinoid K-algebra (A = K allowed); X is a scheme locally of finite type over Spec A, X^an = X ×_{Spec A} Spa(A, A°) its relative analytification (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification; for A = K AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-functor) with the morphism of locally ringed spaces ι_X : X^an → X and F an 𝒪_X-module with analytification F^an (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-of-modules). The comparison map c_F : Hⁱ(X, F) → Hⁱ(X^an, F^an) is the composite of Hⁱ(X, F) → Hⁱ(X, ι_*ι*F) (the unit F → ι_*ι*F) with the edge map Hⁱ(X, ι_*F^an) → Hⁱ(X^an, F^an); it is A-linear and δ-functorial in F. For f : X → Y over Spec A, the relative comparison map (Rⁱf_*F)^an → Rⁱf^an_*(F^an) is the adjoint of the sheafified map V ↦ [Hⁱ(f⁻¹V, F) → Hⁱ((f^an)⁻¹V^an, F^an)], δ-functorial in F and compatible with composition in f. These maps are isomorphisms for proper f and coherent F (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/proper-gaga) and not in general.
hypotheses: K a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value and A an affinoid K-algebra (A = K allowed); X is a scheme locally of finite type over Spec A, X^an = X ×_{Spec A} Spa(A, A°) its relative analytification (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification; for A = K AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-functor) with the morphism of locally ringed spaces ι_X : X^an → X
proofSteps: Unit of the adjunction ι* ⊣ ι_* for sheaves of modules (mathlib:SheafOfModules.pullback and its pushforward adjunction), then functoriality of sheaf cohomology (tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.Cohomology on X; sheaf cohomology on X^an) and the edge map of the Leray spectral sequence for ι (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0).
δ-functoriality: F ↦ F^an is exact (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-of-modules), so short exact sequences go to short exact sequences and the maps commute with connecting morphisms.
Relative version: sheafify the absolute maps over affine opens V ⊆ Y and use (f^an)⁻¹(V^an) = (f⁻¹V)^an (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-fibre-products).
acceptance: For X = A¹_K and F = 𝒪, c_F in degree 0 is the inclusion K[T] ⊂ 𝒪(A^{1,ad}_K), injective and not surjective.
For X proper and F coherent, c_F is an isomorphism (GAGA).

nodes.title: Coherent cohomology of O(m) on analytic projective space
nodes.statement: Let A be an affinoid K-algebra, n ≥ 0 and m ∈ ℤ. The comparison map Hⁱ(Pⁿ_A, 𝒪(m)) → Hⁱ((Pⁿ_A)^an, 𝒪(m)^an) (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/gaga-comparison-map) is an isomorphism of finite A-modules for every i; in particular Hⁱ((Pⁿ_A)^an, 𝒪(m)^an) = 0 for 0 < i < n, H⁰ = A[x₀,…,xₙ]_m and Hⁿ is dual to H⁰ of 𝒪(−m−n−1).
hypotheses: A affinoid K-algebra
n ≥ 0, m ∈ ℤ
proofSteps: Cover (Pⁿ_A)^an by the affinoids W_i = {|x_j| ≤ |x_i| for all j} = Spa A⟨x_j/x_i⟩; finite intersections W_I are affinoid (Laurent domains) and 𝒪(m) is acyclic on them (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-acyclicity-finite-modules), so the Čech complex of {W_i} computes Hⁱ (Leray, DiamondsAndVStacks:D0).

The Čech complex of 𝒪(m)^an on {W_i} is the completion, for the Gauss norms, of the algebraic Čech complex of 𝒪(m) on {D₊(x_i)}; both decompose over monomials x^a (a ∈ ℤ^{n+1}, Σa = m) and the differentials are diagonal in the monomials.

Hence the analytic cohomology is the completion of the algebraic cohomology, which is a finite A-module (Serre's computation on Pⁿ_A; algebraic side from the scheme-cohomology owner, see gap) and so already complete.
acceptance: For n = 1, m = −2: H¹((P¹_K)^an, 𝒪(−2)) = K, spanned by the class of x₀⁻¹x₁⁻¹ on W₀ ∩ W₁.
For n = 1, m ≥ 0: H⁰ = K[x₀, x₁]_m of dimension m + 1 and H¹ = 0.
