nodes.title: Proper GAGA: comparison of coherent cohomology (Köpf)
nodes.statement: Let K a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value and A an affinoid K-algebra (A = K allowed); X is a scheme locally of finite type over Spec A, X^an = X ×_{Spec A} Spa(A, A°) its relative analytification (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification; for A = K AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-functor) with the morphism of locally ringed spaces ι_X : X^an → X, f : X → Y a proper morphism of schemes locally of finite type over Spec A and F a coherent 𝒪_X-module. Then f^an : X^an → Y^an is proper and the δ-functorial comparison maps (Rⁱf_*F)^an → Rⁱf^an_*(F^an) are isomorphisms of coherent 𝒪_{Y^an}-modules for all i. In particular, for X proper over Spec A, Hⁱ(X, F) ≅ Hⁱ(X^an, F^an) as finite A-modules.
hypotheses: K a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value and A an affinoid K-algebra (A = K allowed); X is a scheme locally of finite type over Spec A, X^an = X ×_{Spec A} Spa(A, A°) its relative analytification (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification; for A = K AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-functor) with the morphism of locally ringed spaces ι_X : X^an → X
f proper
F coherent
proofSteps: f^an is proper (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-separated-proper), and in fact proper in Kiehl's sense: the relative analytification over an affinoid carries proper maps to Kiehl-proper maps (Conrad 2006 Example 2.3.11, recalled in Example 3.2.6), which is what AdicSpacesPartII:R3/kiehl-proper-mapping-theorem needs for non-discretely valued K; so the target is coherent. The source is coherent (algebraic coherence of Rⁱf_* for proper f, EGA III 3.2.1, supplied by tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction#layer-2-coherent-curve-theory-duality-and-positivity, and AdicSpacesPartII:R3/analytification-coherent); the comparison map is AdicSpacesPartII:R3/gaga-comparison-map.

Being an isomorphism of coherent sheaves can be tested on completed stalks at classical points; by the theorems on formal functions for schemes (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/theorem-on-formal-functions) and for proper rigid maps (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/proper-cohomology-adic-completion) and 𝒪^∧_{Y,ι(y)} ≅ 𝒪^∧_{Y^an,y} (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-completed-local-rings), reduce to Y = Spec R with R a finite local A-algebra, i.e. X proper over a finite K-algebra (Conrad Example 3.2.6).
Over a field: projective X by Serre's method — for X ⊆ Pⁿ closed, resolve F by sums of 𝒪(−m) and use AdicSpacesPartII:R3/analytic-projective-space-cohomology with descending induction on i.

Proper X: Chow's lemma (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.2) and Grothendieck's dévissage [SGA1 XII] (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.3) reduce to the projective case, as in Conrad Appendix A.1.
acceptance: For an elliptic curve E over K: H¹(E^an, 𝒪) ≅ H¹(E, 𝒪) is one-dimensional.
For X = Pⁿ_K and F = 𝒪(m), the theorem is AdicSpacesPartII:R3/analytic-projective-space-cohomology.
Non-example: for the non-proper X = A¹_K the comparison fails in degree 0.

nodes.title: Proper GAGA: analytification is an equivalence on coherent sheaves
nodes.statement: Let K a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value and A an affinoid K-algebra (A = K allowed); X is a scheme locally of finite type over Spec A, X^an = X ×_{Spec A} Spa(A, A°) its relative analytification (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification; for A = K AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-functor) with the morphism of locally ringed spaces ι_X : X^an → X with X proper over Spec A. Then F ↦ F^an is an exact equivalence of abelian tensor categories Coh(X) → Coh(X^an). In particular it is fully faithful on proper A-schemes' coherent sheaves, line bundles, vector bundles and coherent ideals correspond, and closed analytic subspaces of X^an are analytifications of closed subschemes of X.
hypotheses: K a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value and A an affinoid K-algebra (A = K allowed); X is a scheme locally of finite type over Spec A, X^an = X ×_{Spec A} Spa(A, A°) its relative analytification (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification; for A = K AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-functor) with the morphism of locally ringed spaces ι_X : X^an → X
X proper over Spec A
proofSteps: Full faithfulness: Hom(F, G) = H⁰(X, ℋom(F, G)) ≅ H⁰(X^an, ℋom(F, G)^an) = Hom(F^an, G^an) by AdicSpacesPartII:R3/proper-gaga and ℋom(F, G)^an = ℋom(F^an, G^an) (flatness of ι, AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-map-flat).

Exactness: AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-of-modules; a complex of coherent sheaves on X is exact iff its analytification is (A is Jacobson with K-finite residue fields; check on fibres at closed points, Conrad Example 3.2.6).

Essential surjectivity, projective case: for a coherent 𝒢 on (Pⁿ_A)^an, 𝒢(m) is generated by finitely many global sections and has vanishing higher cohomology for m ≫ 0 (Serre's argument using AdicSpacesPartII:R3/analytic-projective-space-cohomology and induction on n by hyperplane sections); so 𝒢 is the cokernel of a map of sums of 𝒪(−m)^an, which is algebraic by full faithfulness.
Proper case by Chow's lemma (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.2) and Grothendieck's dévissage (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.3), as in [SGA1 XII §4] and Conrad Example 3.2.6.

nodes.title: Finite analytic covers of proper varieties are algebraic
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field, X a proper K-scheme and g : Y → X^an a finite morphism of adic spaces. Then there is a finite morphism of schemes g₀ : Y₀ → X, unique up to unique isomorphism, with an X^an-isomorphism Y ≅ Y₀^an; g₀ ↦ g₀^an is an equivalence between finite X-schemes and finite adic spaces over X^an. g finite
proofSteps: g_*𝒪_Y is a coherent 𝒪_{X^an}-algebra and Y = Spa_{X^an}(g_*𝒪_Y) (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-morphism-coherent-algebra-equivalence).

nodes.title: Trace of endomorphisms of finite projective modules
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring and M a finitely generated projective R-module. The trace tr_M : End_R(M) → R is the R-linear map tr_M = contractLeft ∘ (dualTensorHomEquiv R M M)⁻¹, where dualTensorHomEquiv : M^∨ ⊗_R M ≅ End_R(M) (Mathlib, for M finite projective) and contractLeft(φ ⊗ m) = φ(m). Convention: this is the trace used throughout R3; Mathlib's LinearMap.trace R M agrees with it when M is free but is defined to be 0 when M has no finite basis, so it is not the trace of a finite projective non-free module.
hypotheses: R commutative
M finite projective over R
proofSteps: dualTensorHomEquiv R M M exists for Module.Finite and Module.Projective (mathlib:dualTensorHomEquiv); compose its inverse with mathlib:contractLeft.
For free M with basis b, tr_M = LinearMap.trace R M because LinearMap.trace ∘ dualTensorHom = contractLeft (mathlib:LinearMap.trace_eq_contract).

nodes.title: The trace of a finite locally free algebra
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring and B a commutative R-algebra which is finitely generated and projective as an R-module (a finite locally free R-algebra). The trace Tr_{B/R} : B → R is b ↦ tr_B(m_b), the projective-module trace (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/projective-module-trace) of multiplication by b. It is R-linear, Tr_{B/R}(1) is the locally constant degree function (its image in R_𝔭 is rank_𝔭 B), and the trace form (x, y) ↦ Tr_{B/R}(xy) is symmetric. B finite projective as an R-module
proofSteps: Compose the left-multiplication map B → End_R(B) (Algebra.lmul) with LinearMap.projectiveTrace R B.

nodes.title: Base change of the finite projective trace
nodes.statement: Let R → R' be a homomorphism of commutative rings, M a finite projective R-module, f ∈ End_R(M), and B a finite projective R-algebra. Then tr_{R' ⊗ M}(id ⊗ f) = image of tr_M(f) in R', and Tr_{R' ⊗_R B / R'}(1 ⊗ b) = image of Tr_{B/R}(b) for all b ∈ B.

M, B finite projective over R
proofSteps: R' ⊗ M is finite projective over R' and (R' ⊗ M)^∨ ≅ R' ⊗ M^∨ (M finite projective), compatibly with dualTensorHomEquiv.
contractLeft commutes with base change on pure tensors; conclude by linearity (mathlib:dualTensorHomEquiv, mathlib:contractLeft).

nodes.title: Transitivity of the finite projective trace in towers
nodes.statement: Let R → B → C be homomorphisms of commutative rings with B finite projective over R and C finite projective over B. Then C is finite projective over R and Tr_{C/R} = Tr_{B/R} ∘ Tr_{C/B}. More generally, for a finite projective B-module M and φ ∈ End_B(M), M is finite projective over R and tr_{M/R}(φ) = Tr_{B/R}(tr_{M/B}(φ)).
hypotheses: B finite projective over R
C (or M) finite projective over B
proofSteps: Finite projectivity over R: M is a direct summand of Bⁿ, which is a direct summand of R^{nm}.
Choose M ⊕ N = Bⁿ; both sides of the module identity are additive under direct sums (φ ↦ φ ⊕ 0; API projectiveTrace_prodMap), so reduce to M = Bⁿ.
For M = Bⁿ and φ = (b_ij), cyclicity of the projective trace (API projectiveTrace_comp_comm) gives tr_{Bⁿ/R}(φ) = Σ_i tr_{B/R}(m_{b_ii}) = Tr_{B/R}(Σ b_ii) = Tr_{B/R}(tr_{Bⁿ/B} φ).
The algebra statement is the case M = C, φ = m_c. In the free case this is Mathlib's Algebra.trace_trace.

nodes.title: A finite locally free algebra is étale iff its trace pairing is perfect
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring and S a finite projective R-algebra. Then S is étale over R (Mathlib Algebra.Etale) if and only if the R-linear map S → Hom_R(S, R), x ↦ (y ↦ Tr_{S/R}(xy)), is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: S finite projective over R
proofSteps: Both conditions are compatible with base change (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/algebra-trace-base-change) and a map between finite projective R-modules of the same rank is an isomorphism iff it is so on every fibre R → κ(𝔭) (Nakayama).
A finite projective (hence flat, finitely presented) algebra is étale iff all fibres S ⊗ κ(𝔭) are étale over κ(𝔭) (Stacks Lemma 49.3.1 and its reference Morphisms 29.37.8).

Over a field k: if the pairing is perfect, nilpotents lie in its kernel, so S is reduced, a product of fields, and each factor has a nonzero trace, hence is separable (mathlib:traceForm_nondegenerate_tfae); conversely an étale k-algebra is a finite product of finite separable extensions (mathlib:Algebra.Etale.iff_exists_algEquiv_prod) whose trace forms are nondegenerate (mathlib:traceForm_nondegenerate).
acceptance: ℚ(√2)/ℚ: the trace form has Gram matrix diag(2, 4) in the basis 1, √2, perfect.
k[x]/(x²): x is in the kernel of the pairing; the algebra is not étale.

nodes.title: The trace of a finite étale algebra over a field is the sum over geometric points
nodes.statement: Let k be a field, Ω an algebraically closed field containing k and B a finite étale k-algebra. Then Hom_k(B, Ω) has exactly dim_k B elements and Tr_{B/k}(b) = Σ_{σ ∈ Hom_k(B, Ω)} σ(b) in Ω for every b ∈ B. The formula fails without étaleness: for B = k[x]/(x²), Hom_k(B, Ω) has one element while Tr(1) = 2.
hypotheses: B finite étale over the field k
Ω algebraically closed over k
proofSteps: B ≅ ∏ L_i with L_i finite separable field extensions (mathlib:Algebra.Etale.iff_exists_algEquiv_prod); Hom_k(∏ L_i, Ω) = ⊔ Hom_k(L_i, Ω).
Trace of a product is the sum (mathlib:Algebra.trace_prod); for each L_i, Tr = Σ over embeddings (mathlib:trace_eq_sum_embeddings) and #Hom_k(L_i, Ω) = [L_i : k] (separability).

nodes.title: The trace of a finite locally free morphism of schemes
nodes.statement: Let π : X → Y be a finite locally free morphism of schemes (Mathlib: AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite, Flat and LocallyOfFinitePresentation). The trace Tr_π : π_*𝒪_X → 𝒪_Y is the 𝒪_Y-linear map which on every affine open V = Spec A ⊆ Y with π⁻¹(V) = Spec B is Tr_{B/A} (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-locally-free-algebra-trace); these glue because the affine formula is compatible with localisation (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/algebra-trace-base-change). proofSteps: For affine V ⊆ Y, Γ(V, π_*𝒪_X) = B is a finite projective A-algebra (finite, flat, finitely presented).
For a basic open D(g) ⊆ V, B_g = B ⊗_A A_g and Tr_{B_g/A_g} = (Tr_{B/A})_g (base change lemma); morphisms of sheaves are determined on the affine basis.

nodes.title: Finite locally free morphisms of adic spaces
nodes.statement: A morphism of adic spaces f : Y → X is finite locally free if it is finite (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-morphism) and f_*𝒪_Y is a vector bundle on X (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/locally-free-sheaf). Its degree is the rank of f_*𝒪_Y, a locally constant function on X. Over an open affinoid Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X with A a complete Tate ring such that f⁻¹(Spa A) is affinoid — such affinoids cover X by the definition of finiteness, and every open affinoid with A strongly noetherian qualifies (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-morphism, Zavyalov Theorem B.2.18) — f⁻¹(Spa A) = Spa(B, B⁺) with B a finite projective A-algebra (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheafy-tate-acyclicity-and-kiehl-gluing) and B⁺ the integral closure of A⁺, and for every rational V ⊆ Spa(A, A⁺), f⁻¹(V) = Spa(B ⊗_A 𝒪_X(V)) with the uncompleted tensor product (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-algebra-tensor-complete (iii)). It is not asserted that f⁻¹ of every sheafy Tate affinoid is affinoid (Zavyalov Remark B.2.19; Kedlaya–Liu Remark 8.2.18).
hypotheses: f a morphism of adic spaces
proofSteps: Predicate: IsFinite f ∧ IsVectorBundle (f_*𝒪_Y); degree := rank.

nodes.title: The trace of a finite locally free morphism of adic spaces
nodes.statement: Let f : Y → X be a finite locally free morphism of adic spaces (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-locally-free-morphism). nodes.title: Perfect trace pairing and point-count formula for finite étale morphisms
nodes.statement: Let f : Y → X be a finite étale morphism of adic spaces (étale in the sense of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/differentials-unramified-smooth-etale and finite). Then f is finite locally free and the trace pairing f_*𝒪_Y → ℋom_{𝒪_X}(f_*𝒪_Y, 𝒪_X), s ↦ (t ↦ Tr_f(st)), is an isomorphism. For x ∈ X with residue field κ(x) and an algebraically closed field Ω ⊇ κ(x), Tr_f(s)(x) = Σ_σ σ(s) over the κ(x)-algebra maps σ : 𝒪_Y(f⁻¹U) ⊗ κ(x) → Ω (U an affinoid neighbourhood). Conversely a finite locally free f with perfect trace pairing is étale. Without étaleness both statements fail (z ↦ z² at 0).

proofSteps: Affinoid-locally B = 𝒪_Y(f⁻¹U) is a finite étale 𝒪_X(U)-algebra, hence finite projective (KL §1.2), so f is finite locally free.
Perfectness of the pairing is AdicSpacesPartII:R3/etale-iff-trace-pairing-perfect applied affinoid-locally.

Point formula: Tr_f(s)(x) is the image of Tr_{B/A}(s) in κ(x), which equals Tr_{B ⊗ κ(x)/κ(x)}(s ⊗ 1) (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/algebra-trace-base-change); B ⊗ κ(x) is finite étale over κ(x); apply AdicSpacesPartII:R3/trace-geometric-point-formula.

nodes.title: Pull–identify–trace operators along correspondences
nodes.statement: A correspondence from Y to X is an adic space C with morphisms q : C → Y and p : C → X, p finite locally free. Given vector bundles (or, on locally noetherian analytic spaces, coherent sheaves) E_Y on Y and E_X on X and an 𝒪_C-linear identification φ : q*E_Y → p*E_X, the pull–identify–trace operator T = T(C, φ) : Hⁱ(Y, E_Y) → Hⁱ(X, E_X) is the composite Hⁱ(Y, E_Y) →(q*) Hⁱ(C, q*E_Y) →(φ) Hⁱ(C, p*E_X) = Hⁱ(X, p_*p*E_X) = Hⁱ(X, p_*𝒪_C ⊗ E_X) →(Tr_p ⊗ id) Hⁱ(X, E_X), using that p is finite (p_* exact on coherent / vector bundles) and the projection formula. No normalising factor is included; consumers multiply by their own constants (e.g. 1/q_a in BHW).
hypotheses: p finite locally free
q arbitrary
φ an 𝒪_C-linear map q*E_Y → p*E_X
proofSteps: q*: pullback of sections/cohomology along q (Mathlib pullback of sheaves of modules; AdicSpacesPartII:R3/coherent-sheaf-operations).

Hⁱ(C, F) = Hⁱ(X, p_*F) for p finite: p_* is exact on sheaves that are affinoid-locally associated modules and Rⁱp_* = 0 for i > 0 (p finite ⇒ affinoid preimages; AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-acyclicity-finite-modules or AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-projective-module-acyclicity).
Projection formula p_*p*E_X ≅ p_*𝒪_C ⊗ E_X (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-locally-free-projection-formula), then Tr_p ⊗ id (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/analytic-trace-finite-locally-free).
acceptance: For X = Y, C = X ⊔ X, p = id ⊔ id, q = id ⊔ σ and trivial coefficients, T(s) = s + σ*s.
BHW Definition 10.2: T_a = q_a⁻¹ · T(C, φ) with C = X_{c,Γ₀(pⁿ)∩Γ₀(a)}, p = π₁, q = π₂ and φ the isomorphism π₂*ω ≅ π₁*ω.

nodes.title: The étale site of AdicEtaleGeometry A1 on the analytic carriers of R0 and R1
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally noetherian analytic adic space (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space): every point has an open affinoid neighbourhood Spa(A, A⁺) with A a strongly noetherian complete Tate ring or with a noetherian ring of definition, and every point is analytic. This covers r(X_rig) for a rigid analytic variety X_rig over a complete nonarchimedean field k (R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor) and X^ad for a scheme X locally of finite type over k (R1/analytification-functor). The small étale site X_ét of AdicEtaleGeometry A1 on X is identified with the following structure, and no other étale site is constructed: (i) its underlying category is the full subcategory Et/X of adic spaces over X whose structure morphism is étale in the sense of R0 (Huber Definition 1.6.5: locally of finite presentation, and Hom_X(Spa B, -) -> Hom_X(Spa B/I, -) bijective for every affinoid ring B and square-zero ideal I); on such X this class coincides with A1's class of morphisms that are locally on the source an open immersion followed by a finite étale morphism followed by an open immersion (Huber Lemma 2.2.8; Kedlaya-Liu Definition 8.2.16), so the identity on objects is an isomorphism between the two presentations of the category; (ii) every X-morphism between objects of Et/X is étale, Et/X has a final object X and fibre products, computed as fibre products of adic spaces (R0, Huber 1.2.2(a)); (iii) a family (f_i: U_i -> U)_i in Et/X is a covering exactly when U = ∪_i f_i(U_i) as sets, these families form a pretopology, and the Grothendieck topology it generates is A1's étale topology. Open subspaces of X are objects of Et/X and open covers are étale coverings, so the analytic (open-subset) topology of X is coarser than the étale topology.
hypotheses: X locally noetherian and analytic; for non-noetherian carriers (sousperfectoid, perfectoid) the étale site is A1's local-description site and Huber's infinitesimal definition is not used (see AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-etale-stability).
Étale is taken in the sense of R0 (Huber 1.6.5), which includes 'locally of finite presentation'.
The identification (i) is Huber's Lemma 2.2.8 as imported by A1 (requests entry); only the coverings by jointly surjective families are used, not Huber's strongly surjective rigid coverings.
proofSteps: Objects: by AdicSpacesPartII:R0/differentials-unramified-smooth-etale étale morphisms are defined infinitesimally; by AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-local-open-finite-etale-factorisation (Huber Lemma 2.2.8; for X locally of finite type over a field, de Jong–van der Put Proposition 3.1.4), which A1 re-exports they are exactly the morphisms that are locally an open immersion followed by a finite étale morphism followed by an open immersion; hence A1's objects over X and R0's étale X-spaces are the same adic spaces with the same structure maps.

Morphisms: a morphism g: U -> V of étale X-spaces is étale by cancellation (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-smooth-cancellation, Huber 1.6.7(iii)): the composite U -> V -> X is étale and V -> X is étale, hence unramified.

Finite limits: étale morphisms are locally of finite type, so AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence (case (a)) gives U ×_V W for U, W étale over V; the projection U ×_V W -> W is étale by AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-etale-base-change and U ×_V W -> X is étale by composition (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-smooth-composition); X is final.

Coverings: jointly surjective families contain isomorphisms and are stable under composition (set-theoretic); stability under base change: if (U_i -> U) is jointly surjective and V -> U is a morphism of Et/X, then (U_i ×_U V -> V) is jointly surjective because |U_i ×_U V| -> |U_i| ×_{|U|} |V| is surjective (Huber Corollary 1.2.3(iii)(d), AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-product-points; Huber states it for g adic, which holds here because every morphism into an analytic adic space is adic, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-morphism).

So the jointly surjective families form a pretopology (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Pretopology) whose generated topology (mathlib:CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology) is the topology of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-and-geometric-points.
Open immersions are étale (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/open-embedding-etale, Huber 1.6.7(i)), so open subspaces of X (anchor Layer 5) are objects and open covers are coverings.
acceptance: Huber's definition on p. 109 (objects étale over X, coverings U = ∪ f_i(U_i)) is recovered verbatim on X = r(X_rig) and on X = X^ad.

On the closed unit disc X = Spa(K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩) the rational cover {|T| ≤ |ϖ|}, {|ϖ| ≤ |T|} is an étale covering, and for p ≠ 2 the squaring map Spa K⟨S⟩ -> Spa K⟨T⟩, T ↦ S², is étale over {|T| = 1} but not at the point T = 0, so it is not an object of Et/X while its restriction to the annulus is.
For X = Spa(K, K°) with K algebraically closed, every object of Et/X is a disjoint union of copies of X.

nodes.title: Base change defines a morphism of étale sites f_ét: X_ét -> Y_ét
nodes.statement: Let f: X -> Y be a morphism of locally noetherian analytic adic spaces (R0 carriers). The base-change functor f*: Et/Y -> Et/X, V ↦ V ×_Y X (with its projection to X), is well defined, preserves the final object and fibre products, and sends coverings of Y_ét to coverings of X_ét. Consequently f* is a continuous functor between the étale sites of AdicSpacesPartII:R4/etale-site-on-analytic-carriers (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.IsContinuous) and defines a morphism of sites f_ét: X_ét -> Y_ét, with direct image f_* = f*.sheafPushforwardContinuous, (f_*F)(V) = F(V ×_Y X), and its left adjoint f^{-1} (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPullback). For g: Y -> Z there are canonical isomorphisms (g∘f)* ≅ f*∘g* and id* ≅ id satisfying the usual coherence, hence (g∘f)_* ≅ g_* f_* (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPushforwardContinuousComp) and (g∘f)^{-1} ≅ f^{-1} g^{-1}. For an open immersion j: U -> X, j*V is the open subspace V ×_X U of V (the preimage of U).
hypotheses: X, Y locally noetherian analytic adic spaces; f any morphism of adic spaces (automatically adic since Y is analytic).
Values of sheaves in any category A admitting the sheafification used by mathlib's sheafPullback (sets, abelian groups, modules).
proofSteps: Well defined: V -> Y étale is locally of finite type, so V ×_Y X exists (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence, case (a)) and V ×_Y X -> X is étale (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-etale-base-change).
Finite limits: base change commutes with fibre products over Y by pasting of cartesian squares, and Y ×_Y X = X.

Coverings: if Y' = ∪ g_i(V_i) then Y' ×_Y X = ∪ images of V_i ×_Y X, because |V_i ×_Y X| -> |V_i| ×_{|Y|} |X| is surjective (Huber Corollary 1.2.3(iii)(d), AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-product-points; the adicness Huber requires is automatic since Y is analytic).

Continuity: f* preserves the terminal object and fibre products, and Et/Y has finite limits, so f* is representably flat (mathlib:CategoryTheory.flat_of_preservesFiniteLimits), hence compatible-preserving (mathlib:CategoryTheory.compatiblePreservingOfFlat); together with cover-preservation (mathlib:CategoryTheory.CoverPreserving, previous step) this gives mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.IsContinuous via mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.isContinuous_of_coverPreserving. Then mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPushforwardContinuous is f_* and mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPullback (which exists once the value category has weak sheafification for Et/X) is its left adjoint f^{-1}; flatness makes f^{-1} left exact.

Composition and identity isomorphisms: uniqueness of fibre products up to unique isomorphism gives (g∘f)* ≅ f*∘g*, and mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPushforwardContinuousComp transports it to pushforwards; the pullback isomorphism follows by uniqueness of left adjoints.
acceptance: For j: U -> X the inclusion of a rational subset of an affinoid X, (j_*F)(V) = F(V ∩ preimage of U) and j^{-1}F(W) = F(W) for W étale over U.
For f = r(φ) with φ a morphism of rigid varieties, f_ét corresponds under AdicSpacesPartII:R4/etale-site-and-rigid-comparison to the rigid site morphism of Huber (2.1.3).

nodes.title: Huber 2.1.4: the étale topos of a rigid analytic variety is the étale topos of its adic space
nodes.statement: Let k be a complete nonarchimedean field and X a rigid analytic variety over k, with adic space r(X) (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor). Let X_ét^rig be the rigid étale site: the category of rigid analytic varieties étale over X, with the Grothendieck topology in which a family is a covering exactly when its image under r is a covering of r(X)_ét (equivalently, by AdicSpacesPartII:R4/rigid-strongly-surjective-covers, when it is strongly surjective in the sense of Huber Definition 2.1.1). Then the functor r: X_ét^rig -> r(X)_ét into the étale site of AdicSpacesPartII:R4/etale-site-on-analytic-carriers induces an equivalence of topoi ρ_X: Sh(r(X)_ét) ≃ Sh(X_ét^rig) (Huber Proposition 2.1.4), for sheaves of sets and hence for sheaves with values in any category of algebraic structures.
hypotheses: X any rigid analytic variety (not necessarily quasi-separated): the proof passes through the quasi-separated étale objects.

The rigid category and its étale morphisms are supplied by R1 (rigid-adic comparison, étale comparison 1.7.11, AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-etale-comparison); r is fully faithful and commutes with fibre products.
proofSteps: Let (Et/X)' and (Et/r(X))' be the full subcategories of objects whose structure morphism to X (resp. r(X)) is quasi-separated, with the induced topologies. By the relative form of (1.1.11) ('for every rigid analytic variety X, r induces an equivalence from the category of rigid analytic varieties over X whose structure morphisms are quasi-separated to the category of adic spaces over r(X) whose structure morphisms are locally of finite type and quasi-separated'; AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor) and the comparison of rigid and adic étaleness (Huber 1.7.11, AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-etale-comparison), r restricts to an equivalence (Et/X)' ≃ (Et/r(X))'; by AdicSpacesPartII:R4/rigid-strongly-surjective-covers (Huber 2.1.2) it identifies the coverings.

Every object of r(X)_ét (resp. X_ét^rig) has a covering by affinoid objects (open affinoid covers are étale coverings, AdicSpacesPartII:R4/etale-site-on-analytic-carriers), and the structure morphism of an affinoid object is quasi-separated (an affinoid is quasi-separated over Spa(k, k°), and if Y -> X -> Spa(k, k°) is quasi-separated then so is Y -> X).

Comparison lemma (SGA 4 III 4.1): every object of Et/X (resp. Et/r(X)) is covered by objects of the primed subcategory, and the primed site carries the induced topology, so each inclusion is a dense subsite (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.inducedTopology, whose instance makes a cover-dense fully faithful functor a mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.IsDenseSubsite) and restriction of sheaves is an equivalence (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafInducedTopologyEquivOfIsCoverDense, a special case of mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.IsDenseSubsite.sheafEquiv). Alternatively, as Huber remarks after the proof, apply the comparison lemma directly to r: X_ét^rig -> r(X)_ét, which is fully faithful ((1.1.11)(d)) and cover-dense, with X_ét^rig carrying the induced topology.

Compose the three equivalences; the composite is ρ_X, and it is compatible with the site morphisms induced by morphisms of rigid varieties (Huber (2.1.3); AdicSpacesPartII:R4/etale-site-functoriality).
acceptance: Huber's Proposition 2.1.4 as stated: for every rigid analytic variety X the morphism of topoi ρ_X is an equivalence.
For X = Sp k the topos of both sites is the classifying topos of Gal(k^sep/k) acting on finite sets (continuous G-sets).
Every étale cohomology statement for the adic space r(X) transfers to the rigid étale site, and conversely.

nodes.title: Strongly surjective rigid étale families are exactly those with jointly surjective adic image (Huber 2.1.2)
nodes.statement: Let X be a rigid analytic variety over k and (f_i: U_i -> U)_i a family of étale morphisms of rigid varieties over X. Then the family is strongly surjective (every quasi-compact admissible open of U is the union of the images of finitely many quasi-compact admissible opens of the U_i; Huber Definition 2.1.1) if and only if the family (r(f_i): r(U_i) -> r(U))_i is jointly surjective on points of adic spaces.
hypotheses: Étale morphisms of rigid varieties in the rigid sense; r the functor of R1 (commutes with fibre products, quasi-compact admissible opens of a quasi-separated X correspond to quasi-compact opens of r(X), constructible subsets of r(X) are determined by their rigid points).
proofSteps: Reduce to one morphism: the family (f_i) is strongly surjective iff f = ⊔ f_i: ⊔ U_i -> U is (a quasi-compact admissible open of ⊔ U_i meets finitely many U_i), and jointly surjective iff r(f) is surjective; r commutes with disjoint unions ((1.1.11)(c)).

(=>) (Huber 2.1.2, a => b.) It suffices that r(W) ⊆ im(r(f)) for every affinoid (in particular quasi-compact and quasi-separated) admissible open W ⊆ U, since the r(W) cover r(U) ((1.1.11)(c), AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor). Strong surjectivity gives quasi-compact admissible opens W_1, ..., W_m of ⊔ U_i with W = ∪ f(W_j); since W_j ⊆ f^{-1}(W), r(f) restricts to spectral maps r(W_j) -> r(W) with quasi-compact source, so T := ∪ im(r(f)|r(W_j)) is pro-constructible in the spectral space r(W) and contains every rigid point of W. A pro-constructible subset of a spectral space is an intersection of constructible subsets, each containing all rigid points of W, and a constructible subset of r(W) is determined by its rigid points ((1.1.11), p. 43), so each equals r(W) and T = r(W). (Openness of étale maps is not needed in this direction.)

(<=) (Huber 2.1.2, b => a.) Let W ⊆ U be a quasi-compact admissible open. Since r(f) is surjective and open (étale morphisms are open: AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-morphism-open, applicable by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-etale-comparison), and the r(V), V a quasi-compact admissible open of ⊔ U_i, form a basis of r(⊔ U_i), quasi-compactness of r(W) gives finitely many such V_1, ..., V_n ⊆ f^{-1}(W) with r(W) = ∪ r(f)(r(V_k)). Then f(V_k) ⊆ W, and every rigid point w ∈ W lies in r(f)(r(V_k)) for some k; because r commutes with fibre products ((1.1.11); AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor (e)), the rigid fibre (f|V_k)^{-1}(w) is non-empty (its adic space r(V_k ×_W Sp k(w)) = r(V_k) ×_{r(W)} Spa k(w) is non-empty), so w ∈ f(V_k). Hence W = ∪ f(V_k).
acceptance: A rigid étale family is a covering of X_ét^rig in the sense of Huber Definition 2.1.1 iff its adic image is a covering of r(X)_ét.

The two-piece cover {|T| ≤ |ϖ|}, {|ϖ| ≤ |T|} of the closed disc is strongly surjective. If k is algebraically closed (so the rigid points of the disc are the elements of k° and the residue field is infinite), the family of discs {|T - a| ≤ |ϖ|}, a ∈ k°, covers every rigid point of the closed disc but is not strongly surjective (the disc is not a finite union of images of quasi-compact opens of these discs, which lie in finitely many residue classes), and correspondingly its adic image misses the Gauss point. For k not algebraically closed the family need not even cover the rigid points: for k = Q_p the rigid point T = p^{1/2} satisfies |p^{1/2} - a| ≥ p^{-1/2} > |p| for all a ∈ Z_p.

nodes.title: The morphism of sites X^ad_ét -> X_ét for a scheme X locally of finite type over k
nodes.statement: Let k be a complete nonarchimedean field and X a scheme locally of finite type over k, with analytification X^ad = X ×_{Spec k} Spa(k, k°) (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-functor). The functor (-)^ad: X_ét -> X^ad_ét, from the small étale site of X (mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.smallEtaleTopology on the category mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Etale of schemes étale over X) to the étale site of AdicSpacesPartII:R4/etale-site-on-analytic-carriers, U ↦ U^ad = U ×_X X^ad, is well defined, preserves the final object and fibre products, and sends jointly surjective étale families to jointly surjective families. It therefore defines a morphism of sites λ_X: X^ad_ét -> X_ét, natural in X for morphisms of schemes locally of finite type over k (λ_Y ∘ f^ad_ét = f_ét ∘ λ_X). Only the site morphism is constructed here; comparison theorems for cohomology along λ_X belong to ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology.
hypotheses: X locally of finite type over the complete nonarchimedean field k (so X^ad is locally noetherian: Spa(k, k°) is strongly noetherian).
Schemes are mathlib schemes; étale in mathlib's sense (mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Etale).
proofSteps: Étale goes to étale: for U -> X étale, U^ad -> X^ad is étale (Huber 1.7.3(i), AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-etale-smooth).

Fibre products: (U ×_V W)^ad = U^ad ×_{V^ad} W^ad and U^ad = U ×_X X^ad, by the universal property of the scheme-adic fibre product (Huber 1994 Proposition 3.8; AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification and AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-fibre-products).

Coverings: given (U_i -> U) jointly surjective and x ∈ U^ad with image u ∈ U under the canonical morphism of locally ringed spaces U^ad -> U, choose i and u_i ∈ U_i over u; Huber 1994 Lemma 3.9(ii) (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-points) gives a point of U_i ×_U U^ad = U_i^ad over (u_i, x).

Continuity: mathlib's small étale site has exactly the jointly surjective families as coverings (mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ofArrows_mem_smallEtaleTopology_iff), so (-)^ad is cover-preserving (mathlib:CategoryTheory.CoverPreserving); it preserves finite limits and X.Etale has finite limits, so it is representably flat (mathlib:CategoryTheory.flat_of_preservesFiniteLimits) and compatible-preserving (mathlib:CategoryTheory.compatiblePreservingOfFlat), hence continuous (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.isContinuous_of_coverPreserving, mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.IsContinuous); this defines the morphism of sites with pushforward mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPushforwardContinuous. Naturality in X is the transitivity of fibre products.

For X = G_m and the Kummer cover U = G_m, t ↦ t^n (n invertible in k), U^ad -> G_m^ad is the analytic Kummer cover; the family {U -> G_m} stays a covering after analytification.

nodes.title: The corrected pro-étale site of AdicEtaleGeometry A1 on the analytic carriers, and ν: X_proét -> X_ét
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally noetherian analytic adic space as in AdicSpacesPartII:R4/etale-site-on-analytic-carriers (Scholze's standing hypothesis: locally Spa(A, A⁺) with A strongly noetherian or with a noetherian ring of definition; étale objects are then locally connected). The pro-étale site X_proét of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-site-corrected on X is built on pro-(X_ét) for the étale site X_ét of that node: (i) objects are the pro-objects U = lim U_i of X_ét (formal cofiltered inverse systems; SGA 4 I 8) that are pro-étale over X, with underlying space |U| = lim |U_i|; morphisms are morphisms of pro-objects; (ii) a morphism U -> V is pro-étale if U = lim U_i with U_i -> V étale and U_i -> U_j finite étale surjective for large i > j; (iii) coverings are families (f_i: U_i -> U) of pro-étale morphisms with |U| = ∪ f_i(|U_i|) and, following the erratum, each f_i is a composite U_i -> W_i -> U of a transfinite composition U_i = lim_{μ<λ} U_μ -> W_i (U_0 = W_i) in which every U_μ -> U_{<μ} := lim_{μ'<μ} U_{μ'} is the pullback of a finite étale surjective morphism, and an étale morphism W_i -> U; families indexed by countable presentations are coverings exactly as in the uncorrected definition, and the underlying category is unchanged by the correction; (iv) the functor c: X_ét -> X_proét sending U to the constant pro-object is fully faithful, preserves finite limits and coverings, and defines the morphism of sites ν_X: X_proét -> X_ét (Scholze's ν). No arbitrary open surjection of profinite sets is assumed to split, and the deleted Proposition 3.8 and last sentence of Proposition 3.13 are not used.
hypotheses: X locally noetherian (Scholze 2013 §3); the pro-étale site of a perfectoid or general analytic adic space in the sense of ECD §8 is a different site owned elsewhere (DiamondsAndVStacks).

The form of the corrected covering condition for Definition 3.9 (étale map followed by a transfinite composition of pullbacks of finite étale surjections) is pinned here and requested from A1 (the erratum states that 'a similar condition' applies without displaying it).
proofSteps: The category and the pro-étale morphisms are those of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-site-corrected, applied to the étale site of AdicSpacesPartII:R4/etale-site-on-analytic-carriers; pro-(X_ét) is modelled in mathlib as the opposite of mathlib:CategoryTheory.Ind of (X_ét)ᵒᵖ (Scholze Definition 3.1 / Proposition 3.2; mathlib has no separate Pro), with |U| = lim |U_i|. Fibre products along pro-étale maps exist and are surjective on underlying spaces (Scholze Lemma 3.10(i), in the A1 node).

Corrected coverings: the pinned form is stable under base change (pullbacks of finite étale surjections are finite étale surjections, transfinite compositions pull back termwise) and under composition (concatenate the ordinal-indexed towers), and contains the countable presentations (λ = ω); this is the A1 requests entry.

ν: an étale morphism of X_ét, viewed as a constant pro-object, is pro-étale; a jointly surjective étale family is a corrected covering (λ = 0 in (iii)), so c is cover-preserving (mathlib:CategoryTheory.CoverPreserving); c preserves finite limits (the embedding of a category into its pro-category preserves finite limits, and fibre products of constant objects are those of X_ét), so c is representably flat (mathlib:CategoryTheory.flat_of_preservesFiniteLimits) and compatible-preserving (mathlib:CategoryTheory.compatiblePreservingOfFlat), hence continuous (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.isContinuous_of_coverPreserving, mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.IsContinuous), defining ν with pushforward mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPushforwardContinuous.
Full faithfulness of c: Hom(lim_i U_i, V) = colim_i Hom(U_i, V) for constant V (Scholze Proposition 3.2).
acceptance: For X = Spa(k, k°) with k a field, X_proét restricted to pro-finite-étale objects is the site of profinite continuous Gal(k^sep/k)-sets with coverings restricted as in the erratum (Scholze Proposition 3.5 corrected).
For char k = 0, the countable tower lim_n Spa k⟨T^{±1/p^n}⟩ -> Spa k⟨T^{±1}⟩ (finite étale surjective transition maps) is a covering exactly as in the 2013 paper.

Non-example: an arbitrary open surjection of profinite sets S -> S' with uncountable index (Ribes-Zalesskii Example 5.6.9) gives an open surjective family in pro-X_fét that is not a covering of the corrected site.
Non-example: X_proét is not mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.proetaleTopology (weakly étale schemes with fpqc covers): its objects are pro-objects of étale adic spaces.

nodes.title: Functoriality of the corrected pro-étale site and compatibility with ν
nodes.statement: Let f: X -> Y be a morphism of locally noetherian analytic adic spaces. The functor f*: Y_proét -> X_proét, lim V_j ↦ lim (V_j ×_Y X), is well defined, preserves finite limits and corrected coverings, and defines a morphism of sites f_proét: X_proét -> Y_proét; it satisfies ν_Y ∘ f_proét = f_ét ∘ ν_X on underlying functors (c_X ∘ f* = f* ∘ c_Y), where f_ét is the morphism of AdicSpacesPartII:R4/etale-site-functoriality, and (g∘f)_proét ≅ g_proét ∘ f_proét.
hypotheses: X, Y locally noetherian analytic; f arbitrary (base change of étale objects exists by R0).
proofSteps: Levelwise base change: for V = lim V_j in Y_proét, V_j ×_Y X exists and is étale over X (AdicSpacesPartII:R4/etale-site-functoriality); f* on pro-objects is the pro-extension of the left exact functor f*: Y_ét -> X_ét, so it preserves cofiltered limits and finite limits. A pro-étale presentation V = lim V_j -> V' with V_j -> V' étale and V_j -> V_k finite étale surjective for large j > k stays one after base change: étale and finite morphisms are stable under base change (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-etale-base-change, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-morphism, api IsFinite.baseChange) and surjectivity is preserved by AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-product-points.

Coverings: X -> Y is not a morphism of pro-(Y_ét), so Scholze Lemma 3.10(i) does not apply verbatim. For a covering {g_i: U_i -> U} of Y_proét, f*U_i = U_i ×_U f*U levelwise, and |f*U_i| -> |U_i| ×_{|U|} |f*U| is surjective: at each finite level this is Huber Corollary 1.2.3(iii)(d) (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-product-points), and it passes to the cofiltered limit because a cofiltered limit of non-empty spectral spaces along spectral maps is non-empty (the fibres are pro-constructible), as in the proof of Scholze Lemma 3.10(i). Hence f*{g_i} is jointly surjective. The corrected tower form is preserved since pullbacks of finite étale surjections are finite étale surjections and transfinite compositions pull back termwise.

f* is therefore cover-preserving (mathlib:CategoryTheory.CoverPreserving) and, being left exact on a finitely complete category, representably flat and compatible-preserving (mathlib:CategoryTheory.flat_of_preservesFiniteLimits, mathlib:CategoryTheory.compatiblePreservingOfFlat), hence continuous (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.isContinuous_of_coverPreserving, mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.IsContinuous).
Compatibility with ν: on constant pro-objects the functor is the étale base change.
Composition: transitivity of fibre products levelwise.
acceptance: For j: U -> X an open immersion, j* is restriction to the preimage of U, and ν_U ∘ j_proét = j_ét ∘ ν_X.
For f = Spa(L, L°) -> Spa(K, K°) with L/K finite separable, f* sends lim X_{K_i} to lim X_{L_i}, matching Scholze Proposition 3.15.

nodes.title: The étale site of an étale X-space is the slice site: U_ét ≃ X_ét/U
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally noetherian analytic adic space and u: U -> X an object of X_ét (AdicSpacesPartII:R4/etale-site-on-analytic-carriers). The functor U_ét -> X_ét/U sending an étale V -> U to (V -> U -> X, with its map to U) is an equivalence of categories, and it identifies the étale topology of U with the topology induced on the slice, mathlib's mathlib:CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.over (a sieve on V is covering iff its image in X_ét is). Under this equivalence the morphism of sites u_ét of AdicSpacesPartII:R4/etale-site-functoriality is the slice morphism: restriction of sheaves u^{-1} is mathlib's overPullback, (u^{-1}F)(V) = F(V -> X), and u_*G(W) = G(W ×_X U).
hypotheses: u étale; the étale topologies are those of AdicSpacesPartII:R4/etale-site-on-analytic-carriers on X and on U.
proofSteps: Well defined and essentially surjective: for V -> U étale, V -> U -> X is étale (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-smooth-composition); for W -> X étale with a morphism W -> U over X, W -> U is étale by cancellation (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-smooth-cancellation, Huber 1.6.7(iii)), U -> X being étale hence unramified.
Full faithfulness: morphisms over U are morphisms over X compatible with the maps to U (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Over.iteratedSliceEquiv).
Coverings: both topologies consist of jointly surjective families, and surjectivity does not depend on the base.

Restriction and pushforward: u^{-1} of AdicSpacesPartII:R4/etale-site-functoriality is by definition the left adjoint of u_* = (base change W ↦ W ×_X U).sheafPushforwardContinuous. The forgetful functor from the slice is left adjoint to base change (Σ_u ⊣ u*), and both functors are continuous (mathlib:CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.over), so mathlib:CategoryTheory.Adjunction.sheafPushforwardContinuous gives (forget).sheafPushforwardContinuous ⊣ u_*. The left-hand functor is mathlib:CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.overPullback, so u^{-1} ≅ overPullback by uniqueness of left adjoints, and u_*G(W) = G(W ×_X U).
acceptance: For U = X the equivalence is the identity; for U an open subspace, X_ét/U is the full subcategory of étale X-spaces whose image lies in U.
For U = X ⊔ X (two copies), X_ét/U ≃ X_ét × X_ét and a sheaf on U_ét is a pair of sheaves on X_ét.

nodes.title: The pro-étale site of an open subspace is the slice site: U_proét ≃ X_proét/U
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally noetherian analytic adic space and j: U -> X the inclusion of an open subspace (U ∈ X_ét, viewed in X_proét as a constant pro-object). The functor U_proét -> X_proét/U, lim V_i ↦ (lim V_i with its map to U), is an equivalence of sites for the corrected coverings of AdicSpacesPartII:R4/proetale-site-on-analytic-carriers, compatible with the étale slice equivalence of AdicSpacesPartII:R4/etale-slice-site via ν. More generally the same holds for any U ∈ X_ét.
hypotheses: U open (or étale) in X; X locally noetherian.
proofSteps: Let V ∈ X_proét with a morphism V -> U over X and a pro-étale presentation V = lim W_j -> X (W_j -> X étale, so W_j ∈ X_ét since X is final; transition maps finite étale surjective for large indices). Since U is a constant pro-object, Hom(V, U) = colim_j Hom(W_j, U) (Scholze Proposition 3.2), so V -> U factors through W_j -> U for large j, and after enlarging j this map is over X (two maps W_j -> X agreeing on V agree at a later stage). Each W_j -> U is étale by cancellation (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-smooth-cancellation), the transition maps are unchanged, so V is pro-étale over U. Conversely an object pro-étale over U is pro-étale over X by composition (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-smooth-composition).

For U a quasi-compact open of |X| this is the universal property of Scholze Lemma 3.10(iii); general opens are unions of quasi-compact opens, and a quasi-compact object V maps into a quasi-compact open.
Coverings are defined by surjectivity on underlying spaces and the corrected tower form, neither of which depends on whether the base is U or X.
Compatibility with ν: on constant pro-objects the equivalence is that of AdicSpacesPartII:R4/etale-slice-site.
acceptance: For U = X the equivalence is the identity.
Scholze Proposition 3.15 (X_{L,proét} ≃ X_proét/X_L for a separable field extension) is the analogous statement for a pro-finite-étale object; here the object is étale.

nodes.title: Smooth pairs: a smooth adic space with a strict normal crossings divisor
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field and B^n_K := Spa(K⟨T_1, ..., T_n⟩, K°⟨T_1, ..., T_n⟩) the closed unit polydisc (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.closedPolydisc). A smooth pair over K is a pair (X, D) where X is an adic space smooth over Spa(K, K°) (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-morphism) and D ⊆ X is a closed adic subspace with ideal sheaf I_D ⊆ O_X (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings) such that every x ∈ X has a strict normal crossings chart: an open neighbourhood V of x, integers 0 ≤ r ≤ n and an étale morphism h: V -> B^n_K with I_D|_V = h^*(T_1 ⋯ T_r)·O_V (so D ∩ V = h^{-1}(V(T_1 ⋯ T_r)); r = 0 means D ∩ V = ∅). The boundary complement is the open subspace U := X ∖ D with its open immersion j: U -> X. Conventions: 'strict' means that charts exist on an open cover of X over K itself; the normal crossings divisors of Diao-Lan-Liu-Zhu (charts étale-locally, equivalently analytic-locally after a finite separable extension of K) form the weaker class and are not smooth pairs in this sense unless charts exist over K. D is reduced and an effective Cartier divisor. No condition is imposed on irreducible components, and r may vary with x.
hypotheses: X smooth over Spa(K, K°): locally of finite type (hence locally noetherian and analytic) and smooth in R0's sense.
Charts are analytic-local on X and defined over K; h is étale in R0's sense.
proofSteps: Package X, D and the chart-existence property as a structure; U := X ∖ D is open because D is closed (anchor Layer 5 open subspaces).

Chart restriction and composition with étale maps: restrictions of étale maps to open subspaces and composites of étale maps are étale (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/open-embedding-etale, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-smooth-composition); this gives SmoothPair.restrict and SmoothPair.pullbackEtale.

Effective Cartier and reduced (api isCartier_D): on a chart, h is flat (étale implies flat for analytic adic spaces, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-flat-unramified), and T_1⋯T_r is a non-zero-divisor of K⟨T⟩, so h^*(T_1⋯T_r) is a non-zero-divisor of O_V; D ∩ V = V ×_{B^n_K} V(T_1⋯T_r) is étale over the reduced V(T_1⋯T_r), hence reduced.
Trivial pair (api SmoothPair.trivial): charts with r = 0 are the étale maps to closed polydiscs of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-local-structure (Huber 1.6.10, Tate case with M_i = {1}).
acceptance: The model pair (B^n_K, V(T_1 ⋯ T_r)) is a smooth pair with the identity chart.
A smooth pair (X, ∅) is the same as a smooth X.
(B^1_K, {0}) has complement the punctured closed disc {0 < |T| ≤ 1}, which is not quasi-compact.

nodes.title: Analytification of an algebraic strict normal crossings pair is a smooth pair
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field, X a smooth scheme over K and D ⊂ X a strict normal crossings divisor in the algebraic sense: Zariski-locally on X there are étale morphisms x = (x_1, ..., x_n): V -> A^n_K with D ∩ V = V(x_1 ⋯ x_r). Then (X^ad, D^ad) is a smooth pair in the sense of AdicSpacesPartII:R4/smooth-pair, and (X ∖ D)^ad = X^ad ∖ D^ad as open subspaces, with j^ad the boundary-complement inclusion.
hypotheses: X smooth and locally of finite type over K; D reduced with Zariski-local étale coordinates as stated.
proofSteps: X^ad is smooth over Spa(K, K°) (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-etale-smooth) and D^ad is a closed adic subspace with ideal the analytification of I_D (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-immersions).

V^ad -> A^{n,ad} is étale (Huber 1.7.3(i), AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-etale-smooth); A^{n,ad} is the increasing union of the polydiscs {|x_i| ≤ |ϖ|^{-k}} (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytic-affine-space).

On the preimage V_k of the radius-|ϖ|^{-k} polydisc (an open subspace of V^ad), h_k := (ϖ^k x_1, ..., ϖ^k x_n): V_k -> B^n_K is the restriction of the étale V^ad -> A^{n,ad} to V_k followed by the scaling isomorphism of that polydisc onto B^n_K, hence étale (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/open-embedding-etale, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-smooth-composition), and h_k^*(T_1⋯T_r) = ϖ^{kr} x_1⋯x_r generates the same ideal as x_1⋯x_r, giving a strict chart.
Complements: open immersions analytify to open immersions onto the preimage (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-immersions).
acceptance: For X = A^1_K and D = {0}, the analytified pair is (A^{1,ad}, {0}) with complement G_m^ad; restricted to B^1 it is the model pair (B^1, V(T)).

For X a smooth toroidal compactification of a Shimura variety and D its boundary (a strict normal crossings divisor), (X^ad, D^ad) is a smooth pair whose complement is the analytified open Shimura variety.

nodes.title: Restriction of the étale and pro-étale sites of a smooth pair to its boundary complement
nodes.statement: Let (X, D) be a smooth pair over K (AdicSpacesPartII:R4/smooth-pair) with boundary complement j: U = X ∖ D -> X. Construct: (a) U as an object of X_ét and the equivalence of sites U_ét ≃ X_ét/U (AdicSpacesPartII:R4/etale-slice-site), under which the morphism of sites j_ét: U_ét -> X_ét of AdicSpacesPartII:R4/etale-site-functoriality is the slice morphism; (b) the functors on sheaves of sets and of abelian groups j^{-1}F = F|_U with (j^{-1}F)(V) = F(V) for V ∈ U_ét, j_*G with (j_*G)(W) = G(W ×_X U), and j_! (extension by zero for abelian sheaves), the sheafification of the presheaf W ↦ G(W) if W -> X factors through U and W ↦ 0 otherwise; with adjunctions j_! ⊣ j^{-1} ⊣ j_* and canonical isomorphisms j^{-1} j_* ≅ id ≅ j^{-1} j_! (j is a monomorphism); (c) the same on the pro-étale sites, U_proét ≃ X_proét/U (AdicSpacesPartII:R4/proetale-slice-open-subspace), with j_proét compatible with ν: ν_X ∘ j_proét corresponds to j_ét ∘ ν_U. The inclusion j is in general not quasi-compact (for (B^1, V(T)) the complement is not quasi-compact), so no base-change or continuity statement requiring a qcqs morphism (such as Scholze Corollary 3.17(ii) for j) is part of this construction; exactness properties and derived functors of j_!, j_* belong to ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology.
hypotheses: (X, D) a smooth pair; only the ordinary (non-logarithmic) sites are restricted here.
Sheaves of sets and abelian groups; j_! only for sheaves with a zero object (abelian groups, modules).
proofSteps: U is open, hence étale over X (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/open-embedding-etale, Huber 1.6.7(i)), so it is an object of X_ét (AdicSpacesPartII:R4/etale-site-on-analytic-carriers).
Slice equivalences: AdicSpacesPartII:R4/etale-slice-site and AdicSpacesPartII:R4/proetale-slice-open-subspace.

j^{-1} = mathlib:CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.overPullback (= (Over.forget U).sheafPushforwardContinuous); j_* = its right adjoint, mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous along the cocontinuous forgetful functor (adjunction mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafAdjunctionCocontinuous), equivalently pushforward along base change V ↦ V ×_X U (AdicSpacesPartII:R4/etale-site-functoriality, mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPushforwardContinuous, identified via mathlib:CategoryTheory.Adjunction.sheafPushforwardContinuous as in AdicSpacesPartII:R4/etale-slice-site); j_! = mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPullback along the forgetful functor (the left adjoint of j^{-1}, existing by weak sheafification), computed as the sheafification of the left Kan extension W ↦ colim over Hom_X(W, U) of G, which is G(W) if W factors through U and the initial object (0 for abelian groups, ∅ for sets) otherwise, since Hom_X(W, U) has at most one element.
j^{-1}j_* ≅ id and j^{-1}j_! ≅ id: for V ∈ U_ét, V ×_X U = V.
Pro-étale compatibility: AdicSpacesPartII:R4/proetale-site-functoriality applied to j.
acceptance: For D = ∅, j = id and all three functors are the identity.

For (B^1, V(T)) and the constant sheaf Z/n on U_ét: H^0(X, j_! Z/n) = 0 (a nonzero section of j_!Z/n over X would be a locally constant section on U with support closed in X, impossible since 0 lies in the closure of U), while H^0(X, j_* Z/n) = H^0(U, Z/n) = Z/n (U is connected).

nodes.title: Geometric points of A1 as points of the étale site, and their compatibility with pullback
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally noetherian analytic adic space. A geometric point of X (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-and-geometric-points) is a morphism ξ: Spa(C, C⁺) -> X with C an algebraically closed complete nonarchimedean field and C⁺ ⊆ C an open valuation subring (higher-rank C⁺ allowed). (a) The fibre functor ε_ξ: X_ét -> Set, U ↦ Hom_X(Spa(C, C⁺), U), is a point of the site X_ét in mathlib's sense (mathlib:CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Point): its category of elements (étale neighbourhoods of ξ) is cofiltered and initially small, and coverings are sent to jointly surjective families; the stalk F_ξ = colim over étale neighbourhoods of F(U). The covering property rests on the splitting of étale covers of a geometric point: every jointly surjective family of étale morphisms to Spa(C, C⁺) has a member that admits a section (Scholze, Étale cohomology of diamonds, Proposition 14.3). An étale space over Spa(C, C⁺) is only locally on the source an open subspace of Spa(C, C⁺): when C⁺ ≠ O_C, Spa(C, C⁺) is a chain of at least two specializations and an étale space over it need not be a disjoint union of open subspaces of copies of Spa(C, C⁺). (b) For a morphism f: X -> Y, f∘ξ is a geometric point of Y and ε_{f∘ξ} ≅ ε_ξ ∘ f* naturally, where f* is the base change of AdicSpacesPartII:R4/etale-site-functoriality; hence (f^{-1}G)_ξ ≅ G_{f∘ξ} for every sheaf G on Y_ét, naturally in G. (c) On the pro-étale site of AdicSpacesPartII:R4/proetale-site-on-analytic-carriers, for a point x ∈ X with Y_x = Spa(K, K⁺) -> X, Scholze's morphism of topoi i_x: Sh(Y_x,profét) -> Sh(X_proét) is compatible with pullback: for f: X -> Y, f_proét ∘ i_x ≅ i_{f(x)} ∘ (Y_x -> Y_{f(x)})_profét. Stalks at geometric points alone are not conservative on X_proét, and the deleted final sentence of Scholze Proposition 3.13 (enough points given by profinite covers of geometric points) is not used; both topoi are coherent and have enough points abstractly.
hypotheses: X locally noetherian analytic; geometric points in Huber's sense with arbitrary valuation subring C⁺.
The conservativity of the family (ε_ξ) and the description of strict localizations are A1's (Huber §2.5, via the A1 node).
proofSteps: (a) Cofilteredness: X_ét has fibre products and equalizers (the equalizer of two X-maps U ⇉ V is the preimage of the open diagonal of the unramified V -> X, Huber 1.6.8(c) in AdicSpacesPartII:R0/infinitesimal-criteria), so the category of elements of the left exact functor ε_ξ is cofiltered and the colimit defining F_ξ is filtered (as in Scholze, Étale cohomology of diamonds, proof of Proposition 14.3).

(a) Initial smallness (required by mathlib:CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Point): every étale neighbourhood (U, ξ_U) receives a map from one with U affinoid étale over an affinoid open of X (take an affinoid open of U containing the image of the closed point of Spa(C, C⁺); it contains the whole image because opens are stable under generalization). Isomorphism classes of affinoid étale spaces over a fixed affinoid open of X form a set (standard étale presentations, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-local-structure), so the category of elements has a small weakly initial set and is initially small by mathlib:CategoryTheory.initiallySmall_of_small_weakly_initial_set (it is cofiltered by the previous step).

(a) Coverings: let (U_i -> U) be a jointly surjective family in X_ét and ξ_U: Spa(C, C⁺) -> U an X-morphism. The fibre products V_i = U_i ×_U Spa(C, C⁺) exist, V_i -> Spa(C, C⁺) is étale (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence, case (a); AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-etale-base-change), and the V_i cover Spa(C, C⁺) (point-surjectivity, Huber 1.2.3(iii)(d), AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-product-points). Choose i and v ∈ V_i over the closed point s of Spa(C, C⁺). Near v, V_i -> Spa(C, C⁺) is an open embedding W -> Z followed by a finite étale Z -> W' and an open embedding W' ⊆ Spa(C, C⁺) (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-local-open-finite-etale-factorisation). Every point of Spa(C, C⁺) is a generalization of s, so the open W' ∋ s is Spa(C, C⁺); Z = Spa(B, B⁺) with B a finite étale C-algebra and B⁺ the integral closure of C⁺ (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-etale-algebra-comparison), B ≅ C^n because C is algebraically closed (mathlib:Algebra.FormallyEtale.equivPiOfIsSepClosed), so B⁺ = (C⁺)^n, so Z is a disjoint union of n copies of Spa(C, C⁺); the copy containing v has v as its closed point, so it lies in the open W. Hence V_i contains an open subspace mapped isomorphically onto Spa(C, C⁺), which is a section, and ξ_U lifts to U_i. This is the splitting of étale covers of Spa(C, C⁺) (Scholze, Étale cohomology of diamonds, Proposition 14.3 and Definition 7.15 with Proposition 7.16, stated there for perfectoid Spa(C, C⁺); the argument here uses only the local structure of étale morphisms). Only the member through the closed point is split: no global decomposition of étale spaces over Spa(C, C⁺) is used, and none holds (see the non-example in the acceptance).

(b) Hom_Y(Spa(C, C⁺), V) = Hom_X(Spa(C, C⁺), V ×_Y X) by the universal property of the fibre product (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence), so ε_{f∘ξ} ≅ ε_ξ ∘ f* is mathlib's comap of the point ε_ξ along the flat, cover-preserving functor f* (mathlib:CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Point.comap); the stalk formula (f^{-1}G)_ξ ≅ G_{f∘ξ} is mathlib:CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Point.sheafFiberComapIso.
(c) Scholze Proposition 3.13 (without its last sentence, per the erratum) in AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-site-corrected, and functoriality AdicSpacesPartII:R4/proetale-site-functoriality.
acceptance: For X = Spa(K, K°) with K a complete field and ξ: Spa(C, O_C) -> X a completed algebraic closure, ε_ξ identifies Sh(X_ét) with continuous Gal(K^sep/K)-sets, and stalks are the underlying sets.
For f = j: U -> X the boundary-complement inclusion of a smooth pair and ξ a geometric point of U, (j^{-1}G)_ξ = G_{j∘ξ}; for a geometric point of X not factoring through U, (j_!G)_ξ = 0.
Pro-étale non-example: on X_proét there are nonzero sheaves all of whose stalks at geometric points vanish (Scholze Remark 3.14), so geometric-point stalks are used only on X_ét.

Non-example (C⁺ ≠ O_C): let C⁺ have rank two, s the closed point and η the rank-one point of Spa(C, C⁺); {η} = {|a| ≤ 1} for any a ∈ O_C ∖ C⁺ is open. Gluing two copies of Spa(C, C⁺) along {η} gives a surjective, non-separated adic space Y -> Spa(C, C⁺) which is locally on Y an open embedding, hence étale; Y is not a disjoint union of open subspaces of copies of Spa(C, C⁺) (it is connected and not isomorphic to Spa(C, C⁺)), while each copy is a section of the cover {Y -> Spa(C, C⁺)}.

nodes.title: Sousperfectoid Tate rings and perfectoid frames
nodes.statement: Fix a prime p. Let R be a complete Hausdorff Tate ring (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing) in which p is topologically nilpotent (equivalently, a Tate ring with a continuous ring map Z_p -> R: a complete Tate Z_p-algebra). A perfectoid frame for R is a triple (R̃, ι, σ) consisting of a perfectoid Tate ring R̃ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras: complete, uniform, with a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ such that ϖ^p divides p in R̃° and Frobenius R̃°/ϖ -> R̃°/ϖ^p is bijective), a continuous ring homomorphism ι: R -> R̃, and a continuous R-linear map σ: R̃ -> R (R̃ an R-module through ι) with σ ∘ ι = id_R. R is sousperfectoid if it admits a perfectoid frame; a Huber pair (R, R⁺) is sousperfectoid if R is. Conventions: ι is then injective and a homeomorphism onto the closed subring ι(R) = ker(id - ι∘σ); σ need not be multiplicative and need not map any ring of integral elements into R⁺; no perfectoid base field is fixed, and R̃ is not required to contain one; characteristic p is allowed (then R̃ is a perfect complete Tate ring).
hypotheses: R complete and Hausdorff (anchor convention 3), Tate, p topologically nilpotent in R.
The splitting is in topological R-modules: σ is continuous and R-linear.
proofSteps: Package (R̃, ι, σ) as a structure; IsSousperfectoid R := Nonempty (PerfectoidFrame R).
ι injective: σ(ι(r)) = r. ι is a topological embedding with closed image: σ|_{ι(R)} is a continuous inverse and ι(R) = {x : ι(σ(x)) = x} is closed because R̃ is Hausdorff.
acceptance: Perfectoid rings are sousperfectoid with the frame (R, id, id) (Berkeley Example 6.3.2(1)).
Q_p⟨T⟩ is sousperfectoid with frame Q_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ (Berkeley Example 6.3.2(2)) but not perfectoid.

nodes.title: Topologically split injections are stable under completed base change (Hansen-Kedlaya Remark 7.2)
nodes.statement: Let R be a complete Tate ring, ι: R -> R̃ a continuous homomorphism to a complete Tate ring with a continuous R-linear retraction σ (σ∘ι = id), and R -> S a continuous homomorphism of complete Tate rings. Let R̃ ⊗̂_R S be the completed tensor product of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product (completion of R̃ ⊗_R S for the topology defined by the image of R̃_0 ⊗ S_0 and a pseudo-uniformizer). Then ι_S = ι ⊗̂ id: S -> R̃ ⊗̂_R S has the continuous S-linear retraction σ_S = σ ⊗̂ id_S, so ι_S is a closed embedding. If moreover R̃ ⊗̂_R S is perfectoid, (R̃ ⊗̂_R S, ι_S, σ_S) is a perfectoid frame for S. The completed tensor product is used as it is: no uniform completion is taken (a uniform completion can destroy the splitting).
hypotheses: All rings complete Hausdorff Tate; σ continuous and R-linear.
The frame conclusion needs R̃ ⊗̂_R S perfectoid, which is proved separately in each application (rational localisation, finite étale, Tate algebras).
proofSteps: σ ⊗ id_S: R̃ ⊗_R S -> R ⊗_R S = S is well defined and S-linear (mathlib:TensorProduct functoriality).

Continuity: a continuous R-linear map between Tate R-modules is bounded, σ(ϖ^c R̃_0) ⊆ R_0 for some c; hence (σ ⊗ id)(ϖ^{c+n}·im(R̃_0 ⊗ S_0)) ⊆ ϖ^n S_0, so σ ⊗ id is uniformly continuous for the tensor topology and extends to the completion (universal property of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product and mathlib:UniformSpace.Completion).
σ_S ∘ ι_S = id_S holds on the dense image of S and hence everywhere; closed embedding as in AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-ring.
acceptance: For S = R the lemma returns (ι, σ).
For S = R⟨T/s⟩ a rational localisation, R̃ ⊗̂_R S = R̃⟨ι(T)/ι(s)⟩ and the resulting splitting is the one used in Berkeley's proof of 6.3.3(1).

nodes.title: Sousperfectoid rings are uniform
nodes.statement: Let R be sousperfectoid with frame (R̃, ι, σ). Then R° = ι^{-1}(R̃°), and R° is bounded; that is, R is uniform in the sense of Hansen-Kedlaya Definition 2.3 (anchor Layer 4.2). In particular R is reduced.
hypotheses: R complete Tate with a perfectoid frame.
proofSteps: ι maps R° into R̃°: a continuous homomorphism out of a Tate ring maps bounded sets to bounded sets (the image of a ring of definition R_0 lies in ι(ϖ)^{-N} R̃_0 for some N).

Conversely, if ι(a) is power-bounded then {a^n} is bounded in R, because ι is a topological embedding onto its image (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-ring) and boundedness is a condition on neighbourhoods of 0 (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsBounded).

R̃ is uniform (it is perfectoid, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras), so R̃° is bounded and so is its preimage R° under the embedding ι (Hansen-Kedlaya Definition 2.3: uniformity descends along strict inclusions).
Uniform Huber rings are reduced (a nilpotent x gives unbounded {ϖ^{-n}x} ⊆ R°).
acceptance: Q_p⟨T⟩° = Z_p⟨T⟩ is bounded, as predicted.

nodes.title: Rational localisations of sousperfectoid rings are sousperfectoid (Berkeley 6.3.3(1))

Explicitly: for a frame (R̃, ι, σ) and a ring of integral elements R̃⁺ ⊆ R̃° containing ι(R⁺), the preimage Ũ of U in X̃ = Spa(R̃, R̃⁺) is the rational subset R(ι(T)/ι(s)), R̃ ⊗̂_R O_X(U) ≅ O_X̃(Ũ) = R̃⟨ι(T)/ι(s)⟩ is perfectoid, and (O_X̃(Ũ), ι ⊗̂ id, σ ⊗̂ id) is a perfectoid frame for O_X(U).

nodes.title: Finite extensions of Q_p are sousperfectoid
nodes.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p and K^cycl the completion of K(μ_{p^∞}). Then K -> K^cycl admits a continuous K-linear retraction, so (K^cycl, inclusion, retraction) is a perfectoid frame and K is sousperfectoid. More generally K⟨T_1, ..., T_n⟩ and every rational localisation and finite étale algebra of it are sousperfectoid.
hypotheses: K finite over Q_p (discretely valued, so orthonormal bases exist).
proofSteps: K^cycl is a perfectoid field (PerfectoidSpaces:P1, requested: cyclotomic perfectoid fields).

Retraction: equip the K-Banach space K^cycl with the lattice O_{K^cycl}; it is ϖ_K-adically complete and ϖ_K-torsion-free, so lifting a basis of O_{K^cycl}/ϖ_K O_{K^cycl} over the residue field of K that contains the class of 1 (nonzero since 1 ∉ ϖ_K O_{K^cycl}) gives an orthonormal basis (e_i) with e_0 = 1: every x is uniquely Σ a_i e_i with a_i ∈ K, a_i -> 0. The coordinate x ↦ a_0 is a continuous K-linear retraction.

nodes.title: Étale spaces over a sousperfectoid space are sousperfectoid adic spaces
nodes.statement: Let X be a sousperfectoid adic space and f: Y -> X étale in the local-description sense of AdicEtaleGeometry A1 (Kedlaya-Liu Definition 8.2.16: every y ∈ Y has an open neighbourhood on which f factors as an open immersion, a finite étale morphism and an open immersion, where finite étale means affinoid-locally on the target Spa(S, S⁺) -> Spa(R, R⁺) with R -> S finite étale and S⁺ the integral closure of R⁺). Then Y is an adic space (not merely a preadic space) and is sousperfectoid. In particular every object of the étale site X_ét is a sousperfectoid adic space, and for a finite étale R-algebra S over a sousperfectoid R and a composite of rational localisations and finite étale maps R -> S', the ring S' itself is sousperfectoid. For a general étale map, sousperfectoidness is a property of the space Y, not of a global ring: Y is covered by sousperfectoid affinoids, while the sousperfectoid property of rings is not known to be of local nature.
hypotheses: X sousperfectoid; f étale in A1's local-description sense (for locally noetherian targets this is Huber's étale, AdicSpacesPartII:R4/etale-site-on-analytic-carriers).

V is open in W, hence covered by rational subsets of the Spa(S_k), which are sousperfectoid (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-rational-localisation).
A preadic space covered by affinoid adic spaces is an adic space (anchor Layer 5), and it is sousperfectoid by definition.

nodes.title: Sousperfectoid spaces are stably adic
nodes.statement: Let X = Spa(R, R⁺) with R sousperfectoid, and let B_X be the class of objects Y -> X of X_ét (AdicEtaleGeometry A1's local-description sense) of the form Y = Spa(S, S⁺) with (R, R⁺) -> (S, S⁺) a finite composite of rational localisations and finite étale maps (plus rings the integral closures). Then every such S is sousperfectoid (so Spa(S, S⁺) is an affinoid adic space), every object of X_ét is covered by members of B_X, B_X is closed under fibre products in X_ét, and for Y ∈ B_X every finite étale Y' -> Y and every rational subdomain Y' ⊆ Y lies in B_X. Hence B_X is a stable basis of X_ét in the sense of Kedlaya-Liu Definition 8.2.19 and X is stably adic. Consequently (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/stable-basis-etale-vector-bundles; Kedlaya-Liu Theorem 8.2.22(c),(d)): for every finite projective R-module M, M̃ is an acyclic sheaf on B_X, in particular H^i(X_ét, O) = 0 for i > 0; and finite projective R-modules are equivalent to finite locally free O_{X_ét}-modules. For a general sousperfectoid adic space these statements hold on every sousperfectoid affinoid open, and such opens cover X. The class of all affinoid objects Spa(S, S⁺) of X_ét with S sousperfectoid is not used as the basis: its closure under fibre products would need S_1 ⊗̂_S S_2 to be sousperfectoid for a general étale S -> S_1, which is not known.
hypotheses: X = Spa(R, R⁺) with R sousperfectoid; X_ét in A1's local-description sense.

Kedlaya-Liu define X_ét and stable bases for preadic spaces over an analytic field; here, as in Berkeley §19.5, they are used over Z_p. The proofs of Kedlaya-Liu 8.2.20-8.2.22 do not use the base field.
proofSteps: Members of B_X are sousperfectoid, by induction on the length of the composite (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-rational-localisation, AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-finite-etale). Hence they are sheafy (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-sheafy), and Spa(S, S⁺) is an adic affinoid space.

Covering: every object of X_ét is locally an open subspace of a finite étale space over an open of X. Covering these opens by rational subsets gives a covering by members of B_X (as in AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-etale-stability and in Hansen-Kedlaya's proof of Proposition 5.5).

Fibre products: base changes of rational localisations and of finite étale maps are again such maps (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-rational-localisation; finite étale base change). A morphism Y_1 -> Y_2 of X_ét between members of B_X is itself a composite of this kind: its graph Y_1 -> Y_1 ×_X Y_2 is a section of a separated étale map, hence an open and closed immersion, i.e. a rational localisation at an idempotent. So Y_1 ×_Y Y_2 ∈ B_X.
Stability under finite étale maps and rational subdomain embeddings holds by the definition of B_X.

Consequences: AdicSpacesPartII:R5/stable-basis-etale-vector-bundles. O-acyclicity is the case M = R; compare Hansen-Kedlaya Proposition 5.8 for strongly sheafy R, which applies to sousperfectoid R by Hansen-Kedlaya Corollary 7.4.
General X: apply the above to every sousperfectoid affinoid open (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-adic-space).
acceptance: For X affinoid perfectoid this recovers the stably adic property of perfectoid spaces.
Berkeley §19.5: vector bundles on X_ét for sousperfectoid X are finite projective modules on affinoids, the input to Tannakian G-torsors.

nodes.title: Base change of étale maps to locally noetherian spaces along sousperfectoid spaces
nodes.statement: Let Z be a sousperfectoid adic space, W a locally noetherian analytic adic space (e.g. a rigid space), g: Z -> W a morphism and f: Y -> W étale (R0). Then the fibre product Z ×_W Y exists in the category of adic spaces, the projection Z ×_W Y -> Z is étale in A1's local-description sense, and Z ×_W Y is sousperfectoid. Affinoid formula: if Y' ⊆ Y is open and f|_{Y'} factors as an open immersion Y' -> Y'' followed by a finite étale morphism Y'' = Spa(B, B⁺) -> W' = Spa(A, A⁺) onto an affinoid open W' ⊆ W (A -> B finite étale, B⁺ the integral closure of A⁺; such factorisations exist locally by Huber Lemma 2.2.8), and Z' = Spa(C, C⁺) ⊆ g^{-1}(W') is an affinoid open with C sousperfectoid, then C ⊗_A B is sousperfectoid, Z' ×_{W'} Y'' = Spa(C ⊗_A B, integral closure of C⁺ in C ⊗_A B), and Z' ×_W Y' is its open subspace lying over Y'.
hypotheses: W locally noetherian so that étale maps to W have the local open-immersion/finite-étale description (Huber Lemma 2.2.8 via A1); Z sousperfectoid, possibly non-noetherian (so Huber's fibre-product theorems, which assume noetherian or sheafy charts, do not apply directly).
proofSteps: Local description of f: AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-local-open-finite-etale-factorisation (Huber Lemma 2.2.8 for the locally noetherian analytic W; Berkeley p. 55).

Finite étale piece: C -> C ⊗_A B is finite étale (base change, mathlib:Algebra.Etale); with the natural topology and integral closure it is a complete affinoid ring (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra), sousperfectoid (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-finite-etale) and sheafy (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-sheafy); it is the pushout of complete affinoid rings (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product-universal-property; the completion is not needed since C ⊗_A B is finite projective over C), so Spa of it is the fibre product (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-fibre-product).
Open immersion pieces: base change of an open immersion is the open preimage (anchor Layer 5).
Glue the local fibre products along the canonical isomorphisms given by their universal properties (anchor Layer 5 gluing).
Sousperfectoid: AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-etale-stability applied to the étale projection.
acceptance: For W = B^n_L, Z = X ×_L B^n with X affinoid perfectoid, and Y -> B^n étale, Z ×_W Y = X ×_L Y is the BHW product.
For Y = W' an open subspace of W, Z ×_W Y = g^{-1}(W').

nodes.title: Perfectoid space times a polydisc: sousperfectoid, not perfectoid
nodes.statement: Let L be a perfectoid field, X = Spa(S, S⁺) an affinoid perfectoid space over L and B^n_L = Spa(L⟨T_1, ..., T_n⟩, O_L⟨T⟩). Then the fibre product X ×_L B^n_L exists in adic spaces and equals Spa(S⟨T_1, ..., T_n⟩, S⁺⟨T_1, ..., T_n⟩), which is a sousperfectoid affinoid adic space; for n ≥ 1 and S ≠ 0, S⟨T_1, ..., T_n⟩ is not perfectoid.
hypotheses: L perfectoid; S ≠ 0 for the non-perfectoid clause; n ≥ 1.
proofSteps: S ⊗̂_L L⟨T⟩ = S⟨T⟩ with plus ring S⁺⟨T⟩ (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-restricted-power-series).

S⟨T⟩ is sousperfectoid (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-rings, S perfectoid hence sousperfectoid) and so sheafy (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-sheafy); Spa of the completed tensor product is then the fibre product (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-fibre-product).

Not perfectoid: S is uniform with S° bounded, and S⟨T⟩° = S°⟨T⟩ (for every point v of Spa(S, S°) the Gauss extension v_G(Σ a_α T^α) = max_α v(a_α) is a point of Spa(S⟨T⟩, S°⟨T⟩), and power-bounded elements are ≤ 1 at every point, so v(a_α) ≤ 1 for all v and α, and a_α ∈ S° by the plus-ring criterion tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.mem_iff_forall_vle_one). Then S⟨T⟩°/ϖ^p = (S°/ϖ^p)[T] and, since p ∈ ϖ^p S°, the Frobenius image of (S°/ϖ)[T] consists of polynomials in T_1^p, ..., T_n^p; T_1 is not among them because S°/ϖ^p ≠ 0. So Frobenius S⟨T⟩°/ϖ -> S⟨T⟩°/ϖ^p is not surjective (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras).
acceptance: Q_p^cycl⟨T⟩ is sousperfectoid and not perfectoid; its perfectoid cover Q_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ is a frame.

nodes.title: The product X ×_L Y of a perfectoid space and a smooth rigid space (BHW Corollary 3.4)
nodes.statement: Let L be a perfectoid field, L' a perfectoid field extension of L (complete, with L -> L' continuous), X a perfectoid space over L and Y a rigid space over L' (an adic space locally of topologically finite type over Spa(L', O_L')) that is smooth over L' (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-morphism). Then the fibre product X ×_L Y := X ×_{Spa(L, O_L)} Y exists in the category of adic spaces and is a sousperfectoid adic space. Construction: X ×_L Y = X' ×_{L'} Y with X' = X ×_L Spa(L', O_L') perfectoid; for affinoid perfectoid X' = Spa(S, S⁺) and an open V ⊆ Y with an étale map h: V -> B^n_{L'} (Huber 1.6.10), X' ×_{L'} V = (X' ×_{L'} B^n_{L'}) ×_{B^n_{L'}} V with X' ×_{L'} B^n = Spa(S⟨T_1, ..., T_n⟩, S⁺⟨T⟩); these pieces glue. It is not asserted, and is false in general, that X ×_L Y is perfectoid.
hypotheses: L, L' perfectoid fields (BHW: L a perfectoid extension of Q_p^cyc); the printed hypothesis 'a perfectoid extension of L'/L' means 'a perfectoid extension L' of L' (sourceIssues).
Y smooth over L' (so locally étale over polydiscs); X arbitrary perfectoid over L.
proofSteps: X' = X ×_L Spa L' exists and is perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces), and X ×_L Y ≅ X' ×_{L'} Y by transitivity of fibre products, Y being over L'.
Cover X' by affinoid perfectoids Spa(S, S⁺) and Y by opens V with étale h: V -> B^n_{L'} (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-local-structure; Huber 1.6.10 with M_i = {1} over the Tate base L').
Polydisc step: AdicSpacesPartII:R5/perfectoid-times-polydisc.
Étale step: AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-etale-base-change with Z = Spa(S⟨T⟩), W = B^n_{L'}.
Glue over the covers of X' and Y using uniqueness of fibre products (anchor Layer 5 gluing); the result is sousperfectoid because each piece is.
acceptance: Y = Spa L': X ×_L Spa L' is the perfectoid fibre product.
Y = B^1_{L'}: X ×_L Y = Spa(S⟨T⟩) locally, sousperfectoid and not perfectoid.
BHW Corollary 3.5: for U smooth over L, X*_{Γ(p^∞)}(ε)_a ×_L U exists as a sousperfectoid adic space.
