nodes.title: Products with a smooth space preserve tilde-limits (BHW Corollary 3.5)
nodes.statement: Let L be a perfectoid field, (X_n)_{n ≥ 1} an inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated adic spaces over L with adic transition maps, and X_∞ a quasi-compact quasi-separated perfectoid space over L with compatible maps such that X_∞ ∼ lim_n X_n (Huber's tilde-limit, ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limits-and-cohomological-continuity). Let U be a quasi-compact quasi-separated rigid space smooth over L such that each X_n ×_L U exists as an adic space (e.g. X_n rigid over L, or sousperfectoid). Then X_∞ ×_L U (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/perfectoid-times-smooth-fibre-product) satisfies X_∞ ×_L U ∼ lim_n X_n ×_L U. For U not quasi-compact, the same holds with U replaced by any quasi-compact open U' ⊆ U.
hypotheses: Huber's X ∼ lim X_n (Definition 2.4.2) is defined in the category of quasi-compact quasi-separated (pseudo-)adic spaces with adic morphisms, hence the qcqs hypotheses. BHW Corollary 3.5 states the result for smooth U without quasi-compactness; this is its qcqs form.

No affinoid plus-ring criterion is assumed. The route through such a criterion (the request to ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0) would need A_∞⁺ to be the closure of the integral closure of colim A_n⁺, which does not follow from X_∞ ∼ lim X_n.
proofSteps: Put Y := X_1 ×_L U, which exists by hypothesis and is qcqs. Its projection Y -> X_1 is locally of finite type, being a base change of the smooth, hence locally of finite type, U -> Spa L (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/base-change-stability); in particular it is locally of weakly finite type.

Transitivity of fibre products: Y ×_{X_1} X_n = X_n ×_L U and Y ×_{X_1} X_∞ = X_∞ ×_L U (the latter exists by AdicSpacesPartII:R5/perfectoid-times-smooth-fibre-product). Affinoid-locally these are Spa of completed tensor products (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-fibre-product).
The index category has final object 1, so Huber Remark 2.4.3(ii) (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/tilde-limit-base-change) gives X_∞ ×_L U ∼ lim_n X_n ×_L U.

BHW's pointwise-approximation argument (colim_n (A_n ⊗̂_L B) -> A_∞ ⊗̂_L B has dense image; AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product) is the density condition (b). The homeomorphism condition (a), which BHW do not verify (sourceIssues AdicSpacesPartII/E27), comes from step 3.
For non-quasi-compact U: the tilde-limit condition for X_∞ ×_L U' holds for each quasi-compact open U' ⊆ U by the qcqs case.

nodes.title: Profinite flat modules over the ring of integers of a p-adic field
nodes.statement: Let E be a finite extension of Q_p, O = O_E with uniformizer ϖ. A topological O-module M is linear-topological if 0 has a basis of neighbourhoods consisting of O-submodules (mathlib IsLinearTopology O M), and M is a profinite flat O-module if it is flat over O (equivalently ϖ-torsion-free), linear-topological, compact and Hausdorff (CHJ Definition 6.1; CHJ's "compact" includes Hausdorff). Then the topology of M is profinite, every open submodule has finite index, and M is ϖ-adically complete and separated.
hypotheses: O a complete discrete valuation ring with finite residue field (E/Q_p finite).
proofSteps: Define the predicate as Module.Flat O M ∧ IsLinearTopology O M ∧ CompactSpace M ∧ T2Space M.
Open submodules N have finite index: M/N is discrete and compact, hence finite. So M/N is a finite-length O-module and ϖ^k M ⊆ N for some k.

Hausdorff and ϖ^k M ⊆ N for every open N give ∩_k ϖ^k M = 0 (separated). Completeness: a ϖ-adic Cauchy sequence is Cauchy for the given uniformity, so it converges in the compact Hausdorff (hence complete) M, to x say. Each ϖ^n M is compact, hence closed, so x - x_m ∈ ϖ^n M for m large. So M is ϖ-adically complete (mathlib IsAdicComplete).
acceptance: ∏_{i∈I} O with the product topology is profinite flat for every set I.
Z_p[[T]] (topology (p, T)-adic) is a profinite flat Z_p-module, with pseudobasis (T^n).

nodes.title: Pseudobases of profinite flat modules (CHJ Proposition 6.2)
nodes.statement: A topological O-module M is profinite flat if and only if it is isomorphic, as a topological O-module, to ∏_{i∈I} O with the product topology for some set I. A family (e_i)_{i∈I} realising such an isomorphism is a pseudobasis; the submodules M_{J,n} = ∏_{i∈J} ϖ^n O e_i × ∏_{i∉J} O e_i (J finite, n ≥ 1) form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0.
hypotheses: O a complete DVR with finite residue field.
proofSteps: (<=) Products of compact spaces are compact (Tychonoff); flatness and linear topology are evident.

(=>) CHJ imports this from SGA 3 Exposé VII_B 0.3.8 (not read; gap). Proof route used here: D = Hom_cont(M, E/O) is a discrete ϖ-divisible torsion O-module (divisible because M is torsion-free, discrete because M is compact); divisible modules over the DVR O are injective, hence D ≅ (E/O)^{(I)}; Pontryagin-Matlis duality M ≅ Hom(D, E/O) ≅ ∏_I O identifies the topologies.

nodes.title: Small Z_p-algebras
nodes.statement: A small Z_p-algebra (CHJ §1.4) is a ring R that is reduced, p-torsion-free and finite as an algebra over Z_p[[X_1, ..., X_d]] for some d ≥ 0. It carries its canonical adic profinite topology (the a-adic topology for an ideal of definition a, e.g. the Jacobson radical, independent of choices), for which it is a profinite flat Z_p-module (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/profinite-flat-module) and a noetherian semilocal ring, complete for its p-adic topology.
hypotheses: d unspecified; all constructions are independent of the choice of d and of the ideal of definition.
proofSteps: R is finite over the complete noetherian local ring Z_p[[X]], hence noetherian, semilocal and complete for the topology of the maximal ideal of Z_p[[X]] extended to R; torsion-freeness and compactness give profinite flatness.

nodes.title: The mixed completed tensor product V ⊗̂ M (CHJ §6.1)
nodes.statement: Let E be a finite extension of Q_p with O = O_E, ϖ a uniformizer, and M a profinite flat O-module. For an O-module X define X ⊗̂ M := lim_i (X ⊗_O M/I_i), the limit over any cofinal system (I_i) of open O-submodules of M (CHJ Definition 6.3; independent of the system). For an E-vector space V with an O-lattice V° ⊆ V (V°[1/ϖ] = V) define V ⊗̂ M := (V° ⊗̂ M)[1/ϖ] (CHJ Definition 6.6). When V is an E-Banach space, V° is always taken open and bounded, and V ⊗̂ M is then canonically independent of V°. Suppose V is a Banach E-algebra and M carries an O-algebra structure for which 0 has a basis of open ideals. (CHJ call this a "small O-algebra" without defining it. Examples: a small Z_p-algebra when E = Q_p, or an O-algebra that is reduced, ϖ-torsion-free and finite over O[[X_1, ..., X_d]].) Then choosing V° an open bounded subring and the I_i ideals makes V ⊗̂ M a ring. It is a Banach E-algebra with unit ball V° ⊗̂ M, and with a pseudobasis (e_i) of M it is, as a Banach space, the space of bounded I-indexed families in V.
hypotheses: M profinite flat; V Banach over E with open bounded lattice V° (for non-Banach V the lattice is part of the data and affects the result).
proofSteps: Define the inverse limit and its localisation; independence of (I_i) by cofinality (abstract nonsense).
Ring structure from the ring structures on X ⊗_O M/I_i when the I_i are ideals.
Independence of V°: AdicSpacesPartII:R5/mixed-completed-tensor-exactness (CHJ Corollary 6.5(2)) since two open bounded lattices differ by bounded ϖ-torsion.
Banach structure and bounded-family description: AdicSpacesPartII:R5/mixed-completed-tensor-product-formula.
acceptance: Q_p⟨X⟩ ⊗̂ Z_p[[T]] = (Z_p⟨X⟩[[T]])[1/p] (CHJ proof of Lemma 6.13(1)).

nodes.title: The product formula X ⊗̂ M ≅ ∏_I X̂ (CHJ Proposition 6.4)
nodes.statement: Let M be profinite flat with pseudobasis (e_i)_{i∈I}. The functor X ↦ X ⊗̂ M on O-modules is isomorphic to X ↦ ∏_{i∈I} X̂, where X̂ = lim_n X/ϖ^n X is the ϖ-adic completion; for a Banach space V with open bounded lattice V°, V ⊗̂ M is the space of bounded families (v_i)_{i∈I} in V, with sup norm.
hypotheses: M with a pseudobasis (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/profinite-flat-pseudobasis).
proofSteps: Compute the limit over the neighbourhood system M_{J,n}: X ⊗_O M/M_{J,n} ≅ ∏_{i∈J} X/ϖ^n X; take lim over n then over finite J, using that limits commute with finite products (CHJ proof of 6.4).
Invert ϖ: (∏_I V°)[1/ϖ] is the space of bounded families.

nodes.title: Exactness of - ⊗̂ M (CHJ Corollary 6.5)
nodes.statement: (1) X ↦ X ⊗̂ M is exact on short exact sequences of ϖ-adically complete (and separated) O-modules. (2) If 0 -> X -> Y -> Q -> 0 is exact, X is ϖ-adically complete and ϖ^N Q = 0 for some N, then Y is ϖ-adically complete and (X ⊗̂ M)[1/ϖ] -> (Y ⊗̂ M)[1/ϖ] is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: M profinite flat.
proofSteps: (1) By AdicSpacesPartII:R5/mixed-completed-tensor-product-formula the functor is ∏_I on complete modules, and products are exact.

(2) ϖ^{N+k} Y ⊆ ϖ^k X ⊆ ϖ^k Y, so Y is complete (snake lemma on 0 -> X/ϖ^k X -> Y/ϖ^k X -> Q -> 0 and passage to the limit); Q ⊗̂ M is killed by ϖ^N, so inverting ϖ kills it and (1) gives the isomorphism.
acceptance: Two open bounded lattices V_0° ⊆ V_1° of a Banach space give the same V ⊗̂ M.
Non-example: for the non-complete X = ⊕_N O the functor is not ∏_I X.

nodes.title: Rational and integral coefficient sheaves agree: O_X ⊗̂ M = (O_X⁺ ⊗̂ M)[1/ϖ] on reduced affinoids
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field containing E, X = Spa(A, A°) a reduced affinoid rigid space over K and M a profinite flat O_E-module. For every rational subset U ⊆ X, O_X⁺(U) = O_X(U)° is an open bounded lattice of the Banach space O_X(U), and the natural map (O_X⁺(U) ⊗̂ M)[1/ϖ] -> O_X(U) ⊗̂ M is an isomorphism, compatible with restriction; more generally any two open bounded lattices give canonically isomorphic V ⊗̂ M. The presheaf U ↦ O_X⁺(U) ⊗̂ M ≅ ∏_I O_X⁺(U) is a sheaf on the rational subsets of X. For non-reduced X the power-bounded lattice is unbounded and the formula fails.
hypotheses: X reduced (so O_X(U) is uniform and O_X(U)° is bounded, for all rational U); rigid means A⁺ = A°, so O_X⁺(U) = O_X(U)°.
proofSteps: O_X(U) is a reduced affinoid K-algebra and, since A⁺ = A°, O_X⁺(U) = O_X(U)° (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/reduced-affinoid-rational-localisation, KL Lemma 2.5.9(c),(d)); reduced affinoid algebras are uniform (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/reduced-affinoid-supremum-norm), so O_X(U)° is open and bounded, hence ϖ-adically complete.
Two open bounded lattices V_0°, V_1° satisfy ϖ^N V_1° ⊆ V_0° ⊆ ϖ^{-N} V_1°; AdicSpacesPartII:R5/mixed-completed-tensor-exactness (2) applied to V_0° ∩ V_1° ⊆ V_j° gives the canonical isomorphism.
Sheaf property of O⁺ ⊗̂ M: O⁺ is a sheaf and O⁺(U) is ϖ-adically complete, so by AdicSpacesPartII:R5/mixed-completed-tensor-product-formula O⁺ ⊗̂ M ≅ ∏_I O⁺, a product of sheaves.
acceptance: For X the closed disc over Q_p: (Z_p⟨T⟩ ⊗̂ Z_p[[S]])[1/p] = Q_p⟨T⟩ ⊗̂ Z_p[[S]].
Non-example: X = Spa(Q_p⟨X, Q⟩/(Q²)): (O⁺(X) ⊗̂ Z_p)[1/p] = Q_p⟨X⟩ ≠ O(X) (the test mixedTensor_test_unbounded_lattice).

nodes.title: Finite projective base change of mixed tensors (CHJ Lemma 6.7)
nodes.statement: Let S be a Banach E-algebra, V a finite projective S-module (with its natural Banach topology), U a Banach S-module and M a profinite flat O_E-module. The natural map V ⊗_S (U ⊗̂ M) -> (V ⊗_S U) ⊗̂ M is an isomorphism. If V and U are Banach S-algebras and M is an O_E-algebra whose topology has a basis of open ideals (CHJ's "small O_K-algebra", e.g. a small Z_p-algebra when E = Q_p), it is a ring isomorphism.
hypotheses: V finite projective over S (not merely finite).
proofSteps: Choose an open bounded subring S_0, lattices V_0, U_0 and ideals I_i of M; build V_0 ⊗_{S_0} (U_0 ⊗̂ M) -> (V_0 ⊗_{S_0} U_0) ⊗̂ M levelwise and invert ϖ.
For V finite free the map is an isomorphism componentwise; in general V is a direct summand of a finite free module (mathlib:Module.Projective) and both sides are additive.
acceptance: For V = S^n: S^n ⊗_S (U ⊗̂ M) = (U ⊗̂ M)^n.
For a finite étale S -> S' (e.g. O(U) -> O(U_n) at a finite level of a tower): S' ⊗_S (O(U) ⊗̂ R) = O(U_n) ⊗̂ R.

nodes.title: The coefficient sheaf R = O_X ⊗̂ R on an affinoid rigid space (CHJ §6.3)
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field extension of Q_p, X = Spa(A, A°) an affinoid rigid space over K and R a small Z_p-algebra (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/small-coefficient-algebra). On the site of rational subsets of X with finite rational covers, define R(U) := O_X(U) ⊗̂ R. This is the mixed completed tensor over Z_p of AdicSpacesPartII:R5/mixed-completed-tensor, computed with an open bounded subring of the Banach Q_p-algebra O_X(U); by lattice independence the result does not depend on that choice. Restriction maps are induced by those of O_X, which are bounded. Each R(U) is a Banach K-algebra and the restriction maps are continuous K-algebra maps, so R is a presheaf of Banach K-algebras on the rational site. That R is a sheaf, with vanishing higher Čech cohomology, is the separate theorem AdicSpacesPartII:R5/coefficient-sheaf-tate-acyclicity; it then extends to all quasi-compact opens by finite covers. When X is reduced the unit ball of R(U) can be taken to be O_X°(U) ⊗̂ R (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/rational-integral-compatibility); for non-reduced X it cannot (packet sourceIssue E28).
hypotheses: K a complete nonarchimedean extension of Q_p (characteristic 0 alone is not enough); X affinoid for this node (qcqs X by gluing on finite covers).
No discreteness of K is needed for the construction; it is needed for noetherianity, flatness, Loc and Kiehl.
proofSteps: Functoriality of ⊗̂ in bounded maps of the Banach variable (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/mixed-completed-tensor, Huber.mixedTensor.map) gives a presheaf of Banach K-algebras on rational subsets. K acts through the bounded maps λ·: O_X(U) -> O_X(U).
Independence of the chosen open bounded subring: AdicSpacesPartII:R5/mixed-completed-tensor-exactness (2).
acceptance: For R = Z_p, R = O_X.
For R = Z_p[[T]] and X the closed unit disc over K, R(X) = O_K⟨Y⟩[[T]][1/p]: power series in T whose coefficients are uniformly bounded elements of K⟨Y⟩.

nodes.title: R(U) is noetherian over a discretely valued base (CHJ Lemma 6.13(1))
nodes.statement: Let K be a discretely valued complete extension of Q_p, X affinoid rigid over K and R a small Z_p-algebra. For every rational U ⊆ X, R(U) = O_X(U) ⊗̂ R is a noetherian ring.
hypotheses: K discretely valued (used for noetherianity of O_K⟨X⟩[[T]]); K ⊇ Q_p.
proofSteps: Choose a presentation K⟨X_1, ..., X_m⟩ ->> O_X(U) and let L ⊆ O_X(U) be the image of O_K⟨X⟩. L is an open bounded subring, open by the open mapping theorem (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isOpenMap). So R(U) = (L ⊗̂ R)[1/p] by lattice independence (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/mixed-completed-tensor-exactness).

Choose Z_p[[T_1, ..., T_n]] ->> R. The induced map O_K⟨X⟩ ⊗̂ Z_p[[T]] -> L ⊗̂ R is surjective. At finite level, L ⊗ Z_p[[T]]/m^k -> L ⊗ R/m^kR is surjective and its kernels form a system with surjective transition maps, so the inverse limit stays surjective. The map O_K⟨X⟩^ -> L^ is surjective, applied coordinatewise via a pseudobasis.

O_K⟨X⟩ ⊗̂ Z_p[[T]] = O_K⟨X⟩[[T]] (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/mixed-completed-tensor-product-formula). This ring is noetherian: O_K⟨X⟩ is noetherian by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/restricted-power-series-adic (ii), and power series in finitely many variables over a noetherian ring are noetherian (mathlib:MvPowerSeries.isNoetherianRing). Hence the quotient L ⊗̂ R and its localisation R(U) are noetherian (mathlib:isNoetherianRing_of_surjective, mathlib:IsLocalization.isNoetherianRing).
acceptance: For X the disc and R = Z_p[[T]], R(X) = O_K⟨Y⟩[[T]][1/p] is noetherian.
For K = C_p the ring O_{C_p}[[T]][1/p] is not known to be covered by this argument: the hypothesis is used.

nodes.title: Rational restriction maps of R are flat (CHJ Lemma 6.13(2))
nodes.statement: Let K be a discretely valued complete extension of Q_p, X affinoid rigid over K, R small. For rational V ⊆ U ⊆ X, the restriction R(U) -> R(V) is flat.
hypotheses: K discretely valued, K ⊇ Q_p. No reducedness is needed once presentation lattices are used.
proofSteps: Write V = {|f_1|, ..., |f_n| ≤ |g| ≠ 0} in U with f_1, ..., f_n generating the unit ideal, and factor R(U) -> R(U)[1/g] = O_X(U)[1/g] ⊗_{O_X(U)} R(U) -> R(V). The first map is a localisation, hence flat.

Let L_U be the presentation lattice of AdicSpacesPartII:R5/coefficient-sheaf-noetherian, S := L_U ⊗̂ R (noetherian) and B := S[f/g], the image of S[Z]/(gZ - f) in R(U)[1/g]. B is a finitely generated S-algebra, hence noetherian, and B[1/p] = R(U)[1/g].

The (p, a)-adic completion of B (a an ideal of definition of R) is L_V ⊗̂ R, where L_V is the p-adic completion of L_U[f/g], an open bounded subring of O_X(V) (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/mixed-completed-tensor-product-formula). So after inverting p it is R(V), by lattice independence (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/mixed-completed-tensor-exactness).
Completion of a noetherian ring is flat (mathlib:AdicCompletion.flat_of_isNoetherian), and flatness survives inverting p; so R(U)[1/g] -> R(V) is flat.
acceptance: For U the disc and V = {|Y| ≤ |p|}: O_K⟨Y⟩[[T]][1/p] -> O_K⟨Y/p⟩[[T]][1/p] is flat.
Rational localisations of perfectoid algebras are not flat in general (Kedlaya-Liu Remark 2.7.1); flatness here uses noetherianity.

nodes.title: Finite rational covers give faithfully flat maps (CHJ Lemma 6.13(3))
nodes.statement: Let K be a discretely valued complete extension of Q_p, X affinoid rigid over K, R small, U ⊆ X rational and (U_i) a finite rational cover of U. Then R(U) -> ∏_i R(U_i) is faithfully flat.
hypotheses: K discretely valued, K ⊇ Q_p (for flatness of restrictions).
proofSteps: Flatness: each R(U) -> R(U_i) is flat (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/coefficient-sheaf-flat-restriction), and finite products of flat modules are flat.

The augmented Čech complex 0 -> R(U) -> ∏ R(U_i) -> ∏ R(U_i ∩ U_j) -> ... is exact (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/coefficient-sheaf-tate-acyclicity). It is bounded and all its terms are flat R(U)-modules (restriction to the rational subsets U_{i_0...i_k} is flat). So its syzygies are flat, working from the right end, and it stays exact after ⊗_{R(U)} N for any R(U)-module N.

For a maximal ideal m take N = R(U)/m ≠ 0. Injectivity of N -> ∏_i N ⊗_{R(U)} R(U_i) = ∏_i R(U_i)/m R(U_i) gives m · ∏ R(U_i) ≠ ∏ R(U_i). That is the defining condition of mathlib:Module.FaithfullyFlat.
CHJ's alternative, surjectivity on maximal spectra via Berthelot's generic fibre (de Jong §7), is not needed.
acceptance: For the Laurent cover {|Y| ≤ |p|}, {|p| ≤ |Y|} of the closed disc and R = Z_p[[T]], every maximal ideal of O_K⟨Y⟩[[T]][1/p] is the contraction of a maximal ideal of one of the two localisations.

nodes.title: Tate acyclicity for the coefficient sheaf (CHJ Proposition 6.15)
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean extension of Q_p (not necessarily discretely valued), X affinoid rigid over K and R small. For every rational U ⊆ X and every finite rational cover 𝔘 of U, the augmented Čech complex 0 -> R(U) -> ∏ R(U_i) -> ∏ R(U_i ∩ U_j) -> ... is exact. Consequently R is a sheaf on the rational site and H^i(U, R) = 0 for i ≥ 1.
hypotheses: X affinoid, K ⊇ Q_p. The unit balls are open bounded lattices compatible with the restriction maps on the finite Čech nerve: for reduced X, O_X°(U); in general, lattices chosen inductively on the nerve (see packet E28).
The étale-site analogue (CHJ Remark 6.17) is NOT part of this node: it needs Tate acyclicity of O_{X_ét} on affinoid étale objects (Huber 1996 / KL Theorem 8.2.22(c)), which no packet node supplies.
proofSteps: Choose a pseudobasis (e_i)_{i∈I} of R and open bounded lattices L(W) ⊆ O_X(W) for W in the Čech nerve of 𝔘, with restrictions mapping L(W) into L(W'). Then C^•_aug(𝔘, R) ≅ (∏_I C^•_aug(𝔘, L))[1/p] (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/mixed-completed-tensor-product-formula).

Tate acyclicity for O_X with strict differentials (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-acyclicity-finite-modules with M = A; strictness also from tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isStrictMap_of_isClosed_range) shows that the cohomology of C^•_aug(𝔘, L) is killed by a fixed power p^N.
Products are exact, so the cohomology of ∏_I C^•_aug is killed by p^N, and inverting p gives exactness.

Čech to derived (Cartan's criterion, requested from DiamondsAndVStacks:D0, Stacks 01EW): rational subsets form a basis closed under finite intersections, so vanishing Čech cohomology on all finite rational covers gives H^i = 0.
acceptance: For X the closed disc, R = Z_p[[T]] and the Laurent cover {|Y| ≤ |p|}, {|p| ≤ |Y|}: 0 -> O_K⟨Y⟩[[T]][1/p] -> O_K⟨Y/p⟩[[T]][1/p] × O_K⟨Y, p/Y⟩[[T]][1/p] -> O_K⟨Y/p, p/Y⟩[[T]][1/p] -> 0 is exact.
For R = Z_p this is Tate's theorem.

nodes.title: Local equalizers for the integral and rational coefficient sheaves
nodes.statement: Let X be a reduced affinoid rigid space over a complete nonarchimedean extension K of Q_p, M a profinite flat Z_p-module (e.g. a small Z_p-algebra R), U ⊆ X rational and (U_i) a finite rational cover of U. Then 0 -> O_X⁺(U) ⊗̂ M -> ∏_i O_X⁺(U_i) ⊗̂ M ⇉ ∏_{i,j} O_X⁺(U_i ∩ U_j) ⊗̂ M and 0 -> O_X(U) ⊗̂ M -> ∏_i O_X(U_i) ⊗̂ M ⇉ ∏_{i,j} O_X(U_i ∩ U_j) ⊗̂ M are equalizer diagrams. The integral equalizer holds on the nose; the higher integral Čech cohomology is only bounded p-torsion.

Rational: localise the integral equalizer at p (finite products commute with localisation) and identify (O⁺(V) ⊗̂ M)[1/p] = O(V) ⊗̂ M (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/rational-integral-compatibility); alternatively degree 0 of AdicSpacesPartII:R5/coefficient-sheaf-tate-acyclicity.

nodes.title: The localisation functor Loc for R-modules (CHJ Definition 6.14, Proposition 6.16)
nodes.statement: Let X be affinoid rigid over a complete nonarchimedean extension K of Q_p, R small, U ⊆ X rational and M a finitely generated R(U)-module. Loc(M) is the presheaf of R|_U-modules V ↦ R(V) ⊗_{R(U)} M on rational V ⊆ U. If K is discretely valued: Loc is a fully faithful exact functor from finitely generated R(U)-modules to R-modules on U, Loc(M) is a sheaf, and Ȟ^i(𝔘, Loc(M)) = 0 = H^i(U, Loc(M)) for i ≥ 1 and every finite rational cover 𝔘. If K is not discretely valued, Loc(M) is still a sheaf with vanishing higher cohomology when M is finitely generated projective.
hypotheses: Finitely generated modules; discreteness of K for general M.
proofSteps: Sheaf and acyclicity: tensor the exact augmented Čech complex of R (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/coefficient-sheaf-tate-acyclicity) with M; for projective M this preserves exactness; for general M all terms are flat R(U)-modules by AdicSpacesPartII:R5/coefficient-sheaf-flat-restriction (K discretely valued).
Fully faithful: Loc(M) is generated by global sections.
Exact: kernels, images and cokernels of Loc(f) are Loc of those of f, by flatness of restriction.

nodes.title: Coherent R-modules (CHJ Definition 6.18)
nodes.statement: Let K be a discretely valued complete extension of Q_p, X affinoid rigid over K, R small. For a rational U ⊆ X and a finite rational cover 𝔘 of U, a sheaf F of R|_U-modules is 𝔘-coherent if for every U_i ∈ 𝔘 there is a finitely generated R(U_i)-module M_i with F|_{U_i} ≅ Loc(M_i). F is coherent if it is 𝔘-coherent for some finite rational cover 𝔘. F is locally projective if the M_i can be chosen projective.

proofSteps: Define by existence of a trivialising cover; coherent modules form an abelian subcategory closed under kernels and cokernels (exactness of Loc, AdicSpacesPartII:R5/coefficient-sheaf-loc).

nodes.title: Density of restriction for Laurent covers (CHJ Lemma 6.19)
nodes.statement: Let X be affinoid rigid over a complete nonarchimedean extension K of Q_p, f ∈ O_X(X), X(f) = {|f| ≤ 1}, X(1/f) = {|f| ≥ 1}, X(f, 1/f) their intersection. (1) The restriction s: O_X(X(1/f)) -> O_X(X(f, 1/f)) has dense image. (2) If R is a small Z_p-algebra that is finite free as a Z_p-module (finite pseudobasis), R(X(1/f)) -> R(X(f, 1/f)) has dense image for the Banach structure of the target. For every small R the image is dense for the coordinatewise topology on bounded I-families (after choosing a pseudobasis). (3) For R with an infinite pseudobasis (2) fails in general, so CHJ Lemma 6.19(2) is false. Example: K = Q_p, X = Spa Q_p⟨x⟩, f = x/p, R = Z_p[[T]]; the element Σ_n p^{-n} x^n T^n of R(X(f,1/f)) has norm 1 and distance 1 from the image of R(X(1/f)).
hypotheses: No discreteness of K needed; K ⊇ Q_p.
proofSteps: (1) The map is the completion of the identity of O_X(X)[1/f] for the group topology generated by ϖ^n O_X°(X)[1/f] on the source and by ϖ^n O_X°(X)[f, 1/f] on the target (anchor Layer 3 rational localisation).

(2) For R ≅ Z_p^n, R(U) ≅ O_X(U)^n as Banach spaces (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/mixed-completed-tensor-product-formula with finite I), so density is (1) coordinatewise. Coordinatewise density for general I is (1) applied to each coordinate.

(3) On the annulus the Gauss norm on |x| = 1 bounds every Laurent coefficient by the sup norm, so bounded families in R(X(1/f)) have uniformly bounded x^n-coefficients, while the target element needs x^n-coefficient p^{-n} in its n-th entry.
acceptance: CHJ note that Ardakov-Wadsley §5.3 asserts density for the other restriction map s_1; the correct classical statement is for s_2, as CHJ record.
For R = Z_p[[T]] the element Σ p^{-n}x^nT^n of the example lies in the image of R(X(f)) (the small disc), not in the closure of the image of R(X(1/f)).

nodes.title: Kiehl's theorem for coherent R-modules (CHJ Theorem 6.20)
nodes.statement: Let K be a discretely valued complete extension of Q_p, X affinoid rigid over K, R small, and F a coherent R-module on X (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/coefficient-sheaf-coherent-module). Claim (CHJ Theorem 6.20): there is a finitely generated R(X)-module M with F ≅ Loc(M), namely M = F(X); if F is locally projective, M is projective. Status. (a) Proved when R is finite free as a Z_p-module. (b) The projectivity clause holds whenever F ≅ Loc(M). (c) The existence of M for R with an infinite pseudobasis (e.g. R = Z_p[[T]]) is currently unproven: CHJ's proof uses the false density Lemma 6.19(2).
hypotheses: K discretely valued, K ⊇ Q_p; F coherent for some finite rational cover.

CHJ's proof follows Ardakov-Wadsley §§5.3-5.5 (not read here; gap) and needs Banach-dense restriction on Laurent covers, which fails for infinite pseudobases (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/coefficient-sheaf-dense-restriction (3)). A new argument is needed for (c).
proofSteps: (a) R finite free over Z_p: R(U) = O_X(U) ⊗_{Z_p} R is a finite free O_X(U)-module and Loc_R(M)(V) = O_X(V) ⊗_{O_X(U)} M. So a coherent R-module is a coherent O_X-module, classical Kiehl (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid) gives F = M̃ with M = F(X) finite over O_X(X), hence over R(X), and M̃ = Loc_R(M).

(c) General R (open): reduce to a Laurent cover {X(f), X(1/f)} by the standard refinement (anchor Layer 2, Lemma 7.54 and Laurent refinement). Ardakov-Wadsley Lemma 5.3 (Banach structure plus Tate acyclicity, AdicSpacesPartII:R5/coefficient-sheaf-tate-acyclicity) survives, but their Theorem 5.4 needs density of R(X(1/f)) in R(X(f,1/f)), which fails; gap.

(b) Projectivity: R(X) -> ∏_{U∈𝔘} R(U) is faithfully flat (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/coefficient-sheaf-faithfully-flat-cover). If F ≅ Loc(M) with each R(U) ⊗ M projective, then ∏R(U) ⊗ M is flat, so M is flat (mathlib:Module.Flat.of_flat_tensorProduct), and M is finitely presented (R(X) noetherian), hence projective (mathlib:Module.Flat.projective_of_finitePresentation).
acceptance: For R = Z_p this is Kiehl's theorem for affinoid algebras (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid).
A line bundle glued on the Laurent cover of the disc from units of R(U_12) is Loc of a projective rank-one R(X)-module.

nodes.title: Base change of coefficient sheaves to C (CHJ Lemma 6.21)
nodes.statement: Let K be a discretely valued complete extension of Q_p, C the completion of an algebraic closure of K, X affinoid rigid over K with X_C = X ×_K Spa(C, O_C) and f: X_C -> X, R small with R_C := O_{X_C} ⊗̂ R, and M a finitely generated projective R(X)-module. Put M_C := M ⊗_{R(X)} R_C(X_C), a finitely generated projective R_C(X_C)-module. Then f^{-1}(Loc(M)) ⊗_{f^{-1}R} R_C ≅ Loc(M_C) as sheaves of R_C-modules on the rational site of X_C. If R is finite free over Z_p, R_C(X_C) = R(X) ⊗̂_K C and M_C ≅ M ⊗̂_K C (M with its canonical Banach topology). For R with an infinite pseudobasis, M_C is in general neither M ⊗_K C nor M ⊗̂_K C, so CHJ Lemma 6.21 as printed is false. Example: X = Spa(Q_p, Z_p), R = Z_p[[T]], M = R(X); then M_C = O_{C_p}[[T]][1/p] ⊋ M ⊗̂_{Q_p} C_p. Arbitrary non-flat base change of the coefficient algebra is not part of this statement: for a map R -> R' of small algebras, H^0(Y, F ⊗ R') need not equal H^0(Y, F) ⊗_R R' on non-affinoid Y.
hypotheses: M projective; K discretely valued (so that Loc applies on X), K ⊇ Q_p. On X_C (C not discretely valued) Loc(M_C) is a sheaf because M_C is projective (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/coefficient-sheaf-loc).
proofSteps: M_C is finitely generated projective by base change.

f is open (CHJ), so for rational W ⊆ X_C, f^{-1}(Loc M)(W) is the colimit of R(V) ⊗_{R(X)} M over rational V ⊇ f(W). Tensoring over the colimit of the R(V) with R_C(W) gives R_C(W) ⊗_{R(X)} M = R_C(W) ⊗_{R_C(X_C)} M_C = Loc(M_C)(W). Both sides are sheaves (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/coefficient-sheaf-loc).

Finite free R: R_C(X_C) ≅ O_{X_C}(X_C)^n = (O_X(X) ⊗̂_K C)^n (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/affinoid-completed-field-extension) = R(X) ⊗̂_K C. Then pass to projective M as in AdicSpacesPartII:R5/mixed-tensor-finite-projective-base-change.
acceptance: For M = R(X): R_C(X_C) = O_{X_C}(X_C) ⊗̂ R.

Non-example: for R = Z_p[[T]], R' = R/(T) and a coherent F on a non-affinoid space with H^1(F) having T-torsion, H^0(F)/T -> H^0(F/T) is not surjective (the Tor term of PerfectoidSpaces:P9/derived-coefficient-change); only flat or affinoid base change is asserted.

nodes.title: Tate algebras of polydiscs of radius rho are affinoid, and shrinking the radius is injective with dense image
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K), and let Γ* = √|K^×| ⊂ ℝ_{>0} be the divisible hull of the value group. For n ∈ ℕ and a real ρ > 0 let T_n(ρ) = K⟨ρ^{-1}X_1, …, ρ^{-1}X_n⟩ be the subring of K[[X_1, …, X_n]] of series f = Σ_ν a_ν X^ν with |a_ν| ρ^{|ν|} → 0 as |ν| = ν_1+…+ν_n → ∞ (Mathlib's MvPowerSeries.IsRestricted.subring at the constant tuple ρ), with the Gauss norm |f|_ρ = max_ν |a_ν| ρ^{|ν|}. Then: (a) |·|_ρ is a multiplicative K-algebra norm for which T_n(ρ) is complete; (b) if ρ ∈ Γ*, T_n(ρ) with the |·|_ρ-topology is a K-affinoid algebra, i.e. the structure map K → T_n(ρ) is strictly topologically of finite type (an open continuous surjection from some Tate algebra K⟨Y_1, …, Y_N⟩ onto T_n(ρ) compatible with the K-algebra structures), hence T_n(ρ) is noetherian; (c) for real ρ' ≥ ρ > 0 the inclusion T_n(ρ') ⊆ T_n(ρ) is a continuous injective K-algebra map with |f|_ρ ≤ |f|_{ρ'} and dense image (polynomials are dense in every T_n(ρ)).
hypotheses: K complete, nontrivially and nonarchimedeanly valued (rank one)
n ∈ ℕ
ρ > 0 real; in (b) ρ ∈ Γ* = √|K^×|
in (c) ρ' ≥ ρ
proofSteps: (a) Ultrametric inequality for the coefficients gives |f+g|_ρ ≤ max(|f|_ρ,|g|_ρ) and |fg|_ρ ≤ |f|_ρ|g|_ρ (Mathlib MvPowerSeries.isRestricted.mul supplies closure under products); equality |fg|_ρ = |f|_ρ|g|_ρ is Gauss's lemma for the weight ρ^{|ν|}: compare the lexicographically first indices where |a_ν|ρ^{|ν|} and |b_μ|ρ^{|μ|} attain their maxima. Completeness: a |·|_ρ-Cauchy sequence converges coefficientwise and the limit is ρ-restricted by the uniform bound.

(b) Choose c ∈ K^× and s ≥ 1 with ρ^s = |c|^{-1} (possible because ρ ∈ Γ*). If ρ ≥ 1, the continuous map K⟨T_{il} : 1 ≤ i ≤ n, 0 ≤ l ≤ s⟩ → T_n(ρ), T_{il} ↦ c X_i^l, is well defined because |c X_i^l|_ρ = |c|ρ^l ≤ 1, and surjective: write ν_i = s q_i + l_i with 0 ≤ l_i < s, so X^ν = c^{-|q|-n} Π_i (cX_i^s)^{q_i}(cX_i^{l_i}) and the new coefficient a_ν c^{-|q|-n} has absolute value |a_ν| ρ^{s|q|+sn} ≤ ρ^{sn}·|a_ν|ρ^{|ν|} → 0 (the argument of BGR 6.1.5/4 quoted in the proof of Grosse-Klönne Lemma 1.8). If ρ < 1, use instead K⟨Y_i, Z_i⟩ → T_n(ρ), Y_i ↦ c X_i^s, Z_i ↦ X_i (|cX_i^s|_ρ = 1, |X_i|_ρ = ρ ≤ 1); surjectivity follows from |a_ν| ρ^{s|q|} ≤ ρ^{-sn}|a_ν|ρ^{|ν|}. The map is continuous and surjective, so it is open by the open mapping theorem, which the baseline already packages over a Tate ring as tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isStrictlyTopologicallyFiniteType_of_surjective (π : K⟨Y⟩ →ₐ[K] B continuous at 0 and surjective onto a complete Hausdorff first-countable B ⇒ IsStrictlyTopologicallyFiniteType (algebraMap K B)); its [IsTateRing K] instance for a nontrivially normed ultrametric complete field is not in the pinned baseline (only ℚ_p has one) and comes from the anchor Layer 0. Hence K → T_n(ρ) is strictly topologically of finite type (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsStrictlyTopologicallyFiniteType, presented through tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion identified with the plain restricted-series ring by tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletionEquiv).

nodes.title: The Monsky–Washnitzer algebra W_n = K⟨X_1, …, X_n⟩† of overconvergent power series
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K). For n ∈ ℕ define W_n = K⟨X_1, …, X_n⟩† := ⋃_{ρ>1} T_n(ρ) ⊆ K[[X_1, …, X_n]], the set of power series Σ_ν a_ν X^ν for which there is a real ρ > 1 with |a_ν| ρ^{|ν|} → 0 (equivalently: there are ρ > 1 and C ≥ 0 with |a_ν| ≤ C ρ^{-|ν|} for all ν; equivalently there is ρ ∈ Γ*, ρ > 1, such that the series converges at every point x of K_a^n (K_a an algebraic closure) with max_i |x_i| ≤ ρ; convergence only at the K-rational points of such a polydisc does not suffice when K is discretely valued and ρ < |π|^{-1}, since those points already lie in the unit polydisc). Because ρ ↦ T_n(ρ) is antitone, the union is directed and W_n is a K-subalgebra of K[[X]]; the union may be taken over ρ ∈ Γ* ∩ (1, ∞) (Γ* = √|K^×|) but NOT only over ρ ∈ |K^×|. W_n ⊆ T_n = T_n(1), and W_n carries the Gauss norm |f| = max_ν |a_ν| restricted from T_n. Convention: the variables are X_1, …, X_n, |ν| = ν_1+…+ν_n, and ‘overconvergent’ always means ‘restricted at some radius strictly bigger than 1’.
hypotheses: K complete, nontrivially and nonarchimedeanly valued (rank one)
n ∈ ℕ
proofSteps: Define W_n as the supremum ⨆_{ρ>1} T_n(ρ) of the Mathlib subrings MvPowerSeries.IsRestricted.subring (fun _ ↦ ρ); the family is directed (ρ ≤ ρ' ⇒ T_n(ρ') ≤ T_n(ρ), F1/radius-tate-algebra-affinoid (c)), so membership is ∃ρ>1, restricted at ρ (Mathlib Subring.mem_iSup_of_directed).
Equivalence with the bound |a_ν| ≤ Cρ^{-|ν|}: restricted at ρ implies bounded by C = sup_ν |a_ν|ρ^{|ν|}; bounded at ρ implies restricted at every ρ' ∈ (1, ρ).
Cofinality of Γ* ∩ (1,∞): Γ* is dense in ℝ_{>0} because |K^×| ≠ {1}; for a discretely valued K the radii in |K^×| ∩ (1,∞) are bounded below by |π|^{-1} > 1, which is why they do not suffice.
Algebra structure: constants and the X_i are restricted at every ρ (Mathlib isRestricted_C, isRestricted_monomial).
acceptance: The series Σ_{m≥0} p^m X^{p^m} over K = ℚ_p lies in T_1 but not in W_1.
Σ_{m≥0} p^m X^{2m} over ℚ_p lies in W_1 (restricted at every ρ < p^{1/2}) although it is not restricted at any ρ ∈ |ℚ_p^×| ∩ (1,∞).

nodes.title: Weierstrass division and preparation in W_n, and distinguishedness after an automorphism
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K) and n ≥ 1; write W_n = K⟨Y_1, …, Y_n⟩† and regard g ∈ W_n as g = Σ_{m≥0} g_m Y_n^m with g_m ∈ W_{n-1}. Call g Y_n-distinguished of degree s if g_s is a unit of W_{n-1} and |g| = |g_s| > |g_m| for all m > s (Gauss norms), and call ω ∈ W_{n-1}[Y_n] a Weierstrass polynomial if it is monic with |ω| = 1. Then: (i) (division) if g is Y_n-distinguished of degree s, every f ∈ W_n can be written uniquely as f = gq + r with q ∈ W_n and r ∈ W_{n-1}[Y_n] of degree < s; (ii) (preparation) such g is uniquely e·ω with e a unit of W_n and ω a Weierstrass polynomial of degree s; (iii) (distinguishedness) for every 0 ≠ f ∈ W_n there is a K-algebra automorphism σ of W_n of the form Y_i ↦ Y_i + Y_n^{c_i} (i < n), Y_n ↦ Y_n, with c_i ∈ ℕ, such that σ(f) is Y_n-distinguished.
hypotheses: K complete, nontrivially and nonarchimedeanly valued
Gauss norms on W_n and W_{n-1} (restricted from T_n, T_{n-1})
proofSteps: (iii) For 0 ≠ f ∈ T_n the Tate-algebra statement (BGR 5.2.4: some σ_c with c_i ≫ 0 makes f distinguished; anchor Layer 0.5 Weierstrass theory) gives c; σ_c and its inverse Y_i ↦ Y_i − Y_n^{c_i} map T_n(ρ_0) into T_n(ρ) whenever ρ^{max c_i} ≤ ρ_0, hence preserve W_n; the Gauss norms at radius 1 are those of T_n, and the leading coefficient σ_c(f)_s ∈ W_{n-1} is a unit of T_{n-1}, hence of W_{n-1} (Dagger.isUnit_washnitzerAlgebra_iff, F1/overconvergent-tate-algebra), so σ_c(f) is distinguished in W_n.

(i) existence: g ∈ T_n(ρ_0) for some ρ_0 > 1. Choose N_0 ∈ ℕ such that every coefficient a_ν of g with |ν| ≥ N_0 satisfies |a_ν|ρ_0^{|ν|/2} ≤ |g_s| (possible since |a_ν|ρ_0^{|ν|} → 0), so that |g_m|_ρ ≤ |g_s|ρ^{N_0} for all m and all 1 < ρ ≤ ρ_0^{1/2}, and choose M ≥ N_0; for ρ ∈ Γ* with ρ > 1 close enough to 1 (with ρ^{M+N_0} < ρ_0), g is distinguished of degree s for the Gauss norm of polyradius (ρ, …, ρ, ρ^M): the terms m < s are dominated because ρ^{M(s−m)} ≥ ρ^{N_0} ≥ |g_m|_ρ/|g_s|_ρ, the terms m > s because |g_m| ≤ θ|g_s| (θ < 1) at radius 1 and |g_m|_{ρ_0}ρ_0^m → 0.

Since ρ ∈ Γ*, choose a finite (hence complete) extension K'/K with the polyradius in |K'^×|; then T_n(ρ,…,ρ,ρ^M) ⊗_K K' ≅ K'⟨Y_1..Y_n⟩ by rescaling the variables, where Weierstrass division by a distinguished element holds (anchor Layer 0.5, over the complete field K'). Divide f ⊗ 1 by g ⊗ 1 there, expand quotient and remainder in a K-basis e_1 = 1, e_2, …, e_d of K' (T_n(ρ)⊗_K K' = ⊕ T_n(ρ)e_j), and keep the e_1-components: this gives f = gq + r with q ∈ T_n(ρ,…,ρ^M) ⊆ W_n and r ∈ T_{n-1}(ρ)[Y_n] of degree < s.
(i) uniqueness: W_n ⊆ T_n, g is distinguished in T_n, and division in T_n is unique (anchor Layer 0.5).

(ii) from (i) as in BGR 5.2.2: divide Y_n^s by g, Y_n^s = gq + r, put ω = Y_n^s − r and e = q^{-1}; |ω| = 1 and q is a unit because it is a unit in T_n and units of T_n lying in W_n are units of W_n (Dagger.isUnit_washnitzerAlgebra_iff, F1/overconvergent-tate-algebra).
acceptance: n = 1: g = π + Y_1 ∈ K⟨Y_1⟩† (π a pseudo-uniformiser) is Y_1-distinguished of degree 1 and division by g is evaluation at Y_1 = −π: f = gq + f(−π).

g = Y_1Y_2 ∈ K⟨Y_1, Y_2⟩† is not Y_2-distinguished of any degree (its only Y_2-coefficient g_1 = Y_1 is not a unit of W_1), but σ(Y_1) = Y_1 + Y_2^c turns it into Y_1Y_2 + Y_2^{c+1}, which is Y_2-distinguished of degree c+1 (g_{c+1} = 1, |g| = 1, no higher terms), as (iii) predicts. (By contrast Y_1 + Y_2^2 is already Y_2-distinguished of degree 2.)

nodes.title: W_n is a noetherian factorial Jacobson ring and every ideal of W_n is strictly closed
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K) and n ∈ ℕ. Then (1) W_n is noetherian, a unique factorisation domain, and a Jacobson ring, and W_n/m is a finite field extension of K for every maximal ideal m; (2) every ideal I ⊆ W_n is strictly closed for the Gauss norm: I is closed and for every f ∈ W_n the residue norm inf_{g∈I} |f − g| is attained. Consequently the residue seminorm on W_n/I is a norm.
hypotheses: K complete, nontrivially and nonarchimedeanly valued
n ∈ ℕ
proofSteps: Noetherian (BGR 5.2.6/1 pattern): induction on n; for 0 ≠ f ∈ W_n use F1/overconvergent-weierstrass-division (iii) to make f Y_n-distinguished, then (i) shows W_n/(f) is a finite W_{n-1}-module; W_{n-1} noetherian by induction, so every ideal containing f is finitely generated. (Kedlaya attributes noetherianity to Fulton.)

Factorial (BGR 5.2.6/2 pattern): by Weierstrass preparation every nonzero f is, after an automorphism, a unit times a Weierstrass polynomial in W_{n-1}[Y_n]; factoriality of W_{n-1} (induction) and Gauss's lemma for W_{n-1}[Y_n] give unique factorisation.

Residue fields and Jacobson (BGR 5.2.6/3 and 6.1.2 pattern): for a maximal ideal m, Noether normalisation for the quotient W_n/m — induction on n using only F1/overconvergent-weierstrass-division (iii) + (ii) and the finiteness statement 'a finite W_n-algebra killed by a Weierstrass polynomial ω ∈ W_{n-1}[Y_n] is finite over W_{n-1}' (division by ω) — gives a finite injective W_d → W_n/m; W_n/m is a field integral over W_d, so W_d is a field, which forces d = 0 (Y_1 is not a unit of W_d for d ≥ 1); hence W_n/m is finite over K. Jacobson: for a prime p the same normalisation gives a finite injective W_d → W_n/p; the Jacobson radical of W_d is 0 (every point x of the closed unit polydisc over K_a defines a maximal ideal ker(f ↦ f(x)) of W_d, so an element of the Jacobson radical vanishes on the whole unit polydisc over K_a and has Gauss norm |f| = sup_x |f(x)| = 0 by the maximum modulus principle for T_d, an anchor Layer 0 input), and integrality with going-up transports this to W_n/p. This argument deliberately does not cite F1/dagger-noether-normalisation or F1/overconvergent-faithful-flatness, both of which list the present node as a prerequisite.

Strictly closed (BGR 5.2.7 pattern, induction on n): for I = (f_1..f_r) and f ∈ W_n, after the Weierstrass reductions of F1/overconvergent-weierstrass-division every f has a division remainder of minimal residue norm, so the distance from f to I is attained; closedness and the fact that the residue seminorm on W_n/I is a norm follow. (The route through F1/overconvergent-faithful-flatness, I = IT_n ∩ W_n, is not available here: that node lists the present one as a prerequisite, and Grosse-Klönne's proof of Proposition 1.5 uses 1.4.)

nodes.title: W_n → T_n is faithfully flat, bijective on maximal ideals with equal residue fields, and W_n is regular of dimension n
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K) and n ∈ ℕ. Then (a) the inclusion W_n ⊆ T_n is faithfully flat; (b) for every maximal ideal m of T_n, m ∩ W_n is a maximal ideal of W_n and W_n/(m ∩ W_n) → T_n/m is bijective; m ↦ m ∩ W_n is a bijection Max(T_n) → Max(W_n); (c) every maximal ideal of W_n is generated by polynomials p_1, …, p_n ∈ K[Y_1..Y_n] with p_i monic in Y_i; (d) W_n is a regular ring (Mathlib IsRegularRing), equidimensional of Krull dimension n, and the maps of completed local rings (W_n)^_{m∩W_n} → (T_n)^_m are isomorphisms.
hypotheses: K complete, nontrivially and nonarchimedeanly valued
n ∈ ℕ
proofSteps: Points: as sets Max(T_n) = ⋂_{ρ>1} Max(T_n(ρ)) = lim_ρ Max(T_n(ρ)) (a maximal ideal of T_n is the ideal of a Galois orbit of points of the closed unit polydisc, which lies in every polydisc of radius ρ > 1), and Spec W_n = lim_ρ Spec T_n(ρ) as topological spaces because W_n = colim_ρ T_n(ρ) (EGA IV 8.2.9, a limit statement for affine schemes); maximal ideals of W_n therefore come from compatible systems of maximal ideals of the T_n(ρ) (the contraction of a maximal ideal m of W_n to T_n(ρ) is maximal because T_n(ρ)/(m ∩ T_n(ρ)) ⊆ W_n/m is a domain finite over K, using 'W_n/m is finite over K' from F1/overconvergent-tate-algebra-properties — this is GK's '(use 1.4)'), so Max(T_n) → Max(W_n) is surjective, and injective because a maximal ideal of T_n is generated by polynomials (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/tate-algebra-maximal-ideals-polynomial), so m = (m ∩ K[Y])T_n is determined by m ∩ W_n.

Residue fields: W_n/(m ∩ W_n) → T_n/m is injective and both are finite over K; surjectivity because the point x ∈ K^a of the closed unit polydisc has T_n/m = K(x) = W_n/(m ∩ W_n) (polynomials already surject onto K(x)).

(c) from the corresponding statement for T_n (BGR 7.1.1/3: maximal ideals of T_n are generated by polynomials monic in successive variables), since those polynomials lie in W_n and generate a maximal ideal of W_n by (b).

(d) completed local rings: the map (W_n)^ → (T_n)^ at corresponding maximal ideals is surjective because the associated graded rings agree (m^k/m^{k+1} is a finite K-space generated by polynomials in both), and injective for dimension reasons (both regular local of dimension n by (c)); flatness of W_n → T_n follows by checking at maximal ideals, faithful flatness from surjectivity on maximal ideals (Mathlib Module.FaithfullyFlat, maximal-ideal criterion). Regularity and dimension n follow from (c) and the isomorphic completions.
acceptance: For n = 1 and K algebraically closed, the maximal ideals of W_1 are the (Y − a) with |a| ≤ 1, exactly as for T_1; for |a| > 1, Y − a = −a(1 − Y/a) is a unit of W_1 because Σ_k (Y/a)^k converges on the disc of radius |a| > 1.
W_n is not complete, yet the completion of its local ring at the origin is K[[Y_1..Y_n]], as for T_n.

nodes.title: Dagger algebras over a complete nonarchimedean field
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K). A K-dagger algebra is a commutative K-algebra A for which there exist n ∈ ℕ and a surjective K-algebra homomorphism W_n → A (equivalently A ≅ W_n/I for an ideal I). A morphism of dagger algebras is a K-algebra homomorphism (no continuity is imposed; it is automatic, F1/dagger-norm-and-continuity). Sp(A) denotes the set of maximal ideals of A. Attached data, each independent of the presentation up to canonical isomorphism: the residue norm class of a presentation (F1/dagger-norm-and-continuity), the completion A → Â (written A' by Grosse-Klönne), Â = T_n/IT_n, a K-affinoid algebra (F1/dagger-completion-comparison), the supremum seminorm |a|_sup = max_{m ∈ Sp(A)} |a mod m|, and the integral subring A^int = {a ∈ A : |a|_sup ≤ 1} = A ∩ (Â)°, which is the ring of power-bounded elements of A.
hypotheses: K complete, nontrivially and nonarchimedeanly valued (rank one)
proofSteps: Definition as a predicate on K-algebras: Dagger.IsDaggerAlgebra K A :⇔ ∃ n, ∃ φ : W_n →ₐ[K] A surjective (W_n = F1/overconvergent-tate-algebra).
Sp(A) is Mathlib's MaximalSpectrum A; residue fields A/m are finite over K by F1/dagger-noether-normalisation.
The supremum seminorm is finite because it is bounded by any residue norm (|a mod m| ≤ |a| for the residue norm, BGR 6.2.1 applied to Â via F1/dagger-completion-comparison).
A^int = A ∩ (Â)°: an element of an affinoid algebra is power-bounded iff |·|_sup ≤ 1 (BGR 6.2.3/1), and |a|_sup is computed on Sp(A) = Sp(Â) (F1/dagger-completion-comparison).

nodes.title: Noether normalisation for dagger algebras and finiteness of residue fields
nodes.statement: Let A be a K-dagger algebra (K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K)). Then (a) there are d ∈ ℕ and an injective finite K-algebra homomorphism W_d → A; (b) if the nilradical of an ideal q ⊆ A is a maximal ideal, then A/q is finite-dimensional over K; in particular A/m is a finite field extension of K for every maximal ideal m; (c) if φ : W_n → B is a finite morphism of dagger algebras and the kernel of φ contains a Weierstrass polynomial ω ∈ W_{n-1}[Y_n], then W_{n-1} → B is finite.
hypotheses: A a K-dagger algebra
K complete, nontrivially and nonarchimedeanly valued
proofSteps: (c) By F1/overconvergent-weierstrass-division (i), W_n/(ω) is a free W_{n-1}-module with basis 1, Y_n, …, Y_n^{s−1}; B is finite over W_n/(ω), hence over W_{n-1}.

(a) Induction on n for A = W_n/I: if I = 0 take d = n. Otherwise pick 0 ≠ f ∈ I; by F1/overconvergent-weierstrass-division (iii) and (ii) after an automorphism f = eω with ω a Weierstrass polynomial, so W_{n-1} → A is finite by (c); apply induction to the image of W_{n-1} (a quotient of W_{n-1}) and compose finite maps (BGR 6.1.2/2 pattern).

(b) Apply (a) to A/q: its only prime is the maximal ideal, so A/q is zero-dimensional; a finite injective W_d → A/q forces d = 0 (W_d has dimension d by F1/overconvergent-faithful-flatness and finite injective maps preserve dimension), so A/q is finite over W_0 = K.

nodes.title: Residue norms on dagger algebras and automatic continuity of morphisms
nodes.statement: Let A = W_n/I be a K-dagger algebra with a presentation (K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K)). (1) The residue seminorm |a| = inf{|f| : f ∈ W_n, f ↦ a} (Gauss norm on W_n) is a K-algebra norm on A, and the induced map α : W_n/I → T_n/IT_n is the completion of (A, |·|): an isometric embedding with dense image. (2) Every K-algebra homomorphism φ : W_n/I → W_m/J between dagger algebras is continuous for the residue norms. Consequently the residue norms of any two presentations of A are equivalent, every dagger algebra carries a canonical equivalence class of norms (its ‘affinoid topology’), and every finite A-module M carries a canonical topology, the one induced from the finite Â-module M ⊗_A Â, for which all A-linear maps of finite modules are continuous.
hypotheses: A = W_n/I, B = W_m/J K-dagger algebras
φ a K-algebra homomorphism (no continuity assumed)
proofSteps: (1) I is closed (F1/overconvergent-tate-algebra-properties (2)), so the residue seminorm is a norm; W_n → T_n is an isometry with dense image (F1/overconvergent-tate-algebra), and IT_n ∩ W_n = I (faithful flatness, F1/overconvergent-faithful-flatness), so W_n/I → T_n/IT_n is isometric with dense image into a complete space.

(2) Reduce to A = W_n. Each φ(X_i) has |φ(X_i)|_sup ≤ 1 in B: for every maximal ideal m of B and ν ≥ 1, ψ : W_n → B → B/m^ν factors through W_n/ker ψ ↪ B/m^ν, which is finite-dimensional (F1/dagger-noether-normalisation (b)) and normed by the residue norm (ker ψ is closed, F1/overconvergent-tate-algebra-properties (2)); a linear map out of a finite-dimensional normed space over the complete field K is continuous (mathlib:LinearMap.continuous_of_finiteDimensional, BGR 2.3.3), so ψ is continuous, giving φ(g(X)) ≡ g(φ(X)) mod m^ν; if |φ(X_i) mod m| = δ > 1 then g(φ(X_i) mod m) diverges for g ∈ W_n ∖ T_n(δ), a contradiction. Hence the φ(X_i) are power-bounded in T_m/JT_m (BGR 6.2.3/1 via the Max bijection of F1/overconvergent-faithful-flatness).

Define φ' : T_n → T_m/JT_m continuous by X_i ↦ φ(X_i) (universal property of the Tate algebra for power-bounded images, anchor Layer 0.4, Wedhorn 5.50); φ and φ' agree modulo every m^ν on W_n by the congruence above, and ⋂_{m,ν} m^ν = 0 in the affinoid algebra T_m/JT_m (Krull), so φ = φ'|_{W_n} is continuous.

Finite modules: M ⊗_A Â is a finite module over the affinoid algebra Â with its canonical Banach topology (BGR 3.7.3); restrict to M ⊆ M ⊗_A Â (injective because A → Â = A ⊗_{W_n} T_n is the base change of the faithfully flat W_n → T_n, F1/overconvergent-faithful-flatness (a); F1/dagger-completion-comparison cannot be cited here, since it lists the present node as a prerequisite) and use continuity of Â-linear maps of finite modules.
acceptance: The K-algebra automorphism X ↦ X + π of W_1 is continuous and an isometry; the residue norm of W_1/(X) is the absolute value of K.

nodes.title: A dagger algebra and its completion: faithful flatness, points, completed local rings, reducedness and regularity, supremum norm
nodes.statement: Let A be a K-dagger algebra with completion τ : A → Â (K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K)). Then: (1) τ is faithfully flat and m ↦ τ^{-1}(m) is a bijection Max(Â) → Max(A) with isomorphic residue fields; (2) for corresponding maximal ideals τ induces isomorphisms of completed local rings A^_{τ^{-1}m} ≅ Â^_m; (3) A is reduced (resp. normal, resp. regular) if and only if Â is; (4) if A is reduced, the supremum seminorm |·|_sup on A is a norm lying in the canonical norm class of F1/dagger-norm-and-continuity. Moreover the completion is functorial: every morphism φ : A → B of dagger algebras extends uniquely to a continuous K-algebra map φ̂ : Â → B̂, and φ ↦ φ̂ is a functor.
hypotheses: A a K-dagger algebra
K complete, nontrivially and nonarchimedeanly valued
proofSteps: Write A = W_n/I; then Â = T_n/IT_n by F1/dagger-norm-and-continuity (1). (1): base change of the faithfully flat W_n → T_n (F1/overconvergent-faithful-flatness) along W_n → A; maximal ideals of T_n containing IT_n correspond to maximal ideals of W_n containing I with equal residue fields (same node, (b)).

(2): A^_m = (W_n)^_m ⊗_{W_n} (W_n/I) = (T_n)^_{m'} ⊗_{W_n} (W_n/I) = (T_n)^_{m'} ⊗_{T_n} (T_n/IT_n) = Â^_{m'}, using the isomorphism of completed local rings of W_n and T_n (F1/overconvergent-faithful-flatness (d)).

(3): regularity: a noetherian local ring is regular iff its completion is, and regularity is checked at maximal ideals, which correspond with isomorphic completions by (1),(2) — no excellence needed. Reducedness and normality of Â descend to A along the faithfully flat τ. The converse (A reduced, resp. normal ⇒ Â reduced, resp. normal) needs that these properties pass from A_m to its completion, i.e. that the local rings of A are excellent (EGA IV 7.8.3(v)); Grosse-Klönne only says 'all rings are excellent'. This input is supplied by the proposed node F1/dagger-algebra-excellent (char K = 0 via Matsumura's criterion, as Conrad explains for Tate algebras; in characteristic p it remains open in the packet). Formalisation note: 'normal' must be read as 'every localisation at a prime is an integrally closed domain' (for noetherian rings: IsReduced ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed); Mathlib's IsIntegrallyClosed alone does not mean normal for non-reduced rings.

(4): by (1),(2) α is an isometry for the supremum seminorms (computed on Max(A) = Max(Â)); the statement for the reduced affinoid algebra Â (BGR 6.2.4/1: the supremum norm is equivalent to any residue norm) transfers to A through the isometric dense embedding.
Functoriality: φ is continuous (F1/dagger-norm-and-continuity (2)), so it extends uniquely to completions.
acceptance: A = K⟨X,Y⟩†/(Y^2 − X^3): Max(A) = Max(Â), both are reduced, and neither is normal (the cusp at the origin), as (3) predicts.

nodes.title: Dagger algebras are weakly complete; elements of A^int with reduction 1 are units
nodes.statement: Let A be a K-dagger algebra (K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K)). (a) A is weakly complete: for all power-bounded x_1, …, x_n ∈ A (equivalently x_i ∈ A^int) the K-algebra map K[X_1..X_n] → A, X_i ↦ x_i, extends uniquely to a continuous K-algebra homomorphism W_n → A; moreover for every ρ > 1 the composite T_n(ρ) → T_n → Â factors through some fringe algebra A_{ρ'} of any fringe presentation of A (F1/fringe-presentation). (b) If a ∈ A is topologically nilpotent (|a|_sup < 1) then 1 − a is a unit of A with inverse Σ_{k≥0} a^k; in particular every element of A^int whose image in A^int/{|·|_sup < 1} is 1 is a unit. (c) An element a ∈ A is a unit iff its image in Â is a unit.
hypotheses: A a K-dagger algebra
x_1..x_n ∈ A power-bounded
proofSteps: (a) Write A = W_k/I with I generated by elements of T_k(λ_0). Let ψ : T_n → T_k/IT_k = Â be the continuous map with X_i ↦ x_i (universal property of T_n for power-bounded images, anchor Layer 0.4). For λ > 1, run the argument of F1/fringe-morphism-factorisation (GK Lemma 1.8): choose c ∈ K^×, s with λ^s = |c|^{-1}, present T_n(λ) as a quotient of T_{(s+1)n} via T_{il} ↦ cX_i^l (F1/radius-tate-algebra-affinoid (b)); the images of the topologically nilpotent elements cX_i^l lift to power-bounded elements of some A_{λ''}, and the kernel relations die in some A_{λ'}; so ψ(T_n(λ)) ⊆ image of A_{λ'} ⊆ A. Taking the union over λ gives W_n → A. Uniqueness: two continuous extensions agree on polynomials, which are dense in W_n.

(b) |a|_sup < 1 implies a is topologically nilpotent in some fringe algebra (Kedlaya Corollary 2.3.5, a consequence of (a) applied to x = a^N λ with |λ| > 1); then Σ a^k converges in that affinoid fringe algebra, and its image in A inverts 1 − a.
(c) If τ(a) is a unit of Â, a lies in no maximal ideal of A because Max(A) = Max(Â) (F1/dagger-completion-comparison (1)); so a is a unit.
acceptance: For A = W_1 and the power-bounded element x = X^2 the extension W_1 → W_1 is g(X) ↦ g(X^2); for x = 1 + πX it is g ↦ g(1 + πX), which maps T_1(ρ) into T_1(ρ') whenever |π|ρ' ≤ ρ.

nodes.title: Fringe (radius-indexed) presentations of a dagger algebra
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K) and A a K-dagger algebra. A fringe presentation of A consists of n ∈ ℕ, a radius ρ_0 ∈ Γ* with ρ_0 > 1, elements f_1, …, f_r ∈ T_n(ρ_0), and a K-algebra isomorphism W_n/(f_1, …, f_r)W_n ≅ A. For ρ ∈ Γ* ∩ (1, ρ_0] put A_ρ := T_n(ρ)/(f)T_n(ρ), a K-affinoid algebra (F1/radius-tate-algebra-affinoid), with transition maps A_{ρ'} → A_ρ for ρ ≤ ρ' induced by T_n(ρ') ⊆ T_n(ρ), and put A_1 := T_n/(f)T_n. Then A = colim_{ρ → 1+} A_ρ as K-algebras, and A_1 = Â is the completion. The fringe algebra of the presentation at radius ρ is the image B_ρ ⊆ A of A_ρ (equivalently of T_n(ρ)); A_ρ → A need not be injective. Geometrically, X_ρ = Sp(A_ρ) is a decreasing family of affinoids with ⋂_ρ X_ρ = Sp(Â) and Sp(Â) ⊆ X_ρ the Weierstrass domain {|X_1|, …, |X_n| ≤ 1}; this situation is written Sp(Â) ⊂† X_ρ.
hypotheses: A a K-dagger algebra
ρ_0 ∈ Γ* with ρ_0 > 1 and f_i ∈ T_n(ρ_0)
proofSteps: Existence: A ≅ W_n/I with I finitely generated (W_n noetherian, F1/overconvergent-tate-algebra-properties); finitely many generators lie in a common T_n(ρ_0) (directedness, F1/overconvergent-tate-algebra), and ρ_0 may be shrunk into Γ*.
Colimit: W_n = colim_ρ T_n(ρ) (directed union) and colimits commute with the quotient by the ideal generated by the images of f, so colim_ρ T_n(ρ)/(f) = W_n/(f)W_n.
A_1 = Â: F1/dagger-norm-and-continuity (1).
Weierstrass domain: T_n(ρ)/(f) → T_n/(f) is the restriction to {x ∈ X_ρ : |X_i(x)| ≤ 1}, since T_n(ρ)⟨X/1⟩ = T_n (a Weierstrass localisation of T_n(ρ)).

The elements φ_λ(β_λ(p(T_{il}))) = cX_i^l ∈ A have supremum norm ≤ |c| = λ^{-s} < 1 (|X_i|_sup ≤ 1), and ψ does not increase supremum norms, so b_{il} := ψ(cX_i^l) ∈ B has |b_{il}|_sup,B̂ < 1. Lifting without weak completeness: choose a lift b̃ ∈ B_{λ_1} (B = colim B_μ) and r ∈ Γ* with |b_{il}|_sup < r < 1. The Laurent domain W = {x ∈ X_{λ_1} : |b̃(x)| ≥ r} of X_{λ_1} = Sp(B_{λ_1}) is disjoint from X_1 = Sp(B̂) = {|X_j| ≤ 1 ∀j} (maximum modulus on B̂), i.e. 1 = Σ_j (Y_j − X_j)h_j in O(W)⟨Y⟩; approximating the h_j by polynomials gives Σ_j (Y_j − X_j)h'_j = 1 − e with e a polynomial of Gauss norm < 1, hence of μ-Gauss norm < 1 for μ > 1 close to 1, so W ∩ X_μ = ∅. Thus |b̃| < r on X_{λ''} for some λ'' ∈ Γ* ∩ (1, λ_1], and the image t_{il} of b̃ in B_{λ''} has spectral norm < 1, in particular it is power-bounded, with γ_{λ''}(t_{il}) = b_{il}. (Citing Kedlaya Corollary 2.3.5 here would be circular: its proof uses weak completeness, F1/dagger-weak-completeness, which is itself proved from this lemma, and Kedlaya's Corollary 2.3.3, which is this lemma.)

The continuous map q : T_{(s+1)n} → B_{λ''}, T_{il} ↦ t_{il}, satisfies γ_{λ''} ∘ q = ψ ∘ φ_λ ∘ β_λ ∘ p, so the finitely generated ideal q(ker(β_λ ∘ p))B_{λ''} = (r_1..r_k) maps to 0 in B = colim B_μ; some λ' ∈ (1, λ''] kills all r_j in B_{λ'}, and q descends to A_λ → B_{λ'}.
Corollaries: apply to ψ = id with two presentations (cofinality) and to ψ = id with finitely many fringe algebras (common upper bound: take the minimum of the finitely many λ').

nodes.title: The fringe (direct limit) topology on dagger algebras and their finite modules
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K) and A a K-dagger algebra. The fringe topology on A is the finest locally K-convex topology for which every map A_ρ → A of a fringe presentation is continuous, A_ρ carrying its Banach topology; equivalently the direct limit of the intrinsic Banach topologies of the fringe algebras of A. It does not depend on the fringe presentation, is Hausdorff, is finer than the norm (affinoid) topology of F1/dagger-norm-and-continuity, and every K-algebra homomorphism of dagger algebras is continuous for it. A finite A-module M carries the fringe topology obtained as the quotient topology from A^r ↠ M (equivalently by base extension from a module over a fringe algebra), independent of choices; A-linear maps of finite modules are continuous. If K is spherically complete (in particular discretely valued), A with its fringe topology is a complete reflexive Hausdorff locally convex K-space.
hypotheses: A a K-dagger algebra
for completeness and reflexivity: K spherically complete
proofSteps: Define the topology via Dagger.FringePresentation.stage and the colimit (F1/fringe-presentation); independence of the presentation from F1/fringe-morphism-factorisation (mutually cofinal systems induce the same final topology).
Hausdorff and finer than the affinoid topology: each A_ρ → Â is continuous, so the final topology is finer than the one induced from Â, which is Hausdorff.
Continuity of morphisms: F1/fringe-morphism-factorisation maps each A_λ into some B_{λ'} continuously (a map of affinoid algebras is continuous).
Modules: F1/fringe-module-descent (GK 2.15) descends M to a finite A_ρ-module M_ρ; the final topology from the Banach modules M_{ρ'} (ρ' ≤ ρ) agrees with the quotient topology of A^r → M.

Completeness and reflexivity for spherically complete K: A is a compact-type (regular) inductive limit of the Banach spaces A_ρ with compact transition maps (Morita, A p-adic theory of hyperfunctions I, 3.3, 3.5, quoted by Grosse-Klönne 4.2; not read — recorded as a gap).
acceptance: For A = W_1 over ℚ_p, the truncations g_N = Σ_{m≤N} p^m X^{p^m} are Cauchy for the Gauss norm but not for the fringe topology: the K-seminorm q(f) = sup_k |a_k| p^{√k} is continuous on every stage T_1(ρ), ρ > 1 (p^{√k} ≤ C_ρ ρ^k), hence on W_1 with the fringe topology, and q(g_N − g_M) = max_{M<m≤N} p^{-m}p^{p^{m/2}} → ∞.
For A = K, the fringe topology is the valuation topology of K.

(1) For every finite A-module M there are ρ, a finite B_ρ-module M_ρ and an isomorphism M ≅ M_ρ ⊗_{B_ρ} A. (2) For finite B_ρ-modules M_1, M_2 and an A-linear map ν : M_1 ⊗_{B_ρ} A → M_2 ⊗_{B_ρ} A there is, after shrinking ρ, a B_ρ-linear ν_ρ : M_1 → M_2 with ν = ν_ρ ⊗ A (after base change to the smaller radius); if ν is an isomorphism, ν_ρ can be chosen an isomorphism.

M, M_1, M_2 finite modules

nodes.title: Finite algebras over a dagger algebra are dagger algebras
nodes.statement: Let A be a K-dagger algebra (K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K)) and A → B a finite K-algebra homomorphism (B finitely generated as an A-module). Then B is a K-dagger algebra. More precisely, if A = W_n/IW_n and B = (W_n/JW_n)[X]/(f) with I ⊆ J ⊆ T_n(λ_0) and f ∈ T_n(λ_0)[X] monic with X power-bounded modulo J + (f), then B ≅ W_{n+1}/(J + f)W_{n+1}, and the fringe stages are D_λ = T_n(λ)[X]/(J + f) ≅ T_{n+1}(λ)/(J + f).
hypotheses: A a K-dagger algebra
B a finite A-algebra
proofSteps: Reduce to B generated by one element over a quotient of A: B is a successive extension by finitely many integral generators, each satisfying a monic polynomial (finite ⇒ integral).

Write A = W_n/IW_n and B = (W_n/JW_n)[X]/(f) with I ⊆ J ⊆ T_n(λ_0) and f ∈ T_n(λ_0)[X] monic (fringe presentation, F1/fringe-presentation); after rescaling X by an element of K we may assume X is power-bounded in T_n(λ_0)[X]/(J + f).

For 1 ≤ λ ≤ λ_0 the map D_λ = T_n(λ)[X]/(J + f) → T_n(λ)⟨λ^{-1}X⟩/(J + f) = T_{n+1}(λ)/(J + f) is bijective: a finite T_n(λ)-algebra in which X is power-bounded is already complete and X-restricted (BGR 6.1.1-type finiteness), so every restricted series in X reduces, via division by the monic f, to a polynomial of degree < deg f.
Pass to the colimit over λ > 1: B = colim D_λ ≅ colim T_{n+1}(λ)/(J + f) = W_{n+1}/(J + f).
acceptance: A = W_1, B = W_1[Y]/(Y^2 − X): B ≅ W_2/(Y^2 − X) ≅ W_1 (via Y), a dagger algebra.

A = K, B any finite field extension L of K: L is a dagger algebra — L = W_m/(relations) for power-bounded generators α_1..α_m (integral over O_K after rescaling), and when L/K is simple (e.g. separable) L = W_1/(p) for the minimal polynomial p of a power-bounded primitive element (p is a Weierstrass polynomial, so W_1/(p) = K[X]/(p) by division). In characteristic p a finite extension need not be simple, so one generator does not suffice in general.

nodes.title: Finiteness, surjectivity, injectivity and strictness of morphisms of dagger algebras are detected on completions
nodes.statement: Let φ : A → B be a morphism of K-dagger algebras with completion φ̂ : Â → B̂ (K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K)). Then: (a) φ is surjective (resp. bijective) iff φ̂ is; (b) the following are equivalent: (i) φ is finite, (ii) φ̂ is finite, (iii) the map of reductions φ̃ : Ã → B̃ (R̃ = R°/R°° for the sup norm) is finite; (c) if φ is finite, φ is injective iff φ̂ is; (d) if φ is finite, the norm class on B from F1/dagger-norm-and-continuity coincides with the class of B as a finite A-module, and Â ⊗_A B → B̂ is an isomorphism; (e) if φ is finite, φ and φ̂ are strict.
hypotheses: φ : A → B a morphism of K-dagger algebras
proofSteps: (b)(i)⇒(ii): the construction of F1/dagger-finite-extension at λ = 1 exhibits B̂ = Â[X]/(J + f)-type presentations finite over Â.

(b)(ii)⇒(iii): BGR 6.3.4/2 (finite maps of affinoid algebras induce finite maps of reductions). (b)(iii)⇒(i): as in BGR 6.3.2/1,2 — lift integral equations of the reductions of generators of B over Ã to integral equations over A using weak completeness (F1/dagger-weak-completeness) and Weierstrass division (F1/overconvergent-weierstrass-division).

(d): Â ⊗_A B is a finite Â-module, hence an affinoid algebra whose Banach norm is its finite-module norm (BGR 3.7.3/3, 3.7.4/1); by (b) Â ⊗_A B → B̂ is finite, so the Banach algebra norm of B̂ is an Â ⊗_A B-algebra norm; both norms on B agree, and Â ⊗_A B is the completion of B as a finite A-module.

(a),(c): from (b),(d) and faithful flatness of A → Â (F1/dagger-completion-comparison): Â ⊗_A (coker φ) = coker φ̂ and Â ⊗_A (ker φ) = ker φ̂ when φ is finite; for surjectivity in general, a surjective φ̂ forces φ finite via (iii).
(e): φ̂ finite, so strict (BGR 1.1.9/2, 6.1.3/4); φ is the restriction of φ̂ to dense subspaces with the subspace norms.
acceptance: φ : W_1 → W_1, X ↦ X^2 is finite (W_1 is free over itself with basis 1, X under this map) and φ̂ : T_1 → T_1, X ↦ X^2 is finite.
φ : W_1 → W_1, X ↦ πX is not finite, and neither is φ̂ (its reduction is X ↦ 0).

nodes.title: Approximation of solutions and of morphisms from the completion (Bosch's rigid Artin approximation)
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K). Assume moreover char K = 0 or [K : K^p] < ∞ (the hypothesis under which Vezzani, Proposition 2.8, states the morphism form; Grosse-Klönne 1.13/1.15 state none, and Bosch's paper, which would settle it, was not read). (1) (Bosch) Let I ⊆ W_n, A = W_n/I ⊆ Â = T_n/IT_n with a Banach norm |·|_Â, and let (f_i)_{i∈Λ} be elements of A⟨Y_1..Y_m⟩† = W_{n+m}/IW_{n+m}. If there are ȳ_1..ȳ_m ∈ Â with |ȳ_j|_sup ≤ 1 and f_i(ȳ) = 0 for all i, then for every δ > 0 there are y_1..y_m ∈ A with |y_j|_sup ≤ 1, f_i(y) = 0 for all i, and |y − ȳ|_Â < δ. (2) Let p_1 : A_1 → B_1 and p_2 : A_2 → B_2 be surjective morphisms of dagger algebras, and φ_A : Â_1 → Â_2, φ_B : B̂_1 → B̂_2 morphisms with φ_B ∘ p̂_1 = p̂_2 ∘ φ_A. Then there are morphisms γ_A : A_1 → A_2 and γ_B : B_1 → B_2 with γ_B ∘ p_1 = p_2 ∘ γ_A, and for given ε > 0 and a Banach norm on Â_2, γ_A can be chosen with |γ̂_A − φ_A| < ε; if φ_A is an isomorphism, γ_A can be chosen an isomorphism. In particular two dagger algebras with isomorphic completions are isomorphic (non-canonically).
hypotheses: K complete, nontrivially and nonarchimedeanly valued, with char K = 0 or [K : K^p] < ∞ (Vezzani's hypothesis in Proposition 2.8; GK states 1.13/1.15 without it)
proofSteps: (1) is Bosch, 'A rigid analytic version of M. Artin's theorem on analytic equations' (Math. Ann. 255 (1981)); the source is not public and was not read: recorded as a gap. Grosse-Klönne quotes it as Proposition 1.13 and Vezzani states the morphism form as Proposition 2.8, citing [22, Corollary 7.5.10], where his reference [22] is Fresnel–van der Put, Rigid analytic geometry and its applications (Birkhäuser 2004) — not Grosse-Klönne's thesis.

(2) Write A_1 = W_n/(f_1..f_r), B_1 = W_n/(f_1..f_r, g_1..g_l), ker p_2 = (d_1..d_p). The pair (φ_A, φ_B) is a solution in Â_2 of the system f_q(x) = 0 (q ≤ r), g_j(x) = Σ_k y_{jk} d_k (j ≤ l) with |x_i|_sup ≤ 1; approximate it by a solution in A_2 by (1); this defines (γ_A, γ_B).

If φ_A is an isomorphism and ε < ‖φ_A^{-1}‖^{-1} (operator norms for the chosen Banach norms; GK's '< 1' presumes normalised norms), then γ̂_A = φ_A(1 + φ_A^{-1}(γ̂_A − φ_A)) is bijective by the Neumann series, and γ_A is bijective by F1/dagger-finite-morphism-comparison (a).
acceptance: For A_1 = A_2 = W_1 and φ_A the automorphism X ↦ X + a of T_1 with a ∈ T_1, |a| < 1 not overconvergent, γ_A may be taken X ↦ X + a' with a' ∈ W_1 close to a.
Two dagger algebras A, A' with Â ≅ Â' are isomorphic; e.g. the dagger structure on a smooth affinoid is unique up to isomorphism (used in F1/dagger-to-rigid-functor (6)).

nodes.title: Reduced dagger algebras are integrally closed in their completions; A is a domain iff Â is
nodes.statement: Let A be a K-dagger algebra with completion Â (K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K)). (1) If A is reduced, A is integrally closed in Â (deduced here from F1/dagger-approximation (1), so under its hypothesis char K = 0 or [K : K^p] < ∞; Grosse-Klönne states (1) without a field hypothesis, and Vezzani cites Bosch–Dwork–Robba, Math. Ann. 252 (1979/80), Theorem 2, for it) (every element of Â integral over A lies in A). (2) A is an integral domain if and only if Â is.
hypotheses: A a K-dagger algebra
in (1): A reduced
proofSteps: (1) An element ξ ∈ Â integral over A satisfies a monic equation P(ξ) = 0 with P ∈ A[Y]; after replacing ξ by cξ (c ∈ K^× small, still integral over A) we may assume |ξ|_sup ≤ 1; since Â is reduced with finitely many minimal primes p_1..p_s, a monic P has at most (deg P)^s roots in Â ⊆ ∏ Frac(Â/p_i), so the roots of P are isolated, and Bosch's approximation (F1/dagger-approximation (1)) yields y ∈ A with P(y) = 0 and |y − ξ| small, forcing y = ξ (Bosch, section 2).

(2) ⇐: A ⊆ Â (faithful flatness, F1/dagger-completion-comparison). ⇒: A is japanese (BGR 6.1.2/4 argument via Noether normalisation, F1/dagger-noether-normalisation), so the normalisation A → B is finite; B is a dagger algebra (F1/dagger-finite-extension) and Â → B̂ is injective (F1/dagger-finite-morphism-comparison (c)).

B̂ is normal (F1/dagger-completion-comparison (3)), so its local rings are domains; Sp(B) is connected for the Zariski topology, hence Sp(B̂) is connected (Fieseler, Zariski's main theorem in nonarchimedean function theory, 3.3.3 — not read, gap), so the normal ring B̂ with connected spectrum is a domain, and so is its subring Â.

nodes.title: The dagger (overconvergent completed) tensor product A_1 ⊗†_B A_2
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K) and let α_1 : B → A_1, α_2 : B → A_2 be morphisms of K-dagger algebras with surjections f_1 : W_{n_1} → A_1, f_2 : W_{n_2} → A_2. Define A_1 ⊗†_B A_2 as the image of W_{n_1+n_2} = K⟨X, Y⟩† under the continuous map T_{n_1+n_2} → Â_1 ⊗̂_{B̂} Â_2 into the completed tensor product of the K-affinoid algebras Â_1, Â_2 over B̂ that sends X_i ↦ f̂_1(X_i) ⊗ 1 and Y_j ↦ 1 ⊗ f̂_2(Y_j). It is a K-dagger algebra with maps ι_i : A_i → A_1 ⊗†_B A_2, independent of the surjections up to unique isomorphism, and it is the pushout of α_1, α_2 in the category of dagger algebras: for morphisms u_i : A_i → C with u_1α_1 = u_2α_2 there is a unique u : A_1 ⊗†_B A_2 → C with u ι_i = u_i. Its completion is Â_1 ⊗̂_{B̂} Â_2. Equivalently (Kedlaya) A_1 ⊗†_K A_2 is the direct limit of the completed tensor products B_1 ⊗̂_K B_2 of fringe algebras B_i of A_i. Notation: for λ ∈ Γ*, K⟨λ^{-1}Z⟩† := ⋃_{ρ>λ} K⟨ρ^{-1}Z⟩ and A⟨λ^{-1}Z⟩† := A ⊗†_K K⟨λ^{-1}Z⟩†, A⟨Z⟩† := A⟨1^{-1}Z⟩†.
hypotheses: α_i : B → A_i morphisms of K-dagger algebras
proofSteps: Completed tensor products of K-affinoid algebras: Â_1 ⊗̂_{B̂} Â_2 is the completed tensor product of the Huber pairs (Â_i, Â_i°) over (B̂, B̂°) (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product in the case of K-affinoid Tate algebras), a K-affinoid algebra with its universal property in complete affinoid K-algebras.

The images of the power-bounded f̂_1(X_i) ⊗ 1, 1 ⊗ f̂_2(Y_j) define T_{n_1+n_2} → Â_1 ⊗̂ Â_2 (universal property of the Tate algebra, anchor Layer 0.4); the image of W_{n_1+n_2} is a quotient of W_{n_1+n_2}, hence a dagger algebra.

Universal property: given u_i : A_i → C, the completions û_i (F1/dagger-completion-comparison) induce Â_1 ⊗̂_{B̂} Â_2 → Ĉ; the images of X_i, Y_j are power-bounded in C, so weak completeness (F1/dagger-weak-completeness) gives W_{n_1+n_2} → C, which factors through A_1 ⊗†_B A_2 because its completion factors through Â_1 ⊗̂ Â_2 and C → Ĉ is injective; uniqueness since the X_i, Y_j generate a dense subalgebra.
Independence of the surjections: the universal property.

Kedlaya's description: fringe algebras of A_1 ⊗† A_2 are images of the B_1 ⊗̂ B_2 (F1/fringe-morphism-factorisation), and the direct limit of the B_1 ⊗̂ B_2 maps isomorphically onto the image described above.

nodes.title: Rational localisation A⟨f/g⟩† of a dagger algebra and its universal property
nodes.statement: Let A be a K-dagger algebra (K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K)) and g, f_1, …, f_m ∈ A without common zero on Sp(A) (equivalently generating the unit ideal). Define A⟨f/g⟩† := A⟨X_1, …, X_m⟩†/(gX_i − f_i)_{i≤m} (A⟨X⟩† from F1/dagger-tensor-product). The map A → A⟨f/g⟩† is universal among morphisms of dagger algebras φ : A → C such that Sp(φ) lands in R(f/g) := {x ∈ Sp(A) : |f_i(x)| ≤ |g(x)| for all i}: φ(g) is then a unit and φ factors uniquely through A⟨f/g⟩†. Special cases: Weierstrass localisations A⟨f⟩† (g = 1) and Laurent localisations A⟨f^{-1}⟩† = A⟨X⟩†/(fX − 1). Sp(A⟨f/g⟩†) = R(f/g), the completion of A⟨f/g⟩† is the affinoid rational localisation Â⟨f/g⟩, and A⟨f/g⟩† depends only on the subset R(f/g), not on (f, g).
hypotheses: A a K-dagger algebra
g, f_1..f_m ∈ A generate the unit ideal
proofSteps: Construction: A⟨X⟩† is a dagger algebra (F1/dagger-tensor-product), so is its quotient (F1/dagger-algebra).

Universal property: if Sp(φ) ⊆ R(f/g), then φ(g) vanishes at no point of Sp(C) (the f_i, g have no common zero), so φ(g) is a unit (Max(C) = Sp(C), F1/dagger-weak-completeness (c)); the elements φ(f_i)/φ(g) have |·|_sup ≤ 1, hence are power-bounded, and weak completeness (F1/dagger-weak-completeness (a)) extends X_i ↦ φ(f_i)/φ(g) to A⟨X⟩† → C, killing gX_i − f_i. Uniqueness: X_i must go to φ(f_i)/φ(g).

Completion: A⟨X⟩†/(gX − f) has completion Â⟨X⟩/(gX − f) (F1/dagger-completion-comparison and F1/dagger-tensor-product), which is the rational localisation of the Huber pair (Â, Â°) at T = {f_i}, s = g (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.completionLocalization with its universal property tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset; the identification Â⟨X⟩/(gX − f) ≅ Â⟨f/g⟩ is anchor Layer 3).
Points: Max of the localisation = maximal ideals x of A with |f_i(x)| ≤ |g(x)|, by the universal property applied to C = residue fields.
Independence of (f, g): two presentations of the same subset satisfy each other's universal property (Vezzani Proposition 2.12).
acceptance: W_1⟨X^{-1}⟩† = K⟨X, Y⟩†/(XY − 1) = K⟨X, X^{-1}⟩†, the dagger annulus |X| = 1.
W_1⟨X/π⟩†, the Weierstrass domain {|X| ≤ |π|} of the dagger unit disc, is isomorphic to K⟨Y⟩† via Y = X/π.

nodes.title: The integral Monsky–Washnitzer algebra O_K⟨X_1, …, X_n⟩† = W_n ∩ O_K[[X]]
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K) and O_K = {a : |a| ≤ 1}. Define O_K⟨X_1..X_n⟩† := W_n ∩ O_K[[X_1..X_n]], the overconvergent power series with coefficients in O_K; it is W_n^int (F1/dagger-algebra). If O_K is a discrete valuation ring with uniformiser π, a series f ∈ O_K[[X]] lies in O_K⟨X⟩† iff there is c > 0 with f = Σ_{j≥0} π^j P_j(X), P_j ∈ O_K[X], deg P_j ≤ c(j+1) (the Monsky–Washnitzer degree growth condition), and then O_K⟨X⟩† is noetherian, O_K⟨X⟩†/π^m = O_K[X]/π^m for all m, its π-adic completion is O_K⟨X⟩ = T_n ∩ O_K[[X]], and O_K⟨X⟩† ⊗_{O_K} K = W_n.
hypotheses: K complete, nontrivially and nonarchimedeanly valued; for the degree-growth description, noetherianity and the π-adic statements: O_K a discrete valuation ring
proofSteps: O_K⟨X⟩† = W_n^int: the supremum norm on W_n equals the Gauss norm, because Max(W_n) = Max(T_n) with the same residue fields (F1/overconvergent-faithful-flatness (b)) and on T_n the supremum norm is the Gauss norm (maximum modulus principle, anchor Layer 0); hence |f|_sup ≤ 1 iff all coefficients lie in O_K. (F1/dagger-completion-comparison (4) alone only gives equivalence of norms, not equality.)
Degree growth: |a_ν| ≤ Cρ^{-|ν|} with ρ = |π|^{-1/c'} is v_π(a_ν) ≥ |ν|/c' − const; grouping monomials by j = v_π(a_ν) gives deg P_j ≤ c(j+1), and conversely.

Noetherian (O_K a DVR): supplied by the proposed node F1/integral-overconvergent-noetherian (Kedlaya's Gröbner-basis argument from the proof of Lemma 2.4.1 run with leading terms π^vX^I, or van der Put's integral Weierstrass theory (2.2)). F1/overconvergent-weierstrass-division does not provide this: it concerns Gauss-norm distinguished elements of W_n over K, not π-adically distinguished integral series.
O_K⟨X⟩†/π^m = O_K[X]/π^m: coefficients tend to 0, so all but finitely many lie in π^m O_K; the π-adic completion is therefore lim_m O_K[X]/π^m = O_K⟨X⟩ (van der Put).
⊗ K: every f ∈ W_n has bounded coefficients (|a_ν| ≤ C), so π^m f ∈ O_K⟨X⟩† for m ≫ 0.
acceptance: Σ_j π^j X^j ∈ O_K⟨X⟩†; Σ_j π^j X^{j^2} ∈ O_K⟨X⟩ but ∉ O_K⟨X⟩†.
