nodes.title: The Monsky–Washnitzer weak completion S† of a finitely generated O_K-algebra
nodes.statement: Let O_K be a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformiser π, residue field k = O_K/π and fraction field K (any characteristic; K carries the π-adic absolute value). Let S be a finitely generated O_K-algebra and Ŝ = lim_m S/π^mS its π-adic completion. Choose generators x_1, …, x_n of S. The weak completion S† ⊆ Ŝ is the set of z ∈ Ŝ that can be written z = Σ_{j≥0} π^j P_j(x_1, …, x_n) (convergent in Ŝ) with P_j ∈ O_K[X_1..X_n] of total degree ≤ c(j+1) for some real c; equivalently, S† is the image of O_K⟨X_1..X_n⟩† → Ŝ, X_i ↦ x_i. S† is an O_K-subalgebra of Ŝ containing the image of S, and it does not depend on the choice of generators. The dagger algebra attached to S is A† := S† ⊗_{O_K} K (F1/weak-completion-generic-fibre).
hypotheses: O_K a complete discrete valuation ring
S a finitely generated O_K-algebra
proofSteps: Evaluation O_K⟨X⟩† → Ŝ, X_i ↦ x_i, is defined because Ŝ is π-adically complete and each series Σ π^j P_j(x) converges π-adically (F1/integral-overconvergent-tate-algebra, degree-growth form); its image is the set described.
Subalgebra: sums and products of degree-growth series have degree growth (deg(P_j Q_l) ≤ c(j+1) + c'(l+1) ≤ 2·max(c, c')·(j + l + 1)).

Independence of generators: if y_1..y_m is another generating set, each y_i = Q_i(x) with deg Q_i ≤ d and each x_i = R_i(y); a representation Σ π^j P_j(y) of degree growth c becomes Σ π^j P_j(Q(x)) of degree growth cd.
Mathlib model: Ŝ = AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {π}) S, and S† is the O_K-subalgebra of Ŝ given as the range of the evaluation map O_K⟨X⟩† → Ŝ.
acceptance: S = O_K[X]: S† = O_K⟨X⟩†.
S = O_K[z, z^{-1}]: S† is the ring of Laurent series Σ_{m∈ℤ} a_m z^m with a_m ∈ O_K and v(a_m) ≥ ε|m| − C for some ε > 0.

nodes.title: Presentation, noetherianity and reduction of a weak completion
nodes.statement: Let O_K is a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformiser π, residue field k = O_K/π and fraction field K (any characteristic; K carries the π-adic absolute value) and S = O_K[X_1..X_n]/I a finitely generated O_K-algebra. Then (a) S† ≅ O_K⟨X⟩†/I·O_K⟨X⟩† (compatibly with S → S†); (b) S† is noetherian; (c) S†/π^mS† ≅ S/π^mS for all m ≥ 1; (d) π lies in the Jacobson radical of S†, S† is π-adically separated and its π-adic completion is Ŝ; (e) S† → Ŝ is faithfully flat.
hypotheses: O_K a complete DVR
S = O_K[X]/I finitely generated
proofSteps: Write R = O_K⟨X⟩†. R is noetherian with π in its Jacobson radical (F1/integral-overconvergent-tate-algebra: 1 + πf is a unit); its π-adic completion R̂ = O_K⟨X⟩ is faithfully flat over R (completion of a noetherian ring along an ideal in the Jacobson radical).
Ŝ = O_K⟨X⟩/I·O_K⟨X⟩ (completion of the finite R-module R/IR, exactness of completion for noetherian rings), so the kernel of R → Ŝ is IR̂ ∩ R = IR by faithful flatness: this is (a).
(b): quotient of the noetherian R. (c): R/π^m = O_K[X]/π^m (F1/integral-overconvergent-tate-algebra), so S†/π^m = (R/IR)/π^m = O_K[X]/(I, π^m) = S/π^m S.

(d): π ∈ Jac(R) ⇒ π ∈ Jac(S†); Krull's intersection theorem for the noetherian S† gives ⋂ π^mS† = 0; the completion is lim S†/π^m = lim S/π^m = Ŝ by (c). (e): completion of a noetherian ring along an ideal in its Jacobson radical is faithfully flat.

nodes.title: Weak completeness and the universal property of the weak completion
nodes.statement: Let O_K is a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformiser π, residue field k = O_K/π and fraction field K (any characteristic; K carries the π-adic absolute value). Call an O_K-algebra B weakly complete finitely generated if B ≅ O_K⟨Y_1..Y_m⟩†/J for some m and ideal J. Then: (a) for every finitely generated O_K-algebra S, S† is weakly complete finitely generated, and for all y_1, …, y_r ∈ S† the map O_K[Y_1..Y_r] → S†, Y_i ↦ y_i, extends uniquely to O_K⟨Y⟩† → S†; (b) for every weakly complete finitely generated B and every O_K-algebra homomorphism φ : S → B there is a unique O_K-algebra homomorphism φ† : S† → B with φ†|_S = φ; (c) consequently S ↦ S† is a functor from finitely generated O_K-algebras to weakly complete finitely generated O_K-algebras, left adjoint to the inclusion, and (S†)† = S†.
hypotheses: O_K a complete DVR
S finitely generated over O_K
B weakly complete finitely generated
proofSteps: (a) S† = O_K⟨X⟩†/I O_K⟨X⟩† (F1/weak-completion-presentation). Substitution: for g = Σ π^{j_0} Q_{j_0}(Y) with deg Q_{j_0} ≤ c(j_0 + 1) and y_i = Σ_j π^j P_{ij}(x) with deg P_{ij} ≤ c'(j + 1), a monomial of π-exponent J = j_0 + Σ j_i in g(y) has x-degree ≤ c'(J + |μ|) ≤ c'(J + c(j_0 + 1)) ≤ c''(J + 1); so g(y) ∈ S†.

(b) Existence: write B = O_K⟨Y⟩†/J; for z ∈ S† choose g ∈ O_K⟨X⟩† mapping to z and put φ†(z) := g(φ(x_1), …, φ(x_n)), defined by weak completeness of B (the argument of (a) in B). Well defined: if g maps to 0 in Ŝ, then g ∈ I O_K⟨X⟩† (presentation lemma), and elements of I map to 0 under φ.

(b) Uniqueness: two extensions agree modulo π^m for every m because S†/π^m = S/π^m (presentation lemma (c)); B is noetherian with π in its Jacobson radical (1 + πb is a unit by weak completeness), so ⋂_m π^m B = 0 (Krull) and the extensions agree.
(c) formal from (b); (S†)† = S† because S† is already weakly complete finitely generated.
acceptance: φ : O_K[x] → O_K⟨x⟩†, x ↦ x^q extends to the endomorphism g(x) ↦ g(x^q) of O_K⟨x⟩† (the standard Frobenius lift of RD.0).
For S = O_K[x, x^{-1}] and B = O_K⟨x, x^{-1}⟩†, the map x ↦ x^q(1 + πx) extends because 1 + πx is a unit of B.

nodes.title: The generic fibre S† ⊗ K of a weak completion is a dagger algebra with completion Ŝ ⊗ K
nodes.statement: Let O_K is a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformiser π, residue field k = O_K/π and fraction field K (any characteristic; K carries the π-adic absolute value), S = O_K[X_1..X_n]/I and A† := S† ⊗_{O_K} K. Then (a) A† ≅ W_n/IW_n is a K-dagger algebra; (b) its completion is Ŝ ⊗_{O_K} K = T_n/IT_n; (c) the image of S† lies in (A†)^int; if S is flat over O_K then S† → A† is injective, and if moreover S/πS is reduced then S† = (A†)^int, i.e. S† is exactly the set of elements of A† of supremum norm ≤ 1; (d) for S smooth over O_K, A† is a dagger algebra of Monsky–Washnitzer type with reduction S/πS (F1/mw-type-dagger-algebra).
hypotheses: O_K a complete DVR
S finitely generated over O_K; in (c) S flat over O_K; in (c) second half S/πS reduced; in (d) S smooth over O_K
proofSteps: (a) Localisation at π is exact: A† = O_K⟨X⟩†[1/π]/I = W_n/IW_n (F1/weak-completion-presentation (a), F1/integral-overconvergent-tate-algebra ⊗ K).
(b) Completion of W_n/IW_n is T_n/IT_n (F1/dagger-norm-and-continuity (1)) and Ŝ[1/π] = O_K⟨X⟩/I [1/π] = T_n/IT_n.

(c) Integral series have Gauss norm ≤ 1, so their images have |·|_sup ≤ 1. If S is flat over O_K, so is S† (S → S† is the base change of the flat map O_K[X] → O_K⟨X⟩†, van der Put 2.2), hence S† is π-torsion free and S† → S†[1/π] is injective. If S/πS is reduced, Ŝ/πŜ = S/πS is reduced, so Ŝ = (Ŝ ⊗ K)° (an affinoid unit ball with reduced reduction consists exactly of the power-bounded elements, BGR 6.4.3); thus (A†)^int = A† ∩ Ŝ (F1/dagger-algebra: A^int = A ∩ Â°), and A† ∩ Ŝ = S† because s/π^m ∈ Ŝ with s ∈ S† forces s ∈ π^mŜ ∩ S† = π^mS† (faithful flatness, F1/weak-completion-presentation (e)).

(d) S smooth ⇒ S flat with S/πS smooth, hence reduced; by (c) (A†)^int/π = S†/π = S/πS is smooth over k; A† is regular because Â† = Ŝ[1/π] is the generic fibre of a smooth formal scheme, hence regular, and regularity descends (F1/dagger-completion-comparison (3)).

nodes.title: Dagger algebras of Monsky–Washnitzer type
nodes.statement: Let O_K be a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformiser π, residue field k = O_K/π and fraction field K (any characteristic; K carries the π-adic absolute value). A K-dagger algebra A is of Monsky–Washnitzer type (MW-type) if A is a regular ring and the ring A^int/πA^int is a smooth k-algebra (A^int = elements of supremum norm ≤ 1, F1/dagger-algebra). Its reduction (special fibre) is A^int/πA^int. The regularity clause is part of the definition: it does not follow from smoothness of A^int/πA^int.
hypotheses: O_K a complete DVR
A a K-dagger algebra
proofSteps: Definition: Dagger.IsMWType A :⇔ IsRegularRing A ∧ Algebra.Smooth k (A^int ⧸ π A^int).

Characterisation (Kedlaya: 'formally smooth, weakly complete, weakly finitely generated'): A is of MW-type iff A ≅ S† ⊗ K for a smooth finitely generated O_K-algebra S, and then A^int = S†. ⇐ is F1/weak-completion-generic-fibre (d) (with (c) for A^int = S†). ⇒ needs that A^int is a lift of A^int/πA^int (weakly complete finitely generated and flat), which neither this node nor F1/mw-lift-existence-uniqueness proves (each cited the other); it is supplied by the proposed node F1/mw-type-integral-lift (formal lifts of the smooth reduction are unique, then F1/dagger-approximation (2) descends the isomorphism of completions to the dagger algebras). This characterisation, like the lifting theory it uses, is for O_K of mixed characteristic (0, p).

nodes.title: Lifting morphisms of smooth reductions to weak completions (van der Put 2.4.4 (ii))
nodes.statement: Let O_K be a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic (0, p) with uniformiser π, residue field k = O_K/π and fraction field K (K carries the π-adic absolute value; this is van der Put's standing hypothesis 'K = Qt(R) of characteristic 0' — the Artin approximation property of O_K⟨t⟩† used in the proof is not available in the sources for equal characteristic). Let A_0, C_0 be smooth finitely generated k-algebras and A, C lifts of them: weakly complete finitely generated O_K-algebras, flat over O_K, with A/πA ≅ A_0 and C/πC ≅ C_0. Then every k-algebra homomorphism f : A_0 → C_0 lifts to an O_K-algebra homomorphism F : A → C (F mod π = f). More generally, every O_K-algebra homomorphism F̂ : A → Ĉ into the π-adic completion can be approximated: for every m there is F : A → C with F ≡ F̂ mod π^m.
hypotheses: O_K a complete DVR of mixed characteristic (0, p)
A, C lifts of smooth finitely generated k-algebras
proofSteps: Infinitesimal lifting: A/π^mA is smooth over O_K/π^m for every m (flat with smooth reduction), so f lifts step by step to compatible O_K/π^m-algebra maps A/π^m → C/π^m (formal smoothness, Mathlib Algebra.FormallySmooth); their limit is F̂ : A → Ĉ lifting f.

Approximation: write A = O_K⟨X⟩†/(g_1..g_r). F̂ gives a solution (F̂(X_i)) in Ĉ of the equations g_j = 0; by the Artin approximation property of O_K⟨t⟩† (van der Put 2.4.1–2.4.3, proved by adapting Artin's argument; Bosch [4] in the non-discrete case — not read, recorded as a gap) there is a solution in C congruent to it modulo π^m. This defines F.
F mod π = F̂ mod π = f for m ≥ 1.
acceptance: A = C = O_K⟨x⟩†, f = q-power map on k[x]: F(x) = x^q works, and so does x^q + πx; the lifts differ.
A = O_K⟨x, x^{-1}⟩†: the q-power map lifts to x ↦ x^q(1 + πx) because 1 + πx is a unit.

nodes.title: Existence and uniqueness of dagger algebras of MW-type with a given smooth reduction
nodes.statement: Let O_K be a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic (0, p) with uniformiser π, residue field k = O_K/π and fraction field K (K carries the π-adic absolute value) and A_0 a smooth finitely generated k-algebra. Then (a) there is a smooth finitely generated O_K-algebra B with B/πB ≅ A_0 (Elkik); (b) B† is a lift of A_0 (weakly complete finitely generated, flat over O_K, B†/πB† ≅ A_0) and B† ⊗ K is a dagger algebra of MW-type with reduction A_0; (c) any two lifts of A_0 are isomorphic as O_K-algebras (non-canonically). (That two dagger algebras of MW-type with isomorphic reductions are isomorphic additionally needs that their integral subrings are lifts: F1/mw-type-integral-lift.)
hypotheses: O_K a complete DVR of mixed characteristic (0, p)
A_0 smooth and finitely generated over k
proofSteps: (a) Elkik, 'Solutions d'équations à coefficients dans un anneau hensélien' (Ann. Sci. ÉNS 1973), Théorème 6: smooth algebras over the henselian pair (O_K, π) lift. Not read; recorded as a gap.
(b) F1/weak-completion-presentation (c) gives B†/π = B/π = A_0; flatness from flatness of B; MW-type by F1/weak-completion-generic-fibre (d).

(c) Given lifts A, B, F1/mw-morphism-lifting lifts id_{A_0} to h : A → B; h mod π is bijective, so h is surjective by the Weierstrass theorems (van der Put: B/πB finite over A/πA forces B finite over A for weakly complete finitely generated algebras, which is where integral Weierstrass division enters — Nakayama alone does not apply, since B is not yet known to be a finite A-module; then B = h(A) + πB and π ∈ Jac(A) give B = h(A)), and injective because A has no π-torsion and h mod π is injective (ker h ⊆ ⋂ π^m A = 0 by flatness of B and separatedness, F1/weak-completion-presentation (d)).

The consequence for dagger algebras of MW-type (isomorphic reductions ⇒ isomorphic algebras) is not derived here: it needs that A^int is a lift, which is the content of the proposed node F1/mw-type-integral-lift (the previous version cited F1/mw-type-dagger-algebra for it, which in turn cited this node).
acceptance: A_0 = k[x]: lift O_K⟨x⟩†. A_0 = k[x, y, y^{-1}]/(y^2 − Q(x)) (Q squarefree mod p, p odd): lift the weak completion of O_K[x, y, y^{-1}]/(y^2 − Q̃(x)) for any lift Q̃ of Q; different lifts Q̃ give isomorphic dagger algebras.

nodes.title: Affinoid subdomains of the maximal spectrum of a dagger algebra
nodes.statement: Let A be a K-dagger algebra (K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K)) and X = Sp(A) its set of maximal ideals. A subset U ⊆ X is an affinoid subdomain if there are a dagger algebra B = O_X(U) and a morphism π : A → B with Sp(π)(Sp B) ⊆ U such that for every dagger algebra D the map Hom_K(B, D) → {f ∈ Hom_K(A, D) : Sp(f)(Sp D) ⊆ U}, g ↦ g ∘ π, is bijective. Then B is unique up to unique isomorphism and Sp(π) : Sp(B) → U is a bijection. Rational subdomains R(f/g) with O_X(R(f/g)) = A⟨f/g⟩† (F1/dagger-rational-localisation) and Weierstrass domains (g = 1) are affinoid subdomains; the notion is transitive and stable under base change A → D.
hypotheses: A a K-dagger algebra
proofSteps: Uniqueness of B: two representing objects are isomorphic by the Yoneda argument; Sp(B) → U is bijective by testing the universal property on the residue fields D = A/m (finite over K, F1/dagger-noether-normalisation).
Rational subdomains: F1/dagger-rational-localisation (universal property).
Transitivity and base change: composition of universal properties; for base change A → D, U ×_A D is represented by B ⊗†_A D (F1/dagger-tensor-product).

nodes.title: Affinoid subdomains, stalks, open immersions and Runge immersions agree with their completions
nodes.statement: Let A be a K-dagger algebra with completion Â (K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K)), X = Sp(A), X' = Sp(Â), identified as sets. (a) If A → B defines an affinoid subdomain U of X, then Â → B̂ defines the affinoid subdomain U of the rigid affinoid X'. (b) For x ∈ X put O_{X,x} = colim O_X(U) over affinoid subdomains U ∋ x; the canonical maps O_{X,x} → O_{X',x} are isomorphisms. Hence a morphism of dagger algebras defines an open (resp. locally closed) immersion iff the associated morphism of affinoid algebras does, and it defines a Runge immersion (Weierstrass domain followed by a closed immersion) iff its completion does. (c) If Â → D defines a locally closed immersion of rigid affinoid spaces, there is a finite covering X = ⋃ X_i by rational subdomains X_i = Sp(A⟨f_i/g_i⟩†) such that each Â⟨f_i/g_i⟩ → Â⟨f_i/g_i⟩ ⊗̂_Â D is a Runge immersion.
hypotheses: A a K-dagger algebra
proofSteps: (a) Prove the dagger analogue of BGR 7.2.2/1 (affinoid subdomains are characterised by the universal property for the finite-dimensional test algebras A/m^k), compare completed local rings (F1/dagger-completion-comparison (2)), and apply BGR 7.3.3/5 and 8.2.1/4 on the completions.

(b) Surjectivity of O_{X,x} → O_{X',x}: write A = W_n/IW_n with a fringe presentation, X'(ρ) = Sp(T_n(ρ)/I); O_{X'(ρ),x} = O_{X',x}; a germ g ∈ O_{X'(ρ),x} is represented on a rational neighbourhood (T_n(ρ)/I)⟨f_1..f_r⟩ with f_i ∈ x, and then also by an element of (W_n/I)⟨ρ f_1, …, ρ f_r⟩†; injectivity: a section over a dagger affinoid neighbourhood U of x that vanishes on a rigid affinoid neighbourhood of x vanishes on a smaller dagger rational neighbourhood V ∋ x (rational neighbourhoods defined by overconvergent functions are cofinal), and O_X(V) → O_{X'}(V) is injective (A → Â is injective for every dagger algebra). The open/locally closed immersion statements follow because they are stalk conditions (bijective/surjective on local rings).

(c) On a fringe stage E = T_m(ρ)/I the locally closed immersion extends (after shrinking ρ), and BGR 7.3.5/1 — a locally closed immersion of affinoid rigid spaces becomes a Runge immersion over the members of a finite rational covering of the target — gives finitely many rational subdomains W_i of Sp(E) on which it is Runge; restrict to X (rational subdomains of the fringe restrict to rational subdomains of X defined by overconvergent functions). This input is NOT the Gerritzen–Grauert theorem of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/gerritzen-grauert (which decomposes affinoid subdomains into rational ones; BGR 7.3.5/3) and no packet node provides it: see the proposed node F1/rigid-locally-closed-immersion-runge. nodes.title: Tate acyclicity for dagger algebras
nodes.statement: Let A be a K-dagger algebra (K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K)), X = Sp(A) and M an A-module. Every finite covering X = U_1 ∪ … ∪ U_n by affinoid subdomains is acyclic for the presheaf U ↦ O_X(U) ⊗_A M: the augmented Čech complex 0 → M → ∏_i O_X(U_i) ⊗_A M → ∏_{i<j} O_X(U_i ∩ U_j) ⊗_A M → … is exact.
hypotheses: A a K-dagger algebra
a finite covering of Sp(A) by affinoid subdomains
M any A-module
proofSteps: Reduction to M = A (as in BGR 8.2.1/5): the maps A → O_X(U) are flat (Dagger.IsAffinoidSubdomain.flat, F1/dagger-affinoid-subdomain), so the Čech complex for M is the Čech complex for A tensored with M.

Reduction to Laurent coverings (as in BGR 8.2.1/1, 8.2.2): using F1/dagger-affinoid-subdomain-completion (c), every finite affinoid covering has a refinement by a rational covering, and every rational covering is refined, after a Laurent covering, by coverings whose members are Weierstrass/Laurent domains; Čech acyclicity passes along such refinements.

Simple Laurent covering {|f| ≤ 1}, {|f| ≥ 1}: exactness of 0 → A → A⟨f⟩† × A⟨f^{-1}⟩† → A⟨f, f^{-1}⟩† → 0 is the explicit computation with series Σ a_m X^m (m ≥ 0), Σ b_m X^{-m} (m ≥ 0) and Laurent series: in A⟨X, X^{-1}⟩†/(X − f) every element splits into its X-nonnegative and X-negative parts, each overconvergent (the splitting maps T_1(ρ)-annulus series to T_1(ρ)-disc series, preserving overconvergence), and the kernel computation uses the Weierstrass division of F1/overconvergent-weierstrass-division.
Rigid comparison is not used directly; completions only enter through the Gerritzen–Grauert refinement.

nodes.title: The G-topology of an affinoid dagger space is that of its completion; affinoid subdomains form a basis
nodes.statement: Let A be a K-dagger algebra with completion Â (K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K)). (a) A morphism π : A → B defines an affinoid subdomain iff π̂ : Â → B̂ does; if π defines an open immersion (bijective on local rings), its image is an affinoid subdomain. (b) Give Sp(A) the G-topology induced from the strong G-topology of Sp(Â) via Sp(A) = Sp(Â). Then the affinoid subdomains of Sp(A) form a basis of this G-topology, every admissible covering of an affinoid subdomain has a finite refinement by affinoid subdomains, and every affinoid subdomain of Sp(Â) is a finite union of affinoid subdomains of Sp(A). (c) In adic terms: every rational subset of Spa(Â, Â°) is R(f/g) with f, g ∈ A, and every open covering of a quasi-compact open of Spa(Â, Â°) is refined by a finite covering by such rational subsets.
hypotheses: A a K-dagger algebra
proofSteps: (a) From Tate acyclicity (F1/dagger-tate-acyclicity), exactly as BGR 8.2.1 deduces that open immersions of affinoid spaces have affinoid-subdomain images; combined with F1/dagger-affinoid-subdomain-completion (a),(b).

(b) It suffices that every affinoid subdomain U of Sp(Â) is a finite union of affinoid subdomains of Sp(A). By F1/dagger-affinoid-subdomain-completion (c) reduce to U a Weierstrass domain {|h_i| ≤ 1} with h_i ∈ Â; A is dense in Â (F1/dagger-norm-and-continuity (1)), and a Weierstrass domain does not change when the h_i are perturbed by less than 1 in sup norm, so U is a dagger Weierstrass domain.

(c) The adic form: rational subsets of Spa(Â, Â°) are unchanged by small perturbations of their defining functions (anchor Layer 2, Wedhorn Proposition 7.34), and A is dense in Â; open coverings of quasi-compact opens have finite standard rational refinements (anchor Layer 2, Wedhorn Lemma 7.54).
acceptance: For A = W_1 and K = ℚ_p, let h = Σ_{m≥0} p^m X^{p^m} ∈ T_1 ∖ W_1. The rigid Weierstrass domain U = {|h| ≤ |p|} = {|h/p| ≤ 1} of Sp(T_1) is a proper nonempty subset (|h/p|_sup = p > 1, and h(0) = 0), and U = {|h_N/p| ≤ 1} for every polynomial truncation h_N = Σ_{m≤N} p^m X^{p^m} with N ≥ 1, since |(h − h_N)/p|_sup = p^{-N} < 1; so U is a dagger Weierstrass domain.

nodes.title: Dagger spaces (rigid spaces with overconvergent structure sheaf)
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K). Rigid spaces are, throughout, the quasi-separated Tate rigid-analytic spaces over K of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytic-space (G-topological spaces locally isomorphic to Sp(B) for K-affinoid algebras B), compared with adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(K, O_K) by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor, under which admissible opens and admissible coverings correspond to opens and open coverings. A K-dagger space is a pair (X, O†_X) where X is a rigid space over K and O†_X ⊆ O_X is a subsheaf of K-algebras for the G-topology of X such that X has an admissible covering by affinoids U = Sp(Â_U) together with dagger algebras A_U with completion Â_U (a dagger structure on U) for which O†_X(V) = A_U⟨f/g⟩† for every rational subdomain V = R(f/g) ⊆ U with f, g ∈ A_U. A morphism (X, O†_X) → (Y, O†_Y) is a morphism of rigid spaces φ : X → Y over K with φ^♯(O†_Y) ⊆ φ_*O†_X. The affinoid dagger space of a dagger algebra A is Sp(A) := (Sp(Â), O†_A) with O†_A(R(f/g)) = A⟨f/g⟩†. This is Grosse-Klönne's definition 2.12 (locally G-ringed spaces with saturated G-topology admitting an admissible covering by affinoid dagger spaces, F1/dagger-g-topology) written, as in Vezzani 2.22, as a rigid space with a subsheaf; through AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor it is equivalently a quasi-separated adic space locally of finite type over Spa(K, O_K) with a subsheaf O† ⊆ O that is locally of the form R(f/g) ↦ A⟨f/g⟩† on rational subsets of Spa(Â, Â°). Dagger spaces are assumed quasi-separated.
hypotheses: K complete, nontrivially and nonarchimedeanly valued
X quasi-separated
proofSteps: The presheaf R(f/g) ↦ A⟨f/g⟩† on rational subsets of Spa(Â, Â°) is well defined (independence of (f, g), F1/dagger-rational-localisation), restriction maps come from transitivity, and it is a sheaf on rational coverings by F1/dagger-tate-acyclicity (for M = A) together with F1/dagger-g-topology (c) (rational coverings of rational subsets are refined by finite rational coverings defined over A); it extends uniquely to a sheaf on all opens (sheaf on a basis). O† ⊆ O because A⟨f/g⟩† → Â⟨f/g⟩ is injective (faithful flatness, F1/dagger-completion-comparison).

Affinoid dagger spaces: A ↦ Sp(A) is fully faithful into dagger spaces (GK 2.11; Vezzani Proposition 2.24): a morphism Sp(B) → Sp(A) is determined by global sections A → B, and every K-algebra map A → B is continuous (F1/dagger-norm-and-continuity) so it induces a morphism of the completions and of the adic spectra preserving the O† (universal property of rational localisation).

Gluing, open subspaces, fibre products: open subspaces of dagger spaces are dagger spaces; fibre products are glued from Sp(A_1 ⊗†_B A_2) (F1/dagger-tensor-product) over the fibre products of the underlying adic spaces (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence); base change along a finite extension K'/K by A ↦ A ⊗_K K'.

Adic form: under AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor the G-topology of F1/dagger-g-topology corresponds to the topology of Spa(Â, Â°), rational subdomains to rational subsets (F1/dagger-g-topology (c)), and O† to a subsheaf of the adic structure sheaf; the adic spaces are the anchor's (Layer 5).
acceptance: Sp(W_1) is the dagger closed unit disc D with O†(D) = W_1; its underlying rigid space is the closed unit disc Spa(K⟨X⟩).
The open unit disc D^0 = ⋃_{ε<1} Sp(K⟨X/ε⟩†) is a dagger space whose underlying rigid space is the rigid open disc.

nodes.title: Coherent modules on dagger spaces
nodes.statement: Let X be a K-dagger space. For an affinoid X = Sp(A) and an A-module M, M ⊗ O_X denotes the sheaf extending U ↦ M ⊗_A O†_X(U) on affinoid subdomains (a sheaf by F1/dagger-tate-acyclicity). nodes.title: Strict neighbourhoods of affinoids and the cofinal fringe system
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K). Rigid spaces are, throughout, the quasi-separated Tate rigid-analytic spaces over K of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytic-space (G-topological spaces locally isomorphic to Sp(B) for K-affinoid algebras B), compared with adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(K, O_K) by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor, under which admissible opens and admissible coverings correspond to opens and open coverings. Let W be a rigid space and U ⊆ W an admissible open for which the complement W − U is admissible open (e.g. U an affinoid subdomain or a finite union of such). An admissible open V ⊆ W is a strict neighbourhood of U in W if {W − U, V} is an admissible covering of W; equivalently, in the adic space of W (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor), V contains the closure Ū of U (Vezzani's U ⋐_W V). For a fringe presentation, the affinoid Sp(T_n/IT_n) is written Sp(C) ⊂† Sp(D) inside D = T_n(ρ_0)/I (Grosse-Klönne 2.21), and for dagger spaces Sp(A) ⊂† Sp(B) means Sp(Â) ⊂† Sp(B̂). Cofinality: given ρ_0 ∈ Γ*, ρ_0 > 1, I ⊆ T_n(ρ_0) and an open immersion Sp(T_n(ρ_0)/I) → W, the affinoids V_ρ = Sp(T_n(ρ)/IT_n(ρ)), 1 < ρ ≤ ρ_0, form a cofinal system of strict neighbourhoods of V_1 = Sp(T_n/IT_n) in W. (Strict neighbourhoods of tubes in frames are PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology RD.3's notion, not this one.)
hypotheses: W a rigid space over K
U ⊆ W quasi-compact open
proofSteps: Adic reformulation: the rigid admissible open W − U corresponds to the adic open W ∖ Ū (Huber's comparison, AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor), and admissible coverings correspond to open coverings; so {W − U, V} is admissible iff (W ∖ Ū) ∪ V = W iff Ū ⊆ V.

Cofinality (GK 2.22): reduce to W = V_{ρ_0}; given a strict neighbourhood T of V_1, the covering W = ⋃_{ρ>1}(W − V_ρ) ∪ T is admissible, W is quasi-compact, so a finite subcovering exists, which forces T ⊇ V_ρ for some ρ > 1. Each V_ρ, ρ > 1, is a strict neighbourhood because V_1 ⊆ {|X_i| ≤ 1} and V_ρ ⊇ {|X_i| < ρ} ⊇ closure of V_1 (F1/fringe-presentation: V_1 is the Weierstrass domain {|X_i| ≤ 1} of V_ρ).
acceptance: For W = {|X| ≤ ρ_0} and U the closed unit disc, the discs {|X| ≤ ρ} and {|X| < ρ}, 1 < ρ ≤ ρ_0, are strict neighbourhoods of U, and the discs {|X| ≤ ρ} are cofinal.

nodes.title: Overconvergent sections are sections extending to a strict neighbourhood
nodes.statement: Let X = Sp(A) be an affinoid K-dagger space with an immersion X' ⊂† Y of fringe type (Y = Sp(T_n(ρ_0)/I)), F a coherent O_X-module and F' its rigid counterpart. If G is a coherent O_Y-module with G|_{X'} = F' (such G exists after shrinking Y, by F1/fringe-module-descent), then Γ(X, F) = {s ∈ Γ(X', G) : s extends to a strict neighbourhood of X' in Y} = colim over strict neighbourhoods V of X' in Y of Γ(V, G). In particular Γ(X, O†) = A = colim_ρ Γ(Sp(T_n(ρ)/I), O).
hypotheses: X = Sp(A) with a fringe presentation
F coherent on X, G coherent on Y extending F'
proofSteps: Strict neighbourhoods of X' in Y are cofinal with the V_ρ (F1/strict-neighbourhood), so the colimit is colim_ρ Γ(V_ρ, G).

Write F = M ⊗ O_X with M finite over A (F1/dagger-coherent-affinoid-kiehl); by F1/fringe-module-descent M = M_ρ ⊗ A with M_ρ finite over A_ρ and G|_{V_ρ} ≅ M_ρ ⊗ O_{V_ρ} after shrinking; Γ(V_ρ, G) = M_ρ (rigid Kiehl, AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid), and colim_ρ M_ρ = colim_ρ M_ρ ⊗_{A_ρ} A_ρ = M ⊗ colim... = M (A = colim A_ρ, F1/fringe-presentation).
The map to Γ(X', G) = M ⊗_A Â is injective (faithful flatness of A → Â, F1/dagger-completion-comparison).
acceptance: X = D the closed dagger disc inside Y = {|X| ≤ ρ_0}: Γ(D, O†) = K⟨X⟩† = {f ∈ K⟨X⟩ : f extends to some disc of radius ρ > 1}.

nodes.title: Relative compactness, partially proper and proper morphisms, and Stein spaces for dagger spaces
nodes.statement: Let f : X = Sp(A) → Y = Sp(B) be a morphism of affinoid K-dagger spaces and U ⊆ X an affinoid subdomain. Write U ⊂⊂_Y X if there are a surjection τ : B⟨X_1..X_r⟩† → A and ε ∈ Γ*, ε < 1, with U ⊆ Sp(A⟨ε^{-1}τ(X_1), …, ε^{-1}τ(X_r)⟩†). A morphism f : X → Y of dagger spaces is partially proper if it is separated and there are admissible affinoid coverings Y = ⋃ Y_i and f^{-1}(Y_i) = ⋃ X_{ij} such that each X_{ij} satisfies X_{ij} ⊂⊂_{Y_i} X̃_{ij} for some admissible open affinoid X̃_{ij} ⊆ f^{-1}(Y_i); f is proper if it is quasi-compact and partially proper. A dagger space X is a Stein space if it has an admissible affinoid covering X = ⋃_{i∈ℕ} U_i with U_i ⊂† U_{i+1} for all i (a Stein covering). The same definitions apply to rigid spaces, where they agree with Huber's partial properness (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/partially-proper-morphism).
hypotheses: f a morphism of K-dagger spaces
proofSteps: If f is partially proper then so is f' (Grosse-Klönne 2.25): the defining data (affinoid coverings, surjections τ, radii ε) complete to rigid data, since sup norms of the τ(X_i) on U are computed on the common points of Sp(A) and Sp(Â) (F1/dagger-completion-comparison). The converse — f' partially proper ⇒ f partially proper, used by the API item isPartiallyProper_iff_toRigid and implicitly in Grosse-Klönne 2.27 — is NOT stated by Grosse-Klönne and is not formal: the rigid data involve rigid affinoids and Tate-algebra surjections, which must be replaced by dagger affinoids U ⊂⊂ X̃ inside them (fringe neighbourhoods, F1/strict-neighbourhood, and approximation of the generators τ(X_i) by overconvergent functions, using that the condition |τ(X_i)| ≤ ε < 1 on U is open). It needs its own proof.

Stability: Stein spaces and spaces without boundary are partially proper; compositions of partially proper rigid morphisms are partially proper (Huber); analytifications of finite type schemes are partially proper; if f is partially proper, so is f' (GK 2.25).
Separatedness: defined as for rigid spaces through the diagonal (closed immersion), F1/dagger-coherent-module and AdicSpacesPartII:R0/separated-morphism.
acceptance: The open unit disc D^0 = ⋃ Sp(K⟨ε^{-1}X⟩†) is a Stein space; the closed dagger disc D is not partially proper over Sp(K).

nodes.title: The comparison functor from dagger spaces to rigid spaces
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K). The functor (·)' : (X, O†_X) ↦ X from K-dagger spaces to the quasi-separated rigid-analytic spaces of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytic-space, with the natural inclusion ν : O†_X ⊆ O_{X'} of structure sheaves, is faithful and satisfies: (1) Sp(A)' = Sp(Â) for every dagger algebra A (whose adic space is Spa(Â, Â°)); (2) X is connected (resp. normal, reduced, regular) iff X' is; (3) X and X' have the same opens and coverings (the same underlying G-topological space) and ν is an isomorphism on local rings at classical points; (4) a morphism ρ : X → Y is a closed immersion (resp. open immersion, locally closed immersion, isomorphism, quasi-compact, separated) iff ρ' is; (5) if ρ is finite, so is ρ'; (6) if Y is a quasialgebraic rigid space (admissibly covered by opens of analytifications of affine finite type K-schemes; e.g. Y smooth), there are an admissible affinoid covering Y = ⋃ V_i and affinoid dagger spaces U_i with U_i' ≅ V_i, and U_i is unique up to (non-canonical) isomorphism. On coherent modules, F ↦ F' (with F' = O_{X'} ⊗ (F(X) ⊗_A Â) on X = Sp(A), glued) is a faithful exact functor coh(O†_X) → coh(O_{X'}) with a natural injection of underlying abelian sheaves F → F'.
hypotheses: K complete, nontrivially and nonarchimedeanly valued
dagger and rigid spaces quasi-separated
in (6): Y quasialgebraic
proofSteps: (1),(3) hold by construction (F1/dagger-space: a dagger space is a rigid space with a subsheaf O†); on local rings, F1/dagger-affinoid-subdomain-completion (b). Faithfulness: a morphism of dagger spaces is a morphism of the underlying rigid spaces (Vezzani Remark 2.2).

(2): affinoid-locally from F1/dagger-completion-comparison (3) (reduced, normal, regular) and, for connectedness, from the absence of nontrivial idempotents: an idempotent of Â is integral over A, hence lies in A_red by F1/dagger-domain-and-integral-closure (1); globally by (3). Note that the implications 'X reduced (normal) ⇒ X' reduced (normal)' go through the ascent part of F1/dagger-completion-comparison (3), which depends on excellence (proposed node F1/dagger-algebra-excellent, char K = 0), and that F1/dagger-domain-and-integral-closure (1) carries the approximation hypothesis char K = 0 or [K : K^p] < ∞.

(4): immersions are stalk conditions (F1/dagger-affinoid-subdomain-completion (b)); closed immersions via coherent ideals (F1/dagger-coherent-module) and F1/dagger-finite-morphism-comparison (a); quasi-compactness and separatedness are topological or diagonal conditions, identical by (3) and (4) for the diagonal.
(5): F1/dagger-finite-morphism-comparison (b).

(6): if Y is quasialgebraic, Y has an admissible affinoid covering by V_i ≅ Sp(K⟨X_1..X_{n_i}⟩/(f_{i1}..f_{ir_i})) with polynomials f_{ij} (GK 2.18: via BGR 7.3.5/1, 7.2.3/3, 7.2.4/1, not read — gap); take U_i = Sp(K⟨X⟩†/(f_{ij})), whose completion is V_i. Smooth rigid spaces are quasialgebraic (de Jong–van der Put 3.4.1; Elkik, Théorème 7; not read — gap). Uniqueness: two dagger algebras with isomorphic completions are isomorphic (F1/dagger-approximation (2), under its hypothesis char K = 0 or [K : K^p] < ∞; Grosse-Klönne 2.19(6) itself asserts only existence, uniqueness is stated in the introduction of GK2000 and in §0 of GK2002 for smooth Y).

Coherent modules: F1/dagger-coherent-module (compatibility item) for affinoids; gluing because the local constructions are compatible with restriction (completion of rational localisations, F1/dagger-rational-localisation); faithful and exact because A → Â is faithfully flat (F1/dagger-completion-comparison) and coherent sheaves on rigid affinoids are determined by finite Â-modules (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid).
acceptance: The dagger closed disc D and its completion: D' is the rigid closed disc, Γ(D, O†) = K⟨X⟩† ⊊ K⟨X⟩ = Γ(D', O).
(6) for Y = the rigid closed disc: V = Y, U = Sp(K⟨X⟩†); for Y a smooth affinoid curve with good reduction, U = Sp(S† ⊗ K) for a smooth lift S.
Non-example: (·)' is not full on affinoids: the automorphism X ↦ X + a of the rigid disc with a ∈ K⟨X⟩ ∖ K⟨X⟩†, |a| < 1, does not preserve O† (it maps X to an element of T_1 ∖ W_1).

nodes.title: On partially proper dagger spaces coherent modules are those of the associated rigid space
nodes.statement: Let X be a partially proper K-dagger space. Then the functor (·)' : coh(O†_X) → coh(O_{X'}) of F1/dagger-to-rigid-functor is an equivalence of categories, and Γ(X, M) = Γ(X', M') for every coherent O†_X-module M.
hypotheses: X partially proper (F1/dagger-partially-proper), quasi-separated
proofSteps: Stein case: let X = ⋃_{i∈ℕ} U_i be a Stein covering (U_i ⊂† U_{i+1}) and G coherent on X'. For each i, the formula of F1/overconvergent-sections-formula (with Y = U_{i+1}') defines a finite O(U_i)-module F(U_i) of sections extending to strict neighbourhoods of U_i' in U_{i+1}', hence a coherent O_X|_{U_i}-module; these glue to F with F' = G, and F(X) = G(X') by the same formula. Morphisms: g : F' → G' induces maps on all strict neighbourhoods U_{i,ρ} of U_i in U_{i+1}, hence O(U_i)-linear F(U_i) → G(U_i), which glue.

General case: X has an admissible covering X = ⋃_j S_j with all S_j and all finite intersections Stein: choose an affinoid covering X = ⋃ V_j with V_j ⊂† Z_j for admissible open affinoids Z_j ⊆ X (partial properness), let S_j be the interior of Z_j (Z_j ∩ (D^0)^m for a closed immersion Z_j → D^m); by separatedness finite intersections of the S_j admit closed immersions into open polydiscs and are Stein. Glue the Stein case (sheaf property on both sides).
acceptance: X = D^0 the open unit disc: coherent O†_{D^0}-modules are exactly the coherent modules of the rigid open disc, and Γ(D^0, O†) = Γ(D^0', O) = series converging on the open unit disc.
Non-example: for the closed disc D (not partially proper), Γ(D, O†) = K⟨X⟩† ≠ K⟨X⟩ = Γ(D', O).

nodes.title: Partially proper dagger spaces are equivalent to partially proper rigid spaces
nodes.statement: The functor (·)' of F1/dagger-to-rigid-functor restricts to an equivalence between the category of partially proper K-dagger spaces and the category of partially proper rigid spaces over K. In particular every partially proper rigid space (e.g. every rigid space without boundary, every Stein space, the analytification of every finite type K-scheme) carries a dagger structure, unique up to unique isomorphism.
hypotheses: partial properness over Sp(K) (F1/dagger-partially-proper)
proofSteps: Essential surjectivity: for a partially proper rigid space Z (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytic-space), define a sheaf R of K-algebras on Z whose value on an open affinoid U_1 ⊆ Z admitting U_1 ⊂† U_2 ⊆ Z is the dagger algebra of sections extending to strict neighbourhoods of U_1 in U_2 (F1/overconvergent-sections-formula), with completion O_Z(U_1); such U_1 cover Z by partial properness, and the construction of F1/partially-proper-coherent-equivalence glues R. The resulting dagger space (Z, R) must itself be partially proper (so that it lies in the source category), and uniqueness of the dagger structure among all dagger spaces with underlying rigid space Z also needs that a dagger space X with X' partially proper is partially proper: this is the converse direction flagged in F1/dagger-partially-proper, which Grosse-Klönne uses without statement and which must be proved there.

Fullness: let X, Y be partially proper dagger spaces and g : X' → Y' a morphism. Choose opens U_i^{δ_i} = Sp(T_{n_i}(δ_i)/I_i) of Y' with (U_i^1)_i an admissible covering; put V_i = g^{-1}(U_i^1) (open dagger subspaces of X) and W_i the affinoid dagger subspaces with W_i' = U_i^1. Then O_Y(W_i) = colim_{δ→1} O_{Y'}(U_i^δ) → colim_{δ→1} O_{X'}(g^{-1}(U_i^δ)), and since g^{-1}(interior of U_i^δ) is partially proper (g is partially proper, compositions of partially proper morphisms are partially proper), O_X(g^{-1}(U_i^{δ,0})) ≅ O_{X'}(g^{-1}(U_i^{δ,0})) (F1/partially-proper-coherent-equivalence), giving compatible O_Y(W_i) → O_X(V_i), i.e. morphisms V_i → W_i lifting g.
Faithfulness is F1/dagger-to-rigid-functor.
acceptance: The rigid open unit disc and the rigid affine line A^{1,an} have unique dagger structures, the open dagger disc D^0 and the dagger affine line.
Non-example: the rigid closed disc is not partially proper and its dagger structures are only unique up to non-canonical isomorphism (F1/dagger-approximation).

nodes.title: Coherent cohomology of partially proper dagger spaces equals that of the associated rigid space
nodes.statement: Let X be a partially proper K-dagger space and F a coherent O†_X-module. Then H^i(X, F) = H^i(X', F') for all i ≥ 0. If X is a Stein space, these groups vanish for i > 0.
hypotheses: X partially proper, quasi-separated
F coherent
proofSteps: Stein case: let X = ⋃_{i∈ℕ} U_i be a Stein covering. It consists of affinoids, so it is F-acyclic (F1/dagger-coherent-theorem-b) and induces the F'-acyclic covering X' = ⋃ U_i'. For i = 0 use F1/overconvergent-sections-formula; for degrees ≥ 2 the Čech complexes of nested acyclic coverings indexed by ℕ vanish (lim^1-type argument).

H^1 in the Stein case: H^1(X', F') = 0 by Kiehl's Theorem B for quasi-Stein spaces (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/quasi-stein-theorems-a-b). Given a cocycle (g_i) ∈ ∏ F(U_i), choose affinoids V_i with U_i' ⊂† V_i ⊆ U_{i+1}' and g_i' ∈ F'(V_i) inducing g_i; the cocycle (g_i') for the covering (V_i) is a coboundary, g_i' = f_{i+1}' − f_i', and the f_i' induce f_i ∈ F(U_i) (F1/overconvergent-sections-formula) showing (g_i) is a coboundary.

General case: Čech spectral sequence for an admissible covering X = ⋃ W_j by Stein spaces with Stein finite intersections (as in F1/partially-proper-coherent-equivalence), comparing term by term via the Stein case and F1/partially-proper-coherent-equivalence.
acceptance: X = D^0 the open unit disc: H^i(D^0, O†) = H^i(D^0', O) = 0 for i > 0.

nodes.title: Dagger analytification of schemes of finite type
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K) and X a K-scheme of finite type. Its dagger analytification X^† is the partially proper K-dagger space with (X^†)' = X^an, the rigid analytification (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytification), which exists and is unique up to unique isomorphism by F1/partially-proper-dagger-rigid-equivalence because X^an is partially proper. X ↦ X^† is a functor, compatible with open and closed immersions and fibre products; for X affine with presentation K[X_1..X_n]/(f), X^† = ⋃_{ρ ∈ Γ*} Sp(K⟨ρ^{-1}X⟩†/(f)). For X proper, coherent cohomology satisfies GAGA: H^i(X, F) ≅ H^i(X^†, F^†) for coherent F.
hypotheses: X of finite type over K
proofSteps: Existence and uniqueness: X^an is partially proper (Grosse-Klönne 2.25; Huber), so F1/partially-proper-dagger-rigid-equivalence gives the dagger space; functoriality from fullness of that equivalence on partially proper spaces (morphisms of finite type schemes analytify to partially proper morphisms).
Explicit affine description: the dagger polydiscs Sp(K⟨ρ^{-1}X⟩†) exhaust A^{n,†} (each is ⊂† the next), and closed subspaces are cut out by the polynomials f.
GAGA: for X proper, H^i(X^†, F^†) = H^i(X^an, F^an) (F1/dagger-coherent-cohomology-comparison) = H^i(X, F) (rigid GAGA, AdicSpacesPartII:R3/proper-gaga).
acceptance: (A^1)^† = ⋃_ρ Sp(K⟨ρ^{-1}X⟩†) with Γ = entire power series, the same as for A^{1,an}.

nodes.title: Identity principle on connected smooth dagger spaces
nodes.statement: Let X be a connected smooth K-dagger space (or more generally X' connected and normal) and f ∈ O†_X(X). If f vanishes on a nonempty open subset U ⊆ X, then f = 0; the same holds for sections of a locally free O†_X-module of finite rank, in particular for 1-forms.
hypotheses: X connected and smooth (or X' connected and normal)
U ⊆ X nonempty open
proofSteps: X connected and normal iff X' is (F1/dagger-to-rigid-functor (2)); O†_X(X) ⊆ O_{X'}(X') compatibly with restriction (ν injective), so it suffices to prove the statement for f ∈ O_{X'}(X').

Rigid identity principle (Conrad, Irreducible components of rigid spaces, Lemma 2.1.4): in a connected normal rigid space the only analytic subset containing a nonempty admissible open is the whole space. Apply it to the zero locus Z = V(f): Z ⊇ U, so Z = X' and f vanishes at every point; X' is reduced (normal), so f = 0. (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-identity-principle (i), (iii).)

Locally free modules: a locally free O†_X-module of finite rank gives a locally free O_{X'}-module of the same rank with O†-sections embedded in its sections (ν injective), and AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-identity-principle (iii) applies.
acceptance: On the Coleman wide opens W_r (connected), an element of A+(Y) vanishing on one residue disc of the tube vanishes identically.

nodes.title: The module of (universally finite) differentials Ω^1_A of a dagger algebra and the exterior derivative
nodes.statement: Let A be a K-dagger algebra (K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K)). The module of differentials of A is a finite A-module Ω^1_A = Ω^1_{A/K} with a K-derivation d : A → Ω^1_A that is universal among K-derivations of A into finite A-modules: every K-derivation D : A → M, M finite, is u ∘ d for a unique A-linear u. Explicitly, for a presentation A = W_n/(f_1, …, f_r): Ω^1_A = (⊕_i A dX_i) / (Σ_j (∂f_k/∂X_j) dX_j)_k with d g = Σ_i (∂g/∂X_i) dX_i. Equivalently Ω^1_A = J/J^2 for J the kernel of the multiplication A ⊗†_K A → A (Kedlaya's module of continuous differentials). Put Ω^i_A = ⋀^i_A Ω^1_A with d extended by d(a db_1 ∧ … ∧ db_i) = da ∧ db_1 ∧ … ∧ db_i. These sheafify to coherent O†_X-modules Ω^i_X on every dagger space X, with (Ω^i_X)' = Ω^i_{X'}. For a finitely generated algebra S over a complete DVR O_K the same construction gives Ω^1_{S†/O_K} (van der Put's D^1), with Ω^1_{S†/O_K} ⊗ K = Ω^1_{S†⊗K}.
hypotheses: A a K-dagger algebra
proofSteps: W_n: ∂/∂X_i preserves W_n (Dagger.pderiv_mem_washnitzerAlgebra, F1/overconvergent-tate-algebra), so d g = Σ ∂_i g dX_i defines a derivation into the free module ⊕ W_n dX_i.

Universality for W_n: given D : W_n → M with M finite, δ := D − Σ (∂_i ·) D(X_i) is a derivation vanishing on polynomials. For a maximal ideal m (a point x) and k ≥ 1, g − T_k(g) ∈ m^k where T_k is a polynomial Taylor truncation at x, so δ(g) ∈ m^{k−1}M; hence δ(g) ∈ ⋂_{m,k} m^k M = 0 (Krull intersection for the finite module M over the noetherian W_n, F1/overconvergent-tate-algebra-properties).
Quotients: for A = W_n/I, Ω^1_A = Ω^1_{W_n} ⊗ A/(dI) satisfies the universal property (derivations of A are derivations of W_n killing I). Independence of the presentation: universality.
J/J^2 description: J/J^2 for A ⊗† A (F1/dagger-tensor-product) is finite, generated by 1 ⊗ X_i − X_i ⊗ 1, and is universal by the same argument (Kedlaya 3.1.2).
Sheafification: Ω^1_{A⟨f/g⟩†} = Ω^1_A ⊗_A A⟨f/g⟩† (universal property and F1/dagger-rational-localisation), so U ↦ Ω^1_{O(U)} is Ω^1_A ⊗ O_X, coherent (F1/dagger-coherent-module).

Completion: Ω^1_A ⊗_A Â is the module of continuous differentials of the affinoid Â (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/continuous-differentials for complete f-adic rings topologically of finite type over K), giving (Ω^i_X)' = Ω^i_{X'}; on the rigid space X' these modules glue to the coherent sheaf Ωⁱ of AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheaf-of-continuous-differentials (API affinoidIso), which is the sheaf (Ωⁱ_X)'.

nodes.title: Smooth dagger spaces
nodes.statement: A K-dagger space X (K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K)) is smooth if its associated rigid space X' (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytic-space) is smooth over K, i.e. its adic space (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor) is smooth over Spa(K, O_K) in the sense of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-morphism. Equivalently: for every affinoid Sp(A) ⊆ X, A is regular and Ω^1_A is projective of rank equal to the local dimension; equivalently X is locally étale over a dagger polydisc. X has pure dimension n if dim O_{X,x} = n at every point; then ω_X := Ω^n_X.
hypotheses: X a K-dagger space
proofSteps: Equivalence of the definitions: smoothness of X' is affinoid-local and is the Jacobian condition on Â; Ω^1_A ⊗ Â = Ω^1_Â (F1/dagger-differentials) and A regular iff Â regular (F1/dagger-completion-comparison (3)); faithful flatness of A → Â transfers projectivity and rank (Grosse-Klönne, Finiteness 1.2).

Local étaleness over a dagger polydisc: Vezzani Proposition 3.6 (from the rigid statement AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-local-structure and F1/dagger-approximation to lift the étale coordinates to overconvergent functions).
acceptance: Every open of a dagger polydisc, dagger annuli and dagger analytifications of smooth K-schemes are smooth.

nodes.title: The overconvergent de Rham complex of a smooth dagger space, with coefficients in a module with integrable connection
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth K-dagger space (K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K)). The de Rham complex Ω^•_X = (Ω^0_X → Ω^1_X → Ω^2_X → …) is the complex of coherent locally free O†_X-modules Ω^i_X = ⋀^i Ω^1_X with the K-linear exterior derivative d (F1/dagger-differentials). More generally, for a coherent O†_X-module E with an integrable connection ∇ : E → E ⊗ Ω^1_X (K-linear, ∇(fe) = f∇e + e ⊗ df, ∇_1 ∘ ∇ = 0), DR(E) = E ⊗ Ω^•_X with differentials ∇_i. The de Rham cohomology is the hypercohomology H^i_dR(X, E) := H^i(X, DR(E)) on the site of X, and H^i_dR(X) := H^i_dR(X, O†_X). For X = Sp(A) affinoid, H^i_dR(X, E) = H^i(Γ(X, E) ⊗_A Ω^•_A). For X' the associated rigid space, (Ω^i_X)' = Ω^i_{X'} and DR(E)' = DR(E'); but in general H^i_dR(X) ≠ H^i_dR(X') (see the tests).
hypotheses: X smooth
E coherent with integrable connection
proofSteps: d ∘ d = 0 and the graded Leibniz rule on Ω^•_A: F1/dagger-differentials (universal derivation extended to the exterior algebra, Mathlib ExteriorAlgebra.exteriorPower).
Sheaf level: compatibility with rational localisation (Dagger.Omega.rationalLocalization) glues Ω^•_A into Ω^•_X; locally free by F1/dagger-smooth-space.
Connections: ∇_i(e ⊗ ω) = ∇e ∧ ω + e ⊗ dω is well defined by the Leibniz rule; integrability ∇_1 ∘ ∇ = 0 gives ∇_{i+1} ∘ ∇_i = 0.
Affinoid formula: every term E ⊗ Ω^i_X is coherent, so acyclic on affinoids (F1/dagger-coherent-theorem-b); the hypercohomology spectral sequence degenerates to the cohomology of global sections.
Comparison of complexes with X': F1/dagger-to-rigid-functor applied to Ω^i_X (Dagger.Omega.completion).
acceptance: For char K = 0: H^0_dR(D) = K and H^1_dR(D) = 0 for the closed dagger disc D; H^1_dR of the dagger annulus |X| = 1 is K·dX/X. (In characteristic p, H^0_dR(D) ⊇ K⟨X^p⟩† and H^1_dR(D) ∋ [X^{p−1}dX] ≠ 0.)

F1 supplies the overconvergent de Rham and logarithmic boundary complexes. RD.4 supplies the ordinary dagger-tube/rigid comparison for each smooth quasi-projective boundary stratum (HLTT Lemma 6.8, with its functoriality). AG2.4 separately constructs the boundary-stratum spectral sequence of HLTT Lemma 6.21, with these rigid groups on E₁ and cuspidal boundary-support cohomology as abutment; it does not identify that whole abutment directly with ordinary rigid cohomology by Lemma 6.8. It imports RD.5 finiteness and RD.6 weights on the strata and passes them through the spectral sequence, as in Corollaries 6.22 and 6.24. Generic log/compact-support comparison adapters need separate proofs.

nodes.title: De Rham cohomology of dagger polyannuli and the relative Poincaré lemma
nodes.statement: Let K be a field of characteristic 0 complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value and Γ* = √|K^×|. (a) Let 0 ≤ r ≤ n and μ, γ_i (i ≤ r), δ_i (i ≤ n) in Γ* with γ_i ≤ δ_i and Π_{i≤r} δ_i ≥ μ, and let V ⊆ A^{n,†} be the affinoid dagger space {x : Π_{i≤r}|x_i| ≥ μ, |x_i| ≤ δ_i for all i, |x_i| ≥ γ_i for i ≤ r}. Then H^q_dR(V) has as K-basis the classes of dX_{i_1}/X_{i_1} ∧ … ∧ dX_{i_q}/X_{i_q}, 1 ≤ i_1 < … < i_q ≤ r; in particular for r = 0 (a closed dagger polydisc) H^0_dR(V) = K and H^q_dR(V) = 0 for q > 0. For every smooth dagger space X the Künneth maps ⊕_{q_1+q_2=q} H^{q_1}_dR(X) ⊗_K H^{q_2}_dR(V) → H^q_dR(X × V) are bijective. (b) The same holds, both as a dagger space and as a rigid space, for the open version V° = {x : Π_{i≤r}|x_i| > μ, |x_i| < δ_i for all i, |x_i| > γ_i for i ≤ r} under the hypotheses γ_i < δ_i (i ≤ r) and Π_{i≤r} δ_i > μ (Grosse-Klönne prints Π δ_i < μ, which would make V° empty; see sourceIssues).
hypotheses: char K = 0 (Grosse-Klönne §2 assumes K = Frac(R) for a complete discrete valuation ring R of mixed characteristic (0, p); the proof uses only char K = 0, through the polynomial growth of |1/m|, so the node's generalisation to any char-0 K is justified by the same proof)
radii in Γ*
proofSteps: (i) Division by exponents preserves overconvergence: for X = Sp(B) affinoid and a = Σ_v θ_v X^v ∈ O(X × V) (θ_v ∈ B, θ_v = 0 if v_j < 0 for some j > r), the series b = Σ_{v_l ≠ 0} v_l^{-1} θ_v X^v also lies in O(X × V): present O(X × V) as a quotient of D = B ⊗†_K K⟨X, Y, Z⟩† (Y_i ↦ (γ_i^{-1}X_i)^{-1}, Z ↦ (μ^{-1}Π X_i)^{-1}); D is the colimit of completed tensor products O(X_ε) ⊗̂ K⟨δ^{-1}·⟩ over strict neighbourhoods X_ε of X' and δ > 1 (F1/dagger-tensor-product, F1/strict-neighbourhood), and dividing the coefficient of a monomial by the nonzero integer m = w_l − w_{l+n} − w_{n+r+1} (the exponent of X_l in its image) maps the δ-level to every δ_1 < δ, because |1/m| ≤ max(1, |m|^{-1}) grows at most polynomially in |m| ≤ |w| (char K = 0: |1/m| = 1 if the residue characteristic is 0, and |1/m| = |p|^{-v_p(m)} ≤ m^c otherwise).

(iii) This gives the inverse of the Künneth map and the description of H^q_dR(V) (X = Sp K).

(b) Dagger case: exhaust V° by affinoid dagger spaces of type (a) and pass to the limit (V° is the increasing union of affinoid dagger spaces V_n of type (a) with radii tending to the open bounds; H^q_dR(X × V°) sits in the Milnor sequence 0 → lim^1 H^{q−1}_dR(X × V_n) → H^q_dR(X × V°) → lim H^q_dR(X × V_n) → 0, and by (a) the transition maps are isomorphisms (same basis dX_I/X_I, Künneth), so lim^1 = 0 and the limit is the answer). nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth partially proper K-dagger space. Then the natural map H^i_dR(X) → H^i_dR(X') is an isomorphism for all i. The partial properness hypothesis cannot be dropped: for the closed unit disc, H^1_dR(D) = 0 (char K = 0) while H^1_dR(D') is infinite-dimensional, although D and D' have the same underlying points and G-topology.

nodes.title: De Rham cohomology of a smooth dagger space depends only on its rigid space
nodes.statement: Let K be a field of characteristic 0 complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value. Let X_1, X_2 be smooth K-dagger spaces and φ : X_1' → X_2' an isomorphism of the associated rigid spaces. Then φ induces an isomorphism φ† : H^*_dR(X_2) → H^*_dR(X_1). (Grosse-Klönne states without proof in the source that φ ↦ φ† is compatible with composition; that compatibility is not part of this node.)
hypotheses: char K = 0
X_1, X_2 smooth
φ an isomorphism of rigid spaces (not assumed to preserve O†)
proofSteps: Put X = X_1 × X_2, X' = X_1' × X_2', Δ = image of (id, φ) : X_1' → X', a Zariski-closed subspace isomorphic to X_1'. The projections induce a_1 : H_dR(X_1) → H^*(X, colim_V j_{V*}Ω^•_V) ← H_dR(X_2) : a_2, V over opens of X with Δ ⊆ V'; it suffices that a_1, a_2 are isomorphisms, and φ† := a_1^{-1} ∘ a_2.

Local question: X_1, X_2 affinoid connected, t_1..t_m ∈ O(X_1) with dt_i a basis of Ω^1, and a rigid tubular neighbourhood U' ≅ Sp(K⟨δ^{-1}Z⟩) × Δ with Z_i ↦ t_i ⊗ 1 − 1 ⊗ (φ^*)^{-1}(t_i) (Kiehl, de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties over valued fields, 1.18 — not read, gap). The U_ε' (ε ≤ δ) are Weierstrass domains, hence so are dagger U_ε, and they are cofinal among the V.

Approximate φ by an isomorphism σ : X_1 → X_2 of dagger spaces with (id, σ)(X_1) ⊆ U_{ε/2} (F1/dagger-approximation (2)), and approximate the tubular coordinates by overconvergent ones; the resulting map O(X_1) ⊗†_K K⟨ε^{-1}Z⟩† → O(U_ε) is an isomorphism (its completion is close to an isomorphism, F1/dagger-finite-morphism-comparison / F1/dagger-approximation), so U_ε ≅ Sp(K⟨ε^{-1}Z⟩†) × X_1 with (id, σ) the zero section.

By F1/dagger-polyannulus-de-rham-cohomology (r = 0 Künneth), H_dR(U_ε) → H_dR(X_1) induced by the zero section is an isomorphism, so b_{1,ε} : H_dR(X_1) → H_dR(U_ε) is bijective; symmetrically b_{2,ε}; cohomology commutes with the colimit over V because X is quasi-compact.
acceptance: X_1 = X_2 = D the closed dagger disc and φ the rigid automorphism X ↦ X + a with a ∈ K⟨X⟩ ∖ K⟨X⟩†, |a| < 1: φ does not preserve O†, yet φ† : H_dR(D) → H_dR(D) exists (both are K in degree 0).

nodes.title: Strictness and closed image of de Rham differentials on smooth affinoid and Stein dagger spaces
nodes.statement: Let K be discretely valued of characteristic 0; in the affinoid case let K moreover be the fraction field of a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic (0, p), which is what the finiteness theorem F1/dagger-de-rham-finiteness-and-base-change (Grosse-Klönne's [13]) needs — the footnote hypothesis 'discretely valued and of characteristic 0' does not cover residue characteristic 0. Let X be a smooth affinoid K-dagger space, or a smooth Stein K-dagger space whose de Rham cohomology groups are finite-dimensional (for example the interior X_ρ ∩ {|x_i| < ρ} of a fringe stage of a smooth affinoid dagger space, by F1/dagger-de-rham-finiteness-and-base-change). Then every differential d^i : Ω^i_X(X) → Ω^{i+1}_X(X) is strict and has closed image, for the Fréchet topology of global sections of a Stein space, resp. the fringe topology (F1/fringe-topology) of a finite module over a dagger algebra.
hypotheses: K discretely valued of characteristic 0; for the affinoid case K = Frac of a complete DVR of mixed characteristic (0, p) (finiteness of de Rham cohomology of the fringe interiors)
X smooth and Stein, or smooth and affinoid
proofSteps: Closed image implies strictness (open mapping theorem for Fréchet spaces over K) and conversely closedness follows from strictness by completeness of Ω^i_X(X) (fringe topology complete for spherically complete, in particular discretely valued, K: F1/fringe-topology).

Stein case: by Lütkebohmert (Steinsche Räume, not read — gap) there is a closed immersion X → A^n, and Ω^j_{A^n}(A^n) → Ω^j_X(X) are strict surjections commuting with d. Grosse-Klönne's printed argument stops at this reduction; what closes it is finiteness: H^{i+1}_dR(X) is finite-dimensional (hypothesis; for interiors of fringe stages it is F1/dagger-de-rham-finiteness-and-base-change, whose hypotheses — K discretely valued of characteristic 0 — are the ones added in the arXiv version), so im d^i has finite codimension in the closed subspace ker d^{i+1}, and a finite-codimensional image of a continuous linear map of Fréchet spaces is closed.

Affinoid case: do not reduce to A = W_n by a closed immersion — that reduction has exactly the gap recorded for the Stein case in packet sourceIssue E31 (the image of the closed subspace im d under a strict surjection need not be closed). Instead choose a fringe presentation whose stages X_ρ = Sp(T_n(ρ)/I) are smooth (possible for ρ close to 1, as in the proof of GK2002 Lemma 0.1) and let X_ρ° = X_ρ ∩ {|x_i| < ρ} be their interiors: smooth Stein spaces with finite-dimensional de Rham cohomology (F1/dagger-de-rham-finiteness-and-base-change, T = X_ρ − U with U the quasi-compact union of the Laurent domains {|x_i| ≥ ρ}). The Stein case gives strictness with closed image on each Ω^•(X_ρ°) with its Fréchet topology; the fringe topology on Ω^j_A = colim_ρ Ω^j(X_ρ°) is the finest locally convex topology making all these maps continuous (GK 4.7), and GK concludes from this. (That strictness passes to this inductive limit is asserted by Grosse-Klönne without further argument; it uses that the limit is of compact type, F1/fringe-topology.)
acceptance: For X = Sp(W_1): d : W_1 → W_1 dX is surjective (F1/dagger-polyannulus-de-rham-cohomology), in particular strict with closed image; for the rigid disc, d : K⟨X⟩ → K⟨X⟩dX has non-closed image (its closure contains Σ p^n X^{p^n−1}dX).

nodes.title: De Rham cohomology with supports in the complement of an admissible open
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth K-dagger (or rigid) space and j : U → X the inclusion of an admissible open with complement Y = X − U (a closed subset, not given a space structure). For a sheaf F on X let Γ_Y(F) = ker(F → j_*j^{-1}F) and RΓ_Y its right derived functor; for a complex such as Ω^•_X define H^i_Y(X, Ω^•_X) := H^i(X, RΓ_Y Ω^•_X) (and likewise H^i_Y(X, F) for coherent F). There is a distinguished triangle RΓ_Y(X, Ω^•) → RΓ(X, Ω^•) → RΓ(U, Ω^•) →, a Mayer–Vietoris triangle RΓ_{Y∩Y'} → RΓ_Y ⊕ RΓ_{Y'} → RΓ_{Y∪Y'} → when U ∪ U' is an admissible covering of an admissible open, and for Z ⊆ Y closed a triangle RΓ_Z → RΓ_Y → Rj'_*RΓ_{Y−Z}j'^{-1} → with j' : X − Z → X.

U ⊆ X admissible open, Y = X − U
proofSteps: Γ_Y is left exact; take injective resolutions (sheaves of K-vector spaces on the site of X) to define RΓ_Y and hypercohomology.
Localisation triangle: 0 → Γ_Y(I) → I → j_*j^{-1}I → 0 is exact for injective I (flasque); j_*j^{-1}I computes RΓ(U, ·).
Mayer–Vietoris and the Z ⊆ Y triangle: for injective I, 0 → Γ_Z I → Γ_Y I → j'_*Γ_{Y−Z} j'^{-1} I → 0 is exact (Grosse-Klönne, Finiteness, proof of 1.16(b)); analogous four-term argument for Y, Y'.

nodes.title: Local cohomology of the de Rham complex along closed subspaces: algebraic versus topological supports, Gysin isomorphism and independence of the embedding
nodes.statement: Let K be of characteristic 0 (complete, nonarchimedean), X a smooth K-dagger space and Y → X a closed immersion with coherent ideal J. Let RΓ*_Y (E) = colim_n Hom_{O_X}(O_X/J^n, E) (algebraic local cohomology) and DR the de Rham functor on D_X-modules (Grosse-Klönne, Finiteness 1.5). Then: (a) the canonical map RΓ(X, DR(RΓ*_Y O_X)) → RΓ(X, DR(RΓ_Y O_X)) = RΓ_Y(X, Ω^•_X) is an isomorphism; (b) (Gysin) if Y is smooth of pure codimension d in X, H^i_Y(X, Ω^•_X) ≅ H^{i−2d}_dR(Y) for all i. (Part (c) of the previous version — independence of the embedding, GK2002 Corollary 1.12, and the resulting definition of h^dR_q, 1.13 — is moved to the proposed node F1/dagger-hdr-embedding-independence, because it rests on the trace of GK2002 Proposition 1.11, which itself uses (b).)
hypotheses: char K = 0
X smooth; Y → X closed immersion; in (b) Y smooth of pure codimension d
proofSteps: (a), rigid case: if Y is locally defined by one equation, j : X − Y → X is a quasi-Stein morphism, acyclic for coherent modules (Kiehl, AdicSpacesPartII:R3/quasi-stein-theorems-a-b), so DR(Rj_*O) = j_*Ω^•; Kiehl's comparison DR(O_X(*Y)) ≅ j_*Ω^•_{X−Y} (Kiehl, de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties over valued fields, Theorem 2.3 — not read, gap) gives (a) for such Y; general Y by induction on the number of local equations using Mayer–Vietoris (F1/de-rham-cohomology-with-supports).

(a), dagger case, Y smooth: cover X by affinoids U_i with U_i ≅ D^m × (U_i ∩ Y) (Y the zero section; Grosse-Klönne notes Kiehl's tubular neighbourhood theorem 1.18 holds in the dagger case by inspecting the proof — gap); shrink to D^m(ε) × Y, compactify D^m ⊂ P^m, and use the Gysin sequence of the partially proper dagger spaces {0}, P^m, P^m − {0} (rigid case plus F1/dagger-rigid-de-rham-comparison) and the Künneth formula of F1/dagger-polyannulus-de-rham-cohomology.

(a), dagger case, general Y: reduce to Y a hypersurface on an affinoid, then to a normal crossings divisor by F1/dagger-resolution-lemma, then to smooth Y via Mayer–Vietoris over the components (F1/de-rham-cohomology-with-supports).

(b): Proposition 1.10 of Grosse-Klönne, Finiteness: s_+RΓ*_Z O_Y ≅ RΓ*_Z O_X[d] for closed immersions Z → Y → X of smooth spaces, proved by identifying D_{X←Y} ⊗ O_Y with R^dΓ*_Y O_X = D_X/(x_1..x_d, δ_{d+1}..δ_n) in local coordinates; this uses the D-module formalism of Mebkhout and of Grosse-Klönne's thesis [11] (not public; recorded as a gap), then (a).

nodes.title: Trace on de Rham complexes for finite étale morphisms of smooth dagger spaces
nodes.statement: Let K be of characteristic 0 (complete, nonarchimedean) and f : X → Y a finite étale morphism of smooth K-dagger spaces with Y irreducible and every connected component of X surjecting onto Y. Then there are an integer l = deg f ≥ 1 and a morphism of complexes t : f_*Ω^•_X → Ω^•_Y with t ∘ f^* = l·id. In particular f^* : H^i_dR(Y) → H^i_dR(X) is injective for all i.
hypotheses: char K = 0
f finite étale
Y irreducible; components of X surject onto Y
proofSteps: Locally: for an admissible open connected U = Sp(A) ⊆ Y with f^{-1}(U) = ⊔_j Sp(B_j), B_j free of rank l_j over A, let t_j : B_j → A be the algebra trace (Mathlib Algebra.trace) and define f_*Ω^q_X(U) = ⊕_j Ω^q_{B_j} = ⊕_j Ω^q_A ⊗_A B_j → Ω^q_A by ω ⊗ b ↦ t_j(b)ω (étaleness gives Ω^q_{B_j} = Ω^q_A ⊗_A B_j, F1/dagger-differentials).
Compatibility with d: the same computation as for algebraic de Rham complexes (Hartshorne, On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties, p. 35) since d(t(b)) = t(db) for étale extensions.

Gluing: the local traces are compatible with restriction to smaller U (trace commutes with flat base change), and l = Σ_j l_j is independent of U because Y is irreducible (connected) and each component surjects.
Injectivity: t ∘ f^* = l is invertible in characteristic 0.
acceptance: The Kummer covering z ↦ z^N of the dagger annulus |z| = 1 (p ∤ N): l = N, and f^* is injective (in fact bijective) on H^1_dR = K·dz/z, multiplication by N in the basis dz/z.

nodes.title: De Rham cohomology of tubes in a strictly semistable formal scheme (Grosse-Klönne's Theorem C)
nodes.statement: Let R is a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic (0, p) with uniformiser π, K = Frac(R) and residue field k = R/π. Let 𝔛 be a strictly semistable formal R-scheme — a noetherian π-adic formal R-scheme with a Zariski covering by opens 𝔘_i admitting étale morphisms 𝔘_i → Spf(R⟨X_1..X_n⟩/(X_1⋯X_{r(i)} − π)) — with closed fibre 𝔛_k = ⋃_{i∈I} Y_i (irreducible components), Y_J = ⋂_{i∈J} Y_i. Let 𝔛^† be a K-dagger space whose rigid space is the generic fibre 𝔛_K, and for a subscheme T ⊆ 𝔛_k let ]T[^†_𝔛 be the open dagger subspace of 𝔛^† with rigid space the tube ]T[_𝔛 = sp^{-1}(T). Then for every nonempty J ⊆ I the restriction H^*_dR(]Y_J[^†) → H^*_dR(]Y_J − (Y_J ∩ ⋃_{i∈I−J} Y_i)[^†) is bijective.

𝔛 strictly semistable (locally étale over R⟨X⟩/(X_1⋯X_r − π))
proofSteps: Reduction to (∗)_0 (GK 2.4 (i)): filter by the number of removed components and use Mayer–Vietoris for the admissible coverings (F1/de-rham-cohomology-with-supports), replacing 𝔛 by open formal subschemes.

Reduction to the affine étale-local case 𝔛 = Spf(A) → Spf(R⟨X⟩/(X_1⋯X_r − π)) with f_i = φ^*(X_i) and V(f̄_i) irreducible (2.4 (ii)); exhaust ]Y_J[ by F_λ = {|f_j| ≤ λ, j ∈ J} and E_λ, F_{λ,β} as in 2.4 (iii); exactness of direct limits reduces to the maps (2) H_dR(F_λ) → H_dR(F_{λ,β}), equivalently (4) H_dR(S_{λ,β}) → H_dR(S_{λ,β} ∩ F_{λ,β}).

Tube structure (2.4 (v)): ]Y_I[_𝔛 ≅ Sp(D ⊗ K) × {x ∈ Sp(K⟨T⟩/(T_1⋯T_r − π)) : |T_i| < 1} for a π-adic formally smooth tft Spf(D), built from a section of Â/π → D̄ = A/(π, f) and a smooth lift of D̄ (Elkik; gap) — the tube of a semistable stratum (AdicSpacesPartII:R2/specialisation-map for tubes and generic fibres).

Dagger version (2.4 (vi)): by F1/dagger-de-rham-rigid-invariance replace the rigid isomorphism by one of dagger spaces with a smooth dagger algebra B; then (5) and (6)–(7) follow from the polyannulus computation and Künneth (F1/dagger-polyannulus-de-rham-cohomology).

nodes.title: De Rham cohomology of dagger spaces commutes with finite extensions of the base field
nodes.statement: Let K be complete, nonarchimedean of characteristic 0 and K ⊆ K_1 a finite extension. For a smooth K-dagger space X, X_1 = X ×_{Sp K} Sp K_1 is a smooth K_1-dagger space and H^i_dR(X_1/K_1) ≅ H^i_dR(X/K) ⊗_K K_1 for all i; in particular dim_K H^i_dR(X/K) = dim_{K_1} H^i_dR(X_1/K_1). Likewise dim_K H^i_Z(X, Ω^•) = dim_{K_1} H^i_{Z_1}(X_1, Ω^•) for closed subspaces Z, so h^dR_q(Z, K) = h^dR_q(Z_1, K_1) (h^dR_q as defined in F1/dagger-hdr-embedding-independence, whose hypothesis — K discretely valued of mixed characteristic — this last clause inherits).

nodes.title: Finiteness of the de Rham invariants h^dR_q of quasi-algebraic affinoid dagger spaces
nodes.statement: Let R be a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic (0, p) with uniformiser π, K = Frac(R) and residue field k = R/π. Let H = Sp(K⟨X_1..X_n⟩†/(f_1..f_r)) with f_j ∈ R[X_1..X_n] (an affinoid quasi-algebraic dagger space). Then h^dR_q(H) < ∞ for all q ≥ 0 (h^dR_q as in F1/dagger-hdr-embedding-independence).
hypotheses: R complete DVR of mixed characteristic
H affinoid, defined by polynomials with coefficients in R
proofSteps: Induction on m = dim H. Decompose V = Spec R[X]/(f) into irreducible components; Mayer–Vietoris for supports (F1/de-rham-cohomology-with-supports) and induction reduce to V integral with dim V_K = m; h^dR_q depends only on the reduced structure.

Choose an open immersion V → Y into a projective R-variety; by de Jong's alteration theorem (AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L5/de-jong-6-5-strictly-semistable-alteration: a finite extension R ⊂ R', an R'-variety X and a proper surjective f : X → Y, finite over a dense open, with (X, f^{-1}(Y_k)_red) strictly semistable) — pass to R' using F1/dagger-de-rham-finite-field-extension.

Stein-factorise f_K : X_K → X'_K → Y_K; choose closed T' ⊆ X'_K and S ⊆ Y_K of dimension < m with g_K an isomorphism outside T and X'_K − S' → Y_K − S finite étale; embed H → N and H_{X'} → M into smooth dagger spaces.

Long exact sequences with supports (F1/dagger-local-cohomology-comparison (a), (b)) and the induction hypothesis for H_S, H_{X',S'}, H_{X',T'}, H_{X,T} reduce to finiteness of H_dR(H − H_S), which injects into H_dR(H_{X'} − H_{X',S'}) by the finite étale trace (F1/dagger-finite-etale-trace), then (F1/dagger-proper-modification-sequence) to finiteness of H_dR(H_X).

H_X is an open dagger subspace whose rigid space is the generic fibre of an open formal subscheme of the π-adic completion of the strictly semistable X, so H_dR(H_X) is finite by F1/dagger-semistable-tube-finiteness.

nodes.title: Finiteness of de Rham cohomology of smooth quasi-compact dagger spaces (Grosse-Klönne's Theorem A), and base change to finite extensions
nodes.statement: Let R is a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic (0, p) with uniformiser π, K = Frac(R) and residue field k = R/π. Let X be a quasi-compact (quasi-separated) smooth K-dagger space, U ⊆ X a quasi-compact admissible open subset and Z → X a closed immersion. Then T = X − (U ∪ Z) has finite-dimensional de Rham cohomology: dim_K H^q_dR(T) < ∞ for all q. In particular (U = ∅) dim_K H^q_dR(X − Z) < ∞, and (Z = ∅) dim_K H^q_dR(X − U) < ∞; and for every finite extension K_1/K, H^q_dR(T_{K_1}/K_1) = H^q_dR(T/K) ⊗_K K_1.
hypotheses: R complete DVR of mixed characteristic (0, p) (K discretely valued of characteristic 0)
X quasi-compact, quasi-separated, smooth
U quasi-compact admissible open; Z → X closed immersion
finiteness of Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology (external, through F1/dagger-semistable-tube-finiteness)
proofSteps: Corollary 3.5 (U = ∅): reduce to X affinoid; by F1/dagger-resolution-lemma replace (X, Z) by (X̃, g^{-1}Z) with g^{-1}Z a normal crossings divisor with smooth components on an affinoid covering. Each W = X or W = an intersection of components is smooth affinoid, hence quasi-algebraic: its rigid space is defined by polynomials (Elkik, Théorème 7 — gap) and dagger structures on it are isomorphic (F1/dagger-approximation (2)); so H_W(X, Ω^•) is finite by F1/quasi-algebraic-affinoid-finiteness and F1/dagger-local-cohomology-comparison; repeated long exact sequences (F1/de-rham-cohomology-with-supports) give H_dR(X − Z) finite.

Theorem 3.6 (general U), induction on n = dim X proving (a_n) finiteness of H_dR(X − U) and (b_n) finiteness of H^q_{T}(Y − V, Ω^•) for dim T ≤ n: (b_{n−1}) ⇒ (a_n): reduce to U a rational subdomain of an affinoid connected X; choose an affine formal model 𝔛 (AdicSpacesPartII:R2/admissible-formal-scheme; Bosch–Lütkebohmert admissible blow-ups, AdicSpacesPartII:R2/admissible-blow-up) with X − U = ]Z[^† for a closed Z ⊆ 𝔛_k, defined by polynomials (Elkik); compactify, apply de Jong's theorem to (X̄, Ȳ ∪ X̄_k) (AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L5/de-jong-6-5-strictly-semistable-alteration), and reduce as in F1/quasi-algebraic-affinoid-finiteness (Stein factorisation, finite étale trace F1/dagger-finite-etale-trace, proper modification sequence F1/dagger-proper-modification-sequence) to finiteness of H_dR(]W_k[^†_𝔙) for the semistable model, which is F1/dagger-semistable-tube-finiteness after identifying intersections of tubes with tubes in strata (Grosse-Klönne, Finiteness Lemma 2.6: ]C[_ℜ × (D^0)^{|I|} ≅ ]C[_𝔙, via log smooth lifting — gap).

(a_n) + (b_{n−1}) ⇒ (b_n): resolve T to a normal crossings divisor (F1/dagger-resolution-lemma), reduce to smooth T via Mayer–Vietoris and to (a_n) via Gysin (F1/dagger-local-cohomology-comparison (b)).

nodes.title: Compactly supported coherent and de Rham cohomology of affinoid and Stein dagger spaces
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K). Let X = Sp(A) be an affinoid K-dagger space with a fringe presentation A = W_m/IW_m, I ⊆ T_m(ρ_0), fringe stages X_ρ = Sp(T_m(ρ)/IT_m(ρ)), so X' ⊂† X_ρ. For a coherent O†_X-module F choose (after shrinking ρ_0) a coherent O_{X_{ρ_0}}-module F_{ρ_0} with F(X) = colim_ρ F_{ρ_0}(X_ρ) (F1/fringe-module-descent) and put H^i_c(X, F) := H^i_{X}(X_{ρ_0}, F_{ρ_0}), the cohomology of F_{ρ_0} with supports in the complement of the admissible open X_{ρ_0} − X' (F1/de-rham-cohomology-with-supports). For X smooth, H^i_{dR,c}(X) := H^i_{X}(X_ρ, Ω^•_{X_ρ}). Both are independent of ρ and of the fringe presentation. For a smooth Stein dagger space X with Stein covering (U_j)_{j∈ℕ}, H^i_c(X, F) := colim_j H^i_{U_j}(U_{j+1}, F) and H^i_{dR,c}(X) := colim_j H^i_{U_j}(U_{j+1}, Ω^•), along the extension-by-zero maps. H^i_c(X, F) carries the finest locally convex topology making the boundary maps H^{i−1}(X_{ρ_0} − X', F_{ρ_0}) → H^i_c(X, F) continuous, and a topological A-module structure.

F coherent; for H_{dR,c}: X smooth

Extension of F: F1/fringe-module-descent (1),(2); the extension is unique up to isomorphism after shrinking, so H^i_c is well defined.
Stein version: the transition maps are the extension-by-zero maps H_{U_j}(U_{j+1}) → H_{U_{j+1}}(U_{j+2}) (excision and functoriality of supports).

nodes.title: Serre duality for smooth affinoid dagger spaces
nodes.statement: Let K be spherically complete (complete, nonarchimedean; e.g. discretely valued). Let X be a smooth affinoid K-dagger space of pure dimension d and F a coherent O†_X-module; give Ext^i_{O_X}(F, ω_X) the fringe topology and H^{d−i}_c(X, F) the topology of F1/compact-support-de-rham. Then for 0 ≤ i ≤ d there is a pairing Ext^i_{O_X}(F, ω_X) × H^{d−i}_c(X, F) → K, functorial in F, inducing topological isomorphisms Ext^i_{O_X}(F, ω_X) ≅ Hom_{K,cont}(H^{d−i}_c(X, F), K) and H^{d−i}_c(X, F) ≅ Hom_{K,cont}(Ext^i_{O_X}(F, ω_X), K).
hypotheses: K spherically complete
X smooth affinoid of pure dimension d
F coherent
proofSteps: Polydisc case A = K⟨T_1..T_m⟩†: H^m_c(X, ω_X) = {Σ_{μ<0} a_μ T^μ dT : η^{-|μ|}|a_μ| → 0 ∀ η > 1} (Dagger compactSupport_top_polydisc), and the residue pairing (Σ_{α≥0} b_αT^α, Σ_{μ<0} a_μT^μ dT) ↦ Σ_α b_α a_{−α−1} identifies A ≅ H^m_c(X, ω)ˇ and H^m_c(X, ω) ≅ Aˇ (Robba–Christol 6.5 for m = 1, Etesse–Le Stum, van der Put, Beyer — not read, recorded as a gap).

General case: analyse a closed immersion X → Sp(W_m) and use the standard Ext/local cohomology arguments of van der Put and Beyer (Serre duality for rigid spaces — not read, gap), with the fringe topologies of F1/fringe-topology and nonarchimedean Hahn–Banach duality for spherically complete K (no owner in the atlas — gap).
The pairing is functorial in F because it is built from Yoneda products Ext^i(F, ω) × H^{d−i}_c(F) → H^d_c(ω) and the trace H^d_c(X, ω_X) → K.
acceptance: X = D the closed dagger disc, F = O: Ext^0(O, ω) = K⟨T⟩† dT is dual to H^1_c(D, O) and conversely; the pairing is the residue at infinity.

nodes.title: Poincaré duality for de Rham cohomology of smooth affinoid and smooth Stein dagger spaces
nodes.statement: Let K be discretely valued of characteristic 0, and (for the strictness and finiteness inputs, see below) the fraction field of a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic (0, p). (a) If X is a smooth affinoid K-dagger space of pure dimension n, there are canonical isomorphisms H^i_dR(X) ≅ Hom_{K,cont}(H^{2n−i}_{dR,c}(X), K) and H^{2n−i}_{dR,c}(X) ≅ Hom_{K,cont}(H^i_dR(X), K) for 0 ≤ i ≤ 2n. (b) The same holds for a smooth Stein K-dagger space X of pure dimension n whose de Rham cohomology is finite-dimensional (needed for the strictness of its de Rham differentials, F1/dagger-strict-differentials; cf. packet sourceIssue E31). Since these groups are finite-dimensional (F1/dagger-de-rham-finiteness-and-base-change) and separated (F1/dagger-strict-differentials), (a) is a perfect duality of finite-dimensional K-vector spaces.
hypotheses: K the fraction field of a complete DVR of mixed characteristic (0, p) (discretely valued of characteristic 0, hence spherically complete; mixed characteristic is what the finiteness theorem behind Lemma 4.7 provides)
X smooth of pure dimension n, affinoid in (a), Stein with finite-dimensional de Rham cohomology in (b)
proofSteps: Vanishing: for locally free coherent F, H^q_c(X, F) = 0 for q ≠ n (along a finite surjective X → Sp(W_n) extended to a fringe stage, reduce to X = Sp(W_n), F = O and compute as in van der Put and Beyer — not read, gap); hence H^{q+n}_{dR,c}(X) = H^q(H^n_c(Ω^•_X)) and H^n_c(X, Ω^i_X) = H^n_c(X, O_X) ⊗_A Ω^i_A.
Serre duality (F1/dagger-serre-duality) identifies the complex H^n_c(Ω^•_X) with the continuous dual of the de Rham complex Ω^•_A (shifted), term by term.

Lemma 4.6: for a complex K^• of complete locally convex K-spaces with strict differentials, H^q(Hom_cont(K^•, K)) = Hom_cont(H^q(K^•), K) — an easy consequence of Hahn–Banach over spherically complete K (van Rooij 4.10; no owner in the atlas — gap). The differentials of Ω^•_A are strict (F1/dagger-strict-differentials).
(b): with a Stein covering (U_j), H^i_c(X, F) = colim_j H^i_{U_j}(U_{j+1}, F) vanishes for i ≠ n (proof of (a)); combine Serre duality on Stein spaces with 4.6 and 4.7 as in (a).
acceptance: X = D the closed dagger disc: H^0_dR = K is dual to H^2_{dR,c} = K, and H^1_dR = 0 = H^1_{dR,c}.
X = the dagger annulus |x| = 1: H^1_dR = K·dx/x is dual to H^1_{dR,c} = K.
