nodes.title: Strict normal crossings divisors on smooth dagger spaces (smooth dagger pairs)
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth K-dagger space (K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K)) and D ⊆ X a closed dagger subspace (F1/dagger-coherent-module). D is a strict normal crossings divisor if its associated rigid pair (X', D') corresponds, under AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor, to a smooth pair in the sense of AdicSpacesPartII:R4/smooth-pair (X' smooth over K with the strict normal crossings divisor D'); only this dagger-specific transfer is defined here. Equivalently: every point has an affinoid neighbourhood Sp(A) with elements x_1, …, x_n ∈ A such that dx_1, …, dx_n is a basis of Ω^1_A and D ∩ Sp(A) = V(x_1⋯x_r) for some r ≤ n (as a closed subspace); equivalently, at every point x ∈ D the local ring O_{X,x} is regular with a regular system of parameters x_1..x_d such that D is cut out by x_1⋯x_r. The pair (X, D) is then a smooth dagger pair; D is reduced and an effective Cartier divisor, and locally on an admissible affinoid covering D = V(x_1) ∪ … ∪ V(x_r) with smooth pieces V(x_i) whose partial intersections are smooth of the expected codimension. As in AdicSpacesPartII:R4/smooth-pair no condition is imposed on the global irreducible components: they need not be smooth (e.g. for residue characteristic ≠ 2 the analytified nodal cubic V(y^2 − x^2(1 + x)) ⊆ Sp(K⟨x, y⟩†) is a strict normal crossings divisor in this sense — at the origin it is V((y − x√(1+x))(y + x√(1+x))) with √(1+x) analytic on |x| < 1 — yet it is irreducible and singular).
hypotheses: X smooth
D ⊆ X a closed dagger subspace
proofSteps: Equivalence of the three conditions: local rings of X and X' agree (F1/dagger-to-rigid-functor (3)), closed subspaces correspond (same, (4)), and étale coordinates on X' can be approximated by overconvergent ones (F1/dagger-approximation (2)); the local-ring form is Stacks 41.21.1 (strict normal crossings divisor) applied to the regular local rings O_{X,x}.

Local components: in a chart, D = V(x_1⋯x_r) with dx_1..dx_n a basis of Ω^1, so the V(x_i) are smooth and their intersections V(x_{i_1}, …, x_{i_s}) are smooth of codimension s (Jacobian criterion). Stacks 41.21.1/41.21.2 are statements about Zariski-local rings of locally noetherian schemes; the analytic local rings O_{X,x} of a dagger or rigid space are henselian, so the local-ring form here corresponds to Stacks' normal crossings (étale-local) condition taken over K, not to Stacks' global description of strict normal crossings divisors by smooth irreducible components (41.21.2), which does not transfer.
acceptance: D = V(x_1x_2) in the dagger bidisc Sp(K⟨x_1, x_2⟩†) is a strict normal crossings divisor with components V(x_1), V(x_2).

nodes.title: The logarithmic de Rham complex Ω^•_X(log D) along a strict normal crossings divisor
nodes.statement: Let (X, D) be a smooth K-dagger space with a strict normal crossings divisor (F1/dagger-snc-divisor), j : X − D → X. The sheaf Ω^1_X(log D) ⊆ j_*Ω^1_{X−D} is the O†_X-submodule generated locally, in coordinates with D = V(x_1⋯x_r), by dx_1/x_1, …, dx_r/x_r, dx_{r+1}, …, dx_n; it is locally free of rank n and independent of the coordinates. Ω^p_X(log D) := ⋀^p Ω^1_X(log D), and the exterior derivative of j_*Ω^•_{X−D} preserves these subsheaves, giving the logarithmic de Rham complex Ω^•_X(log D) with Ω^•_X ⊆ Ω^•_X(log D) ⊆ j_*Ω^•_{X−D}. For a smooth component D_1 of D (a smooth closed dagger subspace which is a union of irreducible components of D) with D = D_1 + D' — so that D'|_{D_1} is a strict normal crossings divisor on D_1 — there is a residue map Res_{D_1} and an exact sequence of complexes 0 → Ω^•_X(log D') → Ω^•_X(log D) → ι_*Ω^•_{D_1}(log D'|_{D_1})[−1] → 0. Its hypercohomology is H^i_dR(X, log D) := H^i(X, Ω^•_X(log D)), and (Ω^•_X(log D))' = Ω^•_{X'}(log D').
hypotheses: X smooth
D ⊆ X strict normal crossings
proofSteps: Independence of coordinates: another local equation of D_i is u x_i with u a unit, and dlog(u x_i) − dlog(x_i) = du/u ∈ Ω^1_X (Stacks 50.15, proof of Lemma 50.15.2).
Local freeness: in coordinates, the dlog x_i (i ≤ r) and dx_j (j > r) are a basis because dx_1..dx_n is a basis of Ω^1 and the x_i (i ≤ r) are nonzerodivisors (F1/dagger-snc-divisor).
Closure under d: d(dlog x_i) = 0 and d(f dlog x_I ∧ dx_J) = df ∧ dlog x_I ∧ dx_J; wedge products of log forms are log forms (Stacks Lemma 50.15.4).

Residue sequence: locally Ω^p(log D) = Ω^p(log D') ⊕ dlog x_1 ∧ Ω^{p−1}(log D') modulo x_1-divisible corrections, and Res(ω' + dlog(x_1) ∧ ω) = ω|_{D_1} is well defined and surjective with kernel Ω^p(log D') (Stacks Lemma 50.15.2 for D' = ∅, the same local computation in general); the sign convention d(dlog x_1 ∧ ω) = −dlog x_1 ∧ dω makes it a map of complexes.
Rigid comparison: completion of coherent modules (F1/dagger-to-rigid-functor) applied to the locally free Ω^p_X(log D).
acceptance: For the closed dagger disc D = Sp(K⟨x⟩†) with divisor {0}: Ω^1(log 0) = O·dx/x, and H^0 = K, H^1 = K·dx/x (char K = 0).

nodes.title: The boundary-vanishing (compact-support) logarithmic de Rham complex Ω^•_X(log D)(−D)
nodes.statement: Let (X, D) be a smooth K-dagger space with a strict normal crossings divisor and I_D ⊆ O†_X its (invertible) ideal. The compact-support logarithmic de Rham complex is the subcomplex Ω^•_X(log D)(−D) := I_D · Ω^•_X(log D) of Ω^•_X(log D); in coordinates with D = V(x_1⋯x_r) it is x_1⋯x_r·Ω^•_X(log D) ⊆ Ω^•_X. Its hypercohomology H^i_{c}(X, D) := H^i(X, Ω^•_X(log D)(−D)) is the de Rham cohomology of the pair with vanishing along the boundary. There are natural maps Ω^•_X(log D)(−D) ⊆ Ω^•_X ⊆ Ω^•_X(log D), inducing H^i_c(X, D) → H^i_dR(X) → H^i_dR(X, log D), and on X − D the complex restricts to Ω^•_{X−D}. With coefficients: for a locally free E with integrable connection having logarithmic poles along D, DR_c(E) := I_D·E ⊗ Ω^•_X(log D).
hypotheses: X smooth
D ⊆ X strict normal crossings
proofSteps: Subcomplex: d(x_1⋯x_r ω) = x_1⋯x_r (dlog(x_1⋯x_r) ∧ ω + dω) with dlog(x_1⋯x_r) = Σ_{i≤r} dlog x_i ∈ Ω^1(log D), so I_D·Ω^•(log D) is stable under d (F1/log-de-rham-complex).
Inclusion into Ω^•_X: x_1⋯x_r · dlog x_I ∧ dx_J = (Π_{i∉I} x_i) dx_I ∧ dx_J has no poles.
Independence of coordinates: I_D is intrinsic, and Ω^•_X(log D) is (F1/log-de-rham-complex).
Restriction to X − D: I_D is trivial there and Ω(log D)|_{X−D} = Ω_{X−D}.
acceptance: For (P^1)^† with D = {0, ∞}: Ω^0(log D)(−D) = O(−2) and Ω^1(log D)(−D) = Ω^1_{P^1}; H^0_c = 0, H^1_c = K (the Čech class of the constant 1 on the overlap) and H^2_c = K (the class of dz/z).

uses.how: F1 supplies the overconvergent de Rham and logarithmic boundary complexes. RD.4 supplies the ordinary dagger-tube/rigid comparison for each smooth quasi-projective boundary stratum (HLTT Lemma 6.8, with its functoriality). AG2.4 separately constructs the boundary-stratum spectral sequence of HLTT Lemma 6.21, with these rigid groups on E₁ and cuspidal boundary-support cohomology as abutment; it does not identify that whole abutment directly with ordinary rigid cohomology by Lemma 6.8. It imports RD.5 finiteness and RD.6 weights on the strata and passes them through the spectral sequence, as in Corollaries 6.22 and 6.24. Generic log/compact-support comparison adapters need separate proofs.

nodes.title: Localisation sequences for boundary-vanishing log de Rham complexes and for compactly supported cohomology
nodes.statement: Let (X, D) be a smooth K-dagger space with a strict normal crossings divisor, D = D_1 + D' with D_1 a smooth component and D' the union of the others; write ι : D_1 → X and D'_1 = D' ∩ D_1 (a strict normal crossings divisor on D_1). Then (a) restriction of forms gives an exact sequence of complexes 0 → Ω^•_X(log D)(−D) → Ω^•_X(log D')(−D') → ι_*Ω^•_{D_1}(log D'_1)(−D'_1) → 0, hence a long exact localisation sequence … → H^i_c(X, D) → H^i_c(X, D') → H^i_c(D_1, D'_1) → H^{i+1}_c(X, D) → …; for D' = ∅ this is 0 → Ω^•_X(log D_1)(−D_1) → Ω^•_X → ι_*Ω^•_{D_1} → 0. (b) For an admissible open U ⊆ X with complement Y and a closed Z ⊆ Y, the supports sequence … → H^i_Z(X) → H^i_Y(X) → H^i_{Y−Z}(X − Z) → … (F1/de-rham-cohomology-with-supports) gives, for affinoid U ⊂† X, the extension-by-zero map H^i_{dR,c}(U) → H^i_{dR,c}(X) and its localisation sequence with the cohomology of the fringe annulus.
hypotheses: X smooth; D = D_1 + D' strict normal crossings
in (b) U ⊆ X affinoid with U ⊂† X
proofSteps: (a) Morphism of complexes: ι^* maps Ω^•_X(log D') to Ω^•_{D_1}(log D'_1) because D' meets D_1 transversally (coordinates x_1, x_2..x_r with D_1 = V(x_1), D' = V(x_2⋯x_r)), and maps I_{D'} onto I_{D'_1}.

nodes.title: On a Tate algebra the Gauss norm is the maximum of |f(x)| over Max K⟨X⟩
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one, n ≥ 0 and f = Σ a_ν X^ν ∈ K⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩ with Gauss norm ‖f‖ = max_ν |a_ν|. Then |f(y)| ≤ ‖f‖ for every y ∈ Max K⟨X⟩ (|f(y)| computed in the finite extension K⟨X⟩/m_y with the unique extension of |·|), and there is x ∈ Max K⟨X⟩ with |f(x)| = ‖f‖. Hence the supremum seminorm of K⟨X⟩ (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-supremum-seminorm) is the Gauss norm, and it is attained. Lean name: Huber.TateAlgebra.exists_eval_norm_eq_gaussNorm.
hypotheses: K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one
f ∈ K⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩ = restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n K
proofSteps: Upper bound: the image y_i of X_i in L = K⟨X⟩/m_y (a finite extension of K by AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-residue-fields-finite) is the image of a power-bounded element under the continuous map K⟨X⟩ → L, so |y_i| ≤ 1. By continuity and density of K[X], f(y) = Σ a_ν y^ν in L, so |f(y)| ≤ max_ν |a_ν| = ‖f‖.

Attainment, reduction: f = 0 is trivial. Otherwise ‖f‖ = |a_{ν₀}| for some ν₀ (the coefficients tend to 0), and g = f/a_{ν₀} ∈ K°⟨X⟩ has ‖g‖ = 1, so its reduction ḡ ∈ K̃[X₁,…,X_n] (K̃ = K°/K°°, finitely many coefficients of absolute value 1) is a nonzero polynomial.

The algebraic closure of K̃ is infinite, so there is x̄ ∈ (K̃^alg)ⁿ with ḡ(x̄) ≠ 0 (Mathlib MvPolynomial.funext). For each i lift the minimal polynomial of x̄_i over K̃ to a monic P_i ∈ K°[Z]. Its roots in K^alg have absolute value ≤ 1 and reduce to the roots of P̄_i, so some root x_i reduces to x̄_i. Put K' = K(x₁,…,x_n), a finite extension.

Evaluation at x = (x₁,…,x_n) is a continuous K-algebra map ev_x : K⟨X⟩ → K' (universal property of K⟨X⟩ for power-bounded images, anchor Layer 0.4, requested; Conrad, Several approaches, Exercise 1.1.4). Its image is a domain finite over K, hence a field (Mathlib isField_of_isIntegral_of_isField), so m_x = ker ev_x is maximal. g(x) ∈ K'° has reduction ḡ(x̄) ≠ 0, so |g(x)| = 1 and |f(x)| = |a_{ν₀}| = ‖f‖.
acceptance: For K = ℚ_p and f = T^p − T: ‖f‖ = 1, attained at a root x of an unramified quadratic whose reduction lies in 𝔽_{p²} ∖ 𝔽_p, while |f(c)| ≤ |p| for all c ∈ ℤ_p (Conrad, Several approaches, Exercise 1.1.3(4)).
For f = 1 + ϖT (ϖ a pseudo-uniformizer), ‖f‖ = 1 = |f(x)| at every point: f is a unit of K⟨T⟩.

nodes.title: Adic homomorphisms are bounded and adic for every choice of rings of definition
nodes.statement: Let φ : A → B be an adic ring homomorphism of Huber rings (R0/adic-ring-homomorphism). Then (i) φ is bounded: φ(T) is bounded in B for every bounded T ⊆ A; (ii) for all rings of definition A₀ of A and B₀ of B with φ(A₀) ⊆ B₀ and every ideal of definition I of A₀, the ideal φ(I)·B₀ is an ideal of definition of B₀; (iii) for every ring of definition A₀ of A and every open subring B′ of B with φ(A₀) ⊆ B′ there is a ring of definition B₀ of B with φ(A₀) ⊆ B₀ ⊆ B′. Lean names: `Huber.IsAdicHom.isBounded_image`, `Huber.IsAdicHom.isAdic_map_idealOfDefinition`, `Huber.IsAdicHom.exists_ringOfDefinition_le`.
hypotheses: A, B Huber rings; φ : A → B an adic ring homomorphism.
proofSteps: (i) Fix a witness (A₁, J, B₁) of adicness (φ(A₁) ⊆ B₁, K := φ(J)B₁ an ideal of definition). For T bounded there is n with T·Jⁿ ⊆ A₁, so φ(T)·Kⁿ = φ(T)·φ(Jⁿ)B₁ ⊆ B₁; since Kⁿ is a neighbourhood of 0 and B₁ is bounded, φ(T) is bounded.

(ii) (Huber 1993's proof.) Put A₂ = A₀·A₁ and B₂ = B₀·B₁, rings of definition (Wedhorn Corollary 6.4(1)) with φ(A₂) ⊆ B₂. I·A₂ and J·A₂ are ideals of definition of A₂ and K·B₂ = φ(J·A₂)·B₂ is one of B₂; as I·A₂ ⊇ (J·A₂)ⁿ for some n, L := φ(I·A₂)·B₂ is finitely generated by topologically nilpotent elements and contains (K·B₂)ⁿ, so it is an ideal of definition of B₂. Now L = (φ(I)·B₀)·B₂. Let J₀ be an ideal of definition of B₀; B₂ is bounded, so J₀ᵏ·B₂ ⊆ B₀ for some k, whence φ(I)·B₀ ⊇ J₀ᵏ·L, a product of open ideals of the adic ring B₂, hence open. An open ideal of B₀ finitely generated by topologically nilpotent elements is an ideal of definition of B₀.
(iii) φ(A₀) is bounded by (i); a bounded subring contained in an open subring B′ lies in a ring of definition B₀ ⊆ B′ (Wedhorn Corollary 6.4(4), Huber 1993 (1.3.ii)); take B₀ ⊇ φ(A₀).
acceptance: For the adic inclusion ℤ_p → ℚ_p with rings of definition A₀ = B₀ = ℤ_p and the ideal of definition I = p²ℤ_p, φ(I)B₀ = p²ℤ_p is an ideal of definition although the adicness witness used I = pℤ_p.
For the non-adic ℤ_p → ℤ_p⟦T⟧ ((p, T)-adic) conclusion (ii) fails for every choice: p·B₀ never contains a power of T.

nodes.title: Spa of a continuous homomorphism and the analytic locus (affinoid adicness criterion)
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺), (B, B⁺) be Huber pairs, φ : A → B a continuous ring homomorphism with φ(A⁺) ⊆ B⁺, and g = Spa(φ) : X := Spa(B, B⁺) → Y := Spa(A, A⁺) (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.spaComap`). Write X_a, Y_a for the analytic loci (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.spaAnalytic`: points whose support is not open) and X_na, Y_na for their complements. (1) g(X_na) ⊆ Y_na, and if φ is adic (R0/adic-ring-homomorphism) then g(X_a) ⊆ Y_a. (2) If B is complete (and Hausdorff) and g(X_a) ⊆ Y_a, then φ is adic. Lean names: `ValuationSpectrum.spaComap_nonanalytic`, `Huber.IsAdicHom.spaComap_analytic`, `Huber.isAdicHom_of_spaComap_analytic`.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺), (B, B⁺) Huber pairs; φ : A → B continuous with φ(A⁺) ⊆ B⁺.
For (2): B complete and Hausdorff.
proofSteps: (1), first part: supp g(x) = φ⁻¹(supp x), and the preimage of an open ideal under the continuous φ is open.

(1), second part: take pairs of definition (A₀, I), (B₀, J) with φ(A₀) ⊆ B₀ and J = φ(I)B₀ (adicness). If g(x) were non-analytic, its prime support would contain I (an open prime contains an ideal of definition, Wedhorn Lemma 6.6), so supp x ⊇ φ(I)B₀ = J and x would be non-analytic (Tau Ceti `isAnalyticPoint_iff_exists_mem_extendedIdealOfDefinition_notMem_supp`).

(2): suppose φ is not adic; choose pairs of definition with φ(A₀) ⊆ B₀ and φ(I) ⊆ J. Then √(φ(I)B₀) ≠ √J (otherwise φ is adic, `Huber.IsAdicHom.of_radical_eq`), so some prime 𝔭 of B₀ contains φ(I) but not J. For j ∈ J ∖ 𝔭 every b ∈ B has b·jⁿ ∈ B₀, so B[1/j] = B₀[1/j] and 𝔭 = P ∩ B₀ for a prime P of B, which is not open (P ∩ B₀ ⊉ J).

Wedhorn Lemma 7.45 (requested from the anchor, Layer 2.3: a complete affinoid ring has an analytic point x of height one with supp x ⊇ P for every non-open prime P) gives x ∈ X_a with supp g(x) = φ⁻¹(supp x) ⊇ φ⁻¹(P) ⊇ I, so g(x) ∈ Y_na, contradicting g(X_a) ⊆ Y_a.
acceptance: ℤ_p → ℤ_p⟦T⟧ with the p-adic and (p, T)-adic topologies is not adic, and indeed the T-adic valuation of 𝔽_p((T)) is an analytic point of Spa ℤ_p⟦T⟧ (support (p) not open) mapping to the non-analytic point of Spa ℤ_p.
For φ : ℚ_p → ℚ_p⟨T⟩ both spectra are analytic and φ is adic.

nodes.title: Banach spaces of countable type have t-orthogonal Schauder bases
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value and E a K-Banach space of countable type (E contains a dense K-subspace of at most countable dimension). Then for every t ∈ (0, 1) there is a family (e_i)_{i∈I} of nonzero vectors, I = {1, …, n} or I = ℕ, such that every v ∈ E is uniquely a convergent sum v = Σ c_i e_i with c_i ∈ K and c_i e_i → 0, and t·max_i |c_i|·‖e_i‖ ≤ ‖v‖ ≤ max_i |c_i|·‖e_i‖ (a t-orthogonal Schauder basis). After rescaling the e_i by elements of K so that |ϖ| < ‖e_i‖ ≤ 1 (ϖ ∈ K, 0 < |ϖ| < 1), v ↦ (c_i)_i is a topological K-linear isomorphism E ≅ c₀(I, K) (null families with the supremum norm) with t|ϖ|·|c|_sup ≤ ‖v‖ ≤ |c|_sup. In particular every finite-dimensional normed K-space has a t-orthogonal basis, and any t-orthogonal family in it extends, for every t' < t, to a t'-orthogonal basis. Lean name: `Huber.BanachSpace.exists_orthogonalBasis_of_countableType`.
hypotheses: K complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value
E a K-Banach space of countable type
proofSteps: Orthogonal complement of a vector: a finite-dimensional subspace D ⊆ E is complete and closed (Mathlib FiniteDimensional.complete, Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional), so dist(x, D) > 0 for x ∉ D. For s ∈ (0, 1) choose d ∈ D with ‖x − d‖ ≤ s⁻¹·dist(x, D) and put y = x − d. Then for λ ∈ K, d' ∈ D: ‖λy + d'‖ ≥ |λ|·dist(x, D) ≥ s|λ|‖y‖, and ‖d'‖ ≤ max(‖λy + d'‖, |λ|‖y‖) ≤ s⁻¹‖λy + d'‖ by the ultrametric inequality; so ‖λy + d'‖ ≥ s·max(|λ|‖y‖, ‖d'‖): y is s-orthogonal to D.

Induction: let (x_k) span a dense subspace and drop the x_k lying in the span of the earlier ones. With s_k := t^(2^(−k)), step 1 gives e_k ∈ x_k + span(e_1, …, e_{k−1}) that is s_k-orthogonal to span(e_1, …, e_{k−1}); by induction ‖Σ_{k≤n} c_k e_k‖ ≥ (∏_{k≤n} s_k)·max_k |c_k|‖e_k‖ ≥ t·max_k |c_k|‖e_k‖. The same step extends a given t-orthogonal family in a finite-dimensional space.

Completeness: for (c_i) with c_i e_i → 0 the series Σ c_i e_i converges (E complete, ultrametric), the resulting map is injective and bounded below by the t-orthogonality inequality, so its image is closed; it contains span(e_k) = span(x_k), which is dense, hence it is all of E. Rescaling gives the c₀ description.
acceptance: K⟨T⟩ has the orthonormal Schauder basis (Tⁿ)_{n ≥ 0}.
ℂ_p is a ℚ_p-Banach space of countable type (ℚ̄_p is dense and countable-dimensional), so it has a t-orthogonal Schauder basis over ℚ_p for every t < 1.

nodes.title: Completed tensor products over a nonarchimedean field: cross norm, injectivity, kernels and strictness (Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 2.2.9)
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value and V, W, X Banach K-modules, with the completed tensor product of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-banach-module (A = K). (a) The product seminorm is a cross norm, |v ⊗ w| = ‖v‖·‖w‖, and V ⊗_K W → V ⊗̂_K W is injective. In particular, for w ∈ W with ‖w‖ = 1 (e.g. w = 1 in a complete field extension W = L of K), the map X → W ⊗̂_K X, x ↦ w ⊗ x, is an isometric (hence strict) injection for every Banach K-module X. (b) If X is of countable type and f : V → W is a bounded K-linear map, the natural map ker(f) ⊗̂_K X → ker(f ⊗̂ X) is a topological isomorphism. (c) If moreover f is strict, so is f ⊗̂ X. Kedlaya–Liu state (b) and (c) for arbitrary X, reducing 'immediately' to separable modules; the countable-type hypothesis on X is what the basis argument below proves directly. Lean names: `Huber.BanachModule.CompletedTensor.norm_tmul`, `injective_tensorProduct_of_field`, `ker_map_of_field`, `isStrictMap_map_of_field`.
hypotheses: K complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value
V, W, X Banach K-modules
for (b), (c): X of countable type; f : V → W bounded (for (c): strict)
proofSteps: (a): every presentation of z = Σ_{i≤m} x_i ⊗ y_i lies in D ⊗ G for finite-dimensional D ⊆ V, G ⊆ W, and the product seminorm of z is the infimum of those computed in D ⊗ G. Take the x_i t-orthogonal (a t-orthogonal basis of their span, R0/banach-countable-type-orthogonal-basis) and extend them to a t'-orthogonal basis of D (same node). The coordinate functional φ_i of this basis satisfies |φ_i(d)|·‖x_i‖ ≤ t'⁻¹‖d‖ on D, so ‖y_i‖·‖x_i‖ = ‖(φ_i ⊗ id)(z)‖·‖x_i‖ ≤ t'⁻¹·|z|_{D⊗G}. Hence |z| ≥ t'·max_i ‖x_i‖‖y_i‖ for every t' < 1, which gives the cross norm (m = 1) and injectivity.

(b): choose a t-orthogonal Schauder basis of X (R0/banach-countable-type-orthogonal-basis). By the orthogonal description (R0/completed-tensor-banach-module (f), API orthogonalEquiv), E ⊗̂_K X ≅ c₀(ℕ, E) naturally in E, so f ⊗̂ X becomes the coordinatewise map c₀(ℕ, f) : c₀(ℕ, V) → c₀(ℕ, W), whose kernel is c₀(ℕ, ker f), the image of ker(f) ⊗̂ X ≅ c₀(ℕ, ker f) (ker f is closed, hence Banach).

(c): if f is strict, then f(V) is closed and there is C with every w ∈ f(V) having a preimage of norm ≤ C‖w‖; a null family in f(V) lifts to a null family, so c₀(ℕ, f) has closed image c₀(ℕ, f(V)) and is strict. Transport back along the isomorphisms of (b).
acceptance: For K = ℚ_p, L = ℚ_p(√p) and X = ℚ_p⟨T⟩, the map X → L ⊗̂_K X is the isometric inclusion ℚ_p⟨T⟩ → L⟨T⟩.
For f : ℚ_p⟨T⟩ → ℚ_p⟨T⟩, g ↦ Tg (strict, injective) and X = ℂ_p: f ⊗̂ X is multiplication by T on ℂ_p⟨T⟩, again injective and strict.

nodes.title: The fibre of a morphism over a point (Huber (1.2.4))
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of adic spaces locally of weakly finite type and y ∈ Y, with κ(y) = (k(y)^∧, k(y)⁺^∧) the completed residue affinoid field and ι_y: Spa κ(y) → Y the canonical morphism (Huber (1.1.8)). Then ι_y is adic, Spa κ(y) is covered by a stably sheafy affinoid (R0/nonarchimedean-field-strongly-noetherian; k(y) is discrete if y is not analytic), so the fibre X_y := X ×_Y Spa κ(y) exists (R0/fibre-products-existence (b)); if X = Spa(B, B⁺), Y = Spa(A, A⁺) with (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) topologically of finite type, X_y = Spa(B ⊗̂_A κ(y)) (R0/affinoid-fibre-product, R0/completed-tensor-noetherian-stability). Let G ⊆ Y be the set of secondary generalizations of y (all generalizations of y when y is analytic). Then the projection p: X_y → X induces a homeomorphism from |X_y| onto the subspace f⁻¹(G) of |X|, and for every z ∈ X_y the image of k(p(z)) is dense in k(z).
hypotheses: f locally of weakly finite type
y ∈ Y arbitrary (analytic or not)
proofSteps: ι_y is adic: for y analytic both sides are analytic; for y non-analytic k(y) is discrete and Spa κ(y) has no analytic points (Huber 1996 (1.2.4), 'The natural morphism Spa κ(y) → Y is adic'). Existence and the affinoid form follow from R0/fibre-products-existence (b), R0/affinoid-fibre-product and R0/completed-tensor-noetherian-stability (κ(y) is of noetherian type).
Image: Spa κ(y) → Y is a homeomorphism onto G (Huber (1.1.9)), so p(|X_y|) ⊆ f⁻¹(G), and every x ∈ f⁻¹(G) is in the image by R0/fibre-product-points.

Injectivity and density: a point z of X_y over x ∈ X and over the point of Spa κ(y) mapping to f(x) is a valuation on the compositum of k(x) and k(y)^∧ over k(f(x)); since the image of k(y) is dense in k(f(x)) for f(x) ∈ G (Huber 1.1.10(iii)), the image of k(x) is dense in k(z) and z is determined by x. p is a homeomorphism onto f⁻¹(G) because it is spectral and generalizing on affinoid pieces (compare Huber 1996 Lemma 1.3.15 and Huber 1994, 3.9, which Huber cites for 1.2.3(iii)(d)).
acceptance: For f = id_Y, X_y = Spa κ(y) maps homeomorphically onto the generalizations of y.
For the closed unit disc D → Spa(K, K°) and y the unique point, X_y = D and G = {y}.

nodes.title: Flat locally quasi-finite morphisms stay flat after base change (Huber 1.6.4(ii))
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a locally quasi-finite morphism between analytic adic spaces which is flat (R0/flat-morphism: every stalk map O_{Y,f(x)} → O_{X,x} is flat), and let g: Y' → Y be a morphism of analytic adic spaces with Y' covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings, so that X' = X ×_Y Y' exists (R0/fibre-products-existence (b); g is adic since Y is analytic). Then the projection f': X' → Y' is flat.
hypotheses: f locally quasi-finite and flat; X, Y, Y' analytic
Y' covered by stably sheafy affinoids (existence of the fibre product)
proofSteps: Let x' ∈ X' be a maximal point with images x ∈ X, y' ∈ Y', y ∈ Y. As in the proof of Huber 1.5.4 (R0/quasi-finite-stalk-criterion; affinoid-locally f is finite near x, and fibre products of affinoids are completed tensor products, R0/affinoid-fibre-product), O_{X',x'} is a direct factor of O_{X,x} ⊗_{O_{Y,y}} O_{Y',y'}; the latter is flat over O_{Y',y'} by base change of flatness (Mathlib Module.Flat.baseChange-type instances), so O_{X',x'} is flat over O_{Y',y'}.

For an arbitrary x'' ∈ X', choose a maximal generalisation x' ≻ x''; O_{X',x''} → O_{X',x'} is local and flat (Huber 1.1.10(iii)), and flatness of O_{Y',f'(x'')} → O_{X',x''} follows (Huber: 'Then by (1.1.10.iii), for every x ∈ X', O_{X',x} is flat over O_{Y',f'(x)}').
acceptance: Étale morphisms of analytic adic spaces (flat and locally quasi-finite by R0/etale-flat-unramified, R0/unramified-locally-quasi-finite) stay flat after base change; this is the input of the (b) ⇒ (a) step of R0/etale-flat-unramified.

nodes.title: The closure of a maximal point is the intersection of the rational subsets containing it (Huber 1.5.10)
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a Huber pair with A a Tate ring, X = Spa(A, A⁺) and x ∈ X a maximal (rank-one) point with closure M = closure{x}. Let 𝒩 be the set of rational subsets of X containing M. Then M = ⋂_{N ∈ 𝒩} N = ⋂_{N ∈ 𝒩} closure(N). Consequently every open subset of X containing M contains a rational subset containing M (compactness in the constructible topology, the rational subsets being constructible). Warning: for a non-maximal point x the intersection of the rational subsets containing closure{x} also contains the generalisations of x, so the statement fails; one applies it to the maximal generalisation of x, whose closure contains closure{x}.
hypotheses: A Tate
x maximal (rank-one) point of Spa(A, A⁺)
proofSteps: (1a) For pro-constructible subsets Pᵢ of X closed under generalisation, the closure of ⋂ Pᵢ is ⋂ closure(Pᵢ): a point in ⋂ closure(Pᵢ) specialises from points pᵢ ∈ Pᵢ, which by Huber 1.1.10(i) (generalisations form a chain) have a common maximal generalisation p, lying in every Pᵢ.

(1b) For a rational subset R = {|aᵢ| ≤ |b|} (a₁, …, a_k generating A) and s a topologically nilpotent unit, the rational subsets Rₙ = {|s aᵢⁿ| ≤ |bⁿ|} decrease, and ⋂ Rₙ = closure(R) (every specialisation of a point of R lies in all Rₙ; conversely a point of ⋂ Rₙ has its maximal generalisation in R).

Since x is maximal, {x} is an intersection of rational subsets (points of the Tate affinoid are separated by rational subsets at rank-one points); by (1a) M = ⋂ closure of these, and by (1b) each closure is an intersection of rational subsets, which contain M; so M = ⋂_{𝒩} N, and again by (1a) M = ⋂_{𝒩} closure(N) (Huber's proof).

Compactness: M and the rational subsets are closed in the compact constructible topology, so an open O ⊇ M (open in the constructible topology) contains a finite intersection of members of 𝒩, which is rational (Mathlib compactSpace_withConstructibleTopology).
acceptance: For the Gauss point x of the closed unit disc D, M is x together with the type-5 points around it inside D; the rational subsets {|T − c| ≥ |ϖ|^{1/n}}-type neighbourhoods (for all residue classes) shrink to M.
For a non-maximal x (a type-5 point), every rational subset containing x contains its rank-one generalisation, so the intersection is strictly larger than closure{x}.

nodes.title: Complete nonarchimedean fields are strongly noetherian; affinoid fields are stably sheafy
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field in Huber's sense (a complete topological field whose topology is induced by a valuation of rank one, Huber 1996 (1.1.3)). Then K is a strongly noetherian Tate ring (TauCeti.Huber.IsStronglyNoetherian: every K⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩ is noetherian), hence of noetherian type (R0/noetherian-type-huber-ring) and stably sheafy (R0/noetherian-type-stably-sheafy). Consequently, for every affinoid field (K, K⁺) (K⁺ ⊆ K° an open valuation ring) with K complete nonarchimedean, and for every affinoid field with discrete topology, Spa(K, K⁺) is an affinoid adic space covered by a stably sheafy affinoid; in particular Spa κ(y) → Y (κ(y) = completed residue affinoid field) satisfies the hypothesis on the second factor of R0/fibre-products-existence.
hypotheses: K complete, topology induced by a rank-one valuation (the valuation ring K⁺ may have higher rank)
proofSteps: K is Tate: any nonzero element of the maximal ideal of K° is a topologically nilpotent unit.

K⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩ is noetherian: Weierstrass division and preparation over K° after a change of variables, induction on n (BGR 5.2.6, Theorem 1; recalled in Hübner §3). Only the rank-one topology enters; K⁺ plays no role.
Discrete fields: TauCeti IsStronglyNoetherian.of_discreteTopology. Sheafiness: R0/noetherian-type-stably-sheafy.
acceptance: K = ℚ_p, ℂ_p, or the completed residue field k(x)^∧ of an analytic point of an adic space.
For K⁺ ⊊ K° of rank two, Spa(K, K⁺) has two points and is stably sheafy.

nodes.title: Closure of a pro-constructible set is its set of specializations (Stacks 0903)
nodes.statement: Let X be a spectral space (Mathlib SpectralSpace) and E ⊆ X pro-constructible (TauCeti.IsProConstructible: closed in the constructible topology). Then the closure of E in X is the set of specializations of points of E; in particular E is closed if and only if E is stable under specialization. Local form: if X is locally spectral and E ∩ U is pro-constructible in U for every spectral open U ⊆ X (for instance E quasi-compact open with X quasi-separated), then closure(E) = {x : x is a specialization of a point of E}.
hypotheses: X spectral (local form: X locally spectral, E locally pro-constructible)
proofSteps: Let x ∈ closure(E). The sets E ∩ V, V a quasi-compact open neighbourhood of x, are nonempty (x ∈ closure(E), quasi-compact opens form a basis) and closed in the constructible topology, and have the finite intersection property (quasi-compact opens are stable under finite intersection in a spectral space).

The constructible topology is compact (Mathlib compactSpace_withConstructibleTopology), so some e ∈ E lies in every quasi-compact open neighbourhood of x; hence x ∈ closure({e}), i.e. x is a specialization of e. The converse inclusion is trivial.
Local form: closure and specialization are local on X; apply the spectral case in each spectral open U to E ∩ U.
acceptance: For X = Spec ℤ and E = {(0)} (pro-constructible), the closure is X, the set of specializations of the generic point.
The open unit disc B inside the closed unit disc D is stable under specialization but not closed; B is not pro-constructible (not quasi-compact), so no contradiction.

nodes.title: Images of pro-constructible sets under quasi-compact spectral maps are pro-constructible
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a spectral map between spectral spaces (Mathlib IsSpectralMap). Then f is continuous for the constructible topologies, and f(E) is pro-constructible in Y for every pro-constructible E ⊆ X; in particular f(X) is pro-constructible. Local form (Huber 1996, (1.1.13)): if f: X → Y is a quasi-compact spectral map between locally spectral spaces, then f(T) is pro-constructible in Y for every pro-constructible T ⊆ X.
hypotheses: f spectral between spectral spaces (local form: quasi-compact and spectral between locally spectral spaces)
proofSteps: Continuity for the constructible topologies: TauCeti IsSpectralMap.continuous_constructibleTopology.

E is closed, hence compact, in the compact constructible topology of X (Mathlib compactSpace_withConstructibleTopology); its image is compact in the constructible topology of Y, which is Hausdorff (two distinct points of the T0 space Y are separated by a quasi-compact open U, and U, Y ∖ U are disjoint constructible-open sets); so f(E) is closed there, i.e. pro-constructible.

Local form: for V ⊆ Y quasi-compact open (spectral if Y is quasi-separated, otherwise cover by spectral opens), f⁻¹(V) is quasi-compact and T ∩ f⁻¹(V) is covered by finitely many spectral opens of X; apply the spectral case to each and take the finite union (TauCeti Set.Finite.isProConstructible_biUnion).
acceptance: The image of Spec ℚ → Spec ℤ is {(0)}, pro-constructible and not constructible.

nodes.title: If T generates an open ideal then every T^n·U is a neighbourhood of 0: Huber's 'M·A open' gives a Tau Ceti weight family
nodes.statement: Let A be a Huber ring and T ⊆ A a subset such that the ideal T·A generated by T is open in A. Then for every n ∈ ℕ and every neighbourhood U of 0 in A, the additive subgroup T^n·U generated by the products t₁⋯t_n·u (tᵢ ∈ T, u ∈ U) is a neighbourhood of 0. Consequently: (a) if M₁,…,M_k ⊆ A are finite subsets with every Mᵢ·A open, then M = (M₁,…,M_k) is a weight family in Tau Ceti's sense (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsWeightFamily), so Huber's A⟨X⟩_M is built on Tau Ceti's weightedRestrictedSubring M; (b) if E ⊆ A has E·A open, then for every k ≥ 1 the set E(k) = {e₁⋯e_k : eᵢ ∈ E} generates the ideal (E·A)^k, which is again open.
hypotheses: A a Huber ring (Tau Ceti IsHuberRing); T arbitrary, not necessarily finite or bounded
no open mapping theorem is needed: the argument uses only a pair of definition (A₀, I) with I finitely generated
proofSteps: T^n·A = (T·A)^n is open: T·A contains some I^m for an ideal of definition I, so (T·A)^n ⊇ I^{mn}.
Replacing I by a power, take a pair of definition (A₀, I) with I ⊆ T^n·A, and a finite generating set L of I. Since L ⊆ T^n·A, there is a finite K ⊆ A with L ⊆ T^n·K.
Given an open subgroup U, choose m with K·I^m ⊆ U (K finite, multiplication continuous). Then I^{m+1} = L·I^m ⊆ (T^n·K)·I^m = T^n·(K·I^m) ⊆ T^n·U, so T^n·U contains the open subgroup I^{m+1}.

(a): apply this with T = Mᵢ; neighbourhoods of 0 may be replaced by open subgroups because A is nonarchimedean (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsWeightFamily.of_forall_openAddSubgroup). (b): the ideal generated by E(k) is (E·A)^k, which is open by the first step.
acceptance: A Tate with pseudo-uniformizer ϖ and T = {ϖ}: recovers tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsWeightFamily.of_exists_isUnit.
A = ℚ_p⟨Y, Z⟩, T = {Y}: Y·A is not open and the conclusion fails (this is the counterexample in the docstring of tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsWeightFamily), so the openness hypothesis cannot be dropped.

nodes.title: Extending a valuation along a finitely generated algebra with value group in the divisible hull
nodes.statement: Let φ: A → D be a ring homomorphism making D a finitely generated A-algebra, v a valuation of A with value group Γ_v, and q ⊆ D a prime ideal with φ⁻¹(q) = supp(v). Then there is a valuation r of D with supp(r) = q, r ∘ φ equivalent to v, and Γ_r/Γ_v a torsion group; that is, Γ_v and Γ_r have the same divisible hull. In particular Γ_v is cofinal in Γ_r and the convex subgroup of Γ_r generated by Γ_v is Γ_r. Field form: for a finitely generated field extension L/K and a valuation v of K there is a valuation w of L extending v with Γ_w/Γ_v torsion.
hypotheses: D finitely generated over A (only needed to make k(q) finitely generated over the residue field of supp v; a finite transcendence degree would suffice)
proofSteps: Pass to residue fields: v is the pullback of a valuation v̄ of k₀ = Frac(A/supp v), and k(q) = Frac(D/q) is a finitely generated field extension of k₀ because D/q is a finitely generated (A/supp v)-algebra.

Transcendental part: choose a transcendence basis t₁,…,t_n of k(q)/k₀. The Gauss extension w₀(Σ a_ν t^ν) = max_ν v̄(a_ν) (multiplicative notation) is a valuation of F = k₀(t₁,…,t_n) extending v̄ with the same value group.

Algebraic part: L = k(q) is finite over F. Localise the integral closure of O_{w₀} in L at a maximal ideal and dominate it by a valuation ring W of L (Stacks 00IA; mathlib:LocalSubring.exists_le_valuationSubring); W ∩ F dominates O_{w₀}, hence equals it by maximality (mathlib:ValuationSubring.isMax_toLocalSubring). For x ∈ L^×, a relation Σ_{i≤d} a_i x^i = 0 with a_i ∈ F has two terms of equal largest value, so w(x)^{i−j} ∈ Γ_{w₀} for some 0 < i − j ≤ d; hence Γ_W/Γ_{w₀} is torsion.
Set r(d) := w(image of d in k(q)). Then supp(r) = q, r ∘ φ is equivalent to v, and Γ_r ⊆ Γ_W is torsion over Γ_v. Cofinality: if γ < 1 in Γ_r then γ^m ∈ Γ_v for some m ≥ 1 and γ^m ≤ γ.
acceptance: A = ℚ_p with the p-adic valuation, D = ℚ_p[T], q = 0: the Gauss valuation has value group p^ℤ, while a valuation with |T| = γ for γ infinitesimal relative to |p| (a rank-2 extension) is an extension whose value group is not in the divisible hull, so it is excluded.
A = ℚ_p, D = ℚ_p[T]/(T² − p): the unique extension has value group p^{ℤ/2}, torsion over p^ℤ.

nodes.title: Fibre products of schemes are fibre products of locally ringed spaces
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Z and g: Y → Z be morphisms of schemes and X ×_Z Y their fibre product in schemes, with projections p₁, p₂. Then (X ×_Z Y, p₁, p₂) is also a fibre product in the category of locally ringed spaces: for every locally ringed space T and all morphisms of locally ringed spaces a: T → X, b: T → Y with f ∘ a = g ∘ b there is a unique morphism of locally ringed spaces c: T → X ×_Z Y with p₁ ∘ c = a and p₂ ∘ c = b. Equivalently, mathlib's Scheme.forgetToLocallyRingedSpace preserves pullbacks.
hypotheses: no hypotheses on f, g or T
proofSteps: Affine case X = Spec A, Y = Spec B, Z = Spec R: by the Γ–Spec adjunction (mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.ΓSpec.locallyRingedSpaceAdjunction; Stacks 01I1), Hom_LRS(T, Spec C) = Hom_ring(C, Γ(T, O_T)) naturally in C, so Hom_LRS(T, Spec(A ⊗_R B)) = Hom(A, Γ) ×_{Hom(R, Γ)} Hom(B, Γ) (Stacks 01I4).
Open subspaces: a morphism of locally ringed spaces T → X factors through an open subspace U ⊆ X iff its image lies in U, and then uniquely (Stacks 01HI, Lemma 26.3.5).

General case: cover Z by affine opens W and f⁻¹W, g⁻¹W by affine opens U, V; the scheme fibre product is glued from the affine pieces Spec(O(U) ⊗_{O(W)} O(V)), which are open subschemes. Given (a, b), cover T by the opens a⁻¹U ∩ b⁻¹V ∩ (f∘a)⁻¹W, take the unique lifts of the affine case there, and glue them; they agree on overlaps by uniqueness, via the open-subspace step, and morphisms of locally ringed spaces glue along open covers.
acceptance: X = Y = A¹_K over Z = Spec K and T = (Spa(K, K°))_: pairs (x, y) ∈ K² are the same as morphisms T → A²_K of locally ringed spaces over Spec K.
Used with T = U_ for an adic space U in AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-fibre-products; no analogue is claimed for fibre products of adic spaces.

nodes.title: Finite coverings of Max A by rational subdomains are refined by standard rational coverings (Huber's product trick on classical points)
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value of rank one, A a K-affinoid algebra, and W_j = X(T_j/s_j) = {x ∈ Max A : |t(x)| ≤ |s_j(x)| for all t ∈ T_j} (j = 1, …, m) rational subdomains covering Max A, where T_j ⊆ A is finite, s_j ∈ T_j and T_j has no common zero on Max A. Let S be the finite set of products t_1⋯t_m with t_j ∈ T_j for all j and t_k = s_k for at least one k. Then S generates the unit ideal of A, and for every f = t_1⋯t_m ∈ S with t_k = s_k the rational subdomain X(S/f) is contained in W_k. Consequently the standard rational covering {R(S/f)}_{f ∈ S} of Spa(A, A⁺) (any ring of integral elements A⁺) induces on Max A a covering by rational subdomains refining {W_j}. Lean name: RigidSpace.exists_standard_rationalCover_refining.
hypotheses: K complete, nontrivially valued, rank one; A a K-affinoid algebra
a finite covering of Max A by rational subdomains, each presented with its denominator among its numerators
proofSteps: For x ∈ Max A write |g(x)| for the absolute value of the image of g in the finite extension A/m_x of K (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-residue-fields-finite); g ↦ |g(x)| is multiplicative.

S generates the unit ideal: given x ∈ Max A, pick l with x ∈ W_l (so s_l(x) ≠ 0) and, for j ≠ l, t_j ∈ T_j with t_j(x) ≠ 0 (no common zero); the product with s_l in slot l lies in S and does not vanish at x. So S lies in no maximal ideal.

Containment (two slot replacements, exactly as in the proof of Tau Ceti's rationalSubset_refinementProducts_subset, run with the multiplicative seminorm |·(x)| of a classical point instead of a point of Spa): let x ∈ X(S/f), f = ∏ t_j with t_k = s_k, so f(x) ≠ 0 by step 2, and pick l with x ∈ W_l. If l = k we are done. Otherwise replacing t_l by s_l does not lower |·(x)| of the product, and in that product the k-th slot may hold any t ∈ T_k and stay in S; comparing with f bounds |t(x)| by |s_k(x)|, and s_k(x) ≠ 0 as a factor of f(x). Hence x ∈ W_k.
Since S generates the unit ideal the R(S/f) cover Spa(A, A⁺) (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa_eq_biUnion_rationalSubset_of_span_eq_top), and R(S/f) ∩ Max A = X(S/f).
acceptance: Max K⟨T⟩ covered by W_1 = X({T, ϖ}/ϖ) = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|} and W_2 = X({ϖ, T}/T) = {|T| ≥ |ϖ|}: the products with a denominator slot are ϖ·ϖ, ϖ·T and T·T, so S = {ϖ², ϖT, T²} generates the unit ideal (ϖ² is a unit), and X(S/ϖ²) = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|} ⊆ W_1, X(S/T²) = {|T| ≥ |ϖ|} ⊆ W_2, X(S/ϖT) = {|T| = |ϖ|} ⊆ W_1 ∩ W_2.
The statement is about Max A only: it does not assert that the R(T_j/s_j) cover Spa(A, A⁺) (that is Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 2.5.12, deduced from this lemma).

nodes.title: Morphisms from a rigid space to a finite-type affine K-scheme are K-algebra maps on global sections (Conrad, Lemma A.1.1)
nodes.statement: Let K be complete rank-one, Y a rigid-analytic space over K (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytic-space) and X a K-scheme locally of finite type. A morphism f : Y → X is a map of sets such that preimages of Zariski opens are admissible opens and preimages of Zariski coverings of Zariski opens are admissible coverings, together with a map f^♯ : O_X → f_*O_Y of sheaves of K-algebras; Hom_K(Y, X) is the set of these. Every such f carries points to closed points and every f^♯_y : O_{X,f(y)} → O_{Y,y} is local. If X = Spec C is affine of finite type, then f ↦ Γ(f^♯) : C → O_Y(Y) is a bijection Hom_K(Y, Spec C) ≅ Hom_{K-alg}(C, O_Y(Y)), natural in Y and C. Lean name: RigidSpace.homSpecEquiv.
hypotheses: Y a rigid-analytic space over K
X locally of finite type over K; affine of finite type for the bijection
proofSteps: Closed points and locality: the residue field k(y) of O_{Y,y} is finite over K (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-residue-fields-finite on an affinoid neighbourhood). Let p = f(y) ⊆ C on an affine open Spec C ∋ f(y), and q the kernel of O_{X,p} → O_{Y,y} → k(y). The image of C in k(y) is a domain finite over K, hence a field, so q ∩ C is maximal and contained in p; thus p = q ∩ C is maximal (f(y) is closed) and pO_{X,p} ⊆ q, i.e. f^♯_y is local.

Inverse map: for φ : C → O_Y(Y) put f(y) = ker(C → O_Y(Y) → k(y)) (a maximal ideal); f⁻¹(D(g)) = {y : φ(g)(y) ≠ 0}, which is admissible open, and Zariski covers pull back to admissible covers (Conrad, Several approaches, Exercise 2.3.2, applied on affinoids); φ(g) is invertible on f⁻¹(D(g)), so C_g → O_Y(f⁻¹D(g)) defines f^♯ on the basis {D(g)}.

Bijectivity: Γ of the constructed morphism is φ; conversely a morphism is determined by Γ(f^♯) because, by step 1, f(y) is the kernel of C → k(y) and f^♯ on D(g) is forced by locality — the proof of EGA I (1.8.1) / Stacks 01I1 (mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.ΓSpec.locallyRingedSpaceAdjunction for locally ringed spaces), with admissible opens in place of opens.

nodes.title: Classical points of Spa(A, A°) for a K-affinoid algebra: constructible density, and rational subsets ↔ rational subdomains of Max A (Huber 1993 §4)
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value of rank one and A a K-affinoid algebra. For m ∈ Max A the field A/m is finite over K, so |·| extends uniquely to A/m; the composite |·|_m lies in Spa(A, A°), and m ↦ |·|_m is an injection Max A → Spa(A, A°) whose image is the set of classical points (points x with k(x) finite over K). Let L_A = {v ∈ Spv A : v(a) ≤ 1 for a ∈ A°, v(a) < 1 for a ∈ A°°}. Then: (i) L_A is the closure of Max A in the constructible topology of Spv A (Huber 1993 Theorem 4.1); (ii) Max A is dense in the constructible topology of Spa(A, A°) (Corollary 4.2); (iii) two constructible subsets of Spa(A, A°) with the same classical points are equal (Corollary 4.3); (iv) for every rational subset U of Spa(A, A°), U ∩ Max A is a rational subdomain of Max A, and U ↦ U ∩ Max A is a bijection from the rational subsets of Spa(A, A°) onto the rational subdomains of Max A, preserving inclusions and finite intersections, with a finite family of rational subsets covering U iff their traces cover U ∩ Max A.
hypotheses: K complete, nontrivially valued, rank one; A a K-affinoid algebra with plus ring A° (the statement is not claimed for other rings of integral elements)
'rational subdomain' in the sense of BGR 7.2.3, as in AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affinoid-subdomain
proofSteps: Classical points: A/m is finite over K and m is closed (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-residue-fields-finite), so |·|_m is a continuous valuation, ≤ 1 on A° (power-bounded elements have spectral norm ≤ 1), with support m; distinct m give distinct supports.

(i), Huber's first proof: for A = K⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩ by induction on n — a nonempty constructible subset T of L_{K⟨X₁,…,X_{n+1}⟩} is moved by a Weierstrass automorphism so that its defining elements become units times polynomials in X_{n+1} over K⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩ (Weierstrass preparation, BGR 5.2.2/5.2.4); elimination of quantifiers for algebraically closed valued fields makes the projection to Spv K⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩ constructible; the induction hypothesis gives a classical point below, which lifts. General A: a surjection K⟨X⟩ → A and openness of Spv A → Spv K⟨X⟩ in the constructible topology.

(i)–(iv), Huber's second proof (Remark 4.7, preferred for formalisation, no model theory): identify Spa(A, A°) with the space (Max A)~ of prime filters of rational subdomains of Max A (4.7.1–4.7.3: a point v extends to the rational localisation A_U iff it satisfies the defining inequalities, by the universal property of rational subdomains, AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affinoid-subdomain; primeness uses refinement of finite affinoid coverings by rational ones, AdicSpacesPartII:R1/gerritzen-grauert, tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.exists_span_eq_top_forall_rationalSubset_subset_of_isTateRing), and use that Max A is dense in the patch topology of (Max A)~, a closed subspace of {0,1}^{rational subdomains} (4.7.4).

(ii) from (i): a constructible T ⊆ Spa(A, A°) is M ∩ Spa(A, A°) for a constructible M ⊆ Spv A (Huber 1993 3.5(ii)), and Spa(A, A°) ⊆ L_A. (iii) apply (ii) to the symmetric difference. (iv) rational subsets are constructible, U ∩ Max A is rational by definition, and (iii) gives injectivity; surjectivity and the covering statement follow from (iii) applied to U and ⋃ Uᵢ.
acceptance: For A = K⟨T⟩ the rational subset {|T| ≤ |ϖ|} of Spa(A, A°) corresponds to the Weierstrass domain {x ∈ Max A : |T(x)| ≤ |ϖ|}, and the rational subset {|T| = 1} = {1 ≤ |T|} to the Laurent domain {x : |T(x)| ≥ 1}.

The Gauss point is not classical, yet every constructible set containing it contains a classical point (Corollary 4.2); by contrast the closed set {x_{<1}} (the rank-two point below the Gauss point with |T| < 1) is pro-constructible but not constructible and contains no classical point.

nodes.title: Restricted power series are flat over polynomials for strongly noetherian Tate rings
nodes.statement: Let A be a complete strongly noetherian Tate ring (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsStronglyNoetherian) and d ≥ 0. Then the inclusion A[T₁,…,T_d] → A⟨T₁,…,T_d⟩ is flat.
hypotheses: A complete Hausdorff, Tate, strongly noetherian; no noetherian ring of definition is assumed in general
proofSteps: Choose a ring of integral elements A⁺ and a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ ∈ A⁺. Every restricted series has coefficients tending to 0, so ϖ^N·f has coefficients in A⁺ for N large: A⟨T⟩ = A⁺⟨T⟩[1/ϖ], and A[T] = A⁺[T][1/ϖ]. Flatness is preserved by localisation, so it suffices that A⁺[T] → A⁺⟨T⟩ is flat (Zavyalov, proof of Lemma 6.7).
Flatness of A⁺[T] → A⁺⟨T⟩: Zavyalov cites Fujiwara–Kato, Foundations of Rigid Geometry I, Prop. 0.8.2.18 and Thm. 0.8.2.19 (adhesive rings); not read — recorded as a gap.

Special case with a noetherian ring of definition A₀ ∋ ϖ (for instance A affinoid over a discretely valued K): A₀[T] is noetherian and A₀⟨T⟩ is its ϖ-adic completion, hence flat over it (mathlib:AdicCompletion.flat_of_isNoetherian); invert ϖ.
acceptance: For A = K a complete rank-one field and d = 1: K⟨T⟩ is a torsion-free, hence flat, module over the principal ideal domain K[T].

uses.how: relative case (Zavyalov Lemma 6.7): Spec A⟨T⟩ → Spec A[T] is flat

nodes.title: Affinoid opens locally of finite type over a noetherian-type affinoid are of topologically finite type (Huber 1994 Proposition 3.6)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of adic spaces locally of finite type (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-type-morphism-classes) and U ⊆ X, V ⊆ Y open affinoid subspaces with f(U) ⊆ V, and assume that O_Y(V) has a noetherian ring of definition or is a strongly noetherian Tate ring. Then the morphism of affinoid rings (O_Y(V), O⁺_Y(V)) → (O_X(U), O⁺_X(U)) is of topologically finite type. In particular, for an affinoid adic space Spa(B, B⁺) locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°) (K complete of rank one), B is a K-affinoid algebra and B⁺ = B° (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/tft-plus-ring-power-bounded).
hypotheses: O_Y(V) of Huber's noetherian type; U and V arbitrary open affinoids (not just members of a chosen cover)
proofSteps: Routine part: U is quasi-compact, so it is covered by finitely many rational subsets U₁,…,U_r of U with (O_Y(V), O⁺_Y(V)) → (O_X(U_i), O⁺_X(U_i)) of topologically finite type (definition of locally of finite type; rational subsets form a basis; a rational subset of U inside an affinoid W is rational in W; Huber 1994 Lemma 3.5(ii),(iv) for rational localisations and composites).

Non-routine part: descending topological finite type from the finite rational cover {U_i} to U. Huber 1994 defers the proof to [H2] ('Coherent sheaves on adic spaces', announced, never published); Huber 1996 p. 47 cites the non-public habilitation [Hu4, 3.3.23 and 3.8.15] and [Hu2]. No public proof has been read; recorded as a gap.
Consumer: the proof of Huber 1994 Proposition 4.5(v) (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-quasi-separated-equivalence (iv)).
acceptance: For U = Spa(K⟨T⟩⟨1/T⟩, K°⟨T, 1/T⟩) ⊆ Spa(K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩) over Spa(K, K°), the global ring K⟨T, T⁻¹⟩ is K-affinoid (a quotient of K⟨T, S⟩ by (TS − 1)) with plus ring its power-bounded subring.

nodes.title: A K-scheme locally of finite type is connected iff its rigid analytification is connected
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value of rank one and X a K-scheme locally of finite type, with rigid analytification i_X: X^an → X (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytification). Then X is connected if and only if X^an is connected (X^an has no admissible covering by two disjoint nonempty admissible opens). The core case: if X is normal and connected, then X^an is connected. More precisely, the irreducible components of X^an are the analytifications Z^an of the irreducible components Z of X (Conrad 1999, Theorem 2.3.1).
hypotheses: K complete, nontrivially valued, rank one
X locally of finite type over K; no separatedness or quasi-compactness assumed
proofSteps: X^an connected ⇒ X connected: a decomposition X = U ⊔ V into disjoint nonempty open subschemes analytifies to an admissible covering of X^an by the disjoint admissible opens U^an, V^an (open immersions analytify to open immersions and Zariski covers to admissible covers, AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytification), both nonempty because i_X is onto the closed points.

Reduction to the normal case (Conrad, proof of A.1.3(1)): a scheme or rigid space is connected iff any two irreducible components are joined by a finite chain of components meeting pairwise. For irreducible components Z, Z' of X meeting at a point, Z^an and Z'^an meet (i_X is onto closed points, and Z ∩ Z' has a closed point); the Z^an cover X^an admissibly. So it suffices that Z^an is connected for Z integral; the normalisation Z̃ → Z is finite surjective and (·)^an takes finite surjections to finite surjections, so it suffices that Z̃^an is connected for Z̃ normal and connected.

Normal connected X, reduction to X affine and K algebraically closed (Conrad, proof of Theorem 2.3.1): cover X by affine opens linked by chains; for affine X choose a finite Galois K'/K such that the connected components of X_{K'} are geometrically irreducible (EGA IV₂ 4.5.11); Gal(K'/K) acts transitively on the connected components of (X_{K'})^an (Conrad Lemma 2.3.2, Galois descent over affinoids); pass to the completed algebraic closure, using that a quasi-separated rigid space is connected if it is so after a base field extension (injectivity of A → A ⊗̂_K K').

K algebraically closed, X normal connected affine: embed X as a dense open of a normal projective P; by Lütkebohmert's Riemann extension theorem (bounded functions on the complement of a nowhere dense analytic subset of a normal rigid space extend) applied to idempotents, X^an is connected iff P^an is; by rigid GAGA for projective schemes (Köpf) O(P^an) = O(P), which has no nontrivial idempotents since P is connected.

Gaps to be recorded: Lütkebohmert's Riemann extension theorem, rigid GAGA for projective schemes over a complete rank-one field, change of base field for quasi-separated rigid spaces, and the theory of irreducible components of rigid spaces (Conrad §2.1-2.2; the identity principle is AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-identity-principle) are not yet nodes of this stage.
acceptance: A¹_K is connected and (A¹_K)^an, the increasing union of closed discs of radius |c|^{-j}, is connected although no finite set of discs covers it.

Spec(K × K)^an is two points, disconnected; the nodal cubic y² = x²(x + 1) is irreducible and its analytification is connected (indeed irreducible), even though near the node it has two analytic branches.

nodes.title: Morphisms of locally ringed spaces glue along open covers
nodes.statement: Let X and Y be locally ringed spaces and (U_i)_{i∈ι} an open cover of X. Given morphisms of locally ringed spaces f_i : X|_{U_i} → Y (Mathlib LocallyRingedSpace.restrict) such that f_i and f_j have the same restriction to X|_{U_i ∩ U_j} for all i, j, there is a unique morphism f : X → Y of locally ringed spaces whose restriction to each X|_{U_i} is f_i. Equivalently, U ↦ Hom_LRS(X|_U, Y) is a sheaf of sets on X. (Mathlib has this only for schemes, AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms; formal schemes are locally ringed spaces that are not schemes.)
hypotheses: X, Y locally ringed spaces; (U_i) an open cover of X
f_i agree on pairwise overlaps
proofSteps: Underlying continuous maps glue (Mathlib ContinuousMap.liftCover).

Sheaf maps: for V ⊆ Y open, the ring maps O_Y(V) → O_X(f_i⁻¹(V) ∩ U_i) agree after restriction to the overlaps, so by the sheaf property of O_X (Mathlib TopCat.Sheaf.existsUnique_gluing) they glue to a map O_Y(V) → O_X(f⁻¹(V)); naturality in V and multiplicativity are checked after restriction to the U_i (Mathlib TopCat.Sheaf.eq_of_locally_eq).
The stalk map of f at x ∈ U_i is the stalk map of f_i, hence local (Mathlib IsLocalHom).
Uniqueness: two morphisms with the same restrictions to all U_i have the same underlying map and, by eq_of_locally_eq, the same sheaf maps.
acceptance: For X a scheme and Y = Spec R this recovers, cover by cover, the gluing used in the proof of EGA I, 2.2.4 (Γ–Spec correspondence).

For the cover of X by X itself the statement is trivial; for the cover of Spf A by basic opens D(f) it is what AdicSpacesPartII:F0/spf-morphism-correspondence uses to pass from affine to general sources.

uses.how: general source X: a morphism X → Spf A is glued from morphisms on affine formal opens (EGA I, 10.4.6, 'proof as in 2.2.4').

sources.locator: Ch. I, proof of (2.2.4) Proposition, printed p. 99
sources.match: EGA glues morphisms of ringed spaces defined on the members of an open cover and agreeing on overlaps, as a routine step; EGA I 10.4.6 invokes the same argument for formal schemes.

nodes.title: A nilpotent thickening of an affine scheme is affine
nodes.statement: Let X be a scheme and 𝒥 ⊆ O_X a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf (Mathlib Scheme.IdealSheafData) with 𝒥^n = 0 for some n ≥ 1, and let X_0 = V(𝒥) be the closed subscheme it defines (Mathlib IdealSheafData.subscheme). Then X is affine if and only if X_0 is affine (EGA I, 5.1.9). In particular, in a sequence of closed immersions X_0 → X_1 → ⋯ that are homeomorphisms with nilpotent kernels, all X_n are affine as soon as X_0 is.
hypotheses: 𝒥 quasi-coherent and nilpotent (𝒥^n = 0)
proofSteps: Necessity: a closed subscheme of an affine scheme is affine (Mathlib IsClosedImmersion.isAffine_surjective_of_isAffine / closed immersions are affine morphisms).
Sufficiency, reduction: the closed subschemes X_k = V(𝒥^{k+1}) form a chain in which each X_k is defined in X_{k+1} by an ideal of square zero, so by induction on k it suffices to treat 𝒥² = 0.

Case 𝒥² = 0: 𝒥 is a quasi-coherent module over O_X/𝒥, i.e. over the affine scheme X_0 (same underlying space), so H¹(X, 𝒥) = H¹(X_0, 𝒥) = 0 by acyclicity of quasi-coherent modules on affine schemes (supplier tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge layer B, part (B); EGA I, 5.1.9.2); hence A = Γ(X, O_X) → Γ(X_0, O_{X_0}) = A_0 is surjective with kernel 𝔍 = Γ(X, 𝒥) (TauCeti Scheme.Modules.sections_surjective for 0 → 𝒥 → O_X → O_{X_0} → 0).

Let f = X.toSpecΓ : X → Spec A (Mathlib Scheme.toSpecΓ). Its restriction to X_0 is the isomorphism X_0 ≅ Spec(A/𝔍) = Spec A_0, so f is a homeomorphism; f^♯ restricts to an isomorphism 𝔍^~ ≅ 𝒥 (𝒥 = 𝔍^~ as a quasi-coherent O_{X_0}-module) and induces an isomorphism modulo the ideals, so by the five lemma f^♯ is an isomorphism and X is affine (Mathlib IsAffine: IsIso X.toSpecΓ).
acceptance: X = Spec k[ε]/(ε²) with 𝒥 = (ε): X_0 = Spec k is affine and so is X.
For X_n = Spec(ℤ/p^{n+1}) all X_n are affine; for a non-affine scheme X (e.g. P¹_k) no thickening of X_0 = X by a nilpotent ideal is affine.

uses.how: affine case: if X_0 is affine, every X_n of an adic thickening system is affine.
finiteness of f′: f′ is affine because its restriction over the reduction is (affineness of a thickening).
X_0 affine (closed in the affine Y_0) implies every X_n affine.

nodes.title: Internal Hom of sheaves of modules; compatibility of ⊗ and ℋom with pullback and with M ↦ M~
nodes.statement: Let (X, O_X) be a ringed space (a scheme, or a locally noetherian formal scheme with its sheaf of rings TauCeti.SheafOfModules.ringCatSheaf) and F, G sheaves of O_X-modules. (a) The internal Hom ℋom_{O_X}(F, G) is the sheaf of O_X-modules U ↦ Hom_{O_U}(F|_U, G|_U) (EGA 0, 4.1.5); Γ(X, ℋom(F, G)) = Hom_{O_X}(F, G), ℋom is left exact in each variable and ℋom(O_X, G) = G. (b) For every morphism of ringed spaces f : Y → X, f*(F ⊗ G) ≅ f*F ⊗ f*G canonically (EGA 0, 4.3.3.1; ⊗ is Tau Ceti SheafOfModules.tensorProduct, f* is Mathlib SheafOfModules.pullback). (c) If F is of finite presentation and f is flat, the canonical map f*ℋom(F, G) → ℋom(f*F, f*G) is an isomorphism (EGA 0, 6.7.6). (d) On Spec A, (M ⊗_A N)~ ≅ M~ ⊗ N~, and Hom_A(M, N)~ ≅ ℋom(M~, N~) when M is finitely presented (EGA I, 1.3.12); hence on a locally noetherian scheme ⊗ and ℋom of coherent modules are coherent. (The formal-scheme analogue is recorded in AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-formal-module and deduced from the affine case.)
hypotheses: F of finite presentation for the flat-pullback isomorphism; coherence statements on locally noetherian (formal) schemes
proofSteps: (a) Presheaf U ↦ Hom_{O_U}(F|_U, G|_U) with restriction of morphisms; it is a sheaf because morphisms of sheaves glue (Mathlib TopCat.Sheaf.existsUnique_gluing on components), and an O_X-module via Γ(U, O_X); left exactness and ℋom(O_X, G) = G are sectionwise.
(b) The canonical map f⁻¹F ⊗_{f⁻¹O_X} f⁻¹G → f⁻¹(F ⊗ G) is an isomorphism on stalks (stalks of tensor products are tensor products of stalks); tensor with O_Y (EGA 0, 4.3.3.1).

(c) Both sides are left exact in F and turn finite direct sums into products; from a local presentation O^m → O^n → F → 0 and exactness of f* (flatness) the five lemma reduces to F = O_X, where both sides are f*G (EGA 0, 6.7.6).

(d) On basic opens D(f), (M ⊗ N)~(D(f)) = M_f ⊗ N_f and Hom_A(M, N)_f = Hom_{A_f}(M_f, N_f) for finitely presented M; conclude with Mathlib tilde and tildeEquiv (EGA I, 1.3.12). Coherence on locally noetherian schemes follows.
acceptance: ℋom(O_X, G) = G, ℋom(O_X^n, G) = G^n, and f*O_X ⊗ f*O_X = O_Y.
On Spec ℤ, ℋom((ℤ/p)~, O) = 0 while ℋom(O, (ℤ/p)~) = (ℤ/p)~; applying ℋom(−, O) to 0 → ℤ → ℤ → ℤ/p → 0 gives 0 → 0 → ℤ → ℤ, not right exact.

uses.how: (iv): (F ⊗ G)^ ≅ F̂ ⊗ Ĝ and ℋom(F, G)^ ≅ ℋom(F̂, Ĝ) are (b) and (c) for the flat morphism i_X.
(iii): û = 0 is tested on the coherent sheaf ℋom(F, G).
(ii): (M ⊗ N)^Δ ≅ M^Δ ⊗ N^Δ and Hom_A(M, N)^Δ ≅ ℋom(M^Δ, N^Δ) combine (d) with the compatibilities of completion.

nodes.title: Closure properties of coherent modules on a locally noetherian formal scheme
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally noetherian formal scheme and Coh(X) the category of coherent (locally finitely presented) O_X-modules (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-formal-module). (i) O_X is a coherent sheaf of rings and every ideal of definition is coherent (EGA I, 10.11.1); hence F is coherent iff it is of finite type with kernels of all O_U^n → F|_U of finite type. (ii) Coh(X) is an abelian full subcategory of O_X-modules, closed under kernels, cokernels, images and extensions; F ⊗ G and ℋom(F, G) are coherent for coherent F, G. (iii) For a morphism f : X → Y of locally noetherian formal schemes, f* maps Coh(Y) into Coh(X), and on affine pieces (Spf φ)*(N^Δ) ≅ (A ⊗_B N)^Δ (EGA I, 10.10.8). (iv) Every O_X-linear map of coherent modules is continuous for the limit topologies Γ(U, F) = lim_n Γ(U, F ⊗ O_X/𝒥^{n+1}) (U quasi-compact), and coherent submodules have closed sections (EGA I, 10.11.6).
hypotheses: X (and Y) locally noetherian formal schemes
proofSteps: (i) Local; on Spf A it is AdicSpacesPartII:F0/affine-coherent-equivalence (iii) together with coherence of ideals of definition I^Δ (exactness of (·)^Δ on I ⊆ A).

(ii) Local; on noetherian affine formal opens Coh(Spf A) ≃ finite A-modules by an exact equivalence (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/affine-coherent-equivalence (i), (iv)), and finite modules over a noetherian ring are closed under kernels, cokernels and extensions; ⊗ and ℋom by affine-coherent-equivalence (ii) and AdicSpacesPartII:F0/internal-hom-sheaf-of-modules.
(iii) Local on X and Y; on Spf A → Spf B, f*(N^Δ) = (A ⊗_B N)^Δ (EGA I, 10.10.8; AdicSpacesPartII:F0/associated-formal-module, pullbackIso) with A ⊗_B N finite over A.

(iv) Hom_{O_X}(F, G) = lim_n Hom(F_n, G_n) (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-as-inverse-system (ii)), so every map is a limit of maps of the discrete reductions, hence continuous; a coherent submodule has sections the kernel of a continuous map to a separated group (EGA I, 10.11.6).
acceptance: O_X, every ideal of definition and every M^Δ on Spf A (M finite) are coherent; their ⊗ and ℋom are coherent.
The O-module with sections ℚ_p over the point of Spf ℤ_p is not coherent, and neither is any sheaf whose sections are not finite over the affine rings.

nodes.title: Formal glueing of modules along a flat map that is an isomorphism modulo I
nodes.statement: Let φ₀ : R → S be a flat ring map and I ⊆ R a finitely generated ideal such that R/I → S/IS is an isomorphism (e.g. S = AdicCompletion I R for R noetherian). Given an R-module N, an S-module M′ and an S-linear map φ : M′ → N ⊗_R S whose kernel and cokernel are I-power torsion, there are an R-module M, an R-linear map ψ : M → N and an isomorphism M ⊗_R S ≅ M′ compatible with φ and ψ; moreover Ker ψ ≅ Ker φ and Coker ψ ≅ Coker φ (Stacks Tag 0ALK (1)). The dual statement for φ : M ⊗_R S → N′ holds likewise (Tag 0ALK (2)).
hypotheses: R → S flat; I finitely generated; R/I ≅ S/IS
ker φ and coker φ I-power torsion
proofSteps: Write I = (f_1, …, f_t). I-power torsion modules die after inverting any f_i, so each localisation φ_{f_i} is an isomorphism; hence (M′, N_{f_i}, φ_{f_i}, canonical identifications on overlaps) is a glueing datum for (R → S; f_1, …, f_t) (Stacks, More on Algebra, Remark 15.91.10).

Formal glueing (Stacks, More on Algebra, Proposition 15.91.16: for a flat R → S with R/I ≅ S/IS and I = (f_1, …, f_t), R-modules are equivalent to glueing data (an S-module, R_{f_i}-modules and compatible isomorphisms over S_{f_i}); its proof uses that I-power-torsion R-modules and S-modules coincide, Lemma 15.91.3): the datum comes from an R-module M with M ⊗_R S = M′ and M_{f_i} = N_{f_i} compatibly. This equivalence is part of what this node must formalise.

The morphism of glueing data given by φ and the identities of the N_{f_i} corresponds to ψ : M → N compatible with φ; Ker ψ ≅ Ker φ and Coker ψ ≅ Coker φ because both are I-power torsion and I-power-torsion modules over R and S correspond (Lemma 15.91.3).
acceptance: R = ℤ_(p), S = ℤ_p, I = (p), N = R, M′ = pℤ_p ⊂ ℤ_p = N ⊗ S (cokernel F_p): M = pℤ_(p), ψ the inclusion.
N = 0, M′ = ℤ/p (φ = 0, kernel ℤ/p): M = ℤ/p, whose base change to ℤ_p is M′.

uses.how: affine step: from φ : M′ → N ⊗_A Â with I^t-torsion kernel and cokernel build the A-module M and ψ : M → N.

sources.match: Hypotheses of the formal glueing lemma.

nodes.title: Coherent formal modules with proper support form Serre subcategories
nodes.statement: Let S be a noetherian scheme, f : X → S of finite type, 𝓘 ⊆ O_X a quasi-coherent ideal and Coh(X̂_{/V(𝓘)}) ≃ Coh(X, 𝓘) (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-as-inverse-system). The following full subcategories are Serre subcategories (closed under subobjects, quotients and extensions): (1) the objects G = (G_n) such that Supp G_0 (= Supp G_n for all n) is proper over S; (2) the objects annihilated by the ideal sheaf of some closed subscheme Z ⊆ X proper over S (Stacks Tag 0CYV, Lemma 30.26.11).
hypotheses: S noetherian; f of finite type; 𝓘 quasi-coherent
proofSteps: For a short exact sequence 0 → (G_n) → (F_n) → (H_n) → 0 in Coh(X, 𝓘): G_n → F_n → H_n → 0 is exact for every n, and G_n is a quotient of Ker(F_m → H_m) for some m ≥ n (Artin–Rees, proof of Stacks Lemma 30.23.2).

(1) Supp F_n = Supp F_0 for all n; the supports of G_0 and H_0 are closed subsets of Supp F_0, and Supp F_0 ⊆ Supp G_0 ∪ Supp H_0; closed subsets of proper subsets and finite unions of proper closed subsets are proper over S (Stacks Tag 0CYQ, Lemma 30.26.5, and the reduced-structure argument).

(2) Subobjects and quotients of objects killed by 𝓘_Z are killed by 𝓘_Z; for an extension, if 𝓘_{Z₁} kills (G_n) and 𝓘_{Z₂} kills (H_n) then 𝓘_{Z₁}𝓘_{Z₂} kills (F_n), and V(𝓘_{Z₁}𝓘_{Z₂}) = Z₁ ∪ Z₂ is proper over S.
acceptance: For X = A¹_{ℤ_p} over S = Spec ℤ_p and 𝓘 = (p): Ô_{V(x)} lies in both subcategories, Ô_X in neither (its support A¹_{F_p} is not proper).

uses.how: last step: G is an extension of objects supported on proper closed subschemes, hence supported on one.

sources.match: Both subcategories (support of F_1 proper; annihilated by the ideal of a proper closed subscheme) are Serre subcategories.

nodes.title: Reduction of étale coverings to rational and finite étale coverings on a stable basis (Kedlaya-Liu 8.2.20-8.2.21)
nodes.statement: Let X be an analytic adic space with its étale site X_ét (AdicEtaleGeometry A1's local-description sense), and let B be a class of affinoid objects Spa(C, C⁺) of X_ét with C complete Tate and sheafy that covers every object of X_ét and is closed under fibre products, finite étale extensions and rational subdomain embeddings. (i) Let P be a property of coverings in X_ét of and by elements of B such that (a) a covering with a refinement having P has P, (b) composites of coverings having P have P, (c) every rational covering of an element of B has P, (d) every surjective finite étale morphism Y' -> Y of elements of B, viewed as a covering, has P. Then every covering of and by elements of B has P. (ii) Let F be a presheaf of abelian groups on X_ét such that, for every Y ∈ B and every covering V of Y that is a simple Laurent covering or a surjective finite étale morphism, Ȟ^0(Y, F; V) = F(Y) (resp. Ȟ^i(Y, F; V) = 0 for all i > 0 and Ȟ^0 = F(Y)). Then for every covering V of Y ∈ B by elements of B, H^0(Y, F) = Ȟ^0(Y, F; V) = F(Y) (resp. also H^i(Y, F) = Ȟ^i(Y, F; V) = 0 for i > 0).
hypotheses: Kedlaya-Liu state this for preadic spaces over an analytic field; the argument does not use the field.
B consists of sheafy affinoids so that the Čech complexes are those of adic affinoid spaces.
proofSteps: (i), rational part: by (a) and the quasi-compact factorisation of étale maps (Kedlaya-Liu Lemma 8.2.17(b): Y -> Z -> X with Y -> Z surjective and Z -> X an open immersion), (c) extends to all coverings for the adic topology.

(i), key case (e): a surjective Z -> U between elements of B factoring as an open immersion Z -> V followed by a finite étale V -> U has P. Induct on the maximal degree d of V -> U. For d = 1 the map V -> U is an isomorphism. For d > 1 use the complement W of the diagonal in V ×_U V, which is finite étale over V of degree d - 1, and combine the induction hypothesis with (b), (c), (d) and (a) as in Kedlaya-Liu's proof.
(i), general covering: refine each Y_i -> Y locally into open-in-finite-étale pieces, cover their images by elements of B (Lemma 8.2.17(b)), and apply (e), (c), (b), (a).

(ii): as in the analytic case (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/cech-acyclicity-simple-laurent-reduction, AdicSpacesPartII:R3/rational-covering-reduction), with (i) replacing the rational reduction. Successively F(Y) -> Ȟ^0 is injective, then bijective, and in the second situation every covering of and by elements of B is universally Čech-acyclic. Standard homological algebra (Cartan's criterion) then gives the sheaf cohomology.
acceptance: For X a rigid space and B its étale affinoids, this is de Jong-van der Put Proposition 3.2.2.
Used with B = composites of rational localisations and finite étale maps over a sousperfectoid affinoid (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-stably-adic).

uses.how: acyclicity and descent of M̃ on the étale site

nodes.title: Vector bundles on the étale site of an affinoid with a stable basis (Kedlaya-Liu 8.2.22(c),(d))
nodes.statement: Let X = Spa(A, A⁺) with (A, A⁺) a complete Tate sheafy pair, and let B be a stable basis of X_ét as in AdicSpacesPartII:R5/stable-basis-covering-reduction. (c) For every finite projective A-module M, the presheaf M̃, Y = Spa(C, C⁺) ↦ M ⊗_A C, is an acyclic sheaf on B: H^0(Y, M̃) = M ⊗_A C and H^i(Y, M̃) = 0 for i > 0, for every Y ∈ B. (d) M ↦ M̃ is an equivalence from finite projective A-modules to finite locally free O_{X_ét}-modules, with quasi-inverse E ↦ E(X).
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) sheafy; B a stable basis (closed under fibre products, finite étale extensions and rational subdomains).
Only finite projective modules: rational localisation is not flat in general.
proofSteps: Rational coverings: M̃ is Čech-acyclic on simple Laurent coverings of every Y ∈ B (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-projective-module-acyclicity; AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheafy-cech-acyclicity for M = A).

Surjective finite étale Y' -> Y: the Čech complex of M ⊗_A C -> M ⊗_A C' is exact by faithfully flat descent (C -> C' is finite étale and faithfully flat; AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-projective-etale-descent).
(c) follows from AdicSpacesPartII:R5/stable-basis-covering-reduction (ii).

(d): full faithfulness from (c) in degree 0. For essential surjectivity, a finite locally free O_{X_ét}-module is trivialised on a covering of X by elements of B. The property 'every finite locally free module trivialised on the covering descends to a finite projective module' holds for rational coverings (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheafy-tate-acyclicity-and-kiehl-gluing) and for surjective finite étale maps (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-projective-etale-descent). It is inherited by refinements and composites, so it holds for all coverings by AdicSpacesPartII:R5/stable-basis-covering-reduction (i).
acceptance: For M = A: H^i(X_ét, O) = 0 for i > 0 (Hansen-Kedlaya Proposition 5.8 for strongly sheafy A).
For X a smooth affinoid over a p-adic field, vector bundles on X_ét are finite projective O(X)-modules.

O_{X_ét} is an acyclic étale sheaf and vector bundles descend, for sousperfectoid X

nodes.title: Tilde-limits are stable under base change along morphisms locally of weakly finite type (Huber Remark 2.4.3(ii))
nodes.statement: Let I be a cofiltered category with a final object j, (X_i)_{i ∈ I} a system of quasi-compact quasi-separated adic spaces with adic transition morphisms, and X a quasi-compact quasi-separated adic space with compatible adic morphisms φ_i: X -> X_i such that X ∼ lim_i X_i (Huber Definition 2.4.2). Let f: Y -> X_j be a morphism of quasi-compact quasi-separated adic spaces that is locally of weakly finite type, and assume that the fibre products Y ×_{X_j} X and Y ×_{X_j} X_i exist in adic spaces and are affinoid-locally Spa of completed tensor products (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-fibre-product). Then Y ×_{X_j} X ∼ lim_i Y ×_{X_j} X_i.
hypotheses: The existence of the fibre products is a hypothesis (supplied by AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence in the stably sheafy case and by AdicSpacesPartII:R5/perfectoid-times-smooth-fibre-product for perfectoid X).
proofSteps: By Huber Remark 2.4.3(i) (in ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limits-and-cohomological-continuity) it suffices to show (a)' bijectivity of |Y ×_{X_j} X| -> lim_i |Y ×_{X_j} X_i| and (b)' the density condition together with an open W of some |Y ×_{X_j} X_i| whose preimage lies in the chosen affinoid.

Bijectivity: for x ∈ X with images x_i, condition (a) makes ∪_i k(x_i) dense in k(x). Hence Y ×_{X_j} Spa κ(x) -> lim_i Y ×_{X_j} Spa κ(x_i) is bijective. With the description of fibres of fibre products (Huber (1.2.4)) this gives (a)'.

Density: for a point z over (y, x, x_j), choose affinoid neighbourhoods U_y, U_x (rational in the affinoid U of condition (b) for x) and U_j with O(U_y) of topologically finite type over O(U_j). Then O(U_y)·O(U_x) is dense in O(U_y ×_{U_j} U_x). The images of O_{X_i}(V), for V ⊇ φ_i(U_x), are dense in O(U_x): the defining functions of U_x can be taken from a finite level by Huber 1994 Lemma 3.10. Hence (b)' holds for U_y ×_{U_j} U_x.
Openness: choose P open in some |X_i| with x ∈ φ_i^{-1}(P) ⊆ U_x. Then Q = a^{-1}(P) ∩ b^{-1}(U_y) is open in |Y ×_{X_j} X_i| with z ∈ c^{-1}(Q) ⊆ U_y ×_{U_j} U_x.
acceptance: For Y = X_j the statement is the hypothesis.
BHW Corollary 3.5: Y = X_1 ×_L U for a smooth U (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/perfectoid-times-smooth-tilde-limit).

nodes.title: Rational localisations of reduced affinoid algebras are reduced, and preserve A⁺ = A° (KL Lemma 2.5.9(c),(d))
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value of rank one and (A, A⁺) a Huber pair with A a K-affinoid algebra (KL: an adic affinoid algebra over K). Let U ⊆ Spa(A, A⁺) be a rational subset with representing complete pair (B, B⁺) = (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)). (c) If A is reduced, then B is reduced. (d) If A⁺ = A°, then B⁺ = B°. Hence for a reduced affinoid rigid space X = Spa(A, A°), every O_X(U) with U rational is a reduced affinoid algebra, so it is uniform (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/reduced-affinoid-supremum-norm), and O_X⁺(U) = O_X(U)° is an open bounded subring.
hypotheses: K complete rank-one nonarchimedean, nontrivially valued
A K-affinoid (topologically of finite type)
for (d): A⁺ = A°
proofSteps: B ≅ A⟨T_1, ..., T_n⟩/(gT_1 - f_1, ..., gT_n - f_n), since the ideal is closed in the noetherian Banach algebra (KL Lemma 2.5.9(a); anchor Layer 3.1 rational localisation).

U ∩ Max(A) is a rational subdomain of Max(A) represented by A -> B (KL 2.5.9(b), BGR 7.2.3/4). Reducedness passes to affinoid subdomains (BGR Corollary 7.3.2/10, imported by KL; gap: BGR is not a packet source).
(d) Apply KL Corollary 2.5.7 to the finite morphism A⟨T⟩ -> B: power-bounded elements of B are integral over the image of A°⟨T⟩, hence lie in B⁺ = the completed integral closure of A⁺[f/g].
acceptance: For A = K⟨x⟩ and U = {|x| ≤ |p|}: B = K⟨x/p⟩ is reduced and B° = O_K⟨x/p⟩ = B⁺.
Non-example: reducedness is not created, e.g. A = K⟨x, q⟩/(q²) gives non-reduced B for every nonempty U.

nodes.title: Flatness from flatness modulo powers of an ideal (the adic flatness criterion behind Bosch–Lütkebohmert I Lemma 1.6)
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative ring, I ⊆ A an ideal and M an A-module. Assume that for every finitely generated ideal a ⊆ A (1) the I-adic topology of A induces the I-adic topology of a: for every n there is m with a ∩ I^m ⊆ I^n a, and (2) a ⊗_A M is I-adically separated: ⋂_n I^n (a ⊗_A M) = 0. If M/I^n M is flat over A/I^n for every n ≥ 1, then M is flat over A. In the same situation, if moreover I ⊆ Jac(A) and M/IM is faithfully flat over A/I, then M is faithfully flat over A.
hypotheses: No noetherian or completeness hypothesis on A: (1) and (2) replace Artin–Rees and Krull intersection
For the faithful-flatness addendum, I must lie in the Jacobson radical of A
proofSteps: By the ideal criterion (Mathlib Module.Flat.iff_rTensor_injective) it suffices that a ⊗_A M → M is injective for every finitely generated ideal a ⊆ A.
Let x ∈ a ⊗_A M map to 0 in M. Fix n and choose m with a ∩ I^m ⊆ I^n a by (1).
a/(a ∩ I^m) is an ideal of A/I^m and (a/(a ∩ I^m)) ⊗_{A/I^m} M/I^mM = (a/(a ∩ I^m)) ⊗_A M; flatness of M/I^mM over A/I^m makes its map to M/I^mM injective, so x maps to 0 in (a/(a ∩ I^m)) ⊗_A M.
By right exactness of ⊗, x lies in the image of (a ∩ I^m) ⊗_A M ⊆ image of I^n a ⊗_A M = I^n (a ⊗_A M).
As n is arbitrary, x ∈ ⋂_n I^n (a ⊗_A M) = 0 by (2).

Faithful flatness: if N is a finitely generated A-module with N ⊗_A M = 0, then (N/IN) ⊗_{A/I} (M/IM) = 0, so N = IN and N = 0 by Nakayama (I ⊆ Jac(A)); this is Bosch–Lütkebohmert's argument on p. 296.
acceptance: A noetherian, I ⊆ Jac(A), M finite over a noetherian A-algebra B with IB ⊆ Jac(B): (1) is Artin–Rees and (2) Krull's intersection theorem, giving the noetherian local flatness criterion used in the noetherian case of Bosch–Lütkebohmert I 1.6.
