nodes.title: Conrad's Berthelot-type generic fibre preserves finiteness, smoothness, flatness, properness and fibre dimension (Conrad genpaper Theorem 3.1.6)
nodes.statement: Let C be an adic noetherian ring with a continuous map C → R to the valuation ring of a complete nonarchimedean field k (no discreteness assumption), and let f: X → Y be a morphism in FS_C that is locally topologically of finite type. Then: (a) if f is finite so is f^rig; (b) if f is formally smooth of pure relative dimension d then f^rig is smooth of pure relative dimension d (formally étale ⇒ étale); (c) if f is finite flat of constant rank d so is f^rig; (d) if f is proper so is f^rig; (e) if f is flat (resp. faithfully flat) so is f^rig; (f) if all fibres of f have dimension ≤ d so do those of f^rig; (g) if f is flat with geometrically reduced fibres of pure dimension d, so is f^rig.
hypotheses: f locally topologically of finite type in FS_C; k arbitrary complete nonarchimedean

(d) without discreteness uses Temkin [Te, Cor. 4.4, 4.5] and (f),(g) use Conrad Theorem A.2.1 (change of base field via Raynaud models); neither is a node of the packet: (d) is the recorded gap of node formal-rigid-properness-comparison, and Conrad A.2.1 is an additional unplanned import
proofSteps: (b): locally, a formally smooth f of pure relative dimension d is formally étale over a relative formal affine space Y{{T_1, …, T_d}}, by the structure theorems for smooth and étale maps and topological invariance of the étale site (nodes smooth-formal-scheme, formal-etale-site-invariance); (·)^rig respects open immersions, reducing to B = A{{T}}{{T, U}}/(h(T), Uh'(T) − 1) with h monic, where the claim is direct.

Case Y locally topologically of finite type over Spf C: base change along Spf R → Spf C and pass to Raynaud models (nodes raynaud-generic-fibre, raynaud-theorem); (a), (c), (e) are then the corresponding statements for Raynaud's functor, (d) is Temkin's theorem, (f), (g) are Conrad A.2.1.

General Y = Spf A with A ≅ C[[q]]{{T}}/(h): after replacing C by its image in R (and by C[[π]] if |·| is trivial on C), choose c ∈ C with 0 < |c| < 1; the base change f_c along q_j ↦ cq_j is topologically of finite type and f_c^rig is f^rig over Y_{|c|} = Y^rig ∩ {|q_j| ≤ |c|}.
The Y_r (r ∈ (0,1) ∩ √|k^×|) admissibly cover Y^rig; each property can be checked after a finite extension of k, which reduces Y_r to some Y_{|c|}.
acceptance: For C = Z and the Tate curve over Z[[q^{1/n}]], (d),(e) give a proper flat rigid curve over the open unit disc (Conrad genpaper §3.1, after Theorem 3.1.6).

nodes.title: Coherent modules and coherent rings (the ring case of EGA 0 §5.3, as recalled in Bosch–Lütkebohmert I §1)
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative ring. A finitely generated A-module M is coherent if every finitely generated submodule of M is finitely presented; A is a coherent ring if it is coherent as an A-module (every finitely generated ideal is finitely presented). If two of the modules in a short exact sequence 0 → M' → M → M'' → 0 are coherent, so is the third; hence finite direct sums, kernels, cokernels and images of maps between coherent modules, and sums and intersections of coherent submodules of a coherent module, are coherent. Over a coherent ring a module is coherent iff it is finitely presented, and M ⊗_A N and Hom_A(M, N) are coherent for coherent M, N. If A is coherent and a ⊆ A is a finitely generated ideal, A/a is a coherent ring and an A/a-module is coherent over A/a iff it is coherent over A.
hypotheses: No noetherian hypothesis: the point of the notion is the non-noetherian rings O_K⟨ξ⟩/a
Coherent means finitely generated with all finitely generated submodules finitely presented, not merely finitely presented
proofSteps: Two-out-of-three: standard diagram chases with finite presentations (EGA 0 5.3.2–5.3.4 in the sheaf setting; Bourbaki AC I §2 Exercise 11 for rings), using Mathlib Module.FinitePresentation.
Kernels, cokernels, images, sums, intersections: from two-out-of-three applied to the evident short exact sequences.
Over a coherent ring, finitely presented = coherent: A^n is coherent by two-out-of-three, and a finitely presented module is a cokernel of A^m → A^n.
Tensor and Hom: choose finite presentations and use right exactness of ⊗ and left exactness of Hom.

Quotients by finitely generated ideals: a is coherent (finitely generated submodule of the coherent A), so A/a is coherent over A; A/a-submodules and A-submodules of an A/a-module agree, and finite presentation over A and over A/a agree because a is finitely generated.
acceptance: Every noetherian ring is coherent, and a finitely generated module over it is coherent.

nodes.title: Almost noetherianity of modules over integral affinoid rings (Kiehl, Anhang Satz 5.1)
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value of rank one and valuation ring K°, A an affinoid K-algebra and A₀ ⊆ A a K°-subalgebra which is a ring of definition of A and a quotient of K°⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩ (Kiehl's case; e.g. the image of K°⟨X⟩ under a presentation K⟨X⟩ ↠ A). Let M be a finitely generated A₀-module and N ⊆ M an A₀-submodule. Then for every real ε with 0 < ε < 1 there is a finitely generated A₀-submodule N′ ⊆ N such that a·N ⊆ N′ for every a ∈ K° with |a| ≤ ε. If K is discretely valued, N itself is finitely generated (A₀ is noetherian).
hypotheses: K complete, nontrivially valued, rank one
A₀ a ring of definition of the affinoid K-algebra A, a quotient of K°⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩
M a finitely generated A₀-module, N ⊆ M an A₀-submodule
proofSteps: Discretely valued K: K°⟨X⟩ is the m-adic completion of K°[X], hence noetherian, and so is its quotient A₀; submodules of finite modules are finite.

Reduction: it suffices to treat A₀ = K°⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩ (N and M are then modules over it) and, by the usual induction on the number of generators of M (as for submodules of finite modules over a noetherian ring, shrinking ε at each step), the case M = A₀, N = b an ideal.
n = 0: A₀ = K°, b an ideal; choose x ∈ b with |x| close enough to sup_{y∈b}|y|; then a·b ⊆ K°·x for all a with |a| ≤ ε.

Induction step (n > 0, K not discretely valued, so |K^×| is dense): rescale so that ε < |b| := sup_{f∈b}|f| ≤ 1; pick f′ ∈ b with |f′| > ε and τ ∈ K with |τ| = |f′|, and put f = f′/τ, of Gauss norm 1. If the reduction f̄ ∈ k̃[X₁,…,Xₙ] is a constant, f is a unit of A₀ and a·b ⊆ τ·A₀ = A₀·f′ for |a| ≤ ε. Otherwise, after an automorphism X_i ↦ X_i + X_n^{c_i} (i < n), f is X_n-distinguished and Weierstrass division by it (BGR 5.2.1-5.2.2 for series of Gauss norm 1; the anchor Layer 0.5 Weierstrass request that AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-noether-normalisation also uses) makes A₀/(f) a finite K°⟨X₁,…,X_{n−1}⟩-module (generated by 1, X_n, …, X_n^{s−1}); apply the induction hypothesis to the image of b in A₀/(f) with ε/|τ| < 1 to get f₁,…,f_r ∈ b with (a/τ)·b ⊆ Σ A₀f_i + A₀f, hence a·b ⊆ Σ A₀f_i + A₀f′ for |a| ≤ ε (Kiehl pp. 212-213).
acceptance: For K = ℂ_p, A₀ = 𝒪_{ℂ_p} and N = 𝔪 (not finitely generated): for every ε < 1 one may take N′ = x·𝒪_{ℂ_p} with ε < |x| < 1, since a·𝔪 ⊆ x𝒪 when |a| ≤ ε.
For K discretely valued the lemma is the noetherianity of K°⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩.

nodes.title: Dagger algebras (and affinoid algebras) are excellent in characteristic 0
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value of rank one with char K = 0 (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K, CharZero K). Then W_n = K⟨X_1, …, X_n⟩† and T_n = K⟨X_1, …, X_n⟩ are excellent rings; consequently every K-dagger algebra and every K-affinoid algebra is excellent, and for A a dagger algebra and m a maximal ideal the local ring A_m is reduced (resp. normal) iff its completion is.
hypotheses: K complete, nontrivially and nonarchimedeanly valued (rank one)
char K = 0
proofSteps: W_n and T_n are regular noetherian rings all of whose maximal ideals have height n (F1/overconvergent-faithful-flatness (d) for W_n; the Tate case is the anchor/R0 input), hence Cohen–Macaulay and universally catenary; quotients of excellent rings are excellent, so it suffices to treat W_n and T_n.

Matsumura's criterion (Commutative Algebra, 2nd ed., Thm 102): a regular ring A containing ℚ is excellent if for every maximal ideal m of height n there are D_1, …, D_n ∈ Der(A) and x_1, …, x_n ∈ m with D_i(x_j) = δ_ij. For T_n this is how Conrad (Irreducible components, §1.1) obtains excellence of affinoids in characteristic 0. For W_n use the K-derivations ∂/∂X_i, which preserve W_n (F1/overconvergent-tate-algebra, API pderiv_mem_washnitzerAlgebra); at a K-rational maximal ideal take x_j = X_j − a_j, and reduce the general case to this one by a finite (separable, since char K = 0) extension K'/K over which m becomes a union of rational points, W_n ⊗_K K' being the Washnitzer algebra over K' (as Conrad does for T_n with BGR 6.1.2/3 and Matsumura Thm 23.7).
Excellent local rings: for an excellent noetherian local ring, reducedness and normality are equivalent to those of the completion (EGA IV 7.8.3(v)).

Characteristic p is NOT covered: Conrad attributes excellence of affinoids in characteristic p to Kiehl (with a regularity criterion, Conrad Thm 1.1.1), and no packet source proves excellence of W_n in characteristic p; Grosse-Klönne's 'all rings are excellent' is an unproved assertion there.
acceptance: For K = ℚ_p, W_1 is excellent and the completion of K⟨X,Y⟩†/(Y^2 − X^3) at (X,Y) is K[[X,Y]]/(Y^2 − X^3), reduced but not normal, matching the dagger algebra.

uses.how: ascent of reducedness and normality from A to Â through completed local rings

nodes.title: The integral Monsky–Washnitzer algebra O_K⟨X_1, …, X_n⟩† is noetherian (O_K a DVR)
nodes.statement: Let O_K be a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformiser π and fraction field K. Then O_K⟨X_1, …, X_n⟩† = W_n ∩ O_K[[X]] is a noetherian ring.
hypotheses: O_K a complete discrete valuation ring
proofSteps: Leading terms: order ℕ^n by a monomial order ≤ refining total degree (deglex); for 0 ≠ a = Σ a_I X^I ∈ O_K⟨X⟩† call π^{v}X^I its leading term, where v = min_I v_π(a_I) and I is the ≤-largest index with v_π(a_I) = v; as in Kedlaya's proof of Lemma 2.4.1 the 1-leading term coincides with the ρ-leading term for every ρ > 1 close enough to 1 (only finitely many I have |a_I|ρ_0^{|I|} ≥ |π|^v).

Given an ideal 𝔞, choose a_1, a_2, … ∈ 𝔞 whose leading terms (v_i, I_i) ∈ ℕ × ℕ^n are not divisible by earlier ones (divisibility = componentwise ≤); Dickson's lemma (ℕ^{n+1} is a well partial order) makes the process stop, so every leading term of an element of 𝔞 is a multiple of the leading term of some a_i in the finite set A.

Division: for f ∈ 𝔞 repeatedly subtract monomial multiples c·a_i (c = u π^w X^J, u ∈ O_K^×) cancelling the leading term; each step either raises the π-adic valuation of the remainder or lowers its leading index under the well order ≤, and since the valuation is discrete the valuations tend to ∞, so the quotients converge π-adically; choosing ρ_0 > 1 with all a_i ∈ T_n(ρ_0) and 1-leading = ρ-leading terms for ρ ≤ ρ_0 keeps the quotients in T_n(ρ) with |·|_ρ bounded by that of f (Kedlaya's estimate |z_j|_ρ ≤ |z|_ρ), hence in O_K⟨X⟩†. Thus 𝔞 = (A).
Alternative route: van der Put (2.2) asserts Weierstrass preparation and division for R⟨x⟩† (no proof given) and deduces noetherianity as in BGR 5.2.6.
acceptance: n = 1: every ideal of O_K⟨X⟩† is finitely generated, e.g. (π, X) and (X − π) are, and O_K⟨X⟩†/(X − π) = O_K.

uses.how: noetherianity of O_K⟨X⟩† and of weak completions; faithful flatness of O_K⟨X⟩† → O_K⟨X⟩

sources.match: The Gröbner-basis route of the proof steps (Kedlaya's K is discretely valued, which the termination argument uses).

nodes.title: The integral subring of a dagger algebra of MW-type is a Monsky–Washnitzer lift
nodes.statement: Let O_K be a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic (0, p) with uniformiser π, residue field k and fraction field K, and let A be a K-dagger algebra of MW-type (F1/mw-type-dagger-algebra) with reduction A_0 = A^int/πA^int. Then there are a smooth finitely generated O_K-algebra S with S/πS ≅ A_0 and an isomorphism of K-algebras A ≅ S† ⊗_{O_K} K carrying A^int onto S†; in particular A^int is weakly complete finitely generated and flat over O_K (a lift of A_0), and two dagger algebras of MW-type with isomorphic reductions are isomorphic.
hypotheses: O_K a complete DVR of mixed characteristic (0, p)
A a K-dagger algebra of MW-type
proofSteps: Choose S smooth over O_K with S/πS ≅ A_0 (F1/mw-lift-existence-uniqueness (a), Elkik) and put B = S† ⊗ K, of MW-type with B^int = S† (F1/weak-completion-generic-fibre (c),(d)).

Completions: A is regular, so Â is regular (the regularity part of F1/dagger-completion-comparison (3), which needs only completed local rings), hence reduced, and Â° is the π-adic completion of A^int with Â°/πÂ° = A^int/πA^int = A_0 (A^int = A ∩ Â° is dense in Â° and πA^int = A^int ∩ πÂ°); likewise B̂° = Ŝ. Lifting id_{A_0} step by step through the smooth O_K/π^m-algebras Ŝ/π^m (formal smoothness, as in step 1 of F1/mw-morphism-lifting) gives φ̂ : Ŝ → Â° with φ̂ ≡ id mod π; it is surjective (φ̂ mod π is surjective and both sides are π-adically complete and separated, so successive approximation applies) and injective (Â° is π-torsion free and φ̂ mod π is injective), so φ̂ is an isomorphism.

Apply F1/dagger-approximation (2) (with p_1, p_2 the identities) to φ̂ ⊗ K : B̂ ≅ Â: there is an isomorphism γ : B → A of dagger algebras. Isomorphisms preserve supremum norms, so γ(S†) = γ(B^int) = A^int.
The last claim: two MW-type algebras with isomorphic reductions are both isomorphic to S† ⊗ K for the same S.
acceptance: A = W_n: S = O_K[X_1..X_n], A^int = O_K⟨X⟩†.

nodes.title: A locally closed immersion of affinoid rigid spaces is Runge over a finite rational covering (BGR 7.3.5/1)
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value of rank one, E → D a homomorphism of K-affinoid algebras defining a locally closed immersion Sp(D) → Sp(E) (bijective onto its image and surjective on all local rings). Then there are finitely many rational subdomains W_1, …, W_s covering Sp(E) such that each Sp(D) ×_{Sp E} W_i → W_i is a Runge immersion, i.e. factors as a closed immersion into a Weierstrass domain of W_i.
hypotheses: K complete rank-one nonarchimedean
E → D a locally closed immersion of K-affinoid spaces
proofSteps: Local statement: for x = φ(y), O_{E,x} → O_{D,y} is surjective; choose affinoid generators d_1..d_r of D and a rational neighbourhood U of x with elements a_j ∈ O(U) whose germs map to the germs of the d_j; on a smaller rational neighbourhood the d_j and the images of the a_j agree on φ^{-1}(U), so D ⊗̂_E O(U) is generated by the image of O(U) and φ^{-1}(U) → U factors through the Weierstrass domain {|a_j| ≤ |d_j|_sup} as a closed immersion.
Points outside the image: for x ∉ φ(Sp D) with a neighbourhood missing the (Zariski-closed in a neighbourhood) image, take a rational neighbourhood U with φ^{-1}(U) = ∅ (trivially Runge).
Compactness: rational neighbourhoods refine to a finite rational covering of the quasi-compact Sp(E) (R1/gerritzen-grauert and the rational-covering refinement of the anchor Layer 2).
This is BGR Proposition 7.3.5/1, cited by Grosse-Klönne in the proof of his Proposition 2.5; BGR was not read, so the steps above are a reconstruction to be checked.
acceptance: The inclusion of the Laurent domain {|X| ≥ |π|} ⊆ Sp(K⟨X⟩) is an open (hence locally closed) immersion which is Runge over the covering {|X| ≤ |π|}, {|X| ≥ |π|}.

nodes.title: Trace maps for the projection X × Y → Y with X smooth and proper (Grosse-Klönne, Finiteness, Proposition 1.11)
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth proper K-dagger (resp. rigid) space of pure dimension n, Y a smooth pure-dimensional K-dagger (resp. rigid) space and p : Z = X × Y → Y the projection. For rigid spaces assume char K = 0; for dagger spaces assume moreover K = Frac(R) for a complete discrete valuation ring R of mixed characteristic (0, p) (the proof uses Grosse-Klönne 2000, Theorem 3.5, which is stated under this hypothesis). Then there is a canonical trace map p_+O_Z[n] → O_Y of D_Y-modules. If moreover T → Y and S → Z ×_Y T = X × T are closed immersions, there are canonical trace maps p_+RΓ*_S O_Z[n] → RΓ*_T O_Y and RΓ(Z, DR(RΓ*_S O_Z))[2n] → RΓ(Y, DR(RΓ*_T O_Y)), which are isomorphisms if the composite S → X × T → T is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: X smooth proper of pure dimension n, Y smooth pure dimensional
char K = 0; in the dagger case K discretely valued of mixed characteristic
proofSteps: Rigid case: by Beyer ([3], not read — gap) X has a finite admissible covering by U_i whose finite intersections U_J admit closed immersions into open polydiscs (D^0)^{n_J} with R^j(p_J)_!F = 0 for j > n; Mayer–Vietoris gives R^jp_!F = 0 for coherent F and j > n, hence R^{2n}p_!Ω^•_{Z/Y} = R^np_!ω_{Z/Y}/im(R^np_!Ω^{n−1}_{Z/Y}) and p_+O_Z[n] ≅ Rp_!Ω^•_{Z/Y}.

Define t_p on (D^0)^{n_J} × Ŷ as the residue ω = Σ_{µ<0} a_µT^µ dT ↦ a_{(−1,…,−1)}, precomposed with the Gysin map ω ↦ ω̃ ∧ dX_{n+1}/X_{n+1} ∧ … for U_J ⊆ (D^0)^{n_J}; independence of the embedding and gluing over J give t_p, vanishing on the image of R^np_!Ω^{n−1}_{Z/Y}.

Dagger case: R^jp_!F = R^jp_*F = 0 for coherent F and j > n by Grosse-Klönne 2000, Theorem 3.5 (coherence of higher direct images for proper morphisms, under its hypotheses (1) K = Frac of a complete DVR of mixed characteristic and (2) extendability to a proper rigid morphism over a strict neighbourhood, satisfied here by X' × Y'_ε → Y'_ε); t_{p'} for the associated rigid morphism takes R^np_!ω_{Z/Y} into O_Y ⊆ O_{Y'}, giving t_p (the direct limit of the t_{p_ε}).

Supports: derive the maps with S, T from t_p by the isomorphisms of GK2002 1.9 (RΓ(Z, DR(RΓ*_S O_Z)) ≅ RΓ(Y, Rp_!DR(RΓ*_S O_Z)) because S → T is quasi-compact). Isomorphism when S → T is an isomorphism: local on X, so replace X by (D^0)^n; after passing to an admissible covering of Y choose a section s : Y → Z inducing the inverse of S → T, identify RΓ*_T O_Y ≅ p_+RΓ*_S O_Z[n] via the Gysin isomorphism (F1/dagger-local-cohomology-comparison (b)), and check that the composite O_Y → O_Y is the identity after reducing to Y = Sp(K) (O_Y(Y) is Jacobson).
acceptance: X = Sp(K) (n = 0): p = id and the trace is the identity. X = P^1 over Y = Sp(K): the trace H^2_dR(P^{1,†}) → K is the residue isomorphism.

nodes.title: Independence of the embedding for de Rham cohomology with supports, and the invariants h^dR_q (Grosse-Klönne, Finiteness, 1.12–1.13)
nodes.statement: Let K = Frac(R) for a complete discrete valuation ring R of mixed characteristic (0, p) (the trace of F1/dagger-proper-projection-trace is used for dagger spaces). For closed immersions g_i : Z → Y_i (i = 1, 2) into smooth affinoid K-dagger spaces of pure dimensions n_i, RΓ(Y_1, DR(RΓ*_Z O_{Y_1}))[2n_1] ≅ RΓ(Y_2, DR(RΓ*_Z O_{Y_2}))[2n_2]. Consequently, for an affinoid K-dagger space Z and a closed immersion Z → Y into a smooth affinoid dagger space of pure dimension n, h^dR_q(Z) := dim_K H^{2n−q}(Y, DR(RΓ*_Z O_Y)) = dim_K H^{2n−q}_Z(Y, Ω^•_Y) (F1/dagger-local-cohomology-comparison (a)) depends only on Z.
hypotheses: K discretely valued of mixed characteristic
Z → Y_i closed immersions into smooth affinoid dagger spaces of pure dimension
proofSteps: Reduce to Y_i = D^{n_i} (closed dagger polydiscs) using the Gysin isomorphism for closed immersions Y_i → D^{n_i} (F1/dagger-local-cohomology-comparison (b) and GK2002 1.9, 1.10).

Compare both with the diagonal embedding l : Z → X = Y_1 × Y_2: for i = 1 embed X openly into W = Y_1 × P^{n_2} (Y_2 = D^{n_2} ⊆ P^{n_2}); excision gives RΓ(X, DR(RΓ*_Z O_X)) ≅ RΓ(W, DR(RΓ*_Z O_W)), and the trace isomorphism of F1/dagger-proper-projection-trace for the projection W → Y_1 (with S = Z → Y_1 an isomorphism onto its image) gives RΓ(Y_1, DR(RΓ*_Z O_{Y_1})) ≅ RΓ(X, DR(RΓ*_Z O_X))[2n_2]; symmetrically for i = 2.
The definition of h^dR_q is then independent of Y.
acceptance: Z = a K-rational point: h^dR_0(Z) = 1 and h^dR_q(Z) = 0 for q ≠ 0, whether Z is embedded in D^1 or in D^2.

coverage.note: R0 has four groups of declarations. R0.0: the classical affinoid algebras (Noether normalisation, residue fields and the Jacobson property, supremum seminorm and maximum modulus, power-boundedness, integrality of A°, reductions). R0a: rings of noetherian type, adic homomorphisms, sheafiness for rings with a noetherian ring of definition (Huber 1994 Theorem 2.2, Case I) and discrete pairs, the spectral seminorm and uniformisation, the completed tensor product of Huber pairs with its topology, plus ring, universal property and uniformisation, fibre products of adic spaces under Huber's hypotheses with their points and base change, adic morphisms and the finite-type classes compared with the anchor's locally-finite-type morphisms, locally noetherian adic spaces, closed adic subspaces and the diagonal. R0b: separated, universally closed, proper and partially proper morphisms with the valuative criteria and closure properties, finite and quasi-finite morphisms. R0c: continuous differentials, flat, unramified, smooth and étale morphisms, the Jacobian criterion, standard étale presentations, smooth morphisms as étale over polydiscs, and the local structure of étale morphisms. Every target of the RS-05 narrowing of R0 is realised by a node. The stage is source-decomposed: the proof inputs that were not read (Huber's 1996 book beyond the reviewed decomposition's transcriptions, his habilitation, Huber–Knebusch, Bosch–Güntzer–Remmert, and the propositions Huber asserts 'similarly as for schemes') are recorded gaps, the diagonal lemma carries its own proof, and the anchor's Layers 0–5 are requests.

Every target of the R1 stage text is realised: the analytification from affine charts with independence of presentation and gluing (Huber 1994 Proposition 3.8), its universal property, fibre products, open and closed immersions, finite, étale and smooth maps with converses for maps of finite type, the separatedness and properness comparison, Tate's rigid spaces with affinoid subdomains and Huber's rigid–adic comparison, analytic groups (finite locally free group schemes, abelian varieties, isogenies and quotient maps) with invariant differentials, and the rigid identity principle. Proper GAGA, the second half of the R1 stage text, is realised by AdicSpacesPartII:R3/proper-gaga and AdicSpacesPartII:R3/gaga-finite-covers, which list R1 in realises (restructure proposal). The stage is source-decomposed: the unread proof sources (BGR for the affinoid-subdomain theory, Huber 1994 Proposition 4.5(ii)–(iv), [Hu4]/[L1]) and the unpublished differential comparison are recorded gaps; the anchor's Layers 3–5 are requests.

Every target of the RS-05 narrowing of F0 is realised: Spf and formal schemes for adic rings with a finitely generated ideal of definition (with the noetherian theorems stated as such), independence of the ideal of definition, gluing, the equivalence with compatible systems of thickenings, functorial completion, coherent formal modules with the affine equivalence and the description by inverse systems, the theorem on formal functions, Grothendieck's existence theorem, full faithfulness, and algebraisation under the ample-line-bundle hypothesis (EGA I §10, EGA III §§4–5). gaps.title: Huber 1996, Propositions 1.6.7-1.6.9 are asserted by analogy with schemes; locality of smoothness on the source is not automatic
gaps.detail: The source says 'can be proved similarly as for schemes (cf. [EGA], [I])'. The nodes transport the EGA IV §17 arguments; each is a proof obligation. For injectivity (unramified, étale) and for the examples (open embeddings, relative polydiscs, monomorphisms) the transport is direct. For locality of smoothness on the source (1.6.7), the scheme proof glues local lifts using vanishing of H¹ of a quasi-coherent module on an affine; the test objects Spa A of Definition 1.6.5 are affinoid pre-adic spaces of arbitrary complete Huber pairs, for which Čech acyclicity of M ⊗ O on rational covers is only known under noetherian hypotheses (Huber 1994 Theorem 2.5; anchor Layer 4). Next action: either prove the needed H¹-vanishing for the torsor of lifts (the module Hom(ḡ*Ω, I) with I square-zero) directly, or restrict the test objects in Definition 1.6.5 and prove equivalence with Huber's definition for locally noetherian X, Y. Locality on the source also needs, for a test object Spa A with A not sheafy, that two morphisms Spa A → X agreeing on a rational covering of Spa A are equal; this fails in general, since O_{Spa A}(Spa A) → ∏ O(Wⱼ) need not be injective (Hübner, Example 3.5, after Buzzard–Verberkmoes): for κ ≠ 0 in the kernel and m large, the continuous maps K⟨X⟩ → A, X ↦ 0 and X ↦ ϖᵐκ, give distinct morphisms Spa A → Spa K⟨X⟩ that agree on every Wⱼ. So the unramified and étale cases of locality on the source, and the global step of R0/smooth-etale-base-change (whose chart case is unconditional), are proved here for sheafy test objects; the same next action (restricting the test objects to sheafy A and proving the equivalence with Huber's definition for locally noetherian X, Y) closes both. [REV-AdicSpacesPartII (imprecise): The stated obstruction does not apply to the book. Its standing assumption (1.1.1) (p. 37) restricts every f-adic ring, including the test rings A of Definition 1.6.5 (p. 78), to 'Â noetherian ring of definition / strongly noetherian Tate / discrete'. Such Spa A are sheafy and Čech-acyclic for M⊗O (Huber 1994 Thms 2.2, 2.5), so the Buzzard–Verberkmoes non-sheafy example is excluded. The 'next action' (restrict the test objects) is Huber's own convention. What remains is H¹-vanishing of the coherent torsor sheaf Hom(ḡ*Ω, I⊗O) on such Spa A: Kiehl-type, available for strongly noetherian Tate A, and missing for a noetherian ring of definition (gap 47). Neither library has anything here (no adic]

For étale morphisms of affinoid adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°) the statement is de Jong–van der Put, Étale cohomology of rigid analytic spaces, Documenta Math. 1 (1996), Proposition 3.1.4 (public; proof read), which R0/etale-affinoid-finite-etale-embedding follows. Next action: decompose dJvdP Lemmas 2.1.1, 3.1.5 and 3.1.6 into R0 lemma nodes in adic language; for (1), read Huber 1996 §2.2. The following BGR inputs of F1 are planned nowhere and were not read: 5.2.7/8 (ideals of T_n are strictly closed; F1/overconvergent-tate-algebra-properties (2)); excellence of affinoid algebras (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 2.5.3, Kiehl; F1/dagger-completion-comparison (3)); 6.3.2/1–2 (lifting integral equations from reductions; F1/dagger-finite-morphism-comparison (b)); 7.3.3/5 and 8.2.1/4 (open immersions of affinoid spaces and their images; F1/dagger-affinoid-subdomain-completion (a), F1/dagger-g-topology (a)); the proof pattern of 8.2.1/1 and 8.2.2 transported to dagger algebras (F1/dagger-tate-acyclicity); 9.2.3/1 (extension of sheaves from affinoid subdomains to the strong G-topology; F1/dagger-coherent-module); 7.2.3/3 and 7.2.4/1 (Runge immersions; F1/dagger-to-rigid-functor (6)). [REV-AdicSpacesPartII (imprecise): The first item (BGR 5.2.7/8: ideals of T_n are closed, and quotient maps strict) follows from Tau Ceti once T_n is noetherian, which request 0 asks of Layer 0: TauCeti.Huber.isClosed_of_isNoetherian (RingTheory/Huber/ClosedSubmodule.lean:126) and TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isStrictMap_of_isClosed_range (OpenMapping.lean:199). Drop it. The remaining items (excellence, BGR 6.3.2/1–2, 7.3.3/5, 8.2.1/4, 9.2.3/1, 7.2.3/3, 7.2.4/1) are honestly missing and exactly named.]

gaps.title: Size convention for the étale and pro-étale sites
gaps.detail: The étale sites are large categories; Mathlib's sheafification, sheaf pullback and comparison lemma need essential smallness. No node fixes a universe or a small full subcategory (e.g. affinoid étale objects of bounded cardinality) and proves the comparison. Found by the review.

gaps.title: Adic-proper implies Kiehl-proper beyond discretely valued fields
gaps.detail: Huber 1996 Remark 1.3.19 gives the implication only for discretely valued K and Conrad A.1 does not state it; the review made the general case conditional. A Temkin-style comparison (or a restriction of the proper-mapping chain to discretely valued K) is needed.

gaps.title: Kiehl's theorem for completed coefficient sheaves with R not finite over ℤ_p
gaps.detail: CHJ Lemmas 6.19(2) and 6.21 fail when R is not finite over ℤ_p (e.g. R = ℤ_p[[T]]); the review restricted the node to R finite free. The general statement has no proof.

gaps.title: Ascent of reducedness and normality to completions of dagger algebras in characteristic p
gaps.detail: The review routes these through excellence of dagger algebras, available here only in characteristic 0; the characteristic-p case and the converse 'rigid partially proper ⇒ dagger partially proper' remain unproved.

gaps.title: Unsourced part of geometric-points-pullback
gaps.detail: Part (c) of the node has no source proof (Scholze leaves it to the reader); it should be proved or split off.

restructure.detail: Grosse-Klönne's finiteness theorem for de Rham cohomology of dagger spaces reduces, through semistable tubes, to the finite-dimensionality of Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology of smooth affine schemes over the residue field (Berthelot 1997, Mebkhout 1997). In the atlas that finiteness is owned by PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology RD.5 (finiteness, duality and Künneth), and RD.0–RD.5 consume AdicSpacesPartII F1 (dagger algebras, fringe topology, dagger spaces, de Rham complexes). Citing RD.5 from F1 would create the stage cycle F1 → RD.5 → F1, so six F1 nodes currently rest on the gap 'Finiteness of Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology … cannot be a prerequisite of F1': AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-semistable-tube-finiteness (uses MW finiteness directly for H_dR(Sp B), B = D† ⊗ K), AdicSpacesPartII:F1/quasi-algebraic-affinoid-finiteness (uses it through the semistable tubes of a de Jong alteration), AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-de-rham-finiteness-and-base-change (Grosse-Klönne Theorems 3.6/4.4/4.9, via the previous node), AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-strict-differentials (the Stein case closes only with finite-dimensional H^{i+1}_dR, and the affinoid case reduces to the Stein interiors X_ρ, whose finiteness is the previous node), AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-de-rham-kunneth and AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-poincare-duality (both assume or use the finiteness and the strictness). No other F1 node depends on them (checked on the prerequisite graph).
restructure.proposal: Move these six nodes, unchanged in statement, to PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology RD.5 as applications of MW finiteness to dagger spaces: AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-semistable-tube-finiteness, AdicSpacesPartII:F1/quasi-algebraic-affinoid-finiteness, AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-de-rham-finiteness-and-base-change, AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-strict-differentials, AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-de-rham-kunneth, AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-poincare-duality. F1 keeps every input they use that does not need finiteness (dagger-semistable-tube-invariance, dagger-polyannulus-de-rham-cohomology, de-rham-cohomology-with-supports, dagger-local-cohomology-comparison, dagger-resolution-lemma, dagger-finite-etale-trace, dagger-proper-modification-sequence, dagger-de-rham-finite-field-extension, dagger-serre-duality, compact-support-de-rham, fringe-topology), so the moved nodes depend on F1 and on RD.5's MW finiteness, and the order F1 → RD.5 stays acyclic. F1's stage text 'Prove local acyclicity/base-change statements with convergence and finiteness hypotheses explicit' is then met with finiteness as an explicit hypothesis, and RD.5's description gains 'finite-dimensionality, Künneth and Poincaré duality for the de Rham cohomology of smooth dagger spaces (Grosse-Klönne, Finiteness §§3–4)'. AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.4, which uses F1/dagger-de-rham-finiteness-and-base-change, gains a link RD.5 → AG2.4. The F1 gap on MW finiteness is then deleted.

restructure.detail: R1's description ends its first paragraph with 'Establish the properness comparison and the proper GAGA results required for algebraic coefficient sheaves.' Proper GAGA needs coherent sheaves on adic spaces, Kiehl's theorem on affinoids and the proper mapping theorem, which are R3's (R3 depends on R0–R2 and R2 on R1), so R1 cannot prove it. The packet realises it by AdicSpacesPartII:R3/proper-gaga, AdicSpacesPartII:R3/proper-gaga-coherent-equivalence and AdicSpacesPartII:R3/gaga-finite-covers (the PerfectoidSpaces P8 request), whose realises lists name R1 as well as R3, and by AdicSpacesPartII:R3/analytification-coherent (coherence of F^an).
restructure.proposal: Move the target 'proper GAGA' from R1 to R3. R1 keeps: 'Establish the properness comparison (X proper ⇔ X^ad proper) and the analytification of coherent modules as sheaves of O_{X^ad}-modules (exactness, tensor and pullback compatibility).' R3 gains: 'Prove proper GAGA over an affinoid base: coherence of F^an, the comparison (R^i f_* F)^an ≅ R^i f^an_* F^an for proper f, the equivalence of coherent sheaves on proper X and X^an, and the algebraicity of finite analytic covers of X^an for proper X.' The realises lists of R3/proper-gaga and R3/gaga-finite-covers then name R3 only, and the link R1 → R3 (already implied by R1 → R2 → R3) carries R1/analytification-of-modules, R1/analytification-separated-proper and R1/analytification-reflects-finite-closed-immersion.

restructure.detail: Layer R0 has 121 nodes (PROTOCOL §14: a layer too broad to read as one star may be divided). Its nodes fall into four groups: the classical affinoid algebras (Noether normalisation, residue fields, supremum seminorm, integrality of A°, reductions); with a clear dependency order: affinoid products and fibre products (the ring-level inputs, Huber 1994 Theorem 2.2 Case I, uniformization, completed tensor products, fibre products, adic and finite-type classes, closed subspaces); separated, proper, finite and quasi-finite morphisms (Huber 1996 §§1.3–1.5); differentials, smooth and étale morphisms (Huber 1996 §§1.6–1.7). The R0 planets fall 0 / 2 / 2 / 2.

(1) Huber 1994 Theorem 2.2, Case I (sheafiness of complete Huber pairs with a noetherian ring of definition, and the discrete case, Wedhorn 8.28(c)) had no owner: the anchor's Layer 4 covers only strongly noetherian Tate rings and Buzzard–Verberkmoes. It is now planned in R0 (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-rod-sheafy, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/discrete-huber-pair-sheafy and their lemmas, including Huber's (1.3) for finite modules, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-rod-laurent-cech-strict, moved from R3). (2) Uniformization of completed tensor products (AdicEtaleGeometry A0's supplier contract; consumed by PerfectoidSpaces P2) is planned in R0 (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-seminorm, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product). (3) Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 2.4.23 (Čech acyclicity of O for every sheafy Tate pair) extends the anchor's Layer 4 and is planned in R3 (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheafy-cech-acyclicity); RS-05's narrowing of R3 ('import anchor structure-sheaf acyclicity') assumed the anchor states it, which it does only for strongly noetherian rings. sourceIssues.locator: §3, proof of Proposition 3.7, printed p. 536 (GDZ scan read)
sourceIssues.printed: The source gives D^▷ := E^▷/λ'(ker σ) · E^▷ an f-adic topology making π: E^▷ → D^▷ both open and continuous. It claims the construction is cocartesian among complete affinoid rings (3.5.i).
sourceIssues.correction: D is complete (as needed for 'complete affinoid rings') only because the ideal λ'(ker σ)·E^▷ is closed; this holds since E^▷ = B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)} has a noetherian ring of definition or is a strongly noetherian Tate ring, by Lemma 2.3(ii) / Lemma 2.4(ii). In general the closure of the extended ideal must be taken.
sourceIssues.reason: A quotient of a complete metrisable ring by a non-closed ideal is not Hausdorff, hence not a complete affinoid ring in Huber's convention (complete includes Hausdorff).
sourceIssues.known: Huber 1996, proof of Proposition 1.2.2 (as recorded in the reviewed decomposition) and Hübner 2024, proof of Theorem 9.2(iii), take the closure J_i of the extended ideal.

review.reason: Checked on the page image of printed p. 536 (Huber 1994 scan, pdf p. 25): the quoted sentences are there (D^▷ := E^▷/λ'(ker σ)·E^▷ with the quotient f-adic topology; 'cocartesian in the category of complete affinoid rings (3.5.i)'). Completeness of D^▷ is never argued; it holds because E^▷ = B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)} has a noetherian ring of definition or is strongly noetherian Tate (3.4.ii,iii), so every ideal is closed by Lemma 2.3(ii) resp. Lemma 2.4(ii) (read on p. 525). The step is an omitted routine justification with the needed lemma in the paper, so 'gap/affects the proof' is right in substance but minor.

sourceIssues.printed: The source defines ⟨Γ_x⟩ and ⟨Γ_y⟩ as the convex hulls inside Γ_v of the groups Γ_x and Γ_x associated with x and y. For each i ∈ I, it claims cofinality of w(i) in Γ_w follows from cofinality of x(i) in Γ_x and y(i) in Γ_y.

review.reason: Amend: keep only the first correction. Page image of printed p. 538 shows 'the value groups Γ_x and Γ_x of x and y' (misprint for Γ_y) - confirmed. The second correction is wrong and must be dropped together with its reason: Huber 1993 §2 (OCR of Math. Z. 212, before Lemma 2.4) defines 'an element γ of Γ∪{0} is cofinal in a subgroup H of Γ if for every h∈H there is n with γ^n < h', so 'w(i) is cofinal in Γ_w for every i ∈ I' is correct as printed (it is exactly the continuity criterion of Huber 1993 Lemma 2.5/Thm 3.1); 'cofinality is a property of a subset' is false in Huber's usage.

sourceIssues.locator: §II.3.2, proof of Proposition II.3.2.1 (version of April 22, 2019)
sourceIssues.printed: Using continuity of u′ and v′, the source chooses r ≥ 1 such that u′−1(U) ⊃ (f(I)B0)^r, together with v′−1(U) ⊃ (f(I)C0)^r. It infers ϕ−1(U) ⊃ J^r and concludes that ϕ−1(U) is open.
sourceIssues.correction: Choose an open subgroup V with V·V ⊆ U and r with u′(f(I)^r B0) ⊆ V, v′(g(I)^r C0) ⊆ V; then ϕ(J^{2r}) ⊆ V·V ⊆ U. The second inclusion should read (g(I)C0)^r.
sourceIssues.reason: J^r is generated by products (f(I)^r B0)·(C0), whose images need not lie in U; only the products of two small factors are controlled.
searched: Morel's page (the 2019 notes are the version read)
Wedhorn arXiv:1910.05934v1 §8.6

review.reason: Morel notes (version of April 22, 2019), p. 77, proof of Prop. II.3.2.1: 'there exists r ≥ 1 such that u′−1(U) ⊃ (f(I)B0)^r and v′−1(U) ⊃ (f(I)C0)^r. Then ϕ−1(U) ⊃ J^r' - quoted correctly. J^r is generated by images u(f(i)b)v(c) with i ∈ I^r, c ∈ C0 arbitrary, whose images u′(f(i)b)v′(c) need not lie in U (U is only a subgroup); with V·V ⊆ U and J^{2r} generated by u(f(i1)b)v(g(i2)c), i1,i2 ∈ I^r, one gets ϕ(J^{2r}) ⊆ V·V ⊆ U. Also amend the reason: by the book's standing assumption (1.1.1) (p. 37: every f-adic ring has a noetherian ring of definition after completion, is strongly noetherian Tate, or is discrete) the test rings are noetherian, so Huber 1994 Thm 2.5 (acyclicity of M⊗O_A for finitely generated M) is available; what the gluing still needs is acyclicity of the coherent sheaf Hom(ḡ*Ω_{X/Y}, I⊗O) on Spa A, i.e. a Kiehl-type statement, available for strongly noetherian Tate A but not established in the sources for A with a noetherian ring of definition. So the step is a real gap, but not for the reason 'acyclicity known only for noetherian A'.

review.reason: The book (read directly, p. 61) has the quoted converse of (1.4.2) verbatim, but the book's standing hypothesis (1.1.1), p. 37: 'If not stated otherwise, throughout this book every f-adic ring A is assumed to satisfy one of the following conditions: a) Â has a noetherian ring of definition over which Â is finitely generated, b) A is a strongly noetherian Tate ring, c) the topology of A is discrete.' Under (a)/(b) a finite A-module is complete in its natural topology (Huber 1994 Lemmas 2.3(ii), 2.4(ii)), so the converse is correct in the book. The counterexample K⟨X1, X2, …⟩ (correctly computed: Σϖ^nX_n lies in the closure of the algebraic ideal but not in it) violates (1.1.1). The entry's own caveat ('may be a standing assumption') is what happened. The packet should instead record (1.1.1) as a hypothesis wherever it uses the converse outside Huber's setting.

sourceIssues.printed: Definition 2.8.1 asserts equivalence, for a Banach ring A, of: (a) equivalence of its norm to some power-multiplicative norm; (b) equivalence of its norm to its spectral seminorm; (c) existence of c > 0 with |x2 | ≥ c |x|2 for every x ∈ A; and (d) boundedness of the subring A◦.
sourceIssues.correction: (a)-(c) are equivalent and define uniformity; they imply (d), and (d) implies that the spectral norm defines the topology; (d) implies (a)-(c) when A contains a topologically nilpotent unit z with |z|·|z⁻¹| = 1 (for instance for the norms of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/tate-ring-norm), but not in general.
sourceIssues.reason: On a complete nonarchimedean field K the norm |x| for |x| ≤ 1 and |x|(1 + log|x|) for |x| > 1 is submultiplicative, defines the topology of K (so K° is bounded) and is not equivalent to its spectral norm |·|; so (d) does not imply (b). The authors record this in the errata to the paper.

sourceIssues.locator: item (1), p. 1, in the three-page erratum (SHA-256 3cfa56b9…)
sourceIssues.printed: The source says an analogous condition belongs in the pro-étale covering definition, Definition 3.9, and also in Definition 3.4.
sourceIssues.correction: For Definition 3.9 the 'similar condition' is not displayed. The reading that preserves étale covers: each covering map U_i -> U is a composite of a transfinite composition of pullbacks of finite étale surjections (U_0 = W_i) and an étale map W_i -> U. Requiring U_i -> U itself to be such a transfinite composition, as a literal transfer of the Definition 3.3 condition, would exclude open covers.
sourceIssues.reason: A covering of X_proét by two open subspaces U_1, U_2 ⊆ X is a family of étale (open) immersions; an open immersion onto a proper open is not a transfinite composition of pullbacks of finite étale surjections (each such map is surjective on underlying spaces). So the Definition 3.3 condition cannot be transferred verbatim.

sourceIssues.locator: §3.1, proof of Corollary 3.4, p. 1725 (journal); same in arXiv v4
sourceIssues.printed: The source claims the object now exists and is sousperfectoid, because an étale algebra over a sousperfectoid algebra remains sousperfectoid, citing Proposition 6.3.3.(ii) op. cit.
sourceIssues.correction: Berkeley 6.3.3(2) concerns finite étale algebras only. The step holds in the following form: an étale map to the locally noetherian space B is locally an open immersion followed by a finite étale map (Huber Lemma 2.2.8); pulled back to the sousperfectoid X ×_L B, the finite étale pieces are sousperfectoid by 6.3.3(2) and their opens are covered by sousperfectoid rational subsets by 6.3.3(1). This proves that the fibre product is a sousperfectoid adic space (covered by sousperfectoid affinoids); the algebra-level statement 'étale algebras over sousperfectoid algebras are sousperfectoid' is proved only for composites of rational localisations and finite étale maps, since the sousperfectoid property is not known to be of local nature (Hansen-Kedlaya Definition 7.1).
sourceIssues.reason: Read against Berkeley Proposition 6.3.3 (statements (1)-(3)) and Hansen-Kedlaya Definition 7.1 ('we do not know whether the sousperfectoid property is of local nature').

For X = Spf R, 𝒜 = 𝔍 = πO_X (so φ = id) and ℳ = O_X/π², every section is supported in V(𝒜) (the whole space), but Ann_ℳ(π) = πR/π²R ≠ ℳ; so the two descriptions joined by 'i.e.' disagree and the strict transform would be R/π instead of 0. sourceIssues.printed: The source asserts that a bounded map A → B between uniform Banach rings, with spectral norms on both rings, is always submetric. It characterizes isometry by surjectivity of M(B) → M(A).
sourceIssues.correction: … is submetric in general, and isometric if and only if the image of M(B) → M(A) is a boundary for A (every x ∈ A attains its spectral norm on the image); in particular it is isometric if M(B) → M(A) is surjective, but not conversely.
sourceIssues.reason: By Theorem 2.3.10 the spectral norms are sup-norms over M(A) and M(B), which gives the corrected criterion. Counterexample to 'only if': K⟨T⟩ → K⟨T, T⁻¹⟩ is isometric for the Gauss norms (|Σ aₙTⁿ| = max|aₙ| in both rings), yet the image of M(K⟨T, T⁻¹⟩) is {|T| = 1} ≠ M(K⟨T⟩). Not listed in the Kedlaya–Liu II errata (Appendix A). Checked on the page image.

sourceIssues.printed: The source calls φλ(βλ(p(Til))) topologically nilpotent, as well as ψ(φλ(βλ(p(Til)))) ∈ B. It infers the existence of λ′′ > 1 and power-bounded til in Bλ′′, indexed by i = 1, . . . , n; l = 0, . . . , s, satisfying γλ′′(til) = ψ(φλ(βλ(p(Til)))).
sourceIssues.correction: An argument is needed that a topologically nilpotent element b of B lifts to a power-bounded element of some B_λ''. For instance: lift b to b̃ ∈ B_{λ1}, pick r ∈ Γ* with |b|_sup < r < 1; the Laurent domain {|b̃| ≥ r} of Sp(B_{λ1}) misses Sp(B′) = {|X_j| ≤ 1}, so 1 = Σ(Y_j − X_j)h_j over it, and approximating the h_j by polynomials shows it misses Sp(B_μ) for some μ > 1; then the image of b̃ in B_μ has spectral norm < 1.
sourceIssues.reason: The step is not formal (B_λ'' → B is neither injective nor isometric), and the natural justification via weak completeness (1.9) is circular, since 1.9 is proved 'as in the proof of 1.8'; Kedlaya's Corollary 2.3.5 likewise rests on 1.8.
